items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
Amupitan unveils safeguards against inaccurate IReV results, assures credible polls
By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe
LONDON — The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has announced November 28, 2026, for a nationwide mock accreditation and voting exercise to test its upgraded electoral technology and electronic result transmission system ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The commission also unveiled new technical safeguards to prevent inaccurate election results, including figures reflecting over-voting, from being uploaded to its Result Viewing Portal (IReV).
INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, disclosed this on Thursday in London while speaking at Chatham House during a high-level dialogue organised in partnership with the Kimpact Development Initiative (KDI).
The dialogue was held under the theme, “Nigeria’s 2027 Elections: Democratic Trajectory and Regional Stability Beyond the Ballot.”
According to a statement issued by his Chief Press Secretary and Media Adviser, Adedayo Oketola, and released by INEC’s Gombe office on Friday, Amupitan said the November 28 exercise would simulate the presidential election and test the commission’s accreditation and electronic result transmission processes.
He said the reforms were informed by lessons from the 2023 general elections, which he acknowledged had significantly eroded public confidence in the electoral commission.
“First and foremost, let me speak about what happened in 2023, which resulted in a significant trust deficit for INEC—damage so large that the Commission has not yet fully recovered from it,” he said.
The INEC chairman, who assumed office in October 2025, said the commission had used subsequent off-cycle elections to identify operational weaknesses and strengthen its accreditation, voting and result-management processes.
Citing the Anambra and Osun governorship elections, Federal Capital Territory Area Council polls, Ekiti governorship election and 16 legislative by-elections, he said the commission had recorded improvements in its electoral administration.
He particularly cited the Anambra and Osun governorship elections, where results were declared the day after voting, as evidence of improved coordination.
Amupitan recalled that the 2021 Anambra governorship election took about five days to conclude, arguing that the more recent exercise demonstrated progress.
“Why must Nigerians trust me? Nigerians must trust me because, number one, I have conducted off-cycle elections—and observers agree that the recent election in Osun State marked a clear improvement,” he said.
INEC introduces safeguards for IReV
On electronic transmission of results, Amupitan said the commission’s post-2023 assessment identified weaknesses in the result-management process, particularly at collation centres.
He said INEC had consequently introduced additional technical safeguards to ensure that results uploaded to IReV passed the necessary validation checks at polling-unit level.
“We found that the core problem of election result management and declaration in Nigeria is not even at the polling unit—it is at the collation centres,” he said.
“In 2023, there were instances of inaccurate results or results with over-voting being uploaded onto IReV. We have now devised a technical safeguard: if a result is not accurate at the polling unit, it will not go to IReV at all.”
He said the measures were intended to eliminate discrepancies at the point of entry and improve transparency and accountability in the collation process.
BVAS devices upgraded
On concerns over the performance of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) during the 2023 elections, the INEC chairman said the commission had taken steps to improve the reliability and efficiency of the devices.
He recalled that extreme temperatures and inadequate storage conditions contributed to equipment-related challenges during the previous general election.
To address the problem, he said INEC was constructing climate-controlled storage facilities across the states of the federation.
He added that the commission had procured additional BVAS devices and reduced the maximum number of registered voters assigned to each machine from 1,250 to 850.
Under the new arrangement, polling units with more than 850 registered voters would be provided with multiple devices to ease pressure on the equipment and facilitate accreditation.
Amupitan said the nationwide mock exercise scheduled for November 28 would test the upgraded devices, electronic transmission system and other critical components of the electoral process.
“On the 28th of this month, we will conduct a mock accreditation and voting exercise across all states of the federation to simulate the presidential election and verify that we have gotten both accreditation and electronic result transmission right,” he said.
Outstanding election funds expected this month
On funding for the 2027 general elections, Amupitan disclosed that INEC had received a substantial portion of its approved election budget but was still awaiting the release of the outstanding balance.
He said part of the outstanding funds would be required for the recruitment and welfare of ad hoc election personnel.
The chairman, however, said the commission had received assurances that the balance would be released before the end of November.
He identified insecurity, logistics and election result management as the three major operational priorities requiring sustained attention ahead of the elections.
Amupitan denies political bias allegations
The INEC chairman also reaffirmed his commitment to political neutrality, dismissing allegations circulating on social media linking his telephone number to a controversial account on X, formerly Twitter.
He denied operating an X account and disclosed that an independent forensic examination had been obtained, while the matter had been referred to the Department of State Services (DSS) and the Inspector-General of Police for investigation.
He also dismissed suggestions that his previous professional engagements as a lawyer in political disputes could compromise his impartiality as INEC chairman.
According to him, those engagements were undertaken strictly in his professional capacity as a Senior Advocate of Nigeria before his appointment.
“My loyalty is solely to the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and the Electoral Act,” he declared.
He stressed that all constitutional institutions, including the Presidency, National Assembly and state governments, must operate within the framework of the Constitution and the rule of law.
INEC responds to voter register concerns
On allegations of irregularities in the national voters’ register, including claims of an 85 per cent increase in registered voters in a ward in Ebonyi State, Amupitan said the commission had investigated and addressed the complaint in line with established statutory procedures.
He explained that the Electoral Act provides mechanisms for public claims, objections and requests for certified true copies of the voters’ register.
He urged stakeholders to utilise the established legal channels to raise and address concerns about the register.
Youth participation, misinformation
The INEC chairman also urged Nigerian youths to remain actively involved in the democratic process, warning that misinformation and digital disinformation posed serious threats to electoral credibility and democratic stability.
He called on citizens to verify information before sharing it, particularly on social media, to prevent the spread of false narratives capable of undermining public confidence in democratic institutions.
“This country belongs to young Nigerians, and they must not relent in working for the Nigeria they desire,” he said.
“Misinformation remains one of the greatest threats to our democracy. Citizens must verify information before acting or sharing, and give our democracy the chance to succeed.”
The 2027 general elections are scheduled to begin with the presidential and National Assembly elections on January 16, 2027, while governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections are slated for February 6, 2027.

items.content:
By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) senatorial candidate for Kwara South in the 2027 general elections, Hon. Saheed Popoola, has pledged to address insecurity, infrastructure deficits, agricultural challenges, youth unemployment and poor healthcare delivery in the district if elected.
Popoola, a former commissioner, two-term member of the Kwara State House of Assembly and former Chairman of Offa Local Government Area, made the pledge on Friday during the News Keg Engagement Series organised by the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) in Ilorin.
He identified security as his top priority, arguing that meaningful development could not take place in an environment where residents lived in fear of attacks.
Expressing concern over increasing cases of kidnapping in Kwara South, Popoola said residents could no longer move freely or access their farmlands without fear of being attacked.
He recalled that communities in the district were relatively safe in the past, but said the current security situation had created anxiety among farmers and other residents.
The PDP candidate pledged to replicate the neighbourhood watch initiative he established during his tenure as local government chairman, which he described as effective in maintaining security.
According to him, the initiative would involve youths, Fulani residents and other community stakeholders, with participants properly equipped and registered with the government.
He added that he would deploy personal resources to support the initiative, arguing that residents understood their communities and terrain better than security personnel deployed from other parts of the country.
Popoola, who said his 27 years of political experience had equipped him with the capacity to address the challenges facing the district, also promised to appoint 83 liaison officers across the wards to improve communication and ensure effective representation.
He described the proposed arrangement as unprecedented in Kwara State, saying it would enable him to respond more effectively to the needs of his constituents.
The former lawmaker explained that his decision to join the PDP was informed by his conviction that the party was more committed to the welfare of ordinary Nigerians.
He pledged to use his position in the Senate to lobby the Federal and State Governments, as well as relevant agencies, to address security and infrastructure challenges in the district.
On infrastructure, Popoola lamented the poor condition of roads linking communities in Kwara South, particularly the Iloffa-Ekiti axis.
He promised to engage relevant federal agencies to facilitate the rehabilitation and construction of major roads, including the Ilorin-Omu-Aran-Egbe and Ajase-Offa routes.
He said lobbying government institutions and agencies to attract development projects was an important responsibility of legislators, adding that senators could facilitate infrastructure development through effective engagement.
On his controversial comments at the palace of the Olofa of Offa, Oba Mufutau Gbadamosi, last weekend, concerning his alleged false claims against former Senate President, Dr Bukola Saraki, during the Offa robbery incident, Popoola said he stood by his remarks and had no apology to offer anyone.
“I have no apology to offer anybody on what I said in Olofa’s palace at the weekend. I stand by all that I was quoted to have said. I owe Dr Bukola Saraki an open apology before I enter my grave, and I thank Almighty Allah that He made it possible for me,” he said.

items.title: US says forces responded to suspected drone activity over base in Britain
items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
US forces responded to possible unauthorized drone activity over a military base in Britain on Friday, a US Air Force spokesperson said, in the latest security incident at a facility hosting American military aircraft.
“No personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected” at the RAF Lakenheath base, the Air Force spokesperson said in a statement.
“We continue to work closely with our host nation counterparts to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, US and host nation civilians, contractors, and all of our families,” the statement added.
Nick Timothy, a local member of parliament, said in a statement on Facebook that he had been in touch with authorities at the base and was “told there is no threat to the public, and the incident is now resolved.”
A post on the official RAF Lakenheath Facebook page earlier this week urged people to report “suspicious activity, including unauthorized drone activity.”
“Our strongest security asset is an observant community,” the post said.
The possible drone incident at Lakenheath came after the US Justice Department announced charges earlier in the week against three men it described as “Iranian operatives” over their role in an alleged terrorist plot at RAF Fairford, another British base.
The three men allegedly helped plan and direct the September incident at the base, which came to light when police were called after a local farmer reported seeing a group of men with several white vans engaged in “suspicious” activity.
– Iran war fallout –
A US charging document stated that a man identified as Mohammad Ali al-Hassani directed unnamed individuals to drive to the base in the vans, some of which contained barrels of fuel, and that he earlier paid the group to buy metallic objects that could be used as shrapnel.
Days later, the United States withdrew all its B-1 bombers from the base.
UK police last month charged two British men with national security offenses related to the RAF Fairford incident.
One was charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service, believed to be in Iran, and another with entering a prohibited place for a purpose “prejudicial” to the UK.
Flight-tracking data showed Tuesday that the US military had removed at least a dozen aircraft from another British airbase, RAF Mildenhall, following what the Wall Street Journal said was a threat from Iran.
The United States has flown military aircraft from bases in Britain as part of the US-Israeli war against Iran sparked earlier this year, which saw Tehran respond by launching missiles and drones at countries across the region, while the militant groups it backs also entered the fray.
In an interview broadcast Wednesday, Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei threatened to strike US bases beyond the Middle East, including in Europe, if they are used for attacks against the Islamic republic.
Iranian officials have previously threatened to expand the geographic scope of the conflict should the US attack again.
In late September, an adviser to Iran’s new supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei publicly mused that the war could “expand even further, reaching the Indian Ocean and perhaps beyond.”

items.content:
The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop for all departing flights after serious communications problems disrupted the country’s air traffic control system.
The FAA cited “extraordinary circumstances” and safety concerns for the decision, preventing aircraft on the ground from taking off across the United States. Planes already airborne were allowed to continue to their destinations and land normally.
International departures were being handled on a case-by-case basis, according to Reuters. The nationwide order followed an earlier halt to air traffic in Chicago linked to communications problems.
Communications Problems Hit US Air Traffic Control
The disruption affected communications involving the 22 regional air traffic control centers responsible for directing aircraft traveling between airports across the country. US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said technicians were investigating the problem.
The incident represents one of the most significant disruptions to US aviation in years. Reuters reported that it was only the second nationwide halt of all departures since the September 11, 2001 attacks, following a system failure that temporarily grounded departures in January 2023.
Aging FAA Infrastructure Under Scrutiny
The outage has again drawn attention to aging US air traffic control infrastructure. Congress approved $12.5 billion for modernization last year, including upgrades to communications systems and the replacement of older infrastructure.
The FAA and White House on Friday also sought an additional $30.1 billion from Congress to address remaining problems with the system, according to Reuters.
Passengers with scheduled flights have been advised to check directly with their airlines for flight-specific delays, cancellations and revised departure times.

items.content:
Portugal midfielder Bernardo Silva said Friday his team could cope with any extra pressure on them following Cristiano Ronaldo’s international retirement, ahead of their first match without the superstar forward.
Jorge Jesus’s side host Denmark in Braga on Saturday in the Nations League, with a tribute planned for their all-time leading goalscorer.
Real Madrid’s Silva, who inherits the captain’s armband from Ronaldo, admitted that the striker had been the main focus for much of the past two decades but backed the team to cope with the pressure in the 41-year-old’s absence.
“Everyone knows the weight Cristiano carries. Most people went to the stadium to see Cristiano, many went just for him, and that’s not going to happen now,” Silva told reporters.
“The national team players are used to the spotlight, the pressure, and the responsibility, as well as being pointed at when things don’t go well — so that’s not an issue.”
Portugal will pay tribute to five-time Ballon d’Or winner Ronaldo before the game against Denmark, with media reporting the squad will walk out wearing number seven jerseys, Ronaldo’s number.
Whether Ronaldo will be present is unknown, after he fell out with veteran coach Jorge Jesus in September.
Last week Ronaldo said he was bringing down the curtain on his storied international career.
Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal in 2003 and went on to play a world record 234 times for his country, scoring 146 goals.
“Nobody can forget Cris’s 23 years in the national team and everything he did,” Jesus told reporters.
“I think (paying tribute) is a brilliant idea to continue to remind us that he is a legend of Portuguese football.”
Portugal have already sealed qualification to the quarter-finals of the Nations League, winning all four matches in Group A4.

items.content:
Former Indian cricketer Sachin Tendulkar has joined the cap table of Hyderabad-based cleantech startup Recykal. The startup did not disclose the size of the investment.
In a statement, Recykal said that Tendulkar infused the capital during the extension of the startup’s recently closed $23 Mn bridge round.
Back in June, the clean tech startup had raised $17.6 Mn in equity funding. The round also comprised an additional secondary component worth $5.4 Mn, which saw participation from existing backers and family offices.
“What drew me to Recykal was seeing how technology was being used to solve an everyday problem. Recykal’s mission to use technology to drive behavioural change across 1 Bn people is what really connected with me, and I hope together we can encourage more people to make responsible choices every day,” said Tendulkar in a statement.
Founded in 2016 by Abhay Deshpande, Abhishek Deshpande, Ekta Narain, Vikram Prabakar and Anirudha Jalan, Recykal operates a B2B marketplace for recyclable materials. It also provides software solutions to help brands track plastic and e-waste recycling to meet compliance mandates.
The startup also recently launched a deposit return system (DRS), a reverse vending machine service for recovering consumer packaging. Under DRS, consumers pay a refundable deposit on containers at purchase and get it back when they return the container to a collection point.
Backed by the likes of Morgan Stanley, 360 ONE, Circulate Capital and the Murugappa Group, the startup has raised more than $60 Mn in funding to date. Recykal claims to operate a network of more than 5,000 waste aggregators and recyclers and claims to cater to 650 enterprise brands, including the likes of Hindustan Unilever, Samsung and BMW.
In June this year, the startup had told Inc42 that it closed FY26 with a gross revenue of ₹1,498 Cr, up 53.2% from ₹978 Cr in the year ago fiscal. However, losses jumped 7% to ₹60 Cr compared to ₹56 Cr in FY25.
Interestingly, Tendulkar’s investment in Recykal comes almost two weeks after he backed gaming startup Metasports Interactive, the company behind mobile cricket strategy game Hitwicket.
Besides, the retired cricket icon has also invested in a range of other startups such as used car marketplace Spinny, listed fintech startup Kissht, and former Swiggy Instamart leader Karthik Gurumurthy’s activewear brand Ten X You.

items.content:
By Favour Ulebor, Abuja
The Federal Government has warned Nigerians, particularly those with pre-existing medical conditions, to exercise caution when travelling through Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, following the deaths of 16 Nigerians in the city this year.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed this in a travel advisory issued on Friday, stating that the deaths recorded by Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa were reportedly linked to health complications associated with the city’s high altitude.
The ministry explained that Addis Ababa is situated approximately 2,355 metres (7,726 feet) above sea level, where lower atmospheric pressure results in reduced oxygen availability.
It noted that the conditions could pose increased health risks to travellers with certain underlying medical conditions, particularly cardiovascular and respiratory ailments.
According to the advisory, although healthy individuals are generally able to adapt to reduced oxygen levels in high-altitude environments, people with certain pre-existing health conditions may experience complications.
The Federal Government therefore advised Nigerians whose medical conditions could be worsened by high altitudes to seek appropriate medical advice before undertaking journeys involving transit through the Ethiopian capital.
It also urged travellers with underlying medical conditions to consult medical professionals and obtain necessary guidance before embarking on their trips.
The ministry, however, clarified that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa.
Rather, it said the notice was aimed at ensuring that medically vulnerable travellers were adequately informed about the possible effects of high altitudes and took necessary precautions.
The advisory stated, “This year, Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa has recorded 16 deaths involving Nigerians transiting through the city, reportedly linked to health complications associated with high altitudes.
“While healthy individuals are generally able to adapt to reduced oxygen levels in high-altitude environments, persons with certain pre-existing medical ailments, particularly cardiovascular and respiratory conditions, may experience increased health risks in such conditions.
“In view of the foregoing, Nigerians with pre-existing health conditions that can be exacerbated by high altitudes are strongly advised to exercise caution when planning journeys that involve transit through Addis Ababa.
“Travellers with underlying medical conditions are also urged to obtain appropriate medical guidance before undertaking such journeys.”
The ministry reiterated that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa but to ensure that those vulnerable to the physiological effects of high altitudes were adequately informed.
It reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to protecting the health, safety and wellbeing of Nigerians travelling abroad, adding that it would continue to provide timely information and guidance to safeguard their welfare.

The family reportedly suspects that complications arising from the untreated gunshot wound may have contributed to his death, although the exact circumstances surrounding his demise remain unclear.
The incident has renewed concerns over the activities of armed kidnappers along the Kaduna-Abuja highway, where travellers and residents of adjoining farming communities continue to face security threats.

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono was suspended for 12 matches by the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee on Friday after his challenge on Jesus de Miguel resulted in the death of the Tenerife striker last week.
Equatorial Guinea international Owono was sent off in the second division clash on November 2 after racing into midfield and colliding with De Miguel while trying to clear an aerial ball.
After the collision De Miguel, 30, was placed in intensive care in hospital and the Spanish forward died on November 3.
“The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee’s report, which states that the player was sent off for ‘violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’,” said the committee in a statement.
“The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge.
“In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances… the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified.”
Spanish police sources last week told AFP an investigation into what happened had been opened under judicial supervision.
Owono said he was enduring the “hardest days of my life” after De Miguel’s death.
“These are the hardest days of my life. I struggle to find the words and it is very difficult for me to process anything that has happened,” said Owono in a statement published by his club Andorra last week.
“I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, of his family, and of all the people who loved him.
“I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are going through. Rest in peace, Jesus.”
FC Andorra coach Carles Manso said Thursday it would be Owono who decides if and when he returns to football after the tragic incident.
On Saturday Tenerife fans and players gathered at the club’s stadium for a memorial and farewell to De Miguel.
His funeral took place last Thursday and around 400 mourners attended, including Spain coach Luis de la Fuente and Real Madrid president Florentino Perez.

By Dapo Akinrefon
The governorship candidate of the Action Peoples Movement (APM) in Lagos State, Prince Laja Adeoye, has condemned the attack on supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during their town hall meeting in Lagos, describing the incident as shameful and a threat to democracy.
Adeoye said the disruption of the meeting at Classique Event Centre, Oregun, Ikeja, on Thursday, amounted to an infringement on the constitutional rights of citizens to assemble and freely express their political views.
He warned that the use of thugs to disrupt opposition gatherings could heighten political tension ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Adeoye said, “Nobody should be attacked for supporting a candidate of his or her choice. What happened in Lagos on Thursday was shameful and unacceptable in a democracy.”
He described the incident as particularly disturbing, noting that Lagos had traditionally been regarded as a centre of political activities where parties and candidates could canvass for support.
According to him, the attack was not merely against the NDC but also against the democratic process and Nigerians who believe in free and fair elections.
The APM candidate urged the Lagos State Police Command to identify, arrest and prosecute those responsible for the incident, irrespective of their political affiliation or status.
He warned that failure to bring the perpetrators to justice could encourage similar attacks in other parts of the country as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 elections.
Adeoye also expressed concern over the safety of voters, candidates and journalists during the campaign period, recalling reports that a journalist covering the meeting was attacked and dispossessed of his working equipment.
He called on political leaders to rise above partisan interests and condemn violence, stressing that democracy could not thrive in an atmosphere of fear and intimidation.
The APM candidate commended the NDC supporters for maintaining their composure despite the alleged provocation, saying their conduct demonstrated commitment to democratic values.
“The supporters did not retaliate. They conducted themselves in a peaceful manner. That is the spirit we need to sustain our democracy,” he said.
He urged political parties to caution their supporters against violence and embrace issue-based campaigns rather than intimidation and thuggery.
Adeoye also called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), security agencies and other political stakeholders to work together to guarantee a level playing field for all parties ahead of the 2027 elections.
He said Lagos, as the country’s commercial nerve centre, should demonstrate that elections could be contested and won without violence.
He further urged the National Peace Committee and civil society organisations to intervene by encouraging political actors to embrace peaceful political engagement.
According to him, Nigerians were more concerned about finding solutions to insecurity, unemployment, rising cost of living and poor infrastructure than political violence.
Adeoye sympathised with those reportedly injured during the attack and wished them a speedy recovery, while urging the NDC to remain focused on its campaign.
“We must not allow a few disgruntled elements to derail our democracy. The 2027 election must be about ideas, not violence,” he said.
He reaffirmed the APM’s commitment to peaceful, credible and transparent elections, as well as respect for the rule of law and democratic values.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Edwin Philip, Lafia
A group of 601 retired civil servants in Nasarawa State has commenced enforcement of a court order directing the recovery of over ₦4 billion in outstanding gratuities and other entitlements owed them by the state government.
The pensioners, under the aegis of the Concerned Group of Nasarawa State Pensioners, secured a consent judgment against the state government in 2020 over the alleged non-payment of their retirement benefits.
Their spokespersons, Mr Simon Auna and Mallam Usman Adamu, disclosed the development while speaking with journalists in Lafia on Friday.
The group said it subsequently obtained an order from the National Industrial Court, Makurdi, awarding 25 per cent post-judgment interest on the judgment sum, bringing the total amount being sought to over ₦4 billion.
According to the pensioners, following the alleged failure of the state government to comply with the judgment, their lawyers approached the Senior District Court in Makurdi, presided over by Justice Ada Jack.
The court subsequently directed six commercial banks to release funds belonging to the Nasarawa State Government, amounting to over ₦4 billion, for payment to the affected retirees.
In a move to enforce the order, the pensioners’ legal team, accompanied by court bailiffs, visited some branches of one of the commercial banks in Makurdi, Benue State, where they removed some movable properties.
Speaking on the development, counsel to the pensioners, Mrs Doofan Sefa-Aii, said the legal team would continue to operate within the law to ensure full recovery of the funds owed the retirees.
Another counsel, Mr Awo Matthew, appealed to the Nasarawa State Government and the banks involved to allow the legal process to take its course, considering the hardship the pensioners had endured while pursuing payment of their entitlements.
However, the Director of Corporate Services and Arbitration at the Nasarawa State Ministry of Justice, Mr Usman Aliyu, said the state government had taken all necessary legal steps, including filing a motion for a stay of execution of the court order.
Meanwhile, Adamu, who is the group’s Lafia Local Government Chairman, and Auna, its Legal Adviser, described the court order as a significant breakthrough after years of seeking payment of their entitlements.
They said the development had renewed their hope of recovering the outstanding benefits.
The pensioners reaffirmed their determination to pursue their entitlements through lawful means until the matter was resolved.

“My visit is primarily aimed at exploring measures to strengthen security along the strategic economic corridor, which connects Maiduguri to several communities in eastern Borno and serves as a vital route for trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities,” Zulum said.

He also announced a payment of ₦50,000 to each soldier preparing for the deployment to the two communities.
Koshebe has previously suffered deadly attacks by suspected Boko Haram insurgents.
On November 28, 2020, insurgents attacked rice farmers working in fields around the community, killing more than 100 people, many of whom were seasonal farm labourers from Sokoto State.
Similarly, in November 2023, suspected insurgents attacked farmers harvesting rice in the Karkut and Koshebe areas of Mafa Local Government Area, killing at least 13 people, while others were reported missing.
Zulum’s administration has continued to provide logistics and welfare assistance to security agencies as part of efforts to support military operations, improve security and facilitate the return of displaced residents to their communities.

By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief
NIRSAL Microfinance Bank (NMFB) has clarified that the COVID-19 Targeted Credit Facility (TCF) was an intervention loan, not a grant, stressing that beneficiaries are obligated to repay the funds.
The bank said deductions from the accounts of beneficiaries who accessed the facility would continue until their outstanding loans were fully liquidated, in line with the Global Standing Instruction (GSI) mechanism.
In a statement issued in Abuja at the weekend, the bank explained that the GSI framework allows financial institutions to recover outstanding loan obligations from eligible accounts linked to borrowers’ Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs), subject to applicable regulatory guidelines.
The bank said the clarification became necessary to address concerns surrounding loan recoveries and reassure customers and members of the public of its commitment to transparency, accountability and responsible banking practices.
It explained that the COVID-19 Targeted Credit Facility was introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to support households and businesses affected by the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic.
According to the bank, all beneficiaries were required to accept electronic offer letters before disbursement, with the documents clearly outlining the terms and conditions of the facility, including repayment obligations and recovery mechanisms in cases of default.
“Regarding the recovery process, the Bank operates within the applicable regulatory framework, including the Global Standing Instruction (GSI) mechanism approved by the Central Bank of Nigeria,” it stated.
NIRSAL MFB, however, acknowledged concerns raised by some beneficiaries over the timing and amounts of deductions, outstanding loan balances and access to repayment information.
The bank said it took the complaints seriously, noting that customers must have access to accurate information about their loan accounts.
It stressed that the deductions were intended to settle outstanding contractual obligations, adding that beneficiaries who disputed deductions or identified discrepancies in their repayment records should contact the bank for individual account reconciliation.
“Where any beneficiary has concerns about deductions made, discrepancies in repayment records or the status of an outstanding balance, such cases should be brought to the bank’s attention for individual account reconciliation and appropriate resolution,” it said.
The bank assured that legitimate complaints would be investigated and that any discrepancies established during the reconciliation process would receive the necessary attention.
It urged beneficiaries seeking clarification on their loan status, repayment history or outstanding obligations to contact the bank through its officially designated customer service channels.

By Efe Onodjae
The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Seme Area Command, has intercepted a live endangered sea turtle allegedly being smuggled through a footpath linking Nigeria and the Republic of Benin.
The Olive Ridley Sea Turtle, scientifically known as Lepidochelys olivacea, was intercepted during a routine patrol by Customs officers at about 10.30pm on Thursday, November 12, 2026.
The command said the officers sighted a suspicious individual carrying a sack along the border route, but the suspect abandoned the bag and fled into a nearby bush upon noticing the patrol team.
According to a statement by the command’s Public Relations Officer, Superintendent of Customs, John Tunde Ayagbalo, examination of the abandoned sack revealed the live sea turtle concealed inside.
He said the animal was immediately secured and kept in safe custody before being handed over to relevant wildlife authorities for proper care, rehabilitation and eventual release into its natural habitat.
The Acting Customs Area Controller, Seme Area Command, Deputy Comptroller Norman Olisah Alumanah, described the interception as a demonstration of the vigilance and professionalism of officers in tackling wildlife trafficking.
Alumanah warned smugglers, poachers and their collaborators against using the nation’s borders as corridors for illegal wildlife trade, adding that the command had intensified patrols, surveillance and intelligence gathering across its area of responsibility.
He also called on residents of border communities to provide credible intelligence to support the fight against wildlife trafficking.
The Customs boss said the command would complement enforcement operations with stakeholder education and sensitisation on endangered species, their ecological importance and the legal implications of their unauthorised trade.
Wildlife trafficking remains a major environmental crime, threatening biodiversity and the survival of endangered species through illegal exploitation for meat, eggs, shells, traditional medicine and the exotic pet trade.
Nigeria is a signatory to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), which regulates international trade in endangered wildlife and plant species.
The convention is domesticated in Nigeria through the Endangered Species (Control of International Trade and Traffic) Act, Cap E9, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Chidinma Chukwu
ABUJA — The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has completed the 21-day monitoring of all 62 contacts linked to the imported case of Bundibugyo Virus Disease (BVD), a form of Ebola disease, confirmed in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20, 2026, with no secondary infections recorded.
The Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, disclosed this on Friday during a media briefing in Abuja, saying the last contact had been discharged from monitoring after testing negative for the virus.
Idris said 13 of the 62 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms during the monitoring period, but laboratory tests confirmed that none had contracted the disease.
“The 21-day monitoring period for contacts linked to the index case has been completed, with the last contact discharged today. We are glad to announce that none of the contacts became ill with the disease, meaning no transmission from the index case.
“A total of 62 contacts were identified, placed in quarantine and followed up by our public health teams. During the monitoring period, 13 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms. All 13 were tested for Bundibugyo Virus Disease, and all tested negative,” he said.
The index case was a 42-year-old Ugandan-born woman, who tested positive for the virus in Abuja on October 20. She was subsequently medically evacuated to Switzerland on October 26.
Providing an update on her condition, Idris said the woman had recovered and been discharged from a hospital in Geneva.
He also disclosed that seven additional suspected cases were reported and investigated in Adamawa, Rivers, Borno, Lagos and Ekiti states within the past three weeks. All seven cases tested negative for the virus.
However, the NCDC chief cautioned against interpreting the completion of contact monitoring as a formal declaration that the outbreak was over.
He explained that such a declaration would depend on established public health criteria and findings from continued surveillance.
“It is important to note that the completion of contact monitoring does not, by itself, constitute a formal declaration that an outbreak is over. Such a determination must be based on the applicable public health criteria and the findings of ongoing surveillance.
“Nigeria therefore remains vigilant, particularly given the continued occurrence of Ebola virus disease in the DRC,” he said.
Idris assured Nigerians that disease surveillance and preparedness activities would continue, stressing that the agency remained committed to protecting residents and visitors.
Looking ahead to the December festive season, he warned that increased travel, social interactions and large public gatherings could heighten the risk of disease transmission.
He identified family celebrations, religious activities, political campaigns, concerts, festivals and sporting events as occasions likely to increase human movement and interaction.
He urged anyone who develops symptoms to seek medical attention promptly, warning against automatically assuming that every fever is malaria, particularly among people with recent travel history or possible exposure to infectious diseases.
The NCDC boss also advised the public to avoid unprotected contact with the blood and other body fluids of anyone suspected of having Ebola or another infectious disease.
He urged individuals identified as contacts to cooperate with public health authorities and comply with monitoring instructions.
Idris further called on organisers of mass gatherings, including religious activities, political rallies, concerts, festivals and sporting events, to provide adequate sanitation, safe drinking water, medical assistance and mechanisms for promptly reporting suspected illnesses.
Healthcare workers in public and private facilities were also urged to maintain a high index of suspicion, strictly observe infection prevention and control measures, and report suspected cases without delay.
On international travel, Idris reminded inbound travellers of the requirement to complete the Nigeria Health Declaration Form before arrival.
He encouraged travellers to consult the NCDC website for relevant information, provide accurate details of their health and travel history, and promptly report any symptoms or possible exposure to Port Health authorities.
While assuring the public that there was no reason to panic, he said continued vigilance, early reporting and cooperation with health authorities remained essential to preventing the spread of infectious diseases.
The post Ebola: All 62 contacts test negative after monitoring – NCDC appeared first on Vanguard News.

This comes a couple of weeks after Inc42 reported that SEBI had given its go-ahead to the fintech giant to list on the bourses. At the time, sources had said that the ₹5,000 Cr to ₹6,000 Cr ($530 Mn to $630 Mn) IPO would value the company at around $5 Bn (₹47,000 Cr), with a listing likely between January and March 2027.
Original | November 4, 2026; 11:08 AM IST
Fintech major Razorpay has received SEBI’s approval for its proposed ₹5,000-6,000 Cr IPO, sources told Inc42.
The offering is expected to value the company at around $5 Bn, with a listing likely between January and March 2027, the sources added.
The IPO is expected to comprise a fresh issue and an offer-for-sale (OFS). However, the proposed split could not be ascertained.
The Economic Times first reported the development.
Founded in 2014 by Shashank Kumar and Harshil Mathur, Razorpay offers payment processing, business banking, payroll, and lending solutions. It filed its IPO papers through the confidential route in June, targeting a valuation of $5 Bn to $6 Bn, below the $7.5 Bn valuation it commanded in its last funding round in 2021.
Ahead of the listing, Razorpay shifted its domicile from the US to India. The company slipped into the red in FY25, weighed down by ₹1,209 Cr in ESOP expenses and one-time restructuring and tax costs linked to the move. Operating revenue rose 65% to ₹3,783 Cr during the year.
Razorpay’s Growing AI Offerings
Alongside its IPO preparations, Razorpay has been expanding its AI offerings across payments, marketing, and business operations.
Last month, it announced an expanded partnership with OpenAI to help Indian brands advertise on ChatGPT. Under the partnership, its growth marketing platform, Razorpay Engage, will enable brands to prepare product catalogues and launch and manage campaigns on ChatGPT Ads.
Razorpay has also launched Vulcan, a transformer-based AI foundation model for digital payments. The company claims the model can improve payment reliability and safety by scoring payment routes in real time and identifying fraud patterns across multiple merchants once deployed.
Built using NVIDIA and AWS technology, Vulcan combines Razorpay’s payments data with NVIDIA’s accelerated computing and AWS’ cloud infrastructure.
The fintech major has also been developing Agent Studio, a platform for deploying task-specific AI agents for businesses. Around 200 businesses were using the platform in beta as of August, with use cases spanning reconciliation, abandoned-cart recovery, subscription recovery, and finance operations.
Razorpay has raised over $800 Mn to date from investors including Y Combinator, Tiger Global Management, Ribbit Capital, and Lightspeed.

items.author: Shahzad Paracha
items.content:
The Federal Board of Revenue’s (FBR) surprise competency tests for officers have sparked serious questions over their legality, transparency and credibility. The FBR is scheduled to conduct assessments of Inland Revenue officers in Lahore next Tuesday (November 17), following the completion of assessments in Islamabad and Karachi. The tests assess the sales tax and income tax capabilities of Inland Revenue officials in Grade 17 and above.
According to a report circulated on social media, only 15 out of 150 officers assessed in Sales Tax and 14 out of 143 officers assessed in Income Tax were considered capable of independently adjudicating cases.
Meanwhile, the recently circulated Karachi Inland Revenue Officers’ Capability Assessment Report has triggered serious concerns regarding the legality, transparency, methodology and underlying objectives of surprise competency examinations conducted among serving officers of the FBR.
A critical examination of the report has raised questions about whether a single assessment based on artificially prepared case studies can legitimately determine the professional competence of officers recruited through the competitive Central Superior Services (CSS) examination and entrusted with statutory responsibilities.
Questions have also been raised regarding the legal authority under the Civil Servants Act, 1973, and relevant service rules for conducting such examinations and subsequently recommending restrictions on officers’ statutory functions, postings and professional responsibilities.
While identifying training needs is a legitimate administrative objective, using an inadequately validated examination to impose adverse service consequences raises concerns about procedural fairness and established service protections.
The reported involvement of artificial intelligence, particularly Claude AI, in preparing examination case studies and evaluating answer scripts has also come under scrutiny.
Questions have been raised about the qualifications of examiners, independent human verification, transparency of marking criteria and the absence of an effective mechanism for challenging disputed results. However, the extent of AI involvement remains unverified and requires official clarification.
Concerns have further emerged that such assessments may be used to build a narrative of institutional incompetence to justify sweeping structural reforms within the FBR, potentially benefiting external consulting firms and technology providers.
Significantly, the assessment itself acknowledges that its findings are based on a single test involving three cases in each tax category and should be treated as indicative. Critics argue that such limited findings cannot reasonably justify publicly categorising experienced officers as professionally incapable or unfit for statutory assignments.
The public circulation of individual officers’ names, scores and professional classifications has also raised concerns about confidentiality, institutional morale and reputational damage.
Questions have additionally been raised regarding repeated transfers, administrative pressures and whether responsibility for shortcomings in revenue administration is being disproportionately shifted onto field officers rather than examining the effectiveness of senior management, technological reforms and institutional policies.
There are growing calls for an independent review of the examination framework, disclosure of its legal authorisation, AI usage and marking methodology, and the provision of a fair review mechanism for affected officers.

items.author: Shahzad Paracha
items.content:
The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has separated the administration of sales tax and Federal Excise Duty (FED) from income tax, posting 54 Inland Revenue officers to a newly created wing as part of its proposed restructuring.
The FBR has created the post of Member, Sales Tax & FED (Technical) at its headquarters in Islamabad and, on Friday, transferred and posted 54 officers from BS-17 to BS-21 to the new setup.
According to an official notification, Dr. Muhammad Sarmad Qureshi, a Grade-21 officer of the Inland Revenue Service (IRS), has been appointed Member Sales Tax and FED.
Phased Rollout Till March 2027
Sources said the FBR has prepared a phased plan for the separation:
December 1, 2026: Separate sales tax units will start working in Large Taxpayer Units (LTUs) and Corporate Tax Offices (CTOs), initially under the supervision of the commissioners concerned.
January 1, 2027: Separate sales tax units will become operational in Regional Tax Offices (RTOs).
March 1, 2027: Separate Chief Commissioners for Sales Tax will be appointed.
The restructuring aims to give sales tax and FED their own administrative structure, with dedicated officers and field formations.
What It Means for Taxpayers
FBR’s Board-in-Council has approved the new Member post, and the board’s organizational structure has been revised under its new reporting system. However, FBR has not yet notified a post of Member, Income Tax (Technical).
This means income tax matters of taxpayers will continue to be handled by the Member Inland Revenue (Operations) and the existing income tax setup, while separate sales tax zones will be created in field formations.

items.author: Press Release
items.content:
CodeNinja, an artificial intelligence lab focused on building self-improving systems, and Paranine, an AI infrastructure company serving open-weight models on hardware inside Pakistan, today announced a technology integration and commercial partnership at CodeNinja’s Lahore office.
The partnership brings together CodeNinja’s AI applications, organizational ontology and agentic systems with Paranine’s in-country inference infrastructure to deliver Sovereign AI Operating Systems for organizations in Pakistan. The combined offering is designed to give institutions greater control over where their AI workloads run, how organizational knowledge is used and retained, and how the systems making decisions on their behalf are governed.
Controlling Where the Intelligence Runs
For organizations operating in government, banking, healthcare and other regulated sectors, deploying AI involves more than selecting a capable model. It requires control over the infrastructure running that model, the data informing its outputs and the systems through which its intelligence is applied.
Many organizations still access AI through services hosted outside their national boundaries. This can introduce challenges around data residency, regulatory oversight, infrastructure dependency and long-term control over critical systems.
Sovereign AI requires two complementary capabilities. The infrastructure running the models must operate within the country’s jurisdiction, while the applications and intelligence built around those models must remain under the organization’s governance and control.
The CodeNinja and Paranine partnership brings these capabilities together, combining in-country inference with an organization-owned AI operating layer.
Built on Sovereign Local Infrastructure
The Sovereign AI Operating System is built on Hyper Anthologies, CodeNinja’s ecosystem for engineering self-improving systems, and runs on Paranine’s inference infrastructure in Pakistan. CodeNinja already operates frontier open-weight models on its own Paranine instance, providing an existing foundation for the integration.
The architecture brings together four complementary capabilities:
Hyper Ontology: Establishes a governed model of the organization, connecting its existing systems, knowledge and relationships so applications and agents can work from a shared source of organizational context.
Hyper Pragma: Provides the agentic execution layer, enabling AI agents to operate within the organization’s deployment environment and use models that can be changed as requirements evolve.
Hyper Engram: Provides persistent decision memory, allowing systems to retain relevant context from previous interactions and use it to improve subsequent execution.
Hyper Noesis: Applies interpretability to the open-weight models the organization owns, so teams can inspect the concepts those models rely on and detect when their judgment begins to drift.
Open-weight models can be selected according to the requirements of each deployment and replaced as stronger alternatives become available, without requiring the organization to rebuild the surrounding system. Deployments can run on dedicated in-country infrastructure, within customer environments or in air-gapped configurations where required.
The architecture is designed to ensure that the systems, integrations and organizational intelligence developed for each deployment can be transferred to the customer, supporting long-term operational ownership without dependence on a single model provider.
“Sovereignty is determined not only by where intelligence runs, but by who controls the systems, knowledge and decisions built around it. Our partnership with Paranine gives institutions in Pakistan the ability to deploy AI on infrastructure within the country while building intelligence that remains under their own control.” – Mukhtar Ahmad, CEO and Co-founder, CodeNinja
Built for Institutions That Need Control
The partnership will initially focus on government, banking and financial services, healthcare and other sectors where data governance, regulatory requirements and operational continuity are critical.
The companies will take the combined offering to market together, working with institutions whose deployments require both an enterprise AI operating layer and sovereign inference infrastructure. CodeNinja’s Forward Deployed Engineers will work within customer environments to engineer and integrate the applications, agents and organizational systems, while Paranine will provide and support the underlying inference capacity.
This division of capabilities allows institutions to move beyond isolated AI deployments toward integrated systems that can operate within their existing environments and evolve alongside their requirements.
Bridging Sovereign Infrastructure and Enterprise AI
Paranine is Pakistan’s first sovereign AI Inference Cloud, enabling organizations to deploy and consume AI models on locally hosted infrastructure. Its chip-agnostic platform supports open-weight models across Huawei Ascend NPUs and NVIDIA GPUs, offering an OpenAI-compatible gateway, dedicated inference endpoints, model serving and optimization, and billing in Pakistani rupees.
The partnership with CodeNinja connects Paranine’s inference infrastructure with enterprise AI operating systems, enabling institutions to deploy production-ready applications on sovereign infrastructure. Together, the companies aim to address growing demand for enterprise AI solutions that combine infrastructure, applications and organizational control. By combining their engineering capabilities, both companies intend to expand their reach across regulated industries and accelerate enterprise AI adoption in Pakistan.
“AI adoption in Pakistan will be driven by organizations moving beyond experimentation to real-world deployment. This requires both reliable, sovereign AI infrastructure and applications that address practical business needs. By combining Paranine’s inference capabilities with CodeNinja’s enterprise AI systems, we aim to make that transition easier, more accessible and scalable for organizations across the country.” – Ahad Khurshid, Founder and Chief Executive Officer, Paranine.

items.content:
Islamabad International Airport is expected to become easier to access through the Margalla Avenue Extension project, which has achieved 36 percent overall progress, while the Capital Development Authority (CDA) has completed the structural work of the Sangjani Interchange underpass.
The project involves extending Margalla Avenue from N-5 to M-1 and developing the Sangjani Interchange to improve road connectivity to Islamabad and the airport.
CDA Chairman and Islamabad Chief Commissioner Sohail Ashraf visited the construction site and reviewed the progress. Officials briefed him that construction activities were continuing 24 hours a day to ensure timely completion.
The 2.7-kilometre extension of Margalla Avenue and its connecting service road are under construction. The underpass structure at Sangjani Interchange, including its concrete walls and foundation slabs, has been completed. Earthwork, filling, and other remaining activities are ongoing.
Meanwhile, piling work for the abutments on both sides of the N-5 Interchange Bridge has been completed, while steel fixing and framework activities are underway.
Officials said construction of four culverts had also been completed, while work on the fifth was continuing. Development of all project loops and ramps is also progressing.
During the visit, the CDA chairman directed relevant departments to remove construction obstacles and maintain work quality, speed, and transparency.
Once completed, the Margalla Avenue Extension and Sangjani Interchange project will improve access to Islamabad for commuters travelling from different parts of the country, particularly Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
It is also expected to improve connectivity to Islamabad International Airport.

“Mr President said I should tell you that he will continue to work for you and reforms are over. It’s now prosperity. For the second time, you will feel it,” she said.
The First Lady also expressed excitement over her visit to Zamfara, describing it as one of the happiest moments of her life, particularly because the construction of an airport in the state had made travelling there easier.
She said she had visited all 36 states of the federation but had long wanted to visit Zamfara, adding that the new airport had made the journey more convenient.
“This is just the beginning. I’m coming back. I’m coming back again. I will be coming back with the PCC,” she said.
Mrs Tinubu, who was conferred with the traditional title of Jagaban Marafa Zamfara during the visit, thanked the traditional rulers for the honour and described her reception in the state as overwhelming.
She also commiserated with the people of Zamfara over the persistent insecurity in the state, expressing sympathy for families who had lost loved ones to attacks.
She prayed for the repose of the souls of the victims and asked God to grant their families the strength to bear the losses.
On women empowerment, the First Lady said the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) had continued to support women beyond electioneering periods, stressing that the party’s empowerment programmes were not introduced merely to secure political support.
She disclosed that another round of empowerment for women was scheduled to take place during the rally, noting that activities had started the previous day.
According to her, the administration had also made provisions to support children returning to school and provide funding for agriculture as part of efforts to improve the economy.
She expressed optimism that the ongoing policies and programmes of the Federal Government would translate into better living conditions for Nigerians.
The rally brought together political leaders and supporters from the seven North-West states as part of the APC’s political mobilisation activities.

items.author: ZAFAR BHUTTA
items.content:
The government has decided to impose an Automotive Development Levy (ADL) of 2% to 10% on imported and locally manufactured internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles to speed up electric vehicle adoption, with a clear vehicle classification and the minimum levy on public service vehicles and vehicles up to 2000cc. ICE refers to conventional petrol- or diesel-powered vehicles that use an engine to burn fuel and generate power. The levy will not apply to imported and locally manufactured 2/3-wheelers, tractors and vehicles with engine capacity up to 1000cc, and it will carry a sunset clause while remaining enforced during the policy period.
Production of electric bikes and rickshaws rose from 21,656 units in FY24 to 226,106 units in FY26, while production of NEV cars and SUVs rose from 42 units to 16,126 units. NEV prices remained affordable mainly because of the lower 1% sales tax under the last automobile policy. Therefore, 1% sales tax on BEVs will continue, while REEVs and PHEVs will attract 6% and 9% respectively. To qualify, an NEV must have an external source of charging and a minimum range of 50km under normal conditions on a single battery charge.
The policy proposes a smooth transition from PHEVs to BEVs, with different rates based on hydrocarbon fuel use and pure battery range. PHEVs with a minimum battery range of 50km in a single charge, as per NEV Policy 2025-30, will attract 9% sales tax; REEVs using a generator to charge batteries and having an external source of charging will attract 6%; and pure BEVs will attract 1%. However, this concession will not apply to an imported or locally manufactured NEV (car, SUV, double cabin, 2/3-wheeler) valued above $50,000, for which standard sales tax will apply; the value for imported NEV CBU will be CIF value inclusive of customs duty, while locally assembled or manufactured NEV value will be factory gate value.
A major impediment to quick NEV adoption is higher upfront cost vis-à-vis a comparable ICE vehicle. Federal Excise Duty (FED) and Special Excise Duty (SED) on automobiles shall be levied to eliminate the price disparity between ICE and NEV and to make cars or SUVs above 2000cc expensive. Any change in FED or SED shall be initiated by the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) after consultation with the Ministry of Industries & Production. It is proposed to eliminate FED on small ICE motor vehicles having engine capacity of 1000cc or less, falling under PCT 8703. Further, no FED, SED, Capital Value Tax (CVT) or Withholding Tax (WHT) will be levied on NEVs except those valued above $50,000.
Lowering sales tax and other taxes alone will not sufficiently reduce NEV prices, so ADL will be imposed on ICE vehicles only. The proposed sales tax rate will be the same on imported and locally manufactured motor vehicles, and the ADL rate on imported and locally manufactured ICE vehicles will also be the same. The levy will fund DLTL reimbursement, R&D support, vendor development, third-party audit and the Pakistan Automotive Testing Institute.
To foster quick adoption of BEVs, especially smaller cars, BEVs in CBU condition valued up to $15,000 will be charged a customs duty (CD) of 5% in FY27 and FY28, rising to 20% in FY29 and becoming 15% in the last year of the policy. The concessional 5% CD will only be available on execution of a surety bond and provision of an irrevocable and unconditional bank guarantee of a scheduled bank for the 20% CD differential for FY27 and 17% differential for FY28, with commitment to install an assembly or manufacturing plant for the imported BEV variant and start commercial production on or before September 30, 2028. BEVs valued $15,000 and above in CBU condition will be charged a CD of 25%, which will become 15% in the last year of the policy, 2030-31.
Under State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) regulations, the maximum automobile credit limit is restricted to Rs3 million and tenor to three years; the SBP will favourably consider enhancing NEV credit limits to Rs10 million and tenor to five years to address higher upfront cost. The existing 0% customs duty on import of charging stations in CBU condition will continue, though the arrangement will be reviewed in the second year of the policy. The Ministry of Industries & Production, EDB and NEECA will work jointly with charging service providers and manufacturers to introduce battery swapping and rental regimes, as a good battery could constitute around 40% of the total price; battery swapping will be incentivised under the New Energy Vehicles Policy 2025-30.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Global shipping giant Mediterranean Shipping Company (MSC) has expressed interest in exploring investment opportunities in Pakistan following a high-level meeting in Geneva.
Federal Minister for Board of Investment Qaiser Ahmed Sheikh met with MSC Chief Executive Officer Soren Toft at the company's headquarters to discuss potential investment opportunities and avenues for expanding MSC's engagement with Pakistan, a statement said on Friday.
Sheikh highlighted Pakistan's strategic geographical location, access to major regional markets and the potential of its seaports, including Karachi Port, Port Qasim and Gwadar, as gateways for international trade and maritime connectivity.
The minister invited an MSC delegation to visit Pakistan to explore cooperation. MSC welcomed the invitation and agreed to arrange a delegation visit to advance discussions on potential investment projects.
Headquartered in Geneva, MSC operates a network of approximately 1,000 vessels, serving over 520 ports across more than 155 countries and accounting for around 21–22% of global container shipping capacity.
Potential areas of cooperation include port-related infrastructure, container handling, shipping and logistics services, warehousing, transshipment and integrated supply-chain solutions.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Chinese conglomerate Transsion Holdings has outlined plans to expand its investment in Pakistan and move beyond assembly into component manufacturing, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb was told during a meeting with its Founder and Chairman George Zhu on Friday.
Transsion, operating in Pakistan's smartphone, electric bike and energy storage segments, shared an overview of operations and future investment plans, as discussions focused on strengthening manufacturing and building an industrial ecosystem through supporting industries and supply chains. It highlighted potential to expand towards value addition and component manufacturing.
Aurangzeb said macroeconomic stability provided a foundation for investor confidence and business planning, reaffirming the government's commitment to reforms and export-oriented growth. Pakistan was described as a strategic market, citing consumer base, location and business environment, and discussed using local manufacturing capacity to serve international markets.
Separately, Advisor to the Prime Minister for Industries and Production Haroon Akhtar Khan met a Shenzhen Transsion delegation to discuss investment and export promotion in electronics. Khan said the government was working on a Mobile and Electronics Device Manufacturing Policy (2026-33) to promote domestic manufacturing, attract investment and strengthen the industry, prioritising a move beyond assembly towards comprehensive manufacturing of mobile phones and devices.
The Engineering Development Board was directed to consult stakeholders. Khan invited Chinese firms to invest, saying "Now is the right time to invest in Pakistan," while Transsion representatives expressed interest in expanding their local manufacturing footprint and pursuing deeper localisation. Secretary for Industries and Production Ahsan Ali Mangi and Joint Secretary Freedoon Akram Sheikh attended.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) staged an intraday recovery on Friday, with the benchmark KSE-100 index gaining 500 points to close 0.28% higher at 177,873.88, as buying in oil and gas stocks, led by Mari Petroleum following its copper-gold discovery in Balochistan, helped offset early losses amid concerns over rising international oil prices.
At the close of trading, the benchmark KSE-100 index posted a gain of 500.11 points, or 0.28%, and settled at 177,873.88.
A Topline market review highlighted that the KSE-100 index staged a notable intraday recovery, closing at 177,873, up 500 points (+0.28%). The benchmark remained volatile throughout the session, swinging between an intraday high of 1,910 points and a low of 508 points, reflecting mixed investor sentiment.
Market sentiment received a significant boost towards the latter half of the session following material news from Mari Petroleum (MARI). Through its wholly owned subsidiary, Mari Minerals, the company announced a new porphyry copper-gold discovery at the East Siah Diq (ESD-1) target in Chagai, Balochistan. The development sparked renewed investor interest and helped turn sentiment positive, providing fresh impetus to the market's recovery.
The discovery underscores the potential of Pakistan's mineral resources and adds to the growing optimism surrounding the country's mining and exploration sector.
On the contribution front, MARI, LUCK, PPL, PSEL and FATIMA emerged as the leading positive contributors, collectively adding approximately 722 points to the benchmark index and providing substantial support to the market's overall performance.
Meanwhile, market participation remained robust, with total traded volume reaching approximately 1,042 million shares, while traded value stood at around Rs31 billion.
KTrade stated that the KSE-100 index closed at 177,873 points, gaining 500 points (+0.28% DoD), while total traded volume stood at 195 million shares. The market remained mixed early in the first session amid renewed concerns over rising oil prices. Brent crude surged to around $96/bbl following US President Donald Trump's remarks that the US does not need a deal with Iran and that JD Vance should focus on domestic matters.
However, the market gradually recovered as the oil and gas sector drove the positive momentum. The rally was largely concentrated in a handful of stocks, particularly MARI, LUCK and PPL. MARI emerged as the standout performer, trading close to its upper circuit during the session, while these stocks provided the major support to the benchmark.
Going forward, market direction will largely depend on developments over the weekend, particularly on the geopolitical front and any potential progress in US-Iran negotiations.
Overall trading volume was recorded at 1.04 billion shares compared with the previous session's tally of 1.07 billion. The value of shares traded during the day was Rs31.0 billion. Shares of 497 companies were traded. Of these, 284 stocks closed higher, 184 fell and 29 remained unchanged.
WorldCall Telecom was the volume leader with trading in 303 million shares, gaining Rs0.13 to close at Rs1.38. It was followed by Kohinoor Spinning with 59.5 million shares, gaining Rs0.34 to close at Rs5.90, and LSE Fin. Services with 46.8 million shares, gaining Rs0.28 to close at Rs2.64.
Foreign investors bought shares worth Rs179 million, the National Clearing Company reported.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Pakistan has met three major fiscal conditions of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for the first quarter of this fiscal year by keeping budget consolidation on track, but the Centre received only Rs57.5 billion, or 6% of the annual provincial grant, for national economic initiatives.
Although three of the four July-September targets were met, the combined fiscal operations summary showed that the pace of consolidation had slowed, with an uptick in expenditure at the start of the third year of the governments at the Centre and in the provinces.
According to the finance ministry, it received Rs57.5 billion in cash grants from all four provinces, including Rs12.7 billion from Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), which had publicly linked the grants to a meeting with the imprisoned Leader of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, Imran Khan.
According to an understanding reached between the federal and the four provincial governments in June this year, the four provinces would give Rs1.035 trillion in cash grants to meet expenditures on security and nationally important projects. The federal government has already approved allocations of Rs275 billion for six priority water sector projects this month.
The details, however, showed that only Rs57.5 billion was received from the four provinces for the July-September period, hardly 6% of the annual committed amount. Punjab gave the most, Rs32.5 billion, while Sindh gave Rs8.5 billion.
The second-highest amount, Rs12.7 billion, came from the K-P government, the province where the federal government imposed governor's rule last month. Balochistan gave Rs3.7 billion in cash grant, according to the finance ministry.
The details showed that the four provinces missed the IMF condition on tax collection but met the cash-surplus target. The country met the primary budget surplus condition, while the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) also met its IMF target for the first quarter this time.
The IMF has set multiple fiscal conditions, and their successful completion has so far helped ensure the programme's smooth continuation despite initial setbacks. The IMF board is tentatively scheduled to meet next month to approve loan tranches worth $1.2 billion, according to Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb.
Against a quarterly primary surplus target of Rs1.95 trillion, the federal government reported a surplus of Rs2.97 trillion, or 2.1% of gross domestic product (GDP). This higher surplus was primarily due to fully booking the annual central bank profit in the first quarter.
However, the central bank's profit fell sharply by 20%, or Rs495 billion, to a little over Rs1.9 trillion, according to the finance ministry.
The four provinces collectively generated a cash surplus of Rs599 billion, exceeding the IMF target by Rs83 billion. Three provincial governments showed cash surpluses, but Balochistan ran a budget deficit in the first quarter, according to the ministry.
The federating units generated Rs301 billion in tax revenues, missing the IMF target by Rs88 billion.
Against a three-month revenue target of Rs3.03 trillion, the FBR collected Rs3.089 trillion, exceeding the target by Rs60 billion. But after September, the FBR began facing a revenue shortfall and was Rs95 billion in deficit for the first four months of the fiscal year.
The non-tax revenues of the five governments amounted to Rs2.6 trillion, Rs430 billion, or 14%, less than in the last fiscal year. The key factor behind the dip was the shrinking central bank profit.
The government collected Rs382 billion in petroleum levy during the first quarter, Rs11 billion higher than in the last fiscal year.
Provincial governments enjoy significant fiscal flexibility due to increased revenues under the National Finance Commission award. In July-September, the four provincial governments spent about Rs1.8 trillion, with development spending reaching Rs1.34 trillion. Their total revenues stood at Rs2.4 trillion, of which Rs1.9 trillion came from their shares of federal taxes.
A breakdown of provincial performance showed that Punjab, with total revenue of Rs1.1 trillion, spent Rs785 billion, generating a surplus of Rs333 billion. However, the province recorded a statistical discrepancy of Rs13.2 billion.
Sindh booked a cash surplus of Rs181 billion after spending Rs510 billion, well below its total revenues. The province also reported a Rs20 billion statistical discrepancy.
K-P recorded a budget surplus of Rs102 billion, with Rs414 billion in income and Rs312 billion in expenditures. K-P also had a statistical discrepancy of Rs35 billion.
Balochistan ran a Rs16 billion budget deficit and spent Rs191 billion in three months.
On the expenditure side, the federal government spent a total of Rs3.1 trillion during the first three months, with only Rs81 billion in development expenditures.
The federal government paid Rs1.7 trillion in interest costs, an increase of Rs322 billion, or one-fourth, from the previous year. Defence spending amounted to Rs495 billion.
After distributing the provincial share, the federal government's net income stood at Rs3.8 trillion, mainly because of booking the entire central bank profit in the first quarter.
