items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The federal government has extended the deadline for civil servants to digitally submit their Declarations of Assets for the financial year 2025-26 through the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) portal until November 30, 2026.
According to an Office Memorandum issued by the Establishment Division on November 12, the extension has been granted with the approval of the Prime Minister, in relaxation of Rule 12(6) of the Civil Servants (Conduct) Rules, 2026.
The previous deadline had been communicated through an earlier memorandum issued on September 16, 2026.
More Time for Corrections
The Establishment Division has also extended the deadline for submitting corrections to the declarations until December 31, 2026. However, any correction will need approval from the officer’s respective Cadre Administrator before it is submitted.
The memorandum directed all federal ministries, divisions, and Cadre Administrators to instruct officers under their administrative control to file their asset declarations digitally on the FBR portal within the extended deadline.
What It Means for Officers
Civil servants who have not yet filed now have until the end of November to submit their declarations online, and another month after that to fix any errors with their Cadre Administrator’s approval.
Digital filing of officers’ assets through the FBR has been on the government’s agenda for some time. ProPakistani earlier reported that the government moved to make civil servants declare their assets on a key IMF demand, while it later emerged that the government won’t fully disclose civil servants’ assets to the public.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
Pakistan has reaffirmed its commitment to the agreed $5 billion bilateral trade target with Turkiye and wants more Turkish investment, especially in its Special Economic Zones (SEZs).
The pledge came on Friday when Turkish Ambassador Irfan Nezioglu called on Minister of State for Finance and Revenue Bilal Azhar Kayani in Islamabad, according to a Finance Division press release. The two sides reviewed cooperation in trade, investment, and energy.
Kayani welcomed Turkiye’s strong interest in investing in Pakistan and said both countries should use their strong political goodwill to increase trade volumes.
Minerals, DISCOs, and Ship Breaking
The minister appreciated the active participation of Turkish companies in the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026 (PMIF26) underway in Islamabad, as well as the interest of Turkish firms in the privatization of power distribution companies (DISCOs).
He also pointed to maritime and ship breaking as sectors with significant room for partnerships between the two countries.
Both sides agreed to renew efforts to expand the Pakistan-Turkiye Trade in Goods Agreement, discussed ways to turn political goodwill into actionable targets, and agreed to hold further meetings.
A Target Still Waiting to Be Met
The $5 billion goal is not new. Leaders of both countries have repeated it for years, as ProPakistani reported when Pakistan and Turkey set out to raise trade by $5 billion back in 2020, and again when both countries renewed the target in 2025.

items.title: A Font Choice Got an Author Accused of Using AI
items.summary:
Independent author T.M. Kirk says people accused her of using artificial intelligence in an online post because of the font she chose.
Kirk said on Instagram that the post carried no AI flag, yet commenters blamed her for making it look AI-generated.
Tools such as ChatGPT and Claude have made it quicker and cheaper to create graphics and other content. Their spread has prompted calls to boycott businesses that use what critics call “AI slop” in advertising.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Independent author T.M. Kirk says people accused her of using artificial intelligence in an online post because of the font she chose.
Kirk said on Instagram that the post carried no AI flag, yet commenters blamed her for making it look AI-generated.
Tools such as ChatGPT and Claude have made it quicker and cheaper to create graphics and other content. Their spread has prompted calls to boycott businesses that use what critics call “AI slop” in advertising.
As people look for clues, familiar design choices can draw the same suspicion as obvious errors, such as garbled text or hands with extra fingers.
What Makes a Font Look AI-Generated?
When an image generator renders lettering as part of a picture, it produces the letters as pixels. The results can resemble common styles from ads, posters and banners in its training data.
Small inconsistencies in spacing or letter shapes can give the text an uneven look, even when it resembles a familiar typeface.
Some AI-generated lettering resembles Inter. Slanted brush lettering seen in dramatic ads and flyers has also drawn comparisons to Road Rage.
Designer Ramin Nasibov highlighted the brush style in a November 2 post that rendered the words “Comic Sans” in similar lettering. Human designers can choose the same style, so the lettering alone tells readers little about how an image was made.
Creators Are Changing How They Work
The scrutiny has extended from em dashes and words such as “delve” to typography. Some writers say they use more casual language, deliberately leave in typos or avoid certain words and punctuation.
Artists have shared early sketches, saved layers and recorded time-lapse videos to document their work. AI can also generate footage that imitates a time-lapse.
Some designers say they avoid typefaces that readers associate with AI. As image generators get better at rendering clean, consistent lettering, those visual clues are likely to become less useful.
The stigma around particular fonts may last longer, leaving small creators and self-published authors fielding questions about ordinary design decisions.
The post A Font Choice Got an Author Accused of Using AI appeared first on ProPakistani.

items.author: Shraddha Goled
items.content:
For Kriti, a Gurugram-based marketing professional, Thursday’s workday came to an abrupt halt even before it began, as Microsoft services went down globally.
With her company relying heavily on Outlook for official sign-offs, the outage stalled its approval pipeline, forcing employees to turn to alternative communication channels and negotiate deadline extensions to keep work moving.
“With Outlook inaccessible since morning, external communication has been stalled, delaying roughly half a day’s worth of urgent approvals and project rollouts,” she said.
Kriti’s experience reflects a wider disruption across enterprises and individuals in India and globally. Microsoft Outlook/Office 365 is used at companies such as Infosys, Wipro, Lupin, CitiusTech, CSS Corp, Indigo, along with banks such as State Bank of India, Equitas Small Finance Bank and others.
What Caused The Outage
The outage, which began late on November 12, crippled critical functions across Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, Copilot and several other Microsoft 365 services in 74 countries, including India. By November 13, the disruption was still unresolved.
Downdetector data showed Outlook complaints in the country peaking at 2,157 late night on Thursday, easing overnight, then climbing back to nearly 4,000 by 10 AM Friday before settling to over 2,500 by noon.
Globally, the monitoring website has detected 1,40,000 complaints. To be sure, over 430 Mn people use Microsoft 365 apps according to the company’s website.
The trouble traces back to roughly 11:30 PM IST (6 PM UTC) on Thursday, when a core process responsible for setting up secure connections on Microsoft’s servers became overwhelmed.
Microsoft said a number of servers began failing automated health checks and dropping out of service, which pushed more load onto the machines left standing, a cascade that eventually hit Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, Copilot, Defender for Office 365, Windows 365 Cloud PCs, and even the admin tools IT teams needed to diagnose the mess, such as Intune. Microsoft has attributed this outage to infrastructure failure.
By Friday afternoon (November 13), Microsoft was still offering no confirmed timeline for full recovery, describing progress only as “limited.” The disruption even reached outside Microsoft’s own walls: OpenAI and Anthropic both reported problems with their Microsoft 365 connectors, a small but telling sign of how deeply the Exchange and Graph APIs are now wired into the newer AI tool stack.
India’s Slice Of The Downtime
For workplaces that rely on Outlook and Teams for daily operations, the outage translated into familiar disruptions: employees unable to access calendars, delayed client responses and teams switching to alternatives such as Slack, WhatsApp and phone calls to stay coordinated.
The disruption also spilled over into customer-facing services. IndiGo, India’s largest airline, said its email support services had been affected and that it might be unable to receive customer emails.
Akasa Air reported delays in its email support services, advising passengers to contact its 24-hour Akasa Care Centre or reach out through social media for immediate assistance. Media reports also indicated disruptions at IT services companies, including Infosys and Cognizant.
The impact extended to business operations beyond communication.
HR tech startup Keka told customers that the outage had affected services such as offer letter generation, scheduling one-on-one meetings, and interview scheduling and rescheduling. Equitas Small Finance Bank, meanwhile, asked customers to use its customer service helpline instead of email to reach the bank.
The outage is a reminder of how concentrated enterprise India’s software stack has become. A large share of Indian offices run their calendars, email, files and meetings entirely inside the Microsoft 365 ecosystem, a convenience that turns into a single point of failure the moment Exchange Online wobbles.
“Businesses have a disaster recovery plan for servers, networks and data. Very few have one for the inbox, and the inbox is where contracts, approvals and payments actually move. Today’s Microsoft 365 outage shows email is a single point of failure that boards have never had to sign off,” said Amit Singh, practice head for managed services at WeP Solutions.
It is also not an isolated event. Microsoft’s service-health page has logged a string of outages through 2026 alone, touching Azure, Teams, Copilot and Microsoft 365 at various points in January, May, June, July, August and October, well before this week’s episode.
Each one has drawn fresh scrutiny of how much global and Indian enterprise IT now leans on a small number of hyperscale providers. That scrutiny is starting to translate into advice: analysts are increasingly telling Indian enterprises to treat multi-vendor redundancy as a backup email client, an alternate collaboration tool, contracts that do not assume round-the-clock uptime as a baseline requirement rather than a nice-to-have.
“My larger concern is not that Microsoft had an outage; outages are inevitable. It is that enterprises have progressively concentrated email, identity, collaboration, security, and now AI into the same cloud ecosystem. We have reduced application complexity, but inadvertently increased dependency concentration,” said Ritwik Batabyal, CTO at Mastek, a Mumbai-based digital and cloud transformation.
That is particularly relevant for India, where cloud adoption is accelerating rapidly. The answer is not an expensive multi-cloud copy of everything, but enterprises should identify their few “minimum viable business” capabilities—identity, critical communication, customer transactions and operational control—and ensure these can degrade gracefully or fail independently, he added.
On a side note, Microsoft offers uptime credits to eligible Microsoft 365 customers if monthly service availability falls below its contractual commitment of 99.9%. Depending on the extent of downtime, customers may qualify for credits of 25%, 50% or 100% of the monthly fee for the affected service. However, these are credits are subject to few conditions and is applicable only when the customer purchases products sold through the Cloud Solution Provider programme.
Microsoft’s Restructuring
Microsoft’s latest workforce restructuring has also raised questions about whether cost-cutting could have implications for the reliability of its cloud services.
The company recently confirmed that around 60,000 employees, or 27% of its global workforce, including those in India, are eligible for a voluntary exit offer, following a separate round of 4,800 job cuts in July. The company employs around 23,000 people in India across various products and roles.
However, there is no evidence so far linking the workforce reductions to the Microsoft 365 outage. Microsoft has not attributed the disruption to staffing constraints, and its investigation into the technical cause is ongoing.
The larger question is whether aggressive cost optimisation, even as Microsoft ramps up investments in AI infrastructure, could create operational risks for services used by millions of businesses. Already the outage has stretched into its second day, and if it goes on, this could be a real bodyblow to Microsoft and could hand a big piece of the enterprise productivity software business to its rivals.
The post Microsoft’s Outlook Outage Drags On: Indian Enterprises Are Feeling The Heat appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.title: 27.1% to 2.6%: India's poverty decline significant, but there’s a catch
items.summary: The World Bank currently defines the international extreme poverty line at $3.00 per person per day in 2021 purchasing power parity (PPP) terms. According to the World Poverty Clock, extreme poverty may be considered eliminated when the poverty headcount ratio falls below 3%. With the World Bank estimating India’s extreme poverty rate at about 2% in 2024, India can, on this measure, be considered to have crossed that threshold.

items.title: Judges close part of ICC Afghanistan investigations that could look at US troops
items.summary:
Judges at the International Criminal Court have issued a decision to formally close part of the prosecutor's investigations into Afghanistan that previously ​looked at alleged crimes by US troops and to focus only ‌on actions of the Taliban since 2021, court documents show.
The decision by the chamber formally closes not only the line of inquiry into alleged crimes by US troops, which ​had already lain dormant since 2021, but also a probe into the ​Islamic State Khorasan (ISIS-K) militia. The office of the prosecutor told ⁠Reuters on Friday it had appealed the decision but could not give further ​details.
It is the latest step in a legal tussle between prosecutors and judges ​about the Afghanistan case, and comes after the United States issued institutional sanctions against the court, citing US opposition to arrest warrants issued for Israeli officials and the investigation into actions ​of US soldiers in Afghanistan.
Read: US activists urge ICC to issue arrest warrants for Trump
items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Judges at the International Criminal Court have issued a decision to formally close part of the prosecutor's investigations into Afghanistan that previously ​looked at alleged crimes by US troops and to focus only ‌on actions of the Taliban since 2021, court documents show.
The decision by the chamber formally closes not only the line of inquiry into alleged crimes by US troops, which ​had already lain dormant since 2021, but also a probe into the ​Islamic State Khorasan (ISIS-K) militia. The office of the prosecutor told ⁠Reuters on Friday it had appealed the decision but could not give further ​details.
It is the latest step in a legal tussle between prosecutors and judges ​about the Afghanistan case, and comes after the United States issued institutional sanctions against the court, citing US opposition to arrest warrants issued for Israeli officials and the investigation into actions ​of US soldiers in Afghanistan.
Read: US activists urge ICC to issue arrest warrants for Trump and Rubio over Gaza
This year, judges ordered prosecutors to split their ​Afghanistan inquiries into two separate probes — one focusing on the alleged crimes committed by the ‌Taliban since ⁠2021, and the other on the original Afghanistan inquiry, which also looked at alleged war crimes by US troops but has shifted towards looking at the ISIS-K militia.
Judges said they had decided to close part of ​the case because prosecutors ​had not shown ⁠they would be able to effectively investigate allegations in Afghanistan apart from the Taliban probe. The splitting of the ​cases means the arrest warrants issued against four Afghan Taliban leaders remain ​in effect.
It ⁠is unclear if formally closing part of the Afghanistan case will be enough to allay American fears over the court exerting jurisdiction over US nationals, as it ⁠does ​not change the court's founding statute. The statute ​says the court can prosecute anyone accused of atrocity crimes committed on the territory of ICC member ​states.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
European Union (EU) leaders said on Friday that Europe's security structure should not be a subject for Ukraine-Russia peace negotiations, ‌but they did not answer the question of who should speak for Europe in any future talks.
The Kremlin said on Friday that Russia would be open to European countries taking part in Ukraine peace talks if it saw they were ready to contribute to the peace process.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz described the Kremlin's ​comments as "the same old game" and said that Europe and the United States agreed on a clear message.
Read: Russia demands Finland leave NATO in Abu Dhabi talks: report
"There will be ​no discussions about Ukraine without Ukraine, and no discussions about Europe without Europe. Furthermore, there is no ⁠need to talk about European security architecture. We have that already," Merz told reporters during a summit of European Union leaders in ​Dublin.
Russian officials have called for a broad agreement on Europe's security architecture to be reached before tackling the specifics of the war. Before it invaded Ukraine in 2022, Russia demanded the withdrawal of NATO forces from countries that joined the alliance after 1997. NATO rejected the demand.
US negotiator Jared Kushner said in Moscow on Thursday that he had begun discussions with European partners on the continent's security architecture.
Europe prioritises ceasefire in Russia-Ukraine War
EU foreign policy ​chief Kaja Kallas said Russian calls for discussions about Europe's security architecture risked diverting attention from the need for a ceasefire. Latvian ​Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs called such discussions "a trap".
During a meeting on Thursday, leaders from Poland, the Baltics and Nordic states warned against brainstorming with the ‌US or ⁠Russia about Europe’s security architecture, according to a European diplomat and a European official.
Forty European countries, meeting as a broader group in Dublin on Thursday, signed a declaration saying that any matter affecting European security should be decided with the involvement of Europeans.
EU leaders broadly agreed that Europe needed to speak with one voice, but did not settle on a single individual to do so. Merz said discussions would ​continue.
"There are established institutional forms of (EU) ​representation — Kaja Kallas, for instance, ⁠is part of this — but the E3 format has also proven very effective," he said, in reference to an informal security grouping of France, Germany and Britain, which is no longer an EU ​member but a prominent NATO ally.
"Moreover, we always include Italy and Poland," Merz added.
Representatives from Britain, ​France, Germany, Italy and ⁠the EU attended Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi earlier this week, where both Moscow and Kyiv cited some progress, though there was no sign of a breakthrough on key issues such as territory.
Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said Britain, one of Europe's top three military powers, certainly ⁠had to ​be included in any future talks and that the five countries plus EU ​institutions would make sense.
"I'm quite flexible on that, so I think what we actually say is more important than the exact configuration of the people in the room," ​he said.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The federal government on Friday reduced the price of petrol by Rs2 while keeping the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) unchanged till November 16.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs330 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs360 per litre from November 14 to November 16. 
The revision comes a day after the government reduced the prices of petrol and HSD by Rs3 and Rs4 per litre, respectively, for November 13.
Read: Petrol goes down by Rs3, high-speed diesel by Rs4 for Nov 13
On November 2, the government announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Friday called for an "immediate and drastic reduction" in greenhouse gas emissions, as divisions over fossil fuels ​dominated the first week of COP31 climate talks in Turkiye.
Big fossil fuel producers and consumers at the talks are resisting any deal that would specify firm ‌new targets or a shift away from oil, gas and coal, observers said as the first week of talks drew to a close.
That poses a challenge for summit host Turkiye and lead negotiator Australia, which have another week to land the kind of ambitious agreement climate advocates such as Guterres say is needed.
"The central question is in the hands of member states, particularly the big emitters. They must recognise the ​need for an immediate and drastic reduction in emissions to keep the 1.5 goal still possible by the end of the century," he said, referring to the warming ​limit countries had agreed to pursue under the 2015 Paris Agreement.
A UN report last month found the world is on course to ⁠exceed the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) warming threshold, a limit scientists say should prevent the worst effects of climate change.
As temperatures have risen, this year has been marked by ​extreme heatwaves across Western Europe and a glacier collapse in Nepal that triggered a flood that killed more than 1,450 people. Thousands more are still missing.
The fossil fuel lobby
Major oil producers ​such as Saudi Arabia and Russia have traditionally resisted language constraining fossil fuels, while large developing economies such as India have opposed measures they say could limit their development and energy choices, a dynamic that has compromised the outcomes of past deals.
The world’s biggest oil consumer, the United States, meanwhile, has skipped the talks for the second year in a row under President Donald Trump, who has called global warming a ​hoax and promoted continued use of fossil fuels.
Read More: 67% Pakistanis see climate as lost cause
"We must confront the disproportionate influence of the fossil fuel lobby. The future of our planet cannot be negotiated on the terms of ​those profiting from its destruction," said Guterres, who is leaving his job at the end of December after two five-year terms.
"But I remain hopeful. I've also seen something extraordinary over these 10 years. Renewable ‌energy has ⁠moved from the margins to the mainstream. The economics have changed. The technology has advanced. A cleaner, safer, and more secure energy future is in our hands. The question is whether we have the courage and speed to reach for it."
Electrification and no firm targets
COP31 host Turkiye is striving to place a proposal to expand global electrification at the centre of an eventual deal, saying the plan will lead to emissions cuts by speeding the shift away from fossil fuel-powered cars, boilers and other equipment.
The proposal does not require the increased electricity use ​to come from renewable sources, although some countries, ​including last year’s COP host Brazil, are ⁠advocating for progress on a plan to require countries to more clearly map out their transition away from fossil fuels.
Katrine Petersen, an observer for the non-governmental organisation E3G, said whether those measures survive the talks depends on conversations in the days to come.
"We've also heard quite ​clearly from countries like India, the G77, that they don't want any firm targets. They don't want any kind of technology ​or fuel-specific language," she said. "[These ⁠are] the kind of consistent and ongoing divides that we've seen from those different parties before."
Representatives from India, Saudi Arabia and Russia did not immediately comment.
Diana Acconcia, head of the EU delegation, said Europe backed the electrification goal.
"Electrification is, in a way, an inclusive agenda because it is non-prescriptive in a way on how the electrification is achieved," she said. "Of course, for the European Union, electrification is ​to be achieved by clean sources of energy."
The Australian team, which is leading negotiations under a split presidency ​arrangement, spent the first few days of the summit gathering views on what should be included in a political text agreed by consensus that will be followed by all the negotiated technical points.
Australia is taking further submissions from ​countries until Saturday night, with a view to formulating a draft text early next week.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Mobilink Bank, one of the largest microfinance Banks in Pakistan, has signed a Sale Purchase Agreement (SPA) to acquire 82.51% shareholding in Apna Microfinance Bank Limited (Apna Bank), subject to applicable legal and regulatory approvals. The proposed acquisition is an extension of Mobilink Bank’s “Growth with Purpose” strategy, reflecting our commitment to responsible growth, financial inclusion, and a stronger, more resilient banking ecosystem. The transaction reinforces Mobilink Bank’s position as a trusted leader in the banking sector. The transaction is aimed at safeguarding the interests of Apna Bank’s depositors, preserving stakeholders’ confidence, and creating a stronger institutional foundation for sustainable growth. It also underscores Mobilink Bank’s commitment to contributing meaningfully to the stability, resilience, and continued evolution Pakistan’s financial sector. The agreement was formally signed by Haaris M. Chaudhary, President & CEO, Mobilink Bank, and Muhammad Akram Shahid, Chairman, Apna Bank, in the presence of senior leadership from both institutions and JazzWorld, underscoring the strategic significance of the transaction.
Upon completion of the transaction, Apna Bank’s customers will become part of a larger, financially resilient institution, with continued access to their accounts and services throughout the transaction. They will benefit from Mobilink Bank’s broader nationwide presence, Islamic Banking offerings, and access to an expanded digital financial services ecosystem powered by JazzCash, creating a more secure, convenient, and future-ready banking experience.
“We have been building the foundation of a comprehensive financial services ecosystem for Pakistan, from JazzCash’s extensive reach in payments to JazzSure Insurance (formerly TPL Insurance) and FikrFree’s modern insurance offerings in a market where insurance penetration remains considerably low, and now Mobilink Bank, which extends that same ambition into banking for agriculture and micro-enterprises. Each of these businesses complements the others, and together they bring us closer to a Pakistan where every citizen, regardless of where they live or how they earn a living, has access to the financial tools they need to grow,” said Aamir Ibrahim, Chairman, Mobilink Bank and CEO, JazzWorld.
Speaking on the SPA signing, Haaris M. Chaudhary, President and CEO Mobilink Bank, said,
“Mobilink Bank has built strong digital capabilities, scale and customer reach over time. As a customer-first organization, our focus is to ensure continuity for Apna Bank customers and make their transition into a larger, more future-ready institution as seamless as possible, supported by close coordination across teams throughout the process.”
Commenting on the development, Nazish Ali, Acting CEO of Apna Bank, said: “This agreement marks the beginning of an important new chapter for Apna Bank. We believe that becoming part of Mobilink Bank will provide our customers with access to broader capabilities, stronger digital infrastructure and an expanded range of financial services. Equally important, our priority throughout this journey will remain the interests of our customers, depositors, employees and other stakeholders, while ensuring continuity of service.”

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The federal government has set December 31, 2026, as the deadline to bring all businesses and traders in Islamabad into the digital payments system. The move is part of an initiative to make the federal capital Pakistan’s first fully cashless city.
The decision was announced during a high-level meeting chaired by Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry. Capital Development Authority (CDA) Chairman Sohail Ashraf, representatives of the banking sector, and senior government officials attended the meeting.
Chaudhry said work on the Cashless Islamabad initiative was progressing rapidly under the directives of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Federal Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi. He added that the interior minister had committed to making Islamabad not only Pakistan’s first cashless city but also the world’s first cashless capital.
Islamabad Government Departments to Stop Accepting Cash After November 30
Under the government’s plan, departments of the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) administration and the CDA will no longer accept cash payments after November 30. All transactions at these departments will instead be conducted through digital payment channels.
The move comes as the federal government pushes ahead with its broader digital payment roadmap to reduce reliance on cash and expand access to electronic transactions across Pakistan.
Over 26,000 Merchants Already Integrated Into Digital Payments System
According to Chaudhry, approximately 26,000 merchants in Islamabad have already been integrated into the digital payments system. The government now aims to extend digital payment facilities to all commercial establishments by December 31.
The initiative will cover businesses of all sizes, including street vendors, pushcart operators, small retailers, and large commercial establishments. The minister stressed that cooperation among relevant institutions and input from stakeholders would be critical to achieving the target.
Islamabad was previously identified as a target for a cashless transition by the end of 2026. The latest announcement provides more specific deadlines for government departments and businesses.
What the Cashless Islamabad Initiative Means for Businesses
The minister said the transition would improve financial transparency, strengthen tax monitoring, and make transactions more efficient. Banking sector representatives welcomed the initiative and assured the government of their full cooperation in implementing the plan.
However, the success of the initiative will depend on reliable digital payment infrastructure, internet connectivity, and the ability of smaller merchants and customers to adopt electronic payment methods.
With the December 31 deadline approaching, the key challenge for authorities will be ensuring that digital payment facilities are accessible across the capital, particularly for small traders who continue to rely heavily on cash.

items.title: Apple's iPhone 18 is Missing From This Year's Lineup, and Samsung Could Be the Reason
items.summary: Apple delayed the launch of the iPhone 18 because of a new deal with Samsung, according to a report. The tech giant was reportedly unable to secure an adequate quantity of camera sensors it needed for mass production. The Cupertino company has reportedly been sourcing camera sensors exclusively from Sony. The report now highlights that Sony executives have confirmed that its long-standing partnership with the iPhone maker has come to an end. To diversify its supply, Apple struck a deal with Samsung in August last year, which reportedly allowed the company to “strengthen its manufacturing” base in the US. As part of the new deal, Samsung is said to supply CMOS camera sensors for the newer iPhone models, produced at the South Korean tech giant’s facility in Austin, Texas.

items.content:
Fintech SaaS company Zaggle’s net profit plunged 30% to ₹24.5 Cr in the second quarter (Q2) of the fiscal year 2026-27 (FY27) as against ₹35 Cr in the year-ago period. Sequentially, the company’s profit rose 40% from ₹17.5 Cr in Q1 FY27.
Operating revenue grew 34.2% YoY and 37% QoQ to ₹580 Cr in the quarter under review. In a statement, the company noted that its SaaS business recorded its “highest-ever quarterly performance”, largely driven by revenue recognition from novated contracts following the Dice acquisition.
Including other income of ₹6.3 Cr, Zaggle’s total income for the quarter stood at ₹586.2 Cr.
Meanwhile, total expenses surged 39.9% to ₹555.7 Cr in the quarter under review from ₹397.1 Cr in the year-ago period. The company also incurred a tax expense of ₹7.3 Cr during the quarter. It also incorporated a gain of ₹1.3 Cr from share of profit of an associate.
Zaggle also said that its adjusted EBITDA slipped marginally by 4.2% YoY to ₹44.6 Cr in the quarter under review, while its adjusted EBITDA margin shrunk 310 bps to 7.7%.
“On the business front, we witnessed strong traction in our loyalty and rewards segment, supported by increased festive season activity. This contributed to revenue growth across both Zaggle and Greenedge,” said Zaggle founder and executive chairman Raj P Narayanam.
Alongside the quarterly results, the company’s board has approved an allotment of 1.2 Lakh equity shares under its Zaggle Employee Stock Option Scheme 2022, having a face value of INR 1 each, as fully paid-up to certain “identified” employees.
The exercise price for 1,21,676 equity shares stood at ₹1 apiece, while the price for 828 allotted shares stood at ₹164 per share. Following the allotment, the total paid-up equity share capital of the company has increased to ₹13.45 Cr from ₹13.44 Cr earlier.
As per the stock’s last closing price, the newly allotted equity shares are worth nearly ₹ 2.12 Cr.
Founded in 2011, Zaggle is a spend management and corporate employee benefits platform. It helps businesses automate their accounts and issues prepaid cards, in partnership with banking partners, to reward their employees with incentives and gifts.
Zaggle claims to have built a network of over 4,236 corporate customers and 4.08 Mn users, with more than 50 Mn cards issued to date.
Shares of Zaggle ended Friday’s trading session 0.12% higher at ₹173.2 apiece on the BSE.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Colette Kress spent years as the one Nvidia executive willing to check CEO Jensen Huang’s enormous, ​often risky ambitions. As he drove the chipmaker deeper into multibillion-dollar AI investments, she pushed back, according to two people familiar with the matter on Thursday.
Now the ‌59-year-old finance chief has been handed the top job on an interim basis, while Nvidia searches for a permanent successor. Huang on Thursday stepped down from the company he co-founded and ran for three decades in a cloud of scandal, leaving Nvidia to navigate its first leadership transition without the architect of its rise.
Through their conflicts, Kress served as an important counterweight to Huang, whose success afforded him great latitude on key decisions, the two sources said. Months before news that ​Huang had a relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, some on Wall Street were questioning whether his appetite for risk was sound and if the deals he struck ​were feeding an increasingly circular AI economy.
Kress and her staff clashed with Huang and the company's sales team over the massive and risky financing deals that ⁠fed into what some Wall Street critics deemed a circular AI economy, including investments in OpenAI and AI infrastructure companies such as Lambda, according to one of the people familiar with the matter.
A proposed $250 ​billion plan to support an OpenAI data center project in Ohio was ultimately pared to $120 billion.
"I think it's unlikely anyone but Jensen is going to invest in his own customers as aggressively," said ​a third source, a venture capital investor. Huang has pushed Nvidia to offer financing to startups, the person said.
Kress the pragmatist
People who know her describe Kress as a calming contrast to Huang’s often confrontational style. Kress joined Nvidia in 2013 after a long career at other tech industry giants including Microsoft , Cisco and Texas Instruments.
Read More: US Senate Banking Committee chair calls on Jensen Huang, Lutnick to testify
"Colette is a pragmatist," said a fourth source familiar with the matter. She can project calm and help stabilize markets while the search is ​ongoing, the person said, adding that Kress had been on recent calls to reassure customers and suppliers as the tumult inside the company unfolded.
Under her leadership, Nvidia is likely to "approach DC more like other ​tech companies do, by trying to build capital and make friends," instead of picking "a fight over export controls" the way it did under Huang's leadership, the person said.
But many investors, analysts and industry sources who spoke ‌to Reuters ⁠questioned whether a finance executive could preserve the technological risk-taking that turned Nvidia into an AI chips powerhouse.
"Putting (Kress) in the interim role makes sense to keep the markets calm, but I don't think she is the long-term visionary that Nvidia needs to continue its current trajectory," said Anshel Sag, principal analyst at Moor Insights and Strategy.
Nvidia shares slumped 14% to their lowest in nearly 16 months on Thursday after the company said Huang would step down, but pared losses to close down 4.3%.
Whether Kress will keep the CEO role permanently is yet to be decided. But other names have surfaced, including ​Nvidia executive Ian Buck, who helped launch AI ​on Nvidia chips and led development of ⁠the CUDA software system. AMD CEO Lisa Su as well as Arm boss Rene Haas have also been speculated as potential candidates.
What did Kress know?
Questions are also swirling about how much Kress knew about Nvidia's chip sales and Huang's affairs. China has denied the spying allegations. Reuters was not ​able to contact Alice Huang for comment.
A fifth source said Kress knew about his relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, ​who reported to him. Nvidia ⁠and Powell did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Sunny Cheung, an analyst at the Washington-based Jamestown Foundation, said Kress could face congressional questions about the company's oversight of chip sales involving Chinese military-linked institutions and Southeast Asian intermediaries.
In a 2023 interview with an Israeli publication, Kress credited her two young sons with urging her to join Nvidia in 2013 because they knew its chips from their video games.
She ⁠became a billionaire ​in 2025 based on the value of her Nvidia equity, according to media reports, and Forbes said her net ​worth of $1.2 billion in mid-2026 put her in 32nd place on its list of America's richest self-made women.
Kress, who holds an undergraduate degree in finance and an MBA, was also named among the 50 most powerful women in business on rankings ​compiled by Fortune and Forbes magazines in recent years.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
South African climate-tech startup GreenBDG Africa has developed a platform that helps businesses track energy use, reduce emissions and make better decisions about their buildings and infrastructure.
Founded in 2014 by Songo Didiza, GreenBDG Africa pulls in data that usually sits in silos – utility meters, building management systems (BMS), solar inverters and utility invoices. Using artificial intelligence, the platform checks and analyses this data, helping businesses better understand their energy use and environmental performance. It also helps organisations meet sustainability reporting requirements and make more informed financial and operational decisions.
“The output is tailored to each stakeholder. A CFO sees Rand-denominated risk, tax recovery, such as Section 12L, and fines avoided. A sustainability officer gets framework-ready disclosures. A facility manager gets actionable alerts,” Didiza told Disrupt Africa.
The Sandton-headquartered startup is also a registered Tier 1 Energy Services Company (ESCO) on the South African National Energy Development Institute database, meaning its work does not start and end with sustainability reporting.
“We design and implement energy efficiency, renewable energy and low-carbon projects. Our approach is simple: measure, understand, predict, optimise, decarbonise,” Didiza said.
Turning sustainability data into better decisions
Didiza, an ESG strategist and green building specialist with a background in computational and applied mathematics, leads the business alongside Chief Strategy Officer Sumaya Mahomed and Chief Technology Officer Ridhwaan Mayet. The team was responding to rapidly rising ESG pressure on African asset owners from investors, lenders, regulators and export markets to demonstrate their environmental performance.
“The data they need to respond is scattered across meters, spreadsheets, invoices and consultants’ reports. Sustainability reporting had become a costly annual compliance exercise rather than a source of better decisions,” she said.
Regulation has made the problem more urgent. In South Africa, building owners face requirements to assess and report how efficiently their properties use energy, with fines of up to ZAR5 million (US$300,000) for non-compliance.
Businesses also face carbon tax obligations and growing sustainability reporting requirements, while energy efficiency tax incentives can go unclaimed without verified data.
Meanwhile, exporters face carbon-related trade measures such as the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, which places a carbon-related cost on certain imported goods.
Didiza said GreenBDG Africa’s competition fell into two camps: global sustainability reporting platforms, which are not always designed for African regulations, infrastructure or energy pricing; and local engineering and sustainability consultancies, which often rely on manual reporting processes rather than continuously updated data.
“We bridge this gap: we are locally engineered, AI-enabled, and backed by a Tier 1 ESCO model that can implement the projects the data identifies,” she said.
Growing impact and expanding across Africa
The startup says it has contributed to decarbonising assets by approximately 250,000 tonnes of CO₂e, and supported more than one million square metres of building space with energy performance certificates and over 13.5 megawatts of renewable energy capacity.
The startup’s sustainability engagements have covered portfolios with a combined net asset value of more than ZAR50 billion (US$3 billion).
Flagship projects include the Bertha Solar & Digital Decarbonisation Project, a net-zero precinct pathway for industrial precincts such as the Dube TradePort Special Economic Zone, and energy performance optimisation for Eastern Cape Public Works.
“Uptake has been strongest among organisations with large, distributed portfolios, where ESG risk translates directly into financial risk,” Didiza said.
Clients include manufacturers, property funds, freight and logistics firms, ICT companies and data centre operators looking to decarbonise their portfolios.
GreenBDG Africa has set itself a public target, #1000by2030, of helping more than 1,000 assets reach decarbonisation status by 2030, and is currently a quarter of the way there.
The startup earns revenue in three ways: platform subscriptions per asset or portfolio for ongoing ESG data, analytics and reporting; advisory and certification work, including ESG strategy, green building certification and net-zero pathways; and implementation through its Tier 1 ESCO capability, often structured so that savings from one phase fund the next.
Currently operating in South Africa across six sectors – real estate, financial services, manufacturing, logistics, ICT and mining – GreenBDG Africa plans to expand in two directions – deeper into sectors beyond real estate, particularly export-oriented manufacturers facing carbon border mechanisms, and into the rest of the continent, starting with Botswana and Zimbabwe.
“ESG disclosure requirements and green finance are growing fast but local, data-driven tools are scarce. Our Special Economic Zone methodology is built to be replicable, which makes SEZs and industrial parks across Africa a natural route,” Didiza said.
Overcoming challenges and supporting women in climate tech
“The biggest challenge has been data, not technology. Many facilities still run on manual meter readings, incomplete records and invoices in different formats, so much of our early work went into building integrations with more than 15 hardware brands and AI validation that turns messy inputs into audit-ready data,” Didiza said.
Changing how businesses view sustainability has been another hurdle. It is often seen as a compliance cost rather than an investment, meaning GreenBDG Africa has had to demonstrate its financial value to business leaders before conversations move forward.
Like many African climate-tech businesses, the startup has also faced lengthy enterprise and public sector sales cycles and limited access to growth capital, while competing with well-funded global platforms.
As it navigates these challenges, GreenBDG Africa is also working to strengthen its business model and position itself for growth.
The startup participated in the Standard Chartered Foundation Women in Tech programme, implemented locally by Standard Chartered Bank in South Africa and supported globally by Village Capital across 12 markets in Africa, the Middle East and Pakistan. Through the programme, it received mentorship, investor-readiness training, market access, networking and funding.
Didiza said the programme helped the startup begin developing its own models and solutions to the challenges it faced, and she would “absolutely” recommend that other women founders apply.
“Climate tech in Africa needs more women building and leading it, and programmes like this give founders the network and confidence to scale,” she said.
The post How South African startup GreenBDG Africa is building the “digital brain” behind sustainable assets appeared first on Disrupt Africa.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Paytm’s wholly owned subsidiary, Paytm Payments Services Ltd (PPSL), has received in-principle authorisation from the RBI to set up and operate a payment system for issuing and operating prepaid payment instruments (PPIs), including digital wallets.
The fintech major disclosed that it has been granted the authorisation, under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, from the apex bank in a filing today.
Now, Paytm can commence operations only after fulfilling the RBI’s conditions and securing final authorisation, or a Certificate of Authorisation, from the central bank.
PPSL had submitted its application for a fresh PPI licence to the RBI on December 31, 2025, which Paytm disclosed in its Q1 FY27 earnings release.
The in-principle authorisation comes with compliance requirements around PPSL’s technology infrastructure and cybersecurity systems.
The RBI has directed the subsidiary to undertake a system audit, including a cybersecurity audit, through an eligible auditor. PPSL must submit the audit report to the RBI within six months. If it fails to meet the deadline, the in-principle authorisation will automatically lapse, and the RBI will not consider granting final authorisation thereafter.
The central bank has also directed PPSL to seek prior approval for any change in its shareholding or ownership, in accordance with its July 2022 directions on changes in control of non-bank payment system operators.
Once it secures the final authorisation, PPSL will be able to issue prepaid payment instruments, including wallets, in India.
Paytm’s Wallet Revival Journey
Paytm’s bid to revive its wallet business has been a long-drawn process, with the company spending nearly three years looking for a way back after regulatory action against its payments bank disrupted the service.
The latest in-principle authorisation from the RBI brings the fintech major closer to that goal. But the road to this point has been marked by regulatory uncertainty, shifting plans and repeated reassurances from founder and CEO Vijay Shekhar Sharma.
Setback for the fintech’s wallet business came in January 2024, when the RBI barred Paytm Payments Bank from accepting fresh deposits, credit transactions and top-ups in customer accounts and wallets. The restrictions took effect on March 15, 2024, dealing a blow to Paytm’s wallet operations, which were closely tied to the payments bank.
Paytm continued to signal that it wanted to bring the service back.
The company considered multiple options after the RBI action and saw a breakthrough via PPSL. The company applied to the RBI for a fresh PPI authorisation, which would allow it to issue digital wallets without relying on PPBL’s former banking licence.
The wallet also remained part of Paytm’s broader consumer payments strategy as the application awaited regulatory clearance. During the Q1 FY27 earnings call, the management reiterated its interest in reviving the offering but did not provide an update on the application.
In the Q2 FY27 earnings call, the company pointed to the possibility of bringing the wallet and Paytm Postpaid, its credit-on-UPI offering, together to strengthen its consumer payments ecosystem. It stopped short of providing a timeline for the wallet’s return.
Why Is The Wallet Important For Paytm?
Paytm’s Wallet may not contribute significantly to revenue on its own, but its return could help the company bring more consumers onto its app as well as increase the frequency of transactions. It could also create opportunities to cross-sell financial products, including Paytm Postpaid, personal loans, wealth management and equity broking services.
During the Q2 FY27 earnings call, management pointed to improving monetisation across its consumer business, driven by products such as Postpaid, personal loans, equity broking and wealth management.
Sharma has also identified wealth management as a key area of expansion, indicating that Paytm is looking to build a broader consumer financial services business alongside its payments operations.
This comes as the fintech major reported a sharp rise in profitability for the September quarter. Paytm’s net profit surged 10.7X year-on-year (YoY) to ₹225 Cr in Q2 FY27, compared with ₹21 Cr in the year-ago quarter. It was also marginally higher than the ₹220 Cr reported in the June quarter. Operating revenue grew 28% YoY and 8% sequentially to ₹2,648 Cr during the quarter under review.
Today’s development sent Paytm’s shares to a fresh 52-week high of ₹1,958.80 apiece on the BSE, up about 2% from previous close. However, the stock continues to trade below its IPO issue price of ₹2,150.
The stock closed today’s trading session 1.1% higher at ₹1945 apiece on the BSE.
The post Paytm Set To Revive Wallet Business With RBI In-Principle Nod appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has sought details from home services platforms, including Pronto, Snabbit and Urban Company’s InstaHelp, over the collection of first-person video and sensor data from gig workers for training physical AI models.
As per a report by ET , a meeting chaired by MeitY secretary S Krishnan yesterday brought together senior executives from the quick home services platforms and other technology and robotics companies to discuss concerns around workers’ consent, consumer privacy and data sovereignty.
Officials are concerned that recordings of everyday household activities could infringe workers’ rights, compromise consumer privacy and pose risks to national data security.
The ministry sought details on the standard operating procedures (SOPs) followed by companies for collecting, processing and storing such data. It also sought information on safeguards for obtaining workers’ consent and protecting the privacy of other individuals captured in the recordings.
The ministry also sought clarity on whether companies were selling, sharing or transferring the collected data to physical AI developers outside India. It asked Pronto to submit details of its data collection practices and the SOPs it follows, ET reported, citing people familiar with the discussions.
When asked by Inc42 about the meeting and the details sought by the ministry, Pronto said it had participated in the meeting as part of a broader industry consultation involving home services platforms, robotics companies and other stakeholders.
The spokesperson said that the consultation provided an opportunity for the ministry and industry participants to exchange perspectives, share existing practices and discuss the opportunities and challenges emerging from the evolving AI landscape.
“Pronto shared its current practices as part of this exchange and looks forward to continued engagement with MeitY and other industry stakeholders,” the startup said.
Inc42 has reached out to Snabbit and Urban Company for their comments on the development. The story will be updated upon receiving responses.
Concerns were also reportedly raised about India becoming a source of cheap training data for foreign AI companies. Executives suggested that the country should focus on developing its own physical AI capabilities rather than merely supplying data to overseas developers.
This comes shortly after Pronto faced scrutiny over a pilot programme to record household chores using cameras worn by service professionals to generate training data for robotics systems.
The controversy also brought Snabbit and Urban Company under scrutiny over their potential involvement in this. Snabbit subsequently clarified that it had conducted a limited assessment of the tech in a controlled training-centre environment but decided against proceeding with the proposal.
Urban Company founder Abhiraj Singh Bhal said the company neither records inside customers’ homes nor plans to do so.
Pronto, meanwhile, confirmed that it was running an opt-in pilot involving first-person video recordings of household chores. Initially, it said the feature was available only to customers who actively opted in during booking and was limited to less than 0.01% of its users.
The startup later told Inc42 that raw footage was deleted immediately after the work was completed, while an anonymised, end-to-end encrypted recording remained accessible only to customers for 48 hours.
The anonymised footage was subsequently used for AI training, as outlined in its terms.
This further casts a shadow on Pronto founder Anjali Sardana’s expanding ambitions in physical AI beyond the home services business.
In July, the startup formalised its data collection experiment through Verified, an opt-in premium service in which professionals wear head-mounted or body-mounted cameras during visits.
Last month, Sardana launched Provision Labs, a San Francisco-based physical AI venture that will collect data to train and test AI systems designed to perform real-world tasks using robots and other machines.
Provision Labs also announced the acquisition of Mumbai-based Basilisk Industries, a startup focused on perception technologies. Basilisk founder Shourya Watwani will lead Provision’s hardware efforts and work on its in-house post-processing models.
The relationship between Pronto’s household data collection and Provision Labs’ operations remains unclear.

items.content:
The President’s House on Friday issued a clarification regarding a meeting between President Asif Ali Zardari and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, rejecting media reports suggesting that provincial matters had come under discussion.
The clarification came a day after Naqvi made a surprise visit to Nawabshah to meet the president. Sources had said the meeting focused on proposals for the creation of new provinces and the possibility of holding a referendum on the issue.
Sources also claimed that Naqvi had travelled to Nawabshah on an urgent basis, carrying an important message from a senior national figure, and sought to take the president into confidence over the matters discussed.
Read: Naqvi makes surprise dash to Nawabshah with ‘important message’ for Zardari
Following the reports, the President’s House spokesperson dismissed claims that provincial matters had been discussed during the meeting.
“There is no truth in media reports claiming that matters relating to the provinces were discussed during the interior minister's meeting with the president,” the spokesperson said.
“Matters concerning national security and the regional situation were discussed at the meeting, but no provincial matters were discussed,” the spokesperson added.
صدرِ مملکت آصف علی زرداری اور وفاقی وزیر داخلہ محسن نقوی کے درمیان گزشتہ روز ہونے والی ملاقات کے حوالے سے ترجمان کی وضاحت۔
صدرِ مملکت سے وفاقی وزیر داخلہ کی ملاقات میں صوبوں سے متعلق امور پر گفتگو سے متعلق میڈیا رپورٹس میں کوئی صداقت نہیں: ترجمان
ملاقات میں قومی سلامتی اور خطے…
— The President of Pakistan (@PresOfPakistan) November 13, 2026
The debate over creating new provinces as part of a broader restructuring of the system gained momentum on July 31, when Naqvi called for additional administrative units or provinces to overhaul what he described as the country's outdated governance system.
Addressing the Pakistan Economic Summit 2026 in Islamabad, he argued that the existing governance model had effectively “collapsed” after decades of failing to deliver. He said decentralisation was essential to improving public services, ensuring timely justice and creating opportunities for young people.
His remarks drew a mixed response, with several PML-N leaders criticising him and describing him as one of the beneficiaries of the existing system.
Among them was PML-N leader and Prime Minister's aide Rana Sanaullah, who questioned how Naqvi could criticise the political system after rising to the office of interior minister through the same system in just three and a half years.
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, however, differed with his party colleague, saying he largely agreed with the interior minister's assessment.
Also Read: PML-N's Asif backs twelve new provinces
On September 4, the Sindh Assembly passed a resolution rejecting attempts to divide the province or create new administrative units. Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah declared that “there will be no compromise on Sindh's geographical unity”.
Two days later, Naqvi renewed his call for a “reset” of the country's governance system, stressing the need to restructure its administrative framework.
The proposal has also drawn interest from Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) leader Mustafa Kamal, who heads the federal health ministry and has repeatedly advocated carving out new provinces from Sindh.
Even before Naqvi's July 31 remarks, Kamal had floated the idea of dividing Sindh, drawing strong opposition. He remains a prominent advocate of the demand.
However, the creation of new provinces would require a demanding constitutional process. Legal experts cited by The Express Tribune have pointed out that a public vote alone cannot lead to the creation of a new province. Any change to provincial boundaries must follow the constitutional amendment procedure, including approval by the relevant provincial assembly.
A referendum could potentially provide democratic legitimacy to such a move, but would not replace the constitutional requirements.
The debate over new provinces, therefore, extends beyond administrative restructuring to questions about the distribution of powers between the federation, provinces and local governments, as well as the role of citizens in decisions affecting governance and public service delivery.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
India’s real estate industry is worth an estimated $650 Bn. Yet, for a sector of this scale, the way properties are built, bought, sold and managed remains surprisingly dependent on traditional processes.
From fragmented broker networks and manual verification to lengthy property transactions and construction inefficiencies, large parts of the real estate value chain have yet to experience the technological transformation seen in sectors such as banking, commerce and mobility.
For startups, this presents an enormous opportunity. But building real estate technology comes with a unique set of challenges.
Selling to traditional developers, converting pilots into enterprise contracts, navigating regulatory complexities and building scalable business models require far more than a promising product.
It is this gap between building a solution and scaling a business that Inc42 and publicly listed workspace company DevX are looking to address with the launch of RE:FRAME, a four-week accelerator for India’s emerging PropTech startups.
Designed for founders who have already demonstrated early market traction, RE:FRAME will bring together 10 promising PropTech startups for hands-on learning, mentorship, industry connections, enterprise exposure and investor access.
The programme will culminate in a curated Demo Day, where five shortlisted startups will pitch for potential investment from a ₹15 Cr pool (subject to investment evaluation and terms).
Applications for the inaugural cohort are now open and will close on 20 December 2026.
“We started DevX as an accelerator in 2017, so supporting founders is in our DNA. RE:FRAME brings us back to that root, now with the depth of a listed real estate operator behind it. We’re looking for founders who want to rethink how India builds, leases, manages and invests in property. We’ll give them more than desks: we’ll put real customers, mentors and capital in the room,” said Umesh Uttamchandani, cofounder and MD, DevX.
APPLY NOW FOR RE:FRAME
India’s PropTech Opportunity Is Growing, So Are Its Challenges
India’s real estate industry is undergoing a significant shift. According to a FICCI–KPMG report, India’s real estate market was valued at approximately $650 Bn in 2025 and is projected to reach $5.8 Tn by 2047.
Technology is becoming an increasingly important part of this transformation. While the first generation of PropTech businesses largely focussed on bringing property discovery and transactions online, the opportunity is now expanding across the real estate lifecycle.
Startups are developing solutions for construction automation, developer sales, property management, smart buildings, financing, energy efficiency, land records and AI-powered analytics.
Investor interest has followed.
According to Inc42 Datalabs, India’s proptech sector raised around $834 Mn across 42 funding rounds in 2025. Infra.Market ($254 Mn) and WeWork India ($210 Mn) alone accounted for more than 50% of the total capital raised.
The sector has also witnessed a wave of public listings, with companies such as DevX, Smartworks, IndiQube, WeWork India and ArisInfra making their stock market debuts in 2025.
But for emerging founders, raising capital is only one part of the challenge.
Unlike consumer internet businesses, PropTech startups often operate in an ecosystem characterised by long enterprise sales cycles, multiple stakeholders, legacy business practices and complex regulatory requirements.
A startup may have a working product and paying customers but still struggle to expand beyond a handful of developers, convert pilots into recurring contracts or establish a repeatable go-to-market strategy.
The questions become increasingly difficult as these businesses grow.
How do founders build trust with traditional real estate enterprises? What does it take to scale distribution across developers and property markets? How can AI and technology improve operating efficiency without compromising unit economics? And how should startups position themselves for institutional capital?
Solving these challenges requires more than capital. It requires access to the right industry networks, operators, expertise and opportunities to test business models at scale.
This is the opportunity RE:FRAME aims to address.
Introducing RE:FRAME: A PropTech Accelerator Built For Scale
RE:FRAME brings together Inc42’s experience working with India’s startup, investor and founder ecosystem and DevX’s expertise in developing and operating managed workspaces. The partnership aims to combine startup acceleration with a deeper understanding of the real estate industry’s operational challenges, enterprise requirements and commercial opportunities.
The accelerator is designed for founders who have moved beyond the idea stage, built working products and demonstrated early customer demand, but now face the more complex task of scaling their businesses.
Rather than taking a one-size-fits-all approach to startup acceleration, the four-week programme will focus on the challenges specific to PropTech businesses — from enterprise sales, go-to-market strategy and unit economics to product development, AI adoption and fundraising.
“India’s PropTech opportunity extends far beyond digitising property transactions. The next wave of startups will fundamentally change how real estate is built, financed, managed and experienced. But building a promising product is only the first step. The real challenge is turning innovation into adoption and sustainable businesses. With RE, we want to help founders bridge that gap and build companies that can shape the future of India’s real estate industry,” said Vaibhav Vardhan, Founder and CEO of Inc42.
For the first cohort, 10 startups will be selected, with applications assessed on market traction, the strength of the problem being solved, market opportunity, founding team and potential to scale.
APPLY NOW FOR RE:FRAME
Who Can Apply For RE:FRAME?
The programme is open to startups operating across the real estate value chain, including property discovery and brokerage, construction technology, developer sales and marketing, property management, rental and tenant experience, commercial real estate, real estate financing, smart buildings, sustainability, AI and real estate data analytics.
Inside The Four Weeks Of RE
The inaugural cohort will begin its programme journey in February 2027, and will follow a hybrid format, combining virtual learning with an intensive physical bootcamp in Delhi NCR.
Starting with three weeks of learning, the final week will bring the selected founders together for a six-day physical bootcamp and a demo day in Delhi NCR.
The curriculum will address four interconnected aspects of scaling a PropTech business:
Go-To-Market & Enterprise Sales: Building repeatable sales processes, improving customer acquisition and navigating complex enterprise relationships.
Business Models & Unit Economics: Strengthening monetisation, pricing, financial discipline and the operating foundations required for sustainable growth.
Product, Technology & AI: Building differentiated products, identifying practical AI applications and developing technology roadmaps that support scale.
Fundraising & Investment Readiness: Sharpening investment narratives, understanding fundraising strategies and preparing for investor discussions.
Through the programme, founders will have opportunities to learn from experienced PropTech entrepreneurs, technology leaders, real estate operators, investors and specialists familiar with the commercial and regulatory complexities of the industry.
Demo Day: The ₹15 Cr Investment Opportunity
RE:FRAME will culminate in a curated Demo Day in March 2027, where the top five startups from the inaugural cohort will pitch their businesses to venture capital investors, angel investors, HNIs and industry leaders.
The shortlisted startups will have an opportunity to secure funding from a ₹15 Cr investment pool, subject to investment evaluation and mutually agreed terms.
If you’re building technology to transform how India’s real estate is developed, bought, sold or managed, and have the traction and ambition to scale, RE could be your next big leap.
Applications for Cohort 01 close on 20 December 2026.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Amazon has a secret plan to ensure shoppers never need to leave its site: own the world’s product information.
Called World Product Graph, the initiative seeks to hoover up data on virtually every item for sale on Earth, whether Amazon stocks it or not, ​according to an internal document reviewed by Reuters, and to people familiar with the matter.
In so doing, Amazon could truly become the everything store, offering deep data on a vast array of goods and cutting in to Google's dominance ‌in online search, while also fending off rival Walmart's growing e-commerce business.
It also serves to address the continued rise of AI agents, software that can complete shopping tasks autonomously for users. According to the document, Amazon's own AI-driven search agent often provides inaccurate information.
And if fully implemented, World Product Graph could draw shoppers away from rival e-commerce sites that have far less data.
“Amazon cannot be the go-destination for every shopping mission if customers must leave to research product relationships on Google, brand websites, and review sites,” according to the document. “These answers exist, but the only way to find them has been to leave Amazon for painstaking research on brand websites, third party ​review sites and tech forums.”
Reuters could not determine if or when this plan may be implemented, though the document, written like a press release, has an aspirational future release date of October 1, 2027.
"Draft, outdated documents often paint an incomplete picture and the ​existence of a brainstorming document such as this one doesn't necessarily reflect our current plans," said Amazon, in a statement. "We're constantly working on new ideas and technologies to make Amazon's product catalog comprehensive, accurate, and ⁠helpful for customers."
Already, many consumers begin researching products on Amazon. But according to a 2025 Morgan Stanley research report, the 16% of online shoppers who do so on Amazon is dwarfed by Google’s 57%. However, when customers know exactly what product they plan to buy, Amazon has ​the advantage, with 41% of searches starting there, compared with 23% for Google and 18% for Walmart.
'The everyrhing store'
World Product Graph “depends on discovering how brands organize their products on their own websites,” the document says. That will entail some brands and retailers contributing product data continuously to Amazon, ​but also Amazon independently crawling other retailers’ websites.
Reuters could not determine how Amazon planned to crawl the sites or whether it would need to seek permission in all cases.
Amazon has already signed up Coca-Cola and Bayer, among others, to contribute product data, the document says. And the company held a “CEO-level P&G/Amazon summit” for a trial with Procter & Gamble ,The companies didn't respond to requests for comment.
Amazon is shuffling staff internally to get the project off the ground, according to one of the people, though Reuters could not determine if the October 1 date is a realistic deadline for making the plan public.
Read More: Hours-long Microsoft outage disrupts businesses, governments globally
The document laying out the plan is what ​is known internally as a PR/FAQ — press release and frequently asked questions — which is typically a six-page narrative memo laying out the rationale and business case for a new product or service. Not all PR/FAQs lead to a service being introduced and, the people said, World Product Graph ​could be modified or aborted due to financial or other concerns.
The project is part of Amazon’s Selection & Catalog Systems unit, according to the document, and is being organized under Robert Tekiela, a vice president in the division. He did not respond to a request for comment.
With the more complete data, Amazon ‌can help users determine ⁠with more certainty which is the most recent model or colorway of a vacuum cleaner or tablet computer while also guiding them toward more subjective criteria like which is best for them based on their shopping history or other data, the document shows.
The project would also address problems with Amazon’s own AI-powered search engine known as Rufus, which the company began calling “Alexa for Shopping” in May. “Many Rufus answers are factually wrong or incomplete, but customers lack expertise to detect these errors,” the document says.
Further, users conduct about 83 million searches weekly using Rufus, and running them is “expensive,” according to the document. More data would allow Amazon to use less expensive models, more efficiently.
“I used to spend an hour on Reddit figuring this stuff out,” says a fake customer in an imagined quote in the document. “It’s like the store finally knows what it’s selling.”
In its statement to ​Reuters, Amazon, referring to the PR/FAQ, said, "the usage figures are significantly ​outdated" and that its data shows that Alexa for Shopping ⁠is roughly 97% accurate globally.
Battling agents
World Product Graph would help serve at least one other important function — staving off the growing threat of alternative AI shopping agents, the people said. CEO Andy Jassy sought during the company's third-quarter earnings call to downplay agents' impact, saying “few customers are doing much shopping this way yet” and that Amazon’s advertising business has been minimally impacted.
Yet Amazon executives have grown wary of AI shopping agents that may ​send customer traffic to other sites that have greater or more complete data, according to people familiar with the matter.
Meta’s Muse agent, for instance, has proven popular with customers already, garnering more than 10 million ​users in the US and Canada ⁠since launching in September. Amazon in the same month blocked Muse from its retail site and last year sued AI firm Perplexity to prevent similar access, a case that is still ongoing.
Jassy said Alexa for Shopping has been used by over 400 million people in the past year.
Muse, however, "has the potential to become the most widely used consumer AI application since ChatGPT,” JPMorgan said in a research note. Responding to a post saying xAI's Grok agent was blocked on Amazon, Elon Musk wrote on X last month: “Maybe we should start a competitor to Amazon."
By creating the world's most extensive storehouse of product data, ⁠Amazon could ensure AI ​agents working on behalf of shoppers will be compelled to seek products out on Amazon.com and not other retailers’ sites, the people said. That would also help protect ​Amazon’s growing advertising business.
Employees have described World Product Graph as the beginnings of an effort to make the site a one-stop shop for buying anything imaginable, an expansion of existing services known as “Buy for Me” and “Shop Direct,” which list on Amazon products sold on other sites, allowing customers to buy them with Amazon as an intermediary.
“Customers have always been ​able to find products on Amazon,” Tekiela said in the document. “What’s been missing is understanding – how do these products relate to each other, which one is right for me, and what else should I consider?”
