items.title: Legislature cannot be 'bypassed', minister says on question of referendum on new provinces
items.summary:
Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said on Friday that Parliament and the provincial assemblies could not be "bypassed or negated" on the question of making new provinces through a referendum to determine the public will.
The remarks come in the wake of Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi's renewed call a day earlier for a referendum on the creation of new provinces, saying the people should have the final say on the matter, while making it clear that no such initiative would move forward without the consent of all allied parties in the ruling coalition.
Speaking on a private television programme, Naya Pakistan, Chaudhry stated the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) believed that the creation of new provinces required a “national consensus”, which could only be achieved through the involvement and agreement of all political parties.
Read: Naqvi pitches referendum on new provinces
The minister emphasised that there was a method in the Constitution
items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said on Friday that Parliament and the provincial assemblies could not be "bypassed or negated" on the question of making new provinces through a referendum to determine the public will.
The remarks come in the wake of Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi's renewed call a day earlier for a referendum on the creation of new provinces, saying the people should have the final say on the matter, while making it clear that no such initiative would move forward without the consent of all allied parties in the ruling coalition.
Speaking on a private television programme, Naya Pakistan, Chaudhry stated the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) believed that the creation of new provinces required a “national consensus”, which could only be achieved through the involvement and agreement of all political parties.
Read: Naqvi pitches referendum on new provinces
The minister emphasised that there was a method in the Constitution for the creation of new provinces, noting that legal stipulations mandated a role for the assemblies. "Accordingly, the role of the provincial assemblies cannot be bypassed and negated. This is not appropriate."
نئے صوبوں یا انتظامی یونٹس کا معاملہ پارلیمنٹ میں لایا جائے، تمام سیاسی جماعتیں اس پر بحث کریں
نئے صوبوں کے معاملے پر نیشنل ڈائیلاگ اور سیاسی جماعتوں کا اتفاقِ رائے ناگزیر ہے
پارلیمنٹ میں بحث، جماعتوں کی مشاورت اور کابینہ میں غور کے بعد نئے صوبوں کے معاملے پر پیش رفت ہونی چاہیے… pic.twitter.com/n0xm2DS99K
— Dr. Tariq Fazal Ch. (@DrTariqFazal) November 13, 2026
The minister reiterated that the party’s official position was that the Parliament, where all political parties were represented, was the most appropriate forum for building national consensus in relation to the question of creating new provinces.
"Even if you want to bypass the role of the Parliament and provincial assemblies in this matter, then there should be a method for that as well. It cannot happen simply through verbal statements," the minister stressed.
Chaudhry remarked that if the view of the public emerged through the referendum in favour of new provinces, then those sitting in Parliament would consider the will of the majority, as they were the representatives of the people.
نئے صوبوں یا انتظامی یونٹس کے معاملے پر مسلم لیگ ن کی قیادت میں تاحال باضابطہ بحث نہیں ہوئی
معاملہ پارٹی کے متعلقہ فورمز پر آئے گا تو اس پر بحث اور مؤقف دیا جائے گا
وفاقی وزراء نئے صوبوں/ انتظامی یونٹس اور گورننس میں بہتری سے متعلق اپنی آرا دے رہے ہیں
ملک کے نظام میں موجود… pic.twitter.com/96RjAdBqHn
— Dr. Tariq Fazal Ch. (@DrTariqFazal) November 13, 2026
Referring to the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), Chaudhry implored the party to set aside "political differences" and come to the table and debate the issue.
"The issue should be taken up and debated in parliament and the cabinet, as well as discussed within and among political parties, so that a political consensus can be forged," he stated.
Background of debate over new provinces
The current debate over new provinces began on July 30, when Naqvi called for additional administrative units or provinces as part of a broader overhaul of the country’s governance system. Naqvi argued that meaningful structural reforms were needed to improve governance, deliver justice and create opportunities for young people.
Read More: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi calls for new administrative units citing existing governance failure
The proposal quickly became politically sensitive in Sindh, where the PPP strongly opposed any move to divide the province. Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah rejected Naqvi’s assessment that the governance system had collapsed and called the proposal outdated, warning that no bloodshed would be allowed over the creation of new provinces.
The debate widened in August when Muttahida Qaumi Movement–Pakistan (MQM-P) backed the creation of new provinces and called for a national dialogue with political parties. The party argued that Pakistan’s growing population, poor governance and concentration of political power made greater administrative devolution necessary. The move put the party, which is part of the federal coalition but sits in opposition in Sindh, at odds with the PPP’s position on the province.
The PPP, meanwhile, maintained that administrative reform and the division of Sindh were separate questions. Sindh minister Nasir Hussain Shah said the provincial government was willing to discuss measures to improve governance and devolve power, but rejected linking those reforms to the creation of a new province.
The dispute reached the Sindh Assembly at the beginning of September. On September 3, the house unanimously passed a resolution rejecting any proposal to divide Sindh or alter its territorial limits. The resolution described Sindh as a “historic, civilisational and constitutional entity” and declared that “Sindh is one and shall remain one”.
Naqvi, however, showed no sign of backing away. On September 5, he said he would continue to support new provinces regardless of whether he remained in office, arguing that the ultimate decision should belong to the people rather than politicians or governments. He said the public should first be told the “pros and cons” of creating new administrative units before being allowed to decide.
Also Read: Naqvi vows not to back down from demand for new provinces, says decision must reflect public will
That position has since raised another question over how public opinion could be formally established. A constitutional debate emerged over whether a referendum could be used to gauge support for new provinces. Article 48(6) allows a matter of national importance to be put to a referendum following approval by a joint sitting of Parliament, although a referendum itself would not create a new province; any change to provincial boundaries would still have to follow the constitutional process.
PTI Barrister Gohar Ali Khan warned on September 7 that dividing Sindh or any other province without the consent of its people and representatives would weaken the federation. He called for a commission and extensive deliberations before the issue was taken to parliament.
Also Read: PTI's Barrister Gohar warns against dividing provinces without broad public consensus
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, while accepting that Sindh had the right to take its own position, also said a final decision would have to emerge through consensus. Asif separately suggested that Islamabad could be used as a starting point for any future administrative restructuring, while Prime Minister’s Adviser Rana Sanaullah said the question of new provinces should be taken up at the relevant forums and resolved through consensus among political parties.

items.title: NPCI to Introduce UPI Vyapaar Saksham Scheme to Offer Incentives to Small Merchants, Aims to Promote Acceptance
items.summary: The UPI Vyapaar Saksham Scheme could be launched soon by NPCI, as a leaked memo has surfaced online. The scheme aims to expand the acceptance of the digital payments interface, facilitate the onboarding of new merchants, and to grow the number of UPI transactions. The scheme will focus on Tier 3 to Tier 6 centres, North-Eastern states, and the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. The UPI Vyapaar Saksham Scheme might have a sunset period of three years from the date of implementation of the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) charges, which was earlier expected to come into effect after Diwali. Coming to the incentive structure, NPCI is said to offer an incentive of 0.03 percent of the aggregate value of eligible transactions to small merchants. Meanwhile, shopkeepers and other merchants located in “Targeted Geographies” will receive a 50 percent additional incentive on the base rate.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Honor has officially announced that the Honor 700 series will launch in China on November 23. The upcoming lineup will include three models: the Honor 700, Honor 700 Pro, and Honor 700S. The launch event will take place in Wuhan at 2:30 PM local time.
Honor CEO Li Jian confirmed the launch date through an official announcement. The company has also introduced actress and singer Ju Jingyi as the brand ambassador for the new series. Reservations for all three smartphones are already open in China through platforms such as JD.com.
Honor 700 Series Launch Date Officially Confirmed for November 23
Honor previously showcased the three smartphones during a media briefing in Beijing on November 12. The company described the lineup as its strongest digital series so far, highlighting several upgrades in battery technology, photography, and artificial intelligence.
All three models will feature a 9,000mAh Qinghai Lake battery and an AI-powered rear display. They will also support 4K cinematic Live Photos, bringing improved photography features to the lineup.
Honor has confirmed that the Honor 700 and Honor 700 Pro will use Snapdragon 8-series flagship processors. Earlier reports suggest that the standard Honor 700 could feature the Snapdragon 8s Gen 4, while the Pro model may come with the more powerful Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 chipset.
A recent Geekbench listing also revealed some details about the Honor 700 Pro. The phone appeared with the Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 processor, 16GB of RAM, and Android 17. However, Honor has not yet confirmed the exact processor used in the Honor 700S.
See Also: Honor Is Reportedly Testing Wide-Screen Smartphone With 8,000mAh Battery
200MP Cameras and Telephoto Support
Camera performance will be another major highlight of the Honor 700 series. All three smartphones will feature a 200-megapixel main camera.
The Honor 700 and Honor 700 Pro will also include a 50-megapixel periscope telephoto camera with 3.5x optical zoom. Both models will support Honor’s G200 telephoto extender, an additional accessory that weighs 88 grams and is designed to improve long-range photography.
The lineup will also feature Honor’s third-generation C3 RF chip, which is expected to improve signal performance.
Colours and Expected Pricing
Honor has already listed four color options for the upcoming smartphones: Clear Sky, Pink Mist, Cold White, and Blue Tone.
Although reservations are underway, the company has not announced official prices or released the complete specifications of the three devices. More details are expected during the November 23 launch event.
With a large 9,000mAh battery, 200-megapixel cameras, Snapdragon processors, and an AI-powered rear display, the Honor 700 series is shaping up to be an interesting addition to the company’s smartphone lineup.

The commission issued the direction in an order passed on November 10 by a five-member bench headed by Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja, while hearing a case regarding the delay in holding local government elections in 42 cantonment boards across the country.

items.content:
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has given the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) a fortnight to submit the federal government’s formal written request for local government elections in cantonment boards, warning that it would be constrained to pass appropriate orders in case of no response.
The commission issued the direction in an order passed on November 10 by a five-member bench headed by Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja, while hearing a case regarding the delay in holding local government elections in 42 cantonment boards across the country.
It is noteworthy to mention that the terms of the local governments in the cantonment boards expired on April 11, 2026. Under Section 219(4) of the Elections Act, 2017, the ECP is required to hold local government elections within 120 days of the expiry of their terms. Accordingly, the polls were due by August 8.
Read: 'Unnatural' cantt delimitation challenged
The ECP had issued a schedule for delimitation of wards in all 42 cantonment boards on January 11, with the final delimitation list published on April 20, according to the order.
It said that a consultative meeting was held on April 15 with the additional secretary of the Ministry of Defence and the director general of the Military Lands and Cantonments Department (ML&CD) to discuss the election schedule and obtain the federal government’s formal request under Section 19-D(2) of the Cantonments Act, 1924.
During the meeting, the commission directed the defence ministry to initiate the requisite summary for obtaining the federal government’s written request and forward it to the ECP.
The commission subsequently wrote to the defence secretary on May 14 and June 16, followed by a reminder on June 3, seeking the required document. Chief Election Commissioner Raja also wrote to the prime minister on July 16, requesting his intervention to ensure the submission of the formal request.
However, despite repeated correspondence, the federal government did not furnish the document, prompting the ECP to take up the matter on July 21.
During the proceedings, representatives of the Ministry of Defence and ML&CD expressed their readiness to facilitate the elections. The commission directed them to pursue the matter with the PMO and apprise it of the progress.
The ECP continued to seek updates through letters and reminders issued between July 31 and October 9, but the required formal request remained pending.
Read More: No caretaker yet for cantonment boards
At a hearing on October 28, the legal adviser representing the respondents sought a two-week adjournment, citing the senior leadership’s engagement in important national and international affairs. The commission accepted the request and fixed the next hearing for November 10.
At Tuesday’s hearing, Falak Naaz, legal adviser to the Ministry of Defence, appeared alongside ML&CD Additional Director General Khalil Ahmad Rana. They told the commission that the defence ministry was ready to hold the elections, but the matter remained pending with the PMO.
The legal adviser said the ministry had already forwarded the requisite request to the federal government for further consideration and that there had been no delay on its part. However, no response had been received from the federal government.
He sought further time to pursue the matter and obtain the required response.
Meanwhile, the special secretary (policy) informed the commission that all necessary preparations and arrangements for holding the elections had been completed and requested it to pass an appropriate order.
After hearing the arguments and examining the record, the ECP observed that it had made all possible efforts through correspondence, reminders, meetings and hearings, but the federal government had yet to fulfil the requirement under Section 19-D(2) of the Cantonments Act.
The commission noted that both the ECP and the Ministry of Defence were ready to conduct the elections, while ministry representatives had confirmed that the matter was pending with the PMO.
It further observed that Articles 140-A and 219(d) of the Constitution, read with Section 219 of the Elections Act, 2017, placed an obligation on the ECP to hold local government elections in the provinces, Islamabad Capital Territory and cantonment boards.
To fulfil its constitutional mandate, the commission directed its office to once again approach the PMO through a formal letter, seeking submission of the federal government’s written request within a fortnight.
Read More: Cantt delimitation row deepens
It warned that if no response was received within the stipulated period, the commission would be constrained to pass appropriate orders.
The Military Lands & Cantonments Department dissolved all 44 cantonment boards — including those in Rawalpindi, Lahore and Karachi — on November 11, 2025, upon completion of their four-year tenure, issuing written directives to all Regional Directors of MLC to establish a caretaker set-up through the respective CEOs by November 26, 2025.
Cantonments are permanent bases of the Pakistan Armed Forces, which are administered by Cantonment Boards under the control of the MLC. Cantonments are established under and governed by the Cantonments Act 1924. In recent times, the demographic character of most independence-era cantonments has changed.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Samsung has been experimenting with different smartphone form factors for quite some time, and it appears that the South Korean tech giant could be working on another interesting device. A newly surfaced patent suggests that Samsung is exploring a vertically expandable smartphone that could offer users the flexibility to switch between two different screen sizes.
Unlike conventional foldable smartphones, the proposed device would feature a display that extends vertically, offering a larger viewing area without significantly increasing the width of the handset.
Samsung’s Expandable Smartphone Could Offer Two Display Formats
According to recent reports, Samsung’s proposed smartphone design could allow users to switch between 16:9 and 21:9 display aspect ratios.
In its compact form, the device would feature a relatively shorter display with a 16:9 aspect ratio. However, users could extend the screen vertically to achieve a taller 21:9 format, offering additional screen space for browsing, scrolling through social media, and multitasking.
The design could also make the smartphone more convenient to carry, as users would be able to reduce its overall size when the additional screen space is not required.
Interestingly, the concept differs from Samsung’s existing Galaxy Z Fold and Galaxy Z Flip smartphones, which rely on hinges to fold and unfold their displays.
Samsung Continues to Explore New Smartphone Designs
Samsung has already established itself as one of the leading players in the foldable smartphone market. However, the company appears to be looking beyond traditional foldable devices as it continues to explore new display technologies. As previously reported by PhoneWorld, Samsung’s rollable phone plans are taking shape, although several questions remain about the potential device.
The vertically expandable design could offer a different approach to making smartphones more compact while retaining the benefits of a large display. It could also appeal to users who prefer taller screens without having to carry a larger smartphone at all times.
However, developing such a device could present several challenges, particularly when it comes to display durability, dust protection, battery capacity, and the reliability of the expansion mechanism.
It will also be interesting to see how Samsung optimizes its One UI software for a smartphone that can dynamically switch between two different display formats.
Other manufacturers are also exploring flexible display designs. For instance, the Honor Magic V6 has been among the devices highlighting continued competition in the foldable segment.
Will Samsung Launch an Expandable Smartphone in Pakistan?
For now, the vertically expandable smartphone remains a patent concept, and Samsung has not officially announced any plans to launch a commercial device based on the design.
Therefore, details regarding its specifications, price, and release timeline remain unknown. There is also no confirmation regarding its potential availability in Pakistan.
Nevertheless, considering Samsung’s continued investment in flexible display technology, the latest patent offers an interesting glimpse into what the company’s future smartphones could look like.
If the concept eventually makes its way to the market, it could introduce another alternative to conventional and foldable smartphones, further expanding the options available to consumers.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
Over six months after Rishi Gupta stepped down from his role as CEO of Fino Payments Bank, the fintech company is now set to get a new managing director (MD) and CEO. Today, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) approved the appointment of ICICI Bank veteran Pratap Singh as its new MD and CEO for 3 years.
Singh is set to take charge by November 27.
“The board of directors of the bank shall take necessary steps for his appointment, which will be subject to approval of shareholders of the bank. The bank will be intimate to the stock exchanges when Pratap Singh formally takes charge as the MD & CEO of the bank,” Fino said.
The new CEO brings over 29 years of experience across the banking sector in India and the UK. He has held leadership positions at ICICI Bank India, ICICI Bank UK and SBI UK.
At ICICI Bank UK, he served as head of retail and SME banking for the UK and Europe, and has expertise spanning retail and SME banking, liabilities, digital transformation and branch-led profitability.
The leadership change follows a turbulent year for Fino. Gupta, the company’s former CEO was arrested in February 2026 in connection with an investigation into alleged GST evasion of over ₹840 Cr linked to online betting platforms. Subsequently, Gupta requested for a voluntary early retirement, beginning May 21.
Since then, the bank’s CFO, Ketan Merchant, took charge as interim CEO in May and has held the position since. Fino’s head of finance, investor relations and analytics Anup Aggarwal stepped up to fill in the interim CFO role.
The leadership transition also comes at a time when Fino is bidding to convert to a small finance bank (SFB). Since receiving an ‘in-principle’ from the RBI to convert to an SFB back in December 2025.
However, it must be noted that the RBI has given an 18-month window to complete the transition and meet the net-worth requirement of ₹300 Cr. Despite recent regulatory scrutiny and an investigation involving its CEO, the bank stated it remains on track to finish the process within the stipulated timeline.
Amid all this, Fino’s financial and stock performance has taken a considerable hit.
On the financial front, Fino reported a net loss of ₹20.9 Cr in Q2 FY27, against a net profit of ₹15.4 Cr in the year-ago quarter, marking its second consecutive quarterly loss. At the same time, its total income declined 16.6% YoY to ₹333.6 Cr.
Operationally, Fino reported mixed business performance for the month of October 2026. The company’s transaction throughput declined 18% YoY to ₹3,541 Cr, while the number of deposit accounts opened fell 19% to 2.3 Lakh.
Average total deposits rose 9% to ₹2,886 Cr, while digitally active customers increased 12% to 65.1 Lakh. CMS throughput grew 12% to ₹7,514 Cr. Loan referral disbursals surged 316% to ₹301 Cr. However, the bank’s total deposits crossed ₹3,000 Cr for the first time, peaking at ₹3,044 Cr during the month.
The company’s shares have plunged close to 50% on a year to date (YTD) basis. Fino’s shares closed today’s trading session 2% higher at 129.95 apiece on the BSE.
The post Fino Payments Bank Gets New MD & CEO appeared first on Inc42 Media.

Xiaomi appears to be preparing its next-generation Redmi Note 18 series, even though the Redmi Note 17 lineup launched only a few months ago. A new Redmi smartphone has now appeared on China’s 3C certification website, revealing its charging speed ahead of its expected launch.
Tipster Digital Chat Station shared a screenshot on Weibo showing a Xiaomi device with the model number M841EE. According to the certification listing, the phone supports 67W wired fast charging.
The tipster believes the device belongs to the upcoming Redmi Note 18 series. However, the listing does not confirm its commercial name or whether it will launch as a standard, Pro, or Pro Max model.
Redmi Note 18 Series Appears Online with 67W Fast Charging Support
Digital Chat Station also revealed that three Redmi Note 18 series devices have received certification so far. Although their identities remain unknown, the M841EE model could be the Redmi Note 18 Pro.
This possibility comes from the fact that its predecessor, the Redmi Note 17 Pro, also offered 67W wired charging. Xiaomi may continue with the same charging speed for the upcoming model.
Redmi Note 18 Pro Max May Feature a 10,000mAh Battery
Apart from the certification details, the tipster has shared an early detail about the top-end Redmi Note 18 Pro Max. The device is reportedly being developed with a massive 10,000mAh battery.

For now, Xiaomi has not shared an official launch date or confirmed the specifications of the Redmi Note 18 series. More details are expected to emerge as the devices move closer to launch.

items.title: Apple Adjusts Trade-In Values in India and Adds Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 7 to the List
items.summary: Apple's online store in India has been updated to reflect the adjusted trade-in values for iPhone models. While buying a new Apple device, customers can trade in their older iPhone 17 for up to Rs. 54,000. Meanwhile, the iPhone 15 Plus can be traded in for up to Rs. 33,000. These values reflect the trade-in value of handsets in “Good” condition. Damaged devices could receive a lower trade-in value from the tech giant. Apart from this, Apple has added various Samsung foldables to the list of devices eligible for trade-in. Customers can get up to Rs. 63,000 for the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 7. The list has been updated to include the Galaxy Z Fold 4, Galaxy Z Fold 3 5G, Galaxy Z Fold 2 5G, and the first-generation Galaxy Z Fold, with a maximum trade-in value of Rs. 21,000, Rs. 14,000, Rs. 12,500, and Rs. 9,000, respectively.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) has directed licensed telecom operators to stop supplying internet bandwidth and related services to unlicensed internet service providers and distributors. The move aims to strengthen regulatory compliance and prevent unauthorised businesses from offering internet services in Pakistan.
The regulator reiterated these instructions during a meeting at PTA headquarters with representatives of licensed Long Distance International (LDI), Fixed Local Loop (FLL) and Class Value Added Services (CVAS) operators.
PTA Restricts Telecom Operators from Providing Internet Bandwidth to Unlicensed Providers
During the meeting, PTA clarified that LDI and FLL license holders can provide internet bandwidth, including configured internet packages, only to operators holding valid PTA licences. They cannot supply IP bandwidth, panel services, E1 connections, Domestic Private Leased Circuits (DPLCs) or similar services to unlicensed entities and distributors.
The authority stressed that all internet service providers must operate within the country’s existing licensing framework. This requirement will help ensure that internet services reach customers through authorised businesses rather than unregistered service providers.
PTA Highlights District Class Licence Framework
The meeting also discussed the District Class Licence framework, which allows Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA)-licensed cable operators and last-mile service providers to obtain internet bandwidth from FLL licensees.
Under this arrangement, eligible cable operators and service providers can legally acquire bandwidth and offer internet connectivity after meeting the relevant licensing requirements.
PTA also clarified the rules regarding billing for internet services. Bills and payment receipts must come from the relevant FLL or Class Licensee, depending on the applicable licensing arrangement.
The regulator said the instructions are intended to improve transparency and ensure that internet services are delivered through properly authorised operators.
The latest directions reinforce PTA’s efforts to bring internet service distribution under regulatory control and ensure that telecom companies follow the conditions of their licences. They also clarify which businesses can legally purchase bandwidth and provide internet services to customers in Pakistan.

Eight Nigerian startups have each won NGN5 million (US$4,000) in non-dilutive funding at the pitch day of the Founders Programme run by the Federal Ministry of Youth Development (FMYD), through the Nigerian Youth Academy (NiYA), and Cascador.
The pilot programme drew more than 19,000 applications after launching on International Youth Day in August, with 17 founders from 13 states selected for a four-week accelerator. Participating startups are tackling challenges such as post-harvest losses, malnutrition, waste, vaccine cold chains, clean energy and digital education.
Implemented by technical partner Sapphital, the programme offered training in sales, customer service and investment readiness, as well as regulatory sessions with agencies including NEXIM Bank, SEC, NITDA, NAFDAC and the Nigeria Data Protection Commission.

All graduates keep NiYA alumni status and priority for future opportunities. The academy aims to train 7 million young Nigerians within two years.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
The Karnataka High Court (HC) has rejected a plea by Razorpay cofounders Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar seeking to quash a serious fraud investigation office (SFIO) complaint. The complaint pertains to alleged lapses in merchant onboarding and monitoring of transactions linked to a digital lending company accused of predatory recovery practices.
In a similar matter concerning alleged transactions linked to an illegal digital lending operation, the Karnataka High Court had quashed money-laundering proceedings initiated by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) against Razorpay, observing that there was no prima facie material to establish that the company had knowingly facilitated the transfer of proceeds of crime.
Responding to Inc42’s query, the company said, “This matter pertains to a case from five years ago involving loan apps that operated illegally through multiple payment gateways and banks in India. Razorpay and its directors have no association with these entities. We have full faith in the judicial process and will pursue all appropriate legal remedies. Compliance and good governance remain central to how Razorpay operates, and the company continues to serve its customers and partners with the same commitment.”
For context, in an order dated November 4, Justice M Nagaprasanna held that the allegations against the cofounders involved disputed questions of fact that could only be examined during trial. The court said there was no reason to interfere with the proceedings at this stage, given the matter was still at a nascent stage.
The SFIO has named Razorpay’s whole-time director Mathur and managing director Kumar as accused in the complaint. The allegations concern deficiencies in merchant onboarding, lapses in know-your-customer (KYC) verification of Mad Elephant Network Technology Pvt Ltd (MENTPL), and inadequate due diligence and monitoring of its transactions.
The SFIO is investigating a network of 33 companies allegedly created through dummy directors by Jilian Consultants India Pvt Ltd (JCIPL), a subsidiary of Fininty Pvt Ltd.
One of the companies under investigation, Mad Elephant Network Technology Pvt Ltd (MENTPL), allegedly operated an illegal digital lending business through its arrangement with NBFC X10 Financial Services Ltd.
MENTPL allegedly employed unethical, predatory and coercive loan recovery practices and generated wrongful gains of ₹56.63 Cr.
Where Does Razorpay Fit Into This?
The agency alleged that Razorpay acted as a payment intermediary for MENTPL. During the proceedings, the Additional Solicitor General of India, representing the SFIO, told the court that Razorpay had acted as a conduit for approximately ₹320 Cr worth of MENTPL’s transactions.
Hence, Razorpay cofounders were accused of failing to exercise due care, skill and diligence and independent judgement as directors, attracting provisions under Section 166 of the Companies Act, 2013.
Against this, the company argued that the SFIO had exceeded its jurisdiction by prosecuting them when Razorpay was not among the 33 companies named in the Central government’s 2022 investigation order.
They also contended that payment aggregators did not have a statutory obligation to undertake full KYC verification, which they argued was the responsibility of banks. Mathur had told investigators in a statement recorded on August 16, 2023, that RBI guidelines were still evolving and the onus of conducting full KYC did not rest with the executives.
The cofounders further argued that mere negligence in merchant onboarding could not constitute a criminal offence. They also challenged the proceedings on grounds of limitation, absence of mens rea and lack of any direct nexus with MENTPL. They contended that there was no basis for imposing criminal liability on Razorpay’s directors when the company itself had not been made an accused.
Rejecting the argument, the court referred to Section 212(14) of the Companies Act, which allows prosecution of not only the company under investigation and its officers but also any other person directly or indirectly connected with its affairs.
It observed that whether the executives had discharged their fiduciary duties and exercised adequate due diligence, particularly in transactions involving approximately ₹320 Cr, were questions that required examination during trial.
The court also said Razorpay’s role could emerge as the proceedings progress, despite the company not currently being named as an accused in the complaint.
The court also reiterated that it could not conduct a mini-trial while exercising its powers to quash criminal proceedings.
Consequently, the High Court dismissed the writ petition, allowing the proceedings against Mathur and Kumar to continue.
The court proceedings come as the fintech major prepares to go public. Razorpay has received the final nod from SEBI for its proposed ₹5,000-6,000 Cr IPO, which is expected to value the company at around $5 Bn.
The company pre-filed for an IPO earlier this year and is said to be eyeing a listing between January and March 2027, with the IPO expected to comprise a fresh issue and an offer-for-sale (OFS). More details on the company’s float would become more apparent when the company files its updated draft red herring prospectus.
Update | Nov 13, 15:45 | Story updated to include company statement.
The post Karnataka HC Examines Allegations In SFIO Case Involving Razorpay appeared first on Inc42 Media.

He cautioned that adopting AI without integrating it into existing operations could increase costs and complexity rather than deliver business value.
The discussion also highlighted opportunities for Pakistan’s SME sector, particularly exporters, to benefit from digitalisation. Education and workforce development emerged as another central theme. Addressing Pakistan’s preparedness for AI adoption, Al Faifi emphasised the importance of continuous learning and digital literacy.
SAP reaffirmed its commitment to advancing education and skills development, highlighting that approximately 400,000 students have benefited from training through its global initiatives over the past five years.
In Pakistan, SAP continues to strengthen its engagement with key public-sector stakeholders, including the Higher Education Commission (HEC), the Ministry of Information Technology and the Government of Pakistan, with further opportunities for collaboration and potential developments.
The roundtable concluded with a focus on strengthening Pakistan’s digital foundations through education, infrastructure, cybersecurity and continuous skills development, positioning businesses and professionals to benefit from emerging technology opportunities.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
South African civic-fintech Jumpstarter Crowdfunding is helping entrepreneurs, creatives and social impact organisations raise seed funding directly from their communities through a reward-based, all-or-nothing crowdfunding model.
Founded in 2012 and operating as a registered non-profit company (NPC), Jumpstarter allows project creators to run campaigns of between one and 60 days, with funds only released if 100 per cent of the target is reached. If a campaign falls short, pledges are returned to backers and the creator pays no platform fees. Backers receive non-financial rewards such as pre-ordered products, experiences or project perks, rather than equity or debt.
“South Africa has over 2.5 million micro, small and medium enterprises, and the vast majority of them face an early-stage funding gap estimated at between ZAR80 billion (US$4.8 billion) and ZAR100 billion (US$6 billion),” co-founder and chief operations officer Derek Whitehead told Disrupt Africa.
“Commercial banks demand collateral and historical balance sheets that grassroots innovators simply don’t have, while venture capital is concentrated in late-stage or hyper-scalable tech. Global platforms like Kickstarter and Indiegogo, meanwhile, lack native rand payment rails and add foreign exchange friction.”
Jumpstarter is led by Whitehead alongside co-founder and director Yaseen Kriel and director Zaid Kriel, supported by a network of advisers, digital marketing contributors and technology partners. The platform runs on Amazon Web Services (AWS) infrastructure, is managed via Salesforce CRM, and pairs campaigns with digital marketing support funded through a US$10,000-per-month Google Ad Grant.
That marketing support is central to how the startup differentiates itself from local rivals such as Thundafund, BackaBuddy and Uprise Africa.
“Unlike platforms that function purely as passive software directories, Jumpstarter acts as an active launchpad,” Whitehead said. “Our all-or-nothing model protects backer capital, our non-profit charter lets us charge lower fees, and we actively subsidise creator outreach through our Google Ad Grant.”
The model appears to be gaining traction. Jumpstarter has facilitated more than ZAR1.34 million (US$80,000) in community-backed capital across over 36 successfully funded campaigns, spanning food and beverage, creative arts, software, publishing, green-tech and community development. Notable campaigns include helping Cape Town’s Charly’s Bakery survive lockdown disruptions and backing the commercial launch of the Pirate Masters card game.
“Campaigns that engage our structured preparation and ad-subsidisation workflows regularly achieve between 100 and 108 per cent of their targets,” Whitehead said.
Jumpstarter charges a seven per cent fee on successful for-profit campaigns and five per cent for registered NPOs and schools, with third-party payment gateways PayGate and SnapScan deducting additional processing fees. As a non-profit, all surplus revenue is reinvested into infrastructure, campaign support tools and community pilot programmes. The organisation is self-sustaining, with operations also subsidised through partnerships with AWS, Salesforce.org and Google.
The startup was recently selected for the CATAPULT: Inclusion Africa 2026 cohort run by the Luxembourg House of Financial Technology (LHoFT), and while its operations are currently focused on South Africa, it accepts pledges from backers globally, including diaspora communities. It plans to expand its infrastructure and mobile money integrations into markets such as Kenya and Nigeria within the next 24 to 36 months.
The biggest challenge, Whitehead said, has been overcoming the “cold-start” problem faced by first-time creators.
“Many entrepreneurs mistake crowdfunding for a passive lottery, assuming that publishing a campaign will automatically bring in traffic. In reality, crowdfunding amplifies pre-existing momentum. Projects must rally their first 20 to 30 per cent from their immediate networks within 48 hours to trigger the social proof needed for broader discovery,” he said.
“Because unreached goals generate zero revenue for us, educating creators on narrative clarity, realistic budgeting and early community mobilisation remains our most hands-on task.”
The startup is also working to reduce checkout friction on mobile by integrating lower-friction payment options such as PayShap and instant EFT.

Zong, has won the Operational Excellence Leader award for Innovation at The Fast Mode Awards 2026, for its AI-driven Self-Intelligent RAN Optimization Platform. Marking its second international recognition this year for AI-driven innovation, these accolades underscore a significant milestone in Zong’s advancement towards intelligent, AI-enabled network operations and highlight the strength of its home-grown engineering capabilities in developing world-class technology solutions – further emphasizing Zong’s leading position of network operations and technology innovation in Pakistan.
Developed in-house, the platform marks Pakistan’s first deployment of Level 4 autonomous network operations on a live commercial network, representing a significant advancement in intelligent network management. Aligned with Zong’s AI Enablement strategy, the platform autonomously detects congestion, execute corrective actions, and validates outcomes through an intelligent closed-loop mechanism. By transforming traditionally manual, multi-day optimization processes into automated, AI-driven operations, it enhances operational agility, optimizes network performance, and establishes a scalable foundation for more consistent and reliable customer experiences nationwide.
Commenting on the achievement, Zong’s Chief Technology Officer, Mao Weiliang, said:
“At Zong, we see AI and advanced technologies as fundamental to our technology leadership and the evolution of next-generation intelligent networks. Through our Self-Intelligent RAN Optimization Platform, we are taking AI beyond monitoring and recommendations to autonomous decision-making and execution, transforming network operations. Developed in-house, this innovation reflects our ability to translate advanced AI into real-world operational impact, demonstrating that world-class technology can be conceived, developed and deployed in Pakistan. It also marks an important step towards fully autonomous, self-optimizing networks at scale, delivering greater operational intelligence, network efficiency and superior customer experiences.”
Through sustained investments in 5G, Artificial Intelligence and next-generation digital solutions, Zong continues to translate technological innovation into smarter networks, greater operational efficiency, and enhanced customer experiences. This achievement further reinforces its ambition to lead Pakistan’s transition towards a Digital and Intelligent Future, bringing its brand promise of “Aisa Hai Future” to life through innovation, intelligent connectivity, and transformative digital possibilities.

Vivo is reportedly working on three new flagship products that could expand its lineup beyond the upcoming X500 series. According to a new leak, vivo is developing a standalone pocket gimbal camera, a next-generation foldable smartphone, and a wide-screen flagship phone.
The information comes from tipster Digital Chat Station, who has shared some expected hardware details of the upcoming devices. While Vivo has not officially confirmed these products, the leak also suggests that the pocket gimbal camera could be the first to arrive.
Vivo May Soon Launch a New Foldable and Wide-Screen Flagship Alongside a Pocket Gimbal Camera
The standalone pocket gimbal camera is reportedly the closest product to launch, with an expected arrival around the end of 2026. Previous reports suggest that it could feature a 200MP Sony LYT-901 camera sensor.
Unlike Vivo’s smartphones, which use built-in gimbal stabilization for improved photography and video recording, the upcoming device will reportedly work as a separate camera. Vivo already has experience with this technology, having introduced micro gimbal stabilization with the Vivo X50 series.
A dedicated pocket camera could allow the company to offer advanced stabilization and camera features in a compact device.
New Vivo Foldable Could Feature Snapdragon Chip
The second device is a new book-style foldable smartphone. According to the tipster, the device is already ready and could bring several hardware improvements over previous models.
The upcoming foldable is reportedly powered by Qualcomm’s 2nm Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor. It is also expected to feature a wider inner display with no visible crease.
Another major highlight could be a 200MP camera with gimbal stabilization. However, the leak has not revealed the phone’s official name or expected launch date.
The reported processor would also mark a possible return to Qualcomm chips for Vivo’s X Fold lineup after the current generation adopted a MediaTek chipset.

Vivo Also Working on a Wide-Screen Flagship
The third device is a wide-screen smartphone that is reportedly progressing quickly through development. Unlike conventional smartphones, it could feature a custom 16:9 display with narrow bezels.
The phone is expected to use a flagship MediaTek Dimensity 9-series processor. Its camera setup could also include a 200MP sensor with a large sensor size, potentially making photography one of its key selling points.
The wider display could offer a different viewing experience compared to traditional smartphones, although details about its screen size and other specifications remain unknown.
Launch Details Remain Unconfirmed
These three products suggest that Vivo is exploring different flagship categories, including standalone cameras and alternative smartphone designs. The pocket gimbal camera could arrive by the end of 2026, while the foldable and wide-screen flagship may follow later.
For now, all three devices remain unconfirmed. Vivo has not shared official specifications, product names, or launch schedules. More details are expected to emerge through leaks and reports in the coming months.

items.title: Nigeria’s mobile lines cross 200m as data drives telco growth
items.summary:
Nigeria’s active mobile subscriber base has crossed the 200 million-line mark, as operators recover lost connections and increasingly compete for customers whose demand is shifting from traditional voice services to data.
Latest figures from the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) showed that active mobile subscriptions increased to 200.3 million in October from 195.11million in July, 2026 adding about 5.22million lines in three months.
Experts say the bigger opportunity is increasingly coming from how much data customers consume and the networks required to support that demand.
The increase was supported by major operators, although the market remains heavily concentrated around MTN Nigeria and Airtel Nigeria.
MTN crossed the 100 million subscriber threshold in July, with its active subscriptions rising from 98.64 million in June to 100.86 million.
Airtel Nigeria had 66.12 million subscribers, while Globacom accounted for 23.68 million and T2, formerly 9mobile, had 3.54 million.

items.content:
Ola Electric’s Revenue Dips In Q2
Ola Electric’s Q2 FY27 performance told a tale of two extremes. While revenues continued to decline and cash burn persisted, aggressive cost discipline helped narrow some of the losses. With supply chain woes worsening, did Ola Electric pay the price for its past mistakes in Q2?
Here is a quick look at Ola Electric’s Q2 FY27 numbers:
Operating revenue tanked 39% YoY to ₹421 Cr
Consolidated net loss narrowed 13% YoY to ₹362 Cr
Total expenses declined 28% YoY to ₹639 Cr
Operating EBITDA loss rose 7% YoY to ₹218 Cr, while gross margin tanked 100 bps YoY to 29.9%
Supply Woes Bite: The EV maker’s Q2 performance was defined by supply chain constraints, with component and charger bottlenecks restricting vehicle output and triggering a sharp sales decline. Despite weaker dispatches and rising commodity prices, aggressive cost reductions helped narrow net losses. That said, the management now plans to focus on ramping up supply chain and expects the output to improve to 25,000 in December
The Dealer-Led Pivot: The quarter also saw the EV maker halt orders from company-owned stores and pivoted towards the traditional dealer-led network. By transferring inventory and financing to external partners, Ola Electric aims to trim expenses and streamline working capital cycles. While the initial dealer payouts are expected to compress near-term margins, the company expects improvements in margins as retail velocity stabilises across the new outlets.
The Cash Question: All said and done, Ola Electric continues to report negative free cash flow during the quarter. While the company said that the gap was largely due to capex at the Gigafactory, it claims to have bolstered its cash reserves through fundraises and pared down legacy borrowings. It also expects changes to India’s GST refund mechanism to shorten refund cycles and free up working capital.
With much on its plate, here is how Ola Electric fared on the financial front in Q2…
From The Editor’s Desk
NVIDIA CEO Quits
Jensen Huang has resigned as the chief executive officer of the chipmaker, bringing the curtains down on his 33-year old tenure as the head of the company that he cofounded in 1993.
This follows revelations that he had two extramarital affairs, one of which involved a woman accused of spying for China.
According to the company’s board, Huang had stepped down as president, CEO and board member with immediate effect. Meanwhile, CFO Colette Kress will take over as the interim CEO of the company while the board searches for a new successor.
PlatinumRx Eyes $32 Mn
The online pharmacy startup is in talks to raise over ₹300 Cr in a round, which will likely be led by Belgium-based investment giant Sofina Ventures. The proposed transaction is expected to value the Bengaluru-based startup somewhere in the range of $150-200 Mn.
Founded in 2023, PlatinumRx operates an epharmacy that offers affordable alternatives to prescribed medicines. The startup, which claims to have served over 10 Lakh users to date, previously raised $6 Mn in its Series A round last year.
The development comes amid continued investor interest in specialised healthcare and pharmacy platforms. This is being driven by a combination of digital adoption, convenience and differentiated models around affordability, assortment and access.
OpenAI Deepens India Push
The ChatGPT maker has introduced local inference and data processing for its APIs in India. Initially available only for the GPT-6 Luna model, the service will enable API request processing and the model computation within India.
With this, OpenAI could be looking to leverage data residency as a key lever to scale enterprise deployments. This also makes India the third country globally, after Australia and Japan, where OpenAI has introduced API inference residency.
Separately, OpenAI has also launched a new beta offering to enable businesses to claim and manage their profiles on ChatGPT. It also allows merchants to add product feeds and access insights into how users discover and engage with them on the chatbot.
The New UPI Incentive Scheme
The National Payments Corporation of India has introduced a new initiative, called the UPI Vyapaar Saksham Scheme, to offer incentives to banks and merchants for deploying QR codes and soundboxes to further drive transaction growth.
The scheme will be funded through a portion of the merchant discount rate earned by banks and other UPI ecosystem participants. The scheme will run for a period of three years from the implementation of UPI MDR, which is yet to be notified.
Acquiring banks will receive ₹300 for every QR code and ₹750 for every soundbox deployed at an eligible new small merchant. Financial institutions will also be rewarded for growing UPI transaction volumes among its existing and new merchant cohorts.
Turtlemint’s Mixed Q2 Show
The insurtech company managed to slash its net loss by 67% YoY to ₹25.8 Cr in Q2 FY27 on the back of operating revenue rising 35% YoY to ₹342.2 Cr. However, expenses continued to pinch, rising 25% YoY to ₹375.2 Cr in the quarter under review.
On the operational front, platform premium zoomed 55% YoY to ₹1,214 Cr in Q2 FY27. The company also claimed that it added 69,000 new digital partners in H1 FY27.
On IRDAI’s draft framework that proposes lower commissions for agents, Turtlemint declined to share FY28 stress-case numbers and said it will do so once the final rules are out. However, it expects service EBITDA to hold flat in absolute terms next year.
Inc42 Markets
Inc42 Startup Spotlight
Can Maasi Take The Guesswork Out Of Hiring A Nanny?
For working parents, finding a nanny often means relying on neighbourhood referrals and WhatsApp groups. This leaves many with little clarity on a caregiver’s training, reliability and availability. Maasi wants to turn this informal market into a managed childcare service.
Maasi’s Caregiver Network: Founded in 2025, Maasi connects families with verified, trained caregivers for in-home childcare. Parents can book on-demand nannies starting at ₹199 an hour or choose monthly subscriptions starting at ₹5,999.
Trained Nannies For Kids: Maasi claims that every caregiver onboarded on its platform undergoes a 16-point psychometric assessment and a free training programme, formulated by pre-school directors and nurses. The startup also offers English-speaking governesses, which are trained in screen-free childcare activities.
Growing Traction: Maasi claims to have so far served over 1,200 parents through a network of 500-plus caregivers. Its October 2026 public launch drew a waitlist of over 4,000 parents within five days. Going forward, the startup plans to focus on caregiver recruitment, enhancing its tech stack and expansion in Bengaluru.
Its next challenge will be scaling quality and supply without diluting the trust it promises parents. So, can Maasi bring accountable childcare at the fingertips of parents?

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni
The Lagos State Taskforce has raided suspected criminal hideouts in Cele, Itire, Ilasamaja and other parts of the state, arresting three suspected drug peddlers in an operation aimed at curbing illicit drug activities and other forms of criminality.
The operation was led by the Chairman of the agency, Chief Superintendent of Police (CSP) Adetayo Akerele, who personally supervised the enforcement exercise across locations identified as hotspots for drug-related activities, public disturbances and other criminal tendencies.
During the operation at Itire, Akerele commended the whistleblower and residents for their vigilance and cooperation, saying public participation and timely intelligence-sharing were essential to identifying and dislodging criminal elements from communities.
The taskforce said the operation led to the arrest of three suspects allegedly involved in the sale and distribution of substances, including marijuana, Colorado and Indian hemp, to adults, underage persons and street urchins around Cele Bus Stop, Itire and Ilasamaja.
It added that the activities had reportedly contributed to public disturbances, street fights, cult-related activities, youth violence and other criminal tendencies in the affected communities.
The suspects were identified as Bello Musa, 18; Abubakar Musa, 27, both of No. 23, Adebayo Street, Cele-Ijesha; and Agboola Fuad, 24, of No. 4, Sewage Street, Abaranje, Ijegun, Lagos.
According to the agency, the suspects have been arraigned before a court on three counts bordering on possession and sale of illicit drugs, inciting members of the public against officers performing lawful duties, and conduct likely to cause a breach of the peace.
They all pleaded not guilty to the charges, while the case was adjourned until December 9, 2026, for further proceedings.
Akerele reiterated that active citizen participation, alongside sustained enforcement operations by the taskforce and other relevant security and regulatory agencies, remained essential to maintaining public order, environmental sanitation and lasting peace across the state.
He warned that individuals found engaging in criminal activities or violating applicable environmental laws would be made to face the full weight of the law.
Speaking at the agency’s headquarters in Bolade, Oshodi, the taskforce chairman urged residents to take responsibility for the security of their communities by reporting suspicious activities and cooperating with law enforcement agencies.
He also cautioned young people against involvement in illicit drug activities, street violence and cultism, warning that such conduct could jeopardise their future and undermine the development of their communities.
Akerele further advised residents to be careful about their associations and avoid keeping company with individuals whose activities could expose them to criminality.
He said the Lagos State Government, through the taskforce, remained committed to its zero-tolerance stance against drug peddling, environmental nuisances and criminal activities as part of efforts to build a cleaner, safer and drug-free state.

items.title: Italy stun France 3-1 to hand Zidane first defeat as Les Bleus coach
items.summary:
Italy came from behind to beat France 3-1 in Milan and hand Zidane his first defeat since taking charge of Les Bleus.
France were without Kylian Mbappe and Ousmane Dembele due to injury but Michael Olise pounced on a loose pass from Gianluigi Donnarumma to fire them ahead on 10 minutes.
Francesco Pio Esposito steered in Nicolo Cambiaghi’s pass to bring Italy level before France twice hit the post through Bradley Barcola and Rayan Cherki.
Sebastiano Esposito blazed a second-half penalty wide for Italy, but Roberto Mancini’s side did not rue that miss as Davide Frattesi powered home Federico Dimarco’s cut-back.
Francesco Pio Esposito then doubled his tally for the night, succeeding where his older brother had failed by converting a penalty after Dayot Upamecano fouled substitute Antonio Vergara.
Italy climbed above France at the top of Group A1 on head-to-head record. Both teams have 10 points going into the final round of games, with Belgium just one point adrift.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Social media giant Meta has once again come under the radar of Indian authorities over alleged child sexual abuse material (CSAM) prevalent on Meta-owned platforms.
Now, National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) member Priyank Kanoongo has urged the women and child developement (WCD) ministry to look into the financial relationship between the social media giant and the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF).
Citing advocacy group Legal Rights Observatory, Kanoongo reportedly said that UNICEF is trying to offer its help to Indian authorities in the ongoing government probe into the child sexual abuse material (CSAM), sold as ads, on Meta platforms.
Speaking with news agency PTI, Kanoongo flagged that Meta has given ‘millions of dollars” to UNICEF and continues to fund the organisation. He argued that this financial relationship could create a conflict of interest, particularly because UNICEF is engaged in child-protection work while Meta faces allegations involving exploitative content on its platforms.
In a letter written to WCD secretary Anil Malik, he called for a probe into the financial ties between Meta and UNICEF. Kanoongo also raised concerns that UNICEF could end up serving Meta’s interests rather than supporting child protection. He also urged the government to ensure that Meta is not allowed to use UNICEF as a “shield to evade accountability”.
“Therefore, there is a concern that this organisation, which is supposed to work on the issue of child sexual exploitation material while receiving funding from Meta, might end up serving Meta’s interests. The activist group has expressed apprehension that this organisation could potentially work in favour of Meta’s interests,” Kanoongo reportedly said.
The NHRC member said that he has already brought the matter to the attention of the WCD ministry, external affairs ministry, home affairs ministry and the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre.
He also urged Indian authorities to keep the alleged conflict of interest in mind while conducting investigations and taking enforcement action. The concern, he claimed, was that allegations of vested interests being served through financial funding should not turn out to be true.
This comes a months after a BBC Eye documentary, aired in July, allegedly found that Instagram was running paid adverts promoting CSAM in India. As per Kanoongo, the NHRC has already identified about 100 such instances.
The aftermath saw the Centre pull up the social media giant and summon the company’s top leadership. The government also directed Meta to strengthen CSAM detection, increase human oversight of moderation and improve safeguards for content in Indian languages and local contexts.
Earlier reports suggested that government was considering waving off Meta’s “safe harbour” protection under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act, 2000. This could have potentially forced the company to face greater legal liability in cases of CSAM or other illegal content being posted on Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp.
Post this, the social media giant agreed to report instances of child sexual abuse to the local law enforcement agencies in September. Days later, Meta also said that it has introduced LLM-driven systems to identify “signposting” within ads to counter predators who advertise illicit material in ways that can evade automated detection.
The social media juggernaut also claims to have deployed AI-driven sweeps to uncover missed CSAM material and integrated “red-teaming” AI agents to strengthen detection mechanisms.

items.content:
Alex Baena scored from the spot and Marc Pubill added another seconds from time as Spain beat ten-men Czech Republic 2-0 in the Nations League in Prague on Thursday.
The win leaves Spain unbeaten in 44 competitive games in a row, including five wins in as many Nations League games this season.
Spain, who already secured a quarter-final berth before travelling to Prague, will face England in Madrid on Sunday in their final Group A3 game.
Baena scored on 39 minutes after a VAR check revealed Czech midfielder Lukas Ambros had handled the ball inside the box.
The Atletico Madrid winger blasted his spot kick past Matej Kovar who touched the ball but failed to clear it.
Czech captain Ladislav Krejci was sent off in the 69th minute after bringing down second-half substitute Roberto Fernandez on a counter-attack.
It was a deja-vu for the Wolverhampton defender who also got a red card at the end of Spain’s 3-1 home win over the Czechs last month.
Pubill, another substitute, beat Kovar with a low shot deep into stoppage time after the Czech back four left him alone facing the Eindhoven goalkeeper.
Luis de la Fuentes missed Lamine Yamal, Dani Olmo, Rodri and Eric Garcia over injuries while Mikel Oyarzabal was sidelined with flu for the Prague game.
Spain got off to a slow start on the chilly evening but never really let the hosts get close throughout the first half.
They gradually stepped up their pressure, often confining the Czechs to their box and looking for chances.
Fabian Ruiz hit the post with a curling right-footer three minutes from halftime, while Dean Huijsen’s header found Kovar’s arms.
Yeremy Pino, replacing Yamal on the right flank, saw his goal overturned by VAR for offside just two minutes into the second half.
The Czechs showed higher spirits after the break, but David Zima tipped the ball over the bar from close range on 50 minutes and Adam Hlozek’s glancing header landed on the top of the crossbar.
The Czechs lost momentum after the red card, but Baena had two efforts cleared by Kovar who also denied Fernandez from close range.
The hosts, led by de la Fuente’s long-time collaborator Santi Denia, have lost all their Nations League games this season.
They are next travelling to Croatia for a game they need to win to stay in the top tier of the competititon for the next edition.

items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
Harry Kane celebrated his record-breaking 126th England appearance with a goal from the penalty spot as England beat Croatia 2-1 on Thursday to book a place in the Nations League quarter-finals.
Slaven Bilic’s team were determined to avoid the embarrassment of their 7-0 mauling by England in Rijeka last month and looked much more solid from the kick-off.
But goals from Morgan Rogers and captain Kane kept England second in their group, confirming their place in the Nations League last eight in March.
Neither side got out of second gear in the opening stages of the match at Wembley.
Elliot Anderson fired over in the 16th minute and Croatia’s Josip Misic flashed a shot wide midway through the first half.
Chelsea forward Rogers broke the deadlock in the 24th minute in slightly fortuitous fashion following a neat move by the home side.
Kane floated a ball to Jude Bellingham on the right of the penalty area and the Real Madrid man cushioned the ball first time across the area towards Rogers.
Manchester City’s Josko Gvardiol had a chance to clear but got in a tangle and Chelsea’s Rogers poked the ball past goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic.
England started to find some rhythm as they went in search of a second goal but failed to add to their tally before half-time.
Thomas Tuchel’s men were again the more potent team at the beginning of the second period.
But the visitors levelled against the run of play just before the hour mark after a glaring error by England defender Jarell Quansah, who misdirected a header from close range towards Jordan Pickford following a Croatia corner.
The ball fell to Petar Sucic, who stabbed home.
Minutes later England were back in front, with Bayer Leverkusen defender Quansah again at the heart of the action after his shirt was tugged in the penalty area.
Referee Morten Krogh initially did not award a penalty but he was sent to the monitor by the VAR and pointed to the spot.
Kane made no mistake, drilling home for record-extending 92nd England goal.
Nikola Vlasic gave England a scare, firing just wide of Jordan Pickford’s goal as Croatia showed they were still alive.
James Garner thought he had scored a third for England after a Bellingham cut-back but Bellingham was in an off-side position when he received the ball.
Ballon d’Or winner Kane won his 126th cap when the game kicked off — taking him clear of his tie with former goalkeeper Peter Shilton.
A giant banner was raised before kick-off with a picture of the 33-year-old and the words “England’s Finest”.
Shilton was part of a pre-match presentation to honour the Three Lions skipper, along with Football Association patron Prince William.
England remain second in Nations League Group A3, after leaders Spain beat the Czech Republic 2-0 but are now assured of a place in the quarter-finals.
Spain and England face each other in Madrid on Sunday.

items.title: Online safety concerns are reshaping how people meet strangers

items.content:
It’s hard to ignore how meeting new people online has changed in the past decade. With so many platforms connecting millions, the possibilities feel endless, but the risks have become more visible too.
Stories about scams, harassment, and data breaches are everywhere, and they’ve made people think twice before reaching out to someone they don’t know. Safety concerns aren’t just in the background anymore—they’re shaping the way we start conversations, choose platforms, and decide how much to share.
As awareness grows, so do new habits and expectations for digital introductions. This shift doesn’t just affect individuals; it’s influencing whole communities as we all adapt to a more cautious, connected world.
Changing first steps: why some users now engage with strangers differently online
That growing caution is easy to spot in the way people now approach first interactions with strangers online.
Instead of jumping right into open conversations, many start by looking for platforms that let them control who they talk to, or give them the option to remain anonymous until they feel comfortable.
Features like one-click exit buttons, video previews, or private chat rooms have become popular for exactly this reason.
Women, in particular, are leading this change. They’re more likely to say safety is a top concern, which shows up in everything from avoiding certain apps to using aliases or insisting on in-app messaging only.
The choice of platform matters too. Video chat sites, for example, offer a sense of control because users can see and hear who they’re talking to—and can leave the conversation instantly if something doesn’t feel right.
For many, getting to know LuckyCrush and similar services is part of this shift toward safer, more controlled first steps when meeting someone new.
It’s a sign that concerns are not stopping people from connecting, but are changing the rules for how those first moments happen.
a shift in trust: navigating caution in the age of digital introductions
That change in first steps is really about trust—how it’s built, how it’s lost, and why it matters so much now. People aren’t just jumping into conversations and sharing details the way they might have a decade ago.
Instead, there’s this sense of needing to pause and check for warning signs. With more stories surfacing about online fraud and harassment, it feels riskier to let your guard down. A lot of users now watch for inconsistent stories, pressure to move chats off-platform, or requests for private information as red flags that something isn’t right.
Some of the ways people protect themselves include sticking to messaging within the app, looking for verification badges, or even googling someone before agreeing to meet. These habits are becoming more common, especially as platforms roll out tools designed for safer interactions.
The numbers back up this shift in attitude. In 2023, just under half of U.S. adults said they felt online dating was safe, down from a few years before. Women, in particular, tend to feel more uneasy about sharing personal details, which lines up with reports of higher rates of harassment.
For anyone wanting to understand why trust is changing, the Pew Research on online dating safety is a helpful resource. It highlights how both optimism and skepticism shape the way people meet and interact online now.
Safety in practice: behaviors and community responses on Nigerian social platforms
That skepticism and caution show up in everyday choices for users in Nigeria too. The reality of scams and harmful encounters is hard to ignore, so both individuals and communities have started to change how they approach online connections.
People are much more likely to double-check who they’re chatting with, sometimes even asking for proof of identity before sharing anything personal. It’s now common for users to avoid giving out phone numbers or addresses until they’ve built enough trust within the platform’s chat feature.
Platforms play a role by offering safety tools, but users often take things further by joining moderated groups or relying on word-of-mouth warnings. These groups work together to flag suspicious behavior and alert others, building a sense of collective vigilance that can help everyone feel a little safer.
Community-driven warnings have become especially important after a series of incidents have made headlines. Stories like Rivers Police nab kidnappers serve as stark reminders that online risks have real-life consequences, motivating even more caution among regular users.
The combination of individual caution and group action is changing the culture of meeting strangers online in Nigeria. People are still eager to connect, but staying safe is now a shared priority, not just a personal one.
Looking ahead: the enduring tension between connection and caution
This shift toward community vigilance hasn’t erased the basic human urge to connect online. People still want to meet, form friendships, and build relationships across digital spaces, even as they weigh the risks involved.
The real challenge now is finding a balance between openness and caution. Many users are adapting by taking advantage of improved verification processes, using reporting tools, and staying informed about possible threats. These steps aren’t just about individual safety—they’re shaping the culture of online interaction overall.
Platforms are also responding to these pressures. High-profile actions like WhatsApp bans scam accounts show that companies are working to remove bad actors and create safer environments. These crackdowns send a message that security isn’t optional, but a shared responsibility between users and service providers.
Even with new tools and policies, the tension between wanting to connect and needing to protect yourself is likely to stay. Ongoing education, clear safety features, and active moderation will remain important as the way we meet strangers online continues to evolve.

items.content:
Governor of Enugu State, Dr Peter Mbah, has expressed deep grief over the deaths of four students of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, UNN, who reportedly died during an off-campus sign-out party organised for one of their friends, describing the incident as a heartbreaking loss.
Mbah described the deaths as a grievous loss, not only to the immediate families of the deceased and the university, but also to Enugu State as a whole.
He called for a ban on sign-out parties among undergraduates, noting that the practice had brought too much sorrow to families and tertiary institutions across the country.
This was contained in a press statement issued by the governor’s media aide, Mazi Uche Anichukwu, on Thursday.
“I received with rude shock and deep sense of loss the news of the off-campus sign-out party leading to the death of four students of the University of Nigeria Nsukka, and hospitalisation of six others.
“This is a grievous loss not only to the immediate families of the deceased and the university, but also to us as a state. Losing them in their prime and along with their promising future cuts as deeply as a sharp knife. We, therefore share in this grief and pray God to grant their families, friends, and the UNN community the equanimity to bear the heartbreaking loss.
“Our hearts go out to their parents in particular, who sacrificed personal comforts to sponsor their children through the university, but only to face this sad turn of events.
“As a government, we have ordered a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding their deaths and will work closely with the university authorities and security agencies to get to the roots of the sad development and forestall a recurrence.
“In the meantime, I have suspended my scheduled town hall meeting with the UNN community on Friday, November 13, 2026, as we join the university in mourning the dead.
“Going forward, we will work with the authorities of tertiary institutions to enforce a full ban on sign-out parties and other excessive celebrations, a trend that has cost more lives and brought more sorrows than joy to families and higher institutions of learning,” the governor stated.
Mbah also called for increased public enlightenment campaigns by relevant agencies and institutions on the consequences of drug use and abuse.
He prayed for the peaceful repose of the souls of the deceased.
