items.content:
By Folarin Kehinde
The Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) has disclosed that all locking mechanisms of the passenger-cabin door that detached from a Bombardier Challenger 604 aircraft mid-air during an Abuja-Lagos flight were found in the open position after the incident.
The Bureau also disclosed on its website that the aircraft’s door indicator displayed an ‘UNLOCKED/RED’ warning, while both the internal and external door handles were found in the open position.
These findings were contained in the preliminary investigation report released by the NSIB on November 11, following the October 15 incident involving an aircraft operated by Triton Aviation Limited.
The aircraft, with registration number T7-SEI and operating as flight DWC052, was carrying nine persons, comprising two pilots, one cabin crew member and six passengers, when its passenger-crew door detached during initial climb after take-off from the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja.
Interestingly, the flight crew told investigators that they did not receive any aural or visual door warning before the door separated from the aircraft.
The bureau further disclosed that no door-related faults or warnings were recorded in the aircraft’s downloaded Maintenance Diagnostic Computer (MDC) data.
According to the report, the incident occurred at approximately 5:19 p.m. when the flight crew observed an abnormal increase in cabin altitude and suspected a pressurisation problem.
The captain subsequently instructed the cabin crew to double-check the main cabin door by pushing and pulling it.
However, the cabin crew member told investigators that as she approached the passenger-crew door, it opened without her touching it.
Some passengers also reportedly said they could not recall seeing the cabin crew member touch the door.
The door subsequently detached from the aircraft and struck its lower fuselage, damaging a VHF antenna.
Following the occurrence, the captain took over control of the aircraft while the first officer assumed pilot-monitoring duties.
The pilots declared an emergency and coordinated with Abuja Air Traffic Control for an immediate return to the airport.
The aircraft eventually landed safely on Runway 22 at approximately 5:34 p.m., with all nine occupants disembarking without injuries.
The report also revealed that during the final approach, the pilot monitoring unfastened his seat belt and attempted to close the passenger-crew door by pressing the DOOR CLOSE button.
The detached door was subsequently recovered from a cornfield in Gui Village, Abuja Municipal Area Council, approximately five miles southwest of the airport.
Meanwhile, the NSIB said further investigations would focus on determining whether structural or mechanical failure contributed to the door separation.
It listed metallurgical testing and detailed examination of the detached door, its associated assemblies and locking mechanisms among the next investigative steps.
Investigators will also conduct detailed analysis of the Flight Data Recorder (FDR), particularly the passenger-crew door warning and indication parameters.
The Bureau said the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR) would also undergo further analysis, including spectral examination of a recorded mechanical clicking sound to establish its source.
Other areas of investigation include examination of the door-warning and indication system, associated electrical circuits and their functionality at the time of the occurrence.
The NSIB, however, cautioned that the preliminary report contains factual information and initial findings only, stressing that it does not establish the causes or contributing factors responsible for the incident.
It said the final report, containing the investigation’s analysis, conclusions and further safety recommendations, would be published upon completion of the investigation in accordance with Annex 13 of the Convention on International Civil Aviation.

items.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi
Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, has asked Nigerians to trust him to deliver a free, fair, credible and inclusive election next year, promising to not fail them
This was as he said the commission is yet to recover from the trust deficit created by the technical glitches associated with the 2023 general election, and vowed that inaccurate polling unit results will not reach the INEC Result Viewing Portal IReV in 2027.
Amupitan spoke on Thursday at Chatham House, London, at a dialogue held with the Kimpact Development Initiative (KDI) on the theme, “Nigeria’s 2027 Elections: Democratic Trajectory and Regional Stability Beyond the Ballot.”
His Chief Press Secretary, Adedayo Oketola, said the INEC chairman noted that the controversies over the 2023 presidential election badly dented public confidence in the commission.
“First, let me speak about what happened in 2023, which resulted in a significant trust deficit for INEC—damage so large that the Commission has not yet fully recovered from it,” he said.
He said the commission’s audit after 2023 traced the worst result management failures to collation centres, not polling units.
“In 2023, there were instances of inaccurate results or results with over-voting being uploaded onto IReV. We have now devised a technical safeguard: if a result is not accurate at the polling unit, it will not go to IReV at all. The moment a result appears on IReV, citizens can trust what they see. By eliminating inconsistencies at the source, collation will become a transparent formality”, he stated.
The INEC chairman announced that the commission would hold a nationwide mock accreditation and voting exercise on November 28, 2026.
“On the 28th of this month, we will conduct a mock accreditation and voting exercise across all states of the federation to simulate the presidential election and verify that we have gotten both accreditation and electronic result transmission right,” he said.
Asked why Nigerians should trust his leadership, Amupitan who assumed office in October 2025, pointed to the off-cycle elections he had conducted.
“Why must Nigerians trust me? Nigerians must trust me because, number one, I have conducted off-cycle elections—and observers agree that the recent election in Osun State marked a clear improvement,” he said.
He listed the Anambra and Osun governorship elections, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Area Council polls, the Ekiti governorship election and 16 legislative by-elections.
Amupitan recalled that the 2021 Anambra governorship poll took roughly five days to conclude, whereas results in Anambra and Osun were declared the day after voting under his watch.
“Every election is a lesson. The 2023 general election was a major lesson for Nigeria, and the Anambra election was another,” he said.
He said INEC considered introducing a new electoral technology for 2027 but chose to upgrade its existing infrastructure because of the tight timeline before the polls.
To address the malfunctions of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) linked to heat and storage conditions in 2023, he said INEC was building climate-controlled storage facilities in all states.
The commission has also bought extra devices and cut the maximum number of voters assigned per BVAS from 1,250 to 850, so that polling units with more than 850 registered voters will get multiple devices.
On funding, Amupitan said INEC had received a substantial part of its 2027 election budget and had been assured that the outstanding balance, part of which is meant for the recruitment and welfare of ad hoc staff, would be released before the end of November.
Responding to allegations on social media that linked his phone number to a controversial X account, he denied ever operating one. He said an independent forensic review had been obtained and the matter referred to the Department of State Services (DSS) and the Inspector-General of Police for investigation.
He dismissed suggestions that his past legal representation in political disputes would affect his impartiality. “My loyalty is solely to the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and the Electoral Act,” he said.
On claims of an 85 per cent surge in registrants in a ward in Ebonyi State, he said the commission had investigated and resolved the complaint in line with statutory procedures.
The Presidential and National Assembly elections hold on January 16, 2027, while the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections follow on February 6, 2027.
Amupitan urged young Nigerians to stay involved in the democratic process.
“Misinformation remains one of the greatest threats to our democracy. Citizens must verify information before acting or sharing, and give our democracy the chance to succeed,” he said.
The post 2027: Trust me, I won’t fail you, INEC chair assures Nigerians appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
Pakistani startups using artificial intelligence (AI) to improve people’s finances can now apply for grants of up to £250,000 under a new GSMA Innovation Fund for AI-Enabled Financial Health.
The fund, backed by the UK government’s Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), will give selected companies between £100,000 and £250,000 each. Applications are open until December 17, 2026.
Who Can Apply
The fund is open to for-profit, private small and growing businesses in low- and middle-income countries across Africa, South Asia and Southeast Asia. Pakistan is on the list of eligible countries, alongside Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Indonesia and others.
According to the fund’s terms and conditions, applicants must already have users and revenue, and companies running projects in Pakistan must be registered and operating in the country. They must also put in matching funds of at least 25% of the grant they request, and projects will run for 15 to 18 months.
What the Money Is For
GSMA wants AI solutions that help people handle money shocks, make better financial decisions and build long-term savings and income. Examples include AI fraud detection, personal financial coaching in local languages, market and price information, job matching and savings tools.
Applications from companies serving women, girls and people with disabilities, locally led firms, and businesses that mobile operators could help scale will get special preference.
Besides the grant, winners will get technical help, access to investors and publicity through GSMA events and publications.
Why It Matters
GSMA said account ownership in low- and middle-income countries has jumped from 42% in 2011 to almost 80% in 2024, mainly due to mobile money. However, only about one in four of the world’s 2.3 billion registered mobile money accounts is used every month.
This is not the first such GSMA fund for Pakistan. In 2021, the GSMA Innovation Fund gave Rs. 146 million to three startups. The body has also urged Pakistan to cut telecom taxes to support digital growth.
The post GSMA Offers Pakistani Startups Grants of Up to £250,000 for AI Finance Solutions appeared first on ProPakistani.

items.title: Scaloni to stay on as Argentina coach until 2030 World Cup
items.summary:
Lionel Scaloni on Thursday agreed to stay on as coach of Argentina’s national football team until after the 2030 World Cup, ending the doubts that had been swirling since this year’s World Cup final defeat.

items.content:
United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino is set to be appointed as the new manager of Manchester United after the struggling English giants sacked Michael Carrick on Thursday.
Pochettino is expected to leave his role with the USA following their two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final on Saturday and Tuesday in a move that will see United trigger a release clause worth some $10 million to secure the Argentine’s services.
Pochettino, who signed a contract extension to remain with the United States through to the 2030 World Cup just three months ago, is due to hold a pre-match press conference on Friday.
Former United captain Carrick led the team to an impressive third-place finish in the Premier League last season, but they have taken just eight points from 10 games in the current campaign and are in the relegation zone.
The club confirmed in a statement Thursday that it had parted ways with the 45-year-old, following mounting speculation he would be axed during the international break.
“After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions,” United said.
“Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club.”
Carrick impressed after taking over as interim boss following Ruben Amorim’s acrimonious exit in January, leading United to Champions League qualification.
He was rewarded with a two-year permanent deal but, hampered by the club’s underwhelming recruitment in the summer transfer window, his side have endured a steep decline this season.
Carrick has struggled to maintain discipline, dropping captain Bruno Fernandes after he criticised his manager’s tactics following a 4-1 thrashing at Champions League debutants Como.
And defender Lisandro Martinez spoke out against the club’s hierarchy over their lack of top-quality signings.
Carrick’s final game in charge was a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, after which he stressed he would not walk away despite a paltry record of three wins from 15 games in all competitions this season.
It is believed Carrick’s future was decided on Wednesday during a meeting in Monaco involving co-owner Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.
– ‘Disgusting’ –
Pochettino has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, and he also coached Paris Saint-Germain.
Carrick, who won multiple trophies as a midfielder in the club’s golden era under Alex Ferguson, is the seventh permanent manager to be dismissed by the club since the Scot retired in 2013.
Former United captain Gary Neville, who played alongside Carrick, said his old team-mate had been treated appallingly.
“It’s just quite simply disgusting,” Neville told Sky Sports. “That falls well below the standard of what you would expect in any other business. In any other industry it would be constructive dismissal and you’d be getting sued.”
The Manchester United Supporters’ Trust said Carrick’s departure marked “another depressing moment”, pinning the blame on majority owners the Glazer family and minority shareholder Ratcliffe, with the club yet to win a Premier League title since the end of the Ferguson era.
“The Glazers’ debt-funded takeover continues to burden the club,” MUST said in a statement. “When (Ratcliffe’s) INEOS came in they promised sporting excellence, but yet with repeated changes in football leadership we have seen anything but.”
United’s next game is against fierce rivals Liverpool at Anfield on November 22.

items.content:
Microsoft 365 users around the world are struggling to access Outlook, Teams, and other services as Microsoft deals with a major outage.
Microsoft first reported problems with Exchange Online mailboxes in the Americas at around 10:54 PM PKT on Thursday. Shortly after, the company confirmed that the issue could affect Microsoft 365 users in any region.
Which Services Are Affected
According to the Microsoft 365 status page, the potentially affected services include:
Exchange Online (Outlook email)
Microsoft Teams
SharePoint Online
Microsoft 365 Copilot
Microsoft Defender XDR
Users may be unable to open their mailboxes through Outlook on the web, mobile email apps that use Exchange ActiveSync, and other connection methods.
What Caused the Outage
Microsoft said a portion of its infrastructure is facing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely causing the connection errors. It is also reviewing an unexpected increase in a specific type of service traffic to see whether it added to the problem.
The company said it is “aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact.” It has paused all deployments, spread connection traffic across its worldwide infrastructure, moved more traffic away from the affected systems, and started restarting affected servers. It has not said how many users are affected or when service will be fully restored.
Earlier on Thursday, Microsoft also dealt with a separate Teams disruption in North America, which it said was fully resolved by around 10:09 PM PKT.
The outage comes weeks after a Google Cloud outage disrupted banks, courts, and businesses. Microsoft is sharing updates in the Microsoft 365 admin center under incident EX1550543.

items.content:
‎
‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
‎
President Bola Tinubu on Thursday declared that Nigeria’s economy has moved “from stabilisation to shared prosperity,” citing non-oil exports above $6 billion, external reserves of about $55 billion, and a target of a $1 trillion economy by 2030.
‎
‎Speaking at the public presentation of Economic Diversification and Structural Transformation in Nigeria: Past, Present and Future, authored by Honourable Abdulmumin Jibrin Kofa, Tinubu said the country had abandoned “cosmetic remedies” for what he called the “hard road of surgery.”
‎
‎According to him: “For too long, Nigeria’s story was a song sung in a single note. We were a nation of boundless promise tied to a single product, our budget, our currency and the livelihoods of millions rising and falling with the tides of a distant oil market. We floated on the fragile illusion of oil wealth while the foundations beneath us crackborders.
‎
‎”When I took the oath of office, I did not inherit a calm sea; I inherited a gathering storm: a collapsing naira, debt service that swallowed nearly all our revenue, depleted reserves, a fuel subsidy that bled our treasury dry, and factories falling silent as industries and jobs fled across our borders.”
‎
‎The President said his administration inherited “a gathering storm,” including “a collapsing naira, debt service that swallowed nearly all our revenue, depleted reserves, a fuel subsidy that bled our treasury dry, and factories falling silent.”
‎
‎“We chose reform over ruin. We removed the fuel subsidy. We unified the exchange rate. These were not easy decisions, and I know the weight they placed on every household. But they were necessary, and today the pain is yielding its promise.”
‎
‎He stated that non-oil activities now account for about 96 per cent of Gross Domestic Product, while non-oil exports have crossed $6 billion, which he described as the highest in Nigeria’s history.
‎
‎Tinubu also said external reserves had risen to about $55 billion, representing “more than fourteen months of import cover,” and that non-oil revenue had grown from ₦13.63 trillion in 2023 to ₦16.4 trillion in the first half of 2026.
‎
‎The President said government alone cannot build a $1 trillion economy, adding that wealth must be created by enterprises that “invest, innovate, manufacture and export.”
‎
‎“Our duty is to clear the path before them,” he said. “That is why our 2025 budget introduced a first-of-its-kind De-risking Framework to draw in private capital, which we expect to provide 86 per cent of the investment our 2030 goal demands.”
‎
‎He said the administration was harmonising taxes and ending “the menace of multiple taxation.”
‎“We cannot tax our way into prosperity; we must produce our way there,” Tinubu said.
‎
‎The President said the administration had “fought for Mambilla,” winning a $3.38 billion arbitration at the International Chamber of Commerce in Paris and freeing “a project held hostage for more than nine years.”
‎He added that Geregu Power is moving to raise its capacity to 1,300 megawatts, while the Port Harcourt and Warri refineries are “stirring back to life.”
‎
‎On infrastructure, Tinubu listed the Kano–Katsina–Maradi railway, Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto–Badagry Superhighway, Abuja–Kaduna–Kano Expressway, East–West Road, Ibadan–Ife–Ilesa Expressway, Port Harcourt–Enugu and Enugu–Onitsha expressways, and the restoration of Carter Bridge.
‎
‎He said 52 per cent of legacy highway mileage is in the North and 48 per cent in the South.
‎
‎“We are building fairly and deliberately, so that no zone is left behind and no citizen is a stranger to opportunity,” he said.
‎
‎Tinubu said more than 10,000 homes are rising across 14 states and the Federal Capital Territory under the Renewed Hope Cities and Estates Programme.
‎He said the MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund had provided about ₦128 billion in mortgages to 1,859 families in 25 states, at a fixed rate of 9.75 per cent over 20 years.
‎
‎“As this market grows, so must the confidence of those who invest in it,” he said. “I will therefore work hand in hand with the National Assembly and stakeholders to establish a strong regulatory authority for housing and real estate.”
‎
‎The President also cited NELFUND, university solarisation, Bank of Industry loans and grants across all 774 local government areas, the 3MTT digital-skills programme, and 90,000 kilometres of fibre-optic infrastructure.
‎“Roads and power lines are the skeleton of a nation; its people are its life,” he said.
‎
‎Tinubu commended Jibrin, the member representing Kiru/Bebeji Federal Constituency in Kano State, whose years as a lawmaker and chairman of key National Assembly committees, including Finance and Appropriations, “lend these pages the weight of experience.”
‎
‎“This is the essence of the book we present today,” Tinubu said. “It looks back with honesty, looks around with clarity and looks ahead with courage.”
‎
‎He said: “The days of hardship are temporary; the foundations we are laying are permanent. Let us keep building until the world looks upon Nigeria and sees not promise deferred, but promise fulfilled.”
‎
‎The event was held at the State House Conference Centre in Abuja, with Governor Charles Soludo as keynote speaker, Alhaji Abdulsamad Isyaku Rabiu as book presenter and Dr Reuben Abati as reviewer.

By Adegboyega Adeleye
African Democratic Congress (ADC) chieftain Solomon Dalung has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu would lose the 2027 election even if his opponent were “anybody picked on the street,” arguing that the President was afraid of facing voters.
Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Dalung made the prediction while responding to a question about how the opposition could overcome the APC’s resources amid the current internal leadership and legal crisis in the ADC. He nevertheless insisted the party was ready to challenge Tinubu at the ballot.
“Since my experience in politics, like I always say, Nigerians, I was brought into politics at a much tender age. I have never seen a weak president in an election like Bola Ahmed Tinubu. If you drag anybody on the street and put him on a ballot at a contest with Tinubu, he will defeat him,” Dalung said.
He claimed Tinubu was apprehensive about the election despite having been in office for four years, and challenged the President and APC to let the contest be decided by voters.
“Bola Tinubu is so scared, having been in office for four years, he is so scared of election. And all we are seeing in ADC, let’s meet at the ballot. You claim it was the ballot that brought you to power, let’s meet at the ballot,” he said.
Dalung also accused the APC of obstructing opposition parties’ campaign activities, alleging that venues had been closed, hotels taken over and party offices sealed. He compared the situation with the 2014 election period, saying the APC would have been left with few places to campaign if it had faced similar restrictions then.
“Nobody will be blamed except Tinubu. Why? Because I mean, in the history of Nigeria, we have seen opposition parties contest election, but we have never seen this type of situation. If the PDP in 2014 were closing venues for rallies and taking over hotels, sealing party offices, the APC would have no place to campaign except the streets,” he said.
He argued that moving the opposition onto the streets would not weaken its campaign, claiming those attending its gatherings were genuine supporters rather than people hired to fill rallies.
“Now, for Tinubu and his APC to move the opposition on pit, they have lost the election. This is because the people we are having on the street are organic followers. Those are the Nigerians that will vote. They are not rented crowds from all over the federation,” Dalung said.

items.content:
By By Henry Umoru, and Gift ChapiOdekina
The House of Representatives, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council (APC-PCC) have condemned reported cases of political violence across the country following an attack on NDC supporters during a town hall meeting in Lagos.
While the NDC demanded an immediate investigation, arrest and prosecution of those responsible for the attack in Lagos, the APC-PCC also condemned the incident and called on security agencies to apprehend the perpetrators.
The Lagos State chapter of the APC equally condemned the reported attack but denied any involvement, challenging the NDC to provide credible evidence linking the ruling party to the incident.
The House of Representatives, on Wednesday, also resolved to investigate reported attacks, intimidation and disruption of political activities across the country ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The resolution followed the adoption of a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by the House Minority Leader, Rep. Fred Agbedi, and 16 other lawmakers, amid growing concerns over attacks on political meetings, rallies and processions in different parts of the country.
Presenting the motion on behalf of the sponsors, Agbedi condemned acts of violence, intimidation, assault and destruction of property associated with political activities, irrespective of the political parties or individuals affected.
He appealed to political parties, candidates and their supporters to reject inflammatory rhetoric, discourage violence and cooperate with security agencies to maintain public peace.
Citing Section 40 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, the Minority Leader reminded lawmakers that Nigerians were guaranteed the right to assemble freely and associate with others, including the right to form or belong to political parties.
He also cited the constitutional provision which makes the security and welfare of the people the primary purpose of government, stressing the need to protect citizens participating in legitimate political activities.
Agbedi urged the House to invoke Section 88(1) of the Constitution, which empowers the National Assembly to investigate matters within its legislative competence and examine the conduct of public authorities responsible for administering relevant laws.
To illustrate the growing concerns, he cited several incidents of political violence recorded in different states.
He recalled the disruption of political meetings in Enugu State on September 12, 2026, during which the police reportedly confirmed that two attendees were injured, while one person was allegedly killed.
He also cited an attack on APC supporters travelling to a rally in Katsina State on October 28, 2026, which led to the arrest of 14 suspects.
In Nasarawa State, Agbedi recalled the attack on an APC rally in Lafia on November 4, 2026, where several people were reportedly injured.
He further mentioned a violent incident during a political procession in Asaba, Delta State, on November 7, 2026, in which the police reportedly confirmed that one person was killed and five others injured.
The lawmaker warned that continued attacks, intimidation and destruction of property linked to political activities could result in further loss of lives and injuries, while discouraging citizens from participating in the electoral process.
He, however, stressed that allegations of responsibility for the incidents must be established through impartial, thorough and evidence-based investigations.
The House subsequently constituted an ad hoc committee headed by the Leader of the House, Julius Ihonvbere, to investigate the immediate and remote causes of politically motivated violence and report its findings within three weeks.
The committee comprises the House Leader, Minority Leader, chairmen and deputy chairmen of the House Committees on Police Affairs and National Security and Intelligence, as well as two additional members drawn from the committees.
NDC demands probe, prosecution
Meanwhile, the national leadership of the NDC has condemned the attack on its supporters by suspected political thugs who allegedly invaded its town hall meeting in Oregun, along Kudirat Abiola Way, Ikeja, Lagos.
The party demanded the immediate investigation, arrest and prosecution of those responsible, insisting that the incident would not intimidate its members or silence Nigerians.
In a statement issued on Thursday and signed by the Spokesperson of the NDC National Campaign Council, Dr Chiogo Constance Ikokwu, the party described the incident as an unacceptable assault on democracy, citizens’ fundamental rights and freedom of political association.
It said no political party or group had a monopoly on Nigeria, adding that nobody had the right to deploy violence, intimidation or thuggery to silence opposing voices.
The party also called for an end to what it described as the dangerous culture of political violence being witnessed in some states.
The statement read: “The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) strongly condemns the violent attack on its supporters in Lagos by suspected political thugs during its town hall meeting today.
“We deeply sympathise with anybody injured in the attack and wish them a speedy and full recovery. Our thoughts are with them and their families at this difficult time.
“This incident is an unacceptable assault on democracy, citizens’ fundamental rights and the freedom of political association. No political party or group has a monopoly on Nigeria, and no one has the right to use violence, intimidation or thuggery to silence opposing voices.
“Nigeria is not a conquered territory, and political participation is not a crime.
“We demand an immediate investigation, the arrest and prosecution of those responsible, and an end to the dangerous culture of political violence we are witnessing in some states.
“Those who believe they can intimidate Nigerians into silence must understand that democracy belongs to the people, not political thugs and their sponsors.”
The party alleged that the attack was part of an attempt to intimidate Nigerians, spread fear and discourage participation in the 2027 elections, but insisted that such efforts would fail.
The Lagos meeting was part of the NDC’s campaign activities in support of its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and governorship candidate, Funsho Doherty.
The party urged Nigerians to turn out in large numbers in 2027 to exercise their democratic rights and vote for the Obi/Kwankwaso ticket, describing the call as part of its demand for accountable leadership and a different direction for the country.
It maintained that neither the party nor its supporters would be bullied out of exercising their democratic rights.
APC-PCC calls for arrests
Similarly, the APC Presidential Campaign Council condemned the disruption of the NDC town hall meeting in Lagos and other reported attacks on political gatherings in Edo, Cross River and Gombe states.
In a statement issued on Thursday, the Spokesperson of the APC-PCC, Dele Alake, described the attacks as condemnable, regardless of the political parties or individuals affected.
“We have observed the recent spate of violent attacks at political gatherings in parts of the country. The reported attacks in Edo, Cross River, and Gombe, and other violence targeted at party supporters and political leaders across party lines are condemnable,” the statement said.
On the Lagos incident, the council said: “Our campaign strongly condemns the disruption of today’s scheduled town hall meeting of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Lagos.”
The APC-PCC urged political parties, politicians and their supporters to exercise restraint as campaign activities gathered momentum, warning against actions capable of creating public disorder.
It called on security agencies to strengthen their response to political violence and ensure that those responsible were arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law.
“Political parties and candidates are enjoined to campaign on issues that uplift the lives of Nigerians and not to instigate violence at political events,” it added.
Lagos APC denies involvement
The Lagos State chapter of the APC also condemned the reported attack on NDC members in Ikeja but dismissed allegations linking the ruling party to the incident.
The party’s State Publicity Secretary, Seye Oladejo, described the allegation as baseless, challenging the opposition party to present credible evidence to security agencies rather than make public insinuations.
In a statement, Oladejo said the allegation was an attempt to drag the APC into an incident without credible evidence linking the party to the disruption.
“We consider this allegation not only reckless, baseless and irresponsible but also a desperate attempt to drag Lagos APC into an incident for which the accusers have presented no credible evidence linking the ruling party,” he said.
The party noted that the reported incident in Ikeja coincided with the official flag-off of its 2027 general election campaign in Epe, where its leadership, elected officials and stakeholders were mobilised.
According to Oladejo, the APC could not have abandoned a major statewide political engagement to interfere with an opposition event.
“For the avoidance of doubt, Lagos APC categorically rejects any insinuation of involvement, direct or indirect, in the alleged disruption of the said political gathering. We have neither sponsored, encouraged nor participated in any act capable of undermining the constitutional rights of any political party or group to assemble, deliberate and canvass for political support,” he said.
Oladejo maintained that the APC’s position as the governing party in Lagos did not make it responsible for every breach of public order in the state.
He described the accusation as “a lazy political reflex that substitutes propaganda for investigation and blame-shifting for accountability.”
The APC spokesman urged the NDC to submit any credible evidence linking individuals or groups to the incident to the appropriate security agencies and allow the law to take its course.
He also called on the Lagos State Police Command and the Department of State Services (DSS) to investigate the incident and take measures to prevent any breakdown of law and order.
Reiterating the party’s commitment to peaceful and issue-based campaigns, Oladejo said political ambition should not be used as a justification for lawlessness and urged political actors to avoid intimidation and disorder as the 2027 elections approach.
Vanguard Newspaper

items.title: Join Rainbow Coalition or leave, Fubara warns supporters
items.summary:

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, has warned his supporters who are unwilling to align with the Rainbow Coalition to leave, insisting that his decision to return to his political camp is final.
Fubara gave the warning on Thursday during the inauguration of the Rivers State All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Rainbow Coalition, in Port Harcourt.
Addressing party members and supporters, the governor urged those whose names were not included in the campaign council list not to feel aggrieved, explaining that there were still sub-committees to be constituted and that the list could be updated.
He, however, warned against double-dealing, insisting that those claiming to support him must demonstrate genuine commitment to the coalition.
“We still have sub-committees. The list can also be updated so you don’t have any problems to worry about. The most important thing is to work with your heart sincerely.
“Don’t openly say you’re with me and behold you’re doing a different thing. I’m here, and I say it boldly anywhere, any day. And anybody who says he is not with me, gently go your way,” he said.
Acknowledging that some of his supporters might find it difficult to accept the new political direction, Fubara urged them to put the past behind them and embrace the future.
“Don’t go behind and say this is Fubara, no, no, no. I have said it. It might be difficult but we have gone past that. We are looking at the future and what God holds for us,” he added.
The governor charged members of the campaign council to work together to achieve their political objectives, expressing confidence that the coalition would record more votes in the forthcoming elections than it secured in 2023.
“Nothing is impossible. Provided it’s something that has to do with life, it is possible if we take it as a serious responsibility, a serious task that must be achieved, we will come out with a stronger vote than what we did in 2023.
“It is only for us to say yes, we want to do it. And I am very sure that with the strategy of these forthcoming elections we are going to come out with good results better than what we had before,” he said.
Fubara also thanked the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, and other political leaders for their efforts in establishing the campaign council.
Earlier, Wike, who inaugurated the council, announced plans to establish similar campaign structures across the 23 local government areas of Rivers State.
He said the coalition would abandon conventional campaign rallies in favour of direct engagement with residents through community gatherings, family meetings and age-grade associations.
“We are going away from that ceremonial campaign style. When we are going to Gokana today, we just stay in one field and begin to talk to those we already know.
“It is going to be different. This time around we are going round to communities, to family meetings, to age-grade meetings and other informal sects to talk to them, not necessarily those we meet with every day.
“You and I meet every day; then tomorrow again we gather in one place, we say we are holding a rally. We must depart from that,” Wike said.
The minister commended Fubara for attending the inauguration and other engagements of the council despite his busy schedule.
Wike, who is also the National Leader of the PDP/Rainbow Coalition, said members of the campaign council were selected based on their capacity to participate in its activities and deliver results.
He urged them to mobilise support for APC and Rainbow Coalition candidates in the 2027 presidential, governorship, National Assembly and State House of Assembly elections.
He further disclosed that local government campaign councils would soon be inaugurated to strengthen the coalition’s grassroots mobilisation.
Background
The development is the latest chapter in the prolonged political crisis between Fubara and Wike, who governed Rivers State from 2015 to 2023 and supported Fubara’s emergence as his successor.
Their disagreement, which became public in October 2023, centred on control of the state’s political structures and influence over the Rivers State House of Assembly.
The crisis split lawmakers into opposing camps and triggered repeated impeachment moves against Fubara.
The dispute escalated in March 2025 when President Bola Tinubu declared a state of emergency in Rivers State, resulting in the suspension of the governor, his deputy and members of the State House of Assembly for six months.
The elected officials returned to office in September 2025 following the expiration of the emergency rule.
Reconciliation efforts gathered momentum in 2026 after Wike announced an end to the feud and a reconciliation committee was constituted to engage Fubara and his supporters.
The Rainbow Coalition, led by Wike, comprises political actors from different parties, including the APC and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), working towards Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027.
Fubara subsequently declared support for the coalition and endorsed Kingsley Chinda as his preferred successor in the 2027 Rivers governorship election. He also withdrew from the APC governorship contest, citing the need to promote peace and unity in the state.

Materazzi said the incident, one of football’s most infamous World Cup moments, still troubled him 20 years later. He told Italian newspaper La Gazzetta dello Sport that De Miguel’s death made him grateful he had escaped serious injury.

De Miguel, a Tenerife striker, died after colliding with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a Segunda Division match earlier this month.
Zidane, then captain of France, was sent off for headbutting Materazzi in the chest during the 2006 final, which Italy won on penalties. Zidane, now France coach, said last month he was not proud of the headbutt but did not regret it.
Materazzi said he and Zidane appeared to put the episode behind them when they met before a match in 2010, although Zidane later disputed Materazzi’s account of the encounter.
“When he saw me, he hesitated a little, he even turned to walk back,” Materazzi said.
“But I approached him and shook his hand: ‘I’m glad we’re meeting here, where nobody can see us.’
“He replied: ‘Don’t worry, these things happen, it’s all in the past.’ It’s a shame he later denied everything, saying he thought I was a fan.”
France are scheduled to play Italy in the Nations League later on Thursday.

items.content:
Former Minister of Youth and Sports Development, Sunday Dare, has said President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms and social interventions constitute an important part of a sustainable national security strategy, arguing that insecurity cannot be tackled through military operations alone.
Dare, who disclosed this in a post on his X platform on Thursday, said economic development, effective governance and social inclusion were critical to addressing the underlying conditions that fuel insecurity.
He observed that public discussions on national security often focused largely on military interventions, while overlooking the structural impact of economic policies and social programmes on the factors that sustain insecurity.
According to him, states with poor developmental indices often record high levels of fragility, reinforcing the need to complement military operations with investments in development and effective governance.
Dare cited the security intervention in Birnin Gwari, Kaduna State, as an example of how improved security could support economic recovery and restore livelihoods.
He said the intervention by Tinubu had enabled farmers to return to their farms, created employment opportunities for young people and improved productivity.
He also credited Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, with providing an account of the development and its impact on communities in the area.
Highlighting some of the Federal Government’s policies with security implications, Dare identified the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), local government autonomy and increased Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) allocations to states and local governments.
On NELFUND, he said expanding access to tertiary education would promote social inclusion and create opportunities for young people who might otherwise be excluded from educational advancement.
According to him, providing legitimate pathways to education and economic opportunities could reduce the vulnerability of young people to recruitment by insurgents and other violent groups.
He described education not merely as a social investment but also as a long-term investment in national security.
On local government autonomy, Dare said adequately resourced and accountable councils could strengthen government presence in communities through improved public services and development initiatives.
He argued that responsive governance at the grassroots would reduce the opportunities for violent non-state actors to exploit poorly governed communities and public disaffection.
The former minister also said improved FAAC allocations could enhance the capacity of state and local governments to invest in infrastructure, education, healthcare, employment and other essential services.
He, however, stressed that such resources must be transparently and productively deployed to address socioeconomic grievances and vulnerabilities that contribute to insecurity.
Dare maintained that security should be assessed not only by the government’s ability to confront threats through military force but also by its capacity to address the conditions that make insecurity possible.
He noted that military operations remained necessary, particularly in confronting active armed groups, but argued that their gains would be more sustainable when supported by inclusive development, strong institutions and responsive governance.
He urged Nigerians to broaden the national conversation on security performance by giving greater consideration to the developmental and social impact of government policies.

items.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni
Former Lagos State Governor, Akinwunmi Ambode, has criticised opposition parties seeking to unseat the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general elections, saying they lack the political experience and leadership depth required to govern Nigeria.
Ambode specifically mentioned the African Democratic Congress (ADC), the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and other opposition platforms, arguing that the APC had greater political experience and ideological consistency.
He spoke at the APC East Senatorial District rally held at Epe Recreational Ground, Epe, Lagos State, where he canvassed support for President Bola Tinubu, the party’s Lagos governorship candidate, Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, and other APC candidates ahead of the 2027 elections.
Ambode said the APC had remained consistent in its political identity, unlike some politicians who, according to him, frequently moved from one political party to another.
“APC is our party. We are a collective of the progressives. We have been consistent and delivering for the party. Over the years, we have remained with the progressives and we do not move from one party to another like other people,” he said.
Describing the APC as a party connecting the country’s past, present and future, the former governor argued that its political experience placed it in a different position from opposition parties seeking to take over the reins of government.
He also credited Tinubu’s political vision and record as Lagos governor with contributing to the state’s economic and infrastructural development, particularly its emergence as a major investment destination.
Ambode said the foundations laid during Tinubu’s tenure as governor helped create an environment for financial institutions and corporate organisations to establish and expand their operations in Lagos.
“Whether you like him or not, he is a visionary leader. If not for Tinubu, who laid the foundation for the Lagos of today, all the financial firms that have their headquarters in Lagos would have been struggling to survive. But today, his vision has assisted the country to remain an investor destination,” he said.
He urged Lagos residents and Nigerians across different social and economic backgrounds to support the APC in the forthcoming elections.
Ambode also appealed to members of the Igbo community living in Lagos and other parts of the country to consider national unity and their economic interests when making political choices.
“To my Igbo brothers, wherever you live and get your prosperity, that is where you should call home. We are together,” he added.

items.summary:
Pakistan’s overall car sales jumped sharply in October 2026, but Toyota and Honda moved in the opposite direction as both automakers recorded year-on-year declines.

Indus Motor Company (INDU), which manufactures Toyota vehicles in Pakistan, sold 4,078 units during October, down 10% YoY and 2% MoM.

items.author: Bismah Malik
items.content:
Consumer tech focussed venture capital firm Fireside Ventures has seen a second exit from its leadership and investment team in two weeks.
Prayag Mohanty, principal at Fireside Ventures, who led its early-stage bets, has quit the firm, Inc42 has learnt from multiple sources.
His exit follows a bigger leadership change at Fireside Ventures. Earlier this month, the firm said that cofounder and partner Vinay Singh has stepped down after nearly a decade at the firm.
Responding to Inc42’s query, Fireside Ventures confirmed Mohanty’s exit. “Prayag Mohanty is moving on from his role of Principal at Fireside Ventures. We value his contributions made during his time with us, and wish him the best in his future endeavours,” Fireside said in a statement to Inc42.
Another Blow For Fireside
Mohanty joined Fireside Ventures as a Principal in January 2020. He was one of five principals listed on the firm’s investment team, alongside Ankur Khaitan, Shuchi Pandya, Varun Varma and Ankita Balotia.
As a principal leading Fireside’s early stage investments, Mohanty fronted several of the firm’s seed stage bets over the past year, including a ₹8 Cr round in Gurugram-based men’s personal care brand Unbound, a ₹20 Cr round in Noida-based Oroos Confectionery and another ₹8 Cr seed round in kids wellness startup Wellopia.
In earlier media reports, he was quoted as saying that Fireside Ventures is ramping up investments in pre-product-market-fit and even pre-revenue startups through a co-investment model with other funds and angel investors, with 8-10 such deals in the pipeline from the new third fund.
Before Fireside, Mohanty had spent about seven years as a principal at IvyCap Ventures from 2013 to 2020, and was involved in deals for listed jewellery giant BlueStone, BiryaniByKilo and Vinculum.
The key departures come less than a year after Fireside announced the final close of its Fund IV at ₹2,265 Cr (about $253 Mn) in December 2025. With Singh’s exit, the firm is being led by founder and managing partner Kanwaljit Singh and cofounders and partners Kannan Sitaram and Dipanjan Basu.
The fund drew commitments from LPs including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA), Investment Corporation of Dubai, HarbourVest, Waterfield and Fidelity International. With Fund IV, Fireside’s assets under management across four funds stand at ₹5,300 Cr (about $650 Mn).

items.author: M Yasir
items.content:
The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) has directed commercial banks to increase women’s share of their workforce from the current 17 percent to 22 percent by December 2028.
Under its Banking on Equality Policy 2026, the central bank has asked banks to prepare action plans with clear timelines to recruit more women and improve their representation across branches and offices.
Banks have also been instructed to prioritise posting female employees at branches and in cities of their choice, wherever possible, to address mobility challenges and help women remain in the workforce.
SBP has directed banks to introduce merit-based promotion policies to move more women into management positions. They will also be required to establish mentorship, coaching and training programs to support the career development of junior female employees.
The regulator has further asked banks to appoint more women as financing officers, particularly in microfinance, agriculture, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), housing and sustainable finance. The move is aimed at improving access to financial services for female borrowers.
Banks must also ensure compliance with workplace harassment laws and provide maternity, miscarriage and iddat leave under applicable regulations. The directives also include daycare facilities or allowances to support working mothers.
Female Bank Employees Reach Nearly 50,000
According to SBP data, women’s representation in the banking workforce increased from 13 percent in 2021 to 17 percent in 2025. The number of female employees has reached nearly 50,000, with around 17,500 women joining the sector over the last four years.
Despite the increase, women remain underrepresented in senior management and decision-making positions. The SBP has identified employee retention, mobility restrictions, limited workplace facilities and long working hours as major challenges.
The central bank has also reported progress in women’s financial inclusion. Women now hold more than 78 million bank accounts, including over 45 million active accounts. Active accounts held by women have increased by 116 percent compared with the 2021 baseline.
Meanwhile, nearly 377,000 women in agriculture have received financing worth Rs. 105 billion, while around 2.8 million women have obtained microcredit amounting to Rs. 152 billion.
The number of women-operated branchless banking agent outlets has also exceeded 23,000, representing a 114 percent increase from the 2021 baseline.
SBP introduced its Banking on Equality initiative in 2021 to reduce gender disparities in the financial sector and encourage banks to develop services tailored to women’s needs.
The initiative has helped reduce the gender gap in financial inclusion from 39 percent in 2021 to 29 percent in 2025.
The post SBP Orders Banks to Hire More Women appeared first on ProPakistani.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb said sovereign Sukuk issuance had grown 113% year-on-year, with the outstanding stock reaching Rs10 trillion from about Rs2 trillion a year earlier, reflecting the country's expanding Islamic capital market and efforts to diversify government financing instruments.
He was addressing a ceremony marking the Rs10 trillion milestone, alongside the issuance of hybrid and short-term Sukuk, according to a statement issued on Thursday.
The five-year compound annual growth rate stood at around 22%, compared with nearly Rs761 billion in 2020.
He said the achievement was not merely about the volume of issuance but reflected sustained efforts to diversify the Sukuk market and introduce greater flexibility in sovereign financing instruments.
He said the introduction of hybrid government Sukuk, combining different Shariah-compliant structures, would give the government greater flexibility in using state-owned assets.
Short-term Sukuk, including instruments with three to six-month maturities, addressed a longstanding gap in the market and helped establish a comprehensive Shariah-compliant yield curve across different maturities, he said.
Foreign investment in Sukuk, however, remained below expectations despite positive inflows through Special Convertible Rupee Accounts into Treasury Bills and Pakistan Investment Bonds, and the minister called for active promotion of Sukuk among international investors and a widening of foreign portfolio investment into Shariah-compliant instruments.
Banks, primary dealers and brokers should work collectively towards that objective, he said.
He also sought wider retail participation through digital platforms, saying investment opportunities should not remain limited to institutional and large-scale investors, and that channels could enable individuals to participate with amounts as small as Rs5,000, making Islamic financial instruments more accessible to ordinary citizens and helping broaden the investor base.
Efforts were also under way to promote listed Sukuk, with the Ministry of Power having issued the first mandate to National Debt Company, which was preparing to launch its first listed Sukuk, he said.
He expressed hope the issuance would set a benchmark for other corporate entities, and said the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan, State Bank of Pakistan, Pakistan Stock Exchange and Central Depository Company would need to collaborate in developing a comprehensive Sukuk market ecosystem.
The minister reaffirmed the government's commitment to developing a deep, diversified and liquid Islamic capital market through active cooperation among the government, private sector, regulators and financial institutions.
He said the principles of learning, reflection, mutual understanding and cooperation were equally important for Islamic finance and society, citing Quranic teachings and the place of Ijtihad in Islamic jurisprudence, and that emerging economic and financial challenges required sound scholarship and thoughtful application of the principles of the Quran and Sunnah, encouraging informed reasoning and respectful discussion among scholars and financial experts.
He urged stakeholders to focus on common ground rather than differences, expressing confidence that continued collaboration would further strengthen the Islamic capital market.
Cashless payments
Minister of State for Railways and Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani chaired a follow-up meeting on the Cashless Pakistan initiative at the Finance Division, bringing together senior public and private sector stakeholders to review decisions taken by the committee under the prime minister's chairmanship.
The discussion also covered the direction and targets for expanding digital payments, in light of progress under the prime minister's initiative.
From November 16, all payments for Asaan Assignment Accounts across the country will be made through the Raast digital system, with drawing and disbursing officers already trained.
Active merchants accepting digital payments have grown from 0.5 million to 2.03 million, attributable to measures taken under the initiative.
Raast payment QR codes have been placed on more than 45 million gas and electricity bills, all National Database and Registration Authority centres have been equipped to accept them, and the overall volume of digital payments has doubled in a year.
The discussion focused on refining the framework for the Raast QR merchant discount rate scheme and on ensuring that the high-level dashboard captures values as well as volumes of key digital payment indicators, along with the number of unique account users.
The minister of state also highlighted the importance of measuring outcome-based indicators of the economy.
He directed the State Bank of Pakistan to prepare a working paper to process approval of the scheme so that promotion of Raast QR can continue, and to assess including macroeconomic indicators such as the ratio of payments processed through the Real Time Gross Settlement system to GDP.
He will meet the presidents and chief executives of banks in Karachi to discuss the initiative and the promotion of digital payments, so that all banks can play their part in this national initiative.
The meeting was attended by senior representatives of the Finance Division, the State Bank of Pakistan, the Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication and the registration authority, and by the president of Easypaisa Digital Bank, the chairman of JazzCash, the chief digital officer of Bank Alfalah and officials of JS Bank, Karandaaz Pakistan and other digital payments institutions.
He thanked participants and directed that coordination between public and private stakeholders be strengthened to achieve the initiative's targets. WITH ADDITIONAL INPUT FROM APP

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) witnessed a bearish session on Thursday as investors resorted to profit-taking after the benchmark KSE-100 index briefly crossed the 180,000-point mark intra-day, shedding over 1,700 points to close near 177,375 amid broad-based selling pressure in heavyweight stocks.
At the close of trading, the KSE-100 index fell 1,710.04 points, or 0.95%, and settled at 177,373.76. Arif Habib Limited's (AHL) trading floor note termed the day a session of consolidation at the PSX, with the KSE-100 falling 0.95% after briefly touching the 180,000 level. Market breadth was negative, as only 16 stocks advanced while 83 declined. MARI, MTL and GHNI provided the largest positive contribution, while UBL, LUCK and HUBC were the biggest drags.
The AHL note also highlighted policy and corporate developments: the government anticipated measures in its 2026-31 auto policy to lift exports by assemblers and parts makers, with a five-year target of $6 billion; ATRL was added to the MSCI FM Standard Index while FLYING and PAKOXT left the MSCI Small Cap Index; and car sales rose sharply to 21,635 units in October from 10,939 in September, bringing the year-to-date total to 63,507 units.
"Heading into the final session of the week, the index stood 2.01% higher, with support seen at 174,000-175,000 and an upside objective near 182,500," AHL said.
Domestically, rising political tensions surrounding the proposed 28th Constitutional Amendment added to market uncertainty. With Friday marking the last trading session of the week and clarity still missing on multiple fronts, cautious sentiment and further selling pressure may persist unless positive developments emerge, as per Ahmed Sheraz of KASB KTrade.
Topline's market review stated that the PSX witnessed a bearish trading session on Thursday, as selling pressure weighed on investor sentiment. The benchmark KSE-100 index declined 1,710 points (-0.95%) to close at 177,374, reflecting cautious investor positioning and profit-taking across the market.
Investor interest remained subdued amid broad-based selling pressure, with market participants adopting a cautious stance following the recent rally. The decline reflected profit-taking and weakness in key index-heavy stocks. UBL, FFC, HUBC, LUCK and SYS emerged as the leading negative contributors, collectively shaving approximately 931 points off the benchmark index, Topline added.
Overall trading volume was recorded at 1.07 billion shares compared with the previous session's tally of 1.25 billion. The value of shares traded during the day was Rs31.64 billion.
Shares of 500 companies were traded in the ready market. Of these, 155 stocks closed higher, 316 fell, and 29 remained unchanged.
WorldCall Telecom was the volume leader with trading in 190.62 million shares, gaining Rs0.03 to close at Rs1.25. It was followed by Tasdeeq Information with 147.36 million shares, losing Rs0.31 to close at Rs5.93, and First National Equities with 55.34 million shares, gaining Rs0.03 to close at Rs1.23. Foreign investors bought shares worth Rs361 million, the National Clearing Company reported.

A recent survey conducted by Kaspersky in the META region shows that AI is becoming part of consumers' everyday lives and users are increasingly turning to AI services for personal matters, raising new privacy and cybersecurity concerns.
Almost 79% of respondents across the Middle East, Turkiye and Africa (META) region reported using AI services, including smart chatbots and image and video generation tools. items.title: PTA halts internet service to unlicensed entities
items.summary:
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) held a meeting with licensed Long Distance International (LDI), Fixed Local Loop (FLL) and Class Value Added Services (CVAS) operators at PTA headquarters to reinforce regulatory compliance and address unauthorised internet service provision.
The meeting highlighted the District Class Licence, enabling Pemra cable operators and last-mile service providers to obtain bandwidth from FLL licensees. It was reiterated that LDI and FLL licensees may provide bandwidth, including configured packages, exclusively to PTA-licensed operators and are prohibited from supplying IP bandwidth, panel services, E1s, DPLCs or similar services to unlicensed entities or distributors. "Internet service bills/receipts must be issued by the relevant FLL or Class Licensee, as applicable," it said.

items.title: SBP Reserves Reach Important Level
items.summary:
The State Bank of Pakistan’s (SBP) foreign exchange reserves rose by $11 million to $21.57 billion during the week ended November 06, 2026.
According to the central bank, its reserves increased by $11 million over the week to $21,573 million. This is the 4th weekly gain in a row.
Total Liquid Reserves Near $27 Billion
The country’s total liquid foreign reserves fell by $26 million to $26.839 billion as of November 06.
This includes $21.57 billion held by the SBP and $5.2666 billion in net reserves held by commercial banks.
Commercial bank reserves were down $26 million from $5.303233 billion a week earlier.
SBP Targets $25 Billion by June
The central bank expects its reserves to reach $23 billion by December 2026 and $25 billion by June 2027.

items.summary:

Zupee Disguise
items.author: Debarghya Sil
items.content:
Delhi NCR-based gaming startup Zupee has nothing more to lose. For one, it has laid off its entire workforce. Then, its announcement of a pivot towards AI has failed to see the light of day.
According to sources, the startup has provided severance pay to the affected employees, covering the period until January 2027, and its October pivot was a veiled attempt to present the impending closure.
The final round of layoffs coincided with Zupee’s public announcement of its foray into AI, Inc42 has learnt. On October 16, the startup said it was positioning its existing technological capabilities as the foundation for its AI ambitions. However, it did not disclose its new gig.
Further, the October layoffs followed two earlier rounds of job cuts. Zupee sacked around 200 employees 10 months before its October layoff and nearly 170 employees before that. At its peak, the startup employed close to 500 employees.
Inc42 reached out to Zupee for comment but did not receive a response.
Zupee Disguises Shutdown?
On October 16, Zupee announced that it was exiting the gaming business and would focus on building AI-led ventures. The ailing startup said it would leverage its experience of serving over 200 Mn users to develop AI products for Indian consumers.
“There was no AI plan. It was a damage control exercise to hide the fact that Zupee was winding down its operations. Currently, they have no employees left, barring 3-4 who are working with the founders,” sources told Inc42.
Meanwhile, Zupee has also shut down its astrology platform, NeoAstro, and its microdrama venture, Zupee Studio, as part of its restructuring in October. The closure of these businesses suggest that Zupee may have already been winding down.
Zupee entered the microdrama segment as part of this diversification strategy. It was in advanced discussions to acquire Vertical TV. “However, the proposed acquisition eventually fell through,” sources said. Inc42 could not independently ascertain the reasons behind this.
Zupee’s downfall began with the ban on real-money gaming (RMG), which dealt a significant blow to its revenue streams. Its existing portfolio of casual games failed to generate enough revenue to offset the loss of its RMG business, pushing the startup to explore alternative avenues.
Will Zupee’s Investors Get Their Money Back
Founded in 2018 by Dilsher Singh Malhi and Siddhant Saurabh, Zupee built its business around mobile versions of traditional Indian games, including Ludo, Snakes and Ladders and Carrom.
Over the years, it had raised over $120 Mn from investors, including Z47, Orios Venture Partners, Nepean Capital, WestCap Group, Tomales Bay Capital and AJ Capital.
With its gaming business discontinued and its other consumer ventures reportedly shut down, questions remain about the startup’s remaining cash reserves, assets and outstanding liabilities.
Inc42 reached out to Zupee’s investors, including Z47 Partners and Nepean Capital, to understand whether they were informed about the impending shutdown and workforce reduction, and whether the AI pivot was presented to them as a genuine business strategy.
Investors have also been asked about the current status of their investment, the possibility of recovering unutilised capital and whether the management has initiated discussions around a potential shutdown or liquidation. However, none of the investors responded to Inc42’s queries.
For a startup that raised close to $120 Mn and built a consumer platform with a claimed user base of over 200 Mn, the developments mark a significant reversal from its earlier growth ambitions.
The post Exclusive: Why Zupee’s AI Pivot Was A Smokescreen For Its Shutdown appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
Pakistan has attracted more than 5,000 attendees from over 60 countries to its international minerals investment forum in Islamabad which could help bring foreign investment into the country’s mining sector.
The two-day Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026 (PMIF26) opened on Thursday, November 12, with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar inaugurating the event and its international exhibition.
Addressing the gathering, Dar said Pakistan had significant potential in copper, gold, iron ore, chromite, lead, zinc, coal, rock salt, marble, gypsum and gemstones. He delved into the country’s copper and gold deposits along the Tethyan Metallogenic Belt and mentioned Reko Diq project in Balochistan as an example of international cooperation in the mining sector.
He said mineral development had become a national economic priority, with the government seeking to diversify exports, strengthen the industrial base and attract domestic and foreign investment.
Finance Minister’s Pitch
Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said Pakistan’s fiscal deficit had fallen to a 22-year low, while the country had recorded primary surpluses for three consecutive years. He also highlighted foreign exchange reserves of $21.5 billion, equivalent to more than three months of import cover.
Aurangzeb said mining could become a major contributor to economic growth, exports and investment. He stressed the importance of investor confidence, including the smooth repatriation of profits and dividends.
He added that sustaining economic stability would require structural reforms and a shift towards export-led growth.
Federal Petroleum Secretary Hamed Yaqoob Sheikh said Pakistan was working with provincial governments and federal institutions to make the mining sector more transparent and investor-friendly.
Reko Diq project and said several other mining projects were ready for investment. He also announced that offshore exploration was set to resume after a gap of several years.
Provincial leaders also presented their investment opportunities and incentives during the forum.
Sindh
Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah said the province had identified 27 minerals and was encouraging scientific exploration, responsible mining and value addition. He invited investors to participate in commercially viable projects, highlighting Thar coal and public-private partnerships.
Punjab
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz announced financial incentives, interest-free loans and one-window facilities for mining investors. She said provincial revenue from the Mines and Minerals Department had increased from Rs. 10 billion to Rs. 40 billion in two and a half years.
She also announced financing of up to Rs. 5 billion, with the provincial government bearing the interest cost, alongside concessional land leases and other incentives for eligible investors.
Balochistan
Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti invited investors to develop the province’s mineral and energy resources. He said a separate security division had been established for the Mineral Corridor to protect investors and mining projects.
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi highlighted more than 100 mineral sites identified under a Geological Survey of Pakistan initiative, with 69 sites under process.
Kashmir
Meanwhile, Azad Jammu and Kashmir Prime Minister Iftikhar Ali Gillani highlighted untapped deposits of ruby, tourmaline, topaz, granite, coal and bauxite.
The forum also featured discussions on financing mineral exploration, developing new mining projects, geological surveys, technology transfer and sustainable mining.
Major international and domestic exhibitors included Barrick Mining Corporation, China Molybdenum, Komatsu, Siemens, ABB, Metso, Mari Energies, Pakistan Petroleum Limited and Pakistan Mineral Development Corporation.
The second day of the forum will take place on Friday, November 13, with further industry discussions, strategic announcements and the unveiling of the National Mineral Data Centre, Geological Survey of Pakistan Geoportal and Agreement Exchange initiative.
The post Pakistan Showcases Its Potential as Next Global Mineral Destination At PMIF 2026 appeared first on ProPakistani.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
United Airlines has announced restrictions on third-party AI assistants, preventing unauthorized AI agents from booking flights, checking in passengers, or making changes to customer accounts.
The US airline announced the policy on November 11, citing concerns about passenger privacy, unauthorized purchases, and compliance with federal aviation regulations.
The restrictions apply to AI agents accessing United’s website and mobile app, as well as those operating through travel agencies and booking platforms.
Why United Airlines Is Blocking AI Agents
United Airlines said allowing AI assistants to access customer accounts could expose sensitive personal and financial information.
AI agents that book flights or manage travel arrangements generally require access to customer information, including account credentials and payment details.
The airline warned that these tools could make purchases, change reservations, or use MileagePlus loyalty miles without the customer’s intended authorization.
United said it is strengthening restrictions on unauthorized AI agents to protect customer accounts and reduce the risk of unwanted transactions.
AI Check-In Could Violate Aviation Regulations
United Airlines also raised concerns about whether automated check-ins performed by AI agents comply with federal regulations.
Under US aviation security requirements, passengers must acknowledge that their checked baggage does not contain prohibited materials, including explosives.
The airline said AI agents performing these steps automatically could bypass the required human acknowledgment.
United cited regulations enforced by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and the Department of Transportation (DOT) as another reason for restricting automated actions.
Restrictions Extend to Travel Agencies
The airline is updating its booking, ticketing, and distribution policies to prevent unauthorized AI agents from interacting with its services.
The restrictions will apply directly to United’s digital platforms and indirectly through travel agencies and flight booking aggregators.
However, the decision does not mean customers will lose access to United flights through established travel booking services.
According to aviation industry analyst Henry Harteveldt of Atmosphere Research Group, travelers will still be able to find and book United flights through platforms such as Google Flights, Kayak, and Hopper.
The restrictions specifically target unauthorized AI agents acting independently on behalf of customers.
Airlines Could Also Face Higher Costs From AI Searches
Harteveldt told CBS News that United’s decision may also reflect concerns about giving AI assistants greater control over the flight booking process.
Airlines already depend on intermediaries such as search engines, comparison websites, and online travel agencies to reach customers.
AI agents could introduce another intermediary capable of automatically searching for flights, comparing prices, and making reservations.
Harteveldt also noted that flight searches generate costs for airlines.
A large increase in automated searches by AI agents could therefore add expenses for carriers, even when those searches do not result in bookings.
However, United’s official explanation focuses on customer security, privacy, and regulatory compliance.
United Will Review AI Restrictions as Technology Develops
United Airlines said it will update its Digital Trust Center to explain the new restrictions and provide guidance for passengers concerned about account security.
The airline also plans to explain how customers can seek assistance if an AI agent performs an unintended action.
United noted that companies in the banking and retail sectors have introduced similar restrictions on third-party AI agents.
The company said it will continue evaluating how personal AI assistants interact with its services as the technology develops.
For now, unauthorized AI agents will not be permitted to complete bookings or manage customer accounts through United’s systems.
