items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
By Fred Chukwuelobe
I don’t mind being called a misogynist or accused of generalising on this matter. Frankly, I think we have reached a point where somebody has to speak out loudly against the inhuman treatment some Igbo women mete out to their domestic servants. And while we are at it, we must also call out their husbands, particularly those who watch helplessly as their wives turn other people’s children into household slaves. Some of these men are either complicit or simply too weak to call their wives to order. For quite some time now, stories of Igbo women who mercilessly maltreat their domestic servants have been making the rounds.
The latest is the disturbing incident in Ogidi, Anambra State, where a woman allegedly beat her 10-year-old domestic servant so mercilessly that a neighbour had to intervene to rescue the child. Reports identified the girl as Chizoba Ifeanyi and the alleged perpetrator as her aunt, Mrs Adaobi Agbonta. The incident reportedly occurred because the little girl refused to sweep the house. Imagine that! What manner of woman beats a ten-year-old child to that extent over an ordinary household chore? What exactly does she expect from a child of that age? And what would have happened if that neighbour had not intervened?
Unfortunately, this is not the first time we have heard such stories. In July 2020, Nigerians were horrified by the story of 10-year-old Nneoma Nnadi in Enugu. Her employer, Ifeoma Ozougwu, was accused of inserting a six-inch nail into the child’s skull, using hot pressing irons on her body and subjecting her to other forms of torture. Her husband was also arrested in connection with the incident. It was one of those stories that made one wonder whether some people were actually human beings. In May 2023, another case emerged from Nkpor, Anambra State, involving an eight-year-old househelp who was allegedly brutally beaten by her employer, Chinyere Ifesinachi. The child reportedly sustained multiple injuries. Then there was the March 2018 case in Lagos involving a woman, Nkeiruka Ngwu, who was arrested for allegedly using a hot pressing iron and hot water on her 10-year-old househelp, Chioma Samuel, a child reportedly brought from Abia State after the death of her father.
These are just some of the reported cases. And before anybody accuses me of deliberately picking on Igbo women, let me acknowledge that similar incidents have occurred in other parts of the country. In March 2026, Premium Times reported the arrest of a woman in Cross River State over the alleged assault of her five-year-old niece, who was reportedly being used as a domestic helper. In Delta State, a woman was sentenced to two years’ imprisonment in 2020 for using a hot kitchen knife to disfigure the mouth of her nine-year-old housemaid. I am not aware of any reliable national statistics establishing which ethnic group records the highest number of such abuses.
But the frequency of disturbing stories involving women in our part of the country should worry us. We cannot continue pretending that nothing is happening. Thank goodness I am Igbo, so nobody should waste time accusing me of Igbophobia. I am talking about a problem that deserves to be confronted within our society. And I am certainly not suggesting that all Igbo women behave this way. Far from it. There are countless decent, compassionate and responsible Igbo women who treat their domestic workers with love and dignity. But those who engage in these atrocities must be called out. What exactly is the matter with some of these women? Why are they so wicked to other people’s children?
These are children born to poor parents, just as their own children were born. Some have lost their parents. Others come from homes where their parents cannot afford to provide for them. They are sent to live with relatives or brought into households where they are expected to receive care, assistance and, in some cases, an opportunity to go to school. Instead, some end up living like slaves. They are made to wake up before everybody else, cook, wash, clean, fetch water, look after babies and perform virtually every household chore. They eat last, sleep last and are often the first to be blamed whenever anything goes wrong. Some are fed with leftovers or denied food altogether for the slightest offence. Others are denied access to education and decent clothing. Once you see some of these women and their children on an outing to events and even church services, you can easily identify the househelp. The difference in their dressing alone tells a story. The madam’s children are beautifully dressed, while the little girl or boy accompanying them looks like somebody picked up from the street.
I recall seeing a woman who took her children to a fast-food restaurant. While the children sat comfortably at the table enjoying their lunch, their domestic servant sat somewhere nearby, clutching madam’s handbag and watching them eat. She was not even treated as someone who deserved to sit at the same table and enjoy a meal. I found the sight particularly disturbing.
I also recall a case in which a woman allegedly used a hot pressing iron on her domestic servant because the child drank a soft drink meant for her own children. A bottle of soft drink! Can you imagine burning another person’s child because she drank what your children were meant to drink?
What kind of wickedness is that?
Some of these women apparently believe that because they provide accommodation and food for their domestic servants, they have acquired ownership of their lives. They forget that these children have parents, feelings, dignity and rights. Even if their parents are dead, they remain human beings deserving of compassion. And what is even more disturbing is that some of these women are regular churchgoers. They attend services, participate in church activities, make donations and sometimes occupy prominent positions in their religious organisations. On Sundays, they sing praises and pray fervently. But when they return home, the same hands that are raised in worship are used to beat and torment another person’s child. What manner of Christianity is that? Then there are the husbands. I have a special word for them. Some of you need to grow a backbone. How can you sit in your living room, know that your wife is beating and maltreating a little child, and pretend that nothing is happening? Is the child not a human being? Does your responsibility to protect the vulnerable end because the person abusing the child happens to be your wife?
Marriage does not require you to surrender your conscience. If your wife is cruel to a domestic servant, call her to order. If she refuses to change, protect the child and involve the appropriate authorities.
 Do not become an accomplice simply because you want peace at home. I also have a word for the relatives who send their children away to live with wealthy relations. Please, do not abandon your parental responsibilities simply because somebody has promised to take care of your child. Visit. Call. Ask questions. Find out what the child eats, where the child sleeps and whether the child is attending school. Do not wait until the child returns home with scars or ends up in a hospital before you realise that something has gone terribly wrong.
WE MUST DECLARE WAR ON THIS PRACTICE.
I believe it is time for Igbo sociocultural organisations, town unions, women’s organisations, civil society groups and religious institutions to take this matter seriously. It should no longer be treated as an ordinary domestic disagreement. Where are our women organisations? Where are the church groups that organise meetings every week? Where are the Christian Mothers’ organisations? Where are the wives of our governors? Why should we wait until another child is nearly killed before everybody starts issuing statements? The First Ladies of the South-East states should take up this challenge and champion a regional campaign against the abuse of domestic workers. Traditional rulers, presidents-general of town unions and community leaders should make child protection a regular subject of discussion in their communities. Our governments must also wake up. The Child Rights Act and the corresponding state laws provide a legal framework for protecting children against abuse, exploitation and neglect. These laws must be enforced. Those found guilty of abusing children should face the full consequences of the law. We must stop the practice of settling serious cases of child abuse quietly within families or through some backdoor community arrangement. 
If existing laws are inadequate, the state legislatures should strengthen them. There should also be proper regulation of domestic-worker recruitment, particularly where children are involved. No child should be handed over to an employer under an arrangement that leaves the child without protection or accountability.
Neighbours must also learn to intervene. If you hear a child screaming persistently or notice unexplained injuries, do not look the other way. Report the matter. You may be saving a child’s life.
I am particularly concerned that the behaviour of these women is beginning to cast an unnecessary shadow on other Igbo women who are decent, responsible and compassionate towards their domestic workers. That is unfair to the many women who treat their househelps as human beings, provide for their education and give them opportunities they might otherwise not have had. But decent people must not remain silent while others behave like monsters. We must also stop pretending that every child brought into a home as a househelp is necessarily enjoying some form of privilege. In some cases, what is happening is nothing short of exploitation. A child who is denied education, adequate food, decent accommodation and basic human dignity, while being compelled to work from morning till night, is not enjoying the benefits of living with a wealthy family. That child is being exploited.
Slavery ended centuries ago. It must not be surreptitiously reintroduced through the back door by women who believe that other people’s children are available for them to treat anyhow.
I have said my piece. It is time for our communities, governments, religious institutions and, particularly, the womenfolk to rise against this barbaric practice. We cannot continue to look away while vulnerable children are subjected to indignity and cruelty in the very homes where they should be safe. A househelp is not a slave. A poor child is not a second-class human being. And no amount of wealth, marriage or social status can excuse cruelty. That is the message we must send, loudly and unequivocally.
•Chukwuelobe wrote in from Lagos.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Chimaobi Nwaiwu
NNEWI — South-East governors have been urged to support and patronise factories and companies established by indigenes of the zone to generate employment, tackle insecurity and unemployment, and accelerate regional development.
The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Audi Company Limited, Dr Clem Ifezue, made the call in an exclusive interview with Vanguard in Awka, Anambra State.
Ifezue, an Anambra-born industrialist, said indigenous industries had the capacity to provide jobs for thousands of unemployed people and contribute significantly to the economic growth of the South-East if given adequate government support and patronage.
He said Audi Company Limited was a technical products and services marketing company registered in Nigeria, with a vision to assemble leading global brands and make them readily available to Nigerians.
According to him, the company has been operating for over 20 years, with branches across the country’s regions, including Enugu, and partnerships with several local and international companies.
Highlighting areas where South-East governors could partner with the company, Ifezue said its operations covered automobile assembly, power solutions, marine logistics and engineering works.
He explained that the company’s power solutions included generators powered by Perkins and York engines of British origin, as well as solar systems, hybrid inverters, lithium batteries and solar panels.
“When I say power solution, it means that we have our own brand of generators, using Perkins and York engines, both of United Kingdom origin.
“We have been in existence for a while and Nigerians have been enjoying the quality of our products and can attest to that.
“We have our own brand of solar system, we have our inverter which is hybrid, we have our battery which is lithium and we have our solar panels, with well-trained engineers and technicians working for us. We are a big employer of labour,” he said.
On marine logistics, Ifezue said the company had partnerships in boat construction and the provision of marine facilities for transportation, fishing and movement of goods, among other applications.
He also disclosed that the company was involved in engineering and construction projects for state governments and private individuals.
Ifezue, who is also the Director-General of the Mines Crafts Registered Association of Nigeria, said South-East governors could leverage the company’s expertise to attract investments and accelerate infrastructure development in the region.
The former General Manager of John Holt Plc lamented the difficulties of establishing and sustaining businesses in Nigeria, attributing some of the challenges to what he described as inadequate government emphasis on supporting indigenous enterprises.
He said local companies often competed with foreign operators who had limited investments and business establishments in Nigeria but were still able to secure contracts and patronage.
“We compete with a lot of people who do not have anything here in Nigeria, people who just come with one briefcase, do business and go, but we are established here.
“That is why we said we represent the best brands. Together with Mikano Motors, we assemble cars, sell and maintain the cars in Nigeria,” he said.
He acknowledged the Federal Government’s efforts to reduce high bank interest rates, but argued that more deliberate policies were needed to enable indigenous companies to compete effectively and provide quality products at affordable prices.
According to him, government remains the biggest spender in Nigeria through its activities at the federal, state and local government levels and could significantly influence the growth of local industries through its procurement decisions.
He cited the purchase of official vehicles, equipment for government agencies and vehicles for public officers as areas where governments could patronise locally assembled products.
Ifezue also referenced the Ebonyi State Government’s provision of vehicles to doctors serving in rural communities as an example of how government procurement could support public service delivery and local businesses.
“If government is sincere with their preaching of patronising Made-in-Nigeria goods, it will be a good thing for the economy.
“It is by so doing that our competitors will begin to think of setting up plants here, but as far as the government is ignoring indigenous companies and patronising those that are not established here, that campaign will not be successful,” he said.
He urged governments at all levels to extend their patronage beyond automobile assembly plants to other products manufactured locally, arguing that such a policy would stimulate investment, create employment and strengthen the economy.
Ifezue expressed optimism that a coordinated partnership between South-East governors and indigenous businesses would encourage more investors to establish factories in the region.
“If the South-East governors can come together and form an alliance with us, more industries will be attracted and located here, our people will be employed and more development will come.
“Location of industries goes with numbers. If we are assured of high patronage, more people will set up factories and our people stand to gain. No investor will like to invest where he cannot make a profit,” he said.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
The United Nations General Assembly has, for the first time, formally endorsed a global shift away from the centuries-old Mercator map in favour of projections that show Africa—and other equatorial regions—in their true relative size. This “Correct the Map” resolution, spearheaded by Togo on behalf of the African Group and backed by the African Union, passed by 164 votes to one, with six abstentions.
While non-binding, it marks a watershed moment in how the world visually represents the continent—and, by extension, how it perceives Africa’s weight in global affairs. The root of the misrepresentation lies in the Mercator projection, devised in 1569 by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator for maritime navigation. To keep compass bearings straight, Mercator preserved angles and shapes—but at the cost of area. The result: landmasses near the poles, such as Europe, North America and Greenland, are visually enlarged, while those near the equator, including Africa, Latin America and South Asia, are shrunk.
On typical Mercator wall maps, Greenland appears roughly the same size as Africa. In reality, Africa covers about 30.3 million square kilometres, making it around 14 times larger than Greenland’s 2.1 million square kilometres. This is not a minor quirk; it is a systematic visual bias baked into the most widely used world map for nearly five centuries. The resolution encourages governments, schools, international organisations, media houses and technology companies to adopt equal-area projections, especially the Equal Earth projection, whenever comparative continental size matters. It frames map distortion as more than a technical issue—calling it a cognitive, educational, cultural and geopolitical problem that has contributed to the symbolic minimisation of Africa in the global imagination. While symbolic correction matters, Africa’s greatest vulnerabilities lie in structural exploitation and escalating insecurity, notably from Islamist insurgencies across the Sahel, Lake Chad Basin and parts of the Horn. Map reform must be paired with hard-edged action on multiple fronts.
First, curb external exploitation and illicit financial flows by tightening transparency on extractives, choking illicit financial flows through cross-border tax cooperation, and rebalancing investment terms to prioritise local content and value addition. Second, confront Islamist insecurity with a whole-of-system approach by funding and professionalising regional forces, targeting financing networks that fuel insurgencies, investing in governance at the frontier, and countering extremist narratives through community engagement.
Third, lock in development dividends that undercut recruitment by expanding vocational training and agro-processing corridors tied to the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), funding climate-resilient livelihoods, and prioritising children’s education and primary healthcare. Fourth, reform global governance to reflect Africa’s weight by pressing for permanent African seats at the UN Security Council. The UN’s “Correct the Map” resolution is a necessary correction of a 450-year-old visual injustice. But maps alone do not feed children, stop bullets or reclaim stolen wealth.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Luminous Jannamike
ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has accused President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress, APC, of recycling unfulfilled 2023 campaign promises in their newly unveiled 2027 manifesto, challenging the President to account for his record before seeking another mandate.
The party said the manifesto reads like the programme of a political party seeking power for the first time, rather than that of a government that has controlled the Federal Government for nearly 12 years and has had more than three years under Tinubu to deliver on its promises.
In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC cited healthcare coverage, ICT job creation and electricity generation as examples of promises it said the administration had failed to fulfil, questioning why Nigerians should be asked to embrace another set of commitments without an account of the previous ones.
“The fundamental question Nigerians must ask is simple: Why is a government campaigning on promises it should already have fulfilled? President Tinubu has been in office since May 2023. The APC has controlled the Federal Government for nearly twelve years. Yet, reading this manifesto, one would think they are only now discovering the problems they were elected to solve,” the ADC said.
The party recalled that Tinubu had promised in 2023 to extend health insurance coverage to 40 per cent of Nigerians within two years and create one million ICT jobs within 24 months.
It claimed that barely one in ten Nigerians was now covered by health insurance, while government figures indicated that only about 15,000 jobs and opportunity pathways had been recorded, with the health insurance target shifted to 2031.
The ADC also questioned the administration’s electricity performance, pointing out that the APC had described 4,500 megawatts of power generation as a crisis in 2023, only for its new manifesto to acknowledge average generation of 4,022 megawatts.
“How does a government campaign to solve a crisis it has made remarkably worse?” the party queried.
The opposition party further faulted Tinubu’s promise to introduce a programme for his first 100 days after re-election, arguing that the President already had the executive powers to implement the proposed measures without waiting for another electoral victory.
“Most astonishingly, President Tinubu now promises a programme for his first 100 days after re-election, including measures he already possesses the executive powers to implement right now. What exactly is stopping him from acting today? What stopped him from acting in 2023 when he came into office?” the ADC asked.
On the economy, the party accused the President of seeking another mandate without addressing the hardship confronting millions of households, claiming that poverty had risen to 63 per cent and the N70,000 minimum wage had lost more than a quarter of its purchasing power.
“Yet, rather than account for the hardship he has inflicted on Nigerians and his long catalogue of failures across the economy and security sectors, the president and his party have the temerity to present another colourful brochure full of the same undelivered promises,” the statement said.
The ADC insisted that campaign promises could no longer substitute for an assessment of the administration’s performance.
“A manifesto is a promise of what a party will do. A record is evidence of what it has done. After eleven years, the APC cannot keep presenting promises as a substitute for performance,” it declared.
It challenged Tinubu to publish a comprehensive account of his 2023 commitments, detailing what he had delivered, what remained unfulfilled and why the deadlines were missed, rather than shifting targets and repackaging old promises.
The party said the 2027 election would be a referendum on Tinubu’s performance since assuming office, not an opportunity for him to present his presidency as though it were just beginning.
“The President must understand that 2027 is first a referendum on his abysmal record since 2023, not an opportunity to pretend that his presidency is just about to begin. Nigeria needs a change of government, not another change of slogans,” the ADC declared.Police avert communal crisis as youths clash over colleague’s death in Kaduna
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo
The Kaduna State Police Command has averted a possible communal crisis following a clash between rival youth groups from Kwaru and Unguwar Yero communities in Kaduna North Local Government Area of the state.
The incident, which reportedly left some people injured, occurred on Wednesday morning following tension over the death of a youth who sustained injuries during an earlier confrontation between young people from the two communities.
The deceased, reportedly from Unguwar Yero, was said to have died from injuries sustained during the disagreement about a week ago, triggering anger among his friends, who allegedly attempted to avenge his death on Wednesday.
The development caused panic among residents, with some schoolchildren reportedly fleeing their schools as rival groups engaged in stone-throwing and other acts of violence.
A resident of Kwaru, who identified himself as Sule, said the incident occurred around 9am when he heard noise and came out to see youths throwing stones at one another.
“Some youths from Kwaru and Unguwar Yero had a disagreement about a week ago, during which a young man was injured and later died.
“On Wednesday, after the children had gone to school, we started hearing noise. When I came out, I saw people gathering, while some were throwing stones at one another between the youths from Unguwar Yero and some residents of Kwaru who had gone to the cemetery,” he said.
Sule said the incident heightened tension in the area, recalling that the two communities had experienced similar disagreements in the past before relative peace was restored.
He confirmed that operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS), police and Mobile Police (MOPOL), among other security personnel, were deployed to the area to prevent further escalation and restore normalcy.
Another resident, Mohammed, expressed concern over recurring disagreements among young people from the two communities.
He said many of the youths were friends who often gathered together, adding that it was unfortunate that disagreements between them were sometimes given ethnic or religious interpretations.
“They are youths who are friends, but whenever there is a disagreement among them, some people try to turn it into an ethnic or religious issue. That is not right,” he said.
A teacher in the area, Bashir, also confirmed that three youths sustained injuries during the earlier confrontation, adding that one of them later died.
He, however, said normal activities had started returning to the communities following the deployment of security personnel.
There were also indications that the tension threatened to spread to neighbouring communities before security operatives intervened.
The Kaduna State Police Command spokesman, DSP Mansir Hassan, confirmed the incident, saying the situation had been brought under control following the deployment of security personnel.
“The situation is under control following a massive deployment of security personnel to the communities,” he said.
The police intervention prevented the disagreement from degenerating into a wider security crisis, even as residents called for sustained security presence and peaceful engagement among youths and community stakeholders to forestall further violence.
It was not confirmed as of the time of filing this report whether a curfew had been imposed on the affected communities.

items.content:
By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse
Former Jigawa State Governor, Sule Lamido, has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of using his name to gain political sympathy in the state ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Lamido made the allegation on Tuesday while reacting to Vice-President Kashim Shettima’s declaration at the APC presidential campaign rally in Dutse that all four former governors of Jigawa State, including Lamido, were now supporting the ruling party.
Shettima had, during the rally, declared that Jigawa was firmly behind the APC, claiming that all four former governors of the state, including Lamido, a founding member of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), were now associated with the ruling party.
However, Lamido dismissed the claim as false and unfounded, alleging that the APC was attempting to associate itself with influential opposition figures to gain public sympathy.
He argued that the ruling party could not point to significant achievements in Jigawa State and the wider Northern region, hence its alleged attempt to claim the support of prominent opposition politicians.
“I am not aware of what Vice-President Kashim Shettima was saying. For God’s sake, I was not with the APC in 2014, so why would I be with it now in 2026?” Lamido queried.
The former governor challenged the APC to identify its achievements in Jigawa and other parts of the North, arguing that its inability to demonstrate meaningful accomplishments had made it resort to associating itself with influential Northern politicians.
Lamido, however, outlined conditions under which he would consider joining the APC before the 2027 general elections, challenging President Bola Tinubu’s administration to address insecurity in the North.
He specifically mentioned kidnapping, Boko Haram insurgency, banditry and other security challenges, saying their resolution would make him reconsider his political position.
“I swear to God, if they end kidnapping, Boko Haram, banditry and all the evils in the North, I will definitely join the APC because whatever we are doing, we are doing it for our people,” he said.

items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
Spain coach Luis de la Fuente said Wednesday he is optimistic Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal will be fit to face England in the Nations League at the weekend.
The 19-year-old winger will miss the world champions’ visit to face the Czech Republic in Prague on Thursday with a knee problem and is set to join up with Spain after that game.
Yamal played for Barcelona in the 2-1 La Liga win over Atletico Madrid on Sunday and on Monday Spain said he would not travel to face the Czechs.
“He got hurt in the last match, he had some discomfort in one knee, he went for the usual treatment, a scan in Barcelona, and they saw he had inflammation and fluid in the knee — that meant he needed rest,” De la Fuente told reporters.
“Our medical staff and his medical staff have a fantastic relationship, and I decided that his trip here should be avoided without knowing whether he’d be in any condition to play.”
The coach said he had spoken to the winger and his recovery was looking positive ahead of England’s visit to Madrid on Sunday.
“He’s doing a series of exercises with his physio and with the club that indicate the recovery is going well,” continued De la Fuente.
“We believe, I’m optimistic, that on Friday he’ll be with us.”
De la Fuente dismissed the idea that Yamal, who came third in the Ballon d’Or voting in October, has any special privileges compared to his La Roja team-mates.
“He has no privileges, and his team-mates are relaxed about it, because we treat everyone the same,” added the coach.
“In similar situations we would have done exactly the same for any other player, and the players know that.”
– Unstoppable run –
Spain have won all four games so far in Group A3 and sealed qualification to the quarter-finals.
De la Fuente’s side are unbeaten in their last 43 competitive outings, and the coach said it provided his team with extra motivation.
“We want to keep setting new milestones, and this is another one,” explained De la Fuente.
“None of us would probably ever have thought we’d even reach 35, because we already felt those were astronomical numbers, but having reached 43, you think, my goodness, we want to get to 44, of course we do.”
Spain won their previous outing away in Croatia with a brace from Arsenal’s Mikel Merino.
The midfielder is frequently used as a substitute by De la Fuente to great effect, with Merino netting vital goals against Portugal and Belgium in the World Cup off the bench this summer.
Merino said he would like to be a starter for Spain but he would not kick up a fuss.
“Of course, what player wouldn’t like to get (more) minutes?” Merino told reporters.
“You’ll never hear me complain about the coach’s decision, I will respect it… but all players want to be important, have minutes and enjoy themselves on the pitch.”

items.title: DSS foils major terror plot, intercepts 21 AK-47s, other arms from Niger in Sokoto
items.summary:
By Soni Daniel, Northern Region Editor

By Soni Daniel, Northern Region Editor
Barely 70 days to the the 2027 general elections, the Department of State Security Services has foiled a major terror plot by intercepting a large consignment of high-calibre weapons and ammunition smuggled into the country from Niger Republic.
The weapons, including 21 AK-47 rifles, 4 PKT machine guns and 825 magazines, were intercepted exclusively by DSS officers in Dawakawa, Goronyo Local Government Area of Sokoto State, following intensive surveillance of terror cells seeking to transport deadly weapons into Nigeria ahead of the general elections.
A security source disclosed that, given increased interception of illegal weapons by the DSS around the country, terror groups have turned to women and beasts of burden, particularly camels, to move illegal weapons into and around the country.
It will be recalled that earlier in the week, DSS operatives in Talata Mafaran LGA of Zamfara State, arrested another suspected female arms courier, Hafsat Umar.
Umar, who was arrested with 12 grenades and two ammunition belts, is the 14th female illegal arms courier arrested by the DSS between February 2025 and November 2026.
Intelligence indicated that the suspected illegal arms courier travelled to Niger State to source ammunition for delivery to a notorious bandit leader, Saidu Marafa, who is based in Kani Kawa, Maradun LGA of Zamfara State.
The arrests by the DSS span Zamfara, Nasarawa, Ebonyi, Taraba, Kaduna and Plateau States.
Notable among the arrests was that of Aisha Mohammed, apprehended last month in Keffi, Nasarawa State, while allegedly conveying arms and ammunition through a notorious arms dealer and kidnapper simply called Sani.
Recovered from Aisha were 202 rounds of 7.62mm AK-47 ammunition and three empty AK-47 magazines.
In September, 2026, two female couriers, Chika Aguzie and Blessing Nwamba were arrested at separate locations in Ebonyi State over their alleged involvement in the supply of weapons and explosives to commanders of the outlawed Eastern Security Network (ESN).
The commanders include Chinonso Amobi Okafor, aka Temple, and B44, reportedly based in Anambra State. 14 wraps of IED detonators, were recovered during the operation.
In August, DSS arrested one Rabiatu Halidu, on Abacha Road, Katu LGA of Nasarawa State with 501 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition.
In February, DSS officers arrested one Aisha Ibrahim in Tsafe, LGA of Zamfara State, with 975 rounds of ammunition.
Arested in January were Sakina Muhammad and Badariyya Abubakar, along Wukari-Jalingo Road, Taraba State, with one AK-47 rifle, 984 rounds of special ammunition, 105 rounds of GPMG ammunition and 14 empty AK-47 magazines.
The Service also recorded several arrests in 2025, including Rahane Sanusi, in Talatan Mafara LGA of Zamfara State. She was caught while conveying ammunition from an illegal arms dealer in Sokoto State to a notorious bandit, Ibrahim Bare, aka Baba, in Anka LGA of the state.
Also arrested during the period was Suwaiba Abubakar, Halima Umar, Firdausi Haruna, Saidya Ibrahim and Fatima Sani, with varying quantities of arms and ammunition recovered from them.
Recall that, early in the year, the Federal High Court, Abuja, handed convicted some women for terrorism-related cases involving female arms couriers arrested by the DSS. In two instances, three female couriers, identified as Halima Abdullahi, Safiya Salihu and Halima Umar, were convicted and sentenced to 20 years’ imprisonment each following their arraignment on terrorism-related charges by the DSS.
“Like the others before her,” noted a security source, “Hafsat Umar will also be charged to court, and the DSS will use intelligence at their disposal to bring other criminals to justice.”
“The DSS will continue to leverage on actionable intelligence and sustained tactical operations to identify, identify and apprehend all individuals involved in the illegal arms trade and bring them to justice,” declared the source.

items.content:
By Henry Umoru
Strong indications have emerged that crisis looms in the family of the opposition political party, the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC following the dumping of the party by the Deputy National Publicity Secretary, Hon. Abdulmumin Ohiare Abdulsalami.
Abdulsalami announced his resignation on Wednesday night in a formal letter addressed to the National Chairman, NDC, Senator Moses Cleopas.
He said he was “calling it quits and heading back home and avoiding orchestrated melodrama of exclusion from party affairs”
He explained his decision in his letter titled: “Letter of resignation from the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC: withdrawal from all partisan commitments to the party”
Abdulsalami said, “With a deep sense of gratitude to almighty Allah, I hereby notify the national and sub-national organs of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), through my former ward chairman, of my resignation from the party. I have also, by this notification, withdrawn from all ongoing technical and political commitments entered into at the pleasure of the National Leader of the NDC.
“As a foundation member of the NDC, ditto a critical formative leader in the party, I am compelled to voluntarily take the exit having realized that my sincere and positive contributions to the meteoric rise and success of the party are at odds with the vested interests of a few powerful officers who call the shots.
“More so, this painstaking decision serves my best interest as I prioritise my peace of mind rather than recurrent complaints at the sight of series of injustice meted out to me.
“More so, I wish to sincerely appreciate the opportunity given to me by the National Leader of the NDC, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson to have served, firstly, as the Kogi State Protem Chairman, secondly, as the Deputy National Publicity Secretary/pioneer Spokesperson of the NDC, and, finally, as the Deputy National Director for Labour and Civil Society of the party.
“And to my erstwhile colleague-friends, civil society activists and media practitioners with whom I have worked assiduously to promote the party, I cannot thank you enough for the comradeship and support you all have accorded me since the infancy of the
party, and throughout my partisan stewardship thereupon.”
In a related development, Dr. Yunusa Tanko has dumped the Presidential candidate of the NDC ahead of January 16 2027 election, Peter Obi as the national coordinator of the Obidient Movement for the North for the Social Democratic Party, SDP.
He was announced the National Coordinator in September following a consensus to zone the position to the North.
Obi appointed Tanko as national coordinator of the Obidient Movement in September 2024, following a consensus to zone the position to the North.
Tanko previously served as Obi’s presidential campaign spokesman during the 2023 general elections, when the former Anambra State governor contested under the platform of the Labour Party (LP).
He was also the presidential candidate of the Northern People’s Congress (NPC) in 2019 and became the party’s national chairman in 2023.
The SDP on Wednesday inauagurated Yunusa Tanko as the national coordinator of its presidential campaign council for the 2027 general elections.
Tanko’s appointment was announced during the inauguration of the party’s presidential campaign council in Abuja.
The appointment was also confirmed by Mark Adebayo, Chief Media and Communications Adviser to the Adebayo/Bugaje Presidential Campaign Council.
Speaking at the event, Tanko pledged to work with the SDP presidential candidate, Adewale Adebayo, and his running mate, Usman Bugaje, to secure victory in the 2027 elections.
Describing the SDP as a left-wing, people-oriented political party, Tanko said it was committed to representing the interests of disadvantaged Nigerians who had been neglected by those in positions of authority.
“The SDP is a left-wing political party. For those of you who do not know, we represent the interests of the downtrodden. The SDP represents those people that you neglect on the streets. So, that makes this particular party people-oriented,” he said.
Tanko who disclosed that he resigned as political adviser (North) to Peter Obi, presidential candidate NDC on October 30, explained that his resignation followed his appointment to the leadership of the National Consultative Front (NCFront), following the death of Ghali Na’Abba, the organisation’s former co-chairman and former Speaker of the House of Representatives.
Tanko said he had reached out to Obi and Seriake Dickson, national leader of the NDC, expressing appreciation for their support during his tenure as coordinator of the Obidient Movement.
Tanko who pledged to work with the NCFront leadership and Adebayo, noting that his relationship with the SDP presidential candidate dated back to 2023 and that both shared a commitment to building a better Nigeria, said, “In advancing our political mission to a new Nigeria that works for all, I pledge to remain consistent and committed to our unwavering belief in good governance, justice, equity, national loyalty and dedication, and an unwavering commitment to moving Nigeria from where it is today to a better and more prosperous nation,” he said.
Vanguard News

items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
The Canada government has announced plans to accelerate permanent residence (PR) processing for up to 200,000 foreign nationals already living in the country in 2027, as part of efforts to reduce immigration application backlogs and provide greater certainty for newcomers.
The initiative, announced by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) under the 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan, will provide additional admissions spaces for selected workers and humanitarian applicants seeking to transition to permanent residence.
According to the government, the measure will be implemented through two major groups: a workers’ cohort and a humanitarian cohort, with up to 100,000 spaces allocated to each.
The workers’ category will cover eligible foreign workers already living in Canada, alongside their accompanying family members. The government intends to work with provincial and territorial authorities to identify workers who meet regional labour market requirements.
Eligible workers will include those who qualify for permanent residence through the Provincial Nominee Program (PNP), as well as applicants awaiting decisions under selected federal immigration programmes.
These programmes include the Atlantic Immigration Program, Start-Up Visa Program, Self-Employed Persons Program, Agri-Food Pilot and Home Care Worker programmes.
The humanitarian category, also allocated up to 100,000 spaces, will cover people already in Canada who have been waiting for permanent residence decisions, including applicants under specific family reunification and humanitarian pathways.
Among those expected to benefit from the humanitarian allocation are:
Spouses, common-law partners and dependent children: Family members of Canadian citizens and permanent residents who have already applied for permanent residence and are awaiting final decisions.
Hong Kong residents: Applicants under Canada’s permanent residence pathways for Hong Kong residents, which closed to new applications on August 31, 2026.
Ukrainian nationals: Applicants under the Ukraine Family Reunification Pathway, which closed to new applications on October 22, 2024.
Humanitarian and compassionate applicants: Individuals already in Canada whose applications for permanent residence have received approval in principle. The government said the additional spaces would help it process all remaining applications under the Hong Kong and Ukraine pathways, while also supporting family reunification and fulfilling existing humanitarian commitments.
IRCC also said the initiative would help reduce waiting periods for spouses and partners of Canadian citizens and permanent residents, with the aim of bringing processing times closer to 12 months for applicants destined for provinces outside Quebec.
The department clarified that eligible applicants do not need to submit a separate application or take additional steps to be considered under the temporary initiative.
However, the measure does not represent a new immigration pathway for people applying from outside Canada. It is specifically designed for individuals already living in the country who fall within the selected categories.
The 200,000 additional spaces will also be separate from Canada’s regular permanent residence admissions target of 380,000 for 2027.
Under its 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan, Canada intends to maintain annual permanent residence admissions at 380,000, while targeting 370,000 new temporary resident arrivals, comprising 220,000 workers and 150,000 international students in 2027.
The initiative forms part of Canada’s broader efforts to stabilise its immigration system, address labour shortages, reduce application backlogs and support people who have already established lives and communities in the country.

items.content:
The United States has withdrawn from the upcoming Under-17 soccer World Cup in Qatar due to concerns about security in the Middle East, US media reported Wednesday.
Players were informed of the decision just over a week before the tournament is due to begin on November 19, US Soccer Collective and The Athletic reported, citing anonymous sources.
US Soccer, the sport’s governing body in the United States, did not immediately confirm the news or respond to AFP’s request for comment.
The war in the Middle East began in February with joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran, which retaliated by targeting, among others, Gulf countries allied with Washington.
Diplomatic efforts to end the conflict have been punctuated by repeated threats from the United States and Israel to resume bombardments of Iran.
Multiple sporting events in the Middle East have been affected, including the tennis WTA Finals which were scheduled to be held in Saudi Arabia — which neighbors Qatar — but are instead now taking place at Indian Wells in the US.
This season’s Formula One Grand Prix in Jeddah was cancelled, while the race in Bahrain was called off and later rescheduled under the same name in Malaysia.
Several events in Saudi Arabia have also been cancelled or postponed in recent weeks following attacks on the country by the Houthis in Yemen.
The US is one of 48 teams scheduled to play in the Under-17 World Cup, in a group with Montenegro, Chile and Algeria.
The Under-17 World Cup shifted to an annual event last year, and is being held in Qatar for five consecutive years.
Announcing its host decision in 2024, FIFA said the decision to choose a single host nation for multiple editions centered on the ability to make “use of existing footballing infrastructure in the interest of tournament efficiencies and sustainability”.
Qatar was the venue for the 2022 men’s World Cup.

By Ike Uchechukwu
Cross River State Governor, Sen Bassey Otu, has dissolved the State Planning and Development Control Task Force and ordered compensation for the owner of a nearly completed building its personnel pulled down.
The Governor who described the action as an abuse of power said it was a assault on the rights of a citizen.
In a press statement issued in Calabar on Wednesday by his Chief Press Secretary, Mr. Linus Obogo, the governor described the demolition as brazen, unconscionable and reprehensible.
Governor Otu held the Task Force accountable for what the statement called gross team failure, and directed the immediate suspension of further demolition activities on the affected property.
He also ordered the payment of compensation for the damage caused by the demolition.
“Alleged violations of physical planning regulations cannot constitute a license for lawlessness,” the governor said.
“No public institution can arrogate to itself powers that trample upon the rights and dignity of citizens.”
According to him, such high-handedness, impunity and administrative recklessness are incompatible with the philosophy of his administration.
“No individual, irrespective of position or institutional authority, enjoys the privilege of exercising public power recklessly, vindictively or outside the boundaries of established law and due process,” Otu stated.
The governor warned that his administration would not tolerate official misconduct in any form.
“My administration will neither shield, excuse nor reward official misconduct under any guise,” he declared.
“Public office is a solemn trust, not an instrument of intimidation or oppression.”
He directed all government agencies to operate with discipline, restraint, professionalism and the utmost respect for the rights of the people.
“Under my watch, government will protect citizens and residents, uphold justice and insist that accountability remains non-negotiable,” the governor said.
Checks by Vanguard showed that the demolished building located along parliamentary extension ,boulevard axis calabar Municipality Local Government Area in Calabar .
Further Checks also showed that the building in question belongs to Mr Olajide Jamil who runs the popular Cent Apartment , and reportedly brought in investors from the United States of America to invest in real estate in Cross River State

items.summary:
All seven co-founders of Anthropic will each sell about $250 million worth of shares in the AI company’s upcoming IPO, according to its updated S-1 filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission.
Each founder plans to sell 3,378,378 shares. Anthropic has set a price range of $70 to $78 per share, which puts the IPO at an implied valuation of about $1.4 trillion.
How Much Each Founder Gets
At the midpoint price of $74, each founder would collect just under $250 million. At $70, the payout drops to just over $236 million, while at $78 it rises to just under $264 million. Together, the seven would raise roughly $1.75 billion.

The seven co-founders are Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei, Tom Brown, Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish and Christopher Olah. They left OpenAI in 2021 to start Anthropic over disagreements on how AI should be built.
After the sale, each will own about 3.2% of Anthropic’s Class A shares, or roughly 22% together. Their stake in the overall company is smaller, as investors such as Amazon and Google hold non-voting Class N shares.
However, each founder will also receive one Class F share with super-voting rights. Collectively, the founders will control 51.1% of the votes, keeping the company firmly in their hands.
The update follows an earlier mix-up when Anthropic briefly circulated IPO pricing details and then withdrew them. The company first filed for its IPO in October.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) will use an automated system to check income tax returns filed for tax year 2026 and notify taxpayers about possible errors or discrepancies before taking legal action.
The new system, called Computerized Risk Management (CRM), will electronically review returns and allow taxpayers to explain differences, correct mistakes or take other necessary steps.
FBR has introduced the mechanism through S.R.O. 2098(I)/2026 by adding Rule 38B to the Income Tax Rules, 2002. The new rule covers the electronic scrutiny of returns and notification of issues identified by the automated system.
Under the amended rules, the system will process income tax returns filed under Section 120(2A) of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001. It may send taxpayers online notices through the IRIS portal, highlighting possible factual or legal errors.
Taxpayers will receive at least seven days to respond to the notice, explain the discrepancies or correct their returns. If they do not respond within the given time, the system will send a reminder providing another period of at least seven days.
The rules also allow the relevant Inland Revenue officer to issue advance notices identifying discrepancies in a taxpayer’s return.
All identified issues, notices sent to taxpayers and their responses will be shared with the relevant Inland Revenue officer and recorded on a dedicated dashboard.
The officer will review the taxpayer’s response or failure to respond and decide whether further action is required under the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001.
FBR will implement the automated scrutiny, data matching, discrepancy identification and electronic communication process through a Change Request Form (CRF).

items.author: Abdul Rahman
items.content:
Private sector borrowing from commercial banks surged 3,717 percent during the first four months of FY27, reaching Rs. 217 billion compared with just Rs. 5.685 billion in the same period last year.
According to data released by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP), businesses and other private borrowers took significantly more financing between July and October 2026, despite relatively high borrowing costs.
The data also shows a major difference between conventional banks, their Islamic banking operations and full-fledged Islamic banks.
Pakistan’s six full-fledged Islamic banks recorded net repayments of Rs. 7.6 billion during the period. These include Meezan Bank, Faysal Bank, BankIslami, Dubai Islamic Bank, Al Baraka Bank and MCB Islamic Bank.
In comparison, conventional banks provided around Rs. 70 billion in net financing to the private sector. Their Islamic banking branches and windows extended another Rs. 154 billion.
This means conventional banking groups, including their Islamic banking operations, accounted for the bulk of private sector financing during the four-month period.
The trend is different from the same period last year, when conventional banks recorded net repayments by private borrowers, while the Islamic banking industry continued to provide financing.
Banking analysts attributed the increase in borrowing to government-backed financing schemes for housing, small and medium enterprises (SMEs), agriculture and export-oriented businesses.
They also said companies were borrowing more to meet day-to-day working capital needs and finance new investments despite high interest rates.
Consumer financing has also picked up, with banks reporting stronger demand for car loans, credit cards, personal loans and financing for consumer goods.

items.title: 11 Children Rescued From Burning Van on Major Motorway
items.summary:
The National Highways and Motorway Police (NHMP) rescued 11 children and all other passengers from a burning Hiace van on the M3 Motorway near Sharaqpur.
According to Syed Imran Ahmed, spokesperson for the NHMP Central Region, the van caught fire due to a short circuit while it was travelling from Lahore to Multan. Several passengers, including women and children, were on board. Among them were 11 children.
Quick Response Saves Lives
The spokesperson said Motorway Police officers reached the scene immediately after receiving the report. They safely pulled all passengers and children out of the burning van.
All passengers remained safe, and no lives were lost in the incident. The spokesperson said the timely action of the Motorway Police prevented a major tragedy.
After the rescue, the officers moved the passengers and children to a safe place and carried out the necessary relief work.

items.author: Danial Saigra
items.content:
The Punjab Wildlife and Parks Department has announced new job opportunities for qualified, experienced professionals in several fields.
According to the official recruitment advertisement, the department is offering 11 vacancies across 10 positions at the Changa Manga Research Center.
The recruitment is part of the development project titled “Eco-tourism at Changa Manga and Wetlands, Uchhali & Chashma.”
The positions are contract-based. Interested candidates with a Punjab domicile can apply until November 22, 2026.
Punjab Wildlife and Parks Department Jobs 2026
The department has announced vacancies for Senior Scientific Officer, Biodiversity Specialist, Geneticist, Microbial Data Analyst, Plant Biologist, and Plant Genomics Specialist.
Other positions include Research Collaboration Coordinator, IT Support Specialist, Geospatial Analyst, and Lab Technician.
The recruitment includes two vacancies for Lab Technician, while each of the remaining nine positions has one vacancy.
The jobs fall under Project Pay Scales (PPS) 6 to 9. All positions are based at the Changa Manga Research Center. However, selected candidates may also need to travel to other project locations.
Eligibility Criteria for Punjab Wildlife Jobs
Applicants must meet the educational qualifications and experience requirements for their selected positions.
Candidates applying for Senior Scientific Officer must have an MS or MPhil degree in Zoology, Wildlife, Veterinary Sciences, or a related field. They must also have at least seven years of relevant experience and three research publications in wildlife.
For Biodiversity Specialist, Geneticist, Microbial Data Analyst, Plant Biologist, Plant Genomics Specialist, and Research Collaboration Coordinator positions, applicants must have at least 16 years of education in the relevant field.
These positions also require a minimum of five years of professional experience. The department will prefer candidates with publications in international peer-reviewed journals.
Applicants for IT Support Specialist and Geospatial Analyst must have at least 16 years of education and three years of relevant experience.
Meanwhile, Lab Technician applicants must have at least 16 years of education in Wildlife, Zoology, Botany, Environmental Science, or a related field. They must also have two years of relevant experience.
Age Limit
The department has set different maximum age limits for each position. Candidates applying for Senior Scientific Officer must not exceed 45 years of age.
For Biodiversity Specialist, Geneticist, Microbial Data Analyst, Plant Biologist, Plant Genomics Specialist, Research Collaboration Coordinator, IT Support Specialist, and Geospatial Analyst, the maximum age limit is 40 years.
Meanwhile, the maximum age limit for Lab Technician positions is 35 years. All applicants must hold a valid Punjab domicile.
How to Apply for Punjab Wildlife and Parks Department Jobs
Interested candidates must submit their applications on plain paper through registered post or courier service.
Applicants should send their completed applications to the following address: Punjab Wildlife and Parks Department Central Tower 03, 35-B, Hali Road, Gulberg 2, Lahore.
Applicants must attach attested copies of their educational degrees, certificates, transcripts, experience certificates, CNIC, and two recent passport-size photographs.
Candidates applying for more than one position must submit a separate application for each post.
The department will not accept applications submitted by hand.
Government and semi-government employees must apply through the proper channel and provide a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their department.

items.author: Press Release
items.content:
Jazz, Pakistan’s leading digital services platform, and global technology company ZTE are expanding their collaboration with the introduction of the latest 5G smartphone lineup from nubia, ZTE’s smartphone brand, in Pakistan. The partnership established in early 2026, supports Jazz’s broader efforts to make 5G connectivity more accessible through greater device affordability.
The launch brings four 5G-enabled smartphones to the Pakistani market: nubia Neo 3, nubia Neo 5 Max, nubia Neo 5 Pro and nubia Air Pro. The lineup aims to broaden consumer access to 5G-compatible devices while supporting Pakistan’s evolving digital ecosystem.
Jazz is actively expanding Pakistan’s 5G ecosystem, with more than 1,200 5G cell sites deployed across ten cities. Recognizing that wider 5G adoption requires more than network infrastructure alone, Jazz is pursuing a broader device affordability campaign to make 5G-compatible smartphones accessible to a wider consumer base. Through partnerships with global technology companies such as ZTE, Jazz is working to bridge the device affordability gap and enable more Pakistanis to benefit from next-generation connectivity.
Asad Maqbool, Head of Jazz Consumer Growth, Jazz GSM, said, “Expanding 5G adoption requires a holistic approach that brings together network infrastructure, accessible devices and meaningful consumer experiences. As Jazz continues to strengthen its 5G footprint across Pakistan, our continued collaboration with ZTE is an important part of our efforts to make next-generation connectivity more accessible. Through our continued focus on device affordability, we aim to enable more people to participate in Pakistan’s digital future.”
Noah, CEO, ZTE nubia Pakistan, said, “We are pleased to further strengthen our collaboration with Jazz through the introduction of our latest nubia 5G smartphone lineup in Pakistan. Our ongoing partnership reflects a shared commitment to making advanced mobile technology more accessible and supporting the country’s transition towards next-generation connectivity. We look forward to continuing this collaboration and bringing innovative 5G experiences to more consumers.”
The nubia 5G smartphone lineup is available through Jazz Experience Centers and the Jazz eStore. Customers can purchase the devices through either full payment or convenient installment options, providing greater flexibility and accessibility.
Through continued network investments, strategic technology partnerships and a sustained focus on device affordability, Jazz remains committed to accelerating 5G adoption and advancing Pakistan’s transition towards a more connected, inclusive and digitally empowered future.

items.author: ZAFAR BHUTTA
items.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has approved the Autos and Auto Parts Manufacturing Policy 2026-31 after obtaining a go-ahead from the International Monetary Fund (IMF), setting an export target of $6 billion over the policy period, with sources telling The Express Tribune that the policy draft was shared with the IMF, which raised no objection.
The government will introduce a money bill in Parliament, to be termed a mini-budget, after seeking the federal cabinet's approval.
Adviser to the Prime Minister on Industries and Production Haroon Akhtar Khan said the policy represents a comprehensive shift, moving away from import-dependent assembly towards export-oriented manufacturing, greater localisation and internationally competitive production, and reflecting the prime minister's vision of an export-led, self-reliant economy with emphasis on empowering local manufacturers, strengthening domestic parts production, creating employment and integrating Pakistani industry into global automotive supply chains.
The adviser said the new policy introduces binding localisation requirements to ensure progressive growth in domestic value addition.
Highlighting the domestic vendor industry, he said Pakistan currently has approximately 2,200 auto parts manufacturers whose capacity, technological advancement and integration into international supply chains are essential for the sector's long-term competitiveness.
A Vendor Upgradation and Technology Transfer Programme (VUTTP), with an allocation of Rs2.1 billion, will be implemented through the Engineering Development Board (EDB) and the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority (SMEDA) to facilitate technological upgradation, full access to common manufacturing facilities, skills development, quality certification and export readiness, with at least five anchor firms targeted for investment during the policy period.
OEMs will also be obligated to support local vendors in technology transfer, quality assurance and manufacturing capability development.
Salient features
The policy prioritises domestic auto parts manufacturing in the country over the import of completely built-up (CBU) vehicles, recognising that a competitive and technologically advanced parts base is essential for sustainable industrial development, and moves beyond conventional tariff protection by introducing binding localisation requirements, mandatory export targets, technology transfer obligations and dedicated support for domestic vendors.
Sources said the policy requires all original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) to maintain their existing domestic value addition for each model, so manufacturers already achieving 50% to 65% localisation cannot reduce levels merely because lower minimum thresholds apply to others.
Existing OEMs must increase domestic value addition by an annual 2% on the previous year's base, a cumulative 8% over the policy period, with minimum targets by 2030-31 of 40% for internal combustion engine cars and SUVs, 45% for light commercial vehicles, 80% for tractors and 90% for motorcycles and rickshaws.
NEV localisation
The policy prescribes progressively increasing requirements for new energy vehicles (NEVs), reaching 25% for cars and SUVs and 30% for motorcycles and rickshaws by 2030-31, and failure to achieve applicable targets attracts an additional three percentage points of customs duty on relevant non-localised completely knocked-down (CKD) imports in the subsequent financial year, subject to the prescribed legal process.
Export promotion
Mandatory export targets and financial incentives aim to transform the sector into an export-oriented industry, with cumulative exports of about $6.01 billion targeted during 2026-31, comprising $3.29 billion, or 55%, from auto parts manufacturers and $2.72 billion, or 45%, from automobile manufacturers.
A Drawback of Local Taxes and Levies (DLTL) scheme provides eligible exporters 5% support on net free-on-board export value and an additional 10% on qualifying incremental exports.
OEMs face penalties ranging from 1% to 3% of annual factory-gate sales value for non-compliance, and two consecutive years of failure may result in cancellation of the manufacturing certificate except in cases of force majeure, with manufacturers required to secure export opportunities within the global supply chains of their international principals.
This clearly shows the policy emphasises auto parts manufacturing and export capability over assembly alone.
Import concessions
Customs duty reductions are being implemented progressively over five years alongside mandatory domestic value addition and export obligations.
The concessional 5% customs duty on imported battery electric vehicles (BEVs) valued up to $15,000 during the initial two years is conditional on establishing domestic assembly or manufacturing facilities, and importers must submit a surety bond and irrevocable bank guarantee covering the customs-duty differential.
Companies must commence commercial production of the imported BEV variant by September 30, 2028, failing which bank guarantees will be encashed, while OEMs that fail to enter into agreements with EDB covering localisation, exports and other performance obligations will not qualify for concessionary tariffs on imported parts.
Import concessions are therefore accompanied by specific manufacturing commitments and enforceable obligations rather than being unconditional.
Foreign exchange, industrial development
The policy projects cumulative foreign exchange savings of about $17.7 billion during 2026-31 relative to importing equivalent vehicles in CBU condition.
Export targets and incentives are also intended to generate additional foreign exchange earnings.
Increased NEV adoption is projected to avoid imports of about 1.823 million tonnes of oil over the policy period.
Contract manufacturing provisions will facilitate use of existing industrial capacity, currently estimated at 41% to 80% idle, thereby supporting production efficiency, investment and employment.
The policy envisages periodic monitoring, a mid-term review in 2028 and corrective interventions where necessary to achieve its industrial development objectives.

items.title: Illicit tobacco trade to cause $1b revenue loss
items.summary:
Illicit tobacco trade continues to impose a significant fiscal burden across Asia-Pacific, depriving governments of billions of dollars in potential revenue and weakening legitimate, tax-paying markets.
According to the report "Illicit Tobacco Trade in Asia-Pacific: Taxation, Market Incentives, and Macroeconomic Costs," the illicit tobacco trade is estimated to result in $14.85 billion in annual revenue losses across the economies covered by the study. Pakistan alone accounts for approximately $1 billion in estimated annual fiscal leakage, placing the country among the most significantly impacted markets examined.
In Pakistan, the study estimates an illicit market share of 54%, with foregone revenue equivalent to 117.4% of tobacco tax collected. Recent fiscal outcomes, however, provide grounds for cautious optimism. items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Illicit tobacco trade continues to impose a significant fiscal burden across Asia-Pacific, depriving governments of billions of dollars in potential revenue and weakening legitimate, tax-paying markets.
According to the report "Illicit Tobacco Trade in Asia-Pacific: Taxation, Market Incentives, and Macroeconomic Costs," the illicit tobacco trade is estimated to result in $14.85 billion in annual revenue losses across the economies covered by the study. Pakistan alone accounts for approximately $1 billion in estimated annual fiscal leakage, placing the country among the most significantly impacted markets examined.
In Pakistan, the study estimates an illicit market share of 54%, with foregone revenue equivalent to 117.4% of tobacco tax collected. Recent fiscal outcomes, however, provide grounds for cautious optimism. In FY2025-26, the legitimate cigarette market increased from 36.5 billion to 41.5 billion sticks, representing an estimated 5-billion-stick shift towards the legal market. As per media reports, over the same period, tax revenues increased from Rs284 billion to Rs329 billion.
The improvement in legal volumes, tax revenue and the reduction in illicit market share coincided with stronger enforcement and legislative interventions. Based on industry estimates, every billion sticks moving into the legitimate sector represent around Rs7 billion in potential government revenue.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Pakistan has urged international partnerships to ensure access to artificial intelligence does not become a source of global inequality, with Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja telling an international gathering that the benefits of technological progress must be shared with the Global South.
Addressing Margalla Dialogue 2026, on technology and the transformation of state and society, she said most countries in the Global South had remained outside major AI governance initiatives, with a limited number of developed countries shaping the frameworks, and called for inclusive cooperation, open-source models and equitable access to AI infrastructure. She said AI was expected to become a $4.8 trillion economic sector by 2033 and to affect about 40% of global employment, and that the challenge was not simply fewer jobs but a growing gap between available skills and the changing requirements of the market.
For Pakistan, where two-thirds of the population is young, protecting national identity, languages and culture in the digital age mattered alongside economic and national security, she said.
The government had committed $1 billion to AI, announced during AI Week, across infrastructure, skills, innovation and connectivity. She said a multi-layered stack was being developed to give government, industry and innovators sovereign computing capacity, alongside a planned 8.5-megawatt Sky 47 data centre and investments being explored by the Porton Group and Sapphire Group.
On skills, she said one million young people would be trained in AI and at least 10,000 AI doctorates produced over five years, with a Fund of Funds supported by the World Bank and other partners to widen capital access for startups.
She said internet speeds had risen 60% in two and a half years and fibre-to-the-home house passes from fewer than three million to more than six million, while spectrum capacity expanded from 274MHz to over 750MHz, including 180MHz allocated, and 5G was introduced.
The Digital Nation Pakistan Act had established the Pakistan Digital Authority, which was preparing a National Digital Master Plan with sectoral plans, she said, and a National Data Governance Policy was being developed alongside a pilot National Data Exchange Layer.
More than two million people had obtained verifiable digital credentials through the National Database and Registration Authority, and the RAAST payment system was being developed with the State Bank of Pakistan, she said.
She said Pakistan ranked among the top 40 in the cybersecurity index, and that the May conflict with the neighbouring country had included a significant cyber dimension alongside conventional warfare.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Weak consumer demand and rising prices weighed heavily on the offline smartphone market in the recently-concluded Diwali festive season.
According to industry body All India Mobile Retailers Association (AIMRA), mobile phone retailers saw sales volumes decline by 18-20% over the four-day period between Dhanteras (November 6) and the day after Diwali (November 9).
However, overall sales value remained broadly in line with last year’s festive season on the back of higher average selling prices.
Nevertheless, AIMRA noted that the “steeper contraction” in volumes squeezed margins and store profitability across mainline retail channels.
The industry body also said that offline smartphone sales volumes in the seven days preceding Dhanteras plunged nearly 40% as consumers delayed purchases in anticipation of festive offers. However, the demand picked up as customer footfall grew during the four-day period.
Giving a breakdown of the demand data, the report noted that urban consumers showed muted interest in upgrading devices, while Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets recorded stronger momentum – especially particularly in the mid-segment.
Most purchases were concentrated in the ₹30,000-60,000 price band after offers, while the premium segment also saw healthy demand, as per the report.
The sub-₹20,000 segment was particularly impacted by a shortage of fresh, competitive 5G models from leading brands. As a result, some value-conscious buyers shifted to brands such as HMD, Lava, Ai+, Tecno and itel, while others opted for pre-owned and refurbished devices to access higher specifications at lower prices.
AIMRA also said that financing emerged as another constraint during the festive season. The industry body claimed that only 60-70% of logged loan applications were approved, leaving a significant share of prospective buyers unable to complete purchases due to tighter underwriting and CIBIL-related rejections.
Performance also varied sharply across brands. Apple and Google Pixel saw strong demand, as did Xiaomi, which benefited from competitive pricing. Meanwhile, Vivo, OPPO and Samsung also maintained healthy sales by value but saw weaker unit volumes.
Realme saw volumes plunge by over 50% across regions, as per AIMRA. “This drop was triggered by uncompetitive pricing compared to Xiaomi, Samsung, and Vivo, zero new festive launches, and unlucrative consumer schemes. Market acceptance above ₹40,000 remains weak, dimming its near-term outlook,” said the industry body.
Why Are Smartphones Becoming Pricey?
Largely to blame for the subdued festive season was price hikes by smartphone companies and rising commodity prices. This comes as the ongoing AI boom has dried up the supply of many critical components for entry-level and budget smartphone makers, which operate on razor-thin profit margins.
This is because memory chips makers are actively prioritising the demand from data centres and AI infrastructure providers, where margins are higher.
As a result, the per-device memory cost has already increased to $60-65, a 3X jump from around $20 in 2025, per a recent Jefferies report. As a result, the brokerage firm expects the prices of low-end smartphones to increase nearly 30%.
Overall, consulting giant Deloitte expects the memory shortage to last until as late as 2030.
To tide over this, smartphone makers have resorted to price hikes to pass on the higher component costs to consumers. Retail prices of existing smartphones have increased by as much 21% in India on an average, as per Counterpoint Research.
The memory crisis has also particularly impacted the budget segment of the market, where manufacturers have limited room to absorb cost increases without sacrificing margins. This explains why India, a relatively price-sensitive market, has been heavily impacted.
The trend is expected to hold going forward as well. Xiaomi has already signalled price increases of up to ₹4,000 across product categories, while other smartphone makers are preparing hikes of up to 15%.
With festive footfall already moderating, the AIMRA expects sales volumes at mainline brick-and-mortar stores to contract by as much as 50% over the next three months.
