items.content:
Dismisses alleged anti-Ngwa remark, cautions critics
By Steve Oko
UMUAHIA—Former Chief of Staff to ex-Governor Okezie Ikpeazu, Prof. ACB Agbazuere, who was a vocal critic of Governor Alex Otti during the 2019 governorship election, has declared support for the governor’s re-election bid, saying he deserves a second term.
Agbazuere, now a member of Otti’s Campaign Advisory Council, also dismissed an allegation attributed to former Commissioner, Chief Charles Ogbonnaya, that the governor allegedly described Ngwa people as brainless, describing the claim as unfounded and politically motivated.
Speaking during a radio interview simulcast across several stations in Abia on Tuesday, Agbazuere cautioned politicians against making unsubstantiated allegations, warning that defamatory statements could attract legal consequences under Nigerian laws, including the Cybercrimes Act.
He said the allegation would not undermine Otti’s support base, particularly among the Ngwa people.
“Dr Alex Otti may love peace; Dr Alex Otti may not want trouble, but they should see that people like us are now with him. Anybody who wants to say anything should be careful and say what he knows to be true,” he warned.
Explaining his support for the governor, Agbazuere said the Otti administration had demonstrated commitment to infrastructure development, urban renewal, workers’ welfare and good governance.
He cited the reconstruction of Port Harcourt Road and Bank Road in Aba, the Omenuko Bridge and Arochukwu Road as evidence of the administration’s infrastructure drive.
He also commended the governor for what he described as regular payment of salaries, pensions and gratuities, as well as improvements in allowances for traditional rulers.
On criticisms that increased federal allocations should have translated into more development projects, Agbazuere argued that the rising cost of construction materials must be considered.
He cited the increase in the price of cement from about ₦2,000 to ₦12,000 per bag as an example of the inflationary pressures facing construction projects.
He challenged critics to visit the state and assess ongoing projects rather than evaluate the administration from a distance.
Describing Otti as a banker and trained economist, Agbazuere said the governor understood accountability and prudent management of public resources.
He urged Abians to look beyond party affiliations and support continuity, arguing that a second term would enable Otti to complete ongoing projects and consolidate his administration’s programmes.
He also recalled that during the 2023 governorship election, a leading opposition candidate had reportedly acknowledged Otti as the best candidate.
Vanguard reports that Agbazuere, a former Commissioner for Information, was previously among Otti’s vocal critics but has recently switched allegiance after leaving the All Progressives Congress (APC), where he briefly sought political shelter shortly after Otti assumed office in 2023.
Agbazuere hails from Isiala Ngwa South Local Government Area, the same local government area as Governor Otti.

items.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni
Market leaders and traders across Lagos State have offered special prayers for President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in the state, Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, seeking their victory in the 2027 general elections.
The prayer session, organised by the Lagos State Market Advisory Council (LASMAC) in collaboration with the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy Affairs and Rural Development, was held on Tuesday at the Blue Roof Pavilion, Agidingbi, Ikeja.
The gathering brought together market leaders, traders, religious and traditional leaders, as well as government officials, who prayed for the success of APC candidates and the continued development of Lagos State and Nigeria.
Hamzat, who was represented by the Commissioner for Wealth Creation and Employment, Akinyemi Ajigbotafe, thanked the market leaders for the initiative, describing their prayers and show of support as a demonstration of their commitment to the progress of the state and the country.
He particularly commended the Iyaloja-General of Nigeria and Chairman of LASMAC, Chief Folashade Tinubu-Ojo, for her leadership and efforts in mobilising market stakeholders for the prayer session.
Hamzat urged traders to sustain their partnership with the government, promising that, if elected, his administration would strengthen engagement with the market community and ensure their interests were adequately represented in governance.
“I urge you to sustain your partnership with government. If elected, our administration will strengthen engagement with the market community and ensure your interests are adequately represented in governance,” he said.
He said the commitment was reflected in the inclusion pillar of his manifesto, The Lagos Promise, unveiled on October 30, 2026, adding that his proposed administration would build on the achievements of Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu.
According to Hamzat, markets and their leaders remain indispensable to Lagos’ economic growth and development, stressing that their contributions and concerns would continue to receive attention.
He also appreciated religious and traditional leaders for their spiritual support, assuring residents of his commitment to sustaining development, consolidating existing achievements and extending the benefits of governance to all segments of society.
Earlier, the Special Adviser to the Governor on Rural Development, Nurudeen Agbaje, described the gathering as timely, noting that market leaders remained important to the political and economic development of the state.
Agbaje also commended the Lagos State Government for its development initiatives and urged stakeholders to sustain their engagement with the government.
In her remarks, Tinubu-Ojo said the meeting was convened to deliberate on the forthcoming elections and strengthen cooperation among market leaders.
She reiterated the commitment of the market community to bloc voting, while urging the government to provide market leaders with the necessary opportunities and support to mobilise their members and fulfil their commitments.
The gathering ended with prayers by religious leaders for Tinubu, Hamzat and other APC candidates participating in the 2027 elections.

items.content:
By Cynthia Alo
With many Nigerian farmers still relying on traditional knowledge to identify crop diseases and determine appropriate treatments, delayed access to agricultural advice often means problems are left unresolved until they affect yields.
In some cases, farmers have to wait days for agronomists to visit their farms and recommend solutions.
CropCura, a digital agricultural innovation co-founded by Victor Onyekachukwu, is seeking to change this practice by bringing crop diagnosis and farm advisory services directly to farmers through technology.
Onyekachukwu said the application allows farmers to take pictures of affected crops and receive an AI-powered analysis and recommendations on possible solutions in less than a minute.
Apart from crop diagnosis, the platform provides weather information, an AI advisory service and digital farm mapping which allow farmers to access information needed to make decisions about their farms.
He said the innovation also addresses another longstanding challenge in Nigerian agriculture which is farmers’ difficulty accessing formal credit because of inadequate records.
Through digital farm profiles containing information about farmers, their locations, crops and farm sizes, Onyekachukwu said the technology will also combine a credit-scoring system that can help financial institutions assess farmers for lending.
The platform, he said, currently has more than 2,000 farmers, who have mapped over 10,000 hectares of farmland.
However, Onyekachukwu identified language barriers, limited smartphone access, low digital literacy and farmers’ distrust of technology as obstacles to wider adoption.
He said the government should introduce policies recognising verified digital farm profiles as acceptable evidence for accessing agricultural loans and grants.

The experts spoke during the virtual inaugural episode of the Agricultural Policy Circle, organised by Farmosphere, with the theme, “Finding the Gap where Research, Policy, and Practice disconnect.”
Agriculture researcher, Ifunanya Orisekeh,said research questions were sometimes determined before researchers reached farming communities, leaving farmers to respond to problems that might not reflect their immediate realities.
She said research agendas were often shaped by funding calls, academic requirements and institutional timelines, while the time required to generate findings further widened the gap between research and practice.
She said: “Research agendas are shaped before a funding call comes up. For example, if there is a project that needs a student already set, by the time you reach the field, the question is already printed and the farmer is there to answer your question.
“So we can become very good in the research perspective. We are very good at answering questions that farmers have never asked.”
Orisekeh said research could take three to four years to produce findings, by which time the conditions confronting farmers might have changed.
She also questioned the practice of measuring project success by the number of farmers trained without establishing whether they continued using the recommended practices after project support ended.
Using conservation agriculture as an example, she said, “It is widely promoted and many farmers have widely dropped it as well once the project and even the report is over.”
She identified the mismatch between research schedules and farming seasons, inadequate representation of different categories of farmers and failure to return research findings to communities as other weaknesses.
Also speaking, Founder of AgricIncome Hub and Chief Executive Officer of Maxipharo Farms, Olaoluwa Farotimi, identified inadequate access to credit, unstable markets, poor extension services, logistics challenges and climate-related risks as major constraints confronting farmers.
He said agricultural financing often failed to reflect production cycles, while farmers had little control over market prices and could suffer losses from sudden policy changes.
He said: “There is no access to credit for farmers. For example, you have a production cycle of two months or a month, and you have to pay back in six months while your crop is still in the field’’.
Speaking from the policy perspective, Dr. Gideon Tups, an Economic Geography expert and Agricultural Policy and Global Bioeconomy specialist, said money and power are major constraints to translating research evidence into agricultural transformation.
Tups, a former Policy Adviser for Food Systems Transformation at GIZ, said governments needed to prioritise investments that delivered economic, environmental and social benefits, while recognising that agricultural transformation could face resistance from farmers, businesses and political interests.

items.content:
By Gabriel Ewepu
ABUJA – IN a bid to boost agribusiness, the National Agricultural Development Fund, NADF and Sahel Capital Fund Manager Limited have signed a Memorandum of Understanding, MoU, to expand access to affordable financing for Small and Medium Enterprises, SMEs, in the agricultural sector.
The partnership which seeks to unlock more private-sector investments in agriculture, is expected to reduce the cost of borrowing for agribusinesses through innovative blended financing arrangements.
Speaking at the signing ceremony, Executive Secretary, NADF, Muhammed Ibrahim, said the agreement marked a deliberate shift from conventional agricultural financing towards building an investment ecosystem capable of attracting sustainable capital into the sector.
Ibrahim explained that NADF would bring its catalytic and development mandates, as well as its understanding of national agricultural priorities, to the partnership, while Sahel Capital would contribute investment expertise, market intelligence and experience across different agricultural value chains.
According to him, the collaboration is designed to combine public-sector and concessionary capital with private investment expertise to unlock additional financing opportunities for viable agribusinesses.
Under the MoU, both institutions will explore the feasibility of blended financing arrangements through which NADF provide funding alongside capital managed by Sahel Capital, including the Sahel Agribusiness Private Debt Fund, SAPDF.
The proposed financing framework may feature risk-sharing mechanisms, concessional financing and other innovative funding structures aimed at improving access to capital for eligible agribusinesses.
Sahel Capital is also expected to provide investment structuring, fund management and technical expertise, identify eligible agribusinesses and develop monitoring and reporting frameworks for the proposed facility.
Other areas of collaboration include information sharing, development of a pipeline of bankable agribusiness projects, technical assistance and capacity building.
Also speaking, Managing Partner, Sahel Capital, Mezuo Nwuneli, explained the partnership basically would help reduce borrowing costs for agribusiness SMEs by combining NADF funding with capital managed by the investment firm.
However, Nwuneli lamented many agribusinesses currently obtain loans at interest rates ranging between 24 and 27 per cent, a situation he said makes business expansion, investment in productive capacity and long-term growth difficult.
He said that the proposed collaboration would enable both institutions to provide financing at a lower blended cost, improving the financial viability of businesses and freeing up resources for expansion.

items.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni
The Lagos State Waterways Authority (LASWA), in partnership with global trade association Interferry, has concluded Module 6 of the Africa Ferry Safety Development and Mentoring Programme to strengthen safety standards across the waterways sector.
The training equipped maritime professionals with technical skills to audit and inspect commercial passenger ferries as part of efforts to improve passenger safety and compliance with international maritime standards.
The module, titled “Survey and Inspection”, combined self-paced theoretical lessons from the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) and Lloyd’s Register with virtual mentorship and practical field exercises.
As part of the programme, participants attended a virtual “Ask the Expert” session on October 21 with Interferry specialists, Joep Bollerman, Francesco Ruisi and Darren Johnston, to discuss international ferry safety standards.
This was followed by live condition and safety compliance audits at operational passenger ferry terminals, supervised by Sandra (Okoli) Ubong of ABS and Engr. Frank Fayinto of Lloyd’s Register.
During the field exercises, participants applied an eight-step survey methodology covering preparation, onboard assessment and reporting.
They were trained to identify safety deficiencies relating to hull integrity, life-saving appliances, fire protection systems and machinery, while applying the 5W+1H principle to ensure evidence-based reporting.
The participants also learnt to classify identified risks into immediate, medium-term and low-priority interventions to facilitate timely corrective action.
The initiative is supported by the Lagos State Government and the Special Adviser to the Governor on Blue Economy, Mr Oluwadamilola Emmanuel, alongside Interferry Chief Executive Officer, Mike Corrigan, and Ferrysafe Executive Sponsor, Shari Corrigan.
With the successful completion of Module 6, the programme is expected to progress to Module 7, titled “Watchkeeping”, scheduled for November 2026.
The next phase will further equip participating maritime professionals with competencies in vessel operations, navigational safety and effective watchkeeping practices.
LASWA reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening professional standards, improving passenger safety and developing a more efficient, resilient and sustainable water transportation system in Lagos State and across Africa through international collaboration.

…Extends free screening to public servants, Trade Fair visitors
By Olasunkanmi Akoni
The Lagos State Government has urged residents to embrace HIV testing as part of routine healthcare, rather than wait until they suspect an infection before seeking screening.
The government has also extended free HIV testing and counselling services to public servants and visitors to the ongoing 2026 International Trade Fair as part of efforts to promote early diagnosis and expand access to HIV prevention and treatment.
The interventions, implemented by the Lagos State AIDS Control Agency (LSACA), are aimed at bringing HIV-related services closer to residents, encouraging regular testing and ensuring that individuals who require further care are linked to appropriate treatment facilities.
At the Public Service Week health screening exercise, the Head of Service, Lagos State, Mr Bode Agoro, officially opened the free screening programme and urged public servants to prioritise their health by taking advantage of the opportunity.
Agoro said access to preventive healthcare, including HIV screening, was essential to building a healthy, productive and efficient workforce.
He encouraged workers to embrace regular health checks and utilise the confidential testing, professional counselling and information on HIV prevention, transmission and treatment provided through the exercise.
In a related intervention, LSACA commenced free HIV testing and counselling services at the Lagos Pavilion, Tafawa Balewa Square (TBS), as part of activities at the 2026 International Trade Fair.
The exercise, which began on Friday, November 6, is scheduled to run for 10 days, ending on Sunday, November 15.
It provides visitors, exhibitors, traders and other participants with access to confidential HIV screening, counselling, preventive health information and guidance on accessing treatment and care where necessary.
The Chief Executive Officer of LSACA, Dr Folakemi Animashaun, reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to ensuring that HIV prevention, testing and treatment services remained accessible, confidential and free from discrimination.
Animashaun said knowing one’s HIV status was an important step towards preventing new infections and improving health outcomes, noting that early diagnosis enabled individuals who tested positive to commence treatment promptly and maintain healthy, productive lives.
She urged public servants, Trade Fair participants and residents across the state to embrace HIV testing as part of routine healthcare rather than wait until they suspected an infection before seeking screening.
The LSACA chief executive also stressed the importance of collaboration with ministries, departments and agencies, development partners, civil society organisations and other stakeholders in expanding access to HIV prevention, testing, treatment and care services.
She urged members of the public to visit the LSACA screening centre at the Lagos Pavilion, Tafawa Balewa Square, to access the ongoing free testing and counselling services. Animashaun added that similar services were available at designated health facilities across the state.

items.content:
Zamfara State was ranked among the top 10 states in the Fiscal Viability Index, a new report released by BudgIT has revealed.
The new report titled, “State of States 2026: States ‘ Performance on Pillar B/ Fiscal Viability,” was released on Monday.
This comes days after a renowned economist and former Governor of Nigeria’s Central Bank, Emir Muhammadu Sanusi, said he was impressed with the transformational feats recorded by Governor Dauda Lawal in the last three years in Zamfara State.
The BudgIT report assesses the fiscal performance of 35 Nigerian states in 2025, the organisation said.
“We call this ranking “Fiscal Viability”, but the real name is: Can your state survive without federal handouts?” the organisation said while releasing the report said.
“States that rank higher on the Fiscal Viability pillar demonstrate a comparatively stronger capacity to manage their expenditure obligations within the limits of their available revenue,” BudgIT said in the new report.
The report explained that “True fiscal sustainability means a state can fund its public salaries, overheads and debt obligations from its own pockets, while managing the demands on its total revenue.”
BudgIT is a civic organisation that uses creative technology to simplify public information, stimulate a community of active citizens, and enable their right to demand accountability, institutional reforms, efficient service delivery, and an equitable society.
The new report said Zamfara came in 10th on the Fiscal Viability Index, scoring 74.97 per cent, with Enugu (98.38%) and Bayelsa (88.83%) states clinching the first and second positions.
The report said Zamfara remained the second-least-indebted state in the federation, with a debt per capita of N19,464.
Zamfara is one of the only three states from the northern part of the country that made it to the top 10 positions of the Fiscal Viability Index.
The two other states are Gombe (78.07%) and Niger (76.03%), ranking 7th and 9th positions respectively.
The report also examined how states generated revenue, managed public expenditure, sustained their finances and prioritised spending across critical sectors.
The organisation said the 2026 assessment adopted a revised methodology built around four pillars: revenue performance (40 per cent), fiscal viability (30 per cent), debt sustainability (15 per cent) and spending on selected critical sectors (15 per cent).
It also examined states’ dependence on Federation Account allocations, expenditure patterns, capital investments, debt obligations and fiscal pressures across the federation.
“This edition introduces a revised methodology that gives greater attention to the developmental impact of public spending, with an assessment of expenditure in agriculture, health, education, and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH),” the report said.
Through its assessment of revenue performance, fiscal viability, debt sustainability and spending in critical sectors, the report provides insights into state governments’ fiscal decisions and how public resources are managed to support development.
In 2025, BudgIT revealed in its 2025 States of the States Report that Zamfara’s fiscal performance recorded a boost from 36th position in 2023 to 17th position in 2025 under Governor Lawal.
The report said Zamfara’s fiscal performance took a 13-step up in its fiscal performance ranking to 17th. It ranked 26th in 2024, the report said. The state was ranked 36th in 2023 when Governor Lawal took over.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
…An empty street on a sit-at-home day
By Steve Oko & Chinedu Adonu
Commercial activities are gradually returning to the South-East region after years of an illegal Monday sit-at-home order declared by non-state actors crippled business and social life.
While commercial operations are picking up in some states, others continue to lag behind. For example, the Anambra State Government had to forcefully shut down markets in Onitsha and other areas to compel traders to reopen on Mondays, yet many businesses still remained closed.
The exact reason for this hesitation remains unclear, as the threat of the sit-at-home order has significantly receded across the region, with the violent attacks and harassment of the past now seldom witnessed. However, findings indicate that many South-East residents have simply grown accustomed to this forced Monday routine after experiencing it for so long.
Consequently, many individuals—particularly independent business owners—now voluntarily choose to rest on Mondays. Furthermore, several rural communities have permanently adopted Mondays for communal meetings, neighbourhood policing, road repairs, and other civic activities.
Ultimately, what began as a forced restriction has largely transitioned into a voluntary day of rest, effectively extending the weekend by an extra day.In Aba, Abia State, following disruptions associated with the Monday sit-at-home, major markets in the commercial city are yet to fully recover their usual Monday patronage.
Although Aba, the economic honey-pot of Abia State, is gradually emerging from the disruption associated with the sit-at-home era, investigations have revealed that the psychological and political sentiments that sustained Monday closures continue to influence trading patterns in some parts of the city.
The immediate-past Chairman of Ekeoha Shopping Plaza, Aba, Prince Tochukwu Aguguo, in an interview with SEV, said that while many traders now open their shops on Mondays, a significant number of customers still stay away from the major markets.
Aguguo attributed the situation partly to lingering resentment over the continued incarceration of the leader of the Indigenous People of Biafra, IPOB, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, saying some traders and customers were observing the Monday restriction voluntarily as personal expression of solidarity.
According to him, the situation is no longer principally about coercion or enforcement by any group, but about what he described as a lingering “wound” in the hearts of some Igbo people over Kanu’s detention.
“Aba is gradually recovering, even though customers are not yet coming, especially in the major markets where we deal largely in wholesale.
“The issue of sit-at-home is not really about force by IPOB or anybody anymore. It is a wound in the heart. Some people intentionally decided not to trade, not because anybody is forcing them, but because of the anger and what they feel about the way our son, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, is being treated.
“Even when people open their shops, nobody comes to buy. We don’t normally like staying at home, but the feeling is still there,” he said.
The former Ekeoha Market Chairman said street traders and operators of smaller businesses were increasingly opening for business on Mondays, but the situation was different in the major markets, where customer turnout remained significantly below normal.
He cited Ekeoha Shopping Plaza as an example, saying many traders now open their shops but struggle to attract customers.
“In Ekeoha, for instance, people open, but customers are not coming to patronize them. Some customers still believe that sit-at-home is in force. They no longer see Monday as a normal trading day,” Aguguo explained.
He stressed that the continued low Monday patronage should therefore not necessarily be interpreted as evidence of coercion, noting that some individuals had made a conscious decision to stay away from business as a way of expressing their grievance over Kanu’s continued incarceration.
“We can comfortably conclude that even though people are not being coerced to shut down on Mondays, businesses have not necessarily picked up in Aba because some people still see staying at home as a way of expressing their grievance over the perceived injury and injustice against Mazi Nnamdi Kanu.
“It is not because they are under any coercion not to open their businesses. Some simply believe that Kanu’s imprisonment should not have happened in the first place, and that is why they voluntarily choose not to open on Mondays.
“It is a personal decision. Nobody is forcing anybody, and it is not a government directive. It is simply an individual decision,” he said.
Release Kanu to restore Monday trading in S’East — Ex-ASMATA scribe
Another textile merchant and former Secretary of the Abia State Amalgamated Traders Association (ASMATA), Hon. Ikechukwu Nwafor, popularly known as the Mayor of Ekeoha, called for the release of Nnamdi Kanu as a major step towards ending the lingering Monday sit-at-home and restoring full commercial activities across the South-East.
Nwafor said that while Monday trading was gradually returning in Aba, the recovery remained partial, with many major markets still largely shut as traders continued to stay away.
He explained that traders operating shops and stalls facing the streets were increasingly opening on Mondays, but major markets remained cautious because of the security risks of opening facilities where only a fraction of traders would show up.
“Those that are trading outside the market are doing their normal business but the major markets are usually under lock and key, and you have tens of thousands of traders in them, many of who don’t open on Mondays.
“You cannot open a market when less than 10 per cent of traders are willing to come. You would be exposing the shops to criminality. If you open a line containing about 200 traders and only 10 or 20 people come, you expose the market to a lot of criminality and other negativities,” he said.
Nwafor, who said about 60 per cent of traders operating outside the major market structures were already doing business on Mondays, urged the government to rely on persuasion and orientation rather than coercion.
“As a civilized person, I don’t believe in clamping down on individuals to do what is against their will. A trader is self-employed. The shop is yours and the business is yours, and you can decide when to go out and when not to go out.
“What government can do is orientation — make traders understand the implications of losing that extra business day and how it affects their income and families. If people are convinced, they will return to their businesses, not under force or duress,” he said.
The former market leader, however, identified Kanu’s release as the “bone of contention”, arguing that resolving the issue would remove what he described as the root cause of the Monday disruption.
“I believe that all the governors of the South-East should have come together by now, knowing full well that the release of Kanu is going to solve this situation once and for all.
“You don’t treat an ailment by treating only the symptoms; you go for the root cause of the problem. Once Kanu is released, especially at this particular period of election year, the joy will make people want to trade.
If it is possible, people may even want to trade on Sundays,” Nwafor added.
Our markets have remained open on Mondays-Enugu traders.
A trader at Ogbete Main Market, Mr. Henry Odo, said that traders in Enugu have returned to full business activities on Mondays, following the decline in enforcement of the years-long sit-at-home order. Odo said traders now open their shops on Mondays without fear, although some still stay away based on personal convictions.
He said the sit-at-home was initially observed to show solidarity with Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, adding that it later became violent when it was hijacked by hoodlums as a result of infiltration and crisis over IPOB leadership.
“It was a terrible thing then. Initially, the idea was to show solidarity with Mazi Nnamdi Kanu. Everybody was prepared to sit at home, and even those who came out would hardly find customers.
“But when the ideology behind it became violent, with people being killed and property destroyed, people started questioning it.
“We have resumed Monday business here in Enugu and are doing business with peace of mind. However, some people still choose not to come to the market on Mondays based on their individual ideology,” he said.
Also speaking, a community leader in Igbo-Eze North Local Government Area of Enugu State, Chijioke Ugwu, said it appeared that normal life had returned to the area as residents now freely come out for business on Mondays.
Ugwu said the enforcement of the sit-at-home order had stopped, allowing residents to resume their normal activities.
“Life has returned to the council area, although the effects of those barbaric acts can never be forgotten. Since the enforcers stopped, people have started coming out to do business on Mondays, and life is gradually returning to normal,” he said.

By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi
The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kebbi State has declared that it is united and strong ahead of the 2027 general elections, following a reconciliation exercise aimed at addressing grievances among party members.
The Secretary of the Contact and Reconciliation Committee set up by Governor Nasir Idris, Engineer Ahmed Umar Faruk, made this known on Tuesday in Birnin Kebbi while briefing journalists on the committee’s activities.
Faruk said the committee had completed 10 days of engagements across the state’s 21 local government areas, during which it met with aggrieved party members and resolved several complaints.
He said those engaged included former commissioners, former members of the state House of Assembly and National Assembly, as well as other party members who felt sidelined or had grievances arising from the concluded party primaries.
According to him, the committee recorded significant progress by providing a platform for aggrieved members to express their concerns and ensuring that their complaints received attention.
He said the exercise had helped restore unity within the party, adding that the APC leadership in the state was committed to carrying every member along in its activities.
“We toured the 21 local government areas in Kebbi State and saw loyalty to the governor and the party from top to bottom,” he said.
Faruk urged party leaders at the state, local government and ward levels to sustain regular engagement with members to prevent grievances from accumulating and threatening party unity.
He, however, warned members against engaging in anti-party activities and clandestine meetings capable of creating divisions within the APC.
He said the party would not tolerate actions capable of undermining its unity as it prepares for the 2027 general elections.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
President Bola Tinubu has unveiled a ₦52,500 monthly minimum pension guarantee for 173,209 eligible retirees under the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS), ending a 22-year delay in implementing the provision of the Pension Reform Act.
The President also inaugurated the Pension Industry Healthcare Plan for Retirees, known as PenCare, designed to provide free essential healthcare services to low-income pensioners.
Tinubu, who was represented by Senate President Godswill Akpabio, announced the initiatives on Tuesday at the Presidential Pension Security Initiatives ceremony held at the State House Banquet Hall, Abuja.
Declaring the Minimum Pension Guarantee operational, the President said, “By the authority vested in me as President, Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, I hereby declare the Minimum Pension Guarantee Scheme commenced.”
He explained that the guarantee, first provided for under the Pension Reform Act of 2004 and retained in the 2014 legislation, had remained unimplemented under successive administrations.
“From this day, there is a floor beneath the Nigerian retiree. No one who contributed under the Contributory Pension Scheme will ever be allowed to fall below,” he said.
Tinubu urged future administrations to sustain the initiative, declaring: “Raise it. But never remove the floor.”
On healthcare, he said PenCare would protect vulnerable retirees from medical expenses capable of depleting their pension savings.
“PenCare gives our low-income retirees access to essential healthcare without charge,” he said, adding that beneficiaries would begin receiving healthcare access cards in the coming months.
The President also disclosed that his administration had issued a ₦758bn bond to address longstanding pension arrears and approved a ₦32,000 monthly consequential adjustment for affected federal pensioners.
He said state governments had spent more than ₦1tn settling pension obligations, attributing their improved financial capacity partly to the removal of fuel subsidy.
Citing a World Bank report, Tinubu said state revenues increased by about 93 per cent in real terms between 2023 and 2025, while the proportion of their budgets allocated to capital projects rose from 46 to 61 per cent.
He further disclosed that government-backed credit initiatives had unlocked more than ₦64bn for 174,000 borrowers, while over 350,000 Nigerians had accessed approximately ₦53bn in consumer credit.
In her opening remarks, the Director-General of the National Pension Commission (PenCom), Omolola Oloworaran, announced that the guaranteed minimum pension had been fixed at ₦52,500 monthly.
“The minimum pension in the Federal Republic of Nigeria is ₦52,500 every month,” she said.
According to her, 173,209 retirees qualify for the guarantee, comprising 34 per cent from federal service, 12 per cent from state employment and 54 per cent from the private sector.
She explained that the amount had undergone actuarial validation and would be subject to periodic review.
“The figure was not plucked from the air. It has been validated by an actuary, and it is subject to review,” Oloworaran said.
She disclosed that more than ₦400bn was available in the Pension Protection Fund to finance the guarantee, while over 65 per cent of private-sector retirees currently earned below the new minimum threshold.
The PenCom boss also revealed that state governments inherited more than ₦2tn in pension liabilities, of which ₦1.07tn had been settled.
On healthcare, she said the pension industry had committed more than ₦7bn to PenCare after paying premiums covering nearly 30,000 retirees.
Oloworaran further announced plans to expand pension coverage to informal-sector workers, including traders, artisans and farmers.
She also disclosed that the pension industry had committed 750m to an infrastructure investment platform, with another $50m expected from development partners and initial deployment targeted for the first half of 2027.
In his remarks, the Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Pensions, Hussaini Jallo, described the initiatives as significant steps towards addressing retirees’ healthcare needs and income insecurity.
He pledged the National Assembly’s support for stronger pension governance, improved compliance and expanded pension coverage, particularly for workers in the informal sector.
Also speaking, the Chairman of Heirs Holdings, Tony Elumelu, commended the initiatives, describing them as investments in the welfare of Nigerians who had completed their working lives.
“These are not simply pension reforms. They are investments in human dignity,” he said.
Elumelu pledged private-sector support for partnerships aimed at strengthening retirement security and financial inclusion.
The post Tinubu unveils ₦52,500 minimum pension for retirees appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), has disputed President Bola Tinubu’s criticism of his record on erosion control in Anambra State, insisting that he helped develop the programme currently being used to tackle the environmental challenge.
Tinubu had criticised Obi’s tenure as Anambra governor during an All Progressives Congress (APC) rally in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, over the weekend, alleging that the former governor “ran away from erosion” while highlighting environmental projects undertaken in Lagos.
However, speaking on Tuesday during an interview on Rhythm FM Jos ahead of the NDC town hall meeting in Plateau State, Obi dismissed the allegation as untrue.
The former Anambra governor said he worked with a former Minister of Environment to develop the erosion-control programme, which he said was subsequently adopted following his intervention with the late President Umaru Musa Yar’Adua.
“On what the president said while campaigning in Akwa Ibom, it’s not true. I, working with the former minister of environment, developed what they’re using today to fight erosion,” Obi said.
“I went to President Yar’Adua, made a suggestion to him. He called the minister and said he should go and develop it.”
Obi governed Anambra State from 2006 to 2014, during which the state faced significant erosion challenges.
At the Uyo rally, Tinubu had questioned Obi’s preparedness for the presidency, citing the erosion problem in Anambra as an example of what he described as shortcomings in his record as governor.
Explaining his visit to Plateau State, Obi said it was part of his approach to engaging citizens and understanding their challenges before embarking on campaign rallies.
He argued that political candidates should first listen to the concerns and experiences of the people before explaining how they intend to address them.
The NDC candidate also identified insecurity in central Nigeria as a major challenge, stressing the need to ensure that residents could return to their communities, pursue their businesses and engage in farming without fear.
He said his administration, if elected, would prioritise public services, particularly education and healthcare, as well as insurance coverage for vulnerable Nigerians.
“Unless children go to school without fear, unless parents go to farms without fear, we don’t have a country,” he said.
“You cannot stay in a developing country and a developing world if you have poor health accessibility and poor education accessibility. Education and health are the foundation for development. I will invest in them.”

items.author: Hope Abah
items.content:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Benue State, Prof. Terhemba Shija, has accused the state government of plotting to disrupt the planned visit of the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, to Yelwata community in in Guma Local Government Area.
Shija, who raised the alarm at a press conference in Makurdi on Tuesday ahead of Obi’s visit scheduled for Wednesday, called on security agencies, particularly the police and the Department of State Services (DSS), to guarantee the safety of the presidential candidate and his supporters.
He alleged that the state government was unhappy with Obi’s planned visit and had threatened to prevent him from visiting Yelewata, where he is expected to pay tribute to victims of the last year’s deadly attack that claimed about 271 lives and commiserate with their families.
The NDC candidate further alleged that during Obi’s previous attempt to visit the community about two months ago, suspected political thugs attacked his supporters with stones in an attempt to frustrate the visit.
NERC approves N30bn to meter Band A, B customers
Kwankwaso’s son threatens to sue Kano Information Commissioner
Shija describing the alleged incident as “a monumental national disgrace and a display of immaturity” warned that nobody had the right to prevent the presidential candidate from visiting the community.
“You cannot stop a moving train,” he said, urging the state government to shelve what he described as its “diabolical plan” to disrupt the visit.
He, however, said arrangements had been concluded for Obi’s visit, which would combine humanitarian and political engagements, explaining that the former Anambra State governor would lay a wreath at the cenotaph of the victims along Lafia road in Yelewata before proceeding to Makurdi for a town hall meeting.
Shija clarified that Obi would not visit any government facility or IDP camp but would interact with a cross-section of residents at the Multi-purpose Hall of the Mission House, behind the Benue Links head office, Wurukum, Makurdi.
The NDC governorship candidate urged traditional rulers, civil society organisations, students, women, youths, labour unions and other residents to turn out to receive Obi, whom he described as “the man who would soon be President.”
While insisting that the party would not resort to violence, Shija said the NDC would not succumb to intimidation or abandon its constitutional responsibility to mobilise support ahead of the 2027 general elections.
“The Nigeria Democratic Congress will not yield to any blackmail or intimidation, neither are we going to succumb to the temptation to take laws into our hands,” he said.
Shija also used the occasion to unveil what he described as his “Rescue and Reset Agenda” for Benue, identifying insecurity, displacement and economic backwardness as major challenges confronting the state despite its enormous agricultural and mineral resources.
But, in a swift reaction, the Benue State government dismissed the allegations, insisting that it has no objection to his presence in the state.
The State Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Chief Solomon Iorpev, accused Obi of seeking to create controversy around his visit, claiming that the former Anambra State governor was deliberately generating negative publicity to portray the state government in a bad light.
Iorpev said there was nothing extraordinary about Obi’s visit to Benue, questioning why the administration should be apprehensive about his political activities.
“Why should the Benue State Government be afraid of him? We’re not afraid of him. He can come to Benue State,” the spokesperson said.
He maintained that the government’s position had consistently been that Obi, as a presidential candidate, should follow the necessary protocols by formally notifying the state government of his visit.
The government spokesperson added that Obi had lost the privileges of an ordinary citizen by virtue of his political status and should not enter and leave the state without informing the authorities.
Iorpev, however, acknowledged that Obi had now complied with the requirements, saying the government had seen the letters and acknowledgement documents relating to the visit.
He nevertheless alleged that the controversy surrounding the planned visit was being deliberately orchestrated by Obi’s camp to discredit the state government.
The commissioner described Obi’s approach as an attempt to generate sympathy and online attention even as he accused the presidential candidate of seeking publicity rather than focusing on the purpose of his visit.
Contacted, the Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO) for Benue command, DSP Peter Aondongu, confirmed that Obi had written to inform the police about his visit to the state.
The PPRO said adequate security arrangements were being made to guarantee the safety of the NDC presidential candidate visit to the state.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
Japanese tech investor SoftBank’s Vision Fund 2 (SVF2) booked a valuation loss of $42 Mn on its investment in listed Indian electric vehicle (EV) maker Ola Electric in the quarter ended September 2026 (Q2 FY26 as per the investment firm’s nomenclature).
In its investor presentation, SoftBank said that the EV manufacturer’s gross return to the SVF2 stood at $370 Mn in the quarter under review, down $42 Mn (or 10.2%) from $412 Mn in the preceding Q1 FY26.
The latest gross return figures are almost 30% lower than $556 Mn that the fund claims to have invested in the OEM so far.
In contrast, other listed Indian startups in SVF2’s portfolio – Lenskart and Meesho – together contributed valuation gains worth $394 Mn to the fund’s kitty in Q2 FY26.
SoftBank said that the Indian omnichannel eyewear giant helped SVF2 rake in an additional $273 Mn in gross returns during the quarter under review. With this, the fund’s total gross gains from Lenskart stood at $1.3 Bn in Q2 FY26, up 27% sequentially from $1 Bn in preceding quarter.
On similar lines, Meesho added another $121 Mn in gains to SVF2’s corpus in the quarter under review. Overall, the Japanese tech giant’s fund sat on gross gains worth $642 Mn on account of the homegrown ecommerce giant in Q2 FY26, up from $521 Mn in the previous quarter.
“The investment gain at SVF2 reflected increases in the fair values of certain private portfolio companies due to higher valuations in recent transactions as well as higher share prices of certain public portfolio companies, including Meesho Limited and Lenskart Solutions Limited,” added SoftBank in a statement.
SoftBank claims to have so far invested $225 Mn and $285 Mn in Lenskart and Meesho, respectively.
Meanwhile, another homegrown SVF2 portfolio startup Swiggy saw a valuation gain of nearly $14 Mn in the quarter under review. The foodtech giant minted gross returns worth $451 Mn in Q2 FY26 (up from $437 Mn in Q1 FY26) against a total investment of $450 Mn.
However, the road was not so smooth for listed Indian startups in Vision Fund 1 (SVF1). The fund booked a sequential valuation loss of $34 Mn on account of Delhivery in Q2 FY26. Against a gross return of $701 Mn in Q1 FY26, the logistics giant ended the September 2026 quarter with an even lower gross return of $667 Mn.
Similarly, SoftBank pegged the gross return on its investment in FirstCry parent BrainBees Solutions at $308 Mn in the quarter under review, down 14% or $50 Mn, from $358 Mn in Q1 FY26.
Overall, SoftBank swung to the red and posted a net loss of nearly $7 Bn in Q2 FY26 against a profit of $15.9 Bn in the year ago period. This was its first loss-making quarter in nearly two years as the company was hit by rising buildout costs for data centres in the US and a sharp jump in financing payments.
The investment firm also reported $14.1 Bn in net sales in the quarter under review, up 15.6% from $12.2 Bn in Q2 FY25.
SoftBank is one of the major foreign investors in the country and has so far deployed nearly $16 Bn in Indian startups. Having funded nearly a fifth of India’s 100+ unicorns, SoftBank has previously backed the likes of Flipkart, OYO, Delhivery, OfBusiness, FirstCry and Meesho.

Anyone using the name, logo or emblem of the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) without its permission can face up to three years in prison, a fine, or both, the authority has warned.
In a public notice shared on X, NADRA said its name, its abbreviation, logo, emblem, trademark and other related material are its legal intellectual property.

NADRA said using or copying its name, logo or other marks, or presenting them as one’s own name or identity, without its written permission is strictly prohibited and illegal. The ban covers all media, including print, electronic, digital and social media.
Any violation is an offence under Sections 482 to 486 of the Pakistan Penal Code 1860 and the Trade Marks Ordinance 2001. Legal action can result in imprisonment of up to three years, a fine, or both.
Penalties for Each Offence
NADRA also listed separate punishments for specific violations:
Using a false trademark can lead to up to one year in prison.
Counterfeiting trademarks can lead to up to two years in prison.
False marking can lead to up to six months in prison.
Fake Social Media Pages
The authority said pages on Facebook and other social media platforms using NADRA’s name or similar names also violate these laws. It is taking legal action against such pages and steps to get them taken down.
NADRA urged citizens to confirm that any organization or person claiming to be linked with it is genuine before making any transaction or contact. It also advised people to follow only its official social media accounts for accurate information.
The warning follows earlier alerts from the authority about fake websites using its name and fake agents targeting overseas Pakistanis.

items.content:
Film festivals are not just about watching movies; they also provide filmmakers, artists and enthusiasts an opportunity to connect, exchange ideas and learn about the process of filmmaking.
Speaking on the sidelines of the World Culture Festival, Pakistani filmmaker said that film enthusiasts look forward to such festivals every year, as they offer more than just screenings. Filmmakers from different countries also attend to represent their work, making the event an opportunity for meaningful interaction and discussion.
He said that such gatherings allow filmmakers to understand how projects are initiated and how the filmmaking process begins. The initial discussions and exchange of ideas are particularly important for those working in the industry.
"These festivals also inspire young people. If they want to pursue filmmaking, they get to see different pathways and understand how they can move forward and create better work," he said.
Asked about the audience response after his film was screened at the cinema and later at the World Culture Festival, as well as the criticism it received on social media following its release, the filmmaker said that many viewers had enjoyed the film.
"Not every film is going to be liked by everyone. Even after watching a film like The Odyssey, some people come out saying, 'What did I just watch? What kind of film was that?' So, our film can also have shortcomings. There is nothing unusual about someone not liking it," he said.
Faysal Quraishi is one of Pakistan's highest-paid actors. He is the recipient of more than 20 nationally recognised awards. He first gained recognition for playing the leading role of Boota in the television series Boota from Toba Tek Singh (1999) and has been a part of more than 200 projects. Quraishi hosted a morning show called Muskurati Morning with Faisal Qureshi from 2010 to 2014. From 2016 to 2019, he hosted the morning show Salam Zindagi. He made his film acting debut in 1992. He became a producer in 2017 with the production house Connect Studios, and owns a film production house named Faysal Quraishi Films.
He added that social media had given everyone a platform to express their opinions, and he was open to both appreciation and criticism.
"Some people praised the film, while others did not like it. That's fine. It is good that people are sharing their feedback," he said.
Clarifying his response to the criticism circulating online, he said that the video he had shared was not directed at any particular individual. Rather, it was a response to a message that had reached him.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
Pakistan’s 1,200MW Chashma-5 (C-5) nuclear power plant has reached a key construction milestone with the placement of its reactor dome, less than three and a half years after work began and ahead of schedule.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif attended the dome placement ceremony in Mianwali as chief guest, alongside Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Chinese officials and senior representatives of the organizations involved, the Prime Minister’s Office said.
The dome is the roof of the reactor building, which houses the reactor and its main equipment.
The plant is expected to start producing electricity in September 2030.
Cheaper, Steadier Power
The prime minister said C-5 promised clean, reliable and affordable electricity, and would cut Pakistan’s reliance on imported fuels and global price swings.
Nuclear energy makes up around 16.6 percent of the country’s electricity generation despite being only 8.6 percent of installed capacity, and its share rises to 26 percent in winter.
The project could be commissioned earlier than planned, given the pace of construction since its groundbreaking in July 2023.
Seventh Unit Built With China
C-5 is the seventh nuclear power unit China has helped Pakistan build. The prime minister thanked President Xi Jinping, the Chinese government and the China National Nuclear Corporation, and said the second phase of CPEC would open new economic opportunities for both countries.
The project recently cleared another step when Pakistan and the IAEA signed a safeguards agreement for Chashma-5. Earlier, Chashma-1 set a PAEC record of 427 days of uninterrupted operation.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has allowed late tax filers to join the Active Taxpayer List (ATL) without paying the Rs. 25,000 surcharge, provided they agree not to purchase or acquire property for six months.
It requires individuals filing their income tax returns after the due date or extended deadline to submit an undertaking through Form ATL-U.
FBR introduced the facility through SRO 2097(I)/2026 issued on Tuesday, amending the Income Tax Rules 2022.
Under the undertaking, individuals must agree not to purchase, acquire or obtain ownership or beneficial interest in any property for six months from the date they submit the form.
Those who meet this condition can have their names included in the ATL without paying the surcharge normally charged for late filing.
The six-month restriction will begin on the date shown on the electronic acknowledgement issued by FBR’s IRIS system after successful submission of Form ATL-U.
FBR can verify whether individuals have followed the undertaking using information available with the tax department or obtained from government agencies, property registries, financial institutions and other lawful sources.
If FBR finds that an individual acquired property during the restricted period, it will first provide an electronic opportunity to explain the matter.
If the violation is established, the fee waiver will be withdrawn from the date of the breach, and the individual’s ATL status will be governed by the existing rules.
FBR had previously issued a draft of the scheme on October 6, 2026, through SRO 1619(I)/2026.

items.content:
The Collect & Recycle (CoRe) Alliance called for a harmonized, phased and inclusive Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework to strengthen Pakistan’s waste management and recycling systems and advance the country’s transition towards a circular economy. Alongside the policy dialogue, CoRe Alliance handed over 5,000 co-branded reusable tote bags to the Pakistan Environmental Protection Agency (Pak-EPA) as part of its efforts to promote sustainable alternatives and reduce reliance on single-use plastics in the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT). The initiative supports the implementation of the Single-Use Plastics (Prohibition) Regulations, 2023, applicable to ICT.
Dr. Shezra Mansab Ali Khan Kharal, Minister of State for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, Government of Pakistan, delivered the opening remarks and stated, “Pakistan’s transition towards a circular economy requires collective action and strong collaboration between government and industry. Effective EPR implementation can strengthen waste management and recycling systems, promote responsible resource management and help establish better systems in Pakistan.”
Sheikh Waqar Ahmad, CEO, CoRe Alliance, stated: “Building a circular economy requires both enabling policy frameworks and practical action. We need to emphasize on greater industry participation, tax incentives and easier access to financing to attract private investment in recycling infrastructure. Alongside these policy efforts, the distribution of 5,000 reusable tote bags reflects CoRe Alliance’s commitment to strengthening Pakistan’s waste management systems, promoting responsible consumption and advancing sustainable packaging through collective action.”
The session featured remarks by Amir Mohyuddin, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination (MoCC&EC), followed by a panel discussion featuring Zainab Naeem, Research Fellow, SDPI; Babar Aziz Bhatti, CEO, Green Earth Recycling and Chairperson, EPR Committee, CoRe Alliance; and Zia Hyder, CEO, SPEL Group and Board Director, CoRe Alliance.
Amir Mohyuddin, Additional Secretary, MOCC&EC, also addressed the session, stating, “A harmonized and phased approach, supported by clear responsibilities and coordinated stakeholder efforts, is essential to strengthening better systems in Pakistan.”
The session focused on the need for a nationwide EPR framework, improved waste segregation, stronger recycling infrastructure and greater public-private collaboration to address better systems in Pakistan. CoRe Alliance’s White Paper, previously presented and submitted to the Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination in May 2026. During the session, Namwar Yusuf Rahman, Project Manager, CoRe Alliance, presented a summary of the White Paper, outlining its key recommendations and harmonized approach that promotes regulatory consistency while accommodating provincial and local realities.
Furthermore, Babar Aziz Bhatti, CEO, Green Earth Recycling and Chairperson, EPR Committee, CoRe Alliance highlighted that, “The recycling sector’s capacity to process significant volumes of recyclable material, emphasizing that proper waste segregation is essential to reducing processing costs and improving the quality of recycled products.”
Discussions covered phased targets, shared value-chain responsibilities, industry-led Producer Responsibility Organizations (PROs) under regulatory oversight, green financing, recycling infrastructure, digital traceability and the integration of informal waste workers.
As part of the broader engagement, CoRe Alliance, in collaboration with Pak-EPA, presented 5,000 co-branded reusable tote bags to Dr. Shezra Mansab Ali Khan Kharal. Separately, a reusable tote bag handover ceremony was held a day earlier at the Pak-EPA office in Islamabad, where 5,000 co-branded reusable tote bags were handed over to Pak-EPA in the presence of Dr. Mohsina Zubair and Dr. Zaigham Abbas, Directors (Lab/NEQS), Pak-EPA.
Both engagements took place on 5 November 2026, as part of the 29th Sustainable Development Conference, organized by the Sustainable Development Policy Institute (SDPI) in collaboration with CoRe Alliance at Allama Iqbal Open University (AIOU), Islamabad. The engagements brought together government representatives, industry stakeholders and other partners under the theme “From Policy to Practice: Strengthening Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) for Better Systems in Pakistan” and the “Reusable Tote Bag Ceremony.”

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The federal government has "unconstitutionally" spent over Rs5 trillion on ministries functioning in the provincial domain since the 18th Amendment, according to proceedings of a Senate functional committee panel that on Tuesday barred the release of any further funds for them.
During the meeting, the subcommittee of the Senate's Functional Committee on Devolution also gave a final deadline to the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) to issue orders winding up these ministries, warning that it may have to send a notice to the office if there is no compliance. The office of the auditor general submitted details of spending for the 2011-26 period by ministries functioning in the provincial domain.
More than Rs5 trillion, or $18 billion, has been spent on ministries established in violation of the Constitution since the 18th Amendment, which is more than the $15 billion borrowed from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) during this period, said Senator Zamir Hussain Ghumro, chairman of the committee. He said that had the federal government followed the Constitution and not spent money in areas that are not its responsibility, the country could have avoided the IMF programmes.
The committee instructed the Ministry of Finance, the auditor general and the accountant general to stop releasing funds to ministries working in violation of the Constitution. The proceedings reinforced that Pakistan's problem was not mere taxation but illegal and unconstitutional spending by the federal government, which has been borrowing while continuing to spend in areas that may give it political advantage but add to the debt burden.
According to the details, Rs48.8 billion was unconstitutionally spent over the past 16 years on the Ministry of Climate Change, Rs1.1 trillion on the Ministry of Education, Rs651 billion on the Ministry of Health, Rs398.4 billion on the Ministry of Housing, Rs313 billion on the Ministry of Industries, Rs51.7 billion on the Ministry of Inter-Provincial Coordination, Rs35 billion on the Ministry of Narcotics, Rs270 billion on the Ministry of National Food Security, Rs32 billion on the Ministry of Petroleum, Rs185 billion on the Ministry of Planning, Rs687 billion on the Ministry of Railways and Rs935 billion on the Ministry of Water Resources.
"We are restraining ourselves by not referring the matter of allocating budget to ministries functioning in devolved areas to the National Accountability Bureau under Section 9 for misuse of authority by the Ministry of Finance," Ghumro remarked.
He said the Constitution provided no basis for retaining ministries on the grounds of fulfilling international commitments, adding that under Article 173 provincial governments could also enter into international agreements.
The committee had given the government two weeks to wind up the ministries of health, education, national food security, water resources, climate change, housing, special initiatives, culture and heritage, railways, industries, statistics, petroleum, inter-provincial coordination, narcotics and planning and development.
The committee chairman observed that the panel and the prime minister were aiming at the same thing, saving taxpayers' money and reducing expenditure.
Noreen Bashir, representing the finance ministry, could not give a satisfactory reply and asked Finance Joint Secretary Rashid Zubari to answer the question about the legal authority to release funds to ministries working in devolved areas. He too could not give a satisfactory reply. "You will land in trouble for spending money against the country by allocating budgets to the subjects that have been devolved," Ghumro said, warning the finance ministry representatives.
Cabinet Division Secretary Kamran Afzal also could not report compliance with the committee's instructions to wind up 17 ministries functioning in violation of the Constitution. In light of the committee's instruction a summary had been sent to the Prime Minister's Office, but no instructions had been received, he said.
He acknowledged the committee chairman's knowledge of the Constitution but argued that "there are additional things on the ground". The cabinet secretary was of the view that these ministries are retained because of the practical problems of the "paternalistic role of the federal government and for international coordination".
Ghumro rejected the reply as the "law of necessity", which the committee did not agree to.
For one minister and one federal secretary a ministry is retained in devolved areas, which resulted in over Rs5 trillion of spending in 16 years in violation of the Constitution, he said. The committee noted that under the Constitution international coordination is the responsibility of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, while inter-provincial coordination is the mandate of the Council of Common Interests (CCI). The prime minister heads the CCI while the four chief ministers are its members.
There are also issues, as some provinces are not ready to take responsibility, Afzal said. The cabinet secretary said that for the past two years the federal government has been trying to hand over Sheikh Zayed Hospital, Lahore, and two health institutions in Rawalpindi to the Punjab government, which is refusing to take ownership. The committee chairman said that under the Constitution borrowing is the mandate of the CCI, but the government has not convened a CCI meeting since 2025 and the country was sinking into a debt trap.
The finance ministry is also reluctant to appoint a permanent director general of debt, and the debt office's affairs are run on an ad hoc basis.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) staged a powerful rally on Tuesday as investors returned from the long weekend with renewed buying interest, driving the KSE-100 index up by over 5,400 points amid support from strong remittances and easing international oil prices.
The benchmark index settled at 179,335.24, surging 5,448.56 points, or 3.13%. It remained in positive territory throughout the session and touched the intra-day high of 179,424.04, while the day's low was 176,273.72. The market reopened following a public holiday on Monday on account of Iqbal Day. The return of investors coincided with improving domestic and international developments, triggering across-the-board buying.
On the domestic front, strong remittance inflows helped reinforce investor confidence by supporting the country's external account. Meanwhile, the decline in international oil prices provided additional relief following concerns over Pakistan's exposure to imported energy and the potential impact of higher fuel costs on inflation and the balance of payments. Crude prices extended losses on Tuesday after President Trump downplayed the need for further military action, easing fears of continued supply disruptions in the Middle East.
According to Arif Habib Limited Deputy Head of Trading Ali Najib, the PSX extended its bullish momentum for another session, firmly reclaiming the 175k psychological mark. The market opened on a positive note, buoyed by a sharp correction in global oil prices following the Democrats' sweeping gains in the US midterm elections. WTI crude dipped below $87/barrel, while Brent fell to $96/barrel from the previous session's $102/barrel, marking a decline of over 8%, he said.
The sharp retreat in oil prices improved investor sentiment, which triggered broad-based buying and helped the benchmark index reclaim the 175k level for the first time since September 1, 2026. In the US, the Democrats' gains in elections fuelled optimism about a potential de-escalation in the Middle East and supported a broader recovery in the global risk appetite, Najib said.
UBL, Lucky Cement, Meezan Bank, Systems Ltd, Engro Holdings, Bank AL Habib, HBL, Hub Power, Oil & Gas Development Company and Pakistan Petroleum were the major contributors to the rally, collectively adding 1,981 points to the index. "Going forward, the market is likely to maintain its bullish momentum amid easing oil prices and improved global risk appetite. However, profit-taking may emerge at higher levels, keeping investors selective and cautious," he added.
Topline Securities observed that investor sentiment remained upbeat amid easing international oil prices and diminishing concerns over a potential escalation in geopolitical tensions between the US and Iran. UBL, FFC, HUBC, LUCK and MEBL emerged as the leading positive contributors, collectively adding 1,982 points to the index and providing significant support to the market's overall performance, it said.
Cumulatively, trading volumes decreased to 972.4 million shares from Friday's tally of 1.5 billion. The value of traded shares stood at Rs50.7 billion.
Shares of 501 companies were traded in the ready market. Of these, 363 stocks closed higher, 107 fell and 31 remained unchanged.
Cnergyico Pk was the volume leader with trading in 70.1 million shares, falling Rs0.75 to close at Rs11.35. Foreign investors bought shares worth Rs1.68 billion, the National Clearing Company reported.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Federal Minister for Communications Abdul Aleem Khan endorsed the Global Green Freight Corridors Initiative at a high-level ministerial roundtable during COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, and pledged Pakistan's support for pilot green corridors, according to an official statement issued on Tuesday.
The roundtable was co-hosted by Turkish Minister for Transport and Infrastructure Abdulkadir Uraloglu, the United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) and the Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific and brought together global leaders to address sustainable transit solutions.
He said international freight transport was the lifeblood of global commerce but one of the fastest-growing sources of transport-related greenhouse gas emissions, and that economic growth and environmental stewardship were mutually reinforcing goals.
He said the initiative showed sustainable logistics was the only viable path forward and that COP31 must shift focus toward turning international climate pledges into tangible cross-border outcomes. The minister reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to decarbonising global supply chains and building climate-resilient logistics infrastructure.
Pakistan is strategically placed as a regional trade bridge linking China, Central Asia and the Middle East, with a network of over 500,000 kilometres of roads, a 7,800-kilometre railway, major deep-sea ports and developing trade arteries under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, he said. Road carries 96% of domestic freight, straining national resources and urban air quality, and Pakistan is pursuing a multi-pillar transition, he said.
The Railway Plan 2026 aims to lift rail's freight share to 20% through the modernised Main Line-1 (ML-1) project, alongside the National Electric Vehicle Policy 2025-30, which provides for 3,000 charging stations along major corridors, and complementary maritime reforms across national seaports.
He said TIR transit volumes had risen 200% under the UN TIR Convention, with digital pre-shipment notices integrated into the Pakistan Single Window and an eTIR project with UNECE, positioning Pakistan as one of the fastest-rising countries in regional trade facilitation.
Financing combines Public Sector Development Programme allocations, multilateral support from the Asian Development Bank and Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and private investment under the Public-Private Partnership Authority Act for projects including the M-6 Motorway and ML-1 upgrades, he said.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Pakistan's newly announced auto policy has drawn strong criticism from the domestic automotive parts industry, which warns that its import-centric approach could undermine local manufacturing, threaten 300,000 direct jobs and increase pressure on foreign exchange reserves.
Former President of the Pakistan Association of Automotive Parts and Accessories Manufacturers (PAAPAM) Aamir Allawala said the policy favoured imports of completely built-up electric vehicles and completely knocked-down kits over domestic manufacturing, putting nearly 1,200 engineering and component manufacturing enterprises at risk.
He said the policy could reverse years of progress in localisation, currently estimated at 50% to 65% for several locally assembled models, and that assemblers would find it more economical to import components from foreign partners rather than procure them locally, threatening 300,000 direct jobs and another 1.5 million indirectly associated with the industry.
Increased vehicle imports would create additional demand for foreign exchange, while tax concessions on imported electric vehicles could widen the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR)'s revenue gap, he warned.
Allawala argued that consumers, representing only around 0.1% of the population who buy cars annually, might benefit from a 5% to 7% price reduction, but questioned whether these limited gains justified damage to the wider industrial ecosystem. He said component manufacturers had not endorsed the policy, claiming its final version was substantially different from proposals discussed with the Ministry of Industries and Production up to June 2026.
He suggested renaming it from the "Auto and Auto Parts Policy" to the "Policy for Automobile Assembly and Import of New and Used Vehicles", arguing its incentives primarily benefited imports rather than local manufacturing.
Former PAAPAM chairman Abdul Rehman Aizaz described the policy as import-centred and warned that cutting customs duty on completely built-up vehicles to 15% by 2031 would undermine the entire domestic value chain, with consequences extending beyond component makers to material producers including Aisha Steel, International Steels and People's Steel Mills, as well as local assemblers.
He questioned how Pakistan could compete when India, Thailand and Indonesia impose completely built-up import duties of around 120%, 80% and 52% respectively, against the proposed 15%, warning that around 300,000 direct jobs could disappear by 2031 if domestic production became commercially unviable.
Aizaz also raised concerns over concessions for new energy vehicles, particularly the proposed 15% localisation target over five years, saying low import duties on electric vehicles and components could shift manufacturing and employment abroad. He questioned facilitating commercial imports of used vehicles without an age limit, saying it contradicted the stated objective of reducing carbon emissions.
Auto expert Mashood Ali Khan said two successive policies covering 2016-21 and 2021-26 had failed to deliver meaningful localisation, with companies offered a 25% incentive to establish local manufacturing but many continuing to import components. He questioned how localisation would be achieved when the completely built-up tariff would fall to 15% by 2031, noting Pakistan had already reached around 65% localisation in several categories.
He urged binding localisation requirements for every new model, with at least 10% of components made locally at launch and an annual roadmap for increasing domestic content and questioned the $6 billion export target envisaging equal contributions from parts makers and original equipment manufacturers.
The Pakistan Automotive Manufacturers Association called the policy a need of the time and asked the ministry for an official copy of the policy for its members.
