items.author: Usman Hanif
items.content:
Pakistan's workers' remittances rose to a four-month high of $3.9 billion in October, taking cumulative inflows during the first four months of FY27 to $14.77 billion, almost enough to cover the country's entire merchandise trade deficit of $14.6 billion during the same period.
The latest figures highlight the growing importance of overseas Pakistanis in supporting the external account, as inflows continued to cushion the widening trade gap and helped contain pressure on foreign exchange reserves.
According to data released by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) on Tuesday, October remittances increased 13.8% year-on-year from $3.42 billion and rose 8.5% month-on-month from $3.59 billion in September, the highest monthly inflow recorded so far in FY27. During July to October, remittances increased 14% to $14.77 billion, against $12.96 billion in the corresponding period last year.
JS Global Head of Equity Research and Senior Vice President Waqas Ghani said, "Overseas Pakistanis just covered almost the entire trade deficit, again." He pointed out that remittances of $14.8 billion during the first four months compared with a merchandise trade deficit of $14.6 billion, which had widened 16% year-on-year.
Sustained inflows, particularly from Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) economies, are helping contain pressure on the current account, support foreign exchange reserves and strengthen the country's external financing position, he said. He added that channel checks indicated economic activity in the Gulf was also recovering, reinforcing the resilience of remittance flows from GCC economies and providing continued support to the external account. "Remittances are buying Pakistan time. The question is whether exports can catch up or nah," he remarked.
Gulf economies remain the biggest source
Country-wise data showed Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates remained the largest sources, contributing $3.67 billion and $3.05 billion respectively during July to October.
Together, the two accounted for around 45.5% of total inflows. Including other GCC countries, the region contributed approximately $8.09 billion, or 54.8% of the total.
Saudi Arabia's remittances increased 16.5% year-on-year, while inflows from the UAE grew 13.5%. Among other GCC economies, Bahrain recorded growth of 15.8%, Kuwait 13.9% and Qatar 13.6%. Within the UAE, Dubai remained the dominant contributor, with remittances rising 28% to $2.51 billion. Inflows from Abu Dhabi, by contrast, declined 29.5% to $443.2 million, indicating diverging trends within the country's major corridors.
UK outpaces US as European inflows grow
Outside the Gulf, the United Kingdom emerged as the largest source, sending $2.23 billion during the first four months, up 19.2% from a year earlier.
Inflows from the United States increased 13.8% to $1.26 billion, while remittances from European Union countries rose 9.6% to $1.87 billion.
Italy contributed $565.2 million, Spain $339.9 million and Germany $282.5 million during the period.
Australia and Canada also maintained positive growth, with remittances rising 12.9% to $386.9 million and 11.5% to $268.9 million respectively. The figures indicate that while the Gulf remains the backbone of remittance inflows, overseas Pakistanis in the UK, Europe, North America and Australia continue to provide an important source of foreign exchange.
Sustained growth offers some relief to the external financing position, though the widening trade deficit underscores the need to strengthen export earnings and reduce reliance on overseas transfers to finance external payments. The rupee continued its marginal appreciation against the US dollar in the interbank market on Tuesday, closing at Rs276.65, up Rs0.01 from the previous session. It had gained 0.03%, or Re0.09, last week to settle at Rs276.66, against Rs276.75 a week earlier, according to SBP data.
Gold prices declined on Tuesday, tracking losses in the international market, with 24-karat gold falling Rs1,500 per tola to Rs430,836.
The price of 10-gram gold dropped Rs1,286 to Rs369,372, according to rates released by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association (APGJSA). In the previous session, gold had increased Rs3,200 per tola to Rs432,336.
In the international market, gold fell $15 to $4,083 per ounce, while silver remained unchanged at Rs5,723 per tola in the local market.

items.author: Shraddha Goled
items.content:
The alleged espionage scandal involving NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang and the growing scrutiny of the chipmaker’s business dealings with China have added another layer of uncertainty to the global AI infrastructure market already facing questions about its financing model.
At the same time, political and regulatory resistance to data centre expansion in the US could slow infrastructure investment, putting pressure on companies that have borrowed heavily to build capacity.
While unrelated, these developments present two separate risks to the investment model underpinning the AI infrastructure boom.
The first is already visible in the American stock market. Investors have been selling shares of US neocloud companies since September, with CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN witnessing sharp corrections. The selling intensified through October and into November, as concerns mounted over the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending and the debt these companies have taken on.
The selloff has only intensified talk of an AI bubble, and neoclouds in India face the risk of getting caught in the middle.
Neoclouds – AI infrastructure providers that offer GPU-as-a-service – have emerged as an important part of NVIDIA’s AI ecosystem. They provide GPU compute to customers that may not have the scale or resources to build their own infrastructure.
Neocloud business models are capital-intensive, with GPU procurement, data centre capacity, and financing arrangements determining how quickly they can scale up. NVIDIA has played a significant role in supporting this ecosystem through strategic investments and financing arrangements, helping expand the market for its chips beyond traditional hyperscalers. India is increasingly becoming part of this infrastructure buildout.
That buildout serves two demand pools. One is subsidised compute for domestic startups, researchers and institutions under the IndiaAI Mission, which had onboarded over 45,000 GPUs by June 2026. By August, it had approved 237 projects for subsidised compute, with 93.18 lakh GPU hours sanctioned. The other is commercial workloads from customers willing to pay for guaranteed capacity. The first highlights the scale of the government programme, but sanctioned hours do not necessarily translate into sustained usage. To justify their spending, India’s neoclouds are betting on the second.
Among the main Indian players, Yotta plans to spend over $7 Bn on AI infrastructure by the end of FY27 and is targeting a $1.5 Bn IPO, partly to repay debt. ESDS went to the market after the cost of the GPU servers it planned to buy rose from ₹25 Lakh to ₹1.8 Cr. E2E Networks, meanwhile, reported a 411% year-on-year jump in Q2 revenue.
Besides these, the likes of NxtGen, NeevCloud and Neysa are also building their neocloud infrastructure in India in anticipation of a big adoption wave.
US giant CoreWeave is also entering India as the sole tenant of a planned 240 MW AdaniConneX data centre campus. However, any sustained pressure on its financing or expansion plans could have implications for the project.
If concerns in the US around data centre build-up trickle down to India, neoclouds will be one of the first to get hit as a lot of their build-up depends on institutional funding commitment. The question is whether Indian companies will continue to enjoy the financial backing and attract customer commitments to withstand the headwinds if and when they come.
No Anchor Customers In India
The investment case for US AI infrastructure companies is underpinned by large customers such as Meta and OpenAI, whose scale and long-term compute requirements offer some visibility into future demand. These anchor customers make it easier for infrastructure providers to secure financing and justify large upfront investments.
Indian neoclouds, however, do not yet have comparable customer base to underwrite their expansion plans. International customers now account for 75-80% of Yotta’s customer base, partly because they are willing to pay more. Within India, however, the IndiaAI Mission is emerging as an important source of demand, although it utilised less than half its FY26 outlay of ₹10,000 Cr, which has directly impacted hardware procurement and deployment timelines, as Neysa mentioned in one of its blogs.
A recent Moneycontrol report highlighted a mismatch in the Indian market: some GPUs are underused, while startups and researchers say fragmented capacity, allocation delays and the type of hardware on offer can make suitable compute difficult to obtain. A headline GPU count may therefore obscure both the quality of available clusters and the path from allocation to actual use.
The mismatch makes domestic demand hard to read. The demand exists, but it does not always reach the neoclouds that have built capacity for it. Even well-funded companies are waiting. Juspay, which buys GPUs with its own cash, has been “given commitments that it will take three to six months” to receive them, co-founder and COO Sheetal Lalwani said at a media briefing. When large customers buy and run their own hardware, and smaller ones struggle to find suitable clusters, aggregate capacity figures say little about how much will turn into long-term, paying contracts for neoclouds.
Can government-backed compute requirements offer the kind of long-term revenue visibility that hyperscaler contracts provide in the US? Or will Indian neoclouds remain dependent on international customers to sustain utilisation and justify their infrastructure investments?
GPU infrastructure requires substantial upfront capital, while the returns depend on sustained utilisation, predictable demand and long-term customer commitments. Notably, government-led regulations as well as citizen pushback could limit data centre build; it even emerged as a major factor for voters in the recent US midterm elections. For Indian neocloud players, which are increasingly catering to foreign and especially US-based clients, could suffer a trickle-down effect. Neocloud stocks, those of Coreweave, Nebius and Iren, among others, battered after the Democratic win in the recent elections.
Closer home, ESDS and E2E stocks are already suffering from the second order impact of the sharp selloff in US tech stocks, following the mid-term results. On November 9, ESDS closed at approximately ₹1,147.25, against a September 24 high of ₹1,864.35, while E2E Networks ended at around ₹490.50, significantly lower than its October 14 high of ₹769.
The NVIDIA Question
NVIDIA’s role in the neocloud ecosystem goes beyond supplying GPUs. Its investments, financing arrangements and partnerships with infrastructure providers have helped bring new compute capacity online. But the relationship varies across Indian companies.
NeevCloud said its engagement with NVIDIA covers technical planning, GPU availability and deployment readiness. Procurement, financing and customer contracts are separate arrangements. The company acknowledged the concentration risk of relying on a single technology provider, but said it ties investments to customer commitments and available financing.
“The market correction reinforces the need for discipline. We assess each project on its commercial viability and phase investments accordingly,” Narendra Sen, founder of NeevCloud and RackBank Datacenters, told Inc42.
ESDS said it has no direct commercial or financing relationship with NVIDIA. The company buys systems from OEMs and system integrators such as Supermicro, Dell, Lenovo and WWT. It has also signed a $1.25 Bn, seven-year agreement with Australia’s Sharon AI. Sharon AI owns and operates an 8,000-GPU cluster, which ESDS uses to serve its domestic and global customers. ESDS plans to explore similar partnerships.
“I would separate technology dependence from financial dependence,” said Piyush Somani, founder of ESDS. He pointed out that all of ESDS’s deployed GPU capacity runs on NVIDIA.
Financing is a different matter. ESDS commits capex only after a customer has paid at least 35% of the project cost, and only then does it place orders with OEMs or system integrators, Somani said.
Both companies say financing for neocloud centres is getting more selective. Lenders and investors now favour projects with confirmed customers, predictable revenues and substantial upfront advances. Sen added that older GPUs could face more pricing pressure as newer generations arrive.
This is where the economic model gets complicated. NVIDIA has offered neoclouds worldwide a revenue-sharing and credit-support model in July, but later paused some of the deals, as reported by The Wall Street Journal.
Yotta is exploring similar structures where partners fund and own the GPUs, while the company installs and operates them in its data centres and signs customer contracts.
Gorilla, the Nasdaq-listed British tech company, is one such partner. In April, the two companies deepened their partnership, adding another $2.8 Bn to an agreement that was initially valued at $500 Mn.
Such partnership models depend on GPU rental prices holding up. If compute prices fall or older GPUs lose value faster than expected, who absorbs the loss: the neocloud, the customer or the financing partner?
The Jensen Huang Overhang
NVIDIA’s chips, software stack and partnerships shape how quickly new compute capacity comes online. That is one of the reasons The Economist has called it the “central bank of AI”. This also highlights growing concerns about the AI ecosystem’s dependence on NVIDIA.
On November 8, NVIDIA’s board launched an independent investigation into reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Huang has acknowledged an extramarital affair with a woman alleged to be spying for the Chinese government. The NVIDIA board, however, has maintained that it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.
Questions about her alleged links to Chinese intelligence, and what they mean for NVIDIA’s China business, remain open.
For Indian neoclouds, the direct exposure is less about a change in NVIDIA’s leadership and more about their dependence on globally-sourced GPUs and NVIDIA’s software ecosystem. The Government of India has said its compute ecosystem currently relies on globally-sourced GPUs and any change in chip availability, export controls, pricing or allocation could affect deployment schedules and project economics.
There is no evidence yet that the controversy has affected NVIDIA’s relationships with Indian neoclouds. But any fallout for its leadership, China business or financing strategy would hit an ecosystem that leans heavily on NVIDIA’s technology. There are concerns regarding what a potential wider restructuring of NVIDIA might mean for the neocloud business, especially if the build-up of data centres slows down in the US.
Incidentally, NVIDIA is set to announce its third quarter earnings on November 17, 2026, and this will reveal much more about the underlying numbers for the data centre business. Will the corporate governance issues have an overhang on the stock till then?
In February this year, the fear was that AI would trigger a SaaSpocalypse. Since then, models have advanced and the opportunities have grown bigger, but the concern now is whether the companies building AI infrastructure can carry the debt and capital commitments needed to keep this boom going.
The post NVIDIA Scandal & AI Selloff In the US: India’s Neocloud Boom Faces Twin Tests appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.content:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, on Tuesday, declared that the federal government will not reverse its decision on fuel subsidy, saying bringing back subsidy would jeopardise the future of Nigerian children.
‎
‎Speaking at the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign rally in Dutse, Jigawa State, Tinubu said claims that the subsidy would be restored were false.
‎
‎”To those who say subsidy is coming back, it’s a lie. Don’t let them lie to you again. It’s not going to come back,” he said.
‎
‎The president said resources previously spent on fuel subsidy would instead be channelled into education, agriculture and infrastructure development.
FG commissions three CNG facilities in Kano
PHOTOS: Supporters Await Tinubu at APC Rally in Jigawa
‎He pledged interest-free loans for smallholder farmers and announced plans to establish mechanised farming service centres across the country’s six geopolitical zones to boost food production and reduce food prices.
‎
‎”We have to invest in agriculture. There will be interest-free loans for farmers. Prosperity is coming. Food security will happen,” he said.
‎
‎Tinubu also assured Nigerians that his administration was taking decisive steps to tackle insecurity, urging citizens to support security agencies by reporting suspicious activities.
‎
‎”We are working hard to ensure that Nigeria is safe. We will conquer insecurity. We will defeat the enemies of unity, stability and hope,” he said.
‎
‎The president said the government had strengthened security agencies through improved welfare and better remuneration for personnel.
‎
‎On education, Tinubu said funds recovered from corruption-related cases by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) would be channelled into the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) to support access to education and reduce poverty.
‎
‎He described NELFUND as “our weapon against poverty” and promised continued investment in human capital development.
‎
‎The president also highlighted his administration’s plans to improve power supply, support small and medium-scale enterprises, expand job opportunities and develop skills among young Nigerians.
‎
‎Earlier, Tinubu commended Governor Umar Namadi for his developmental strides in Jigawa State and called on residents to support him for a second term in office.
‎
‎”I have been here a number of years. I have never seen so much progress. This man has worked tirelessly for all of us,” he said.
‎
‎The APC rally drew party supporters from across the state as the president formally presented the party’s manifesto and roadmap for economic prosperity.

items.author: M Yasir
items.content:
Commercial banks in Pakistan are prepared to spend Rs. 100 billion from their own resources during fiscal year 2026-27 to attract more remittances and reduce the cost of sending money to Pakistan, Pakistan Banks Association (PBA) Chairman Zafar Masud has said.
Speaking at a media meetup at the Karachi Press Club, Masud said banks had decided to fund the initiative after the government stopped providing subsidies for remittance transactions.
He said overseas Pakistanis currently pay between 18 and 20 riyals to send every $200 to Pakistan. Banks are now covering this cost from their own profits to make formal money transfers cheaper and encourage more people to use banking channels.
Banks have also allocated Rs. 16 billion for the Pasban Remittance Reward Scheme. The program encourages overseas Pakistanis to send money through formal channels and offers rewards for their families in Pakistan.
PBA Chief Executive Officer Munir Kamal said the scheme aims to help maintain annual remittance inflows at around $41 billion. Its first balloting is scheduled for January, with an audit planned to ensure transparency.
Masud also shared details of banks’ financing activities in other sectors. He said the number of people benefiting from bank financing for housing had increased to more than 350,000 from 65,000. The housing loan portfolio has grown to Rs. 455 billion from Rs. 200 billion over the past two years.
Banks have also maintained a 4 percent refinancing rate for exporters despite higher interest rates, providing nearly Rs. 100 billion in subsidies from their own resources, he said.
In the energy sector, banks are restructuring Rs. 1.3 trillion in debt over the next two years to help address circular debt. The process is expected to reduce electricity bills by nearly Rs. 3 per unit once completed.
Masud said banks had also committed to increasing annual agricultural financing from Rs. 1.3 trillion to Rs. 3.3 trillion and expanding lending to farmers.
Meanwhile, Kamal said bank financing to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) had increased to Rs. 1.2 trillion from Rs. 490 billion over the past couple of years.
Masud also called for reducing cash transactions and expanding digital payment methods, including QR codes, to limit the undocumented economy.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
The controversy surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has expanded beyond reports of an extramarital affair, with new allegations linking his relationship with a Chinese businesswoman to at least $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chip shipments to China.
According to a November 10 report by The Information, Alice Huang, a business executive suspected by US intelligence officials of working for China, allegedly used her relationship with Jensen Huang and a network of companies to facilitate the movement of advanced AI chips to Chinese firms.
The report claims the network helped supply approximately 240,000 Nvidia H100, H200, and A100 chips to China, including models subject to US export restrictions.
Reuters reported the allegations but said it could not independently verify them.
Who Is Alice Huang?
Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, is a Chinese businesswoman who held an executive position at Singapore-based Megaspeed International, a major Nvidia customer.
According to The Information, she worked with her husband and sister to establish a network of companies across China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia processors.
One of the companies, Shanghai Century Litong, was established in June 2023 and secured preferred cloud partner status with Nvidia by October of that year.
The designation reportedly gave the company priority access to Nvidia chips.
US intelligence officials reportedly suspect Alice Huang of working for Chinese intelligence. However, China has rejected the espionage allegations as unsubstantiated.
How Nvidia Chips Allegedly Reached China
The Information reported that Alice Huang used connections at Nvidia and its distributors to secure chip supplies when orders involving US-restricted processors stalled.
The network allegedly moved around 240,000 Nvidia chips into China through companies operating across China and Southeast Asia.
Shanghai Century Litong reportedly operated data centers and rented computing capacity using Nvidia processors, including chips restricted from sale to China.
Some of the computing services reportedly reached major Chinese technology companies, including Alibaba, Tencent, and smaller AI laboratories.
Megaspeed and its Malaysian subsidiary, Speedmatrix, were also linked to the supply network.
According to the report, Megaspeed supplied computing capacity to Chinese customers through Southeast Asian data centers and allegedly transferred physical hardware into China.
The allegations have not been independently verified by Reuters.
Nvidia Reportedly Intervened in US Chip Investigation
Separately, Bloomberg reported that Nvidia’s general counsel, Tim Teter, contacted US Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler in 2025 about an investigation involving Megaspeed.
Teter reportedly asked whether US authorities were involved in the detention of Alice Huang by Singapore officials.
According to Bloomberg, Commerce Department investigators subsequently faced restrictions on their ability to investigate Megaspeed and communicate directly with Nvidia.
However, it remains unclear whether Nvidia requested those restrictions or whether the contact directly caused them.
Nvidia said Teter was unaware of Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang when he contacted US officials.
Megaspeed has denied allegations of illegal chip transfers, saying reviews by US, Malaysian, and Nvidia officials found no evidence of violations.
Nvidia CEO Admits Affair as Investigations Begin
Jensen Huang acknowledged on November 8 that he had been unfaithful to his wife and apologized to his family and Nvidia employees.
Nvidia’s board subsequently launched an independent investigation into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation and whether the relationship created security risks.
The FBI is also examining the allegations surrounding the suspected espionage operation.
Nvidia said its board had no reason to believe company secrets or national security had been compromised, although the investigation would examine the available information.
The company also confirmed that Huang would continue serving as CEO during the investigation.
The latest reporting raises questions about the relationship between Nvidia’s chip distribution network, its customers, and US export restrictions.
However, investigators have not established that Jensen Huang knowingly facilitated illegal chip exports or that Nvidia deliberately created a secret channel to bypass US restrictions.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Tuesday defended his brief interaction with former army chief Gen Qamar Javed Bajwa, saying political hostilities should end, and clarified that the two had merely exchanged greetings at a wedding.
A picture of the PTI chairman shaking hands with the former army chief at the function began circulating on social media last week, drawing criticism from PTI supporters and party officials.
They criticised Gohar for interacting with Gen Bajwa, whom they accused of playing a role in the PTI government's ouster in 2022, with some also calling for the PTI chairman's resignation.
Read: Gohar demands immediate implementation of SC order on Imran's medical treatment
Speaking to reporters on Adiala Road in Rawalpindi, Gohar defended his interaction with Gen Bajwa, saying that there had been no discussion beyond exchanging greetings at the wedding ceremony while condemning what he described as propaganda against him over the encounter.
He said political differences should not be allowed to turn into permanent animosity, adding that relationships could change over time.
“Enemies can become friends and friends can become enemies with the passage of time. Hatred should come to an end,” he said.
Defending his interaction with Gen Bajwa, the PTI chairman said there had been no discussion beyond exchanging greetings at the wedding ceremony while condemning what he described as propaganda against him over the encounter.
Meanwhile, Gohar rejected the possibility of PTI boycotting the upcoming local government elections, saying the party would participate like other political parties.
He said candidates had been directed to prepare their nomination papers for the three constituencies in Islamabad.
The PTI chairman said the PTI did not want confrontation with any state institution, adding that heads of all institutions should remain within their constitutional limits.
Gohar welcomed the Islamabad High Court's order regarding meetings with incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, expressing hope that it would be implemented this time.
He said court orders had not been followed for the past two years and that restrictions on meetings with the former prime minister had contributed to political tensions.
The PTI chairman said the information about Imran Khan's health brought by Barrister Salman Safdar after meeting him was not encouraging. He also called for implementation of the Supreme Court's Aug 18 order.
Asked about contacts with the government, Gohar said the party remained in touch with the government and the interior minister, but there were currently no negotiations or backchannel discussions underway.
Read More: Gohar refutes reports of Imran welcoming end of K-P government
He said dialogue was necessary to ease political tensions.
Regarding meetings with Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, Gohar said the discussions had taken place in connection with the proposed All Parties Conference (APC).
He said the two parties could join hands on issues of common concern; however, it was too early to discuss a joint movement.
Commenting on the situation in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, the PTI chairman said governor's rule or an emergency could not serve as an alternative to a democratic government.
He demanded an end to governor's rule, saying the fact that people had not taken to the streets in protest should not be interpreted as an indication that public anger had subsided.

A statement by the commission on Tuesday said the Tranche C is an approval of N30bn to be allocated among the eleven Distribution Companies (DisCos) in proportion to their respective contributions to the Fund.

“Under the Order, DisCos are required to undertake transparent procurement processes involving eligible Local Meter Manufacturers and Assemblers (LMMAs) and Meter Asset Providers (MAPs) with verified meter stock.
“The Commission has prescribed maximum procurement prices based on the median national MAP online bid prices from the September 2026 bid cycle.
“Payment to selected providers shall be made in two stages: 70% upon verified delivery of meter stock and the remaining 30% upon confirmation of complete installation.”
It stressed that all meters supplied and installed under the MAF programme will be provided free of charge to customers, adding that every meter must prominently display the relevant DisCo’s name, the applicable MAF tranche and the inscription “NOT FOR SALE”.

items.title: Binance Spots iOS Bug That Could Put Cryptocurrency Wallet Keys at Risk
items.summary: Binance has warned iPhone users about a potential iOS security vulnerability known as worse_query, which could allow malicious applications to access files belonging to other apps. The issue reportedly affects multiple iOS 26 and iOS 27 versions and could expose sensitive information, including cryptocurrency wallet recovery phrases and private keys. The exchange advised users to remove untrusted applications, update their software, and create new wallet credentials on a fresh device if they suspect their information has been compromised. There is currently no confirmed evidence of cryptocurrency theft linked to the vulnerability.

items.content:
The Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) on Tuesday said it had agreed with the government on the broad outlines of an agreement to extend petroleum-related relief to consumers, but warned it could resume its long march if the negotiations failed to produce a concrete outcome on its demand for abolishing the petroleum levy.
The government and JI held a 10th round of talks on the petroleum levy, with both sides agreeing on the need to provide relief to consumers, particularly low-income households, while discussions on a phased reduction of the levy also came under discussion.
Speaking at a press conference after the 10th round of talks with the government committee, JI deputy chief Liaquat Baloch said the two sides had agreed on the need to expand the existing relief measures, while the government would consult the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on continuing the relief.
اسلام آباد: نائب امیر جماعتِ اسلامی لیاقت بلوچ کی پیٹرولیم لیوی کے معاملے پر حکومتی کمیٹی سے مذاکرات کے بعد اہم پریس کانفرنس۔
لیاقت بلوچ نے کہا کہ آج حکومتی کمیٹی کے ساتھ مذاکرات کا دسواں دور تھا۔ ہمارے سامنے عوام کو ریلیف دلانا اہم ترین معاملہ تھا۔ حکومت نے تسلیم کیا ہے کہ… pic.twitter.com/c9VCU9rXLS
— Jamaat e Islami Pakistan (@JIPOfficial) November 10, 2026
He said providing relief to the public remained the foremost concern during the negotiations and that the government had acknowledged difficulties in the supply of petroleum products due to the global situation.
Baloch said JI had proposed including vehicles with engines of up to 1,000cc and the agricultural sector in the relief scheme.
He said the government had also acknowledged that JI's demand for abolishing the petroleum levy was legitimate.
“Our demand is that the levy should be abolished immediately and the public should be given clear relief,” he said, criticising the government for being unwilling to cut its luxuries and putting the burden of the Federal Board of Revenue's (FBR) failures on consumers.
Baloch said the two sides had agreed on the broad outlines of a draft agreement during Tuesday's meeting, with the government expected to share further details in the coming days.
He said that the government had informed the JI delegation that it had started working on a plan to address its revenue requirements and would share a framework for gradually reducing the levy after consultations with the IMF.
Read: JI to march on Islamabad in mid-November if govt fails to end petroleum levy: Hafiz Naeem
He said another meeting was expected on Wednesday or Thursday, while the final decision on the proposed agreement would be taken during a possible meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and JI chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman.
Following that meeting, the party would decide whether to proceed with its planned long march, he added.
The JI leader claimed that the party's protest had helped halt increases in petroleum prices and secured relief of Rs146 per litre on diesel and Rs120 per litre on petrol.
“The process has now reached the stage of final decisions,” he said.
He said JI remained committed to peaceful political engagement but would withdraw from the negotiations if it found that the government was unwilling to move forward.
“Our only goal is that the people should get relief, that there should be a reduction in production costs, that the economy should run and that people should get employment,” he said, adding that the party's protests and political pressure were aimed at securing relief for the public.
The government also confirmed the talks, with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar holding a follow-up meeting with a JI delegation led by Baloch to continue consultations on petroleum prices and relief for consumers, according to a statement issued by the DPM's Office.
Held a follow-up meeting with a delegation of Jamaat-e-Islami (JI), led by Mr. Liaquat Baloch, today to continue consultations on petroleum prices and public relief. https://t.co/oTRkVyH1gm
— Ishaq Dar (@MIshaqDar50) November 10, 2026
The statement said both sides held constructive discussions on measures to provide relief to consumers, particularly low-income households.
There was broad agreement on the need to address public concerns through continued consultation and cooperation, it added.
Dar welcomed the positive spirit of the engagement and reiterated that the government remained focused on supporting ordinary households amid prevailing economic challenges.
The meeting was attended by Adviser to the Prime Minister on Inter-Provincial Coordination Rana Sanaullah, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister Tariq Bajwa, the special secretary of the Petroleum Division, an additional secretary of the Finance Division and JI delegation members Syed Firasat Shah, Nasrullah Randhawa and Inayatullah Khan.
Background
JI’s campaign against the petroleum levy intensified in August, when the party organised demonstrations and sit-ins across the country against rising fuel prices, inflation and what it described as an additional tax burden on consumers. On August 16, JI workers staged sit-ins outside governors’ houses in the provincial capitals, demanding the withdrawal of the levy and a reduction in petrol prices.
The party subsequently expanded its protests to other cities, including Karachi, where it established additional protest camps across Sindh. JI maintained that the government should abolish the levy rather than offer limited reductions in fuel prices.
On September 3, the government and JI agreed to establish technical committees to examine proposals for reducing the petroleum levy and fuel prices. During the first round of negotiations on September 7, the party submitted six proposals to the government, while insisting that its protests would continue until meaningful relief was provided.
However, the negotiations failed to resolve the dispute. On September 12, JI chief announced a long march towards Islamabad for September 20, warning that the party would intensify its campaign if the government did not abolish the levy.
Read More: JI launches third phase of protest campaign against petroleum levy
The march began on September 20, with participants travelling from Karachi by train. The caravan moved through Sukkur towards Multan, where Naeem addressed supporters. The march was subsequently suspended after PM Shehbaz telephoned the JI chief and requested that the party postpone its protest to allow further negotiations.
JI agreed to give the government an opportunity for talks but maintained that it had not abandoned its demand. The party’s position was that negotiations and protests could continue simultaneously, with any agreement required to address the complete abolition of the levy.
The JI chief then gave the government 10 days to abolish the petroleum levy and provide meaningful relief to the inflation-hit public, warning that his party would resume its long march towards Islamabad in mid-November if its demands were not met.

items.title: Why an Instagram Following Tracker Can Reveal More Than a Profile’s Follower Count
items.summary:
A popular Instagram account can attract thousands of followers, but that number rarely tells the whole story. For businesses, content creators, and people researching social media trends, another question can be just as interesting: which accounts does that person choose to follow?
Someone may publicly promote fashion, technology, or entertainment while following creators in entirely different fields. A business account may begin following emerging influencers long before announcing a collaboration. A public figure may gradually change the types of accounts appearing on their Following list.
These observations can provide useful context, particularly when viewed over time.
An Instagram following tracker helps organize changes to the accounts a public Instagram profile follows. Rather than relying on a single snapshot, tools such as Snoopreport record detected follows and unfollows across reporting periods.
The results can support social media research, although they cannot explain why
items.author: Ison Etim
items.content:
A popular Instagram account can attract thousands of followers, but that number rarely tells the whole story. For businesses, content creators, and people researching social media trends, another question can be just as interesting: which accounts does that person choose to follow?
Someone may publicly promote fashion, technology, or entertainment while following creators in entirely different fields. A business account may begin following emerging influencers long before announcing a collaboration. A public figure may gradually change the types of accounts appearing on their Following list.
These observations can provide useful context, particularly when viewed over time.
An Instagram following tracker helps organize changes to the accounts a public Instagram profile follows. Rather than relying on a single snapshot, tools such as Snoopreport record detected follows and unfollows across reporting periods.
The results can support social media research, although they cannot explain why someone followed an account or reveal information that Instagram keeps private.
Why Follower Counts Don’t Tell the Whole Story
Follower numbers are among Instagram’s most visible statistics.
They influence how people assess popularity, reach, and sometimes commercial value. Yet having a large audience doesn’t necessarily mean an account has a clearly defined set of interests or strong connections within a particular industry.
The Following list offers a different perspective.
Consider a technology commentator who starts following several artificial intelligence researchers, software companies, and digital policy organizations. Those additions may suggest topics worth investigating.
Similarly, a lifestyle influencer who follows numerous local restaurants might be exploring a new content category.
Neither example proves a professional plan or future collaboration. Following someone can reflect curiosity, personal connections, or temporary interest.
Still, when researchers compare several observations across time, they may discover changes worth examining further.
The Difference Between Following and Followers
Before using an Instagram following tracker, it’s important to distinguish two commonly confused terms.
Followers are people who subscribe to an account’s updates.
Following refers to the accounts that the profile has chosen to follow.
For example, a creator may have 40,000 followers while following only 600 accounts. A following tracker focuses on changes within those 600 connections, not on identifying people who recently followed the creator.
Instagram allows users to inspect the Following list of an accessible public profile. However, the list doesn’t provide a dependable chronological history of when each connection was added.
The order in which accounts appear should not be treated as a reliable record of recent follows.
To understand changes, the list needs to be observed across different periods.
What Changes in the Following List Can Tell You
Imagine a small fashion retailer researching potential brand ambassadors.
A popular stylist’s profile looks promising, but the retailer wants to understand which types of creators, labels, and businesses attract the stylist’s attention.
A single visit to the Following list offers a snapshot. Regular observations can reveal which accounts were added or removed during a particular period.
If the stylist begins following several sustainable clothing labels, the retailer might investigate whether environmentally conscious fashion is becoming a more prominent topic in that creator’s public activity.
The important word is might.
Following an account is not an endorsement, a commercial agreement, or confirmation of an individual’s private interests.
The value comes from generating research questions that can be checked against public posts, published partnerships, and other evidence.
How Snoopreport Tracks Public Following Activity
Snoopreport is a service that monitors certain publicly observable Instagram actions and organizes detected changes into reports.
Its Instagram following tracker focuses on accounts that a selected public profile begins or stops following.
The process starts with an Instagram username. Users don’t need to provide their own Instagram password.
Once an eligible public account is added, Snoopreport begins collecting detectable activity and presents the findings in weekly and monthly reports.
These reports can help users identify:
Accounts the tracked profile recently followed.
Accounts it stopped following during a reporting period.
Changes that appear across successive weeks or months.
A regular report establishes that a detected change occurred within a period. It doesn’t provide a guaranteed exact timestamp or explain the reason behind the action.
The service does not provide access to private profiles, direct messages, or information about who viewed someone’s Stories.
Why Time Matters More Than a Single Snapshot
A public Following list can change without attracting much attention.
An account may add several new connections in one week and remove others the following month. Without a record, those changes may be difficult to reconstruct later.
An Instagram following tracker makes comparisons easier by grouping detected activity into defined reporting periods.
Weekly reports can be useful when examining a developing topic, such as the emergence of a new group of creators in a particular industry.
Monthly reports offer a broader perspective, helping separate recurring interests from isolated additions.
For example, if a public business profile repeatedly follows entrepreneurs working in renewable energy, that pattern may be worth exploring.
But the observation should be interpreted carefully. It could reflect market research, general curiosity, networking, or another explanation entirely.
A pattern is a reason to investigate, not a conclusion.
The Difference Between a Feed and an Activity Record
Instagram has introduced several ways to help people control the posts appearing in their feeds.
In its official explanation of Following and Favorites, Meta describes a chronological Following feed that displays posts from accounts a user follows.
That feature serves a different purpose from monitoring changes to someone else’s Following list.
A chronological feed organizes content by publication time. It doesn’t tell an observer which accounts another person followed last week.
This distinction matters because social media platforms offer several features with similar names but very different capabilities.
People researching past changes need an activity history rather than simply a different way to browse posts.
Practical Uses for Businesses and Social Media Researchers
For a small business, following activity can support creator discovery.
A company may observe public profiles within its industry and use changes in their connections as clues for finding unfamiliar creators, businesses, or communities.
Journalists and media researchers may also find the information useful when studying publicly visible networks around a cultural trend.
For instance, tracking selected public accounts associated with entertainment, technology, or fashion could help identify new voices worth interviewing.
The data can also complement conventional social media research.
Rather than treating a follow as evidence of a relationship, analysts can compare it with published content, public announcements, and direct statements.
This approach is especially important where a mistaken conclusion could affect someone’s reputation.
What Snoopreport Costs and What It Cannot Capture
Snoopreport’s plans start at $4.99 per month for tracking two public Instagram accounts. Higher tiers support larger account lists, while optional AI Summary plans cost more.
The service also offers retrospective reports for eligible earlier periods at a separate price.
However, the available data is incomplete by design.
Not every Instagram action is publicly observable, and Snoopreport states that its detection may capture up to 75% of public activity rather than every follow or unfollow.
A missing result shouldn’t be interpreted as proof that an action never occurred.
Likewise, reports don’t show private-account activity, direct messages, or the motivations behind a decision to follow someone.
These limits should be considered before using the information for professional research.
Privacy and Responsible Interpretation
Public social media information can be useful, but it still needs to be handled responsibly.
Someone following a political commentator, health organization, business, or public figure does not necessarily share that account’s views or have any personal connection to it.
People follow accounts for many reasons, including research, disagreement, entertainment, and professional curiosity.
Businesses should avoid using isolated following activity to make judgments about someone’s character or suitability for employment.
Researchers should also respect privacy, avoid harassment, and verify important findings through independent sources.
A Better Way to Understand Instagram Connections
Instagram is a network of evolving interests, communities, and public connections.
Follower totals show the size of an audience, while following activity can offer clues about the accounts attracting someone’s attention.
Tools such as Snoopreport make it easier to review detected changes to public Following lists across weekly and monthly periods.
For creators, businesses, and researchers, the most useful findings usually come from patterns supported by other evidence.
A follow is a visible action, not an explanation. Understanding that difference makes social media research more accurate and responsible.

items.content:
The National Accountability Bureau (NAB) on Tuesday issued a second call-up notice to the son of Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, Asad Mahmood, directing him to appear before the anti-graft watchdog on November 13 in an inquiry into alleged illegal appointments in the Pakistan Post Office Department (PPOD).
NAB Rawalpindi is conducting an inquiry against officials and employees of the PPOD and others over allegations of illegal recruitment.
Mahmood, who served as federal minister for communications and postal services from 2022 to 2023, was summoned in connection with the alleged appointments made during his tenure.
Read: Noose tightens for Fazl, inner circle
Mahmood was required to appear before NAB on November 10 but failed to do so and instead had submitted a written response through his lawyer.
NAB officials declared his response unsatisfactory and issued a fresh notice, directing him to appear in person at 11am on Friday.
The notice warned that failure to appear could lead to legal proceedings under Section 31 of the National Accountability Ordinance, 1999.
NAB had earlier summoned Rehman's son on November 5 over alleged irregularities in the appointments at the PPOD during his tenure.
According to the earlier NAB notice, the Establishment Division had authorised recruitment against 3,938 posts at the Pakistan Post Office, but 4,252 people were allegedly appointed. The inquiry has also flagged appointments against 2,646 abolished posts, allegedly in violation of cabinet committee directives.
NAB maintains that despite recommendations for contractual recruitment through a testing agency, a large number of permanent appointments were made, potentially placing an additional financial burden on the department.

On November 2, the government announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
Mohalla Tech, the parent of social media platforms ShareChat and Moj, reported a 78.5% YoY increase in its consolidated net loss to ₹1,978.4 Cr in the financial year ended March 2026 (FY26), weighed down by higher share-based payment expenses, foreign exchange losses and finance costs.
The loss for the fiscal year widened despite a 40.4% jump in operating revenue to ₹1,016.3 Cr from ₹723.4 Cr in FY25.
Further, the startup also reported an improvement in its operating performance. ShareChat’s management claims that it managed to narrow its FY26 EBITDA loss by 58% YoY to ₹91 Cr and recorded its first EBITDA positive quarter in Q1 FY27.
The company reported an EBITDA profit of ₹9.5 Cr and a margin of 0.3% in the June quarter. Its EBITDA margin improved to over 2% in Q2 FY27, the management claimed.
QuickTV Subscription Drives Revenue Growth
The startup’s management said its FY26 top line growth was led by the launch of QuickTV, its subscription-based microdrama platform launched in February 2025.
The subscription vertical, which accounts for subscriptions from both Quick TV and Moj (Moj+ and Moj Blue), raked in a revenue of ₹292.7 Cr in the fiscal, accounting for almost 30% of the top line in the fiscal.
Mohalla Tech had counted advertising and livestreaming as its two major pillars for revenue generation since its inception over a decade ago. In the previous fiscal year, it aggressively expanded into monetising the content on its platform amid a growing fervour for microdramas in the Indian content landscape.
Hailed as the “next phase of evolution for the entertainment industry“, Microdrama adoption picked pace in the Indian market early in FY26. ShareChat had launched its vertical microdrama platform, QuickTV, earlier in February 2025. Since then, the app has been downloaded by over 5 Cr users from the Google Play Store.
As its content monetisation took shape, the social media unicorn faced some operational turmoil for its long-set revenue driver — advertising.
Advertising revenue dipped 13% YoY to ₹251.8 Cr in the fiscal year. This decline came as advertisers from the real money gaming (RMG) stopped promotional spends. To note, ShareChat had already diversified its offerings for clients across FMCG and mid-market advertisers. Hence, it managed to offset the dent anticipated from the RMG ban.
On the other hand, ShareChat’s livestreaming segment grew almost by 9% YoY to ₹471.8 Cr. This segment registers revenue from paying users on both ShareChat and Moj platforms.
ShareChat’s FY27 Outlook
For the fiscal year FY27, Mohalla Tech is targeting an EBITDA profit of ₹25 Cr, including at least ₹15 Cr in the second half of FY27.
The startup reported around ₹740 Cr in revenue in the first half of FY27, while its Q2 FY27 annualised revenue run rate reached approximately ₹1,500 Cr. It did not disclose its bottom line performance for the September half of the ongoing fiscal.
To fuel this financial improvement, the startup is expecting both of its content monetisation models — subscription video on demand (SVOD) and advertising-based video on demand (AVOD) — to shoulder its next phase of growth.
ShareChat is expecting its advertising to make a stronger contribution in FY27, growing by 40% YoY. While it is expecting its AVOD revenue to surpass the ₹350 Cr mark, this particular revenue stream touched ₹160 Cr in the first half.
The management didn’t share any projections for revenue from SVOD in the fiscal. It believes that most Indian internet users are unlikely to pay for microdrama subscriptions, with the number of paying users for the format expected to remain below 100 Mn even as the market matures, making advertising an important monetisation opportunity.
The Microdrama Dillema
Mohalla Tech’s push into microdrama comes as the format draws growing interest across businesses.
EloElo Group, the parent of microdrama platform Story TV, recently raised $80 Mn (around ₹756 Cr) in a Series C round led by Hornbill Capital and NBCUniversal. The company plans to invest in original content across Indian languages, expand Story TV internationally and strengthen its AI-powered production capabilities. Story TV has more than 5,000 microdramas across six languages, while EloElo claims over 40 Mn monthly active users across its apps.
The space has also attracted startups such as Kuku TV, Flick TV, ReelSaga and Chai Shots, alongside larger platforms including JioHotstar’s Tadka, Zee Entertainment’s Bullet and Amazon MX Player’s MX Fatafat. Businesses and platforms are utilising the short-story format to plug in marketing and products while capitalising on the rise in vertical content consumption.
However, rising customer acquisition costs and the difficulty of converting free viewers into paying subscribers continue to weigh on the economics of standalone microdrama platforms. For instance, Mohalla Tech said acquiring a user on its free-to-use platform Moj costs around ₹14-15 per download, while acquiring a paying subscriber for QuickTV costs hundreds of rupees, given the latter’s newer brand and subscription paywall. It claimed that competing subscription platforms could be spending upwards of ₹1,000 per subscriber.
Owing to this, platforms like Mohalla Tech are instead banking on advertising revenue and marketing plug-ins to increase monetisation.
Where Did ShareChat Spend In FY26?
Mohalla Tech’s total expenses surged 65.6% to ₹3,083 Cr in FY26 from ₹1,862.1 Cr a year earlier.
During its FY26 earnings call, management said the reported loss was largely driven by non-cash and notional accounting items, including provisions for interest on hybrid debt instruments, unrealised foreign exchange losses and ESOP expenses.
Employee Benefit Expenses: Expenses under this head more than doubled to ₹959.5 Cr from ₹445.8 Cr in FY25. A large part of the increase came from share-based payments, which climbed 302% to ₹739 Cr in FY26 from ₹183.8 Cr in FY25, following an expansion of the company’s ESOP pool and additional grants to key employees.
Foreign Exchange Losses: Owing to rupee-dollar depreciation, non-cash expenses under this head rose more than fourfold to ₹566.9 Cr from ₹128 Cr in FY25. The increase was largely driven by unrealised forex losses of ₹566 Cr.
Business Development: Expenses under this head, which usually covers functions like marketing, promotions and customer acquisition, surged 7.7X to ₹334.8 Cr from ₹43.4 Cr in FY26.
The post ShareChat Parent Mohalla Tech’s FY26 Revenue Crosses ₹1,000 Cr Mark; Loss Widens 79% To ₹1,978 Cr appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Healthcare AI startup Froncort.AI has secured $2.3 Mn (₹21.5 Cr) in fresh capital from Google’s philanthropic arm, Google.org, to scale its AI-powered disease surveillance and detection platform.
The support also includes $200K in Google Cloud credits and pro bono technical expertise from Google’s AI specialists.
The funding will help Froncort.AI develop mAI-NETRA, a mobile version of its public health platform AI-NETRA, which uses AI, satellite imagery and government health data to identify higher risk areas for catching infectious diseases. It also guides frontline health workers towards targeted screenings.
The startup is among 15 organisations selected globally for Google.org’s Impact Challenge: AI for Government Innovation.
Founded in 2024 by physician-scientist Dr Ujjwal Rao, Froncort.AI aims to improve early disease detection by helping frontline health workers enhance their vigil over disease prone areas.
In a validation study conducted with Maharashtra’s state TB programme,Froncort.AI claims that teams using its AI-NETRA identified a similar number of confirmed pulmonary TB cases while screening two-thirds fewer people than conventional methods.
The cost per confirmed case also declined from around $29K to $10K, while 92% of participating frontline workers reported a lower workload.
The platform combines government health programme data with Google’s Earth AI models and local risk indicators, including settlement density, land use, rainfall and flooding, to identify high-risk geographical clusters.
It then converts these insights into ranked work paths, mapping household clusters and builds routes for health workers to follow during field visits.
With the latest funding, Froncort.AI bids to enhance its platform to extend its capabilities across 6 infectious diseases — TB, Leprosy, Malaria, Dengue, Cholera and Leptospirosis.
Froncort.AI also plans to release mAI-NETRA as an open-source blueprint, allowing governments to adopt and adapt the technology for their public health programmes.
Apart from its public health platform, the startup also operates RegDoc, a regulatory technology platform that prepares compliant submissions for clinical research organisations, pharmaceutical companies and medical device manufacturers.
The capital raise comes at a time when AI’s deployment in strengthening India’s public healthcare infrastructure, particularly in areas such as disease surveillance and early diagnosis, is picking up. In a statement issued in February, the government said that India is fundamentally restructuring its public health delivery by integrating AI into a unified strategy.
“By deploying AI-enabled tools within the National TB Elimination Programme, the National Diabetic Retinopathy Screening Programme, and the Media Disease Surveillance System, the government has empowered non-specialists to perform high-level screenings, resulting in a 27% decline in adverse TB outcomes and over 4,500 outbreak alerts,” the statement read.
It is pertinent to note that AI is attracting a growing share of investor capital even as funding across the wider startup ecosystem remains under pressure. The IndiaAI Mission is expanding access to compute, supporting indigenous foundation models and providing assistance for AI startups.
Based on Inc42’s Indian Tech Startup Funding Report Q3 2026, AI funding in India grew 235% YoY, while the number of deals rose 35% to 35 from 26 in Q3 2025.

items.content:
As neither the Supreme Court nor the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) has fixed a date for hearing the matter concerning former prime minister Imran Khan's transfer from Adiala jail to a private medical facility, an application was filed in the Supreme Court on Tuesday on behalf of his sister, Uzma Khan, seeking early hearing of the case.
Uzma, who has herself been detained under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) at Kot Lakhpat Jail, moved an application requesting the apex court to urgently take up the matter concerning Imran's transfer from Adiala jail to Shifa International Hospital in compliance with its August 18 order.
Earlier, Senator Mashal Yousafzai had also filed an application seeking early hearing of the case.
Read: PTI seeks Imran's immediate transfer to Shifa International Hospital over renewed blood pressure concern
Uzma had already filed a contempt petition against the prime minister and other executive authorities over their alleged failure to implement the August 18 order.
The latest application also urged the court to depute one of its officers or appoint a local commission to oversee Imran's transfer to Shifa International Hospital for a medical examination.
Explaining the urgency, the applicant submitted that, according to media reports, the PTI founder's blood pressure had recently risen to 192, raising serious concerns about his health.
"If an early hearing of this matter is not granted, the applicant's and Imran guaranteed rights will continue to be prejudiced; in particular, his fundamental right to health and well-being, access to medical advice and facilities as well as to members of his family will continue to be violated.”
The application further stated: "The material showing the precarious state of his health and the widespread public concern about it has already been filed with the petition.”
The SC was also requested to fix the main case for hearing next week.
On September 14, the FCC had summoned the record of the case concerning Imran's health from the SC.
Subsequently, on September 16, a three-member bench headed by Justice Shahid Waheed raised questions about the FCC's order. During the hearing, Attorney General for Pakistan Mansoor Awan sought three weeks to assist the SC in the matter.
Also Read: Gohar demands immediate implementation of SC order on Imran's medical treatment
Despite two months having passed, the SC has not fixed the matter for hearing. The FCC, meanwhile, listed the three-prisoners case in which it had sought the record of Imran's health-related case.
A lawyer believes that the matter's continued absence from the cause lists of both courts suggests there may be an informal understanding between the SC and the FCC.
He said that instead of allowing the matter to linger, the jurisdictional question between the two apex courts needed to be resolved.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Senior PTI leader Shah Mahmood Qureshi was on Tuesday transferred to Lahore's Punjab Institute of Cardiology (PIC) after reportedly collapsing inside Kot Lakhpat jail, prompting his family to seek urgent medical investigations and treatment.
The former foreign minister's lawyer Rana Mudassar Umar confirmed the transfer on Tuesday, saying Qureshi had fainted and suffered a fall a few days earlier. His family has separately called for a CT scan and dental treatment, while the PTI's core committee has urged authorities to ensure his complete medical examination.
Qureshi is currently being kept under observation for 24 hours, after which doctors will decide whether he needs to be admitted to the hospital.
Read: ATC extends Qureshi's bail in several cases
His counsel said Qureshi was taken to PIC today after he fainted and suffered a fall a few days ago, adding that an application had been in the anti-terrorism court but the issue was delayed due to holidays.
He added that Qureshi was being kept under observation for 24 hours, “after which it will be decided whether he has to be admitted to the hospital”.
The hospital transfer comes after repeated expressions of concern by Qureshi's family over his condition in prison. Last week, his daughter Meher Bano said in a post on X that she had learnt about her father's fall from family members who met him at Kot Lakhpat jail.
I learnt of my father Shah Mahmood Qureshi's fall from family after they met him in Kot Lakhpat jail today.
Three and half years ago a hale and hearty lion heart was sent to jail on trumped up charges. He not only fought the cypher case with resolve and courage but refused to…
— Meher Bano Qureshi (@MeherBanoQ) November 4, 2026
“Three-and-a-half years ago a hale and hearty lion heart was sent to jail on trumped-up charges … For over two years, he has been in Kot Lakhpat jail now facing ludicrous and false charges relating to May 9. He has been acquitted multiple times but [remains] behind bars due to the government’s mala fides,” she alleged.
Qureshi's son, Zain, said on Wednesday that his father had told him during a jail meeting that he collapsed while walking inside his barracks.
Seeking further medical intervention, he urged the prison authorities to arrange a CT scan and specialised dental treatment.
“I request the prison authorities to immediately arrange for a CT scan so that his health condition can be thoroughly assessed. Furthermore, he should be taken to a qualified dentist for the treatment of a cracked tooth,” he said on X.
آج کوٹ لکھپت جیل میں والد مخدوم شاہ محمود قریشی سے ملاقات ہوئی۔ ملاقات کے دوران والد صاحب نے بتایا کہ جیل کی بیرک کے احاطے میں چہل قدمی کرتے ہوئے اچانک بے ہوش ہو کر گر پڑے تھے۔
جیل میں ان کا بلڈ ٹیسٹ لیا گیا ہے۔ اس کی روشنی میں میری جیل حکام سے درخواست ہے کہ والد صاحب کا فوری…
— Zain Hussain Qureshi (@ZainHQ) November 4, 2026
The PTI's core committee had also raised concerns over Qureshi's condition at a meeting on November 6, expressing alarm over his fall and its possible impact on his health.
It called on the relevant courts, the government and the prison administration to ensure his immediate transfer to a hospital, followed by a complete medical examination and necessary treatment.
The PTI vice-president is facing several charges related to the May 9, 2023 riots. In July 2024, he was indicted by an anti-terrorism court in a case concerning the alleged attack and arson at Shadman police station.
Previously held at Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi, Qureshi was moved to Kot Lakhpat Jail last year due to logistical concerns over frequent court appearances in Lahore.
Earlier this year, an anti-terrorism court acquitted Qureshi in the May 9 case involving the arson of police vehicles in Mughalpura. However, he remains in jail in connection with other cases, including those related to rioting.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) has conducted a firefighting and emergency evacuation drill at its headquarters in Islamabad, successfully evacuating the entire building in approximately two and a half minutes.
The exercise, held on November 10 in collaboration with the Capital Development Authority (CDA) Fire Brigade, aimed to strengthen workplace safety and assess the authority’s preparedness for potential fire emergencies.
According to PTA, the activity began with a one-hour training session conducted by CDA Fire Brigade officials, during which employees were briefed on fire prevention, emergency response procedures, and workplace safety measures.
The training also covered the proper use of firefighting equipment and safe evacuation practices to ensure employees understand how to respond during an emergency. Similar fire safety awareness initiatives have been undertaken within Pakistan’s telecom sector.
Following the training session, a practical firefighting and evacuation exercise was carried out to evaluate the effectiveness of the building’s emergency response arrangements.
During the drill, the entire PTA Headquarters building was successfully evacuated within approximately 2.5 minutes, demonstrating the ability of employees to follow established evacuation procedures.
Meanwhile, CDA Fire Brigade fire tenders promptly reached the premises after receiving an emergency call as part of the exercise.
PTA Tests Emergency Response and Coordination With Rescue Services
The exercise was designed to assess how effectively employees could respond to an emergency situation while testing coordination between PTA officials and external rescue services.
According to the authority, the drill helped employees become familiar with evacuation routes, emergency procedures, and the importance of timely action during fire-related incidents.
It also provided an opportunity to evaluate existing safety arrangements and identify areas where emergency preparedness could be further strengthened.
The participation of the CDA Fire Brigade allowed PTA to test its emergency response coordination under simulated conditions rather than relying solely on theoretical training.
Workplace fire preparedness has also featured in other telecom-sector initiatives, including firefighter awareness activities.
The regulator appreciated the support and cooperation of CDA Fire Brigade officials in conducting the exercise.
PTA reiterated its commitment to maintaining a safe working environment for employees and visitors while promoting awareness of fire safety and emergency preparedness.
Beyond workplace safety, the authority has previously emphasized emergency preparedness in telecom services during flood-related disruptions.
Although the exercise demonstrated an evacuation time of approximately two and a half minutes, the authority did not disclose the number of people evacuated or provide additional details about the building’s emergency response capacity.
Such drills are intended to familiarize staff with emergency procedures and improve coordination with rescue personnel, helping organizations respond more effectively when an actual emergency occurs.

Earlier today, US President Donald Trump nominated Chargé d’Affaires Natalie A Baker as the next US ambassador to Pakistan, paving the way for the appointment of a permanent envoy to Islamabad after a gap of nearly two years.
The White House announced the nomination in a list of appointments sent to the US Senate on Monday.
Read: Trump nominates Natalie Baker as next US ambassador to Pakistan
Her nomination is subject to confirmation by the US Senate. If confirmed, Natalie will become the first US ambassador to Pakistan since Donald Blome left the post in early 2025.
The Pakistan-US relationship experienced a significant thaw in 2025–2026, transitioning from a cold period to warm, strategic, and pragmatic engagement during Trump's second term. This shift was largely driven by a major reset in relations following President Trump's intervention in regional conflicts, particularly his role in brokering a ceasefire between Pakistan and India in May 2025.
The first thaw in Pakistan-US relations came via secret counterterrorism exchanges, signalling substantive cooperation. In March last year, Trump unexpectedly praised Pakistan’s counterterrorism efforts during a national address, prompting a policy shift.
The short but intense May skirmish with India in May 2025 became a decisive turning point, showcasing Pakistan’s military discipline, strategic focus, and asymmetric capabilities — qualities that reportedly surprised Trump.
Despite India’s repeated denials, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif continued to praise President Trump for his role in brokering a ceasefire between the two nuclear-armed neighbours, and nominated him for the Nobel Peace Prize, saying his intervention had helped save millions of lives.
The praise was reciprocated, with Trump commending the premier and also lauding CDF Munir, as he reiterated claims that he had helped avert a war between Pakistan and India in May 2025.
Ties between the countries took a further turn when Trump invited CDF Munir to a luncheon — the first such meeting for a Pakistani military chief — followed by a red-carpet visit to US Central Command headquarters for high-level talks.
Following a ceasefire after the prolonged war in Gaza, Trump announced the formation of a “Board of Peace” that included Pakistan, again singling out PM Shehbaz for praise during its inaugural summit.
Addressing the event, Trump said, “I like this guy,” referring to the premier, as he recounted efforts that led to last year’s ceasefire between Pakistan and India. He also praised CDF Munir during his remarks.
In June this year, President Trump credited Pakistan with “really helping” the United States secure a peace deal with Iran while especially praising Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir and PM Shehbaz.
“In Pakistan, you have Field Marshal Asim Munir, who is great, and you have the Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, and they just get along great,” he said during an interview with Axios.
