items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
The 4-4 draw against Aston Villa felt like a victory at Old Trafford, but the fact that supporters could celebrate a point while their club sits in the relegation zone tells a more troubling story about how far United’s expectations have fallen.
There was a time when a draw at Old Trafford felt like a defeat. Manchester United were a club built around winning, where anything short of three points could leave supporters disappointed, regardless of the performance. The expectation was not simply to compete but to dominate, to set the standards and to make winning feel like an obligation.
Those expectations seem increasingly distant.
On Sunday, Manchester United celebrated a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa with the sort of emotion usually reserved for a significant victory. Two goals in stoppage time, courtesy of Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu, rescued a point after Michael Carrick’s side had twice fallen two goals behind. The comeback was extraordinary, the atmosphere was electric and the players had every reason to appreciate their resilience.
But perhaps the most revealing aspect of the afternoon was not the comeback itself. It was how much it meant.
Manchester United are now in a position where avoiding defeat feels like an achievement. A point against Aston Villa, under ordinary circumstances, would hardly have been considered a successful afternoon for a club of United’s stature. Yet the circumstances have become so desperate that the draw felt like a victory.
That is how quickly footballing standards can collapse.
United sit 18th in the Premier League with eight points from 10 matches. They have managed just one league victory, recorded against Ipswich Town in August, and Sunday’s result extended their winless league run to eight matches. It is a club-record sequence in the Premier League.
The numbers are alarming, but the deeper concern is what they reveal about the club’s changing relationship with success.
Manchester United have become a team defined by what they are trying to avoid rather than what they are trying to achieve. Instead of discussing title challenges, European qualification or the development of a convincing footballing identity, the conversation increasingly revolves around managerial uncertainty, defensive mistakes, relegation calculations and the possibility of another disappointing weekend.
Survival has become the immediate ambition.
And that is a remarkable development for a club whose history was built on refusing to accept anything less than excellence.
Sunday’s performance captured both sides of United’s current identity. There was the determination to fight back, the willingness to keep attacking and the refusal to surrender even when the game appeared beyond them. Coming back from 2-0 down, reaching 2-2, falling behind again and eventually recovering from 4-2 demonstrated a spirit that supporters have desperately wanted to see.
However, resilience cannot become an excuse for repeated carelessness.
United conceded twice inside the opening four minutes. They then surrendered their defensive organisation again immediately after half-time, allowing John McGinn to score from the penalty spot before Leon Goretzka extended Villa’s advantage. The attacking response was admirable, but the defensive problems that made such a dramatic recovery necessary were equally concerning. 
There is a difference between fighting back from adversity and repeatedly creating adversity for yourself.
For Carrick, the challenge is no longer simply convincing supporters that his team can produce entertaining football. He must demonstrate that Manchester United can become dependable again. The occasional spectacular comeback cannot compensate for a team that struggles to manage the opening minutes of matches, protect advantages or maintain concentration.
There is also a wider question about the club’s direction.
Manchester United’s problems cannot be reduced to one manager, one transfer window or one poor run of results. The instability surrounding the club has created an environment in which every setback becomes another argument about leadership, recruitment and the footballing structure. The manager becomes the immediate subject of scrutiny, but the problems appear considerably deeper.
The danger is that United become accustomed to this existence.
When a club repeatedly lowers its expectations to accommodate its circumstances, mediocrity can gradually become normal. Supporters who once demanded victories begin celebrating draws. A team that once approached matches expecting to dictate proceedings now approaches them hoping to survive the next defensive crisis.
That is perhaps the most disturbing part of United’s current predicament.
The 4-4 draw against Aston Villa should not be dismissed. There was genuine character in the comeback, and the players deserved credit for refusing to surrender. Football supporters should be allowed to enjoy extraordinary moments, even in difficult seasons.
But one dramatic afternoon cannot disguise a deeply troubling campaign.
Manchester United have spent years searching for a return to the standards that made them one of football’s most formidable institutions. Now, with the relegation zone beneath their feet, the immediate concern is no longer how quickly they can return to the summit but whether they can first escape the bottom three.
A draw that once would have been considered two points dropped has become a reason for celebration.
Perhaps that is the clearest indication of how far Manchester United have fallen.
The problem is no longer just that United are struggling to win football matches. It is that a club built on ambition is beginning to look increasingly comfortable with survival.

items.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi
The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has explained why those who registered in the third phase of its Continuous Voter Registration CVR are yet to have their Permanent Voter Cards even as it announced a massive purge of the national voter register ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Addressing a press conference in Abuja, the INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Ojo Amupitan, SAN, disclosed that the commission has successfully removed 1,609,553 invalid and deceased records from the system.
“The Commission recognises that the detection of irregularities raises legitimate questions about how they arose. The response is evidence-led investigation, completed corrective action and stronger preventive controls.
“1,609,553 records have been removed, comprising 1,608,660 confirmed invalid registrations and 873 verified deceased-voter records. INEC will continue to communicate verifiable aggregate outcomes while protecting personal information and the integrity of ongoing investigations”, said Amupitan.
Addressing reporters regarding the status of unprinted cards, the INEC Chairman stated: “The distribution of Phases 1 and 2 of the PVC and transferred PVCs is on-going at the various LGAs in Nigeria. Some of the PVC for the third and final Phase are being delivered and they would be dispatched to the States by next week.
“Meanwhile as from 1st December 2026, distribution will go back to the Registration Areas all over Nigeria. We appeal to those that registered in the third pahse to be a little bit patient since the production is done outside the country”.
Vanguard recalls that those who registered in total in the third phase were 2,970,257 before the commission’s de-duplication protocol.
The sweeping clean-up of the register followed widespread public outcry and intense scrutiny over anomalies spotted on the preliminary register displayed between October 9 and 15, 2026.
A rigorous technical audit utilizing the Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) uncovered systemic manipulations, including unusual registration patterns, substituted photographs, and fraudulent multiple registrations.
Crucially, the investigation indicted internal personnel who abused their offices. Prof. Amupitan revealed that the commission identified 54 staff members cutting across 10 states who deliberately bypassed standard operating procedures and exploited special provisions meant for vulnerable citizens, such as persons with disabilities. Disciplinary actions and possible prosecutions have been initiated against the culprits.
Reacting to media inquiries surrounding court cases involving political actors, the INEC Chairman maintained that the electoral umpire operates strictly on authenticated legal instruments rather than speculative reports.
“On ADC/Atiku: as of today, we have not received the Certified True Copy of the court judgment and we don’t act based on what we see on the social media”, he said.
INEC noted that while the recent 2025/2026 CVR clean-up resolved immediate anomalies, historical data carried over from 2011 to 2023 continues to present legacy duplications. Consequently, the commission’s board has directed that flagged entries from past cycles be expunged after verification.
To further safeguard the integrity of the upcoming 2027 polls, INEC assured the public that robust mechanisms—including the mandatory physical presence of voters and biometric authentication via the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) using fingerprints or facial recognition—remain firmly in place to prevent multiple voting and unauthorized accreditation.

FEDERAL CAPITAL TERRITORY LOTTERY REGULATORY OFFICE (FCT-LRO)
Oﬃce of the Director-General
PUBLIC NOTICE TO GAMING OPERATORS AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC.
FCT-LRO COMMENCES FULL BUSINESS OPERATIONS
The Federal Capital Territory Lottery Regulatory Oﬃce (FCT-LRO) hereby informs gaming
operators, industry stakeholders and the general public that the Oﬃce has commenced
operations as the regulatory authority responsible for the oversight, regulation and supervision
of gaming activities within the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).
1. REGULATORY JURISDICTION
Following the Supreme Court judgment in Attorney-General of Lagos State & 21 Others v.
Attorney-General of the Federation & 15 Others, Suit No. SC/1/2008, the constitutional
position on the regulation of lotteries and gaming has been clarified. By virtue of Section
299 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended),
the FCT has a distinct constitutional status, with the National Assembly exercising
legislative powers ordinarily vested in a State House of Assembly.
Accordingly, gaming operators conducting business within the FCT are required to comply
with the applicable FCT licensing and regulatory requirements and engage with the FCT-
LRO on all regulatory matters.
2. ONLINE GAMING OPERATIONS
The Oﬃce clarifies that the Supreme Court judgment did not expressly settle the full
regulatory framework applicable to online gaming. In particular, the judgment did not
establish that any one State has exclusive regulatory control over the online gaming
market.
Accordingly, the online gaming market remains open to operators and investors. Operators
are free to choose the regulator from whom they wish to obtain their gaming licence or
authorisation, based on their business model, operational needs and the regulatory
framework they consider most suitable and beneficial to their business.
This choice may be exercised without undue interference, intimidation or coercive
treatment by any State regulator solely on the basis that an operator has elected to obtain its
licence from another regulator, as every state is duly empowered to regulate gaming
activities within its relevant jurisdiction.
Operators are, however, reminded that the online nature of a gaming platform does not, in
itself, exempt an operation from applicable licensing and regulatory obligations where
such obligations arise.
The FCT-LRO remains committed to providing a transparent, consistent and predictable
regulatory environment for digital gaming operations within the Federal Capital Territory.
3. NOTICE TO FORMER NLRC LICENSEES
All gaming operators previously licensed by the National Lottery Regulatory Commission
(NLRC) who are currently operating, or intend to operate, within the Federal Capital
Territory (FCT) are hereby required to approach the FCT-LRO to regularise their regulatory
status.
The Oﬃce further clarifies that any NLRC licence that remains valid and has not expired
will be recognised for the remainder of its validity period and converted to the
corresponding FCT-LRO licence. Accordingly, holders of former NLRC licences will
retain the benefit of their unexpired licence terms, subject to the regularisation process
prescribed by the FCT-LRO.
Aﬀected operators are required to present and hand over their former NLRC-issued
licences for verification and documentation, complete the applicable regularisation
procedures and obtain the appropriate FCT gaming licence.
All aﬀected operators are required to commence the regularisation process within 7 days of
publication of this notice.
4. RECOGNISED FCT-LRO OPERATORS
For public awareness and regulatory transparency, the following operators are currently
recognised as licensed operators within the FCT:
(INSERT LIST)
Members of the public are encouraged to verify the licensing status of gaming operators
before engaging their services.
5. OFFICIAL CONTACT DETAILS
All licensing applications, regulatory enquiries, compliance matters and oﬃcial
correspondence should be directed to the FCT-LRO through the following channels:
Oﬃce Address: 2B Embu Crescent, Ishaku Rabiu Estate, Oﬀ Aminu Kano Crescent, Wuse
2, Abuja.
Telephone: +234 802 347 6076 / +234 813 052 5876
Email: info@lro.abj.gov.ng
The FCT-LRO reiterates its commitment to promoting responsible gaming, protecting
consumers, strengthening regulatory oversight and fostering a transparent and investment-
friendly gaming industry within the Federal Capital Territory.
All operators and stakeholders are advised to take note and ensure compliance.

items.content:
By Henry Umoru
Ahead of January 16 2027 election, the Vice Presidential Candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso has promised Nigerians that an NDC-led Federal Government under Peter Obi and himself will operate an all-inclusive government.
According to him, the Obi-led government would prioritise the interests of every Nigerian, irrespective of political, ethnic, religious or social affiliations.
The former Kano State Governor spoke while addressing party leaders, stakeholders and supporters during a carnival-like reception organised in his honour at Toru-Orua, the country home of Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, National Leader of the NDC and the party’s Senatorial candidate for Bayelsa West.
In a statement signed by the Coordinator, Ofurumapepe Media of the NDC Campaign Council, Gabriel Ukuta, he explained that Kwankwaso said that what Nigeria needed at this moment in the nation’s political history is a government that would deliberately carry its citizens along in the formulation, implementation of policies and programmes.
He said that governance must be people-oriented and responsive to the needs and aspirations of the population.
Kwankwaso said the NDC has positioned itself as a credible alternative political platform with the capacity, leadership and commitment to deliver the inclusive governance Nigerians desire.
The NDC Vice Presidential Candidate said, “Nigerians deserve a government that will listen to them, accommodate their interests and ensure that no section of the country is left behind. An NDC-led Federal Government will be an all-inclusive government that will carry everybody along in its policies and programmes,”
Kwankwaso who condemned what he described as the prevailing hunger, economic hardship and insecurity under the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led Federal Government, urged Nigerians to take advantage of the 2027 general elections to vote out the ruling party.
The Vice Presidential Candidate who called on citizens to take collective responsibility for the electoral process by coming out en masse to vote for the NDC and ensuring that their votes count, expressed concern over alleged attempts by anti-democracy forces and agents of the ruling party to manipulate the outcome of the forthcoming elections, insisting that Nigerians must remain vigilant and protect their votes.
“Voting is not enough; Nigerians must also take responsibility for protecting their votes. We must all work together to ensure that the wishes of the people are respected and that the outcome of the elections reflects the collective decision of the electorate,” he added.
He expressed appreciation to Senator Dickson, members of the NDC National Working Committee (NWC), the National Campaign Council (NCC), party stakeholders, candidates and supporters across Bayelsa State for the impressive reception accorded him.
In his remarks, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, who is also the NDC candidate for Bayelsa West Senatorial District, decried what he described as the growing hardship, hunger, insecurity, victimisation, inducement and intimidation allegedly being experienced by the people of Bayelsa State under the APC-led Federal and State Governments.
Dickson maintained that the NDC presidential and vice-presidential candidates were tested and trustworthy leaders with the requisite experience, competence and commitment to restore good governance and bring the dividends of democracy to the doorsteps of Nigerians.
He expressed confidence in the Obi-Kwankwaso ticket, describing both candidates as individuals capable of providing purposeful leadership and addressing the country’s numerous socio-economic challenges.
The former Bayelsa State governor urged Bayelsans to return to their various communities and intensify mobilisation for the NDC, emphasising the need for collective support for all the party’s candidates, from the presidential election to the State House of Assembly polls.
He called on party faithful and supporters to sustain the momentum generated by the reception and translate it into grassroots political mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Dickson also thanked the dignitaries, party leaders, candidates, stakeholders and supporters who attended the event, expressing his appreciation in the Ijaw language and reaffirming the inclusive character of the NDC.
He declared that the NDC was a political platform for all Bayelsans and Nigerians, irrespective of their backgrounds or previous political affiliations.
The statement further said, ” A major highlight of the reception was the participation of Engineer Kwankwaso in the traditional Ijaw war boat display, popularly known as Ama-Aru, alongside Senator Dickson and other NDC leaders and executives in Bayelsa State, all of whom were led to the even by the party’s National Chairman, Sen. Moses Cleopas.
“The colourful cultural display, which took place along the Toru-Orua axis of the River Forcados, showcased the rich cultural heritage and traditional identity of the Ijaw people.
“The event also featured the formal presentation of party flags to the NDC candidates contesting the National Assembly and State House of Assembly elections in Bayelsa State, signalling the party’s readiness for the 2027 electoral contest.”

items.content:
A 56-year-old civil servant in the United Kingdom, UK, Kashim Chowdhury has been convicted of nine counts of fraud after secretly holding multiple full-time government jobs and fraudulently earning more than £284,000 in taxpayers’ money.
Chowdhury, from east London, held five overlapping government positions in the spring of 2023, concealing his multiple employment arrangements from the departments that hired him.
After seven hours of deliberation, a jury unanimously found him guilty of eight counts of fraud by false representation and one count of fraud by failure to disclose.
The prosecution accused Chowdhury of “deliberate, intentional dishonesty” and “exploiting the system” to secure multiple salaries from public sector employers.
During the proceedings, the judge said Chowdhury faced a “very significant custodial sentence”. He also refused him bail, citing the seriousness of the offences and Chowdhury’s own wellbeing.
Sarah Melo, a specialist prosecutor at the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) Serious Economic Organised Crime and International Directorate, described his actions as sustained dishonesty.
“This was sustained and deliberate dishonesty,” Melo said.
“He knew he could not legitimately hold multiple full-time positions at the same time, but continued to conceal what he was doing.”
A spokesperson for the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said Chowdhury had “abused the trust placed in him as a public servant”.
The department added that it would use all available avenues to recover the proceeds of his offending.
Between 2020 and 2023, Chowdhury held eight overlapping full-time public sector positions and earned a total of £350,000, according to evidence presented in court.
Prosecutors told the court that he provided inaccurate information about his employment status on job application forms and failed to disclose to government departments that he was already employed as a civil servant.
After securing the positions, he also failed to inform his employers that he was working for other government departments.
Chowdhury was permitted to work entirely from home after telling his employers he was caring for his mother, with whom he lived in east London.
His mother had dementia and was diagnosed with terminal cancer in 2023. However, rather than reduce his workload to care for her, he continued taking on additional government positions.
In the spring of 2023, he held positions across the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, the Department of Health and Social Care, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency
and the Home Office.
During the period, he was contracted to work 183 hours a week, exceeding the total number of hours available in seven days.

items.author: Kamran Yousaf
items.content:
Pakistan is expected to host the third meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee of the Makkah Defence Alliance in the last week of November, as the three member countries seek to strengthen their security coordination amid mounting regional tensions and uncertainty surrounding the Iran conflict, diplomatic sources told The Express Tribune here on Monday.
The meeting is expected to bring together the foreign and defence ministers as well as the military chiefs of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, with discussions likely to focus on the implementation of the trilateral defence agreement and the evolving regional security situation.
The meeting comes at a particularly critical juncture, with the possibility of renewed military strikes against Iran still looming even as diplomatic efforts to find a way out of the conflict remain on the table. The three countries are expected to discuss the implications of these developments for regional stability and their collective security arrangements.
The Islamabad meeting will be the first gathering of the committee since the Turkish parliament formally ratified the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement on November 7, completing a major step towards bringing the trilateral arrangement into effect.
The Turkish parliament approved the agreement by 279 votes to 119, following a debate in which government lawmakers maintained that the pact was defensive in nature and was not directed against any third country.
The agreement was signed on August 7 by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan. It provides for collective assistance in the event of an armed attack against any of the three countries, with the nature and extent of assistance to be determined collectively.
The upcoming meeting will be the third session of the committee established under the agreement to translate the political commitment into practical defence cooperation.
The first meeting was held in Istanbul on August 31, bringing together the foreign ministers, defence ministers and military chiefs of the three countries. The meeting agreed to institutionalise cooperation through a permanent secretariat in Riyadh, which would initially be headed by a Pakistani secretary general for three years.
It also envisaged greater cooperation in the defence industry, joint technology development and production, and measures to strengthen the capabilities and coordination of the three armed forces.
The second meeting was convened on an emergency basis in Riyadh on October 5, following escalating security threats to Saudi Arabia, including attacks attributed to Yemen's Houthi movement.
The committee condemned attacks targeting Saudi cities and civilian and economic infrastructure, including threats to Makkah and Madinah. More significantly, it agreed to move towards the practical implementation of collective defence commitments, including measures to provide agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in Saudi Arabia, subject to the national laws of the member states.
The Riyadh meeting also appointed retired Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood as the alliance's first secretary general for a three-year term.
The November meeting is expected to take stock of progress on these decisions and consider further steps to strengthen military coordination, intelligence-sharing and defence cooperation.
The Turkish parliament's ratification has added significance to the upcoming deliberations. While Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had completed their respective ratification processes earlier, Türkiye was awaiting parliamentary approval under its domestic constitutional requirements.
However, ratification does not automatically authorise the deployment of Turkish troops abroad, which would require a separate parliamentary mandate.
The alliance has also attracted attention because of the wider geopolitical circumstances in which it was formed. The agreement brings together Pakistan, the only nuclear-armed Muslim-majority country, Saudi Arabia, a major Gulf power, and Türkiye, a NATO member with one of the region's largest militaries.
All three countries have maintained that the arrangement is defensive and intended to strengthen regional stability rather than target any particular state.
For Islamabad, the challenge will be to advance the collective defence framework while maintaining its diplomatic engagement with Tehran and supporting efforts to prevent another escalation in the wider Middle East.

items.content:
Canada has outlined six eligibility requirements for foreign nationals seeking permanent residence through its Rural Community Immigration Program, a pathway designed to attract skilled immigrants to participating rural communities across the country.
The programme offers permanent residence to eligible foreigners who want to work and settle in selected Canadian communities, particularly areas seeking skilled migrants to fill positions that cannot be filled by local residents.
According to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), participating communities will approve designated employers to recruit skilled foreign nationals for available positions.
To qualify for permanent residence under the programme, applicants must obtain a valid recommendation certificate from a participating community and secure a valid job offer from a designated employer within that community.
They must also have at least one year, equivalent to 1,560 hours, of related work experience within the previous three years.
Other requirements include demonstrating language proficiency through an approved test, possessing a Canadian educational credential or its foreign equivalent, and providing proof of sufficient funds to support themselves and their families.
Full list of eligibility requirements
According to IRCC, foreigners seeking permanent residence through the programme must meet the following six requirements:
Community recommendation: Obtain a valid recommendation certificate from a participating community in Canada.
Valid job offer: Secure a valid job offer from a designated employer within the participating community.
Work experience: Have at least one year (1,560 hours) of related work experience within the past three years.
Language proficiency: Demonstrate English or French language ability by taking an approved language test.
Educational qualification: Possess a Canadian educational credential or a foreign equivalent.
Proof of funds: Provide evidence of having sufficient money to support themselves and their families after arriving in Canada.
The programme is designed to help participating rural communities attract skilled foreign nationals while providing immigrants with an opportunity to obtain permanent residence and establish themselves in Canada.
Applicants are required to satisfy the eligibility conditions and secure the necessary community recommendation and employment offer before applying for permanent residence.

By Olasunkanmi Akoni
The Lagos State Government has said its investigation found no encroachment on government drainage alignment at Abba Court, Mahogany Close, Osborne Foreshore Phase II Estate, Ikoyi, following complaints by residents against a developer.
The government also announced plans to increase its flood control management measures from 75 per cent to 90 per cent by 2027 as part of efforts to minimise flooding across the state.
The Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, disclosed this during an inspection of drainage and environmental services projects in Oregun, Ojota, Surulere and Osborne Foreshore Estate, Ikoyi.
He was accompanied by the Permanent Secretaries, Office of Drainage Services, Mahmood Adegbite, and Environmental Services, Omobolaji Gaji.
The inspection came amid complaints by residents and property owners against Kenshad International Limited, led by Chief Ken Ukaoha, over alleged planning violations, construction under high-tension cables, obstruction of drainage channels and the deployment of unauthorised security personnel to intimidate residents.
Vanguard had reported on October 31, 2026, that the Deputy Governor, Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, and a state government delegation were kept waiting outside Abba Court for more than 30 minutes after the estate’s gates remained locked during an inspection visit.
Hamzat had expressed displeasure over the incident, assuring residents that the government would investigate their complaints and stressing that land use and physical planning were within the jurisdiction of the state government.
However, Ukaoha denied the allegations, insisting that his company neither built on a canal nor deliberately locked out the deputy governor.
He explained that the site was closed after workers were instructed to stay away following a government circular, adding that he was in London at the time and had not been notified of the official visit.
The developer also claimed to have personally funded parts of the estate’s drainage infrastructure and maintained that the project had the necessary government approvals.
He attributed the flooding in the estate to its low-lying, sand-filled terrain and undersized public drainage infrastructure rather than his property.
Speaking after inspecting the disputed location, Wahab said officials of the ministry had visited the site three times and found no encroachment on the government’s drainage alignment.
“This is our third time coming to that particular project point, and there are no encroachments.
“I was here with the Deputy Governor last weekend after leaving the sanitation; there are no encroachments on our own alignment.
“We may not have access now, but we have been here before. The drainage that is there is not in any way encroaching on our own drainage; it was done to discharge into the Simpson Channel,” he said.
The commissioner said the ministry had advised those involved not to remove the culvert installed at the site, explaining that it was necessary for safety reasons.
He also said the high-tension cables were not affected by the structure.
“You all went in there with us. There are no encroachments. Once they are non-existent, we cannot allow people to dog-whistle us to do what they want,” Wahab added.
On other locations inspected, the commissioner said the ministry intervened at the Oregun Mixed-Use Scheme following complaints by property owners that auto mechanics had occupied their land and encroached on a natural drainage route known as System One.
He said the ministry directed the mechanics to vacate the affected properties to enable the owners to regain access to their land.
In Surulere, Wahab said the ministry investigated a petition alleging that construction by the Lagos State Development and Property Corporation had encroached on the right-of-way of a drainage channel.
According to him, officials conducted physical measurements in the presence of stakeholders and established that the construction had not encroached on the drainage channel.
He added that the ministry had approved a culvert for the development and confirmed during the inspection that it was constructed in accordance with the approved design.
On the state’s flood management strategy, Wahab said the government was targeting an increase in flood control measures from 75 per cent to 90 per cent by 2027.
He, however, urged residents to stop dumping refuse into drainage channels, warning that such practices could trigger severe flash flooding.

items.content:
Supreme Court Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail, who was among the judges to declare the trial of civilians in military courts unconstitutional, is set to retire on Wednesday, bringing to a close a judicial career spanning nearly 17 years and marked by several consequential rulings on constitutional, political and legal matters.
From his tenure at the Balochistan High Court (BHC) to his elevation to the Supreme Court in 2021, Justice Mandokhail authored and participated in several important judgements concerning property rights, parliamentary proceedings, reserved seats, military trials and the constitutional jurisdiction of courts.
His judicial career was also marked by close associations with former chief justice Qazi Faez Isa and incumbent Chief Justice Yahya Afridi, while some of his positions and decisions attracted criticism from sections of the legal fraternity and PTI supporters.
Justice Mandokhail began his judicial career on September 7, 2009, when he was appointed as a judge of the Balochistan High Court.
During his tenure at the BHC, he authored several important judgements, including a ruling declaring that the "unsettled land" of Balochistan, the country's largest province, belonged to the indigenous tribes inhabiting its plains and mountains for centuries, rather than the provincial government.
In another significant judgement, he declared several provisions of the Defence Housing Authority (DHA) Act, 2015, unconstitutional. In his ruling, he held that the DHA functioned like a non-government agency and that its acquisition of property would consequently violate the constitutional right to property.
The Supreme Court subsequently suspended that ruling. Appeals against both judgements are now pending before the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), it is learnt.
In 2021, Justice Mandokhail was elevated to the Supreme Court, at a time when judicial politics was in full swing at the apex court. He was associated with the camp of former chief justice Qazi Faez Isa and became part of several benches that delivered significant verdicts during Isa's tenure.
Justice Mandokhail was a member of the bench that set aside former deputy speaker Qasim Suri's ruling rejecting the no-confidence motion against then prime minister Imran Khan under Article 95 of the Constitution.
He was also among the minority judges who held that the votes of defecting lawmakers should be counted under Article 63A of the Constitution.
The judge was among those who opposed the suo motu proceedings initiated by former chief justice Umar Ata Bandial to hold elections to the Punjab and Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) provincial assemblies within 90 days.
Justice Mandokhail, along with Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah, maintained that the Lahore High Court should first be allowed to proceed with the matter. During former CJP Isa's tenure, Justice Mandokhail maintained a close association with him and frequently served on benches that delivered important judgements. He rarely dissented from Justice Isa's opinions in significant cases. His association with the former chief justice continues to draw criticism from PTI supporters.
The constitutional bench question
Following the 26th Constitutional Amendment, Justice Mandokhail was nominated as a member of the constitutional benches and also served on the committee responsible for constituting benches to hear cases. Like Justice Isa, he maintained a close association with incumbent Chief Justice Yahya Afridi.
However, some lawyers have questioned why Justice Mandokhail, despite being a member of the committee, did not play a more active role in securing the hearing of petitions challenging the 26th Constitutional Amendment.
They believe that if the Supreme Court had reviewed the 26th Amendment, the subsequent 27th Constitutional Amendment could have been halted. Justice Mandokhail was also a member of the constitutional bench that ruled that the trial of civilians in military courts was unconstitutional.
He was also among the members of the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) who did not support the appointment of Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar as chief justice of the Islamabad High Court.
'Confused jurisprudence'
Supreme Court advocate Faisal Siddiqi described Justice Mandokhail as a polite judge with some prominent dissenting judgements, but criticised his overall judicial approach.
"His overall jurisprudence of balancing between executive interests and citizens' rights ended up in a confused jurisprudence, destroying the power and reputation of the Supreme Court as the apex court".
Waqas Ahmed, an advocate who worked as a law clerk with Justice Mandokhail, offered a more favourable assessment of the judge's personality and professional conduct.
He said that beyond his judicial legacy, Mandokhail was a humble and gracious human being who listened to lawyers with patience and respect and remained particularly encouraging and supportive of young members of the bar.
"His legacy is not confined to his judgments; it also lives in the dignity, humility and kindness with which he treated the legal fraternity."
Waqas Ahmed said Justice Mandokhail would also be remembered for his contributions to constitutional jurisprudence and the protection of fundamental rights.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The Supreme Court has ruled that civil cases should ordinarily be decided on merit rather than dismissed on technical grounds, observing that courts must strike a balance between procedural discipline and the demands of substantive justice.
A three-member bench, comprising Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar, Justice Musarrat Hilali and Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan, gave the ruling while allowing two civil petitions filed by Safdar Ali Butt against orders of the Lahore High Court refusing to restore his civil revision petitions.
In a judgment authored by Justice Mazhar, the court observed that the scales of justice neither favoured automatic dismissal nor automatic restoration of proceedings. Courts must examine the circumstances of each case, particularly whether a genuine and sufficient reason existed for a party's failure to appear.
The case concerned two civil revisions, pending before the Lahore High Court since 2016, which were dismissed on February 2, 2026, after the petitioner's counsel failed to appear. Restoration applications were filed the following day.
The petitioner's counsel explained that the lawyer representing him, Shahid Azeem Bajwa, was suffering from coronavirus and had remained outside the courtroom. When the cases were called, he rushed towards the courtroom but could not reach the bench because of heavy congestion.
The Supreme Court noted that the explanation had not been denied by the opposing counsel, who also failed to establish any deliberate attempt by the petitioner's lawyer to delay proceedings.
It observed that no previous record indicated that the counsel had been negligent or responsible for the prolonged pendency of the cases.
The judgment stressed that lawyers must carefully monitor hearing dates, cause lists and court benches, make alternative arrangements when commitments overlap, and keep clients informed about case progress, potential risks and settlement offers. It said clients must also remain vigilant and regularly follow their cases rather than leave the entire responsibility to their lawyers.
The court warned that dismissing proceedings because of a lawyer's negligence, without a reasonable explanation, seriously damages professional credibility and may provide grounds for complaints of professional misconduct before bar councils under the Legal Practitioners and Bar Councils Act, 1973.
The court set aside the Lahore High Court's orders, restored both civil revisions subject to payment of Rs10,000 in each case, and directed the petitioner to deposit the Rs20,000 with the Lahore High Court Bar Association's Medical Centre.

items.content:
The Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (DRAP) has urged consumers to use its Mehfooz Dawa app to check whether medicines are genuine and verify their prices before buying them.
The app uses a 2D barcode system that allows smartphone users to scan medicine packaging and access information about the registered product. The app aims to curb counterfeit medicines, overpricing and other illegal practices in the pharmaceutical market.
More Than 90,000 Medicines Registered With DRAP
Ministry of National Health Services spokesperson Sajid Shah said around 800 pharmaceutical companies and more than 90,000 medicines are registered with DRAP.
Consumers can scan the barcode printed on medicine packs through their smartphones to verify product details and check the registered price.
Medicine Track and Trace System Now Operational
The centralised Track and Trace System for medicines distributed across Pakistan became operational on October 9, 2026.
Besides helping consumers, the system allows regulators to monitor medicines as they move through the supply chain.
This could make it easier for authorities to identify and recall specific products if complaints, safety problems or quality issues emerge.
How Mehfooz Dawa App Works
Consumers need a smartphone to use the verification system.
They can scan the 2D barcode on a medicine pack through the Mehfooz Dawa app. The system then displays details about the product and its price.
This gives buyers a way to check whether the medicine matches DRAP’s registered information and whether the price being charged is correct.
Barcode System Faced Years of Delays
Pakistan first proposed introducing the medicine barcode system in 2015.
The federal cabinet approved the initiative in 2017, but administrative delays prevented its full implementation for several years.
Health Minister Mustafa Kamal later took notice of the prolonged delay and directed authorities to introduce the system.
DRAP had subsequently set October 1, 2026, as a cut-off date for launching the barcode mechanism as part of efforts to tackle counterfeit and expired medicines as well as black marketing.
DRAP Steps Up Action Against Fake Medicines
The digital verification system comes as DRAP continues to issue alerts over counterfeit, substandard, adulterated and unregistered medicines.
In a November 5 alert, the regulator advised consumers to purchase therapeutic products only from authorised or licensed outlets and carefully check their authenticity and condition.
The Ministry of National Health Services said the government remains committed to improving access to safe, effective and quality medicines across the country.

items.author: ProPK Staff
items.content:
The historic Gurdwara Chhevin Patshahi Sri Guru Hargobind Sahib on Temple Road in Mozang, Lahore, reopened on Sunday after remaining closed since the Partition of 1947.
The Evacuee Trust Property Board (ETPB), Pakistan Sikh Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (PSGPC) and the Punjab government jointly held a ceremony to mark the reopening after 79 years.
A large number of members of the Sikh community attended the event. Punjab Minister for Minorities and PSGPC President Sardar Ramesh Singh Arora, ETPB Secretary Nasir Mushtaq, Deputy Secretary Shrines Usman Khan, Deputy Secretary General Saadat Shehbaz and other officials were also present.
Gurdwara Linked to Guru Hargobind Sahib
The gurdwara is historically associated with Guru Hargobind Sahib, the sixth of Sikhism’s 10 gurus.
Guru Hargobind, who lived from 1595 to 1644, is remembered as a warrior-saint who strengthened the Sikh community to defend itself against religious oppression.
According to Sikh historical accounts, Guru Hargobind Sahib accepted an invitation from the local Sikh congregation and stayed for three days at the home of Bhai Jiwan, a devotee living in Mozang, which was then located on the outskirts of Lahore.
Bhai Jiwan later converted his house into a gurdwara to honour the Guru’s stay.
Shrine Also Associated With Bhai Bidhi Chand
The site also has historical links with Bhai Bidhi Chand, who is remembered for recovering two horses named Dilbagh and Gulbagh.
According to Sikh accounts, the horses had been seized by the Mughal governor of Lahore, identified in different accounts as either Khalil Beg or Qasim Beg, from a devotee who intended to present them to Guru Hargobind Sahib.
Bhai Bidhi Chand reportedly made two visits to Lahore and succeeded in recovering both horses from the royal stables inside Lahore Fort.
He is also believed to have stayed at the site of the gurdwara during those visits.
Gurdwara Expanded in 1915
The local Sikh congregation expanded the gurdwara hall in 1915.
In 1921, members of the Sangat took control of the shrine’s management after allegations of misconduct against Mahant Hari Singh. They later formed a local management committee.
The old gurdwara building was established in 1926 through the efforts of Sardar Mehar Singh.
The Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) took administrative control of the shrine in 1927.
The original structure of the gurdwara dates back to the period of Maharaja Ranjit Singh.
Regular Sikh worship at the shrine ended after the Partition in 1947.
More Than 50 Gurdwaras Under Renovation
Speaking at the reopening ceremony, Sardar Ramesh Singh Arora said restoration work on the historic shrine had been completed and it was now open to the Sikh community for religious worship.
He said more than 50 gurdwaras across Pakistan were currently undergoing renovation as part of efforts to preserve Sikh religious heritage and provide better facilities to pilgrims.
ETPB Vows to Protect Religious Heritage
ETPB Secretary Nasir Mushtaq said the restoration and reopening of Gurdwara Chhevin Patshahi would provide improved worship facilities to the Sikh community while also protecting Lahore’s historical and religious heritage.
He said safeguarding places of worship belonging to Sikh and Hindu communities was one of the ETPB’s major responsibilities.
Mushtaq described the restoration of the gurdwara as an important step in that direction.
He also appreciated the contributions of Giani Balwant Singh and PSGPC committee member Professor Dr Mampal Singh in the restoration work.
Mushtaq said the ETPB’s shrines department would continue efforts to restore historic gurdwaras and temples across the country.

Rs. 455 Million Spent on Restoration
Lahore Railways Divisional Superintendent Inamullah Khan said the restoration project cost around Rs. 455 million.
The project included civil, mechanical and electrical work.
Engineers also constructed a stronger embankment and created water passages under nearby bridges to reduce the risk of similar damage during future floods.
Major Trains Use Lahore-Faisalabad Route
The Lahore-Faisalabad railway section is considered an important revenue-generating route for Pakistan Railways.
Passenger trains operating on the route include the Shalimar Express, Badar Express, Ghauri Express and Karakoram Express.
Freight trains also use the route depending on the availability of goods for transportation.
Officials Inspect Restoration Work
Deputy Divisional Superintendent (Infrastructure) Qazi Jawad Ahmed conducted a motor trolley inspection of the Lahore-Sheikhupura railway track on Sunday.
Divisional Engineer Chaudhry Nasir Hanif and other railway officials also took part in the inspection.
The team reviewed construction and rehabilitation work and assessed the remaining steps required before the route could reopen.
Floods Forced Pakistan Railways to Suspend Services
Flooding in the Ravi and Chenab rivers, along with breaches in Nullah Deg and Bherr, caused extensive damage across the region.
Floodwater eroded soil underneath railway bridges and forced Pakistan Railways to suspend traffic on the Lahore-Faisalabad section via Shahdara and Sheikhupura.
The railway line was cut off at two bridges, including a major bridge near Qila Sattar Shah on the Lahore-Shahdara-Sheikhupura-Faisalabad route.
As a result, Pakistan Railways cancelled trains originating from Lahore for Faisalabad. It also suspended Lahore-Karachi and Khanewal-Lahore services operating through Faisalabad.
The restoration on November 15 is expected to bring those operations back to the important rail corridor and provide passengers with a more affordable travel option.

items.content:
inDrive, a global mobility and urban services platform, has partnered with the CIRCLE Women Association and Tech Valley to launch a comprehensive, free STEM and artificial intelligence education programme for the children of its driver community.
Against the backdrop of Pakistan’s broader educational landscape, there are roughly 25 million children between the ages of 5 and 16 who are not in school, marking the second largest out-of-school population in the world. Providing accessible, high-quality learning opportunities has never been more urgent. To bridge this divide, the initiative delivers targeted training through two specialized pillars.
Launched in September, 2026, the programme is an exclusive benefit for drivers enrolled in the platform’s Platinum and Legend loyalty tiers, the initiative provides over 750 children across Pakistan with professional training in coding, digital citizenship, and generative AI.
Awais Saeed, Country Manager for inDrive Pakistan, highlighted the core motivation behind the initiative, stating, “Our drivers are the true backbone of inDrive, working tirelessly every day to keep our communities connected. This initiative is a direct investment in their children’s future. By collaborating with trusted leaders like CIRCLE Women and Tech Valley, we are proud to offer this benefit to our drivers, equipping the next generation with the tech and AI skills to thrive in tomorrow’s economy.”
Sadaffe Abid, Founder and CEO of CIRCLE Women, commented, “A child who can build an app sees the world differently than a child who can only use one. With inDrive, CIRCLE Women is giving children of drivers hands-on digital and AI skills. In an AI-shaped economy, these skills aren’t optional; they’re the entry ticket. And the earlier a child learns to build with technology instead of just consuming it, the more of the world they get to build.”
Umar Farooq, Founder and CEO of Tech Valley, said, “Every child deserves to grow up digitally literate, safe, and AI-ready, not just those with access to the best schools. This partnership enables real skills, real reach, and real accountability by bringing structured digital learning straight to the families of inDrive drivers.”
The in-person component is being delivered by the CIRCLE Women Association, a non-profit organisation focused on women’s economic empowerment, engaging between 300 and 320 children aged 8 to 18 through dedicated training centers in Karachi, Lahore, and Islamabad. Over a three-month period, participants receive fully equipped laptops and hands-on guidance across three distinct age-specific tracks, including Scratch Game Studio, AI Web Prototyping, and App Engineering, enabling students to build functional digital portfolios.
Complementing the physical workshops, Tech Valley, an official Google for Education partner, is delivering online digital literacy and AI training via Google Classrooms for 400 to 450 students in grades 6 to 10. The curriculum features Google’s ‘Be Internet Awesome’ digital citizenship module and the ‘Gemini Academy’ for ethical generative AI prompt engineering, supported by live weekly sessions and expert facilitation.
By combining community-focused support with cutting-edge technical education, inDrive continues to invest directly in the long-term future of its driver ecosystem, empowering families and building sustainable pathways for the youth of Pakistan.

items.author: ProPK Staff
items.content:
Pakistan’s first VXR Festival, dedicated to virtual and extended reality art, has opened in Lahore with work from 70 artists from Pakistan and several other countries.
The inaugural festival opened at Alliance Française de Lahore on Sunday, bringing artists, creative professionals and visitors together to experience art through virtual reality, augmented reality and other immersive technologies.
Artists From Pakistan and Abroad Participate
The festival, titled “Between the Prompts // V.1,” features artists from Pakistan, France, Spain, Canada, the United States and other countries.
It has been curated by Dr Najamul Assar and Sarah Rajper, with Zainab Aamir serving as assistant curator.
The project is supported by the Embassy of France in Pakistan, Alliance Française de Lahore, Institut français, Embassy of Spain in Pakistan and AECID, in collaboration with UNESCO.
Sixteen artists were featured during the opening programme. They included Adriaan Lokman, Amna Tariq, Anusha Khalid, Asma Kazmi, Che-Kuang Chuang, Jérémy Griffaud, Jill Miller, Lola Zoido, Manel Pascual Bafaluy, Mansoor Ali, Marie Lienhard, Marion Pédebernade, Nicolas Thépot, Pierre-Alain Pédebernade, Sana Akram and Sandrine Deumier.
Visitors Experience Art Through VR Headsets
Unlike a conventional art exhibition, the VXR Festival allows visitors to experience artworks using VR headsets, screens and augmented-reality technology.
The “Between the Prompts” theme examines the relationship between human instructions and machine-generated visual output. It also explores how artists are responding to algorithms and emerging technologies that increasingly influence the creation of images and digital content.
A meet-the-artists session was also held during the opening, featuring AB Rehman, Anusha Khalid, Lola Zoido, Mansoor Ali, Marie Lienhard and Sandrine Deumier.
Festival Combines Traditional Art With New Technology
Several projects at the festival use immersive technology to reinterpret traditional art, cultural heritage and storytelling.
One of the major attractions is a Claude Monet virtual reality experience, being presented in Pakistan for the first time through the Institut français collection. The experience takes visitors from Monet’s garden in Giverny into his famous Water Lilies works at the Musée de l’Orangerie.
Pakistani artist Sana Akram’s “Sun” adapts the Urdu Tilismi Dastan storytelling tradition into an immersive environment.
Meanwhile, AB Rehman’s “Al Buraq 2.0” places a figure rooted in cultural and religious memory into a futuristic setting.
Other works include Jérémy Griffaud’s “Under the Sky,” which uses almost 300 watercolour paintings created in Borneo, and Faqeha Nadeem’s “Every Day,” which uses augmented reality to animate drawings from a sketchbook.
Festival to Move From Lahore to Islamabad
Following its opening at Alliance Française de Lahore, the festival is continuing at different venues in the city.
Its program includes activities at R Space at the Mariam Dawood School of Visual Arts and Design and Beaconhouse National University, with another program scheduled at BNU on November 12.
The festival will then move to Islamabad from November 13 to 15, where audiences will get another opportunity to experience the VR and XR installations.
The VXR Festival is an initiative of the team behind the Lahore Digital Arts Festival, which has promoted digital art and creative technology in Pakistan since 2019.

items.author: Shahbaz Rana
items.content:
Pakistan plans to draw the full $1.7 billion multi-tranche World Bank loan to widen the tax base and align expenditure with the Constitution, even though the lender has twice rated implementation on the approved $600 million tranche as moderately satisfactory and the government has itself breached one of the package's conditions twice.
One condition of the package is implementation of the National Tariff Policy. Ironically, the government breached it in June when it raised taxes on imports, and again last month when the Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) of the Cabinet approved additional customs duty to extend protection to a tyre manufacturing company.
The $1.7 billion is being taken in the name of Public Resource for Inclusive Development under the Multiphase Programmatic Approach, with $700 million approved last year.
Beneficiaries of the tranches will be the federal and all four provincial governments, according to World Bank documents. The loans have been taken once again to ensure equity in taxes, cut expenditure and bring it in line with the constitutional scheme, and withdraw electricity and agriculture subsidies.
Government officials said there were no plans to abandon the package despite slow implementation on the first phase of the $700 million loan. Of that amount, $600 million was taken by the federal government in December last year.
The World Bank's last two implementation status reports on the $600 million loan declared the programme moderately satisfactory. In April this year, it described the federal component as moderately satisfactory on the grounds that "the operation was approved by the World Bank Board on December 19, 2025, but was not yet effective".
In the second report, released last month, the bank retained the rating while noting some improvements. It said the $600 million operation became effective on May 14, 2026, and an advance disbursement of $164.5 million was made on June 29, 2026.
The next $200 million tranche is being approved for the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa government.
The bank said the roughly $1.7 billion package will have four overlapping phases. The first, of $700 million, included two operations under the federal government and the Sindh government "to provide enhanced support for complex activities and procurements and enhanced project oversight".
Under the $600 million loan, the federal government is committed to implementing the National Fiscal Pact to end federal funding for projects and subjects of a provincial nature. However, the government is constantly violating the pact, and in June this year approved Rs87 billion for a Sindh project.
The Sindh government has taken a $100 million loan in the first phase to "demonstrate proof-of-concept for supporting provincial reforms under the national fiscal pact including reforms to mobilize agricultural and property taxation".
Under the third and fourth phases, the Balochistan and Punjab governments would receive loans.
World Bank documents state that accelerated progress on reforms, including trade liberalisation, a new National Finance Commission Award, power sector restructuring, private participation in state-owned enterprises and strengthened social service delivery, remains essential to support higher growth, create sufficient jobs for a fast-growing working-age population and reverse the recent trend of increasing poverty.
The bank said the fiscal pact aims to rebalance federal-provincial fiscal arrangements by reducing federal spending in areas devolved under the 18th Amendment and strengthening provincial revenue handles such as agricultural and property taxation.
The World Bank has set three main objectives for the $1.7 billion debt package: raising tax revenues; improving the efficiency and prioritisation of public expenditure; and strengthening the fiscal and service delivery data ecosystem.
The bank will support improvements in tax policy, including assessing the equity, efficiency and revenue impacts of proposed reforms. Activities include mobilising key underused provincial revenue sources, implementing and operationalising effective taxation of agricultural income through the establishment of data systems, strengthening property taxation through digitalisation of land records and standardisation of valuation approaches and records, and supporting continued strengthening of General Sales Tax on Services collections through digital data integration.
Under the second objective of strengthened allocation, efficiency and accountability in expenditure, the bank will fund a programme of expenditure reviews to streamline government processes and administrative structure and reduce federal spending on constitutionally devolved functions. It will also support reforms to the electricity subsidy policy, including the design and implementation of a welfare-based subsidy system for residential consumers, and improvements to the federal budget process with continued rollout of the Integrated Financial Management Information System and the e-procurement system to improve tracking and integrity of resource use across federal entities.
Proposed provincial operations under the programme will focus on improving allocative and technical efficiency to adequately and effectively resource human development needs.
Under the third component of an improved statistical and data landscape for policymaking, the bank will fund improvements to the performance of the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, including governance through the establishment of a Governing Council and Users' Council, and facilitate data flow between federal and provincial bureaus and other national entities through a National Data and Statistics Hub.

items.content:
Farmer Mehmet Kabak has grown cotton on the same land in drought-prone western Turkey for decades. This year he is planting wheat and sunflower instead, in part because they require less water, making them cheaper to grow.
Kabak is one of many farmers worldwide forced to find their own way to cope with a changing climate rather than wait for countries to settle long-standing arguments at annual climate talks over who should finance adaptation.
Agriculture accounts for around 5% of Turkey's economic output. It also consumes 79% of the country's water, almost half of which is lost because of inefficient infrastructure and irrigation, the government has said.
As the next round of climate talks begins on Monday at COP31 in Antalya on the Mediterranean coast, 59-year-old Kabak, who farms 900 decares (about 220 acres) in Soke, hundreds of kilometres to the west, cannot afford to keep making losses.
Government support payments have not kept pace with rising fuel and fertiliser costs linked to irrigation and the US-Israeli war with Iran.
"We had increases in irrigation costs even though our harvest is damaged," Kabak said. "Our input costs increased by 40%, 50%, 60% continuously. Fuel prices did not stop."
Shrinking cotton acreage
Turkey was the world's eighth-largest cotton producer, according to 2023 data from the UN's Food and Agriculture Organisation, but its overall seed cotton output is expected to fall 38% year-on-year to 1.2 million metric tons in 2026, according to the Turkish statistics institute.
Drought and increased costs have led farmers in the Soke region to shrink cotton acreage by around 60% to around 120,000 decares in 2026, a local farming group said.
More than 30 farmers, lenders, companies and non-profit organisations told Reuters in interviews the sector needed more technical support and help gaining access to finance.
"Adaptation is no longer optional for farmers, but it is expensive, and today they largely pay for it themselves," said Aysegul Selisik, Turkey representative of the FAO.
Temporary reprieve from water shortage
For agriculture, water is the most pressing adaptation issue.
Last year, Turkey suffered the worst drought in over 50 years. Rainfall was 27% below the long-term average. Dam levels have recovered to an extent, government data showed, but analysts say the reprieve is likely to be temporary.
Reuters analysis of data from the WWF and Lincoln Institute of Land Policy showed water use in Turkey's cotton-producing basins needs to fall 25% to 60% to sustain healthy ecosystems.
Existing infrastructure is inefficient. Water drawn from dams and rivers often arrives unfiltered, clogging drip hoses before infrastructure to clean it is built.
But farmers are reluctant to invest for a variety of reasons.
In some cases, switching to newer systems can lead to an initial drop in yield that farmers may struggle to absorb. In addition, many work on rented land, meaning they are reluctant to invest, industry representatives said.
State and private sector offer some support
Turkey said in October, when it laid out next year's budget, the amount set aside for land and water resources management would rise 40.5%, with 174 billion lira ($3.5 billion) earmarked for agricultural irrigation investments.
The Agriculture Ministry told Reuters further support would be needed to supplement that, including from the private sector.
Turkey's largest private lender bank has opened 56 specialist agricultural branches and offers financing for drip and sprinkler irrigation with repayments tied to harvest cycles.
Sekerbank, which has a history of supporting farmers, says around a quarter of loans made under its sustainable-finance framework in the first nine months of 2026 went to agricultural water management and climate adaptation.
A lack of equity or collateral and the inability of some farmers to repay the loans, however, have limited the amount of help the private sector can deliver. Many farmers also have to pay upfront and get reimbursed later, if conditions are met.
"That makes it very difficult for them," said Liam Chicca, country director for Turkey at the International Fund for Agricultural Development.
The fund, which has invested $850 million in Turkey since 1982, estimates between 5% and 10% of Turkish farmers have virtually no capacity to finance major investments themselves.
For Turkey - and other governments - failure to adapt could cost more than acting now.
World Bank analysis in 2022 estimated a 10% reduction in water supply could cost Turkey 6% of GDP, or about $50 billion because of the impact on agriculture.

The RCCI delegation welcomed Punjab's new industrial policy, describing it as business- and industry-friendly, and appreciated income tax exemptions in industrial zones and the provision of interest-free loans.

The group will bring together the RCCI, the Islamabad chamber and government officials to take the project forward.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Gold prices in Pakistan increased on Monday, tracking gains in the international market, as a weaker US dollar and easing concerns over inflation supported demand for the precious metal ahead of key US inflation data due later this week.
In the local market, the price of gold per tola rose by Rs3,200 to reach Rs432,336, according to rates released by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association. Similarly, the price of 10-gram gold increased by Rs2,744 to Rs370,658. On Saturday, gold prices had remained unchanged at Rs429,136 per tola.
In the international market, spot gold gained 1.2% to $4,116.15 per ounce by 11:30 am ET (1630 GMT). US gold futures for December delivery also advanced 1.2% to $4,125.40, according to Reuters.
Market analyst Jim Wyckoff of American Gold Exchange said the US dollar index had weakened at the start of the trading week, making dollar-denominated bullion more affordable for buyers holding other currencies. He added that declining crude oil prices were also helping gold and silver by easing inflationary concerns and potentially giving central banks greater room to adopt less restrictive monetary policies.
Oil prices fell sharply after US President Donald Trump downplayed the possibility of renewed strikes on Iran. However, attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz continued to raise concerns about potential disruptions to global energy supplies.
Higher energy prices have fuelled inflationary concerns since the US-Israel war with Iran began in late February. Persistent inflationary pressures could force central banks to maintain higher interest rates for longer, reducing the appeal of non-yielding assets such as gold.
Investors are now awaiting US consumer price index (CPI) data scheduled for Tuesday, which could provide fresh indications about inflation trajectory and the Federal Reserve's future monetary policy.
Market participants were pricing in an 82.2% probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December, according to estimates cited in international trading reports.
Meanwhile, China's central bank continued adding to its gold reserves, purchasing approximately 25.8 tonnes of the precious metal in October, reflecting sustained official-sector demand.
Globally, spot silver climbed 1.6% to $52.69 per ounce, platinum gained 2.1% to $1,564.95, and palladium rose 0.2% to $1,025.46. In Pakistan's market, silver prices also moved higher, increasing by Rs55 to reach Rs5,723 per tola.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Infinix Note 60 Pro has entered a difficult price bracket in Pakistan. Once discussed around the Rs 100,000 mark, the phone is now officially listed at Rs 130,999 for its 8GB/256GB variant after a Rs 5,000 increase effective November 3, 2026. At this price, the question is no longer whether the handset has attractive specifications. It is whether buyers should spend nearly Rs 131,000 on Infinix when several alternatives are available.
The Note 60 Pro offers a 6.78-inch 144Hz AMOLED display, Snapdragon 7s Gen 4 processor, 50MP optically stabilized main camera, 8MP ultrawide lens and 13MP selfie camera. Its 6,500mAh battery, 90W wired charging and 30W wireless charging are particularly appealing. An aluminum build also helps it feel more premium than a typical midrange phone. However, the 8GB RAM/256GB UFS 2.2 configuration and IP64 protection are less impressive at this price.
Infinix Note 60 Pro Price in Pakistan: What Changed?
Price revision moved the official 8GB/256GB price from Rs 125,999 to Rs 130,999. Buyers may encounter quotations in the Rs 122,000–130,000 range, but these are not independently confirmed uniform street prices. The approximately Rs 100,000 introductory figure is also not verified as an official launch price. The current official listing is the stronger benchmark for judging value.
Infinix Note 60 Pro vs OPPO Reno16 F, Motorola Edge 70 Fusion, POCO M8 Pro and nubia Neo 5 Pro
Here is how the phones compare on published Pakistan prices and headline hardware. The prices are reference listings as of November 9, 2026, not guaranteed transaction prices; buyers should confirm PTA approval, warranty, availability and variant before purchasing.

Which Phone Offers Better Value?
For an all-round experience: The Note 60 Pro still has a persuasive case. Its 144Hz screen, Snapdragon 7s Gen 4, premium construction and wireless charging make it a well-rounded option. Buyers who specifically want wireless charging will find that feature harder to match in this shortlist.
For durability and fast charging: The POCO M8 Pro 5G costs around Rs 9,000 more at its listed price, but offers Gorilla Glass Victus 2, higher IP ratings and 100W wired charging with the same chipset. That makes it a serious alternative, especially for buyers who do not need wireless charging.
For cameras: The OPPO Reno16 F is more expensive, but its dedicated 3.5x telephoto camera and 50MP selfie camera make it more versatile on paper. This is a specification-based advantage, not a claim that it wins every real-world photo test.
For design and water resistance: Motorola’s Edge 70 Fusion deserves consideration for its 144Hz display and IP68/IP69 protection. Buyers should verify the precise local battery and charging variant before comparing endurance.
For gaming-oriented features at a lower price: The nubia Neo 5 Pro is around Rs 11,000 cheaper than the Infinix at listed prices and offers shoulder triggers and 12GB RAM. Its Unisoc chipset and less versatile camera hardware mean it is not automatically the best choice for every buyer.
Should You Buy the Infinix Note 60 Pro for Rs 122,000–131,000?
At approximately Rs 122,000 with genuine local warranty, the Note 60 Pro looks substantially more attractive. At the official Rs 130,999 price, the decision becomes tougher: the POCO M8 Pro is only about Rs 9,000 more, Motorola brings stronger advertised ingress protection, and OPPO offers a more flexible camera setup at a higher cost.
Choose the Infinix if its premium build, display and wireless charging are your priorities, particularly if you find a verified discount. Consider the POCO for wired charging and protection, OPPO for telephoto photography, Motorola for design and water resistance, or nubia for dedicated gaming controls on a lower budget.
Final Verdict: Which Smartphone Offers the Best Specifications and Features?
Comparing all five smartphones on their listed specifications, the POCO M8 Pro 5G emerges as the strongest overall alternative to the Infinix Note 60 Pro, particularly for buyers who prioritize durability, display protection and fast wired charging. At Rs 139,999, it offers the same Snapdragon 7s Gen 4 processor as the Infinix, a slightly larger 6.83-inch AMOLED display, Gorilla Glass Victus 2 protection, stronger advertised water and dust resistance, and faster 100W wired charging. These advantages make its Rs 9,000 premium relatively easy to justify.
Our Overall Pick: POCO M8 Pro 5G. Based on the published specifications and listed prices, the POCO offers the most compelling combination of performance, protection, charging technology and everyday practicality. Real-world testing and verification of local variants would still be needed for a definitive performance ranking.

items.author: AFP
items.content:
The title is widely expected to become the biggest game of the decade, with its launch coming 13 years after the previous edition scaled new heights in terms of gameplay and profitability.
Here are five things to know about GTA.
Trailblazer
The first two games in the series, which debuted in 1997, offered a top-down view of the action as players took on the role of a criminal on missions around cities.
But "GTA III" set the standard in 2001 for what games could be like, offering a combination of a three-dimensional open world, advanced graphics and gameplay that won widespread critical acclaim and legions of fans.
Read: GTA 6 reportedly generates $751m in pre-orders ahead of launch
Each new GTA title since then has been hailed by both industry analysts and gamers for pushing the boundaries of what is possible in the medium.
Cash cow
And they have all been bestsellers, bringing in billions of dollars for Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of the Rockstar Games studio.
Despite not releasing a flagship GTA game for more than a decade, the series has remained a cash cow, especially thanks to its multiplayer online version, where users can buy in-game items.
The last game in the franchise, "GTA V", was released in 2013 and reached $1 billion in retail sales "faster than any entertainment release in history", Take-Two has said.
"GTA V" has sold around 230 million copies, according to the company's latest figures, making it the second-best-selling game of all time, behind Minecraft.
The entire GTA franchise has sold a mammoth 470 million units, according to Take-Two.
Hi everyone,
Grand Theft Auto VI will now release on Thursday, November 19, 2026.
We are sorry for adding additional time to what we realize has been a long wait, but these extra months will allow us to finish the game with the level of polish you have come to expect and… pic.twitter.com/yLX9KIiDzX
— Rockstar Games (@RockstarGames) November 6, 2025
Magnet for controversy
With the wild success came a wave of controversies. Critics have from the start accused the series of glorifying violence and encouraging players to engage in criminal behaviour -- allegations Take-Two executives have denied.
GTA games have also faced strong criticism for misogynistic portrayals of women, caricatures of ethnic minorities and depictions of torture.
Despite being praised for their often biting cultural satire, the level of violence in the games has at times led to bans and restrictions in some countries.
Target Australia stopped selling "GTA V" in 2014, citing customer concerns. GTA games also carry a content rating for mature audiences only. Take-Two executives have said customers should be free to choose what games they buy.
A cultural institution
GTA has become a cultural institution despite the criticism, with its content spawning countless online memes and fans around the world referencing its scenes and dialogue.
Read More: Terminally ill longtime 'Grand Theft Auto' fan passes away weeks before 'GTA 6' release
Its growing influence has attracted some of the biggest names in entertainment to its cast. Tommy Vercetti, the main character in 2002's "GTA: Vice City", was voiced by Hollywood star Ray Liotta.
Other cameos in the series include Samuel L Jackson, Burt Reynolds, musician Phil Collins and comedian Ricky Gervais. In 2021, hip-hop superstar Dr Dre featured.
The French electro duo Justice is composing the soundtrack for "GTA VI" and an album built around the game's universe brings together musicians including rapper Travis Scott and Rolling Stones guitarist Keith Richards.
The next chapter
The studio formally revealed "GTA VI" with a trailer in December 2023.
Watch the Grand Theft Auto VI Launch Trailer, featuring the debut of “Flower in a Hurricane" from original score composers Justice feat. Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard.
Grand Theft Auto VI arrives November 19: https://t.co/WC41QIhkKd pic.twitter.com/KpnUHs47JC
— Rockstar Games (@RockstarGames) October 15, 2026
The new game is set in Leonida, a fictionalised version of Florida that includes a return to the Miami-inspired Vice City. It follows a criminal couple, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos.
Goodbye, Los Santos.
Welcome to Vice City. pic.twitter.com/ViS0EKtS3A
— GTA 6 Updates (@gtasix_) November 9, 2026
Originally targeted for late 2025, "GTA VI" was pushed back twice before settling on its November 19 release date on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S.
The game reportedly cost between $1 billion and $1.5 billion to produce, which would make it the most expensive cultural product ever.
