items.author: Gargi Sarkar
items.content:
The 2026 festive season began in muted fashion, but the performance of some of the key new-age tech stocks in the pre-festive quarter (Q2 FY27) shows that even in this environment businesses are able to extract and expand profits, and grow their topline.
When we see the financial performance of ecommerce, fintech and logistics stocks, it’s clear companies entered this period with a lot more confidence and absorbed some of these headwinds. Pretty much each one of them improved on their profitability metrics and their topline.
As Inc42 reported in October, early data from the festive season sales indicated that Indian consumers kept shopping, but with more abandon.
Online sales slipped from last year, card spending and smartphone sales weakened, and surveys suggest urban households are trimming discretionary budgets too. Rising household costs, uncertainty over jobs and incomes, and discounts that no longer feel compelling have made shoppers wary of big-ticket purchases.
Consumers are still browsing for products, but in the current climate, conversion rates have fallen for premium products, which usually see a big uptick.
A lot of this has to do with the macroeconomic factors, rising energy prices and logistics costs, and lingering grave geopolitical concerns that have dented consumer confidence and spending.
In Q2, logistics tech players expanded capacity ahead of the festive shopping rush, with higher volumes offering an opportunity to improve operating leverage. Ecommerce companies capitalised on seasonal demand, even as the pressure to balance growth with profitability persisted.
Meanwhile, fintech companies, particularly those with a big UPI focus, faced a different equation: the prospect of merchant discount rates (MDR) on select UPI transactions. While MDR itself is yet to come into effect, the fintech ecosystem’s quarter was defined by swelling toplines, which bodes well for the next quarter where MDR is likely to become a real factor.
Profitability broadened across the listed new-age tech universe, with nine of the 11 large tech stocks (with a market cap of over ₹10,000 Cr) across these key sectors reporting a net profit in Q2 FY27.
The combined bottomline of these companies improved by around ₹1,100–1,400 Cr year-on-year (YoY), depending on how exceptional items in the base quarter are treated, according to market data.
More importantly, EBITDA grew faster than revenue at all nine profitable companies, suggesting that operating leverage is beginning to show up in reported performance.
But a significant profit pool remained concentrated in a handful of companies, while businesses such as Swiggy and Meesho continue to report losses despite improving operating metrics.
Atul Thakkar, executive director at Anand Rathi Investment Banking, believes the market is moving towards rewarding earnings delivery rather than growth narratives. “Over the next 12–18 months, we expect earnings delivery, rather than growth narratives, to be the main driver of returns in this space,” he said,
This distinction is particularly relevant when the three major segments, fintech, logistics and ecommerce are assessed separately.
Fintech has delivered the strongest operating performance, logistics has shown some of the clearest margin improvement, and ecommerce has produced a wide range of outcomes. But how did the profitability story unfolded across these three sectors?
Logistics Tech Shifts Into High Gear
It was largely a capacity-building quarter for logistics companies, with the full benefit of festive demand expected to play out in Q3. Yet, the results already point to improving operating leverage, as shipment volumes grew faster than revenue at the larger third-party logistics (3PL) players.
Shadowfax’s revenue rose 57%, while express and hyperlocal orders grew nearly 70%. Adjusted EBITDA increased sharply, with margins expanding to 5%. Delhivery reported a similar divergence: express shipments grew 32%, against 22% growth in express revenue. Its adjusted EBITDA margin also improved, while first-half operating cash flow more than doubled.
The gap between volume and revenue growth suggests that incremental shipments are not translating into proportionate revenue. Profitability, therefore, will depend on whether higher volumes can offset pricing pressure and rising costs across fuel, wages and last-mile delivery.
Delhivery’s return to profitability also needs context: the year-ago quarter included acquisition-related integration costs linked to Ecom Express. Its adjusted EBITDA and cash generation offer a more useful measure of underlying progress.
Shiprocket, meanwhile, turned profitable, reporting a net profit of ₹60 Lakh against a loss of ₹20.3 Cr a year ago. Revenue grew 35%, while adjusted EBITDA more than tripled. Its core business continued to expand, with transactions growing 31% and adjusted EBITDA margin improving to 12.8%. The results point to improving economics, although the reported profit remains modest.
Across the sector, technology and network utilisation are central to the margin story.
Shadowfax is deploying AI-led route optimisation and expanding its seller platform, while Delhivery is investing in automation and autonomous material-handling systems. These initiatives could improve productivity, but their returns will depend on execution and the ability to absorb peak-season volumes without adding costs at the same pace.
The festive quarter will be the real test. Stronger volumes should support operating leverage, but sustained margin expansion will require better network utilisation, disciplined pricing and control over fulfilment costs. Logistics is showing clearer signs of improving economics, though the gap between shipment growth and revenue realisation remains a key risk.
Fintech’s Profit Engines Roar
Fintech was the strongest performer in Q2 FY27, with all the major companies in the segment reporting profits. Moreover, EBITDA growth outpaced revenue growth at each, pointing to improving operating leverage. The gains, however, are coming from deeper monetisation of existing customers rather than payment volumes alone.
Paytm is increasingly diversifying beyond payments, with financial services distribution contributing about a third of its revenue. Its merchant subscription base and financial services business continue to expand, reducing its dependence on payment processing.
Meanwhile, Pine Labs is extracting more value from its merchant network through subscriptions, affordability products and transaction-linked services. PB Fintech’s growing renewal book offers a similar advantage: recurring insurance revenue is expanding faster than its core insurance business, making growth less dependent on fresh policy acquisition.
The bigger question for fintech is whether these operating gains can withstand regulatory changes. The proposed UPI MDR framework could create an additional revenue stream, but the benefit to payment companies will depend on how the pool is shared between banks and other ecosystem participants. With implementation postponed beyond the festive period, it remains an opportunity rather than an earnings driver for now.
Insurance distribution faces a more direct overhang. The proposed changes to commission structures and expense limits could alter the economics of online intermediaries such as PB Fintech. Its growing renewal revenue offers some cushion, but the impact on new-policy distribution remains uncertain.
“While fintech companies have demonstrated an ability to improve monetisation and operating leverage, the regulatory environment remains a key determinant of how sustainable these gains will be. For this segment, regulation is a bigger variable than execution,” said Thakkar.
Ecommerce’s Profitability Divide Widens
Ecommerce delivered the widest divergence in Q2 FY27. While revenue growth remained strong across quick commerce, ecommerce and consumer brands, profitability varied sharply, reflecting differences in scale, cost structures and monetisation.
For example, Meesho saw its net loss narrow to 68%, while marketplace contribution margin improved to 6% of NMV from 3.3% a year ago. However, newer initiatives remain loss-making and are yet to establish meaningful scale.
Consumer brands delivered a more consistent earnings performance. Nykaa’s profit more than tripled, supported by margin expansion and growth across beauty and fashion. Lenskart also reported strong profit growth, with expansion across its India and international businesses. Higher store productivity, rising volumes and operating cash flow suggest that growth is being supported by better utilisation of the existing network, alongside store additions.
Input-cost inflation remains another pressure point for consumer brands. Passing on higher costs through pricing could protect margins but risks weighing on demand and average order values. Gross margins, customer retention and acquisition costs will be as important as revenue growth in assessing the durability of earnings.
Why Profits Are Just Half The Story
As these sectors continue to mature, operating leverage is becoming more important than headline growth. However, profitability remains concentrated, with a handful of companies accounting for a substantial share of the sector’s earnings.
The ownership shift is also worth watching.
Foreign investors have reduced exposure to several listed new-age tech companies, while domestic institutions have increased participation. But domestic ownership is no guarantee against corrections when earnings or regulatory developments disappoint.
According to market analysts, retail investors are likely to increasingly favour companies that are not only profitable but also generate revenue from multiple products within their existing customer base and use operating cash flow to fund expansion.
We can see this in the aggressive diversification across the industry, particularly in fintech and logistics tech.
This wave favours established fintech businesses, asset-light logistics networks and ecommerce companies where the seller-customer flywheel is up and running.
Post the festive season spike, even if it may be a relatively smaller spike compared to previous years, the cash generation and regulatory resilience of these companies will be worth watching. That could very well mark the next phase of maturity.
MARKETS WATCH: NEW ISSUES, POST-IPO JOURNEY & MORE
Inside Razorpay’s ₹6,000 Cr IPO: As Razorpay gears up for its ₹6,000 Cr IPO, the proposed UPI merchant discount rate and its AI ambitions could shape its valuation. But can these growth levers convince public market investors to look beyond its thin margins?
Honasa’s Profit Up 87%: The Mamaearth parent reported an 87% YoY jump in Q2 FY27 net profit to ₹73.2 Cr, while revenue rose 36% to ₹731.2 Cr. Growth across focus categories, offline channels and younger brands helped drive the company’s quarterly performance.
Go Digit PAT Dips: Go Digit’s net profit declined 31.1% YoY to ₹142.4 Cr in Q2 FY27 despite a marginal 1.7% rise in insurance revenue to ₹2,720.5 Cr. Higher insurance service expenses and claims weighed on profitability, even as motor insurance revenue grew.
RateGain Profit Rises 47%:The travel-focused SaaS company’s profit rose 46.5% YoY to ₹74.7 Cr in Q2 FY27, driven by operating revenue zooming 152.6% YoY to ₹745.4 Cr. This came on the back of the consolidation of travel marketing platform Sojern, which RateGain acquired for $250 Mn last year.
Moneyview Revenue Grows 41%: The fintech company’s consolidated net profit surged 417.6% YoY to ₹200.7 Cr in Q2 FY27, while operating revenue grew 41% to ₹1,120.2 Cr. The fintech reported a managed AUM of ₹23,892 Cr, with its shares gaining 5.7% following the earnings announcement.
[Edited by Shishir Parasher]
The post Profits Are Just Half The Story This Earnings Season appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.content:
The government has raised the personal loan limit under the Prime Minister’s Youth Business and Agriculture Loan schemes from Rs. 7.5 million to Rs. 25 million, according to the premier’s office release this week.
The minimum age to apply has also been cut from 21 to 18 years.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced the changes while chairing a review meeting on the schemes. He also directed that 30 percent of all loans be reserved for women.
Loans Offered on Easy Installments
Officials told the meeting that the higher loans will be offered on easy installments. A total of Rs. 292 billion has been allocated for the schemes this year.
The prime minister directed the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority (SMEDA) to help young people with business start-ups, mentoring, advice and technical support. He also ordered a nationwide awareness campaign so more young people can benefit.
Loans Given Since 2023
According to the briefing, 581,341 young people have received loans since January 2023, worth Rs. 313.9 billion. That is ten times more than in the previous ten years. Around 266,700 young people are expected to receive Rs. 292 billion in 2026-27.
The prime minister praised Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb and his team for arranging financing for young entrepreneurs and farmers. He said young people are a valuable asset for Pakistan and the government is committed to giving them decent and productive jobs.
The meeting was also attended by Aurangzeb, Special Assistant on Youth Affairs Rana Mashhood Ahmad Khan and Special Assistant on Political Affairs Talha Burki.
What It Means
The higher ceiling and lower age limit widen access for first-time entrepreneurs and young farmers. The women’s quota follows earlier figures that showed women entrepreneurs securing Rs. 29 billion under the youth loan scheme. Details of how to apply for the loans were published earlier.

Because the edit happens as the video streams, viewers would not know what was actually said. That opens the door to misinformation and fraud. The filing reportedly includes only one dependent claim that keeps the original recording.

items.content:
By Ugochukwu Alaribe
UMUAHIA — Aba South Local Government Area of Abia State has established commercial poultry and piggery farms as part of efforts to boost its internally generated revenue (IGR), create jobs and equip residents with skills in animal husbandry.
The Executive Chairman of the council, Chief Obialo Anyanwu, disclosed this while briefing journalists on his administration’s two-year achievements, explaining that the initiative was aimed at making the local government more financially self-reliant.
Anyanwu said his administration was exploring sustainable revenue sources to strengthen the council’s capacity to deliver services rather than depend entirely on external funding.
He explained that the farms would also serve as training centres where residents would acquire practical skills in animal farming, enabling them to establish their own businesses and employ others.
He said: “We don’t believe in all these 10kg of rice empowerment. What we want in Aba South is giving our people that level of empowerment that will make them self-sustaining and employ others. So, we’ll teach the techniques needed to succeed in the business.
“The three buildings in the poultry section are up, two are already roofed, and the staff quarters are at the lintel stage because it’s a proper farm and people must reside there.
“Possibly by the end of the year, everything will take off. So, we’re envisaging such a future. We, as the third tier of government, must stand for ourselves, and it has pushed us into doing commercial poultry and commercial pig farming.”
The chairman disclosed that the poultry farm occupies 14 plots of land, while the piggery farm covers seven plots.
He added that the projects would generate revenue for the council, create employment opportunities and provide practical agricultural training for residents, including staff of the council’s agriculture department.
On healthcare, Anyanwu said the council had established and equipped 22 Glycoster World Primary Healthcare Centres in partnership with the Abia State Government.
He said the facilities had been commissioned and made operational, adding that the council had also organised free medical tests and treatments for residents.
On education, the chairman said the council was supporting Governor Alex Otti’s free back-to-school programme through the distribution of 4,000 school bags to pupils in primary schools across the local government area.
He explained that the initial target was 10,000 beneficiaries but that the distribution would be carried out in phases after an enumeration exercise showed that the number of eligible pupils exceeded the target.
Anyanwu also disclosed that the council was partnering with the state government on primary school development, including the ongoing construction of a smart school along Etche Road.
He said the administration had equally invested in digital skills training, with more than 130 residents trained in three cohorts.
According to him, the first cohort graduated 50 participants, the second had 30, while the third produced another 50 graduates.
On road infrastructure, Anyanwu said the council commenced road grading shortly after he assumed office on November 4, 2024.
He disclosed that more than 20 kilometres of roads across the 12 wards were graded between late November 2024 and early January 2025, while another 28 kilometres were covered by the end of 2025.
The chairman commended security agencies in the area for their professionalism and commitment, saying Aba South had remained peaceful.
He identified the removal of individuals and companies allegedly operating unauthorised revenue collection arrangements as one of his administration’s major achievements.
“One of the biggest achievements we’ve made in this administration so far was the chasing out of one revenue vampire with one company called Chicotax out of the Aba South LGA. He has been doing this for several years, but this time around, we’ve arrested the situation, and we’ve moved on,” he said.
Anyanwu described the relationship between the council and the state government as cordial, commending Otti for supporting road infrastructure projects in Aba South.
He expressed optimism that ongoing and planned road projects would improve transportation and access to several communities in the council area.
He specifically mentioned the ongoing work on Obohia Road, which he said included a drainage system designed to channel floodwater from different parts of Aba into the river.
He also listed Umuebeke Road, Uratta Road and Old Express Road among the projects expected to improve road connectivity in the area.
The chairman said the projects, when completed, would improve access to communities and enable the Abia State Environmental Protection Agency (ASEPA) to extend its operations to previously inaccessible areas.

US President Donald Trump said that his mass deportation of undocumented immigrants was “too tough,” according to an excerpt of an interview with CBS aired Sunday.
Asked about his deportation policy, Trump told CBS’ “60 Minutes”: “I think it was too tough…I think it might be too tough.”

items.content:
US President Donald Trump said that his mass deportation of undocumented immigrants was “too tough,” according to an excerpt of an interview with CBS aired Sunday.
Asked about his deportation policy, Trump told CBS’ “60 Minutes”: “I think it was too tough…I think it might be too tough.”
The excerpt was published by CBS on X ahead of a broadcast of the interview on network TV later Sunday. It was recorded after the Republican Party’s heavy loss in midterm elections on Tuesday.
While Trump has won some domestic support for securing the US southern border, his administration’s aggressive push to deport millions of undocumented migrants has drawn widespread criticism.
However, Trump on Friday appointed the architect of that hardline policy, Stephen Miller, as his chief of staff on Friday, signaling a bare-knuckle fightback after the Republican election loss.
Miller has been synonymous with scenes of masked immigration agents committing violence after he backed federal agents who shot and killed two Americans early this year.

By Steve Oko
UMUAHIA—Former member of the House of Representatives, Uko Nkole, has predicted a landslide victory for the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, in the 2027 general elections.
Nkole, who is the NDC senatorial candidate for Abia North, said Obi’s economic management record, national appeal and popularity among youths positioned him to win the presidency.
He spoke during a political debate at the grand finale of the 2026 Press Week organised by the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Abia State, in Umuahia.
He predicted the defeat of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), blaming its economic policies for the hardship facing Nigerians.
Nkole also vowed to unseat incumbent Abia North Senator, Orji Uzor Kalu, accusing him of failing to deliver meaningful development to the district.
He urged Kalu to support Obi’s presidential ambition rather than President Bola Tinubu, saying both politicians belonged to the same political generation.
“President Bola Tinubu is his mate. They were governors of the 1999 class. It’s very wrong for him to be clapping for his mate. The challenge all of us have today is how to produce a Nigerian President of Igbo extraction, which Obi represents,” he said.
Unveiling an eight-point development agenda, Nkole promised 20 town hall meetings annually across the five local government areas of Abia North, revival of 217 primary healthcare centres, intervention in 415 public schools, restoration of 15 regional water schemes and completion of abandoned federal projects.
He also pledged to attract a Federal Medical Centre, facilitate 1,000 federal jobs for youths within four years and pursue the establishment of the proposed Federal Polytechnic, Abiriba.
Meanwhile, the PDP senatorial candidate for Abia North, Jude Udeachara, promised to sponsor legislation compelling mining and construction companies to rehabilitate lands degraded by their operations.
He also pledged monthly accountability briefings to journalists, including disclosure of project costs, contractors and contract details.
The NDC House of Representatives candidate for Isuikwuato/Umunneochi, Evangeline Iwenjiora, also promised improved infrastructure, youth and women empowerment and quality representation.
Earlier, Chairman of the Correspondents’ Chapel, Deacon Steve Oko, urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to consider engaging experienced journalists with proven integrity as ad-hoc electoral officials, particularly returning officers, in the 2027 elections.
He said journalists’ experience in observation, documentation and verification could strengthen electoral credibility.
Oko also demanded real-time transmission of polling unit results, improved electoral logistics and better security and insurance for journalists covering the elections.
He disclosed that the Chapel had trained more than 50 journalists at a two-day retreat on artificial intelligence, disinformation, fact-checking, election reporting and journalists’ safety.
Delivering the keynote address, Rector of Ogbonnaya Onu Polytechnic, Aba, Prof. Christopher Okoro, cautioned journalists against spreading fake news, urging them to deploy technology and artificial intelligence responsibly.
The Chapel also honoured Prof. Nnenna Oti, the Returning Officer in the 2023 Abia governorship election, for her conduct during the poll.

SOKOTO – The Sultanate Council of Sokoto has called on Muslims across Nigeria to search for the new crescent moon of Jumada Assaniya 1448AH on Monday, November 9, 2026.
The directive was contained in a statement dated November 8, 2026, signed by Professor Sambo Wali Junaidu and made available to journalists on Sunday.
According to the statement, the Advisory Committee on Religious Affairs of the Sultanate Council identified Monday as the 29th day of Jumada al-Ula 1448AH and the appropriate date for the nationwide moon-sighting exercise.

The council stressed the importance of timely and credible reports of confirmed sightings to enable the Sultan to make the appropriate religious announcement on the commencement of the new Islamic month.
It noted that the Sultan remains the recognised authority responsible for communicating the outcome of the moon-sighting exercise to Muslims across the country.
The announcement underscores the role of the Sultanate Council in coordinating Islamic religious affairs and guiding the Muslim Ummah on matters concerning the Islamic lunar calendar.
In a prayer, Professor Sambo Wali Junaidu, Waziri and Chairman of the Advisory Committee on Religious Affairs of the Sultanate Council, asked Allah (SWT) to grant Muslims the guidance and strength to discharge the religious responsibility successfully.
The council also prayed for divine assistance and acceptance of the exercise, urging Muslims to approach the assignment with sincerity, vigilance and a strong sense of religious commitment.

items.content:
Fermin Lopez struck twice to help Barcelona come from behind to beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 and move three points clear at the top of La Liga.
The Spanish champions lead second place Real Madrid, who beat Valencia 3-0 on Saturday, with Atletico third, now five points behind.
Giuliano Simeone fired Atletico ahead in a high-octane start, before Lopez pulled Barca level shortly before the interval at the Metropolitano stadium.
The 23-year-old Spain international netted the winner after 66 minutes when Lamine Yamal slipped him in.
The match started at a fast pace and both teams hit the woodwork in the opening stages.
Alvarez, who tried and failed to force a move from Atletico to Barca in the summer, rounded goalkeeper Joan Garcia but could not finish off the chance as the defence blocked his route to goal.
From the resulting corner Atletico defender Marc Pubill headed against the crossbar with Garcia beaten.
At the other end Pedri crashed a strike against the woodwork after being fed by Barca’s teenage star Lamine Yamal.
Atletico took the lead in the 10th minute, slicing Barca’s defence open. Alvarez crossed for Giuliano Simeone to turn home from close range.
The game settled down after that pulsating start, although Alvarez came close to scoring Atletico’s second.
The Argentine international’s shot was fumbled by Garcia, but the goalkeeper was able to collect the ball quickly afterwards.
Yamal blasted into the side-netting from a tight angle with Barcelona not able to click into their top gears.
Despite their struggles they went in level at the break, with a goal out of nowhere.
Lopez’s path to the box was blocked but the ball bounced loose to the midfielder and he quickly smashed a strike past Jan Oblak.
Early in the second half Alvarez lobbed over the crossbar when running in on goal.
The forward came to rue the miss when Barcelona took the lead.
Yamal played a clever pass through Atletico’s defence and Lopez kept his cool to beat Oblak. It was his seventh league goal in 11 top flight appearances this season.
Barcelona kept Atletico at bay well in the final stages to take three points home from the capital before the international break.
Earlier on fourth-place Real Betis earned a 2-0 win at Elche, while Real Sociedad, fifth, defeated Rayo Vallecano 1-0.
Villarreal beat Getafe 2-0 to move eighth and Celta Vigo and Levante shared a goalless draw.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
…Says decision can jeopardise academic future of more than 21,000 students
The National Teachers’ Institute (NTI) Centre Managers’ Forum has appealed to President Bola Tinubu and the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, to review the cancellation of the institute’s programmes and the 2026 admissions, warning that the decision could jeopardise the academic future of more than 21,000 students.
The forum, in an appeal signed by its National Chairman, Dr Tam Loveday Frank Jumbo, and National Secretary, Dr Mamuda Inuwa Doguwa, urged the Federal Government to allow affected students to complete their programmes while necessary regulatory reforms are undertaken.
The appeal followed an announcement by the Federal Ministry of Education on November 7, cancelling all admissions into NTI’s National Certificate in Education (NCE) and degree programmes for the 2026 academic session over alleged regulatory breaches involving admissions, accreditation and university affiliations.
The ministry also directed the institute to discontinue all university affiliations and degree-awarding arrangements, stating that NTI was not authorised to award NCE and university degrees.
Reacting to the development, the Centre Managers’ Forum said it received the announcement with concern, particularly because thousands of students had already secured admission, registered for their programmes and participated in academic activities.
According to the forum, many of the affected students had attended physical and virtual lectures and sat for their first-semester examinations in August 2026, with some awaiting the release of their results.
It said the students enrolled in good faith, believing they were gaining admission into a legitimate, government-owned institution operating under the supervision of the Federal Ministry of Education.
The forum noted that for more than 45 years, NTI had provided educational opportunities to Nigerians who, because of financial constraints, work commitments, family responsibilities and geographical barriers, could not easily access conventional universities and colleges of education.
It claimed that the institute had provided educational opportunities to more than one million Nigerians, contributing to teacher development, human capital development and access to higher education across the country.
The forum argued that students should not bear the consequences of institutional or administrative shortcomings beyond their control, particularly after making financial commitments and participating in academic activities organised by the institute.
It also expressed confidence in the current Director-General, Professor S.S. Daura, saying efforts under his leadership had restored hope among students.
While acknowledging the Federal Government’s commitment to improving educational standards and ensuring regulatory compliance, the forum appealed to the minister to adopt what it described as a more inclusive and compassionate approach to resolving the matter.
Specifically, it asked the ministry to reconsider the cancellation of the programmes and 2026 admissions, allowing affected students to complete their studies.
It also called for a review of NTI’s operations, admission procedures and academic activities to ensure compliance with established regulatory guidelines.
Other requests included transitional arrangements for students already admitted, registered, taught and assessed, as well as consultations with relevant stakeholders, including the Centre Managers’ Forum, to develop a sustainable solution.
The forum maintained that educational reforms should strengthen institutions and improve quality without abruptly terminating the aspirations of students who had relied on government-owned institutions.
“Our appeal is not against educational reforms or quality assurance. Rather, it is a call for fairness, justice, compassion and a carefully considered transition that does not sacrifice the future of thousands of Nigerians,” it said.
However, the Federal Ministry of Education had explained that the decision followed violations of the Ministerial Operational Guidelines issued on September 12, 2025.
In a statement issued by its Director of Press and Public Relations, Boriowo Folasade, the ministry said NCE admissions must comply with the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) requirements and accreditation standards of the National Commission for Colleges of Education (NCCE).
It also directed the National Universities Commission (NUC) to notify affected universities and ensure compliance with the discontinuation of NTI’s degree-awarding arrangements.
The ministry clarified that no further admissions into the affected programmes, whether full-time, part-time or through Distance Learning Studies (DLS), would be permitted.
However, in a measure to protect students already enrolled, the ministry said the NCCE would conduct comprehensive accreditation of existing NCE II–IV Distance Learning programmes and study centres across the six geopolitical zones.
It added that eligible students could complete their programmes, subject to accreditation outcomes and regulatory requirements.
The ministry further stressed that NTI’s statutory mandate remained teacher training, retraining, in-service development and continuous professional development.
It said the mandate also covered pedagogical capacity-building and the three-to-six-month Special Abridged Programme for serving teachers with non-education degrees to acquire professional competencies required for registration with the Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN), subject to applicable regulations.
The ministry urged prospective students, parents and the general public to verify programme accreditation and admission status through relevant regulatory authorities and official government channels before seeking admission or making payments.
The post NTI managers to Tinubu, education minister: Review admission cancellation appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
At least seven people have been killed and more than 100 injured after two trains collided near Giza, Egypt, causing several carriages to derail and plunge down an embankment.
The country’s railway authority said the trains, travelling south from Giza and Cairo, collided in the area between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations in Al-Ayyat.
Egypt’s President, Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, said he had directed relevant authorities to investigate the circumstances surrounding the accident and ensure that anyone found negligent was held accountable.
The public prosecutor’s office warned that the death toll could rise as rescue and recovery operations continued.
The government said hospitals in the affected area had been placed on heightened alert to handle the large number of casualties.
Health Minister, Dr Khaled Abdel Ghaffar, said victims were receiving treatment for various injuries, including broken bones and head injuries.
The Egyptian Red Crescent also deployed personnel to provide emergency assistance and psychological support to victims and their families at the scene.
The ministry confirmed that the driver of one of the trains was among those killed in the collision.
According to reports, the first train was travelling from Giza to Fayoum when it crashed into the rear of another train heading from Cairo to Aswan, which was stationary on the tracks.
Photographs from the scene showed several overturned carriages, with emergency responders and members of the public searching through the wreckage for survivors.
Train services between Giza and the Upper Egypt region were suspended as cranes were deployed to remove the damaged trains. The railway authority had yet to announce when services would resume.
The crash occurred close to the location of Egypt’s deadliest railway disaster, which happened in February 2002 when a fire engulfed a passenger train travelling from Cairo to Luxor, killing more than 370 people officially, although some estimates put the death toll higher.
Two other train accidents in the area in 2009 also claimed dozens of lives.
The latest disaster sparked calls on Sunday for Egypt’s transport minister to resign over the recurring railway accidents.
Meanwhile, foreign governments and diplomatic representatives expressed condolences and solidarity with Egypt over the tragedy.
Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed solidarity with Egypt and wished the injured a speedy recovery.
Turkey’s Ambassador to Egypt also conveyed his condolences on X to the victims, their families and the Egyptian people.
BBC

The commissioner also urged members of the public attending political rallies and other public events to remain vigilant, safeguard their valuables and promptly report suspicious movements to security operatives.
He called for continued public cooperation through the provision of timely and credible information to assist the command in preventing and controlling crime.

The operation also led to the arrest of three suspects identified as Umaru Janyo, 49, and Bube Kwaire, 28, both from Bendu Village, and Muhammadu Gyade, 22, of Tindifai Village.
The police said other members of the criminal gang escaped with suspected gunshot injuries.
Items recovered during the operation included an unregistered Haojue motorcycle, ₦308,000 in cash, a chain and a jerrycan.
The command said it had intensified security patrols and surveillance in the area, adding that efforts were ongoing to track down the fleeing suspects and bring all those involved to justice.
The Commissioner of Police, CP Umar M. Hadejia, commended the operatives and their local vigilante collaborators for their prompt response, courage and effective coordination.
He reiterated the command’s commitment to protecting lives and property, disrupting criminal networks and ensuring that perpetrators of violent crimes were brought to justice.
Hadejia also urged members of the public to continue providing timely and credible information to security agencies to strengthen collective security efforts.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Golok Nanmwa
JOS – Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples’ Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has backed the establishment of state police, pledging to decentralise Nigeria’s security architecture if elected president in the 2027 general elections.
Makinde stated this on Sunday during a live political programme on Jay FM 101.9 in Jos, Plateau State, where he outlined his proposed security reforms ahead of the party’s presidential campaign activities in the city.
“I believe that we need to decentralise our security architecture. State police is one of the ways to achieve this, but it must be properly structured.
“States that are ready should be allowed to establish their own police formations, while others can come on board when they are prepared,” he said.
Recalling his engagement with former President Muhammadu Buhari on the issue in 2019, Makinde said the former president had expressed concerns about the ability of some states to fund their police formations.
“When we approached President Buhari in 2019, one of the concerns he raised was that some states could not even pay workers’ salaries. He questioned how such states would be able to fund state police,” he said.
Explaining the alternative adopted by governors in the South-West, Makinde said they settled for a regional security arrangement through Amotekun.
He said the operatives gather intelligence and work with federal security agencies, adding that the initiative had helped improve security coordination in the region.
The APM presidential candidate acknowledged concerns that state police could be abused by governors to intimidate political opponents and other citizens, but insisted that appropriate safeguards could address such risks.
“We must not pretend that there are no concerns. Some people are worried that governors could use state police to oppress their opponents or intimidate citizens. Those concerns are valid, and we must put safeguards in place.
“But the fact that something can be abused does not mean we should not do it. We must design a system that ensures accountability and protects the rights of the people,” he said.
On the pace of implementation, Makinde said states should be allowed to establish their police formations at different times, depending on their readiness and capacity.
He cited Nigeria’s transition to self-government and independence as an example of how states could adopt the arrangement at different paces.
“We had self-government in 1957 and independence in 1960. We did not achieve everything at once. In the same way, states can move at different paces,” he said.
Makinde also warned that Nigeria’s growing population, particularly its large youth population, required urgent government attention through job creation and opportunities for economic advancement.
“We are talking about a country that could have a population of over 300 million people, with more than 70 per cent below the age of 34. We must create opportunities for these young people.
“If we fail to provide pathways for them to succeed, we should not be surprised when some of them turn to crime or other activities that threaten the stability of the country,” he said.
Beyond security, the governor said his proposed Reset Agenda would address the country’s economic and governance challenges, insisting that Nigeria needed fundamental changes rather than superficial adjustments.
“When you talk about reform, it means that there is something good in the system that you want to improve upon. But when the bad outweighs the good, you need to take a different course of action.
“If what you have in the system is only about 20 per cent of what you expected, you don’t need to continue tweaking it. You need to press the reset button, shut it down and reboot it. That is what Nigeria needs at this point,” he said.
On the economy, Makinde said government policies should be assessed by their impact on the living conditions of ordinary Nigerians rather than economic statistics alone.
“The economy must work for everybody. We should not just be talking about foreign reserves, World Bank figures or inflation statistics. What matters is whether ordinary Nigerians can afford to feed themselves and meet their basic needs.
“If the people on the streets are not feeling any improvement, then we cannot say that the economy is doing well. The real test of economic performance is the condition of the people,” he said.
He said his proposed administration would prioritise skills acquisition, entrepreneurship, education and production to create jobs and stimulate economic growth.
“We must encourage our people to acquire skills and become entrepreneurs. We must invest in education and move towards intensive production. Government must provide an environment where businesses can thrive and young people can find meaningful employment,” he said.
Explaining his decision to join politics, Makinde said he was motivated by concerns about the country’s future rather than a desire to pursue a career in politics.
“I am not a career politician. I came into politics because I believe that the future of millions of Nigerians is at stake. We have the potential to become the greatest Black nation on the face of the earth, but we must make the right decisions to achieve that destiny,” he said.

He also said their entry would strengthen grassroots mobilisation, expand the party’s political reach and enhance its engagement with voters across the state.
The latest defections come amid growing political realignments in Gombe State as political parties intensify efforts to consolidate their structures and mobilise support ahead of the 2027 general elections.

items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
The governorship candidates of the Labour Party (LP), Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Funso Doherty, have criticised the Lagos State Government’s waste management system, describing it as inefficient and in need of urgent reform.
The candidates made their positions known during the Lagos governorship debate in Lagos on Friday organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium comprising Vanguard, Channels Television, TVC News, The PUNCH and TheCable.
Rhodes-Vivour argued that waste management in Lagos was too centralised, with local governments having little or no involvement in the system.
He said the state had failed to develop a waste-to-wealth value chain, relying instead on a system focused largely on collecting and dumping refuse.
“The management of the system is too centralised. Local governments are not involved. We have failed to create a waste-to-wealth value chain. We don’t have a proper waste management system; we have a waste-pick-and-dump system,” he said.
The LP candidate promised to decentralise waste management by involving local governments and creating opportunities to generate economic value from waste.
“Under my government, that will change. We will get local governments involved. We will create value from waste, so that people, local governments and the state government can all benefit,” he added.
Similarly, Doherty described the state’s waste management challenges as a failure of government, noting that while some parts of Lagos were clean, others continued to struggle with poor sanitation.
“Parts of Lagos are smelling, while other parts are clean. We have a waste management problem, and I would characterise it as a failure of government,” he said.
The NDC candidate identified inadequate investment in waste collection trucks as one of the factors worsening the situation.
He also blamed the problem on the government’s approach to public services, arguing that successive administrations had increasingly withdrawn from the social sector while expecting private operators to fill the gap.
“Part of the problem is that we don’t have enough investment in trucks. It goes back to the government stepping back from the social sector and wanting the private sector to do everything,” he added.

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
Governorship candidates of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), All Progressives Congress (APC), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) have presented their proposals for addressing some of Lagos State’s major challenges, including housing, transportation, and healthcare, ahead of the 2027 governorship election.
The candidates made their positions known during the 2027 Lagos State governorship debate organised by Vanguard Channels Television, TVC, Punch Newspapers, and The Cable on Sunday.
Housing
The ADC candidate, Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, promised to deliver more than 100,000 housing units if elected, saying his administration would prioritise affordable accommodation for ordinary residents rather than the wealthy.
He said the proposed houses would be allocated transparently to prevent individuals from acquiring multiple units under the scheme.
“The elites, the rich, can do it for themselves. The government’s role is to lift up people that cannot do it for themselves, and this comes into housing to ensure that we deliver 100,000-plus housing units and make it affordable so that it is transparently allocatable. We are not going to have a situation where one person can own ten units,” Rhodes-Vivour said.
The ADC candidate also promised legislation to protect tenants against arbitrary rent increases, proposing that landlords should give at least six months’ notice before increasing rents, with the increment guided by a stipulated percentage.
He added that a feedback mechanism would be established to enable tenants to report landlords who violated the proposed regulations, assuring that offenders would be brought to justice.
The All Progressives Congress candidate, Obafemi Hamzat, who is the incumbent deputy governor, pledged to enforce existing regulations against arbitrary rent increases and the demand for multiple years’ rent in advance.
Hamzat said his administration would ensure compliance with the Lagos State Real Estate Registration Agency Law, stressing that tenants should not be required to pay two or three years’ rent upfront.
“The next chapter for Lagos is to enforce. To make sure people are not asked two or three years ahead, because people don’t get paid two or three years ahead,” he said.
He also said the state had established 24 housing estates in the last eight years, promising to expand access to quality accommodation through increased mortgage facilities and the completion of ongoing housing projects across the state.
The NDC candidate, Funsho Doherty, called for greater government involvement in providing affordable housing, arguing that private developers alone could not meet the accommodation needs of low- and middle-income residents.
He also proposed the establishment of an ombudsman’s office to address what he described as exploitation of tenants through excessive agency, legal and other charges.
Doherty said the housing shortage was largely driven by the failure of supply to keep pace with population growth and demand, particularly in the affordable and social housing segments.
He argued that government should take the lead in addressing the gap rather than leaving housing provision largely to private investors. According to him, the last major government-led housing intervention in the state was during the administration of former Governor Lateef Jakande.
Meanwhile, the PDP candidate, Adedeji Doherty, proposed that the Lagos State Government should become a major property developer and build houses which residents could rent directly from the government.
He argued that government regulation alone could not force private landlords to reduce rents, insisting that the state should compete with them by providing more affordable accommodation.
“There is no landlord, and there is no government that can control a landlord. What we are going to do is very simple. “We are going to rent those houses ourselves, and then you can come and rent from us if you want to,” he said.
Doherty maintained that government must become the biggest housing developer in the state and provide alternatives to private rental accommodation.
“If they cannot compete with the landlords, then let us forget it,” he said.
Infrastructure
On flooding and infrastructure, the candidates offered different approaches to managing Lagos State’s environmental challenges, with proposals ranging from improved drainage systems and wetland protection to climate adaptation, better road construction standards and infrastructure maintenance.
The ADC candidate, Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, said Lagos needed visionary leadership and modern engineering solutions to address flooding, particularly given its low-lying coastal geography.
He cited cities such as Japan, Venice and the Netherlands as examples of places that had adopted innovative approaches to managing water, arguing that Lagos should learn from their experiences.
Rhodes-Vivour criticised the practice of indiscriminate sand-filling of wetlands, saying alternative construction methods could allow water to flow naturally without worsening flooding. He cited the Makoko community as an example, arguing that building structures on concrete stilts could provide an alternative to filling wetlands.
“There’s a technology there that they could have used, where we can build on concrete steels that still allow for water to flow,” he said.
The ADC candidate also called for stricter standards for road construction, arguing that some newly constructed roads developed potholes shortly after the rainy season began.
He also promised to protect wetlands from indiscriminate development, suggesting that such areas could be used for parks and solar farms.
The All Progressives Congress candidate, Obafemi Hamzat, however, defended the state’s drainage infrastructure, describing it as extensive and stressing that its effectiveness depended largely on regular maintenance and preventing blockages.
Hamzat, who IS a former commissioner for works and infrastructure, said Lagos faced significant environmental challenges because of its low-lying geography, heavy rainfall and large population. According to him, the priority should be ensuring that water moves freely through drainage channels into the creeks and lagoon.
“Our going forward for us is to make sure that we maintain what we have built. Our climate change is real,” he said.
Hamzat also defended the environmental assessment of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Road project, saying the assessment had been conducted when he was commissioner for works and infrastructure.
He explained that the removal of structures from certain locations was necessary where buildings obstructed floodplains and the natural movement of water.
The PDP candidate, Funsho Doherty, attributed Lagos’s flooding and environmental problems to what he described as years of governance failures, particularly the destruction of wetlands and development on drainage channels.
He said the state’s coastal and low-lying geography required stronger environmental management to prevent residents from being exposed to avoidable flooding risks.
Doherty described wetlands as natural systems that absorb excess water during rainfall, warning that destroying them and attempting to replace their functions with artificial drainage channels would not adequately address the problem.
He also criticised the practice of allowing buildings to spring up on drainage channels before demolishing them years later, arguing that proper planning and enforcement would prevent such situations.
The PDP candidate further faulted the Lagos State Government for what he described as its failure to insist on an environmental impact assessment before construction began on the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Road. Although the project is being undertaken by the Federal Government, he argued that the state government had a responsibility to protect its residents and ensure that environmental concerns were addressed.
Meanwhile, the NDC candidate, Adedeji Doherty, identified drainage as a major concern, calling for the redirection of drainage channels to improve water movement and reduce flooding.
He described flooding as a geographical phenomenon occurring in different parts of the world, arguing that the priority should be how effectively governments manage its effects.
Doherty also called for improved transportation arrangements for elderly and physically challenged residents, saying their transportation needs should be separated from the BRT vehicles operating on dedicated lanes.
Transportation
The ADC governorship candidate, Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, proposed decentralising development across Lagos State and expanding public transportation infrastructure to reduce traffic congestion, saying residents should not have to spend hours commuting to work.
He promised to deliver rail services across the state within two and a half years through partnerships with private investors and infrastructure finance companies, arguing that the project could generate enough revenue to repay its financing over 30 years without burdening the state’s balance sheet.
“Traffic is not a lifestyle, and we should not have to work to get to work,” Rhodes-Vivour said, adding that the state should also develop short bridges connecting different parts of Lagos, expand water transportation, introduce cable cars and establish dedicated bicycle lanes.
He further proposed ferry terminals with adequate parking facilities to enable residents to park their vehicles and continue their journeys by water, while advocating improved inner roads to make movement within local communities easier.
The APC candidate, Obafemi Hamzat, promised to expand the state’s Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) system from 1,000 to 4,000 buses, with a target of transporting one million passengers daily using compressed natural gas-powered vehicles.
Hamzat, who is the incumbent deputy governor, said the plan would also include additional BRT lanes linking Marina with areas such as Epe and Badagry, alongside the integration of road, rail and water transportation through a single payment system using the Cowry Card.
“There is nowhere in Africa, none, that private sector has funded a rail. No, in the whole of Africa,” he said, while defending government-led investment in rail transportation.
He also proposed introducing 77 electric ferries to reduce travel time on waterways, establishing a major ferry terminal at Oworonshoki and completing improvements at 63 traffic junctions, of which he said 42 had already been addressed.
The NDC candidate, Funsho Doherty, criticised the state of public transportation in Lagos, saying existing roads were poorly managed and residents continued to depend on ageing and dilapidated commercial buses.
He argued that the state needed to modernise its public transportation system, describing the continued operation of poorly maintained buses as a major contributor to traffic congestion and disorder on Lagos roads.
“In my opinion, the lack of a modern transportation system in Lagos is not by accident. I think there’s a vested interest in operating the bus system the way we’re operating it, with many small buses chaotically operated,” Doherty said.
He attributed the situation to a lack of political will, alleging that vested interests within the existing transport system had prevented necessary reforms. He promised to modernise public transportation, saying his administration would be accountable to voters rather than what he described as an entrenched transport network.
The PDP candidate, Adedeji Doherty, identified poor roads, traffic congestion around the Apapa port, ageing commercial buses and the activities of transport unions as some of the challenges confronting Lagos’s transportation system.
He said addressing the gridlock would require road rehabilitation across local government areas, improved management of trailer movements and the construction of additional bridges to provide alternative routes for commuters.
“The trailers coming in and going out of Lagos is one issue. NURTW is one issue. The bad roads is one issue. The rickety buses is one issue. The Fourth Mainland Bridge not being built up to date after 10-15 years is a big issue,” he said.
Doherty also proposed additional bridges linking different parts of the state, including routes connecting Kara to Lagos Island and Badagry, as well as Oworonshoki to Epe and Ibeju-Lekki. He said such infrastructure would help divert traffic and reduce congestion in busy parts of Lagos.
Healthcare
The ADC governorship candidate, Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, promised to establish 245 emergency response centres across Lagos State, with each ward having two ambulances to improve access to urgent medical care and reduce deaths caused by delays in reaching hospitals.
He said the centres would also provide wellness services and promote preventive healthcare through medical education, exercise facilities and community-based programmes, particularly for retirees and pensioners.
“Our focus will first be to establish emergency response in every ward in Lagos State. So that’s 245 emergency response centres in Lagos State with two ambulances, because there are too many people that are dying because they are moving from one place to the other, trying to find a hospital, a bed, oxygen,” he said.
Rhodes-Vivour also promised to increase healthcare funding to as close to 15 per cent of the state budget as possible, improve doctors’ salaries, train support staff and introduce artificial intelligence to strengthen medical diagnosis and healthcare delivery.
The APC candidate, Obafemi Hamzat, promised to expand enrolment in the state’s health insurance scheme, Ilera Eko, from its current 1.4 million beneficiaries to one in every three Lagos residents to reduce the financial burden of accessing medical care.
He also outlined plans to expand general hospitals, upgrade primary healthcare centres and increase the number of medical professionals, including through the establishment of a new university of medicine.
“Ilera Eko currently has 1.4 million people on it. We must push it to one in every three people in Lagos. That allows you to make sure that when illness comes, you don’t get ruined,” Hamzat said.
He said the state was developing new 150-bed facilities, including Massey Children’s Hospital and another general hospital, while promising to increase bed capacity at nine general hospitals by 50 per cent. He also pledged to upgrade about 150 primary healthcare centres to 24-hour flagship facilities and expand medical training to produce up to 1,000 doctors.
The NDC candidate, Funsho Doherty, called for increased government spending on healthcare and education, proposing that their combined allocation should rise from about 15 per cent of the state budget to 28 per cent during his first term.
He also promised fully free maternal and child healthcare, including consultations, medical tests and drugs, arguing that the cost of obtaining medicines and carrying out tests outside public hospitals prevented many low-income residents from accessing treatment.
“We’ve also said that maternal and child care for us, free, not nominally, but fully free, inclusive of drugs,” Doherty said.
He argued that health insurance schemes alone would not adequately address the needs of poor residents without direct government funding for medical care, saying the administration should begin with free maternal and child healthcare before gradually expanding the programme.
The PDP candidate, Adedeji Doherty, promised to strengthen the healthcare system by addressing shortages of doctors, nurses, hospital beds, medicines and other essential medical supplies.
He said Lagos needed more medical personnel and better-equipped hospitals to meet the healthcare demands of its growing population, while also identifying primary healthcare centres and pharmacies as important parts of the system.
“We have to work on the doctors. Those doctors, we need to train more doctors and more nurses because we are a growing state,” he said.
Doherty also proposed supporting local industries involved in producing medical equipment, hospital beds and pharmaceutical products, saying the government would reduce charges imposed on such businesses to encourage local production and improve the availability of essential medicines.

items.author: Daily Trust
items.content:
The Adamawa State Poverty Alleviation and Wealth Creation Agency (PAWECA) has commenced a statewide needs assessment exercise for its Technical Skills Acquisition Programme across the 21 Local Government Areas of the state.
The initiative, introduced under the administration of Governor Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri, is aimed at tackling unemployment, reducing poverty and equipping young people with practical vocational and entrepreneurial skills to promote economic self-reliance.
The exercise is designed to assess successful candidates and match their interests, abilities and career aspirations with appropriate vocational training programmes.
Speaking on the implementation of the initiative, PAWECA Director-General, Dr. Michael Zira, reaffirmed the agency’s commitment to ensuring that beneficiaries receive relevant, market-driven skills capable of improving their livelihoods and creating sustainable employment opportunities.
As part of efforts to ensure effective implementation, Dr. Zira visited the Jimeta training centre, where he inspected the ongoing assessment exercise and interacted with candidates and officials.
During the visit, he monitored the assessment process and emphasised the importance of proper coordination, transparency and effective placement of beneficiaries into suitable training programmes.
The initiative covers a broad range of technical and vocational fields, including Artificial Intelligence, Renewable Energy, Mechanical Engineering, Tailoring and other specialised trades designed to respond to emerging economic opportunities.
The programme is expected to provide thousands of Adamawa residents with opportunities to acquire practical skills, establish businesses, improve their earning capacity and contribute meaningfully to the state’s economic development.
The statewide exercise forms part of the Fintiri administration’s broader commitment to human capital development, youth empowerment, entrepreneurship and sustainable wealth creation.
With assessment activities taking place across all 21 LGAs, PAWECA aims to ensure wider access to skills development opportunities, particularly for young people seeking alternatives to unemployment and economic dependence.

Michael Carrick said he expects to “move forward and keep working” as Manchester United manager despite dropping into the Premier League relegation zone.
United twice came from two goals down to salvage a remarkable 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday.
Goals in stoppage time from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu rescued a point and potentially gave Carrick a stay of execution ahead of a two-week international break.
“We haven’t won enough games, but I expect to move forward and keep working on the things that we’ve been working on,” Carrick told Sky Sports.
“Showing a lot of the good (things) in the game today, tighten up on a few mistakes and win football matches.”
Results this weekend dropped United into the bottom three after August for the first time in 40 years.
“We’re in November,” added Carrick. “I don’t like the situation where we are, I don’t like the results that we’ve had, but we can definitely do something about it.”
The former United midfielder dismissed any suggestion he could resign if it was in the best interests of the club and said he would not seek out discussions with his superiors on where his future lies.
“That’s not going to happen,” said Carrick when asked if he would resign.
“I’m quite clear what direction the club needs to go in, and we’ve just got to win games.”
The 45-year-old added: “I’m pretty clear where we need to go and how we need to get there… as a normal international week is, we’ll have some training, we’ll have one or two days off, not too much, but we’ll train and get ready for the next game.”
United travel to rivals Liverpool when they are next in action on November 22.

items.content:
Adamawa State has received national recognition for its contributions to cooperative development following the presentation of a Recognition Award to the state chapter of the Institute of Cooperative Professionals of Nigeria (ICOPRON) at the institute’s 2026 National Conference in Lagos.
The award, presented during the five-day conference held from November 2 to 6, 2026, at ASSBIFI Hall, Ikeja, Lagos, acknowledged the Adamawa State Chapter’s efforts in promoting and strengthening cooperative institutions across the state.
The Adamawa State delegation to the conference was led by the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Entrepreneurship Development, Dr. Yusufu Peter Adilbakirya.
The conference, themed “Strengthening Nigerian Cooperatives for Economic Resilience, Financial Inclusion and National Development: The Role of Stakeholders,” brought together government officials, cooperative professionals and other stakeholders to explore strategies for improving cooperative administration and strengthening the sector’s contribution to national economic development.
Deliberations centred on professionalism, digitalisation, effective management, good governance and the adoption of international best practices to enhance the efficiency, transparency and sustainability of cooperative societies.
Addressing participants, the Minister of State for Agriculture and Food Security underscored the critical role of cooperative societies in agricultural development, economic empowerment, financial inclusion and food security.
Participants also stressed the importance of transparent leadership, sound institutional management and digital innovation in improving accountability and service delivery within the cooperative sector.
The presentation of the Recognition Award to the Adamawa State Chapter was among the highlights of the conference, drawing attention to the state’s efforts towards strengthening cooperative development.
The recognition further highlights the growing importance of cooperative institutions in promoting entrepreneurship, creating employment opportunities, expanding access to finance and supporting sustainable economic growth in Adamawa State.
The conference also provided an opportunity for participating states to exchange experiences, share best practices and explore innovative approaches to cooperative management and development.
Adamawa State’s participation is expected to strengthen ongoing efforts to build a more inclusive, professionally managed and sustainable cooperative sector capable of supporting economic empowerment and improving livelihoods across the state.

items.content:
A former chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kwara State, Saheed Popoola, has admitted that he played a leading role in the political campaign linking former Senate President Bukola Saraki to the 2018 Offa bank robbery.
He said the allegations were used to settle political scores.
Popoola, who is now the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) senatorial candidate for Kwara South, said he regretted joining forces with the APC during the O To Ge movement, which culminated in the removal of Saraki’s political structure from power in the state in 2019.
He made the disclosure at the palace of the Olofa of Offa during Saraki’s political tour of Kwara South on Sunday.
Popoola acknowledged that some of those who campaigned against the former governor deliberately associated him with the robbery for political reasons.
The robbery, which claimed more than 25 lives, including policemen, had become a major political issue in Kwara.
The state government is prosecuting Saraki over alleged sponsorship of the attack, an allegation he has denied.
Popoola, who was among the prominent figures in the APC-led O To Ge struggle, said their opposition to Saraki had been driven by political interests and misinformation rather than the facts surrounding the robbery.
“I was a leading member of the APC then that started the politicisation and revival of the issue of Offa robbery just to get to Saraki. But after we finished and won, it was me that was being persecuted.”
“This includes the use of songs and slogans to associate Saraki with the incident just because of politics. However, God has intervened and the reality is that Saraki is back in Kwara”, he said.
Popoola also challenged those outside Offa who continued to politicise the tragedy to demonstrate genuine concern for the victims and their families.
He alleged that many of them had neither reached out to the affected families nor offered meaningful support since the incident.
Dismissing suggestions that Saraki could have been motivated by financial considerations to sponsor the robbery, he declared: “All the money in the entire banks in Offa, Ilorin, Patigi and the entire Kwara state put together is not enough for Saraki to spend in three days.”
He said the former Senate President’s return to Offa was not merely about political calculations but also reflected his concern for the people.
Saraki, in his remarks, recalled his role in the emergence of the Olofa, Oba Mufutau Gbadamosi Esuwoye II, in 2010.
He said he stood by the traditional ruler’s selection despite petitions and opposition from some quarters.
He said his support for the monarch was based on his acceptance of the community’s preference, adding that the history of Offa and the traditional ruler’s reign would be incomplete without acknowledging his role.
“I recall 2010 when the chiefs and kingmakers decided they wanted you. I accepted you as the preferred candidate against petitions and complaints from many quarters,” Saraki said.
“Some people attempted to influence me into rejecting you, but I refused. I stood my ground. Now is the time I seek your support.”
The former Senate President appealed to the monarch and the people of Offa to support the PDP in the 2027 general elections, assuring them that the party would not disappoint the community.

items.content:
By Golok Nanmwa, Jos
Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples’ Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has said Nigeria needs a fundamental reset rather than mere reforms to address its economic, security and governance challenges ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Makinde spoke on Sunday during a live political programme on Jay FM 101.9 in Jos, Plateau State, ahead of the party’s presidential campaign flag-off scheduled for Monday in the city.
Explaining his position, the governor argued that reforms were insufficient where the problems in a system outweighed its strengths.
“When you talk about reform, it means that there is something good in the system that you want to improve upon. But when the bad outweighs the good, you need to take a different course of action.
“If what you have in the system is only about 20 per cent of what you expected, you don’t need to continue tweaking it. You need to press the reset button, shut it down and reboot it. That is what Nigeria needs at this point. Reform will not work in the present environment,” he said.
The governor said he did not initially intend to become a politician but was motivated by concerns about the country’s future.
“I am not a career politician. I came into politics because I believe that the future of millions of Nigerians is at stake. We have the potential to become the greatest Black nation on the face of the earth, but we must make the right decisions to achieve that destiny,” he said.
On the economy, Makinde identified it as the foremost priority of his proposed Reset Agenda, arguing that economic performance should be measured by improvements in the living conditions of ordinary Nigerians.
“The economy must work for everybody. We should not just be talking about foreign reserves, World Bank figures or inflation statistics. What matters is whether ordinary Nigerians can afford to feed themselves and meet their basic needs,” he said.
He added that economic progress should be assessed by its impact on households rather than statistical indicators alone.
“If the people on the streets are not feeling any improvement, then we cannot say that the economy is doing well. The real test of economic performance is the condition of the people,” he said.
The APM candidate said his proposed administration would prioritise skills acquisition, entrepreneurship, education and production, while creating an enabling environment for businesses to grow and generate employment.
“We must encourage our people to acquire skills and become entrepreneurs. We must invest in education and move towards intensive production. Government must provide an environment where businesses can thrive and young people can find meaningful employment,” he said.
On insecurity, Makinde advocated decentralising Nigeria’s security architecture through the establishment of state police, arguing that states should be allowed to adopt the arrangement when they are ready and necessary safeguards are in place.
“I believe that we need to decentralise our security architecture. State police is one of the ways to achieve this, but it must be properly structured. States that are ready should be allowed to establish their own police formations, while others can come on board when they are prepared,” he said.
Recalling his engagement with former President Muhammadu Buhari on the issue in 2019, Makinde said the former president had expressed concerns about the ability of some states to finance their own police formations.
“When we approached President Buhari in 2019, one of the concerns he raised was that some states could not even pay workers’ salaries. He questioned how such states would be able to fund state police,” he said.
He explained that governors in the South-West subsequently adopted the Western Nigeria Security Network, popularly known as Amotekun, as an alternative arrangement to strengthen security in the region.
“We decided to find a middle ground through Amotekun. The operatives gather intelligence and work with the federal security agencies. It has helped to improve security coordination in the region,” he said.
Makinde acknowledged concerns that state police could be abused by governors to intimidate political opponents and ordinary citizens but insisted that appropriate safeguards could address such risks.
“We must not pretend that there are no concerns. Some people are worried that governors could use state police to oppress their opponents or intimidate citizens. Those concerns are valid, and we must put safeguards in place.
“But the fact that something can be abused does not mean we should not do it. We must design a system that ensures accountability and protects the rights of the people,” he said.
On Nigeria’s growing population, the governor warned that failure to provide opportunities for young people could worsen insecurity and social instability.
He said the country could have a population of more than 300 million, with over 70 per cent below the age of 34, stressing the need to create opportunities for the youthful population.
“If we fail to provide pathways for them to succeed, we should not be surprised when some of them turn to crime or other activities that threaten the stability of the country,” he said.
Makinde also cited Nigeria’s gradual transition to self-government and independence as an example of how different parts of the country could adopt new arrangements at different times.
“We had self-government in 1957 and independence in 1960. We did not achieve everything at once. In the same way, states do not necessarily have to establish state police at the same time. Those that are ready can begin, provided the necessary safeguards are in place,” he said.
Recalling his handling of the COVID-19 lockdown in Oyo State in 2020, the governor said he opposed a blanket shutdown because of the hardship it could impose on residents who depended on daily earnings for survival.
“I remember that during COVID-19, there was a proposal for a mandatory lockdown. I raised the concern that many people depended on what they earned each day to feed their families. If you locked them down completely, what would they eat that night or the following morning?” he said.
He maintained that decisions on public health and governance should be guided by science, data and logic, while taking into account the realities of ordinary citizens.
“We had to look at the situation and make decisions based on science, data and logic. We also had to understand the realities of our people. Some people were more worried about dying of hunger than the risk of contracting COVID-19,” he said.
On education, Makinde praised the legacy of the late nationalist and statesman, Chief Obafemi Awolowo, particularly his free education policy, which he said expanded opportunities for generations of Nigerians.
“Chief Awolowo understood that education was an investment in the future. The cocoa farmers paid their taxes, and the government used the resources to provide free education for children.
“Those children grew up, became professionals and contributed to society. That is the kind of investment we must make in our people,” he said.
The governor said his proposed administration would also prioritise honesty, transparency and accountability in the management of public resources.
“The first thing I will do is to tell Nigerians the truth about the state of the country. People deserve to know where we are and what needs to be done.
“The next thing is accountability. If you have accountability, then the chances are that public resources will be used for the benefit of the people,” he said.
