items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Environmental groups worldwide are using artificial intelligence to analyze climate data, track forest fires and count endangered wildlife – embracing a technology they also warn is driving a surge in electricity demand, water use and greenhouse-gas emissions.
The contradiction is forcing these organizations to justify their AI use in carrying ​out missions to combat climate change or protect natural resources.
"We recognize that AI can come with environmental costs, and we need to be thoughtful about how we use it," said Ali Swanson, AI lead at the US ‌nonprofit Conservation International. "But at a time when the climate and biodiversity crises are becoming more urgent, AI can help us move faster and make better use of the information we're collecting."
The group recently started using AI to assess hotspots detected by satellites and send real-time alerts to community forest patrols about potential wildfires in remote and environmentally sensitive parts of Cambodia.
Reuters interviewed 15 major environmental, conservation and development organizations about their AI use. All said they used the technology in some form and expressed concern about the environmental impact of the data centers powering it. The centers, filled with servers, can require vast amounts of ​electricity, along with water for cooling.
It's a global dilemma for individuals, governments and industries balancing AI's benefits with its enormous risks. The tradeoffs likely will grab attention at the UN's COP31 climate conference this month, when host Turkey will call on ​governments, businesses and other institutions to sign a pledge outlining principles to ensure AI is developed and deployed sustainably.
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres wants major AI companies to publicly disclose their systems' environmental impacts.
Researchers ⁠at the United Nations University Institute for Water, Environment and Health estimate the global data-center footprint could more than double by 2030, reaching a size about twice that of Jakarta, the Indonesian megalopolis.
The International Energy Agency, meanwhile, estimates global data centers will consume about ​945 terawatt-hours of electricity annually by 2030, producing the equivalent of more than 300 million metric tons of carbon dioxide. That's double current consumption and about equal to Japan's annual electricity use.
The agency also projects that global data center water consumption will increase from about 560 ​billion liters (147.9 billion gallons) in 2023 to about 1.2 trillion liters (317 billion gallons) annually by 2030.
Technology giants including Microsoft Amazon and Alphabet's Google have reported rising emissions linked in part to data center expansion, raising questions about their ability to meet their own long-term climate goals.
Amazon told Reuters its artificial-intelligence products were among the most sustainable due to the company's purchases of low-carbon energy and its efforts to use power and water efficiently.
Microsoft and Google didn't respond to requests for comment.
Breakthrough once thought impossible
Many of the organizations that spoke to Reuters believe AI's benefits currently outweigh its costs because the technology is enabling work ​that was previously difficult, expensive or impossible.
Kenya's Save the Elephants, a partner of the Wildlife Conservation Network, said it is using machine learning to improve population surveys and study elephant communication.
Frank Pope, the group's chief executive, said an aerial survey of Kenya's largest protected area ​last year generated roughly 200,000 images that took nine people nine months to review manually. AI models trained on Nvidia's GeForce graphics platforms can now complete similar analyses in hours.
"The results have been eye-opening," Pope said. "We found that human surveys were missing about a third of the elephants, roughly ‌half of zebras ⁠and giraffes, and three-quarters of oryx populations."
More accurate wildlife data can help secure financing for conservation, he said.
"Ultimately, these tools make nature measurable and therefore investable," he said. "That's a critical transformation, if we're going to conserve biodiversity at scale."
At the institute founded by the late conservation icon Jane Goodall, researchers are using AI to digitize decades of field notes about chimpanzee behavior in Tanzania's Gombe National Park.
The project was once expected to take 13-15 years because the records were written by hand using the local Kiha language and scientific shorthand.
Thanks to a tool developed with Amazon Web Services, the notes can now be scanned, translated and structured in minutes, slashing the time needed to about two years, said Lilian Pintea, the Jane Goodall Institute's vice president of conservation science.
During her lifetime, Pintea said, Goodall supported the use of ​AI to advance conservation science, provided people remained firmly in control ​of how it was used.
"AI technology should be seen as ⁠tools which are human-centered," Pintea said.
Limiting the environmental impact
Some organizations are experimenting with ways to limit the environmental impact of their AI use.
The World Resources Institute (WRI), a research group that uses AI to accelerate its climate and environmental analyses, said it limits resource-intensive applications such as generating videos and images, while caching AI query results so identical searches don't need to be reprocessed.
Read More: Trump declares full support for ‘super intelligence’
The US-based Nature Conservancy has adopted ​a similar approach. It uses AI to analyze video captured on commercial fishing vessels for information on how many fish of different species they catch. But instead of uploading huge numbers of ​videos to centralized data centers, it has ⁠installed AI-powered digital cameras to process information aboard the vessels, reducing energy use and data-transfer requirements, said Vienna Saccomanno, a senior scientist at the organization.
"It takes a lot of engineering to make computation on the edge possible," she said. "This was worth it to reduce both our carbon footprint and deliver these sustainability insights."
Greenpeace International said it, too, uses some AI tools, mainly because software platforms it relies upon include AI features.
It's imposing internal guidelines emphasizing transparency, human oversight and "intentional" AI use, the group said. But it would prefer to sidestep the technology due to its environmental ⁠impacts and is pushing ​back hard on the data center buildout.
"While other organizations are asking how to use AI responsibly, Greenpeace is asking whether it's necessary to build all these ​massive data centers in the first place," said Katrin Xueying Wu, a climate and energy campaigner with the organization.
Other groups now see AI as vital to effective environmental activism.
"It's our job to save the planet. If we can do that more effectively and efficiently with the limited resources we've got by using AI, then we have ​to seriously engage in that possibility," said Stuart Butchart, chief scientist at UK-based BirdLife International.
"If we don't do it, then we're sort of being derelict in our duty."

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Benjamin Netanyahu's main rival secured nods on Thursday from a majority of ‌lawmakers to try to form a government, but Israel's president said it was still unclear who could break the election deadlock as he pledged to nominate a candidate on Sunday.
Israel's October 27 national ballot ended with no clear winner. Neither Prime Minister Netanyahu nor Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief, secured a clear path to a majority in parliament.
That has ​set up a tough task for President Isaac Herzog, whose mostly ceremonial role comes with the post-election responsibility of picking a candidate he believes ​has the best chance to form a coalition in a deeply divided country.
Read: Israeli president receives official election results as committee rejects fraud allegations
Herzog held marathon talks with elected factions ⁠on Wednesday and Thursday, during which 67 of parliament's 120 elected lawmakers endorsed Eisenkot, while 46 endorsed Netanyahu.
Eisenkot secures 67 endorsements to Netanyahu's 46, paving way to form gov't https://t.co/pg7cwHjKl5
— Haaretz.com (@haaretzcom) November 5, 2026
In televised remarks at the end of the ​talks, Herzog said that while the "results of the consultations may appear clear", there were "mutual vetoes between the blocs and within the blocs themselves" that make it ​difficult to say who has the best shot at forming a government.
Herzog said he would make a pick on Sunday, and that he would hold "personal talks with some of the party leaders" over the Israeli weekend, which runs Friday-Saturday.
🇮🇱 #Israeli President Isaac Herzog said he will announce on Sunday, November 8, whom he will task with trying to form a new government, following post-election talks with all party leaders.
46 parliament members recommended Prime Minister Benjamin #Netanyahu, while 67 backed… pic.twitter.com/576KGAK9rZ
— FRANCE 24 English (@France24_en) November 6, 2026
Candidate would have up to 42 days to try to form a government
Once nominated by Herzog, the candidate will have 28 ​days to try to forge a government, with a possible 14-day extension.
Netanyahu will remain prime minister in a caretaker government until a new coalition is ​formed, or through another election which must be held if no candidate succeeds.
Netanyahu's Likud won the most seats of any single party with 27 in the 120-seat Knesset, ‌but Netanyahu's ⁠wider religious-nationalist coalition garnered only 53 in total.
That was still better than Eisenkot's anti-Netanyahu coalition spanning four centre-left to right-wing Jewish-led parties, which won just 48 seats despite pre-election polls pointing to a close race. Two parties representing Israel's Arab minority won an unprecedented 19 seats.
In a setback for the prime minister on Thursday, United Torah Judaism, one of two major parties representing ultra-Orthodox Jewish voters and a longstanding Netanyahu coalition ally, declined to recommend any candidate to form ​a government during talks with Herzog.
Read More: Israeli opposition leaders say Netanyahu cannot remain in power after US midterm elections
And while ​Eisenkot, like Netanyahu, has so ⁠far ruled out forming a government with Israel's two Arab-led parties, both factions endorsed Eisenkot, giving him backing from a comfortable majority of lawmakers.
Critics accuse Netanyahu of trying to undermine election results
Netanyahu, at risk of losing power, has seized ​on an investigation by election officials into possible vote tampering to cast doubt on the results, accusing Arab-led ​parties of stealing the ⁠vote. Critics accuse Netanyahu and his partners of trying to undermine the results, which he denies.
Israel's Central Election Committee said on Wednesday that the election's integrity had not been compromised. The head of the committee, Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, has called on Israel's elected officials to protect public trust, rather than shake it.
Israel’s Central Elections Committee says it reviewed all party complaints and found no evidence of election irregularities. pic.twitter.com/B0q5kgpBHZ
— Clash Report (@clashreport) November 4, 2026
"This ⁠is a ​real danger. One of the foundations of democracy is the peaceful transfer of power," Sohlberg ​told Herzog at his residence on Wednesday. High voter turnout, including among the Arab minority, was a blessing, he said.
Netanyahu's allies on the far-right, including National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, have called ​for the immediate arrest and interrogation of Arab party leaders.

items.author: Pop Culture & Art
items.content:
Godzilla Minus Zero is heading towards a strong opening weekend at the North American box office, with the Japanese monster sequel expected to outperform new releases including Warner Bros.’ animated adaptation of The Cat in the Hat.
Directed by Takashi Yamazaki, Godzilla Minus Zero is projected to earn approximately $30 million from 3,254 theatres across the US and Canada during its opening weekend. The film is expected to secure the top position, marking another significant theatrical success for the Japanese franchise.
The sequel follows the success of 2023’s Godzilla Minus One, which earned $11.4 million during its North American opening weekend before eventually collecting approximately $57 million domestically. The previous instalment also received widespread critical acclaim and won the Academy Award for Best Visual Effects.
The new film is benefiting from strong audience interest, positive early reactions and its availability on IMAX and other premium large-format screens. Its projected opening could also make it the biggest North American debut for distributor GKIDS.
Meanwhile, The Cat in the Hat is expected to finish in second place with an estimated $20 million to $25 million from approximately 4,000 theatres. The animated film features Bill Hader voicing the iconic Dr Seuss character, with Warner Bros. hoping to attract family audiences during the November release period.
However, early tracking has suggested a more modest opening for the animated adaptation than initially anticipated. Its performance will be closely watched as Warner Bros. introduces a new interpretation of the familiar children's character.
Another newcomer, Wild Horse Nine, directed by Martin McDonagh and starring Sam Rockwell and John Malkovich, is targeting between $4 million and $7 million from around 1,000 theatres.
The weekend's box office competition also includes returning titles such as Clayface and You Can See Everything, which are expected to experience declines as the new releases enter cinemas.
Although the projections remain subject to change as weekend ticket sales come in, Godzilla Minus Zero is currently positioned to lead the North American box office, continuing the franchise's impressive theatrical momentum following the success of Godzilla Minus One.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has moved to tighten control over the State Department, telling senior ​officials that staff must stay in their lanes and avoid actions that present conflicts of interest, four people familiar with the matter said.
Rubio's message, delivered in a meeting last ‌week before the Republican Party's electoral losses on Tuesday, comes as its leading figures attempt to put distance between themselves and an increasingly unpopular Trump administration.
The meeting followed the high-profile resignation of US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle in mid-October after news reports raised concerns that she sold access to Trump administration officials in exchange for money, gifts and favours.
Guilfoyle has called the reports false and, in a post on social media, said she would defend her reputation.
Rubio told the meeting, which included ​many of the roughly two dozen assistant secretaries of state, that unethical behaviour would result in a firing, regardless of how well-connected an official might be, said one of the people.
He added ​that too many officials were making decisions or pushing policy agendas without coordinating and that significant decisions required his sign-off or that of Deputy Secretary of ⁠State Christopher Landau, according to the people, who spoke on the condition of anonymity. Details of the meeting have not previously been reported.
The State Department declined to comment on the meeting.
Soon after the meeting, three ​of the people said the State Department's policy chief, Jeremy Lewin, was forced out of his job in part due to concerns that he was working on matters outside his area without proper coordination. The exact ​details of those concerns remain unclear.
None of the people who spoke to Reuters suggested Lewin’s departure was linked to any incidents of ethical misconduct. Lewin joined the government as part of Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency and helped dismantle the US Agency for International Development, which oversaw US foreign assistance.
Rubio and others within the State Department leadership were frustrated with his "freelancing" and going against "certain directives from the secretary", one of the people said, without providing specific examples.
Lewin, who was appointed to ​his senior role just over two months ago, said on social media last month that he had stepped down from his role to return to the private sector.
Asked for comment, a State Department official said: "It ​was mutually agreed it was time [for Lewin] to move on."
Lewin said in a statement to Reuters that his departure was planned several weeks before it was announced and he denied he was fired.
Read More: Trump makes hardliner Stephen Miller his chief of staff after midterm defeat
"The suggestion that I was fired is ‌false. As ⁠planned for weeks with the Secretary and his team, after staying longer than expected to finish key projects, I resigned my position prior to the midterms to assume a private sector role and plan my wedding," he said.
"It had nothing to do with any meeting or policy regarding the management of the department."
Rubio's frustrations also included excessive overseas travel by political staff, which has led to a requirement that Rubio's office approve all political travel, according to another one of the people.
Republicans look beyond midterm losses
The 2028 presidential race began shifting into gear almost immediately after Tuesday's midterm elections delivered control of Congress to the Democrats. Vice President JD ​Vance and Republican Senator Ted Cruz offered post-mortems on ​X that many strategists saw as political ⁠vision statements as the campaign season begins.
Rubio himself has sought to play down reports that he is considering a run, but he has also not publicly ruled it out. If he does, his management of the State Department could emerge as a topic of conversation on the campaign trail.
President Donald Trump's administration has faced ​consistent accusations of self-dealing and Democrats have said they will put dealings between Trump aides and foreign officials under the microscope when they take control ​of Congress in January and ⁠begin launching official investigations.
The Trump administration has denied allegations of self-dealing.
Shortly after Guilfoyle left the administration in October, Rubio sent a department-wide memo reminding diplomats to "avoid conflicts of interest", according to multiple media outlets.
He subsequently denied that the memo was sent as a result of Guilfoyle's departure, telling reporters that he had in fact meant to send it weeks earlier, but that it had been held up for bureaucratic reasons.
Like other parts of the Trump administration, Rubio's ⁠department has lost ​officials recently.
In October, US Special Representative for Global Partnerships Paolo Zampolli was fired after Politico reported an email thread between him ​and Landau, in which Landau accused Zampolli of working outside his "lane" of cultural diplomacy, saying Zampolli kept wanting to work on issues outside his remit in contravention of Landau's orders.
Reuters could not determine what those issues were.
Shortly after his departure, Zampolli wrote on X ​that special envoy appointments last one year by statute and that Trump had extended his appointment by more than six months.

items.author: Yasir Ali
items.content:
The Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Saturday removed all writ petitions challenging the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), as well as arrests made under the Maintenance of Public Order (3-MPO) ordinances, from its cause list.
A day earlier, the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) stripped PHC of jurisdiction over post-Oct 12 K-P cases, including cases related to emergency and governor’s rule. Before that, on November 5, it barred the PHC from hearing cases concerning arrests under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance.
The directions came after the PHC granted bail to 23 Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) workers arrested under Section 3 of the MPO Ordinance. The court also sought replies from the governor and the speaker against the governor’s rule in the province.
The petitions removed from the cause list include those seeking the recovery of K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, Provincial Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati and PTI provincial president Junaid Akbar.
Several high-profile petitions challenging the emergency and governor’s rule were pending before the PHC. These included pleas filed by PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, National Assembly Opposition Leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai, the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Bar Council, National Democratic Movement Chairman Mohsin Dawar and Member of the National Assembly Shandana Gulzar.
Read: Gohar demands immediate implementation of SC order on Imran's medical treatment
The PHC’s Administrative Committee issued a formal notification in compliance with the FCC’s orders, directing that no writ petitions filed on or after October 12 be fixed for hearing. It also ordered that petitions filed under Article 199 of the Constitution be returned to the petitioners.
The committee advised the petitioners to approach the appropriate forum for relief.
The latest development effectively halts judicial scrutiny of the extraordinary measures at the provincial high court level, leaving petitioners to seek relief before forums designated by the FCC.
K-P governor's rule and emergency
On October 11, President Asif Ali Zardari approved Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s advice to impose an emergency and governor’s rule in the province under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, citing a deterioration in the security situation, an increase in terrorist attacks, and what it described as the provincial administration’s failure to cooperate effectively in counter-terrorism efforts.
Under the new arrangement, executive powers were transferred to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, assisted by an advisory council, while emergency measures were imposed in 12 districts. The PTI rejected the federal government’s position and opposed the move.
The decision followed weeks of tensions between the Centre and the PTI-led provincial administration, alongside negotiations aimed at securing agreement on a joint strategy against terrorism.
The measures resulted in the removal of Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and his cabinet from office, with executive authority transferred to the governor.
The decision followed weeks of escalating confrontation over counterterrorism policy, the PTI’s planned long march to Islamabad and the province’s deteriorating security situation. The federal government had repeatedly warned that governor’s rule or an emergency could be imposed, accusing the provincial administration of failing to cooperate adequately with the Centre on counterterrorism.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Xiaomi appears to be preparing to launch its standard Xiaomi 18 smartphone in China next month. The device has reportedly appeared on China’s 3C certification platform, revealing support for 100W fast charging ahead of its expected launch.
The certification listing went live on November 6, 2026, under model number M261DB. According to reports, this model belongs to the standard Xiaomi 18. However, the certification does not mention the phone’s name or confirm its launch date. Xiaomi has also not officially announced the device.
Xiaomi 18 with 100W Fast Charging Gets 3C Certification Ahead of Launch
The latest certification suggests that Xiaomi is moving closer to introducing the standard Xiaomi 18. The company launched the Xiaomi 18 Pro series on September 23 but did not introduce the regular model at the event.
Xiaomi Group President Lu Weibing previously confirmed that the standard Xiaomi 18 would arrive separately at a later date. Earlier, tipster Digital Chat Station also suggested a December launch timeline for the device.
The recent 3C certification adds weight to these reports, although Xiaomi has yet to confirm the schedule.
Expected Xiaomi 18 Specifications
Several specifications of the standard Xiaomi 18 have already surfaced through leaks. The smartphone is expected to feature Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 processor, a 200MP camera sensor and a 7,200mAh battery.
If these details prove accurate, the standard model could offer a larger battery than the Xiaomi 18 Pro, which reportedly packs a 7,000mAh battery.
The reported 100W fast charging support could also make the device an attractive option for users who want faster charging and longer battery life.
However, Xiaomi has not confirmed any of these specifications apart from the details revealed through the certification listing.
See Also: Xiaomi Reportedly Developing a Wide-Screen Candybar Smartphone
Global Launch Details Remain Unclear
Xiaomi has confirmed plans to bring the Xiaomi 18 Pro series to global markets this year. However, the company has not shared any information about the international availability of the standard Xiaomi 18.
For now, the device is expected to make its debut in China in December 2026. More details about its specifications, pricing, and availability should emerge as the launch approaches.

items.content:
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Saturday issued a notice to Information Minister Attaullah Tarar for allegedly violating the code of conduct during the by-election in NA-77 Gujranwala.
According to a press release issued by the office of the Punjab Provincial Election Commissioner, the district monitoring officer issued the notice after Tarar participated in the election campaign of Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) candidate Rashid Bashir Warraich.
The press release said: "The Election Commission of Pakistan has taken notice of an alleged violation of the code of conduct by Federal Minister Attaullah Tarar during the by-election for NA-77 Gujranwala. According to media reports, the federal minister toured the constituency by helicopter and attended a gathering."
Read: ECP sets Nov 8 for by-polls at NA-77 Gujranwala
The notice stated that the participation of federal ministers in election campaigns violated paragraphs 18 and 41 of the ECP's code of conduct.
پریس ریلیز
7 نومبر 2026
الیکشن کمیشن آف پاکستان نے این اے 77 گوجرانوالہ کے ضمنی انتخاب کے دوران وفاقی وزیر عطا اللہ تارڑ کی جانب سے ضابطۂ اخلاق کی مبینہ خلاف ورزی کا نوٹس لے لیا ہے۔ میڈیا رپورٹس کے مطابق وفاقی وزیر نے ہیلی کاپٹر کے ذریعے حلقے کا دورہ کیا (1/2)

It also cited Section 182 of the Elections Act 2017, pertaining to participation in election campaigns during the prohibited period.
Tarar has been summoned to appear before the district monitoring officer at 11am on November 8 to explain his position.
The notice further stated: "The commission has sought a report from the district monitoring officer and the district returning officer to investigate the matter. The federal minister has been directed to appear before the commission in a personal capacity. The constituency’s result may be withheld until a final decision is made in the matter."
اور ایک اجتماع میں شرکت کی۔کمیشن نے اس معاملے کی انکوائری کے لیے ڈسٹرکٹ مانیٹرنگ آفیسر اور ڈسٹرکٹ ریٹرننگ آفیسر سے رپورٹ طلب کر لی ہے۔ وفاقی وزیر کو ذاتی حیثیت میں کمیشن کے سامنے پیش ہونے کی ہدایت کی گئی ہے۔ معاملے کے حتمی فیصلے تک حلقے کا نتیجہ روکا جا سکتا ہے۔
ترجمان(2/2)
— Election Commission of Pakistan (OFFICIAL)🇵🇰 (@ECP_Pakistan) November 7, 2026
Meanwhile, the ECP also issued a notice to PML-N candidate Rashid Bashir Warraich for allegedly violating the code of conduct ahead of the NA-77 Gujranwala by-election.
Warraich has been accused of violating the code of conduct by inviting Tarar to the constituency to participate in his election campaign and has further been directed to appear before the district monitoring officer at 11am on November 8 and submit an explanation.
The notice issued to Warraich warned that one-sided proceedings would be initiated if he failed to appear and that compliance with the code of conduct would be ensured at all costs during the by-election.
By-elections will be held in National Assembly constituency NA-77 (Gujranwala-I) and Punjab Assembly constituency PP-203 (Sahiwal-VI), both of which fell vacant after the deaths of their respective PML-N lawmakers.
Read More: Army, Rangers to assist in security during Punjab by-polls
NA-77 fell vacant following the death of five-time MNA Chaudhry Mehmood Bashir Virk on September 11 after a prolonged illness. His son, Rashid Basheer Virk, is among the candidates contesting the by-election.
Similarly, PP-203 fell vacant following the death of PML-N MPA Chaudhry Muhammad Hanif Jutt on September 17, reportedly from cardiac arrest.
Hanif Jutt had won the seat in a by-election held in November 2025 after the constituency's original winner, PTI-backed independent Rai Murtaza Iqbal, was disqualified following his conviction by an Anti-Terrorism Court.
The upcoming by-election will therefore be the second electoral contest for PP-203 since the 2024 general elections. PML-N candidate Muhammad Asad Hanif Jutt is among the contenders for the vacant seat.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Late in his blitz to salvage Republicans' midterm fortunes, Vice President JD Vance shifted strategy. He talked less about President Donald Trump and more about the issues that define his own political identity.
Vance argued the case ​for Republicans, who lost control of Congress in Tuesday’s vote, almost exclusively through the lens of his policy portfolio, according to a Reuters review of half a dozen speeches since the ‌Republican convention in September.
He bypassed Trump's signature policies, including the Iran war and deportations, as polls showed the president's sagging popularity dragging down Republican office-seekers.
The change was deliberate, according to two people familiar with the strategy. Vance and his advisers saw the issues he championed — economic nationalism, foreign policy restraint, and public safety — as politically potent subjects he could address with authority. While Trump embraced them as part of his MAGA movement, Vance had emerged as their lead crusader, the people said.
The shift offered an early glimpse of ​how the 42-year-old vice president could chart his own course as Republicans begin looking beyond Trump.
Vance hasn’t said whether he will run for president in 2028, and Trump hasn’t endorsed him or anyone else. ​But Vance is viewed as a leading potential contender who some Republican officials say will need to inherit much of Trump’s coalition while separating himself from his boss's ⁠baggage.
Read More: Trump makes hardliner Stephen Miller his chief of staff after midterm defeat
Vance took a more public step on Wednesday towards reinforcing his own political brand with an unusually blunt election postmortem. In a social media post, he blamed the Iran war for Republicans’ midterm defeat and laid out a ​platform for a Republican rebound.
He called for a swift end to the conflict and urged Republicans to focus on affordability, reevaluate foreign relations and overhaul the US relationship with Israel.
Trump has called Americans’ affordability concerns a Democratic “hoax”. He ​launched a war against Iran following sustained lobbying from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Trump went on to endorse Netanyahu in the Israeli election.
Vance makes unease at the war public
The post for the first time put Vance openly on the side of ending the war.
Three people familiar with the White House and Vance's communications told Reuters that the vice president was not breaking with Trump and said White House chief of staff Susie Wiles knew in advance about Vance's post.
On Friday, Trump reshuffled senior White House leadership, replacing ​Wiles with Stephen Miller in a move that suggests the White House plans to double down on some of Trump’s more hardline policies.
Trump has acknowledged the Iran war played a role in the Republican rout because of the ​resulting high gas prices but has continued to defend it. "I would have done nothing different," he told reporters on Wednesday.
Reuters could not determine whether Trump was aware of the post in advance.
Donald Trump Jr., the president's eldest son, endorsed Vance's remarks ‌on social media, ⁠along with some conservative allies.
The dialogue further elevated Vance as a potential post-Trump conservative standard-bearer, said Michael Ricci, a Republican strategist and former adviser to House Speakers John Boehner and Paul Ryan.
Using the megaphone of the vice presidency
He said Vance’s message forced conservatives to debate the merits of the war, and more broadly, what core tenets Republican presidential candidates should embrace in 2028.
"It’s simplistic to say this about him looking for ways to differentiate himself from Trump," Ricci said. "This is about him using his megaphone of the vice presidency to set the terms of debate."
Representatives for Vance declined to comment. White House representatives referred Reuters to Trump's comments on Wednesday, when he told reporters he understood ​Vance's perspective on the election results.
Democrats are poised to ​tie Vance, or any Republican nominee, to Trump ⁠in 2028, especially if Trump plays a large role in vetting conservative hopefuls.
"There’s a real challenge of how you position yourself to be viable in a general election while winning a primary that still requires you to bow down and kiss the ring,” said Igor Volsky, a Democratic strategist.
Vance’s brand did not emerge from the midterms unscathed. ​Republicans lost in states where he campaigned. Some of the strategies he endorsed, including an ad by Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy that cast doubt on the ​sexual abuse suffered by the ⁠victorious Democratic candidate, Amy Acton, may have swung races away from Republicans.
Other possible 2028 presidential contenders have offered their diagnoses of the midterm defeat. US Senator Ted Cruz of Texas said Republicans hadn't done enough on affordability. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said losing candidates had focused too heavily on transgender issues and neglected voter concerns about data centres and artificial intelligence. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has stayed silent.
Vance's effort to shape the debate was visible during the closing days of ⁠the campaign.
In stump ​speeches, he told voters to support Republicans because they would investigate fraud in federal health care and antipoverty programmes, tying that to the ​White House's immigration agenda and cost of living. He almost entirely ignored the Iran war and gas prices, and seldom mentioned Trump by name.
“I want my kids to raise a family in a country that is vibrant and thriving and free and prosperous. I want the ​simple things,” Vance told one of his final rallies in North Carolina. “And because I want that for me, I want it for you too.”

The decision came during a meeting between Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and visiting Sudanese Interior Minister Lt Gen Babiker Samra Mustafa Ali at the Ministry of Interior in Islamabad on Saturday. Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry also attended the meeting.
According to a statement from the Ministry of Interior, Sudan has expressed interest in benefiting from Pakistan’s experience and expertise in tackling cybercrime.
Pakistan and Sudan Agree to Cooperate in Combating Cybercrime
During the meeting, both sides agreed to broaden cooperation in several areas, including internal security, police training, institutional development and cybercrime prevention.
The two countries also discussed cooperation with the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA).
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said Pakistan was ready to provide all possible support to Sudan in its efforts towards peace-building and reconstruction. He also offered professional training opportunities for Sudanese police officers.
NADRA to Continue Supporting Sudan
Naqvi highlighted NADRA’s contribution to Sudan’s civil registration system. He said that with NADRA’s assistance, Sudan had issued 36 million citizenship cards, 9 million national identity cards, 18 million birth certificates and 500,000 death certificates.
He added that NADRA was ready to continue supporting Sudan in improving its civil registration services.
The two ministers also discussed other matters concerning Sudanese citizens living in Pakistan. Following a request from his Sudanese counterpart, Naqvi directed officials to immediately resolve visa-related issues faced by married Sudanese women in Pakistan.
He also assured the visiting minister that Sudanese citizens could access medical facilities in Pakistan and would receive all possible support in the health sector.
Sudan Seeks Stronger Ties with Pakistan
The Sudanese interior minister appreciated Pakistan’s cooperation and described the country as a brotherly partner. He expressed his government’s interest in expanding bilateral relations across different sectors.
The visit also included meetings with other senior Pakistani officials. A day earlier, Lt Gen Babiker Samra Mustafa Ali met the Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff, Field Marshal Asim Munir, to discuss ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation.
He also met Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday and appreciated Pakistan’s support for efforts to restore peace and security in Sudan at international forums.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
WhatsApp is developing new privacy controls that will allow users to decide who can see their phone numbers when they use usernames on the platform. The feature will give users more control over their personal information and help them manage their phone number visibility in chats and calls.
WhatsApp Tests New Phone Number Privacy Controls for Usernames
Currently, WhatsApp hides a user’s phone number from people who do not have it saved in their contacts when they communicate through a username. However, the upcoming feature will allow users to change this setting according to their preferences.
Four Options to Control Phone Number Visibility
According to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is working on a new phone number privacy section within its existing privacy settings. The feature was spotted in the WhatsApp beta for Android 2.26.45.1 update.
The new setting will offer four options: Everyone, My Contacts, My Contacts Except, and Nobody. Users will be able to select who can view their phone numbers when they interact through usernames.
WhatsApp will set the option to Nobody by default for users who have a username. This will maintain the current privacy behavior. However, people who already know and have saved the user’s phone number will continue to see it.
Users Will Get More Control Over Their Privacy
The new controls will help users manage their phone number visibility in different situations. For example, someone may want to remain accessible through a username while allowing their saved contacts to see their phone number.
Similarly, users will be able to hide their numbers from selected contacts while keeping them visible to others.
WhatsApp will also display a confirmation message when users change their phone number visibility settings. The warning will explain that switching to another option will reset the existing exceptions list. This means people previously excluded from viewing the number may gain access to it under the new setting.
Feature Still Under Development
The new phone number privacy controls are currently under development for WhatsApp on Android. The feature is not yet available for beta testing, and WhatsApp has not announced an official release date.
Once released, it will give users more flexibility in deciding how they share their contact information without affecting those who prefer to keep their phone numbers hidden.

— Raja Muhammad Farooq Haider Khan (@farooq_pm) November 6, 2026
The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) also said that it was "deeply concerned by reports of a fresh spate of violence in Rawalakot in AJK, with allegations of casualties among both protesters and law enforcement personnel".
It further said: "As raised in our fact-finding mission to AJK earlier in August, we reiterate that the federal and AJK governments must prevent the situation from deteriorating further and immediately begin a meaningful dialogue to address citizens' concerns. The media must also be given unhindered access to report from the region independently. On Thursday, the AJK government directed all weapon licence holders residing in the region to register their licences at the nearest police stations within 10 days, warning that unregistered licences would be treated as cancelled.
Read: AJK orders registration of all weapon licences within 10 days
According to a notification issued by the AJK Home Department, President Dr Najeeb Naqi approved the measure in the interest of public safety and maintenance of law and order.
The unrest in AJK stems from a prolonged protest movement led by the JAAC for constitutional and governance reforms, including the abolition of 12 refugee-reserved seats in the AJK Legislative Assembly, an end to privileges for the political elite and changes to the quota system.
Tensions escalated after the AJK government proscribed the JAAC on June 6, ahead of a planned long march and protest on June 9. The government said 35 of the committee's 38 demands had been accepted or implemented, yet they allegedly resorted to a series of violent attacks on state-backed personnel and assets.
"The Government of AJ&K has reasonable grounds to believe that Jammu Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee (JK-JAAC), also known by the names Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) and Awami Action Committee (AAC), is engaged in terrorism," the notification stated.
On June 11, the government reinstated 177 FIRs against JAAC members, withdrawing concessions previously granted under an October 4, 2025 agreement. Authorities accused the committee of violating the agreement by returning to street protests.
The situation further deteriorated in July, when clashes between protesters and law enforcement personnel in Rawalakot resulted in casualties. The HRCP subsequently called for an independent investigation as the two sides presented conflicting narratives.
In August, the PML-N formed a government in the region after securing a majority in the AJK elections, with Barrister Syed Iftikhar Ali Gilani elected as the prime minister.
However, tensions have persisted despite the formation of a new government, with protests and clashes reported in Rawalakot and Muzaffarabad. The Express Tribune could not independently verify the authenticity of the claims.

Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Alphabet, Google’s parent company, has acquired a stake worth nearly $548 million in Qualcomm, strengthening its ties with the chipmaker as it expands its presence in the data center and artificial intelligence (AI) markets.
The investment took place during the third quarter of 2026. It comes as Qualcomm looks to reduce its reliance on the smartphone market and become a major supplier of processors for AI infrastructure.
Qualcomm shares gained 3% in premarket trading following the news. The stock had fallen more than 9% on Thursday after the company reported disappointing results for the September quarter.
Alphabet Invests $548 Million in Qualcomm as Chipmaker Expands Data Center Business
Google and Qualcomm have maintained a long-standing business relationship. Qualcomm processors power many major smartphones running Google’s Android operating system.
The companies have also expanded their cooperation into other areas. They recently worked together on Google’s new premium laptop lineup, called Googlebook, which uses Qualcomm processors.
In 2024, the two companies also signed an agreement to develop chips and software to support the adoption of AI technology in vehicles.
Qualcomm Targets the AI Data Center Market
Qualcomm is expanding its business beyond smartphone processors as demand for AI computing continues to grow.
Over the past year, the company has approached cloud service providers with custom AI processors. These chips offer alternatives to expensive processors from Nvidia as major technology companies look for ways to develop and manage their own AI infrastructure.
Qualcomm expects its data center chip business to generate $15 billion in revenue by 2029.
The company has already secured support from several major technology players. In September 2026, Amazon signed an agreement that allows it to purchase up to $60 billion worth of Qualcomm’s AI data center chips and related products. The deal also gives Amazon warrants to purchase Qualcomm shares.
Microsoft and Meta have also placed orders for Qualcomm’s data center processors, supporting the company’s expansion plans.
Alphabet Also Increases Its SpaceX Stake
Alongside its Qualcomm investment, Alphabet slightly increased its stake in Elon Musk’s SpaceX.
The company reported holding approximately 555 million SpaceX shares, compared with 551.2 million shares previously.
Alphabet’s investment in Qualcomm highlights the growing importance of AI infrastructure and the competition among chipmakers to supply processors for the expanding data center market.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The National Cyber Emergency Response Team (National CERT) has warned of growing cyberattacks from artificial intelligence (AI)-powered attacks targeting banks, financial institutions, and critical national infrastructure.
According to the advisory, cybercriminals could use AI technology to automate attacks, identify system vulnerabilities and launch coordinated cyber operations.
The warning highlights the potential risks to the banking sector, particularly core banking systems, digital banking platforms and online payment services.
National CERT Warns of AI-Powered Cyberattacks on Banks and Critical Infrastructure
National CERT has warned that AI-powered cyberattacks could allow attackers to manipulate the account balances displayed to bank customers. Such activities could create confusion and spread panic among customers about the reliability and security of the financial system.
Cybercriminals could also use AI to identify weaknesses in banking networks and exploit them through automated attacks.
The advisory identifies several warning signs that financial institutions should monitor. These include an increase in automated login attempts, unusual financial transactions and suspicious API activity.
National CERT has advised banks and financial institutions to strengthen their security arrangements. It has particularly recommended implementing multi-factor authentication (MFA) and improving the protection of banking systems.
Critical National Infrastructure Also at Risk
The warning also covers essential national infrastructure, including oil and gas facilities, power plants, water supply networks and industrial systems.
These facilities increasingly rely on connected technologies and automated control systems. A successful cyberattack could disrupt their operations and affect the delivery of essential services.
National CERT has recommended that organisations strengthen the security of their Internet of Things (IoT) devices and industrial control systems. It has also advised them to restrict unnecessary remote access to reduce potential entry points for attackers.
Organisations Urged to Strengthen Cybersecurity
National CERT has urged all organisations to improve their monitoring, security and emergency response capabilities to deal with AI-powered cyber threats.
The advisory highlights the need for continuous monitoring and stronger security controls to detect suspicious activities before attackers can cause significant damage.
As cybercriminals increasingly adopt artificial intelligence, financial institutions and operators of critical infrastructure need to review their existing security measures and prepare for more sophisticated attacks.

Key Startup Funding Highlights Of The Week
On the back of GIVA’s mega $103 Mn fundraise, ecommerce emerged as the most funded sector this week. Besides GIVA, early-stage BPC brand Hyeglo Beauty also raised $744K in a round led by Sauce.vc.
Deeptech minted the highest number of deals this week. Four startups, operating across the advanced hardware and technology segment, raised a nifty $21 Mn.
Omnivore emerged as the most active investor this week, backing altM and Two Point O Capital.
Other Development Of The Week
Wealth management group Daksham Capital launched its maiden consumer-focused fund with a target corpus of ₹300 Cr. This also includes a ₹150 Cr greenshoe option.
SEBI has greenlit Razorpay’s ₹5,000 Cr-₹6,000 Cr IPO. The issue is expected to value the company at around ₹47,000 Cr, with a listing likely scheduled between January and March 2027.
Early backer Blue Ashva Capital has exited iD Fresh Food. The VC firm offloaded its entire stake in the startup for ₹50 Cr via a secondary transaction. Upsurge India, Triumph Global Fund and White Whale Ventures lapped up the shares.
D2C home appliances brand Nuuk is in talks to raise ₹100 Cr in a round, which will likely be led by Wipro Consumer Care Ventures and RPSG Capital Ventures, at a valuation of about ₹500 Cr.
Fireside Ventures’ cofounder and partner Vinay Singh is stepping down from the investment firm after a near-decade-long stint.

items.author: Oboh
items.content:
•Says, I share your pain, we’re out of dark tunnel •Knocks Atiku, Obi in Uyo, approves Ibom Deep Sea Port •Bus conveying women to welcome President crashes
By Egufe Yafugborhi
UYO — PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu yesterday promised a better future for Nigerians even as he took a swipe at former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), declaring that they lacked the leadership qualities to govern Nigeria.
Read Also: 2027: Obi couldn’t confront Anambra’s erosion, he lacks leadership traits — Tinubu
Tinubu, presidential candidate of the All Progressives Congress (ADC), spoke during his visit to Akwa Ibom State, where he urged voters to support his administration and Governor Umo Eno, insisting that continuity was necessary to sustain development.
His visit, however, was overshadowed by a road crash involving an Akwa Ibom State Transport Corporation (AKTC) bus conveying women to welcome him, in which one person was feared dead and several others sustained serious injuries.
The accident occurred along Oron Road, Uyo, when the bus, reportedly heading towards the airport, collided with a security Hilux van. Both vehicles were badly damaged.
Addressing supporters at the rally, Tinubu described his visit as a homecoming, recalling his professional connection with Akwa Ibom through his early employment with Mobil Oil.
“It’s like a homecoming for me. I remember having cut my teeth with Deloitte, the greatest accounting firm in America. I expressed the desire to come home. Mobil Oil recruited me.
“Part of the first assignment I was given was to audit the operations of Mobil in Eket. We used to go by boat to Ibono Terminal at that time. Akwa Ibom and I have been united ever since then. Till now, they decided that we are going to keep good company,” he said.
The President urged the electorate, particularly young people, to obtain their Permanent Voter Card (PVCs), describing it as their most potent instrument for determining the country’s political future.
“To you, the youth, do you have your PVC? Show me your hand if you have your PVC. To me, that is your sword. That is the weapon you need to defeat tyranny, to defeat those who deceive, those who don’t appreciate the value of a growing economy and the value of promising prosperity.
“The weapon you have is the PVC. I don’t have to enumerate what I’ve done for you. I’ve committed my last years to struggling for democracy, freedom, authenticity, development and progress,” Tinubu said.
He urged the people to support continuity, arguing that his administration had delivered improvements in education and other sectors.
“Have you seen development or not? You have seen progress. Your university is no longer on strike. There’s economic value being added to your life,” he told the crowd.
Tinubu then promised a better future through infrastructure development, education, skills acquisition and employment opportunities. “I’m begging you for the sake of your future. I promise you a better future; I promise you development; I promise you education; I promise you skill development; I promise you jobs. We are going to plant a lot of economic trees. There’s no reason why Akwa Ibom cannot use the value of palm trees,” he added.
Defends his economic policies
He described the January 16, 2027 election as consequential, saying it would determine the country’s direction. He also defended his economic policies saying his administration had moved Nigeria away from the brink of financial collapse.
According to him, “This coming election, on January 16th is a consequential election. It will define the direction of this country. When I took over, 27 governors out of 36 of this country were unable to pay salary, not to talk of pension, and gratuity. Today I can say that we are out of that tunnel. And I can beat my chest to say we are out of the despair, the dark tunnel of uncertainty and the calamity of a possible bankruptcy. By now if we didn’t take over, if we didn’t do what we did, we will be using the wheelbarrows to move our naira about because it will have become valueless.”
Acknowledging the hardship associated with his economic reforms, he added: “It was difficult; it was hard. It was hard for me, too. I don’t know the pain of the market, but I share your pain. I share your difficulty.
He also defended the student loan programme, saying it was designed to remove the burden of tuition fees from parents and widen access to education. “We’re taking education as the greatest weapon against poverty and creating opportunity for those who are still coming behind. From today on, as we are fighting corruption, any recovered corruption proceeds would be channelled into the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND)
Tinubu further insisted that Nigeria would not return to fuel subsidy, using a biblical analogy of Moses and the Israelites crossing the Red Sea to argue that the country must move forward rather than return to its previous economic policies.
Knocks Obi, Atiku
Taking a direct swipe at Obi, the NDC presidential candidate, Tinubu said: “Obi ran away from erosion in Anambra and he will now want to be president? President of where?” He also criticised Atiku over his political movements, questioning his ability to manage a political party and lead the country.
“Immediately a little inclination came that they were going to challenge leadership, he ran away. He abandoned the party. He now belongs to another party, and he’s looking for the presidency? Will you give such a person opportunity who has no leadership quality, no sense of responsibility?” he asked.
Approves deep sea port
A major highlight of the rally was Tinubu’s response to Governor Eno’s appeal for Federal Government approval of the Ibom Deep Sea Port. Responding to the request, the President declared: “On behalf of the people and leadership of Akwa Ibom, the governor requested for Ibom Deep Sea Port. It’s approved.” The declaration drew loud cheers from supporters, who repeatedly chanted: “Thank you, President! Thank you, President! Thank you, President!”
Tinubu said the project would generate economic value and accelerate development in the state. “Ibom Deep Sea Port will bring associated economic value and economic development,” he said.
He also praised Eno for what he described as his commitment to addressing erosion and promoting development, urging the people to support the governor. “Governor Eno confronted the erosion in Akwa Ibom, and it’s working for you. It’s stable. They lack the leadership character and traits,” he said in an apparent reference to his political opponents.
Praises Eno, defends reforms
At a reception held in his honour at Ibom Palm Resort, Tinubu praised Eno, describing the resort as evidence of purposeful leadership and the possibility of reclaiming environmentally degraded land for productive use.
“We are standing on a resort to the glory of God, which is a product of 73 acres of land of gully erosion, reclaimed, surrounded with a good, romantic, artificial lake, demonstrating a serious vision that is achievable when honest people are working for their homes,” he said.
Auto crash
Meanwhile, during the President’s visit there was a crash involving the AKTC bus conveying women mobilised to join supporters welcoming him. The bus reportedly collided with a security Hilux van along Oron Road as the women headed towards the airport.
Eyewitnesses said one person was feared dead, while several others sustained serious injuries and required emergency assistance.
Footage of the aftermath shared by Nsikakabasi Akpan showed early responders and other persons struggling to evacuate injured occupants from the wreckage.
Akpan described the incident as a collision involving a bus conveying women to the airport to receive the President and a security vehicle.
Confirming the accident, Paul James, Public Relations Officer, Road Safety Operations, Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Akwa Ibom State Command, said the command had dispatched a response team to the scene.
James, however, said the command was yet to establish the extent of casualties and the circumstances surrounding the collision as of the time of filing this report.
Vanguard News

items.author: Oboh
items.content:
•Sets N15bn capital requirement
By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief
The Central Bank of Nigeria has issued guidelines for virtual asset providers in the country, setting minimum capital requirement of N10 billion and N15 billion for Classes 1 and 2 issuers, respectively.
 This was contained in a circular with reference number PSP/DIR/PUB/CIR/001/004, date November 5, 2026 and signed by the Director of Payments Systems Policy, Mr. Musa Jimoh.
According to the bank, “A Class 1 Licensed Issuer shall maintain paid-up capital of N10 billion Naira or such higher amount as the Bank may prescribe, on entry and at all times thereafter. Class 2 Licensed Issuer shall maintain minimum paid-up capital of N15 billion or such higher amount as the Bank may prescribe, on entry and at all times thereafter.
“Both classes shall comply with the capital deposit and corresponding evidence and supplementary requirements in Section 17. There is no offshore issuer exemption from incorporation, licensing or capital.”
Class 2 stablecoins are digital tokens designed to maintain a stable value against foreign currencies, including the US dollar, while Class 1 refers to issuers of naira-referenced stablecoins.
 CBN said the emergence of virtual assets, stablecoins, and tokenised payment instruments “presents significant opportunities for innovation in payments, remittances, settlement, and digital commerce,” but that, “their growing adoption also introduces risks relating to financial stability, monetary policy, consumer protection, illicit finance, operational resilience, and foreign exchange management.”
It added that the guidelines were issued pursuant to its statutory mandate to promote monetary and financial stability and regulate Nigeria’s payments system.
“These Guidelines establish a risk-based framework for the licensing, regulation, supervision, and oversight of Non-Security Virtual Assets, including stablecoins, Deposit Money Tokens (DMTs), and related Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs).
 “These Guidelines seek to support responsible innovation while safeguarding the integrity, stability, and efficiency of the Nigerian financial system.
“These Guidelines also seek to provide regulatory requirements relating to governance, prudential standards, consumer protection, operational resilience, AML/CFT/CPF compliance, and reporting obligations for entities and persons engaged in regulated non-security virtual asset activities within or involving Nigeria,” the bank explained.
The CBN’s updated framework outlines clear boundaries for Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs), with a sharp focus on foreign exchange liquidity, consumer protection, and peer-to-peer (P2P) trading identity protocols.
Curbing money laundering
 The guidelines place great responsibilities on issuers to ensure that their activities do not aid money laundering or terrorism financing, as they are required to provide detailed data on their customers.
To avert it from being used for money laundering on terrorism financing, the CBN said “A provider shall maintain criteria, approved by its board and notified to the Bank, for identifying a customer that buys, sells or exchanges Regulated Tokens on the Person-to-Person (P2P) Service as a business, having regard to transaction volume, frequency, number of counterparties and advertising of rates.
“The provider shall apply enhanced due diligence and transaction limits to such customer and report the customer to the Bank under Section 10.8. Such identification shall not constitute authorisation to conduct a regulated activity. A customer conducting an activity requiring authorisation shall obtain the applicable licence or authorisation, cease the activity, or operate as an agent of the provider under Section 21, as the Bank may direct.”
Among others, the objectives, the apex bank said were to: establish a comprehensive, risk-based regulatory framework governing the issuance, distribution, conversion, custody, transfer, redemption and settlement of Non-Security Virtual Assets, including stablecoins and Deposit Money Tokens; preserve the effectiveness of the Bank’s monetary policy instruments and its capacity to monitor and manage capital flows and foreign exchange dynamics; and protect holders and consumers from issuer insolvency, reserve or backing mismanagement, redemption denial, fraud and other conduct risks; safeguard the stability and integrity of the Nigerian financial system.
The regulations applied to Naira-Referenced Stablecoins; Foreign Currency-Referenced Stablecoins;  Deposit Money Tokens (DMTs); Other Designated Tokens determined by the CBN to fall within its mandate over payments, settlement, foreign exchange, banking or financial stability; and any other token designated by the bank as a Regulated Token under these Guidelines.

items.author: Oboh
items.content:
•Judgement that gave Uzodimma governorship victory fingered
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri
A retiring Justice of the Supreme Court, Justice Uwani Abba-Aji, disclosed on Friday that some justices of the court had been placed on a visa ban by the United States of America.
Read Also: Uzodinma sworn-in as sixth governor of Imo
Justice Abba-Aji, speaking during a valedictory session held to mark her retirement from the bench, said the travel ban followed a judgment of the apex court that she described as widely misinterpreted.
She said: “My time on the Supreme Court bench was filled with challenges, some of which have served as additional opportunities to stand firm on the side of justice, regardless of the consequences.
“One of such challenging judgments was widely misinterpreted and led to a travel ban to the United States of America being imposed on all members of the panel, a ban which still holds today.”
Even though Justice Abba-Aji did not mention the specific case that led to the imposition of a US visa ban on Supreme Court Justices, Vanguard understands that it was connected to the legal tussle that followed the 2019 governorship election in Imo State.
A seven-member panel of the Supreme Court, which included the current Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, and Justice Abba-Aji, had on January 14, 2020, nullified the election of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate, Emeka Ihedioha, and ordered the swearing-in of the candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Senator Hope Uzodimma, who had initially finished fourth in the governorship election.
In the lead judgment delivered by the CJN, the apex court ordered the immediate withdrawal of the Certificate of Return that had already been issued to Ihedioha by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).
It ordered that a fresh Certificate of Return be issued to Uzodimma as the validly elected governor of Imo State.
To arrive at the decision, the apex court panel vacated the concurrent verdicts of both the Court of Appeal and the Imo State Governorship Election Petitions Tribunal, which had earlier affirmed the PDP candidate as winner of the gubernatorial contest.
Votes counted in courtroom
The panel went ahead to add election results from 388 polling units, amounting to 213,295 votes, which were tendered before the tribunal by a police officer who testified as PW-54, but which INEC disowned.
After all the votes were computed inside the courtroom, Uzodimma was declared the candidate who secured the majority of lawful votes cast at the election, a judgment that elicited wide reactions and protests.
Other members of the panel, which was led by the then CJN, Justice Tanko Muhammad, were Justices Sylvester Ngwuta, Kayode Ariwola and Amiru Sanusi.
Although Ihedioha subsequently approached the apex court again for a review of the judgment, which he insisted occasioned a miscarriage of justice, his application was refused.
Only one member of the panel, Justice Centus Nweze, gave a dissenting verdict that ordered Ihedioha’s reinstatement as governor, declaring the judgment that removed him from office a nullity.
Justice Nweze then warned the Supreme Court panel about the consequences of the judgment, which he said was delivered in bad faith.
“This decision of the Supreme Court will continue to haunt our electoral jurisprudence for a long time to come,” he warned.
Meanwhile, at the valedictory session on Friday, Justice Abba-Aji who is exiting the apex court having reached the 70-year mandatory retirement age, said the US visa ban was part of the price she paid for her service on the bench.
“Such inconveniences were a small price to pay to preserve the chastity of justice,” she added.
In her address, the CJN, Justice Kekere-Ekun, extolled the virtues of the retiring jurist, who she said had served in various administrative capacities as a Clerical Assistant, Assistant Registrar, Acting Registrar and Higher Registrar since 1973, when she joined the judicial service in Borno State.
She noted that Justice Abba-Aji had served at various Divisions of the Court in Benin, Abuja, Ekiti, Owerri and Kaduna since September 22, 2004, when she was elevated to the Court of Appeal, before she was promoted to the Supreme Court on January 8, 2019.
“For many of us, particularly the women who have entered the Nigerian Judiciary in more recent years, Hon. Justice Abba-Aji’s career is part of the story of how the place of women in our Judiciary has evolved.
“Long before the presence of women on the Bench became as familiar as it is today, she was already serving, quietly establishing a record of competence and service.
“Hon. Justice Abba-Aji’s journey into the legal profession began at a time when the professional landscape was very different from what we know today.
“Her leadership roles in the Federation of Muslim Women Associations of Nigeria and, particularly, her service as President of the National Association of Women Judges Nigeria (NAWJN), demonstrate that her interest in the progress of women was not merely incidental to her career.
“She contributed to creating a space in which other women could find their voices and assume positions of leadership,” the CJN added.
Vanguard News
The post Supreme Court Justices placed on US visa ban – Retiring jurist appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
IPO-bound hospitality chain PRISM, the parent entity of OYO, reported a consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of ₹353 Cr in the first quarter (Q1) of the fiscal year 2026-27 (FY27), up 17.3% from ₹301 Cr in the year-ago period.
According to PRISM’s audited financials seen by Inc42, the profitability came largely on the back of a deferred tax credit of nearly ₹244 Cr in the quarter under review.
Nevertheless, PRISM continued to grow its top line and generated an operating revenue of ₹2,814 Cr in Q1 FY27. This was nearly 35% higher than ₹2,078 Cr reported in the year ago quarter.
The IPO-bound startup also managed to improve its EBITDA by 24.3% to ₹760 Cr in the quarter under review as against ₹611 Cr in Q1 FY26. On the operational front, PRISM’s gross booking value (GBV) stood at nearly ₹9,600 Cr in the quarter ended June 2026, up nearly 30% from ₹7,408 Cr in Q1 FY26.
This is largely in line with what PRISM founder and CEO Ritesh Agarwal had said during the company’s extraordinary general meeting (EGM) in October this year.
“Our performance (in Q1 FY27) across segments on hotels or on vacation homes has demonstrated improving gross margins, higher operating earnings, even as we invest in expanding our brands and strengthening customer demand,” Agarwal had said then.
During the EGM, Agarwal also attributed PRISM’s performance to investments made in technology, brands and distribution capabilities over the past few years.
Founded in 2012 by Agarwal, OYO initially operated a budget hotel chain. It has since grown into a hospitality giant that offers holiday homes, coworking spaces, motels and corporate stays in more than 35 countries. The startup’s parent Oravel Stays rebranded to PRISM last year ahead of its initial public offering (IPO).
The startup has raised about $3.5 Bn in funding to date and counts the likes of SoftBank, Lightspeed India, Peak XV Partners and Microsoft among its backers.
The Q1 FY27 performance comes as PRISM is gearing up to list on the bourses. The hospitality giant first filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the SEBI via the confidential pre-filing route in December last year.
It then received the market regulator’s approval for its IPO in June this year. Right after, the startup filed its updated DRHP with SEBI for a ₹6,650 Cr IPO, which will comprise entirely of a fresh issue of shares.
The Ritesh Agarwal-led startup is said to be eyeing a valuation of $7 Bn to $8 Bn for the public issue.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
…says professionals behind major governance failures
…challenges graduates to choose integrity over wealth
By Joseph Erunke, Abuja
Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has accused educated Nigerians of masterminding some of the country’s most damaging corruption scandals, financial fraud and institutional abuses, saying the nation’s governance crisis is not a result of a shortage of intellectual capacity but a failure of conscience.
Mutfwang said some of the most sophisticated acts of financial fraud, contract manipulation, money laundering and subversion of public institutions were perpetrated by people whose academic qualifications and professional expertise should ordinarily be deployed for national development.
The governor spoke on Friday in Abuja while delivering the convocation lecture at the 15th Convocation Ceremony of Veritas University.
In his lecture titled, “Building the Nigeria We Want: The Role of the Educated Mind,” he warned that education without moral discipline had become a dangerous instrument against the country’s progress.
He challenged the graduating students to rethink the purpose of university education, insisting that academic certificates and intellectual brilliance would amount to little if deployed for selfish interests at the expense of society.
According to him, Nigeria’s development challenges cannot be blamed entirely on inadequate manpower or lack of expertise, as many individuals responsible for undermining public institutions are highly educated and professionally trained.
Describing the situation as an uncomfortable reality the country must confront, Mutfwang said some of Nigeria’s most entrenched governance failures were products of educated minds.
He said: “Indeed, I make an uncomfortable observation: the afflictions I diagnosed earlier, prebendalism, the privatisation of public office, grand corruption, the capture of institutions, are almost never the work of illiterate minds. They are overwhelmingly executed by educated minds.
“The contract, the doctored account, the laundered fund, the ingenious evasion of law. All these are the signatures of trained minds. This is the paradox we must confront. The educated mind is at once our greatest hope, and when corrupted, it becomes our most sophisticated danger.”
The governor also cited internet fraudsters, popularly known as Yahoo boys, as an example of intelligence deployed in the wrong direction, arguing that criminal ingenuity reflected a lack of moral restraint rather than an absence of intelligence.
“The Yahoo boy is certainly not a derelict. He is a work of intelligence, but intelligence wrongly applied,” he said.
Mutfwang maintained that Nigeria had no shortage of brilliant citizens, noting the achievements of Nigerians across different professions and on international platforms.
However, he lamented that the country had failed to translate its abundant intellectual resources into responsible leadership, accountable governance and sustainable development.
He urged the graduating students not to measure success solely by their earning capacity, professional positions or social standing, but by the extent to which their knowledge improved the lives of others.
According to him, intellectual capacity must be matched with conscience, warning that an educated person without moral discipline could inflict greater damage on society than someone without formal education.
“Knowledge tells you what you can do, but conscience tells you what you should do. An educated mind without a formed conscience is not an asset to any nation. It is a very efficient danger,” he declared.
The governor identified integrity, responsibility and competence as three critical attributes Nigeria needed from its educated population to overcome its development challenges.
He explained that responsibility required citizens to accept the consequences of their decisions rather than hide behind claims of good intentions.
Citing the principles in The Ethics of Responsibility, Mutfwang said national development required individuals willing to take ownership of the outcomes of their actions.
He described the Nigeria of his aspiration as a country where hospitals delivered quality healthcare, courts dispensed justice, schools provided meaningful education and public office holders regarded their positions as opportunities to serve rather than avenues for personal enrichment.
“The Nigeria we want is a nation of institutions that work, where the hospital heals, where the courts deliver justice, where the schools teach, and public office serves truly the public.
“It is a nation where merit is rewarded and mediocrity is not enthroned, where security is felt in the farm, in the market, at home, where prosperity is shared rather than captured, and where leaders understand office as stewardship and not as a spoil,” he said.
Mutfwang, who reaffirmed his belief in Nigeria’s unity, said the country’s ethnic, linguistic and cultural diversity should be regarded as an opportunity to build a stronger nation rather than an excuse for division.
He also disagreed with the notion that the 1914 amalgamation was necessarily a mistake, arguing that Nigeria’s diverse peoples had a common responsibility to determine the country’s future.
“I do not share the view that the amalgamation of 1914 was necessarily a mistake. I acknowledge our extraordinary diversity and the fact that our peoples have distinct histories, distinct languages and distinct identities. Yet I believe God has a purpose for bringing us together. Our responsibility is to decide what we will make of this country,” he said.
The governor further expressed concern over the withdrawal of credible and competent Nigerians from politics and public service, warning that their absence was worsening the country’s governance challenges.
He urged educated Nigerians to stop abandoning the public space to individuals who might not possess the integrity and commitment required to serve the country.
“One reason our public square so often disappoints is that too many good people have vacated it, abandoning it to those least fit to occupy it.
“Government and public service are not dirty words. They are the arenas in which the future of a nation is decided. If the best remain outside, the worst will not,” he warned.
Mutfwang stressed that nation-building was not the exclusive responsibility of elected officials or political appointees, but required the everyday commitment and responsible decisions of citizens across different professions.
The post Mutfwang: Educated Nigerians masterminding corruption, institutional decay appeared first on Vanguard News.
