items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The federal government on Friday slashed the price of petrol by Rs6.59 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs4.25 per litre for the next four days.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs346 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs378 per litre from November 7 to November 10.
The latest reduction brings petrol prices below Rs350 per litre for the first time since September 7, exactly two months after the government raised the rate by Rs12.90 to Rs358.77 from Rs345.87.
The revision also comes a day after the government slashed the price of petrol by Rs9.41 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs5.56 per litre for November 6.
Read: Govt slashes petrol by Rs9.41, diesel by Rs5.56 for Nov 6
On November 2, the government announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.

items.title: Vivo V80 FE India Variant Appears on Geekbench With MediaTek Dimensity 7400-Turbo SoC Ahead of Launch
items.summary: Vivo V80 FE has been spotted on the Geekbench benchmarking platform with the model number V2624. The handset was earlier spotted on the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) database with the same model number, hinting at an imminent launch in the country. The Geekbench listing suggests that the Indian version of the Vivo V80 FE will be powered by the MediaTek MT6878 chipset, which is the octa-core MediaTek Dimensity 7400-Turbo SoC. It appears to have four efficiency cores clocked at 2.0GHz and four performance cores, delivering a peak clock speed of up to 2.6GHz. The Vivo V80 FE has been spotted with 7.31GB of RAM, which could be marketed as 8GB of RAM. Further, the handset is listed with Android 17. It managed to score 911 points on Geekbench’s single-core performance test and 3,041 points on the multi-core performance test.

items.content:

TECNO, the AI-driven innovative technology brand and Title Sponsor of the TECNO SAFF Championship Bangladesh 2026, marked the opening of the tournament with a technology-led celebration at the National Stadium in Dhaka, as football fans across South Asia, including Pakistan, tuned in to follow the action.
Bringing together immersive projections, laser-mapped field visuals, music and South Asian culture, TECNO placed technology innovation at the centre of the opening experience and created memorable moments for fans across the region.
Sharing TECNO’s wider vision for the partnership, Jack Guo, General Manager of TECNO, added: “Football brings people together through passion, determination and unity. These values deeply rooted in TECNO’s DNA. South Asia is one of the world’s youngest and most vibrant regions. Through our partnership with the SAFF Championship, we want to bring progressive technology closer to local communities, inspire young people to dream bigger, embrace innovation and pursue their goals.”
TECNO Moments at the Opening Celebration
The opening celebration began with a large-scale projection and laser show across the stadium. The experience then moved onto the pitch through laser-mapped field visuals featuring the championship identity and participating nations.
Bangladeshi American DJ and music producer Sanjoy took the stage as TECNO’s Special Guest Performer, wearing a custom TECNO jacket. After performing “Siir Siir” at the FIFA World Cup, he brought that global energy to Dhaka with a 20-minute set that blended international music with South Asian sounds and tributes to the participating nations.
ELLA AI Extends the Championship Experience
Throughout the tournament, TECNO users in Pakistan can follow the championship through ELLA AI, which offers AI-generated score predictions, highlights and interactive football content. TECNO is turning smartphones into intelligent tournament companions, with interactive zones at the stadium in Dhaka, digital initiatives and prediction campaigns where fans can win TECNO CAMON smartphones.
Bringing the “Stop at Nothing” Spirit to South Asia
TECNO SAFF Championship Bangladesh 2026 represents the latest chapter in TECNO’s global football journey, building on its partnership with Manchester City Football Club from 2016 to 2022, its ongoing engagement with the CAF Africa Cup of Nations and its sponsorship of leading AFC club competitions.
As Title Sponsor, TECNO is bringing its “Stop at Nothing” spirit to South Asia and connecting with a new generation of fans, including football lovers across Pakistan, through technology, creativity and shared experiences.
Running at the National Stadium in Dhaka from 5 November to 17 November 2026, the championship brings together six national teams, and football fans from across the region. Throughout the championship, TECNO will continue creating moments that connect communities, celebrate South Asian football and inspire young people to pursue their ambitions.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
MobiKwik’s wholly owned subsidiary, MobiKwik Financial Services Pvt Ltd (MFSPL), has received a Certificate of Registration (CoR) from the RBI to operate as a non-banking financial company (NBFC).
The certificate was issued on November 5, following the RBI’s in-principle approval in April 2026. The dedicated NBFC was officially incorporated on March 13, 2025.
With the regulatory clearance in place, MFSPL intends to commence operations over the next three to six months. It intends to operate on an asset-light co-lending model, partnering with banks and other NBFCs.
In a statement, the company said that it plans to complement its existing lending service provider (LSP) business with the ability to originate credit directly through its NBFC.
“This will provide greater flexibility in product development, faster go-to-market execution and opportunities to improve lending economics, while allowing the group to continue leveraging its partnerships with established lenders,” the company said.
MobiKwik aims to disburse loans worth ₹5,000 Cr over the next three to four years, covering secured and unsecured credit for consumers and MSMEs.
Cofounder and CFO Upasana Taku said that the NBFC extension would allow MobiKwik to build on its existing lender partnerships and technology infrastructure while participating more actively in the lending value chain. The company plans to focus on responsible lending, prudent underwriting and sustainable growth.
During its Q2 earnings call, the CFO noted that MobiKwik could initially route around 10% of its digital lending disbursals through the NBFC. If the company disburses ₹6,000 Cr through its digital lending business next year, it would aim to route ₹600 Cr through MFSPL.
Under a proposed 10:90 co-lending arrangement, MobiKwik would contribute 10% of the loan amount, while its lending partner would fund the remaining 90%. This would require around ₹60 Cr in capital from MobiKwik to support ₹600 Cr in disbursals, allowing it to limit its on-book exposure while leveraging its existing underwriting and collections capabilities.
The NBFC launch comes amid an uptick for MobiKwik’s business. MobiKwik reported a consolidated net profit of ₹11.8 Cr in Q2 FY27 against a net loss of ₹28.6 Cr in the year-ago quarter.
Operating revenue increased 9.4% YoY to ₹295.7 Cr from ₹270.2 Cr. The company said it recorded its highest-ever quarterly net profit, marking its fourth consecutive profitable quarter.
During the quarter, MobiKwik’s financial services business segment, which includes its ZIP EMI credit offering, increased 41.8% YoY to ₹86.9 Cr.
Loan disbursals through its lending partners rose 34.1% YoY to ₹1,082.6 Cr, up 46.9% sequentially from ₹736.7 Cr. The sequential recovery followed a temporary dip linked to technology infrastructure migration during the transfer of its lending business.
MobiKwik increased its major lending partners to 11 from six a year earlier. It classifies partners with quarterly disbursals exceeding ₹5 Cr as major lenders. Of the total disbursals, 21% came through its distribution model, while the remaining 79% were under its first-loss default guarantee (FLDG) model, under which it shares credit risk with lending partners.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Indian stockbrokers’ combined total active user base shrunk by 0.5% to 4.59 Cr in October, dropping from 4.61 Cr users in September. Despite the broader market plateau, user consolidation accelerated in favour of newer players.
Groww continued to cement its market-leading position with 1.38 Cr active users in October, commanding a 30% market share. Notably, it added 3.04 Lakh users in the month, more than any other competitor in the top 10.
To note, Groww’s net active client additions in October were approximately 1.5X the combined additions of the next four largest brokers by active client base, Angel One, Zerodha, ICICI Securities and Upstox, which collectively added around 2.02 lakh active clients.
But the positions below saw an intriguing shakeup.
Zerodha, after losing clients in many months over the past year, slipped from second place.
Angel One overtook Zerodha, adding around 2.4 Lakh users to take its active user count to 69.99 Lakh and its market share to 15.3%. It grew at a 3.3% rate over the past month to overtake Zerodha.
“During the quarter, Angel One acquired nearly 15 lakh new clients, up 11.6% from the previous quarter, taking its client base to 3.99 Cr by September before it crossed 4 Cr in October. Its wealth management business continued to scale, with assets under management rising 19.1% quarter-on-quarter and 160.5% year-on-year to ₹16,000 Cr,” the company said in a statement.
Meanwhile, more than 32K users or around 0.5% of Zerodha’s active user base turned inactive over the previous month. It ended the month with 67.59 Lakh users, compared to 67.92 Lakh users in the previous month, although its market share remained nearly unchanged at 14.7%.
ICICI Securities held its fourth place with 21.64 Lakh active users, adding 3.7 Lakh users in October to take its market share to 4.7% market share.
In fifth place, Upstox shed 0.6% of its user base as the startup saw 11.3 Lakh users leave to bring its active user count down to 18.43 Lakh with a market share of just 4%.
Kotak Securities occupied sixth position with 14.05 Lakh active users while HDFC Securities finished seventh with 13.61 Lakh active users. The two bank-linked brokerages grew their user base by 0.9% and 0.5% respectively.
Meanwhile, Dhan, in eighth place, added nearly 26K users over the past, as its user base increased 2.3% to 11.47 Lakh from 11.21 Lakh in September. It was able to match Groww in terms of growth rate to become the second fastest growing brokerage among the top 10 after Angel One.
SBI Securities lost the most users after Zerodha, with an exodus of 17K users or 1.7% of its user base. The retail stockbroking subsidiary of SBI Capital Markets saw its active user count decline to 10.04 Lakh compared to 10.21 Lakh in September.
Rounding off the top 10, Motilal Oswal’s active user count grew 0.8% to 9.16 Lakh from 9.09 Lakh.
Beyond the top 10, Sahi added 34,372 active clients during October, adding to its bid to solidify its name in the discount brokerage space.
Markets Recover In The Month Of October
October marked a modest recovery for Indian equities after September’s sharp correction, although foreign investor selling remained elevated. The Nifty 50 rose 2.81% while Sensex gained over 3%. The gains ended the benchmarks’ two-month losing streak, but the recovery was not broad-based, with mid- and small-cap stocks continuing to face pressure.
As per data shared by Bajaj Broking, foreign institutional investors (FIIs) were net sellers of ₹45,162 Cr in October, while domestic institutional investors (DIIs) bought shares worth ₹62,220 Cr on a net basis. However, foreign selling eased in the second half of the month, with FPIs turning net buyers and investing ₹13,112 Cr between October 16 and 31, after pulling out nearly ₹47,955 Cr in the first fortnight.
“Going ahead, the reversal in FII flows is an encouraging signal for sentiment, though elevated crude and global event risk could temper the momentum,” Pabitro Mukherjee, Deputy Vice President-Research, Bajaj Broking had noted.

items.content:
Operator group Veon inked a deal to buy a stake of almost 33.8% in Jungo TV for $5 million in cash and around $42.3 million worth of shares in Kyivstar, with plans to offer content from the provider across its markets post completion.
Veon anticipates the move will strengthen its digital entertainment business. Access to fresh content is expected to increase customer engagement and revenue through increased subscriptions, sponsorship and content licensing.
It intends to distribute Jungo TV programming across Pakistan, Bangladesh, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan and Ukraine.
US-based Jungo TV’s headline offering among its streaming and TV channels is All Women’s Sports Network (AWSN), a service co-founded by actress Whoopi Goldberg dedicated to female sport.
Its channels are streamed in 65 countries through various platforms and partners in each market.
Veon CEO Kaan Terzioglu noted entertainment is “central to our digital operator strategy: bringing customers services they value throughout the day”.
“Jungo TV, and particularly AWSN, bring together distinctive content, an exciting women’s sports platform and established international distribution. By combining these strengths with our digital platforms and customer relationships, we aim to bring compelling entertainment to more people, deepen engagement and build new sources of digital revenue,” he added.
The share element of the deal is 2.35 million existing shares in Veon-owned Ukrainian operator Kyivstar valued at $18 each. Veon’s investment is subject to the usual closing conditions including regulatory approvals and is expected to complete in 2027.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
AvenuesAI (formerly Infibeam Avenues) reported a 6% growth in its net profit to ₹71.7 Cr in the quarter ended September (Q2 FY27) from ₹67.7 Cr a year earlier. On a sequential basis, net profit declined 15.4% from ₹84.8 Cr.
Meanwhile, its operating revenue grew 46.5% YoY and 7.4% QoQ to ₹287.9 Cr during the quarter under review. Including other income of ₹2.8 Cr, total income during the quarter stood at ₹290.7 Cr.
The fintech company’s operating EBITDA, excluding other income, grew just 3% YoY to ₹9.9 Cr. This came as its total expenses rose 49.4% YoY and 7.7% QoQ to ₹282.5 Cr in Q2 FY27, outpacing the growth in operating revenue.
At the same time, its consolidated net revenue, after accounting for payment processing and other costs, declined 1% YoY to ₹151.3 Cr in Q2 FY27.
AvenuesAI attributed the decline to its ‘competitive pricing strategy’ amid efforts to deepen merchant relationships and increase transaction volumes. As a result, its net take rate moderated 4% to 5.06 bps despite a 19% sequential increase in its total payments volume to ₹1.77 Lakh Cr.
The company generated ₹282.2 Cr in revenue from its payment business, which includes its CCAvenue payment gateway, payment infrastructure services to banks (CPGS), and credit and lending-related services, accounting for nearly 98% of its operating revenue during the quarter. The remaining ₹5.7 Cr was derived from its ecommerce platform business, Rediff.
AvenuesAI Looks To Unlock Value Across Subsidiaries
Alongside its financial performance, AvenuesAI outlined its plans to expand its AI capabilities, with advanced technology development and AI software-related work remaining among the key objectives of its rights issue.
In June last year, the company had raised ₹700 Cr via a rights issue, primarily for the repayment of outstanding loans, expansion of its IPO-bound digital content and ecommerce marketplace Rediff and further investments in its AI arm, Nueromind, for which it had earmarked ₹294 Cr.
Almost 42.7%, or ₹297.2 Cr, of the net proceeds remained unutilised at the end of the September quarter.
AvenuesAI has now announced that it will directly utilise the funds for AI development and software-related activities instead of routing the investment through Nueromind. It clarified that the change was limited to the mode of implementation, with no alteration to the end use of the proceeds.
In the June quarter, AvenuesAI announced plans to amalgamate Nueromind with itself, subject to NCLT approval.
It is also developing its Transaction Intelligence Score (TISco), an AI-led initiative that will use permitted transaction and merchant-behaviour signals for risk assessment, fraud prevention, merchant intelligence and financial services workflows.
The company aims to use its transaction infrastructure to build an intelligence layer that can support merchant and enterprise services.
On the investment front, AvenuesAI said it made investments in two financial services companies during the September quarter. It acquired a stake of up to 7% in Online PSB Loans Limited for a consideration of up to ₹65 Cr. It also invested up to ₹34.5 Cr to acquire a stake of up to 1.38% in Ratnaafin Capital Private Limited.
The company also reiterated its plans to expand CCAvenue’s international payments business, particularly in the US, by leveraging its payment technology, enterprise relationships and regulated infrastructure.
Meanwhile, its ecommerce arm, Rediff, is on its way to the bourses for a separate listing. After filing for an IPO confidentially earlier this year, the markets regulator SEBI approved the draft papers in August.
However, the Q2 disclosure did not provide an update on Rediff’s proposed IPO. As per sources, Rediff would look to raise in between ₹600-800 Cr via the IPO
AvenuesAI outlined that unlocking value from Rediff is one of its three strategic priorities for FY27. It plans to integrate Rediff’s consumer and enterprise digital ecosystem with its payments and AI capabilities. This includes RediffOne, which offers digital commerce and communication services, and RediffPay, which is intended to expand consumer payment engagement.
AvenuesAI has maintained its FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of ₹1,100-1,300 Cr.
The company said its focus for the remainder of FY27 will remain on expanding merchant relationships, improving operating discipline and creating additional monetisation opportunities through Rediff, enterprise technology and applied AI.
It is also monitoring potential changes to the merchant discount rate (MDR) policy for eligible UPI transactions, with any introduction, timing or scope remaining subject to government and regulatory decisions.
Shares of AvenueAI ended today’s trading session 3.72% lower at ₹129.25.

items.title: Sony MDR-3R Headphones Launched With USB-C Connectivity, Retro Walkman Design
items.summary: Sony has introduced a new pair of wired headphones that brings back the design of one of its most recognisable audio products. According to the company, the MDR-3R takes inspiration from the original MDR-3 headphones, which debuted in 1979 alongside the company's first Walkman. The new model retains the lightweight, open-ear design and several visual details of its predecessor, while swapping the traditional 3.5mm audio connector for a USB Type-C port. The headphones also feature 23mm drivers, an in-line remote, and a built-in microphone.

items.title: Bitget to Be Blocked in Thailand From December 5, Over Unlicensed Cryptocurrency Trading
items.summary: Thailand's Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has filed a criminal complaint against BG Limited, the operator of cryptocurrency exchange Bitget, for allegedly providing digital asset services without a licence. The regulator has referred the case to the Economic Crime Suppression Division and instructed the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society to block the exchange's website and mobile application from December 5. Authorities have asked customers to take necessary measures before the deadline. The investigation covers Bitget's activities in Thailand between 2022 and 2025.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has introduced a new facility on its IRIS portal that allows taxpayers to amend or cancel electronic sales tax invoices even after the existing 72-hour deadline. However, taxpayers must obtain prior approval from the concerned Commissioner Inland Revenue (CIR) before making any changes.
According to a user manual issued by Pakistan Revenue Automation (Private) Limited (PRAL), the facility will help businesses and taxpayers correct mistakes or discrepancies in electronic invoices discovered after the permitted 72-hour period.
FBR Allows Changes to Sales Tax Invoices on IRIS After 72-Hour Deadline
Under the new procedure, taxpayers can submit amendment or cancellation requests through the IRIS portal. The relevant commissioner will review each application and decide whether to approve or reject it.
To use the facility, taxpayers must open the Sales Tax applications section on IRIS and select the option for amending electronic sales tax invoices after 72 hours. They can then choose the relevant tax period and search for invoices using their FBR Invoice Transaction Numbers.
Taxpayers can either request changes to invoice details or seek cancellation. However, they cannot request both actions for the same invoice in a single application.
The system also allows applicants to upload supporting documents in PDF format. If tax officials need further information, they can contact applicants through the Internal Correspondence facility available on the portal.
Restrictions on Invoice Amendments
The FBR has also introduced certain conditions to prevent taxpayers from changing invoices that have already become part of their tax returns.
Invoices included in Annexure-C of a sales tax return or a Federal Excise Return cannot be amended or cancelled through this facility. Similarly, taxpayers cannot submit new requests for invoices that the commissioner has already approved or rejected.
ITaxpayers cannot include invoices with pending applications in new requests. However, they can submit multiple applications for the same tax period if each application covers different eligible invoices that the FBR has not yet processed or reviewed.
Another important condition concerns the submission of sales tax returns. Taxpayers cannot submit Annexure-C while an amendment or cancellation application is awaiting the commissioner’s decision.
Once the commissioner approves an amendment, the revised invoice will become available for inclusion in Annexure-C, subject to the system’s validation requirements.
If the application is rejected, the original invoice details will remain available for Annexure-C and the Federal Excise Return, where applicable.
The new facility provides taxpayers with an additional way to correct invoice-related mistakes after the standard 72-hour period. However, all changes will remain subject to the FBR’s approval process and eligibility conditions.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
WhatsApp is working on a new feature that will allow users to share photos and videos in their original quality without compression. The feature is currently under development for Android and is expected to become part of the paid WhatsApp Plus subscription.
According to WABetaInfo, the new option was spotted in WhatsApp beta for Android version 2.26.44.12. However, it is not yet available for beta testers, as the company is still developing it.
The upcoming feature will add a third media quality option to WhatsApp’s existing sharing settings. Users will be able to select their preferred quality directly from the drawing editor when sharing photos or videos.
WhatsApp Tests Original Quality Photos and Videos Sharing on Android
Currently, WhatsApp offers two options: Standard quality and HD quality. Standard quality compresses photos and videos to reduce their file sizes, allowing users to share media more quickly and use less mobile data. HD quality applies less compression and preserves more details, but it still reduces the original file size.
The new Original Quality option will work differently. It will allow users to share photos and videos without any compression, ensuring that recipients receive the media in the same quality as it was saved on the sender’s device. WhatsApp will still apply certain file size and resolution limits, although these limits are expected to be high enough for most regular photos and videos.
Original Quality Sharing Will Be Exclusive to WhatsApp Plus
WhatsApp plans to make the new feature available exclusively to WhatsApp Plus subscribers. The company will also highlight original quality media sharing during the subscription onboarding process so that new subscribers know about the feature.
Once available, users will be able to select Original Quality from the drawing editor before sending a photo or video. This will make it easier to share high-quality media without using the document-sharing method.
However, users who do not subscribe to WhatsApp Plus will still have a way to send uncompressed photos and videos. They can share media as documents, which prevents WhatsApp from applying its usual compression. This method already works for free users, but it requires additional steps and can be less convenient.
With the upcoming option, WhatsApp Plus subscribers will be able to send original quality media directly through the drawing editor.
See Also: WhatsApp Rolls Out AI Photo Expansion Feature on Android
When Will the Feature Arrive?
WhatsApp’s original quality media sharing feature is still under development. It has not yet reached beta testing, and the company has not announced an official release date.
The feature is expected to arrive in a future Android update as part of WhatsApp Plus. Users will have to wait for further updates to find out when it becomes available.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) has proposed a new licensing framework for Internet of Things (IoT) services in Pakistan, introducing mandatory licensing and registration requirements for companies operating Low Power Wide Area Networks (LPWAN) and providing IoT connectivity.
Under the draft Internet of Things and Low Power Wide Area Networks (IoT-LPWAN) Licensing Regulations 2026, the regulator has proposed a five-year license for companies offering commercial IoT connectivity services to third parties, with an initial licensing fee of Rs. 100,000.
The proposed regulations, which have been circulated for consultation, aim to establish a structured regulatory framework for IoT networks, technology platforms, private deployments, and research activities.
The move follows previous efforts to tighten the regulatory framework for IoT and LPWAN services as connected technology gains importance in agriculture, manufacturing, transportation, healthcare and smart infrastructure.
According to the draft, PTA plans to introduce separate regulatory categories depending on the nature and purpose of IoT operations.
Companies establishing private IoT networks within their own premises, including industrial facilities, farms, campuses, and project sites, will be required to obtain registration rather than a commercial license.
Such registrations will remain valid for five years, with an initial registration fee of Rs. 10,000 and an additional processing fee of Rs. 5,000.
Similarly, IoT platform and application providers will require five-year registration, subject to the same Rs. 10,000 initial fee and Rs. 5,000 processing charges.
For research, development, testing, and trial activities under the proposed regulatory sandbox category, PTA has suggested a one-year registration period with an initial fee of Rs. 2,000 and a processing fee of Rs. 1,000.
The draft also proposes exemptions for certain categories of IoT activities to facilitate innovation and encourage wider adoption of connected technologies.
PTA Proposes Strict Operational Requirements for IoT Operators
Beyond licensing and registration fees, the proposed framework introduces several operational requirements for companies providing IoT connectivity services.
Under the draft, licensed operators will be required to begin commercial operations within one year of their license becoming effective.
They must also obtain a commencement certificate from PTA. Failure to meet the requirement could result in cancellation of the license.
However, the regulator may grant a one-time extension of up to six months if an operator submits a justified request before the original commencement deadline expires.
Another important requirement involves the registration and monitoring of IoT gateways.
Operators will be required to register every gateway through PTA’s online portal and submit quarterly reports detailing active IoT connections and the number of operational gateways.
Licensed operators will also need to provide district-wise information about their gateway deployments, allowing the regulator to monitor IoT network expansion across Pakistan.
The proposed regulations further require operators to route backend network traffic, including traffic using satellite backhaul, through a PTA-licensed Local Access Provider.
PTA has also included national security and public safety obligations, under which the authority may direct operators to suspend or restrict services when required.
Companies applying for licences or registrations will need to provide technical deployment plans, geographical locations, indicative gateway details, network connectivity diagrams and other prescribed documents.
Meanwhile, existing IoT licensees will be allowed to continue operating under the new framework for the remaining duration of their current licences.
However, existing LPWAN licensees will be required to register their gateways within 90 days and obtain commencement certificates in accordance with the proposed regulations.
The draft identifies several potential applications for IoT technology, including smart cities, connected buildings, electricity and water management, smart agriculture, livestock monitoring, industrial automation, logistics, healthcare, education, transportation infrastructure and disaster management.
For Pakistan, the proposed framework could provide greater regulatory clarity for businesses planning to deploy connected devices and smart infrastructure.
However, requirements involving gateway registration, reporting and licensed traffic routing could also introduce additional compliance responsibilities for IoT service providers.
The regulations are currently at the consultation stage and have not yet been finalized or enforced.
The final requirements, licensing conditions and implementation timelines will depend on PTA’s review of stakeholder feedback and the subsequent approval of the regulatory framework.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Samsung appears to be preparing a much-needed battery upgrade for its upcoming Galaxy A38 5G. A fresh leak suggests that the smartphone could feature a 6,000mAh battery, marking a 20 percent increase over its predecessor, the Galaxy A37.
According to Dutch publication GalaxyClub, the Galaxy A38 has a rated battery capacity of 5,882mAh, which Samsung is likely to advertise as a typical capacity of 6,000mAh.
This would be a significant improvement over the 5,000mAh battery found in the current Galaxy A37 5G.
Samsung has continued using 5,000mAh batteries across several generations of its popular Galaxy A-series smartphones, despite competing brands increasingly offering larger batteries.
If the latest information proves accurate, the Galaxy A38 could become a more attractive option for users who prioritize battery life, particularly those who rely heavily on mobile internet, video streaming, and social media.
However, the battery may be the only major hardware upgrade.
Earlier reports indicate that Samsung is unlikely to introduce significant camera improvements with the upcoming handset.
The Galaxy A38 is expected to retain a 50MP primary camera with optical image stabilization (OIS) and phase detection autofocus (PDAF), accompanied by an 8MP ultrawide camera and a 5MP macro sensor.
A 12MP front-facing camera is also expected for selfies and video calls.
This would leave the camera resolution largely unchanged from the Galaxy A37, which was launched earlier this year.
Previous Galaxy A37 and A57 camera leaks also highlighted Samsung’s preference for incremental improvements across its mid-range lineup.
The upcoming Galaxy A38 is expected to retain conventional lithium-ion battery technology rather than adopting silicon-carbon batteries, although Samsung has not confirmed the battery chemistry.
Meanwhile, there is speculation that the higher-end Galaxy A58 could receive a similar battery upgrade. However, this remains unverified.
Earlier Galaxy A58 camera leaks have already offered an early look at what Samsung may be preparing for its next-generation mid-range lineup.
Samsung Galaxy A38 Expected Price and Release Timeline in Pakistan
Samsung has not officially announced the Galaxy A38, and its pricing and release schedule remain unconfirmed.
However, based on the company’s previous Galaxy A-series launch pattern, the handset is expected to make its global debut around March or April 2027, potentially alongside the Galaxy A58.
A Pakistani release could follow around April or May 2027, although this is only an estimate based on Samsung’s previous launch schedule.
For reference, Samsung officially introduced the Galaxy A37 5G and Galaxy A57 5G in Pakistan in April 2026.
The Galaxy A37 5G launched in Pakistan at Rs. 149,999 for the 8GB RAM and 256GB storage variant.
Meanwhile, unofficial Pakistani smartphone listings suggest that the Galaxy A38 could cost around Rs. 154,999.
The final retail price could be higher or lower depending on the storage variant, exchange rates, taxes and Samsung’s pricing strategy.
Internationally, reports suggest that Samsung could position the Galaxy A38 close to the €500 mark in Europe, although no official price has been disclosed.
The potential price increase raises an important question: will a larger battery be enough to convince customers to upgrade when the cameras could remain largely unchanged?
Samsung’s Galaxy A-series has traditionally appealed to buyers looking for reliable performance, good displays, long software support and a familiar user experience.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
Ethiopian gaming startup Rise of Fearless has raised US$1 million in funding from advisory firm Epic Edges Capital as it looks to scale its African history-inspired battle royale mobile game.
Launched in 2025, Rise of Fearless offers an African take on the battle royale genre, drawing narrative inspiration from Ethiopia’s victory over Italian forces at the Battle of Adwa in 1896. The game’s characters, environments, hairstyles and attire are designed to reflect African identities, offering an alternative to the Western-centric narratives that have long dominated mainstream gaming.
Free-to-play on the Apple App Store and Google Play, the game has surpassed 15,000 downloads to date, with its largest player communities in Nigeria, Ethiopia and South Africa.
The previously bootstrapped startup’s new funding, structured as a SAFE, will be used to invest in talent, technology, infrastructure, marketing and community-building, as Rise of Fearless looks to expand its audience beyond its existing markets.
“The launch of Rise of Fearless filled a gap in the gaming space, but it has also forced us to think beyond game downloads, shifting our focus towards a much wider African gaming ecosystem where African intellectual ownership and talent development are key,” said founder Kanessa Muluneh. “As a bootstrapped company, this investment is pivotal to our ambitions and the future of African gaming.”
Muluneh said the startup also plans to use its growth to help tackle some of the structural challenges facing African gaming companies, including access to reliable technology, servers and cross-border payment infrastructure.
Remco Coerman, founder of Epic Edges Group, said Rise of Fearless was the kind of ambitious, culturally-rooted IP with the potential to resonate far beyond its home market.
“We believe there is a significant opportunity for African creators to build globally relevant gaming experiences that reflect the continent’s stories, identities and talent,” he said.

items.author: Bismah Malik
items.content:
In March this year, on the sidelines of Razorpay’s annual flagship event FTX, CEO Harshil Mathur told Inc42 that what mattered most to him was how Razorpay stands in the public markets, and not the fact that it went public.
Eight months on, that test now has a rough date as the company sets off on the last leg of its IPO journey.
Razorpay has received SEBI’s approval for its proposed IPO. The fintech major is looking to raise ₹5,000-6,000 Cr through a mix of fresh issue and offer for sale at a valuation of around $5 Bn, with a listing likely between January and March 2027. Axis Capital, Kotak Mahindra Capital, JP Morgan and Citi are the reported bankers.
The headline number when it comes to Razorpay’s listing, or for that matter any listing within fintech circles, has been that of valuation.Sources suggest that Razorpay may be looking to list at a $5 Bn valuation, a markdown from the $7.5 Bn valuation that the company commanded in December 2021.
But back in 2021, fintech valuations were sky high amidst a pandemic led funding boom that witnessed sharp corrections years down the line.
Another fintech major, PhonePe, paused its mega listing in March 2026, with reports suggesting that volatile geopolitical tensions and valuation concerns led the payments company to put its IPO plans on hold. It has since revived them on the back of MDR. Sources told Inc42 in September that PhonePe is targeting a listing between February and March 2027 at a valuation of about $10 Bn.
But Razorpay has a different story to tell the public investors as it seeks ₹5,000-6,000 Cr from them.
The first part of that story is profit. “When you take out that one-time cost of the reverse flip, Razorpay was profitable — that profitability streak is maintained throughout. We hope the financials will continue to improve from here as a company that’s continuously growing,” Mathur had told Inc42 earlier.
In FY25, Razorpay slipped into the red, weighed down by ₹1,209 Cr in ESOP expenses and one-time restructuring and tax costs from moving its domicile to India. It did not disclose the size of the loss. The reverse flip tax bill has been reported at about ₹1,245 Cr, or about $150 Mn. A year earlier, in FY24, its payments business had reported a ₹34 Cr profit against a total revenue of ₹2,068 Cr or a net margin of 1.6%.
The company claims to lead India’s digital payments processing market in terms of total payments volume and is expanding across Southeast Asia and other geographies, but monetising this scale has always been a problem when it comes to payments companies.
The 0.4% merchant discount rate (MDR) on large UPI payments, due after Diwali, would be the first fee on a bulk of these payments, and it would arrive just ahead of the listing window.
How much reaches Razorpay’s bottom line depends on two things: how it negotiates with the banks that receive the fee and the large merchants that pay the MDR.
Sources we spoke to suggest that much of the revenue bump that companies like Razorpay will get out of MDR would not boost their topline significantly, but could feed profits strongly because it is a fee on rails that companies have already built. For Razorpay, it’s a boost to its search for the right valuation just in time.
MDR on UPI would likely narrow the gap between the company’s sought valuation and its bottomline. It also gives Razorpay a growth story to take to public investors as it heads into the IPO.
A Profitable Core
Unlike many of its contemporaries eyeing a listing at the scale of Razorpay, the fintech has no major debt overhang and nearly half of the IPO proceeds are expected to be allocated for OFS.
Company sources told us that the core online payments business is EBITDA profitable and generating strong cash flows, which is why the company is making bold investments in allied businesses and AI.
Sources pointed towards capital allocations “between mature, cash-generating units and high-potential growth bets”, with AI-first products, financial infrastructure and new verticals taking the investment.
The company has also given a timeline on profitability. “By the end of FY26, our India business should be solidly profitable. At the consolidated level, we’ll reach profitability about two to three quarters after that,” the company’s CFO, Arpit Chug, told Inc42 in October 2025.
But FY26 has since closed, and Razorpay is yet to make those numbers public. The biggest factor in Razorpay’s IPO will be the profitability and the margins earned by its core business.
In lieu of actual profit figures, Razorpay’s pitch to public investors rests on scale. It described itself in 2024 as India’s market leader in digital payments processing, with a majority share, and said in 2025 that it served 105 of India’s 119 unicorns. It claims to be processing a total payments volume (TPV) of over $180 Bn (as of 2024 end).
When compared against its primary competitors Cashfree and PayU, Razorpay stands out for its scale and its focus on small and medium businesses.
Razorpay claims to lead on overall volumes, enterprise accounts drive the bulk of volumes at Cashfree, Inc42 reported earlier. Razorpay, on the other hand, claims that 80% of its client base comprises SMBs and startups.
Among the three, PayU India leads in terms of the topline. Its payments business alone earned $523 Mn (about ₹4,420 Cr) in FY25. It pulled ahead of Razorpay which reported ₹3,783 Cr in FY25, while Cashfree stood at ₹640.1 Cr. PayU owner Prosus claims the company has a 25% share of the Indian online payments, while processing $90 Bn in TPV in FY26.
In a bid to race past the competition, Razorpay has been eyeing overseas markets by strategic tie-ups and acquisitions. Mathur earlier said that international was its fastest-growing business, with payments growing about 40% and newer segments at 70-90%.
Outside India, Razorpay currently operates in Malaysia and Singapore and is eyeing expansion into the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam as its next Southeast Asian targets.
The company, according to sources, is expanding majorly within Southeast Asia and expects the revenue from these countries to contribute 15% of its overall topline by 2030.
Razorpay entered Malaysia by buying a majority stake in Curlec in 2022, launched its gateway there in 2023 and entered Singapore in March 2025.
Closer to home, the biggest expected lever is UPI and the introduction of MDR soon after the festive season. About half of the payments flowing through Razorpay are on UPI, and that rail is about to start earning the fee that can feed the company’s bottomline.
The Two Negotiations Behind Razorpay’s MDR Upside
The first critical negotiation for Razorpay will be with banks. Payment aggregators such as Razorpay get no fixed share under NPCI’s stated framework, because they are not direct members of the UPI network and are part of it only through sponsor banks.
So the aggregator’s cut has to come out of the acquirer bank’s share in the MDR, under a private contract between the two.
Reports suggest that the talks have centred on aggregators keeping 50-80% of the acquiring bank’s MDR share. But there is also a flip side to it.
Payment aggregators and gateways already earn technology, checkout and reconciliation fees from merchants, and with MDR coming into effect, the merchants can move to the aggregators and gateways that offer more reasonable take rates.
Pine Labs CEO Amrish Rau has already flagged that talks with merchants have yielded this view among the primary customer base for payments aggregators. “From a commercial standpoint, I absolutely do believe when it comes to the largest of large merchants that we have with us, there will be a commercial conversation to be had, for sure,” Rau said in October 2026 after the Q2 results.
Notwithstanding the restructured commercial agreements that the payment aggregators and gateways will sign with banks and merchants for the MDR regime, sources say that the fee could support higher valuations for IPO-bound companies such as Razorpay and PhonePe.
“The headline MDR pool is not the same as revenue accruing to an individual participant. It depends on eligible transaction volumes, merchant mix and the prescribed distribution across the ecosystem,” PhiCommerce CEO Rajesh Londhe told Inc42.
Listed peer Paytm has already put a number on what MDR will bring to the table. With its Q2 results, Paytm said it expects an uplift of about 2.5 bps in its overall payments processing margin, and that the actual outcome may stabilise in 2-3 quarters after implementation.
As per sources, MDR could bring Razorpay ₹192-461 Cr of revenue a year once implemented, which would be about 5-12% of its FY25 revenue and 15-36% of its FY25 gross profit.
As a result, analysts believe that Razorpay could see a valuation bump of $300 Mn-$1 Bn from the existing ask. That’s what the MDR effect can actually unlock, though much would also depend on the commercial agreements with banks and merchant talks.
Razorpay’s technology prowess and merchant scale could be a huge lever in any talks with banks and merchants.
However, what matters more than the scale will be the value of transactions and the scale of the clients themselves, which would directly boost revenue and improve margins. Nearly 80% of Razorpay’s customers are small businesses, digital-first brands and startups, and it has not disclosed how many of their tickets cross the ₹2,000 threshold required for the MDR boost.
There is also no certainty as yet on the timeline by which fintech companies can expect the MDR outcome to start showing up on their P&L.
Analysts tracking the industry, however, say that the companies would need a few quarters of data to give investors a credible outlook. For Paytm, that could be 2-3 quarters, and with Razorpay coming to the IPO table, investors would want to hear a number for the company. Will a listing between January and March of 2027 be enough to give investors a clear answer?
The AI Story Needs Numbers
Then there’s the AI story, which we had written about extensively earlier this year.
According to Mathur, Razorpay is building a long-term business bet on AI and this is not related to the IPO and its outcome. The fintech sector has been one of the earliest adopters and partners of frontier AI models such as ChatGPT and Claude, experimenting with AI use cases for the millions of merchants on its platform.
 
Razorpay’s Agent Studio, built on Anthropic’s Claude, offers small businesses task-specific agents for abandoned carts, disputes, subscription recovery and cash flow forecasting. Mathur wants Razorpay to be known as “an operating system for businesses” which is run on AI.
That story gives investors a reason to look past the thin margins in the payments business, but the AI theme is not strong enough in the case of Razorpay yet. It has to make a bigger splash in terms of the outcomes it is seeing. .
Rivals Cashfree, PayU and Pine Labs are also accelerating their AI led partnerships to offer new products to their existing merchant base. All these AI offerings have been particularly concentrated towards agentic workflows and ecommerce enablement.
However, there is still little public evidence of what these agents earn. Mathur earlier told us that it will take a few years to assess the real term monetisation value that these AI capabilities can unlock for any fintech.
Hence for an IPO-bound Razorpay, its core payments business is the only true and measurable metric for the public investors. The future bets may fructify but for now, they are unlikely to be a factor for investors.
Even at a reported $5 Bn valuation, Razorpay goes to market with some real strengths such as 65% YoY revenue growth in FY25, about $180 Bn in annualised TPV, and a profitable core. While it is banking on the MDR regime to solve a lot of headaches, investors will want to see a lot more to justify the valuation ask.
Whether the price holds depends on disclosures still to come, including its FY26 and subsequent financial performance and the results of its MDR negotiations with banks. And only then will Razorpay find out how much of its story the public market is willing to pay for.
[Edited By Nikhil Subramaniam]
The post MDR And AI: Inside The Two Acronyms That Could Shape Razorpay’s ₹6,000 Cr IPO appeared first on Inc42 Media.

The beauty and personal care (BPC) company’s operating revenue rose 35.9% to ₹731.2 Cr from ₹538.1 Cr in Q2 FY26.

items.author: Vinaykumar Rai
items.content:
Mamaearth parent Honasa Consumer reported an 86.7% increase in its consolidated net profit to ₹73.2 Cr in the September quarter (Q2 FY27) from ₹39.2 Cr in the year-ago period.
The beauty and personal care (BPC) company’s operating revenue rose 35.9% to ₹731.2 Cr from ₹538.1 Cr in Q2 FY26.
“We delivered our highest growth since listing, with revenue growing 36% YoY and EBITDA nearly doubling to ₹93 Cr. What makes this growth particularly encouraging is the strength of the business behind it. Our focus categories grew over 40% and now contribute more than 80% of our business, with strong momentum across general trade, modern trade and ecommerce,” company’s cofounder and CEO Varun Alagh said.
Sequentially, net profit declined 19% from ₹90.4 Cr, while operating revenue fell 3.3% from ₹755.9 Cr.
Honasa’s profit growth outpaced revenue growth on an annual basis, with total expenses increasing at a slower pace than its top line. The company’s expenses during the quarter surged 29.1% to ₹652.4 Cr from ₹505.5 Cr. The company’s tax expenses for the quarter more than doubled YoY to ₹27.6 Cr.
For the first half of the fiscal year, the Mamaearth parent reported an 31% YoY uptick in its top line to ₹1,487.1 Cr. Meanwhile, the company’s profit more than doubled YoY to ₹163.7 Cr.
Honasa’s Operational Updates
The BPC major said that its focus categories grew by 40%, taking their contribution to 80% of the company’s total income. The company estimates its shareholding in categories like face cleansers, shampoos, face serums, sunscreens, among others, to be about 5% in a market worth about ₹50,000 Cr.
In terms of channel growth, Honasa claims to have achieved a 40% YoY growth in general trade secondary sales and modern trade offtake as well as a 20% growth in ecommerce. The company’s general trade presence expanded to about 3.2 Lakh outlets across India,
Beyond Mamaearth, Honasa’s ‘house of brands’ strategy sees it operate The Derma Co, Aqualogica, Staze, Dr Sheth’s, BBlunt, among others. In this, the company says that younger brands grew 45%+ during the quarter, with each brand building on its own growth drivers.
The company doesn’t disclose particulars of the financial performance of its brands. For Mamaearth, Honasa said that it continued on its high-teens growth trajectory with mid-teens EBITDA.
Shares of Honasa were trading 4.02% lower at ₹462.30 apiece on the BSE at 15:21 IST.

items.title: Anthropic Introduces Claude Personal Finance as an Integrated AI Financial Management Tool
items.summary: Claude Personal Finance has been launched by Anthropic as the AI giant's new financial management tool. The financial management tool will start rolling out later this week and will be available to Pro, Max, and Ultra subscribers in the US, the company said. On top of this, Anthropic assures that, “like the rest of Claude”, Personal Finance will not present any ads or sponsored recommendations, such as credit cards, loans, or savings accounts of “its own”. The company says that the Claude Personal Finance tool will be able to create spending charts, calendars of scheduled payments, and a dashboard including the figures a user chooses to see. After the AI tool has generated the chart, users can choose to make adjustments based on their preferences. Users can ask the chatbot to generate a spending chart and place each transaction in a category.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has recommended a separate authorisation for satellite network providers and proposed permitting direct-to-device services using satellite and terrestrial mobile spectrum.
The proposals can enable compatible smartphones to connect directly to satellites, potentially extending connectivity to areas without conventional mobile coverage.
Under the proposed Satellite Communication Network (SCN) Provider Authorisation, companies can build and operate satellite networks and sell capacity to eligible telecom service providers. They cannot serve end users directly under this authorisation.
The recommendations require government approval and do not immediately permit commercial D2D services.
What Changes For Operators?
The framework would give telecom operators a way to access satellite infrastructure through partnerships, while continuing to manage their customer relationships.
For satcom companies, it would create a separate route to sell network capacity to telecom operators, without requiring them to build a consumer-facing service under the same authorisation.
In effect, one company can operate the underlying satellite network while another sells connectivity to customers. This will support partnerships between satellite infrastructure providers and telecom operators seeking to extend their coverage.
However, the SCN authorisation alone would not allow a satellite company to sell mobile or broadband services directly to consumers. It would require the relevant service licence or authorisation.
The proposed nationwide authorisation would remain valid for up to 20 years, with renewal permitted for another period of up to 20 years.
Connecting Phones To Satellites
TRAI has proposed two routes for D2D connectivity – using spectrum earmarked for mobile satellite services or using spectrum already assigned to terrestrial mobile operators.
For the first route, it has recommended that the government encourage handset manufacturers to include support for the relevant satellite bands in future smartphones sold in India.
For the second, telecom operators can partner with satellite network providers to use their existing mobile spectrum for satellite connectivity.
However, participating operators would collectively need to hold the relevant frequency channel across all 22 licensed service areas and agree to its use.
TRAI has recommended permitting this arrangement without waiting for the World Radiocommunication Conference 2027. The satellite services would have to avoid interfering with existing authorised services and cannot claim protection from interference caused by them.
TRAI has proposed an authorisation fee of 8% of adjusted gross revenue (AGR), without a minimum authorisation fee.
Satellite network providers can obtain spectrum directly from the government or use spectrum held by eligible partner operators. In a partnership, spectrum rights would remain with the operator.
Government-assigned satellite spectrum would be valid for up to five years, with a possible extension of up to two years. It would attract an annual minimum spectrum charge of ₹3,500 per MHz.
For D2D services using a telecom operator’s existing mobile spectrum, TRAI has proposed no additional spectrum charges. Existing spectrum charges would continue.
The proposals come amid efforts by Starlink, Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb, and Reliance Jio to tap India’s satellite connectivity market.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA), in collaboration with Meta, has blocked 176,000 WhatsApp accounts registered against recycled mobile numbers, as the regulator moves to establish a permanent mechanism to prevent cyber fraud through inactive and cancelled SIMs.
PTA officials said that the accounts had been blocked at the authority’s request after complaints emerged that recycled mobile numbers were being exploited to commit cyber fraud through WhatsApp.
The authority has shared around 10 million recycled mobile numbers with Meta for verification and blocking of WhatsApp accounts associated with these numbers. The regulator has also agreed on a permanent mechanism with Meta under which 5,000 recycled numbers will be shared with the platform every month to identify and deactivate associated accounts.
According to PTA officials, telecom operators currently hold around 16 million recycled mobile numbers, posing a growing risk of fraud when WhatsApp accounts registered against these numbers remain active even after the original SIMs have been deactivated or cancelled.
Officials said that such accounts could be misused by new subscribers acquiring recycled numbers, creating opportunities for fraudulent activities and cybercrime.
Under the agreed mechanism, WhatsApp accounts associated with recycled numbers will be blocked in phases to prevent their misuse. The development follows complaints regarding cyber fraud through WhatsApp accounts linked to inactive mobile numbers, prompting the PTA to engage with Meta for a coordinated solution.
PTA officials further disclosed that Meta had resolved 82 percent of the complaints forwarded by the regulator during the previous year, reflecting improved coordination between the two sides. The latest initiative is aimed at strengthening digital security, protecting mobile subscribers and preventing the misuse of WhatsApp accounts following the recycling of mobile numbers by telecom operators.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) has decided to expand its mobile network quality inspections to more cities across Pakistan, following its recent field survey in Islamabad and Rawalpindi.
According to PTA officials, the regulator is planning to conduct similar field surveys in Lahore, Karachi, and Peshawar to assess the performance of cellular mobile operators and identify areas where consumers continue to face connectivity issues.
The authority is expected to begin the next phase of inspections in Lahore and Karachi in the coming days, while Peshawar is also included in the broader inspection plan. However, specific dates for the upcoming visits have not yet been announced.
The surveys will focus on mobile network coverage, voice call quality, call connectivity, mobile internet performance, and the overall quality of services being provided to consumers.
PTA officials, along with representatives of the Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication and cellular mobile operators, will participate in the field exercises.
The regulator’s zonal office teams are already monitoring mobile network performance across different parts of the country, according to officials.
The decision comes shortly after PTA Chairman Major General (R) Hafeez Ur Rehman personally led a high-level Quality of Experience (QoE) and Quality of Service (QoS) survey across Islamabad and Rawalpindi on November 5.
During the exercise, three dedicated teams conducted live voice calls and mobile internet speed tests at several locations, including Islamabad International Airport, Constitution Avenue, Murree Road, Rawal Road, and T-Chowk.
PTA initially described the network performance observed during the twin cities survey as excellent. However, individual speed test readings highlighted significant variations in download and upload speeds across different mobile operators and locations.
PTA Preparing Detailed Report on Twin Cities Survey as 5G Rollout Remains a Priority
PTA officials have confirmed that a comprehensive report on the Islamabad and Rawalpindi field survey is currently being prepared and will be submitted to the authority.
The report will examine mobile network performance, service quality, and connectivity issues identified during the inspection.
It is expected to help the regulator identify areas requiring further improvement and assess the quality of services available to mobile consumers.
Meanwhile, the expansion of field inspections also comes as Pakistan moves forward with the deployment of 5G services following the spectrum auction.
According to PTA officials, particular attention is being given to the availability of 5G services in major cities.
However, the regulator is also emphasizing that the expansion of 5G networks should not come at the expense of existing 4G services.
PTA intends to focus on improving current 4G network coverage, service quality, and connectivity alongside the rollout of next-generation mobile technology.
This is particularly important for millions of consumers who continue to rely on 4G networks for everyday communication, online work, education, and digital services.
The upcoming inspections in Lahore, Karachi, and Peshawar will provide another opportunity to assess how mobile operators are performing in different urban environments.
For consumers, however, the real test will be whether these regulatory inspections result in measurable and sustained improvements in mobile internet speeds, call quality and network availability.
The authority has not yet shared a detailed schedule or specific inspection routes for the next phase of surveys.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) recently conducted a high-level mobile network quality inspection across Islamabad and Rawalpindi, reporting excellent initial performance. However, location-wise speed test results reveal considerable differences in mobile internet speeds between Jazz, Zong and PTML (Ufone).
The results from six locations, including Khanna East, Koral Chowk, Japan Road, PWD, T-Chowk Rawat, and DHA Phase 2, show that network performance varies significantly depending on the operator and location.
According to the shared speed test figures, Zong recorded the highest download speed of 93.1 Mbps in DHA Phase 2, followed by 75.6 Mbps at Koral Chowk and 72.6 Mbps at Khanna East.
Jazz, meanwhile, recorded its highest reported download speed of 51.4 Mbps at Khanna East, but its performance dropped sharply to just 4.09 Mbps in PWD.
PTML, which operates Ufone, delivered its strongest reported download speed of 72.6 Mbps in DHA Phase 2, although its upload speed at the same location stood at just 3.70 Mbps.
The figures highlight an important point: strong mobile internet performance in one area does not necessarily translate into a similar experience elsewhere, even within the same city.

One of the most striking differences was recorded in PWD, where Zong achieved a download speed of 65.6 Mbps compared to just 4.09 Mbps on Jazz.
This means Zong’s measured download speed was approximately 16 times higher than Jazz’s at that particular location.
A similar gap was observed at Koral Chowk, where Zong delivered 75.6 Mbps, followed by PTML at 47.3 Mbps and Jazz at 23.6 Mbps.
However, download speeds alone do not tell the complete story.
At DHA Phase 2, Zong achieved the highest download speed of 93.1 Mbps, but its upload speed was limited to 4.49 Mbps. PTML displayed a similar pattern, recording 72.6 Mbps download and just 3.70 Mbps upload.
Jazz, despite recording a lower download speed of 28.7 Mbps at the same location, delivered a considerably higher upload speed of 18.4 Mbps.
The results suggest that users may experience different network performance depending on whether they are downloading content, uploading videos, making video calls or using other data-intensive applications.
Upload performance was particularly strong for Zong at PWD, where it reached 42.4 Mbps, the highest upload reading in the shared results.
At Japan Road, both Jazz and PTML recorded relatively modest download speeds of 16.6 Mbps and 18.5 Mbps, respectively.
At T-Chowk Rawat, PTML led in download performance with 48.8 Mbps compared to Jazz’s 22.4 Mbps, while Jazz delivered the faster upload speed.
The latest figures come after PTA Chairman Major General (R) Hafeez Ur Rehman personally led a Quality of Experience (QoE) and Quality of Service (QoS) field survey across the twin cities on November 5.
PTA’s official statement described the initial survey findings as excellent, reflecting generally reliable telecom services along the inspected routes.
However, these individual speed readings demonstrate that considerable variations can exist between operators and locations, even when the overall assessment is positive.
It is important to note that the shared figures represent individual speed test readings rather than a comprehensive network benchmark. Details such as the exact testing times, devices, signal conditions, and number of test repetitions were not provided.
Therefore, the results should not be used to declare any operator the overall fastest network in Islamabad or Rawalpindi.
With thousands of telecom complaints recorded by PTA in September, the findings reinforce the importance of checking actual network performance in their own areas instead of relying solely on advertised coverage and download speeds.
The bigger question is whether PTA’s ongoing monitoring will translate into more consistent 4G performance, particularly in locations where significant differences between operators remain visible.

Nothing Teases New AI-Native Product Ahead of December Launch
Nothing has also shared a teaser image that provides a limited look at the upcoming device. The image shows a product with rounded corners and curved edges, but it does not reveal enough details to identify its exact form or purpose.
Pei said the product will carry the personality and attention to detail associated with Nothing’s existing devices. He also highlighted the company’s ability to develop both hardware and software internally, which gives it an advantage when building new AI-focused products.
However, Nothing has confirmed whether the device will be a wearable, a personal AI assistant, or something entirely different.
See Also: Nothing Phone (4a) Series Arrives in Pakistan with Updated Design and Enhanced Performance
Nothing’s Plans for AI Hardware
In his article, Pei discussed how artificial intelligence could gradually move beyond its current role as a productivity tool. He suggested that future AI technology could become more closely integrated into everyday life and handle tasks on behalf of users.
He also pointed out that new technologies often gain acceptance in workplaces before becoming common in homes.
Nothing is reportedly exploring other AI-powered devices as well. Previous reports have suggested that the company is working on smart glasses, potentially including versions with and without built-in cameras.
For now, the company has kept most details about its upcoming product under wraps. More information is expected to emerge as the December launch approaches.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Fintech soonicorn Cashfree Payments has launched ‘Checkout for Agents’, a new tool that enables AI agents to process customer payments seamlessly.
The new feature is built on the open-source WebMCP (model context protocol). The startup claims that merchants using Cashfree’s checkout page can avail the service without requiring any code changes or technical updates.
The new solution aims to address a critical friction point in agentic commerce. While global purchases initiated by AI agents are projected to hit $1.5 Tn by 2030, traditional web interfaces remain optimised for human navigation. Hence, AI agents consume nearly 2 Mn tokens on average to decode the web page when they need to execute a transaction.
By leveraging WebMCP, Cashfree claims that its new checkout tool directly communicates all the available actions to the AI agents, including reading order total and selecting payment mode. The startup claims its solution reduces token consumption by over 40%.
The architecture also allows personal AI assistants like Instinct, Meta’s Muse, and Grok Bot to reach the final payment step with fewer errors and lower drop-off rates, while leaving the final transaction authorisation with the user.
“If an agent is visiting and browsing the merchant’s website, there will not be any drop off at the payment layer. Your speed of conversion will increase, token usage will drop, and the success rate will be near 100% as far as an agent making a payment is concerned,” Cashfree cofounder Reeju Datta told Inc42.
He foresees AI agents driving a significant share of traffic to Cashfree’s customers in the future. “Agent traffic has grown around 4-5X annually and converts 5X better than my SEO traffic. The lifetime value (LTV) of such users is also much much higher,” Datta added.
On a question about AI agents taking unauthorised or unintended actions, Datta claimed that Cashfree’s latest offering preserves existing authorisation mechanisms and creates no heightened vulnerabilities. For instance, if the final payment authorisation step requires an OTP, then the user would still have to enter the pin to approve the payment.
Founded in 2015 by Datta and Akash Sinha, Cashfree Payments offers digital payment solutions such as payment gateway, cross-border payments, payout solutions and banking APIs. It claims to process over $80 Bn in annual transaction volumes for over 10 Lakh businesses, including the likes of MakeMyTrip, Zomato, CRED, and Delhivery.
Cashfree isn’t the only one in India’s startup ecosystem betting on agentic commerce. Its IPO-bound rival Razorpay is also repositioning itself as an AI-powered business operating system through its Agent Studio and agentic commerce push.
Then, there is Bengaluru-based Nudge that helps ecommerce brands optimise product discovery and conversions inside AI platforms. Foodtech giant Swiggy is also enabling users to interact with its app through external AI agents to discover food, build carts, place orders, and book restaurant tables.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
Nigerian e-health startup Helium Health has received a US$2.5 million grant from Google.org to roll out artificial intelligence (AI) solutions that improve maternal healthcare delivery in the country.
Founded in 2016, Helium Health takes hospitals and clinics instantly digital with its flagship Electronic Medical Records/Hospital Management Information System (EMR/HMIS) product, the most widely used such solution in West Africa.
The company is among 15 global recipients of the US$30 million Google.org Impact Challenge: AI for Government Innovation. The initiative backs organisations that work with governments to improve public service delivery.
The funding will support the deployment of clinical AI models through Helium Health’s maternal health initiative, HeliumMum, across the Lagos, Delta, Kano and Oyo states. Lagos will serve as the main launchpad. Helium Health will also join a dedicated Google.org Accelerator programme, where it will receive technical support from Google engineers and AI product experts.
Through HeliumMum, Helium Health will deploy AI tools that help pregnant women identify potential complications early and connect them with appropriate healthcare providers. The platform links women to facilities equipped with electronic medical records and AI-powered clinical decision support systems, so healthcare professionals can make better-informed decisions. It will also give governments actionable data to strengthen maternal health services and identify gaps in care.
The startup aims to reach an additional 1.9 million women over three years and contribute to a 30 per cent reduction in maternal mortality. Helium Health has already reached more than 3.5 million women through its maternal health initiatives over the past decade.
“Nigeria accounts for nearly three in every 10 maternal deaths globally. Behind every maternal death is a woman whose family expected her to come home,” said Dr Shona Oluwatola, head of public health at Helium Health.
“By equipping the 15 selected organisations with funding and pro bono support from Google’s own AI experts, we are empowering the people closest to the problem to show what is truly possible,” said Maggie Johnson, global head of Google.org.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Airlink Communication Limited has officially entered Pakistan’s electric vehicle industry with the launch of AirV, its new electric bike brand. The move marks a major step in the company’s business expansion as it looks beyond smartphones and consumer electronics to explore opportunities in electric mobility.
AirV has entered the market with 11 electric bike models divided into six different series. The lineup targets customers with varying riding needs and preferences, including individual and enterprise users.
Airlink Launches AirV Electric Bike Brand in Pakistan With 11 Models
The new electric bikes come with several technology-based features, including cruise control, regenerative battery technology, NFC functionality, and anti-theft protection. AirV also offers lithium battery options, while selected models provide a riding range of up to 200 kilometres on a single charge.
The company aims to offer different mobility options through its new brand by combining modern designs with practical features and improved battery technology.
Airlink Brings Its Manufacturing and Distribution Experience
Airlink plans to use its existing manufacturing, distribution, and retail network to establish AirV in Pakistan’s growing electric vehicle market. The company has more than seven years of industry experience and operates across manufacturing, nationwide distribution, retail, e-commerce and consumer financing.
It also has partnerships with several international technology brands, including Samsung, Xiaomi, TECNO, itel, Hisense and Acer. Airlink is also an Apple Authorized Reseller.
The company operates a manufacturing facility at Sundar Industrial Estate in Lahore. It plans to use this infrastructure and its nationwide network of retailers and business partners to make AirV products accessible to customers across Pakistan.
This existing business network could help the company build customer trust and provide better market coverage as it expands into electric mobility.
Airlink Chairman Shares Vision Behind AirV
The AirV brand was formally inaugurated by Aslam Hayat Piracha, Chairman of Airlink Communication Limited.
Speaking at the launch, Piracha said the company wants to support Pakistan’s progress through innovation and modern technology. He added that AirV aims to make reliable and technology-driven transportation more accessible and affordable.
He also highlighted the company’s interest in contributing to Pakistan’s electric vehicle ecosystem through local manufacturing, technological development and sustainable business practices.
Meanwhile, Muzzaffar Hayat Paracha, Group CEO of Airlink, said the company has always focused on identifying new business opportunities and turning them into successful ventures.
He noted that Pakistan’s shift towards electric mobility presents significant opportunities for the transportation industry. According to him, Airlink’s plans extend beyond electric bikes, as the company wants to develop a broader mobility business for individual and enterprise customers.
See Also: Thatta Cement Enters Pakistan’s EV Market With Plans to Import Affordable Chinese Electric Cars
AirV Marks Airlink’s Business Expansion
The launch event brought together industry representatives, business partners, media professionals, influencers and other guests.
With AirV, Airlink is entering a new business segment while using its existing strengths in manufacturing, distribution and retail. The company aims to develop the brand into a major player in Pakistan’s electric mobility market.
The launch also reflects growing interest among local businesses in electric transportation and the potential of domestic manufacturing. However, AirV’s market performance will depend on factors such as pricing, battery performance, after-sales support, and the availability of charging facilities.
For now, the introduction of 11 models gives Airlink a starting point to compete in Pakistan’s expanding electric bike market.
