The auction will be conducted on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (E-Kuber) system on November 09, 2026 (Monday). The Government Stock up to ten per cent of the notified amount of the sale of each stock will be allotted to eligible individuals and institutions, subject to a maximum limit of one per cent of its notified amount for a single bid per stock as per the ‘Scheme for Non-competitive Bidding Facility’. Individual investors can also place bids as per the non-competitive scheme through the Retail Direct portal (https://rbiretaildirect.org.in).
Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (E-Kuber) system on November 09, 2026 (Monday). The competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 A.M. and 11:30 A.M. and non-competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 A.M. and 11:00 A.M.
In case of technical difficulties, Core Banking Operations Team may be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-69870466, 022-69870415).
For other auction related difficulties, IDMD Auction Team can be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-22702431, 022-22705125).
Only in the event of system failure, physical bids would be accepted. Such physical bids should be submitted to the Public Debt Office (email; Phone no: 022-22603456, 022-22603457, 022-22603190) in the prescribed form obtainable from RBI website (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewForms.aspx) before the auction timing ends.
The yield per cent per annum or the price as the case may be, expected by the bidder should be expressed up to two decimal points. An investor can submit more than one competitive bid at same/different rates of yield or prices in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (E-Kuber) system. However, the aggregate amount of bids submitted by a bidder should not exceed the notified amount for each State.
The Reserve Bank of India will determine the maximum yield / minimum price at which bids will be accepted. Stock will be issued for a minimum nominal amount of ₹10,000.00 and in multiples of ₹10,000.00 thereafter.
The results of the auction will be announced on November 09, 2026 (Monday) and payment by successful bidders will be made during banking hours on November 11, 2026 (Wednesday) at Mumbai and at respective Regional Offices of RBI.
The new State Government Stocks will bear interest at the rates determined by RBI at the auctions. For the new stock, interest will be paid half yearly on May 11 and November 11 of each year till maturity. For the re-issued Government Stock, interest will be paid at the rate as determined on the date of original issue of Government Stock and will be paid on half yearly basis till maturity. The Stocks will be governed by the provisions of the Government Securities Act, 2006 and the Government Securities Regulations, 2007.
The investment in State Government Stocks will be reckoned as an eligible investment in Government Securities by banks for the purpose of Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) under Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949. The stocks will qualify for the ready forward facility.
Ajit Prasad          
Deputy General Manager
(Communications)

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has tied property valuations in Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) rural areas to the latest rates issued from time to time by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue)/District Collector, Islamabad, and has also set fresh fair market values for immovable property in Abbottabad, through two notifications dated November 5, 2026.
Under SRO 2061(I)/2026, the FBR amends SRO 644(I)/2026 of April 16, 2026 so ICT rural valuations follow the District Collector’s latest tables rather than a fixed federal schedule. Separately, SRO 2060(I)/2026, issued under Section 68 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, replaces the earlier Abbottabad schedule in SRO 1679(I)/2024 of October 29, 2024.
Abbottabad Residential Open Plots
Residential open plots in Main Bazaar, Sadar Bazaar, Jinnah Masjid Bazaar, Sarafa Bazaar, Gurdwara Gali and Kutcheri Road have been valued at Rs. 1.25 million per marla. Abbottabad Bazaar is set at Rs. 970,000 per marla, while Iqbal Road is valued at Rs. 800,000 per marla.
Commercial Rates Peak at Main Bazaar
Commercial open plots in Main Bazaar and adjoining specified areas carry the highest rate at Rs. 5.8 million per marla. Abbottabad Bazaar is valued at Rs. 4.4 million per marla, and Mansehra Road from Fawara Chowk to Mian Gi Hotel at Rs. 4 million per marla.
Other commercial rates include Rs. 3.1 million per marla for Jinnahabad, Rs. 3 million for Havelian Bazaar and Nathia Gali Main Road, and Rs. 2.5 million for College Road Mandian, Old College Road Mandian, Comsats Road, Murree Road and Changla Gali.
Built Property Rates by Age
For constructed residential and commercial properties, the notification adds age-based rates to the land values: Rs. 2,000 per square foot for buildings up to five years old, Rs. 1,000 per square foot for those more than five and up to 10 years old, and Rs. 500 per square foot for buildings older than 10 years.
The revisions follow earlier FBR moves on capital property tables, including when Islamabad property valuations were cut by up to 30 percent and when the board reduced property valuation rates in five Punjab cities.
The post FBR Sets New Property Rates for Islamabad Rural Areas and Abbottabad appeared first on ProPakistani.

items.content:
By John Alechenu
ABUJA — High Chief Peter Ameh, the National Democratic Congress (NDC) senatorial candidate for Kogi East, has warned opposition parties against celebrating the court judgment that sacked the David Mark-led National Working Committee of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and nullified Atiku Abubakar’s candidacy.
Ameh said the ruling should not be seen as a victory for any political camp, warning that the All Progressives Congress (APC) stood to benefit from divisions within the opposition.
He spoke in Abuja on Thursday, urging opposition parties to resist attempts to turn the judgment into an opportunity for political infighting.
According to him, the APC would be comfortable with any opposition party being weakened, regardless of the party’s identity or political affiliation.
“The APC, which is the ultimate beneficiary of this judgment, will be happy keeping any party in the opposition weakened. They do not care which party logo you wave. They want us fighting each other so we never notice the real game being played against all of us,” he said.
Ameh cautioned that what might appear to be a victory for one faction today could become a tool against another political group tomorrow.
“Before anyone starts dancing, remember: today’s victory for one camp is tomorrow’s weapon against another. The same forces that can erase one candidate or one leadership structure can just as easily turn on yours when it becomes convenient. Political affiliation is not a shield,” he said.
He added: “Stay alert. This is not a win for any side. It is a warning.”
The NDC candidate urged opposition parties to channel their energy towards demanding free, fair and credible elections, rather than engaging in disputes over political leadership and candidacies.
He also criticised the APC-led administration, accusing it of failing to deliver good governance to Nigerians over the past 11 years.
“For 11 years, this APC government has failed to provide good governance to Nigerians. We must collectively work to bring an end to its rule. APC is the problem,” Ameh declared.
The post Atiku Verdict: APC wants opposition fighting – Ameh appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
…Zulum pledges business-friendly reforms
By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri
The United Nations (UN), European Union (EU), German Government and other development partners are supporting efforts to attract private investment to Borno State to create jobs and help displaced families rebuild their livelihoods.
At the third Borno State Private Sector Engagement and Investment Roundtable in Abuja on Thursday, representatives of the UN, EU and German Embassy pledged continued support for the state’s recovery through private sector investment.
The Governor Babagana Zulum-led administration initiated the roundtable series with a meeting in Lagos, focusing on financing bankable projects and supporting small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).
The second edition was held in Kano, with emphasis on agriculture, livestock, fisheries and infrastructure.
More than 50 prospective investors attended the Abuja roundtable.
The representative of the UN Resident Coordinator’s Office in Nigeria, Thembekile Dube-Nanbe, urged development partners to translate the investment initiative into concrete action.
“Let us identify viable investment opportunities, mobilise capital, establish lasting partnerships, and commit to measurable results,” Dube-Nanbe said.
The EU Head of Human Development, Laila Ben Amor Mathieu, said the Union had supported Borno through its most difficult years by providing humanitarian assistance and backing stabilisation and recovery efforts.
“Grants and public budgets alone will not finance recovery at the scale Borno needs. Private capital must play its part, and the role of us partners is to make that possible,” Mathieu said.
She said investors could support the proposed Borno State Durable Solutions Trust Fund or pursue commercially viable projects backed by incentives, including access to land, industrial hubs and tax measures.
Mathieu urged businesses to identify projects for further consideration, partner with local companies and create opportunities for women and young people.
“Borno is becoming an investment story. The European Union is proud to be part of it,” she said.
The Head of Development Cooperation at the German Embassy, Dr Karen Jansen, commended Governor Zulum for restoring communities, rebuilding infrastructure and public services, and opening the state’s economy to investors.
She urged investors to sustain their commitments as the economy grows, assuring the state of Germany’s continued support.
“Mobilising private sector investment, including through blended finance, will be essential to complement development cooperation and support Borno’s sustainable reconstruction,” Jansen said.
Governor Zulum, who was represented by his Chief of Staff, Dr Babagana Mustapha Mallumbe, urged private investors to take advantage of business opportunities in the state, assuring them of government support and simpler administrative procedures.
He said improvements in security and ongoing reforms were helping Borno move from emergency humanitarian assistance towards economic recovery.
The governor invited businesses to invest in commercial farming, livestock production, fisheries and manufacturing, while encouraging financial institutions to expand credit facilities for small businesses.
“Government’s role is to build the foundation, establish the security, and create the regulatory framework. But the private sector is the ultimate engine of wealth creation, job opportunities, and lasting prosperity,” he said.
Zulum said the Borno State Investment Promotion Agency was simplifying procedures for investors, supported by land administration reforms, fiscal incentives and public-private partnership frameworks designed to protect investments.

He said the agency had received numerous requests for medical intervention from different parts of the state, reflecting growing concern over the incidents.
According to him, two snakebite patients were successfully discharged within the last two weeks, while others remained on admission and were receiving treatment.
Dzungwe warned against delays in seeking medical attention, stressing that late presentation at health facilities could result in severe complications and poor health outcomes.
He urged members of the public to seek immediate medical attention at appropriate health facilities whenever snakebite incidents occur.
Meanwhile, Benue SEMA has urged the public to disregard what it described as misleading reports and politically motivated narratives surrounding snakebite incidents in the state, particularly those involving IDPs.
The agency maintained that health emergencies and the lives of vulnerable citizens should not be subjected to political manipulation.
It reaffirmed its commitment to providing timely medical assistance to snakebite victims and others affected by emergencies, irrespective of their status or location.

items.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni
The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) has inducted more than 100 volunteers into its LASTMA Mayors traffic advocacy network to support efforts to manage anticipated traffic congestion during the Yuletide and year-end ‘Detty December’ celebrations.
The investiture and induction ceremony, held at the agency’s headquarters in Lagos, was part of efforts to strengthen community participation in traffic management, promote voluntary compliance with traffic regulations and support enforcement officers along busy roads.
Speaking at the event, LASTMA General Manager, Olalekan Bakare-Oki, said managing traffic in Lagos required collective responsibility rather than reliance on government enforcement alone.
He said the newly inducted volunteers would strengthen public enlightenment campaigns and support field operations through grassroots advocacy, voluntary interventions and targeted sensitisation.
“Sustainable mobility governance relies on collective ownership, shared accountability, and the active participation of every citizen.
“The enlistment of these LASTMA Mayors will substantially reinforce our public enlightenment architecture and augment field operations through voluntary interventions, grassroots advocacy, and targeted sensitisation,” Bakare-Oki said.
He described the volunteers as community ambassadors whose closeness to residents, commercial transport operators and market associations would help promote road discipline, particularly during the festive season.
The LASTMA boss also appealed to Christian and Islamic leaders to use their platforms to reinforce road safety messages among their congregations.
“We are soliciting the strategic partnership of religious leaders to deploy their moral authority towards amplifying our road safety campaign.
“Clerics, imams, and pastors should consistently incorporate messages of responsible motoring, pedestrian awareness, and strict adherence to traffic laws into their sermons and fellowship gatherings,” he said.
Bakare-Oki cautioned motorists against dangerous practices, including driving against traffic, popularly known as one-way, excessive speeding, reckless overtaking and indiscriminate parking.
He also urged vehicle owners to ensure proper maintenance of their brakes, tyres, steering systems and lights before embarking on journeys.
“The commercial excitement and social festivities associated with December must not degenerate into traffic indiscipline or preventable road tragedies,” he said, urging motorists to exercise patience and restraint.
Also speaking, LASTMA’s Director of Traffic Advocacy and Special Mayors, Mr Awoyemi Jimmy, assured residents that the agency would sustain operational surveillance and strategic deployment of officers along critical traffic corridors throughout the holiday season.
The Coordinator of the State Mayors of Traffic (SMT), Mr Tajudeen Othman, pledged that the newly inducted volunteers would discharge their responsibilities with integrity and discipline, using their community networks to complement the state’s traffic management efforts.

ONITSHA — Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has called for a strategic partnership between the state government and the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) to strengthen the healthcare system and improve access to quality pharmaceutical services.
Soludo made the call on Wednesday while declaring open the ongoing four-day 99th Annual National Delegate Conference of the society in Awka, stressing that pharmacists played a critical role in building an effective healthcare system.
Describing the gathering, tagged ‘Ijele 2026’, as historic, the governor said his administration had prioritised human capital development, education and healthcare.
He cited the introduction of free education from kindergarten to Senior Secondary School Three (SS3), as well as free antenatal care in government hospitals, as part of his administration’s interventions in the sectors.
Soludo also said his government had revamped the state’s primary healthcare system, disclosing that more than 250,000 expectant mothers had benefited from zero-cost antenatal care, while over 950 free Caesarean Section operations had been performed.
“To further solidify Anambra’s position as the nation’s premier pharma hub, let me also inform you that work on the development of the state-of-the-art Pharmaceutical Hub in Oba, alongside the upcoming Coordinated Wholesale Centre slated for delivery early next year, is currently ongoing in the state,” he said.
The governor urged the PSN leadership to work closely with the state government to enforce safety standards in pharmaceutical operations and tackle the circulation of counterfeit drugs.
He also challenged the society to address unethical practices within the profession, particularly the activities of illegal drug outlets operating under the guise of licensed pharmacies.
Earlier, the President of the PSN, Pharm. Ayuba Tanko Ibrahim, expressed appreciation to Soludo for his support for the pharmaceutical profession and the decision to host the society’s flagship national conference in Anambra.
Ibrahim said the conference, themed, “One Health, One Pharmacy: Bridging Knowledge, Practice and Policy for National Impact”, was designed to strengthen collaboration among stakeholders and promote the contribution of pharmacy to national development.
He commended the governor’s vision and leadership, recalling that his earlier prediction of Soludo’s electoral victory had come to pass.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
…says N16.27bn disbursed to 115,000 beneficiaries in 25 states, FCT
…as agriculture records 4.39% growth, contributes 26.15% to GDP
By Gabriel Ewepu
The Federal Government has urged state governments to align agricultural production with consumption and industrial demand to protect farmers from losses, strengthen food supply chains and stabilise food prices.
The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Abubakar Kyari, gave the charge on Thursday, November 5, 2026, at the 48th meeting of the National Council on Agriculture and Food Security (NCAFS), held at Hotel Presidential, Enugu.
The meeting, themed, “Enhancing Agricultural Value Chains, Agro-Industrialisation and Market Access for Economic Growth,” brought together commissioners of agriculture from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, development partners and other stakeholders to discuss strategies for strengthening the agricultural sector.
Kyari said developments in the past three years had exposed an imbalance in agricultural markets, with rising food prices putting pressure on households, while subsequent price declines left farmers struggling to recover production costs.
He recalled that food inflation peaked at 40.87 per cent in June 2024 before declining to 8.89 per cent in January 2026, its first single-digit reading in more than a decade. However, it rose again to 19.59 per cent by September 2026, as production and input costs continued to affect farmers and consumers.
The minister attributed part of the renewed pressure to escalating conflict in the Middle East, which disrupted energy, shipping and fertiliser markets, pushing urea prices above $850 per tonne in April 2026 and increasing input, energy and transportation costs across agricultural value chains.
He said President Bola Tinubu had responded by prioritising investment in agricultural production, financing and market development.
According to him, the President has strengthened the operationalisation of the National Agricultural Development Fund (NADF), prioritised the recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture (BOA) and supported the introduction of the N200 billion Guaranteed Minimum Price Programme.
Kyari said the interventions were designed to protect farmers’ incentives to produce while ensuring the availability of affordable food for households, rather than relying solely on short-term price relief.
He disclosed that the NADF’s Farm Input Support Programme had reached more than 115,000 beneficiaries across 25 states and the FCT, with N16.27 billion disbursed through agribusiness financing.
Similarly, he said the Bank of Agriculture had financed more than 500,000 smallholder farmers and was anchoring the Guaranteed Minimum Price Programme, which seeks to protect eligible farmers against distress sales through structured purchases and commodity aggregation.
On mechanisation, Kyari said the second phase of the Renewed Hope National Agricultural Mechanisation Programme, involving 1,500 tractors and more than 8,000 pieces of complementary equipment, was underway.
He said the first phase had delivered 2,000 tractors and more than 9,000 implements, adding that the initiative was intended to expand farmers’ access to mechanised services, reduce production costs and improve productivity.
Using maize production as an example, the minister explained that fluctuations in commodity prices affected not only farmers but also feed mills, poultry producers, food processors and consumers.
He stressed that processors needed raw materials in the right quantities and quality, delivered at commercially viable costs, rather than relying on production estimates.
Kyari said this made it necessary to build agricultural value chains that effectively linked production with processing, investment and dependable markets.
He further disclosed that the Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones initiative was expanding domestic value addition, while the Rural Access and Agricultural Marketing Project was improving connectivity between farming communities and markets.
He added that the World Bank-supported AGROW Project, which was being prepared for implementation, would strengthen commercial partnerships between smallholder farmers and agribusinesses.
The minister also said the African Continental Free Trade Area offered opportunities for Nigerian agricultural products but cautioned that access to regional and international markets depended on compliance with accepted standards for quality, safety, traceability and consistency of supply.
Ahead of the 2027 farming season, Kyari challenged commissioners of agriculture to improve production forecasts, align agricultural supply with industrial demand and strengthen coordination between producing and consuming areas.
He said such alignment would protect farmers from losses, ensure factories received raw materials in the required quantities and quality, stabilise food prices and minimise waste across agricultural value chains.
Citing figures from the National Bureau of Statistics, the minister said Nigeria’s economy grew by 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, while agriculture recorded 4.39 per cent growth and contributed 26.15 per cent to real Gross Domestic Product.
He added that agricultural value added reached N101.46 trillion at current prices in 2025.
Kyari described the progress as a collective achievement of the Federal and state governments, ministries, departments and agencies, development partners, research institutions, farmers’ organisations and the private sector.
He also commended Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah, for what he described as his commitment to accountability and measurable governance, noting that the governor’s presentation of his administration’s achievements against its manifesto commitments demonstrated an understanding of public service.
Reflecting on projects visited across the state, Kyari said, “Tomorrow is truly Here,” adding that he was particularly impressed by the governor’s humility and proactive approach to governance.
Mbah seeks shift from production to agro-industrialisation
Declaring the meeting open, Governor Mbah said Nigeria’s agricultural challenge was not a shortage of potential or policies but the inability to translate available opportunities and policy frameworks into an agricultural economy capable of delivering prosperity on a large scale.
He said farmers could record impressive harvests and still struggle to earn decent incomes, stressing the need to move beyond production figures to building viable agricultural businesses and markets.
Mbah disclosed that his administration was pursuing a plan to grow Enugu State’s economy from approximately $4.4 billion to $30 billion, with agriculture identified as one of the principal drivers.
He said agriculture contributed approximately 40 per cent of the state’s GDP when his administration assumed office, adding that his government had since repositioned the sector towards agro-industrialisation.
According to him, the policy shift moved the focus of the Ministry of Agriculture from how much farmers could produce to how much economic value could be created from their output.
Listing the administration’s initiatives, the governor said it had supported more than 60,000 farmers, assembled 107 tractors in Enugu, digitally registered over 84,000 farmers, introduced the 260 Farm Estates Programme and established a 187,000-hectare Land Bank.
Other initiatives, he said, included the expansion of palm and Songhai projects, the revival of Sunrise Flour Mills, the establishment of a livestock centre at Ubahu and the development of a cargo terminal to connect Enugu’s agricultural produce to international markets.
Mbah said the meeting’s theme aligned with his administration’s strategy of connecting production with processing and markets, equipping farmers with machinery, knowledge and technology, attracting private investment and strengthening partnerships with communities.
He declared that Enugu was open for agribusiness, adding that agriculture must make a substantial contribution to President Tinubu’s ambition of building a $1 trillion Nigerian economy by 2030.
Enugu targets $12bn agricultural contribution
Earlier, the Enugu State Commissioner for Agriculture and Agro-Industrialisation, Dr Patrick Nwabueze Ubru, welcomed delegates to the state, which he said was hosting the council meeting for the first time in 14 years.
Ubru said the state was transitioning from largely subsistence agricultural production to a more productive, commercially driven and agro-industrialised economy under Mbah.
He said the transformation had received recognition from the Agricultural Society of Nigeria and the Nigerian Veterinary Medical Association.
The commissioner disclosed that delegates had visited the Enugu Tribu Songhai Farm, Enugu Ranch, an International Fund for Agricultural Development-supported rice mill and a cashew processing plant to assess the state’s agricultural investments and ongoing projects.
He also welcomed the extension of the IFAD programme into next year, describing it as a boost to the state’s agricultural development drive.
According to him, the investments were aimed at supporting farmers, who account for about 75 per cent of the state’s population, while advancing the administration’s ambition of growing the economy to $30 billion by 2031.
He said agriculture was expected to contribute 40 per cent, or $12 billion, to the target.
Ubru called on investors to explore opportunities in Enugu and the South-East, assuring them of the state’s readiness to provide warehouses for federal agricultural inputs and venues for relevant programmes.
He, however, stressed that increased agricultural production must be supported by processing facilities, storage infrastructure, efficient logistics and reliable markets to deliver sustainable economic benefits.

The mcap first crossed ₹100 lakh crore on March 12, 2014, and took 1,494 sessions to reach ₹200 lakh crore on February 4, 2021. The ₹300 lakh crore milestone was reached on July 6, 2023, after another 586 sessions, while the subsequent rise to ₹400 lakh crore took 181 sessions.135589318The latest milestone is significant because it comes even as the benchmark Sensex and several broader market indices remain below their record highs. The Sensex is still 7.6% below its peak of 85,836, recorded on September 26, 2024.The BSE MidCap 150 is 5.3% below its record of 17,373, reached on August 26, 2026, while the BSE SmallCap 250 is 8.4% below its peak of 7,514, recorded on September 23, 2024. The BSE MicroCap 250 is 7% below its record of 19,988, reached on September 8, 2026.Read more: Why Nithin Kamath believes NRI investing in India has become easier than everA steady stream of initial public offerings (IPOs) has also contributed to the expansion of the overall mcap, even as several benchmark indices remain below their peaks. In 2024, 94 companies made their mainboard debut, adding around ₹12 lakh crore to mcap on their listing days. In 2025, 115 companies listed, adding nearly ₹14 lakh crore, while 107 companies have listed so far in 2026, adding above ₹25 lakh crore."The large number of IPOs has added to the overall mcap. At the same time, several companies outside the main indices have participated in the rally, helping total mcap reach a record even as major indices remain below their peaks," said Ankur Punj, MD, Equirus Wealth.The latest milestone has also coincided with a sharp recovery in equities. The Sensex and Nifty have gained more than 8.1% each in six consecutive sessions. The BSE MidCap 150 has advanced over 8.4% in eight of the past nine sessions, while the BSE SmallCap 250 has risen around 7% in seven of past eight sessions.Read more: Titan Q2 Results: Profit jumps 54% YoY to Rs 1,722 crore; total income up 25%The rally has been supported by a decline of more than 19% in crude oil prices over the past three sessions, easing concerns over inflation, India's import bill and the rupee. Strong foreign portfolio investor (FPI) buying, with net inflows of over $3.4 billion in the past 12 sessions, positive global cues, reduced uncertainty following the US midterm elections and better-than-expected second-quarter earnings have also lifted investor sentiment."The momentum could continue in the near term if crude prices remain stable at lower levels and foreign inflows sustain. However, investors should remain cautious as geopolitical developments, crude price volatility and profit booking after the sharp rally could limit further upside," said Ravi Singh, chief research officer at Master Capital Services.

The recent listing activity, including the large Jio Platform IPO and several smaller issues, has contributed to the increase," said Sunny Agrawal, head of fundamental equity research at SBICAPS Securities.Growing interest in gold and silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs) has also encouraged retail investors to open demat accounts, Agrawal said. Investors can purchase these products through the secondary market using a demat account.Read more: Equity mutual fund inflows may drop 18% in October as midcap and hybrid funds lose momentum: NomuraThe pickup in demat account additions came with gains in benchmark indices, with the Sensex rising 2% and the Nifty gaining 1.9% in October. However, broader market segments, which see greater retail participation, underperformed.

By Olasunkanmi Akoni
LAGOS — The Society of Women Accountants of Nigeria (SWAN) has identified poor financial record-keeping, inadequate cash flow management, ineffective pricing and limited understanding of profitability as some of the factors undermining the survival and growth of businesses in Nigeria.
The association said many promising businesses struggle not necessarily because of a lack of opportunities or customers, but because their owners lack the financial knowledge required to manage resources and make informed decisions.
SWAN stated this at its 2026 Accounting for Non-Accountants Workshop, held on Thursday at the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (ICAN) Annex, Ebute-Metta, Lagos.
The workshop, organised as part of the association’s Corporate Social Responsibility initiatives, had the theme, “Business Made Easy: Practical Financial Skills.”
Speaking at the event, Chairperson of the Planning Committee, Mrs Ruth Jawo, said financial literacy had become essential for entrepreneurs, traders, professionals, employees and business managers, particularly amid the country’s challenging economic conditions.
According to her, financial knowledge would enable business owners to make informed decisions, manage resources effectively, avoid penalties and achieve sustainable growth.
“The theme reflects SWAN’s commitment to simplifying financial concepts and equipping participants with practical knowledge,” she said.
Jawo explained that the workshop was designed to bridge existing financial knowledge gaps and empower participants to manage their finances more confidently.
She expressed the expectation that participants would apply the knowledge acquired to improve their businesses, workplaces and households.
“Our expectation is that every participant leaves with valuable knowledge, practical tools and a renewed determination to develop better financial habits.
“The true success of this workshop will be measured not merely by attendance, but by the positive changes it inspires in businesses, workplaces and households,” she said.
Jawo urged participants to put the lessons into practice, describing the workshop as an opportunity to promote financial empowerment and sustainable growth.
She also commended SWAN’s leadership, facilitators, sponsors, partners, planning committee members and volunteers for their contributions to the programme.
Earlier, the National Chairperson of SWAN, Mrs Blessing Osakwe-Ogo, challenged participants to consider why businesses that record daily sales could still struggle to meet their financial obligations.
She said the problem was often not a shortage of customers, but inadequate financial records and the inability of business owners to interpret them.
“You cannot successfully grow what you do not properly measure, and you cannot protect a business whose financial position you do not understand,” she said.
Osakwe-Ogo explained that the programme was designed to equip entrepreneurs and business owners with practical knowledge of basic bookkeeping and accounting records.
She said the skills would help them track income and expenditure, monitor profitability, control costs and make informed business decisions.
The SWAN chairperson added that the association had expanded the programme to include discussions on emerging financial and tax laws, particularly Nigeria’s recent tax reforms and their implications for small businesses, entrepreneurs and business owners.
The workshop featured presentations by various facilitators on practical financial management skills.

items.content:
By Elizabeth Onyogha
Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) WKND 2026 opened in Lagos yesterday, bringing together leading creatives, investors, policymakers, business leaders and cultural figures from across Africa and the diaspora to explore investment, financing and commercial opportunities in the continent’s creative economy.
Hosted by the Federal Government of Nigeria and organised by the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) through its Creative Africa Nexus programme, the four-day event runs from November 5 to 8 under the theme, “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World.”
The programme covers film and television, music, fashion, sport, literature and publishing, gastronomy and visual arts, with emphasis on financing, intellectual property, technology, skills development, investment and market access.
Through platforms such as the CANEX Deal Room and Creative Pitch Sessions, the event seeks to connect entrepreneurs with financiers and investors, turning creative ideas and talent into viable businesses, partnerships and commercial opportunities.
The initiative builds on Afreximbank’s commitment to Africa’s creative and cultural industries, which began in 2020 and has since expanded to $2 billion in available financing.
The funding is designed to help African creators and businesses develop scalable enterprises, strengthen ownership of intellectual property and retain more of the economic value generated by the continent’s cultural and creative industries.
The opening ceremony is expected to feature addresses by ministers responsible for culture and creative industries from 11 African countries; Dr. George Elombi, President and Chairman of the Board of Directors of Afreximbank; Dr. Olajumoke Omoniyi Oduwole, Nigeria’s Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment; Wamkele Mene, Secretary-General of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat; and Babajide Sanwo-Olu, Governor of Lagos State, among other dignitaries.
Participants include Nobel Laureate, writer and playwright, Professor Wole Soyinka; Emmy Award-winning actor Uzo Aduba; filmmaker and actor Funke Akindele; actors Richard Mofe-Damijo and Thuso Mbedu; and former professional footballers Didier Drogba and Jay-Jay Okocha.
Musicians and entertainers, including Davido, Fally Ipupa, Flavour, Libianca and Charlotte Dipanda, are also scheduled to perform.
On November 6, a high-level conversation titled “One Market, One Culture: Building the Creative Economy of Global Africa” will examine how to translate the growing global influence of African culture into stronger creative businesses, exports and investment.
Speakers will include Soyinka; ministers responsible for culture and the arts from Côte d’Ivoire, South Africa and Rwanda; representatives of the International Finance Corporation; and Afreximbank officials.
Financing will also take centre stage at the Creative Economy Finance Summit, organised by Afreximbank in partnership with the Creative Economy Practice at Co-Creation Hub.
The summit will bring financial institutions and investors together to examine how creative-economy transactions can be structured, financed and de-risked.
CANEX Creations Inc. will lead discussions on unlocking investment in African intellectual property, while technology-focused sessions will examine artificial intelligence, authorship, intellectual property and the use of digital tools to develop globally competitive creative products.
The CANEX CreaThon, organised in partnership with pan-African technology company Gebeya, will bring creators, developers and innovators together to develop projects in music, video and gaming. Participants will have access to digital tools, mentorship and computing resources, alongside a $50,000 prize pool.
Film and television sessions will explore storytelling and the commercial infrastructure required to distribute African content internationally. These include “Stories Without Borders: Africa, Hollywood & the Global Diaspora,” featuring former Afreximbank President, Professor Benedict Oramah, and “Made in Africa, watched in Africa,” which will examine research on film distribution, audiences and financing across Egypt, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, Senegal and South Africa.
Sport will feature prominently, with discussions on athlete development, management and commercialisation. Drogba and Okocha are scheduled to participate in “When Giants Speak: The Business of the Game,” while a Legends Football Match will hold at Onikan Stadium on November 8.
Fashion activities will include masterclasses on building profitable African brands, strengthening textile value chains, expanding market access and protecting intellectual property, alongside the CANEX Fashion Show and Awards Night.
In gastronomy, the CANEX Junior Chefs Competition, Africa Jollof Wars Competition and live demonstrations will explore opportunities to commercialise African food, ingredients and culinary traditions in domestic and international markets.
Publishing and literature activities will feature the CANEX Book Factory, Book Fair, writers’ workshops, manuscript pitching sessions and the CANEX Prize for Publishing.
Visual arts programming will include exhibitions, collector engagement and practical sessions for artists.
On November 7, the event will host a major concert featuring performers from across Africa and the diaspora.
The final day, November 8, will feature cultural excursions, gastronomy activities, the CANEX Music Factory Songwriting Camp and the Legends Football Match.

By Udeme Akpan
The Rural Electrification Agency (REA) has flagged off the development of 37 mini-grid projects with a combined solar generation capacity of approximately 18.8 megawatts-peak (MWp) in Zamfara State.
The projects, comprising two interconnected and 35 isolated mini-grids, are expected to connect 125,106 households across Gummi, Gusau, Kaura Namoda, Maradun, Shinkafi, Tsafe and Zurmi Local Government Areas.
The groundbreaking ceremony on Wednesday also featured the unveiling of the Zamfara State Electricity Policy and the signing of a collaboration agreement between REA and the state government for the solarisation of public institutions.
Speaking at the event, Governor Dauda Lawal described the initiatives as important steps towards building an investment-friendly electricity market and accelerating economic development.
“Today, we are taking deliberate steps to redefine Zamfara’s electricity future. The unveiling of our State Electricity Policy is a statement of our intention to build a structured, investment-friendly and sustainable electricity market,” he said.
Lawal said reliable electricity was essential for agricultural transformation, industrial development, healthcare delivery, education and job creation.
Also speaking, the Minister of Power, Chief Joseph Olasunkanmi Tegbe, said the projects demonstrated the Federal Government’s commitment to expanding electricity access through decentralised infrastructure, state-level market development and private-sector investment.
“Electricity must do more than illuminate homes. It must power hospitals, strengthen educational institutions, support agricultural productivity, enable businesses and improve the quality of public services,” Tegbe said.
He pledged continued Federal Government support for states taking practical steps to develop their electricity markets.
In his remarks, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of REA, Dr. Abba Aliyu, said the intervention marked a shift from isolated infrastructure projects to an integrated electricity development model.
“Through the REA, we are advancing 37 mini-grid projects comprising two interconnected and 35 isolated systems, with approximately 18.8MWp of solar generation capacity and 125,106 planned electricity connections across seven Local Government Areas,” he said.
Aliyu estimated that the connections could potentially reach more than 625,000 people, based on an illustrative average of five persons per household-equivalent connection.
He said the initiative would support businesses, strengthen agricultural value chains, create jobs and attract private investment.
“Infrastructure without an enabling market framework risk becoming a collection of disconnected assets. When electricity infrastructure is supported by clear policies, effective institutions and predictable investment conditions, it becomes the foundation of a sustainable electricity economy,” he added.
Aliyu said the projects aligned with the $750 million World Bank-supported Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Scale-up (DARES) programme, which targets electricity access for approximately 17.5 million Nigerians through about 1,350 mini-grids and other distributed renewable energy solutions.
Meanwhile, Tegbe commissioned two solar mini-grid projects developed by the Zamfara State Government: a 1MW facility at Yariman Bakura Specialist Hospital and a 1.2MW installation at the Zamfara State Government House. Together, they have 2.2MW generation capacity and more than 3MW of battery storage.
The event also featured the unveiling of 100 electric vehicles under the ZamTaxi initiative, 10 electric tricycles for maternal healthcare transportation and two compressed natural gas buses donated by the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas.

items.content:
… Experts say poor tests fuel malaria misdiagnosis
By Chioma Obinna
Poor laboratory testing, inaccurate malaria diagnosis and unnecessary prescription of antimalarial drugs remain major challenges undermining Nigeria’s fight against malaria, health experts have warned.
The experts spoke as the Global Fund supported the training of 464 laboratory personnel across nine states to strengthen malaria and tuberculosis (TB) diagnosis, improve disease surveillance and ensure reliable laboratory results.
The integrated capacity-building programme, implemented through the National Malaria Elimination Programme (NMEP) and the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, was inaugurated at Mokland Hotel, Ibara, GRA, Abeokuta, Ogun State.
Speaking at the event, Consultant Medical Parasitologist, College of Medicine, University of Lagos, Professor Wellington Oyibo, said accurate diagnosis was critical to effective treatment, warning that laboratory personnel must be equipped to identify different malaria parasite species and distinguish infections from other illnesses.
He said microscopy remained essential despite the availability of rapid diagnostic tests and molecular technologies, stressing the need for quality assurance, proper documentation and timely reporting.
Oyibo said participants would be trained in slide preparation, microscopy, parasite identification, quality management and diagnostic best practices, including standards under ISO 15189.
He said the programme was designed to produce a critical mass of competent laboratory professionals who would also mentor colleagues in their respective facilities.
In a troubling revelation, Ogun State Malaria Elimination Programme Manager, Mrs Olamide Adeyinka, said patients’ insistence on having malaria despite negative test results was contributing to inappropriate treatment and unreliable malaria statistics.
She explained that some patients pressured health workers into prescribing antimalarial drugs even when laboratory investigations showed otherwise.
She said, “We have always recorded a high malaria test positivity rate, but many of these cases are linked to the failure to conduct proper tests or patients refusing to accept test results.”
Adeyinka disclosed that participants were drawn from all 20 local government areas of Ogun State, covering primary, secondary and tertiary health facilities, as well as private and faith-based institutions.
Also, Assistant Director, Medical Laboratory Services, Ogun State, Dr Simon Ijiezie, warned that inaccurate diagnosis was exposing people without malaria to unnecessary medication and financial losses.
He appealed to the state government to provide quality laboratory equipment, particularly microscopes, to ensure that the training translates into improved services.
“Without a good microscope, accurate diagnosis becomes difficult,” he said.
The Assistant Director, Medical Laboratory Services, Ogun State Primary Health Care Board, Mr Atinsola Ayodeji Olalekan, said strengthening primary healthcare laboratories would reduce pressure on secondary and tertiary hospitals.
“We believe that when primary healthcare facilities get things right, there will be less pressure on higher levels of healthcare institutions,” he said.
On tuberculosis diagnosis, the State TB Quality Assurance Officer, Mr Ogundimu Olusola, representing the state TB Programme Manager, Dr Jimoh Babatunde, warned that the growing use of molecular diagnostic technologies had reduced interest in microscopy among some laboratory workers.
“With the introduction of molecular diagnostic methods, some people have gradually lost interest in microscopy,” he said.
He expressed confidence that the training would produce 44 re-energised and better-equipped personnel in Ogun State.
Meanwhile, Assistant Director, Medical Laboratory Services, Hospital Management Board, Ogun State, Mrs Adebola Oke, urged participants to transfer their knowledge to colleagues after the programme.

Recall that the Federal High Court in Abuja had sacked the Senator David Mark-led executives of the African Democratic
Congress (ADC) and invalidated all actions they took on behalf of the party.
The actions included the nomination of a former vice president, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, as the party’s presidential candidate for the 2027 general elections.Track Exec Orders.
Atiku, whose name was earlier published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) as a candidate for the presidential poll, has since chosen a former governor of Rivers State, Rotimi Amaechi, as his running mate.Track Exec Orders
In the judgment delivered on Thursday by Justice Peter Lifu, the court declared illegal the Senator Mark-led Caretaker Committee of the ADC, which organised the primary election that produced Atiku as the party’s presidential flag bearer.
While reacting to the judgement of the court against the David Mark led leadership of the ADC, the NDC National Publicity Secretary said, “We have noted the Federal High Court judgment derecognizing the David Mark-led leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC).
“While we respect the judiciary as the last hope of the common man, we are concerned that judgments of this nature, if not carefully handled, risk creating the impression that the courts are being used to scuttle democracy and weaken opposition.
“The way some of these judgements are being churned out, especially from the High Courts suggests a deliberate effort to shut out the ADC from the forthcoming general elections by other means. This would amount to further shrinking the chances of multi-party democracy which is already under a big threat under the APC-led government of President Bola Ahmed
Tinubu.
“We therefore caution the judiciary to guard its independence, impartiality, and integrity at all times.

items.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
Ahead of January 16, 2027 presidential election, the former Minister of Defence, General Theophilus Danjuma (retd) and political leaders from the Northeast and North-Central geopolitical zones yesterday, met behind closed doors with President Bola Tinubu at the Aso Villa, Abuja.
The meeting it was gathered was part of have consultations aimed at mobilising support for the President.
The meeting focused on forging political cooperation, security and other issues affecting their communities, just as the visitors said there have been remarkable improvements in security and the administration’s contributions to the development of their communities.
The delegation was made up of the Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang; his Taraba State counterpart, Agbu Kefas; former Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Yakubu Dogara; Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (retd); and National Chairman of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), Professor Nentanwe Yilwatda.
Speaking with journalists after the meeting, Dogara disclosed that the delegation visited the President to express solidarity with his administration and explore strategies for strengthening political support for him across their communities.
He said the consultations were particularly significant as political activities gathered momentum ahead of the next general elections.
According to him: “We’re all here to show solidarity to Mr. President and then, in the spirit of the season, which you know is all about politicking, to discuss matters that affect our community and how we can best help in mobilising support for the President, who has done so much for our community.
“That is basically the reason why we’re here.”
The former House of Representatives Speaker expressed satisfaction with what he described as remarkable improvements in the security situation across parts of the country previously affected by insurgency, banditry and other violent crimes.
He said, although isolated security challenges persist, sustained government interventions have considerably reduced the frequency and severity of attacks in several troubled areas.
He recalled the dangerous security situation along the Abuja-Kaduna corridor, where travellers previously faced frequent attacks and kidnappings, noting that the situation had substantially improved.
“The issues relating to insecurity that accentuated over time, we have noticed that there is remarkable decline in these issues.
“Of course, there are pockets of crisis in some places, short of declaring victory, but there has been remarkable improvement.
“To travel from here to Kaduna, everybody knows what it was. At a point, they even brought down a moving train, but right now, some of those crises are not there”, he said.
Dogara attributed some of the improvements to the contributions of capable individuals appointed into strategic positions in the administration, particularly those familiar with the security challenges confronting affected communities.
He expressed optimism that continued commitment to the current interventions would produce more sustainable peace and stability.
“We believe that through some strategic placement of our sons and daughters within the government, they have shown remarkable leadership in dealing with these challenges.
“We believe that if these efforts are sustained going forward, we will arrive at a place where most of us will be very, very comfortable”, Dogara added.
Also speaking, Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, said political and community leaders in his state were making significant progress in rebuilding trust and promoting reconciliation among communities previously divided by ethnic and religious tensions.
He explained that the renewed engagement among leaders was beginning to encourage similar cooperation at the grassroots, particularly among young people.
“We are making tremendous progress, trying to make sure that leaders come together at various levels to rebuild the broken walls of trust, to rebuild understanding.
“Once people begin to see that kind of cohesion among leaders, it inspires them. It cascades down, and so this is what we are doing at the moment”, the governor said.
Mutfwang noted that political leaders on the Plateau were deliberately demonstrating unity through regular engagement and consistent messages encouraging peaceful coexistence.
He said the approach was beginning to yield encouraging results, with youth leaders from different ethnic and religious backgrounds initiating dialogue independently of government intervention.
“I believe that for us on the Plateau, those of us who are in the front lines of leadership are trying to demonstrate that by being seen together, by saying the same things, urging people to unite, to come together.
“People are taking responsibility, even among the youths. We are seeing a new vista in that direction, where youth leaders across the divides of faith and ethnicity are beginning to have conversations without even government support”, he stated.
Describing the development as a significant breakthrough in the state’s peacebuilding efforts, Mutfwang expressed confidence that sustained dialogue, cooperation and responsible leadership would help overcome longstanding divisions.
“This is quite encouraging to me that there is light at the end of the tunnel, and by the grace of God, we will continue to sustain these initiatives.
“Hopefully, a lot of the things that have happened in the past will become stories of the past, and we will be able to build a better, stable and prosperous future”, the governor said.
Vanguard News

Bournemouth extended their perfect Europa League record on Thursday as they came from behind to win 3-1 at 10-man Sparta Prague, while Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan suffered a third defeat in four matches.
Gambian Ebrima Singhateh ran from his own half to score a fine individual goal as Sparta took the lead in the Czech Republic after Bournemouth midfielder Lewis Cook hit the post with a first-half penalty.
Sparta had Tobias Guddal sent off before half-time and Bournemouth equalised through Tyler Adams on 57 minutes.
Evanilson steered the Cherries ahead nine minutes from time and Rayan bagged a late third as Bournemouth’s substitutes sent the European newcomers top of the table with a fourth successive victory.
Marco Rose’s side have won each of their past seven matches in all competitions ahead of a Premier League trip to Ipswich this weekend.
“It’s a big achievement and we have to continue, we need to stay alert, sharp,” Rose told TNT Sports.
“It’s up to us to use this momentum. Everyone tries to beat us, if we get in a comfort zone just a little bit we get in trouble.”
Milan lost 2-0 at home to Ferencvaros as the Hungarians kept pace with Bournemouth, maintaining their 100 percent record in Europe.
Haiti international Lenny Joseph struck twice in the second half at San Siro to earn Ferencvaros a deserved win over the seven-time European champions despite having Bamidele Yusuf sent off.
“We gifted opportunities, made stupid errors. We were not prepared to play football tonight,” Amorim told Sky Sport.
“I don’t want to lie to my players. We cannot play like this in front of our own fans. It was a very poor performance.”
Milan are languishing outside the top 24 with just three points at the halfway stage of the league phase.
“I won’t give up on this competition. As long as we’re not mathematically out of it, we’ll keep fighting,” Amorim added.
Crystal Palace snatched a 1-1 draw at home to Hoffenheim as Japanese midfielder Daichi Kamada levelled in stoppage time.
Alexander Prass gave Hoffenheim an early lead at Selhurst Park and Palace lost Adam Wharton to a second yellow card before Kamada rescued a point for Pierre Sage’s struggling side.
Palace, last season’s UEFA Conference League winners, have five points from four outings in the Europa League but sit in the Premier League’s relegation zone, just behind Manchester United on goal difference.

items.author: AFP
items.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football on Thursday to bring down the curtain on more than two decades in the Portugal shirt.
He scored a record 146 times in a mammoth 234 appearances for his country having made his debut in 2003.
Here are his five stand-out games with the Selecao.
2013: Outclassing Zlatan
Having won the World Cup play-off first leg 1-0 against Sweden thanks to the iconic No. 7, Portugal headed to Stockholm for the return fixture.
Ronaldo opened the scoring before Zlatan Ibrahimovic brought the sides level in the tie with a double in the Swedish capital. But the then Real Madrid attacker claimed Portugal's spot at the tournament in Brazil by completing his hat-trick in two minutes.
2016: Tears before the joy
Portugal reached the Euro 2016 final having failed to win a single group game.
Ronaldo's side went into the decider against hosts France in Paris searching for their first major international trophy and to make up for the past after losing to Greece on home soil 12 years earlier.
The forward left the field injured and in tears after just 25 minutes before spending the rest of the game on the touchline cheering on his teammates.
Eder scored the winner in extra-time to the relief of Ronaldo and 11 million Portuguese compatriots.
2018: One-man mission
Fresh from winning three straight Champions Leagues with Real, Ronaldo faced Spain in Portugal's World Cup opener in 2018.
CR7 opened the scoring in Sochi with a penalty before grabbing a hat-trick, including a superb late free kick, to fire Portugal to a thrilling draw.
2025: 40 years young
Three months after turning 40, Ronaldo helped Portugal to the Nations League final against Spain in Munich.
He scored the winner over Germany in the semi-final before claiming the equaliser against Spain to send the decider to extra time.
The Selecao eventually won on penalties, six years on from winning the same crown.
2026: Outplayed Croatia 
Following a lacklustre group stage, Ronaldo and Portugal faced Croatia in the last 32 of this year's World Cup in Toronto.
Despite the prospect of it being his final ever World Cup match, Ronaldo took control of things.
He had an early effort chalked off for offside and Ivan Perisic put Croatia ahead, but Ronaldo equalised for Portugal from the penalty spot. 
Goncalo Ramos' late header gave Portugal a memorable 2-1 victory and sent them into the last 16, where they lost to eventual winners Spain.

items.title: Alcaraz into Paris Masters quarters
items.summary:
Carlos Alcaraz moved into the quarter-finals of the Paris Masters on Thursday after his last 16 opponent Matteo Berrettini withdrew.
Alcaraz, a seven-time Grand Slam champion, was scheduled to play the Italian, but Berrettini pulled out ahead of their encounter with an elbow injury.
"Unfortunately, the pain in my arm that I've been putting up with for the past few days means I won't be able to take to the court tonight," Berrettini posted on social media.
After receiving a bye through the first round as a top-eight seed, Alcaraz is into the last eight with only one match under his belt in Paris, a straight-sets success against Alex Michelsen.
He will meet American Taylor Fritz on Friday for a spot in the semi-finals. Fritz beat French sixth seed Arthur Fils 6-3, 6-4 to stay in the running for a place at the ATP Finals.
Alcaraz has never won the Paris Masters. The Spaniard is the top-ranked player remaining in the draw after world number one Alexander Zverev lost on Wednesday.

items.author: AFP
items.content:
Spain's World Cup-winning coach Luis de la Fuente and the president of Real Madrid were among several hundred mourners who paid their respects at Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel's funeral on Thursday.
De Miguel, 30, died following a sickening collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a second division match on Monday.
Around 400 mourners, most dressed in traditional black, gathered outside the church in the village of Navahermosa, around 100 kilometres (62 miles) southwest of Madrid, to greet the funeral cortege.
They included De la Fuente and Real Madrid chief Florentino Perez.
Flags flew at half mast in Navahermosa, the birthplace of De Miguel's parents and where his grandparents still reside, after the council declared three days of mourning.
"We do not have enough words to thank all those who have sent messages, called or attested how much affection they had for him," said De Miguel's agent, reading out a statement on behalf of the family, who stood with him outside the funeral home before setting off for the church.
They added they would like their privacy to be respected and expressed "their need to be allowed to grieve in peace as is normal in such a situation." 
Once the cortege arrived at the church, De Miguel's Tenerife teammates acted as pall bearers and carried his coffin into the church.
'Immense pain'
Earlier on Thursday Spain's footballers' union asked that all this weekend's matches be postponed as a mark of respect.
The men and women players "in every category", who were polled by the AFE union, believe "unanimously" that this weekend's matches "should not be played", it said.
Tenerife's second division match at Granada and Andorra's clash with Mallorca have already been postponed, as were several midweek cup fixtures.
"The footballers have expressed their deep sorrow for this loss and do not believe that there are the psychological and humane conditions necessary for the competition to be played in normal circumstances," AFE added.
Tenerife are to pay homage to De Miguel -- who last season played a pivotal role in the club being promoted to the second tier -- on Saturday afternoon at the club's stadium.
Spanish police sources have told AFP an investigation into what happened has been opened, under judicial supervision.
Owono, for his part, has been subjected to a torrent of online abuse, a lot of it racist.
The 25-year-old Equatorial Guinea international spoke on Wednesday of his "immense pain over the loss of Jesus".
"These are the hardest days of my life," he said in a statement issued by his club.
"I struggle to find the words and it is very difficult for me to process anything that has happened.
"I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, of his family, and of all the people who loved him.
"I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are going through.
"Rest in peace, Jesus."
De Miguel was the second player to have died in a matter of months after being taken ill on the pitch.
Portuguese midfielder Quevin Castro passed away on August 25 in hospital after collapsing the night before, minutes into the Portuguese third division match between his club Real Sport Clube and Estrela da Amadora.

Member of the Edo State Consumer Protection Committee led by its chairman, Osaro Culture Iyamu were, on Thursday, attacked by some beverage sellers while trying to enforce ban on sales of fake, adulterated and unauthorised drinks along Mission Road in Benin City, the state capital.
The committee members were on a routine mission to the area when they noticed that some sellers were removing cartons, bottles and cans of drinks from their shelves on seeing the committee members.
The infuriated sellers then prevented the committee members from accessing their shops to ensure that what they had were genuine products.
Consequently, security agencies have invited beverage sellers, including Beverages and Alcohol Dealers Association, for a meeting over the incident.
Iyamu alleged that his committee had been under pressure to compromise. But he vowed to ensure that the essence of the committee, which is to rid Edo markets of fake and adulterated products, was fulfilled.
“We will continue to safeguard the health and protect the rights of consumers in line with the SHINE Agenda of Governor Monday Okpebholo.”

items.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (retd), has advocated restoring tollgates on major highways and deploying modern technology to enhance highway security and help identify and track criminals.
Musa noted that tollgates could play a valuable security role, especially with modern technology that can identify and track vehicles without requiring drivers to stop for manual payments.
The minister made the remarks at the Abuja roundtable, “Promise to Proof: The Renewed Hope Conversation,” organised by the APC Progressive Strategy Roundtable.
It was convened by the Executive Chairman/CEO of PICNG and EVs, Ismaeel Ahmed.
Responding to concerns about highway security and a suggestion that motorists could contribute through security levies at tollgates, Musa described the reintroduction of tollgates as a good idea, noting that Nigeria might have made a mistake by dismantling them.
He explained that modern tolling systems in other countries use technology to identify vehicles through their registration numbers, with payments processed electronically, adding that such systems could also assist security agencies in identifying and tracking vehicles.
The minister also called for the strengthening of Nigeria’s identification system through the use of personal identification numbers, facial recognition and fingerprints to improve security monitoring.
He said technology would make it easier for security agencies to establish people’s identities and track criminal activities.
On the broader security situation, Musa said the Federal Government was recording progress in tackling terrorism, banditry and kidnapping through increased defence investment, improved intelligence gathering, joint military operations and stronger cooperation among security agencies.
He disclosed that the Federal Government allocated ₦5.4 trillion to defence in the 2026 budget and was recruiting an additional 12,000 military personnel to strengthen manpower and security coverage.
According to him, the government was also investing in modern weapons, surveillance systems and operational platforms to improve intelligence gathering, mobility, firepower and rapid response capabilities.
He further disclosed that Nigerian security forces killed more than 300 terrorists and bandits, including over 10 commanders, in operations conducted in the week preceding his presentation.
The minister identified porous borders as a major challenge, noting that Nigeria shares extensive borders with neighbouring countries, particularly Niger Republic, through which criminal groups and illicit arms can move.
He said the government was strengthening border security and expanding bilateral, regional and international defence cooperation through intelligence sharing, specialised training and technological support.
Musa added that Nigeria continued to maintain security relationships with Niger, Burkina Faso and Mali despite their withdrawal from ECOWAS, including military training and cooperation around border areas.
He warned that instability in the Sahel posed a serious threat to West Africa and urged regional countries to work together to
prevent the collapse of neighbouring states.
The minister also highlighted the importance of local defence manufacturing, disclosing that the government had strengthened the country’s defence industry through legislative reforms and partnerships with equipment manufacturers.
He said Nigeria recently hosted the first African International Military Defence Exhibition, which attracted 63 countries and provided opportunities for local manufacturers to meet international partners and sign investment agreements.
According to him, domestic production of military equipment would reduce dependence on foreign suppliers, create employment and generate foreign exchange.
He called on Nigerians with expertise in cybersecurity, drone manufacturing and other defence technologies to bring forward their ideas for possible collaboration with the Defence Industry Corporation of Nigeria.
Addressing concerns about the increasing involvement of the military in internal security operations, Musa acknowledged that soldiers had become overstretched by prolonged deployments across the country.
He said the military’s involvement was necessary in situations where security challenges exceeded the capacity of the police but stressed that the armed forces were working to strengthen police capacity to enable soldiers to gradually return to their primary responsibilities.
According to him, the military was already assisting the police while the government pursued additional recruitment, equipment procurement and institutional reforms.
He disclosed that security agencies were enjoying unprecedented cooperation, describing the current level of interagency coordination as a significant improvement.
Musa also highlighted the role of communities in combating insecurity, urging Nigerians to report suspicious activities rather than remain indifferent.
He said criminals often operated within communities and depended on local support, adding that security agencies could not succeed without the cooperation of citizens.
The minister cited community-based intelligence and the use of civilian joint task forces as important components of the security strategy, noting that local residents could provide timely information to security operatives.
He also disclosed that the military was working with forest rangers and other community-based security structures to protect farmers and enable agricultural activities to continue in vulnerable areas.
On the welfare of military personnel, the minister said the government had increased soldiers’ salaries and was improving their living conditions, healthcare and operational support.
He recalled that a private soldier previously earned about ₦49,000 monthly before the amount was increased to approximately ₦100,000 and subsequently to nearly ₦200,000.
He said military personnel and their families were entitled to free medical treatment, adding that soldiers requiring specialised treatment could be flown abroad.
Musa also explained that military personnel underwent psychological preparation before deployment and assessment after operations to address the effects of traumatic experiences.
He said returning soldiers were monitored for psychological challenges, including post-traumatic stress disorder, anger and other behavioural changes.
According to him, military personnel could undergo two to three weeks of post-deployment assessment and support before returning to their families and units.
He added that the military provided support systems for soldiers’ spouses and families, including access to loans, medical care and educational assistance for their children.
On fallen military personnel, Musa said their families were entitled to salaries, allowances and other benefits, while their children were supported through university education.
He stressed that caring for injured soldiers and families of fallen heroes was essential to maintaining the morale and commitment of troops serving in dangerous conditions.
Also speaking at the roundtable, the Executive Secretary of the Nigerian Police Trust Fund, Alhaji Mohamed Shaidou, said the Federal Government was addressing longstanding challenges in police funding, training, equipment and welfare.
Shaidou said the police had suffered years of underfunding and neglect, making it difficult for the force to effectively discharge its responsibility of maintaining internal security and enforcing the law.
He explained that the Nigerian Police Trust Fund was established as an intervention agency to support police training, equipment
procurement and officers’ welfare.
He said the current administration had placed greater emphasis on strengthening policing, adding that the government had also
begun considering ways to improve funding through the proposed establishment of state police.
According to him, the government approved about ₦100 billion for the rehabilitation of police training institutions following an assessment of training facilities across the country.
He said the Trust Fund was also investing in continuous training, police stations, operational vehicles, bulletproof vests and other equipment required by officers.
Shaidou argued that improving police training institutions was particularly important because officers needed the right professional and mental preparation before being deployed to protect lives and maintain law and order.
He also disclosed that the Trust Fund had entered into partnerships with the Rural Electrification Agency (REA), the National Agricultural Land Development Authority (NALDA) and Family Homes Funds to improve the welfare of police officers and their dependants.
Under the housing initiative, he said the Trust Fund was working towards providing 1,000 housing units per state for police officers to enable them to own their homes.
He disclosed that a groundbreaking ceremony had already been conducted for about 250 housing units in Nasarawa State.
Shaidou said the Trust Fund was also working with the REA to provide electricity for housing projects and police facilities.
He revealed that some smart police stations had been equipped with off-grid solar power systems to ensure that their operations were not disrupted by electricity challenges.
On transportation, he said the Trust Fund had introduced welfare buses to convey police officers in Abuja from locations including Mararaba, Zuba and other communities to their duty posts.
He said the initiative was designed to reduce the financial burden on officers who previously spent their personal resources commuting to work.
He acknowledged contributions towards the transportation initiative, including the donation of a 40-seater bus and a 50-seater bus to support police transportation.
The Trust Fund, he added, was considering the use of compressed natural gas (CNG) buses to reduce fuel and maintenance costs and ensure the sustainability of the programme.
Shaidou further disclosed that the Fund had partnered with NALDA to provide agricultural opportunities for dependants of police officers.
He said the initiative would enable families of officers to access farmland and engage in farming as an additional source of income and food supply.
He explained that discussions had already commenced with governors of Kano and Niger states on the programme.
On the proposed establishment of state police, Shaidou said the Trust Fund supported the initiative but stressed the need to
strengthen the existing federal police structure.
He argued that countries operating state police systems also maintained federal police institutions, adding that Nigeria must ensure its federal police force was adequately strengthened as the country considers the proposed reform.
Earlier, participants at the roundtable raised concerns about the protection of citizens who provide security intelligence, particularly whistleblowers who fear possible exposure or retaliation.
Responding, Musa said the protection of informants was important and encouraged Nigerians to continue providing credible intelligence to security agencies.
He also said the Defence Ministry and military service headquarters received correspondence from citizens and were working towards establishing an emergency reporting line to facilitate the transmission of security information.
Participants equally called for stronger collaboration between security agencies and private-sector organisations, particularly in the power sector, to provide reliable electricity for local defence manufacturing.
Musa welcomed the proposal, describing energy supply as a major challenge facing defence manufacturers, and pledged to connect the relevant parties for further engagement.
The minister also urged Nigerians to promote national unity, saying the country’s security challenges required collective responsibility beyond religious, ethnic and regional differences.
He maintained that the ultimate measure of security success should be farmers returning to their farms, travellers moving safely on highways, markets reopening and businesses operating without fear.
The post Nigeria must deploy tollgates, technology to improve highway security – Musa appeared first on Vanguard News.
