items.content:
An Italian chef in Australia has lost an unfair dismissal claim after being sacked for, among other workplace issues, refusing to serve ham and pineapple pizza, describing the topping as an insult to his culture.
Davide Tamburella was dismissed from the now-closed La Costa restaurant in Brisbane in May, following a meeting with management over several complaints about his conduct.
One of the issues raised was his refusal to prepare ham and pineapple pizzas for guests attending an event at the restaurant.
According to a ruling by Australia’s Fair Work Commission, Tamburella argued that instructions from management “need not be followed when it is offensive to his culture”.
The commission noted that the chef’s objection to the fruit was because “he considers, as an Italian, that putting pineapple on a pizza is an insult to his culture”.
It also found that this was not the first time he had refused to use pineapple on pizzas, recording three such instances over four years.
On a previous occasion, Tamburella had asked his employer to “check how important it is for Italians not to put pineapple on a pizza”.
Beyond the dispute over pizza toppings, management raised concerns about his use of foul language, communication style and what it described as an “escalation of frustration in the workplace”.
The ruling also detailed an incident in April when Tamburella fractured bones in his right hand after striking a metal handrail at work.
The chef had reportedly hoped to secure employer sponsorship for a visa that would allow him to remain in Australia as a permanent resident. However, following his dismissal, the restaurant discontinued the sponsorship process.
Tamburella subsequently approached the Fair Work Commission, challenging his dismissal. However, the commission rejected his unfair dismissal claim because it was lodged outside the permitted timeframe.
The restaurant’s managing director, Elliot Ingram, told the Daily Mail there was “more to this story than a pizza topping”.
The BBC said it had contacted Tamburella for comment.
On his LinkedIn profile, the chef describes himself as someone whose career has focused on “delivering exceptional food” and “improving business performance”.
He also shared a post titled “letter for chefs” three months ago, centred on the theme of “respecting the ingredients”.
His LinkedIn profile indicates that he now works at another restaurant in Brisbane. A BBC check found that pineapple is not included on its menu.
Meanwhile, Queensland, where the restaurant was located, is regarded as Australia’s pineapple heartland and produces the country’s commercially grown pineapples. The state is also home to the Big Pineapple, a 16-metre fibreglass structure on the Sunshine Coast that has become a popular local landmark.

items.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
The Federal Government is exploring the use of mobile Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) refuelling stations to improve gas availability in rural areas, especially for farmers who need more affordable energy for irrigation and agricultural production.
The disclosure was made by Ismaeel Ahmed, Chairman/CEO of the Presidential CNG Initiative and Electric Vehicles (Pi-CNG & EV), at the APC–Progressive Strategy Roundtable event in Abuja, themed Promise to Proof: The Renewed Hope Conversation
Speaking at the session, “Fuel That Works: Reliable Energy, Affordable Transport and Fair Prices for Every Household and Business,” Ahmed said the government was considering mobile CNG stations to bring fuel to remote communities, where permanent facilities may not be commercially attractive to private investors.
He explained that consultations with state governments, particularly in northern Nigeria, had revealed that the demand for CNG was increasingly extending beyond transportation to agricultural activities.
He said farmers are seeking to switch from expensive diesel and petrol to CNG-powered irrigation pumps to reduce production costs.
Ahmed, the Convener of the Roundtable, cited Jigawa State as an example, noting that the governor had told the initiative that more than two million farmers in the state could benefit from affordable energy for irrigation
He explained that mechanical irrigation pumps could cover about three hectares of farmland, compared with solar-powered pumps, which typically cover about one hectare.
He said although solar-powered irrigation had been introduced as an alternative, some farmers preferred mechanical pumps because of their greater coverage and operational capacity.
Ahmed said the Federal Government was committed to aggressively pursuing the expansion of gas infrastructure, adding that President Bola Tinubu had given the initiative the go-ahead to intensify its activities.
However, he identified gas supply and delays in obtaining licences for CNG refuelling stations as major challenges that needed to be addressed.
He appealed to the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) to help accelerate the licensing process for investors seeking to establish CNG stations.
He acknowledged the importance of safety regulations, explaining that gas infrastructure required strict safety considerations, but urged the regulator to find ways of expediting the process in view of the urgency of the programme.
He also raised the possibility of deploying mobile CNG stations to serve farmers and other users in remote communities where investors might not immediately find it economically viable to establish permanent facilities.
Ahmed said the CNG programme had recorded about 143,000 vehicle conversions, with investments estimated at $2.6 billion.
The roundtable also featured presentations by the Managing Director of the Rural Electrification Agency, Dr. Abba Abubakar Aliyu; the representative of the Niger Delta Power Holding Company, Mr. Abdullahi Kassim; the Chairman of the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission, Dr. Musiliu Oseni; and the representative of the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, Dr. Mustapha Lamorde.
On rural electrification, Aliyu discussed electricity-access gaps, national mapping, least-cost electrification planning and the deployment of mini-grids and captive power projects.
The meeting was informed of plans to deploy 1,350 mini-grids under a $750 million project to improve electricity access in underserved communities.
Kassim, while presenting the activities of the Niger Delta Power Holding Company, discussed the company’s ownership structure, the history of the National Integrated Power Projects assets and its contribution to electricity generation.
He disclosed that the company operates 10 power plants with a combined generation capacity of 4,000 megawatts.
He also highlighted the company’s transmission and distribution infrastructure, industrial power initiatives, solar deployments and recently awarded community infrastructure contracts.
Oseni addressed electricity tariffs, affordability and service delivery, explaining the different customer bands and the relationship between electricity tariffs and hours of supply.
He said electricity costs were estimated at about ₦200 per kilowatt-hour, while the commission was pursuing measures to improve power supply through investments in generation, mini-grids, debt recovery and net billing.
NERC also reported an increase of approximately 780 megawatts in installed generation capacity.
On fuel availability and energy security, Lamorde discussed the regulatory framework for petroleum supply, domestic refining, product pricing and strategic fuel reserves.
The presentation highlighted efforts to monitor fuel availability, with a target of 30 days of supply monitoring and an eventual goal of building strategic reserves capable of covering 90 days.
The meeting was also informed that the Port Harcourt, Warri and Kaduna refineries, with a combined capacity of about 445,000 barrels per day, were currently shut down.
The representative said the government was engaging international technical expertise to facilitate the resolution of challenges affecting the facilities.
He further disclosed that more than 26 refineries had been licensed across the country, while a pre-start-up safety review had recently been conducted for a 30,000-barrel-per-day Brenco refinery, which is expected to commence operations soon.
The discussion also addressed product quality, with the petroleum regulator highlighting the modernisation of laboratories across the country. Two laboratories had recently been completed, while another was expected to be commissioned before the end of the year.
Participants raised questions about historical electricity generation capacity, additional refinery investments, local production of electric vehicles and solar panels, diaspora investment opportunities and complaints against electricity distribution companies.
On electric vehicles and battery production, Ahmed said lithium development was being handled by the Ministry of Solid Minerals Development, adding that the government was interested in encouraging local battery manufacturing, vehicle assembly and the production of electric vehicles.
Responding to concerns about electricity disconnections, Oseni explained that mass disconnections were prohibited and outlined complaint channels available to electricity consumers.
He also discussed possible compensation arrangements for customers who finance improvements to electricity distribution networks.
The NERC chairman acknowledged that electricity supply to Band A customers had improved but admitted that overall service delivery remained below the desired level.
Vanguard News

items.content:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta
Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun has declared his administration’s readiness to establish a state police force, describing it as a critical step towards strengthening security, protecting investments and sustaining the state’s growing economic activities.
The governor also announced the immediate commencement of a social investment cash transfer programme for vulnerable residents to cushion the effects of rising food and transportation costs.
Abiodun made the announcements at a town hall meeting on the 2027 budget and the 2027–2029 Medium Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) for Remo Division, held at the Akarigbo Palace, Sagamu.
Speaking on the proposed establishment of state police, the governor, who chairs the Nigeria Governors’ Forum Committee on State Police, said Ogun was prepared to embrace the initiative, noting that the state’s expanding industrial and commercial activities required a more robust security framework.
He declared: “I am the Chairman of the Governors’ Forum on State Police creation. Ogun State is ready for state police.”
Abiodun said his administration had consistently strengthened the state’s security architecture through the provision of operational vehicles, allowances and equipment, as well as increased recruitment into the Ogun State Security Network, popularly known as Amotekun.
He disclosed that Amotekun and the So-Safe Corps currently had a combined strength of about 6,000 personnel.
“To protect the gains we have made, we have continued to strengthen our security architecture by providing them with vehicles, allowances and equipment. We have empowered our Amotekun and increased their recruitment,” he said.
On the cash transfer initiative, the governor said the programme was designed to provide direct financial support to vulnerable households grappling with the rising cost of living, particularly food and transportation.
He linked the prevailing economic pressures partly to disruptions in the global oil and gas supply chain arising from the ongoing Israel-American-Iran conflict, which he said had contributed to rising oil prices and transportation costs.
“We are going to start the implementation of our social investment cash initiative. We are going to transfer cash to our people to cushion the effects of this America-Israel-Iran war,” he stated.
The governor disclosed that the programme would commence immediately in Sagamu, with beneficiaries already identified and captured in the state’s database expected to receive payment alerts.
He added that the initiative would subsequently be extended to other communities across Remoland and the entire state.
“I am starting that today in Sagamu. I’m going into Ogijo from here. All those who have been generated to benefit will get their alerts today while I’m there. I’m going to do the same across Remoland and of course, the whole state,” he said.
Abiodun further announced plans to sink boreholes in all 236 wards across the state, while also providing transformers and solar-powered streetlights to improve access to basic amenities and enhance security in communities.
He assured residents that Remoland remained central to his administration’s development agenda, stressing that the division was an active participant and beneficiary of the economic transformation taking place across Ogun.
“Remoland is not on the sidelines of these developments. You are right in the middle of it. You are a participant and a contributor to this economic improvement,” he said.
Earlier, the Economic Adviser to the Governor and Commissioner for Finance, Mr Dapo Okubadejo, said effective governance depended on open dialogue, active citizen participation and mutual accountability between the government and the people.
He noted that the performance of any administration should ultimately be assessed by the tangible improvements its policies and programmes brought to the lives of citizens, particularly through infrastructure development and social interventions.
Providing an overview of the state’s fiscal performance, Okubadejo disclosed that Ogun recorded an expenditure performance of N490 billion out of the N703 billion budget estimate for 2024, representing approximately 70 per cent.
He said the 2025 budget of N1.05 trillion recorded expenditure of about N700 billion, representing 65 per cent performance.
According to him, the 2026 budget, valued at N1.67 trillion, had continued to support government interventions in infrastructure, education, youth empowerment, agriculture and other critical sectors.
“As we commence preparation for the 2027 budget within the 2027–2029 Medium Term Expenditure Framework, this town hall meeting provides the opportunity to share the policies, programmes and projects that would be embarked upon next year,” he said.
Speaking on behalf of the chairmen of Sagamu, Remo North and Ikenne Local Government Areas, the Chairman of Sagamu Local Government, Afolabi Odulate, appealed to the state government to address what he described as the encroachment of Lagos into Ogun through border communities.
He also called for the rehabilitation of deteriorating roads across the three local government areas to facilitate movement, stimulate commercial activities and improve the living conditions of residents.
The Akarigbo of Remoland, Oba Babatunde Ajayi, commended the state government for the development projects executed across the division but called for the establishment of a monitoring team to ensure that public facilities were properly utilised and maintained.
The monarch also appealed for the establishment of federal tertiary institutions in Remoland and urged the state government to ensure that indigenes of the division were adequately included in the state’s economic development initiatives.
Similarly, the Chairman of the Remo Division of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (ICAN), Chief Adewale Kalejaye, called for stronger collaboration between the professional body and the state government to broaden the tax base and improve revenue generation.
He also advocated increased funding for Sustainable Development Goals initiatives, particularly programmes targeted at reducing poverty and hunger and improving access to education for children.
The post Ogun ready for State Police – Abiodun appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
By Joseph Erunke
The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) has moved to tighten its grip on the conduct of the 2027 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME), warning that computer-based test (CBT) centres that fail to meet its prescribed standards will be denied accreditation.
The Board said only centres with adequate facilities, reliable infrastructure and the operational capacity to guarantee a credible and hitch-free examination would be approved to host candidates in the 2027 exercise.
JAMB Registrar, Prof. Segun Aina, gave the indication during a meeting with the leadership of the Chief External Examiners, where preparations and readiness for the accreditation exercise ahead of the 2027 UTME were reviewed.
According to a post on the Board’s official X handle on Thursday, the meeting was part of efforts to strengthen examination administration and ensure strict compliance with established operational standards.
The Board said the accreditation exercise would serve as a critical screening mechanism to prevent inadequately equipped centres from participating in the examination, thereby protecting candidates from avoidable disruptions and compromising examination conditions.
Reiterating its position, JAMB declared that accreditation would not be automatic for CBT centres seeking to participate in the exercise.
“Only centres that meet JAMB’s standards will be accredited to host the examination. For candidates, that means a fair and secure place to sit the UTME, wherever they write it,” the Board stated.
The development signals JAMB’s determination to strengthen the credibility of the UTME by ensuring that candidates, irrespective of their examination locations, have access to a secure, reliable and conducive testing environment.
The strict accreditation regime is also expected to address operational shortcomings that have historically threatened the smooth conduct of computer-based examinations, including inadequate facilities and poor technical readiness.
With preparations for the 2027 UTME gathering momentum, the Board maintained that compliance with its accreditation requirements would remain non-negotiable for all CBT centres seeking approval to participate in the nationwide examination.

items.content:
Zong, Pakistan’s Leading Technology Services Enterprise, showcased its network strength, 5G-ready infrastructure and intelligent capabilities during the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority’s (PTA) on-ground Quality of Experience (QoE) assessment across Islamabad and Rawalpindi.
As part of the wider multi-city survey, Islamabad International Airport served as key demonstration of Zong’s leadership, where the company is the only operator to have deployed a 5G active DAS Indoor Building Solution (IBS), reflecting its continued investment in advanced connectivity, future-ready network infrastructure and reliable customer experience.
Led by PTA Chairman Major General (Retd.) Hafeez Ur Rehman, who personally tested voice call quality and mobile internet services, the exercise brought together senior PTA officials, including Member (Finance) Muhammad Naveed, Member (Compliance and Enforcement) Dr. Khawar Siddique Khokhar, Member (Telecom) Muhammad Jahanzeb Rahim and DG (Enforcement) Brigadier (Retd.) Amer Shahzad, alongside representatives of MoITT, mobile network operators, media and Zong Leadership.
Three dedicated teams conducted parallel on-ground assessments across the twin cities, evaluating real-world voice and data experiences, including download speeds, call stability, connectivity and service continuity across multiple locations. The field assessment reinforces Zong’s leading position in PTA’s independently published Q2 2026 QoS Survey and Mobile Network Experience Benchmarking Opensignal Reports.
Nationwide, Zong has surpassed 1,000+ 5G sites, including 275+ 5G-enabled sites across the Twin Cities, the highest deployment in the industry. Moreover, Zong has industry highest # of 1,000 sites in the twin cities. The company continues to strengthen network capacity, reduce congestion, and enhance data performance, particularly in high-traffic locations and during peak usage hours. Advanced technologies such as Carrier Aggregation, which combines multiple spectrum carriers to deliver greater bandwidth, further optimize spectrum utilization, improve network efficiency, and enhance the overall customer experience.
Zong’s 5G DAS IBS at Islamabad International Airport demonstrates its commitment to extending high-performance connectivity beyond conventional outdoor coverage. Designed to deliver seamless indoor connectivity across the airport, the infrastructure provides a foundation for next-generation digital, intelligent travel experiences and a dedicated Customer Facilitation Desk, offering travelers convenient SIM activation, data services and on-ground support.
The PTA noted that initial findings reflected Zong’s strong network performance and improvements in the quality and reliability of services across the surveyed areas. The regulator emphasized that the field assessment was designed to evaluate actual consumer experience, identify potential service gaps and drive further improvements. It reaffirmed its commitment to sustained field monitoring, evidence-based evaluation and close coordination with operators to strengthen service quality and ensure continuous improvement across the sector.
For Zong, network excellence is the foundation of its transformation into a Technology Services Enterprise, enabling the shift from connectivity to intelligent, technology-led services. Zong’s infrastructure reflects its readiness to support the country’s growing digital ambitions, with independent assessments consistently recognizing its performance across speed, reliability and latency.
Looking ahead, Zong remains committed to working with PTA and industry partners to advance network excellence and accelerate Pakistan’s digital transformation. Through innovation, sustained investment and future-ready connectivity, Zong aims to bridge the digital divide, unlock new opportunities and contribute to building an intelligent, inclusive and digitally empowered society.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has introduced a new facility allowing taxpayers to amend or cancel electronic sales tax invoices even after the expiry of the existing 72-hour limit.
The facility has been added to the FBR’s IRIS system and allows taxpayers to request changes to invoices after the prescribed time limit, subject to approval from the concerned Commissioner Inland Revenue (CIR).
According to a user manual issued by Pakistan Revenue Automation (Private) Limited (PRAL) on Thursday, the new feature aims to help taxpayers correct errors and discrepancies in electronic sales tax invoices that cannot be changed through the existing system.
Taxpayers can access the facility by logging into IRIS, opening the Sales Tax applications section and selecting the option titled “Application for Amendment in Electronic Sales Tax Invoice (after 72 hrs).”
They can then select the relevant tax period, identify invoices through their FBR Invoice Transaction Numbers and submit requests for amendment or cancellation.
The system also allows taxpayers to attach supporting documents in PDF format. Tax officers can request further explanations through IRIS’s Internal Correspondence facility before deciding on an application.
However, taxpayers cannot amend and cancel the same invoice through one application. Once an invoice is selected for amendment, it cannot be selected for cancellation under that application, and vice versa.
Another important restriction applies while an application is pending. Taxpayers will not be able to submit Annexure-C (Sales) of their sales tax returns until the Commissioner Inland Revenue decides their request.
If the application is approved, the corrected electronic invoices will become available for inclusion in Annexure-C, subject to system validations. If the application is rejected, the original invoices will remain applicable and will be loaded into Annexure-C and the Federal Excise Return, wherever applicable.
FBR has also restricted applications involving invoices already linked with Annexure-C of a Sales Tax Return or Federal Excise Return. Invoices previously approved by the Commissioner under another application are also ineligible.
Taxpayers can submit multiple applications for the same tax period. However, invoices already included in previous applications, rejected invoices and those with pending decisions cannot be submitted again.
The new facility provides taxpayers with an additional opportunity to correct or cancel electronic sales tax invoices after the 72-hour deadline, although all requests remain subject to the regulator’s approval.

items.author: News Desk
items.content:
Pakistani architect Yasmeen Lari's humanitarian approach to architecture features prominently in a major exhibition in Qatar, that brought together the work of more than 40 architects and practices from across the Middle East, North Africa and South Asia.
Titled 'Beyti Beytak – My Home Is Your Home', the exhibition, organised by the future Art Mill Museum and presented by Qatar Museums, opened at Fahad bin Ali Palace in Doha on October 26 and will remain on display until May 29, 2027, according to Qatar Times.
The exhibition examines how architecture can respond to the needs of communities while fostering hospitality, collective care and a sense of belonging. Its expanded Doha edition follows its earlier presentation at the 19th International Architecture Exhibition of the Venice Biennale in 2025, which marked Qatar's first official participation in the event.
Lari's contribution is particularly significant for Pakistan, with her Community Centre, designed in 2024, demonstrating how locally adaptable materials and traditional construction techniques can serve communities affected by natural disasters.
"I realised her work is a direct legacy of (Egyptian architect) Hassan Fathy. Like him, she empowers the poor to build their own futures," Aurelien Lemonier, architect and curator at the Art Mill Museum, and the exhibition's co-curator, told Arab News.
The bamboo structure was developed around techniques deployed by the Heritage Foundation of Pakistan, an organisation co-founded by Lari in 1980. The foundation has continued its work establishing shelters and villages for people affected by a devastating earthquake and repeated flooding in Pakistan.
Featuring a perimeter veranda and a dome topped with a waterproof palm-frond roof, the community centre demonstrates the versatility of bamboo through different structural assemblies. The installation also highlights Lari's humanitarian, social, cultural and architectural development model.
The exhibition brings together architectural drawings, photographs, models, films and archival material, examining three generations of architects whose work has shaped the MENASA region. Its themes include community centres, city housing, mosques, museums, gardens and the reinvention of traditional oases.
Among the participating Pakistani architects is Nayyar Ali Dada, while Lari is represented through the Heritage Foundation of Pakistan. The international line-up also includes pioneering architects Hassan Fathy, Balkrishna Doshi, Rifat Chadirji and Geoffrey Bawa, alongside contemporary architectural practices.
The exhibition features projects ranging from the Mleiha Archaeological Centre in the United Arab Emirates and the Palestinian Museum to the Jadgal Elementary School and Qatar National Library, highlighting the relationship between architecture, local environments and community needs.
Curated by Lemonier and Sean Anderson, the exhibition is organised into seven sections and includes archival research into Doha's urban development. It also marks the first time Qatar Museums and the Art Mill Museum have opened Fahad bin Ali Palace to visitors.
The exhibition's presentation at the historic palace seeks to establish a dialogue between contemporary architectural practices and regional heritage, placing particular emphasis on architecture as a means of strengthening social connections and collective identity.

Saudi Arabia on Thursday “categorically denied” a Wall Street Journal report claiming that Yemen’s Houthi militia had demanded $51 billion and formal recognition as the country’s rulers in exchange for ending hostilities with the kingdom.
In a post on X, Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly said the report had “no basis in truth”, describing the claims as fabrications by the newspaper’s writers or their alleged sources.
I categorically deny the claims published by The Wall Street Journal regarding demands made by this militia. All of this is pure fabrication by the writers or their alleged sources. These militias turned against the Yemeni government, caused famine among the Yemeni people, and…
— AMB Dr. Rayed Krimly (@Rayedkrimly) November 5, 2026
Krimly accused the Houthis of rebelling against Yemen’s government, contributing to the starvation of its people and dragging the country into conflicts and agendas that did not serve its interests.
He also accused the militia of attacking commercial shipping in the Red Sea, as well as civilian and economic facilities, and rejecting peace efforts.
He stressed that Yemen “already has an internationally recognised government”.
Read: Yemeni army says it carried out over 1,200 operations against Houthi positions
According to the Wall Street Journal, the Iran-backed Houthis had demanded $51 billion and formal recognition as Yemen’s rulers in return for ending hostilities with Saudi Arabia, presenting Riyadh with a difficult choice as renewed missile attacks threatened the kingdom’s oil facilities, airports and cities.
The newspaper, citing people briefed on the discussions, reported that the Houthis had said the amount was needed to cover the cost of years of Saudi strikes and a prolonged blockade.
The group also sought Saudi Arabia’s recognition as Yemen’s legitimate rulers, a concession that would undermine the internationally recognised Yemeni government backed by Riyadh and potentially strengthen an Iran-aligned movement along the kingdom’s southern border.
The report said the demands emerged after Saudi Arabia approached the Houthis to explore a negotiated end to the conflict following attacks on Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea and the group’s seizure of strategic territory overlooking the Bab Al Mandab Strait.
Also Read: Saudi, Syrian defence ministries sign cooperation agreement, SPA reports
The development comes amid escalating hostilities between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition, which supports Yemen’s internationally recognised government.
Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia intensified as the group advanced towards the Bab Al Mandab Strait, a key shipping chokepoint on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula from the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: PM Shehbaz Sharif Inaugurates Rs. 1.45 Billion Underpass
items.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif inaugurated the Kashmir Chowk Underpass in Islamabad on Thursday, a Rs. 1.45 billion project aimed at reducing traffic congestion in the capital.
The 500-meter underpass was completed in just 27 days through round-the-clock construction work, according to the prime minister.
Speaking at the inauguration ceremony, Shehbaz congratulated Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, the Capital Development Authority (CDA), project officials and contractors on completing the project.
He said the development also includes a four-kilometer road network, two monuments and thousands of newly planted trees. The prime minister said the underpass would improve traffic flow in the area, particularly as Islamabad prepares to host the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) conference next year.
He also said the project was completed transparently and in accordance with government procurement rules at a cost 2.5 percent below the estimated amount.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
ISTANBUL
Egyptian Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade Mohamed Farid Saleh told Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan that Pakistani investors could establish manufacturing operations in Egypt and use Cairo's preferential trade arrangements with the United States to access the American market, subject to applicable trade requirements.
Saleh encouraged Pakistani companies to explore manufacturing and industrial partnerships in Egypt and highlighted investment opportunities in the country.
He also requested details of Pakistani companies expected to participate in the upcoming business forum to facilitate direct engagement between the business communities and identify potential investment partnerships.
The Egyptian minister further highlighted educational opportunities for Pakistani students in Egypt, particularly in science, technology, medicine, healthcare and engineering, noting the availability of educational facilities at competitive costs.
The offer came during a series of bilateral meetings Khan held with counterparts from Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Tunisia on the sidelines of the 42nd session of the Standing Committee for Economic and Commercial Cooperation (COMCEC) in Istanbul, Türkiye, according to a statement issued on Thursday.
Khan emphasised the need to develop joint ventures between Pakistani and Egyptian private-sector companies and to explore opportunities in textiles, manufacturing and other mutually beneficial sectors.
He stressed that closer business-to-business engagement and stronger institutional linkages could help both countries expand their commercial partnerships and explore new international markets.
Talks with Egypt covered opportunities to enhance bilateral trade, investment and industrial cooperation between the two countries, particularly in the cotton and textile sectors.
In a separate meeting with Fareed S Alasaly, Deputy Governor for International Organisations and Agreements of Saudi Arabia, both sides agreed to further strengthen cooperation in agriculture and industrial development, particularly in human resource development, livestock and food security.
Khan emphasised the importance of identifying new avenues for mutually beneficial joint ventures between Pakistani and Saudi companies, and particularly proposed partnerships between leading businesses of the two countries to explore emerging trade opportunities in African markets. He also stressed the need for greater institutional and private-sector engagement to translate economic potential into practical business partnerships between the two countries.
He invited the Saudi representative to visit Pakistan during the upcoming FoodAg exhibition in Pakistan to explore opportunities in agriculture, livestock and food-related industries.
In a separate meeting with Tunisian Minister of Trade and Export Development Samir Abid, Khan discussed possibilities for enhancing bilateral trade and exploring new avenues of economic and industrial cooperation between the two countries.
Both ministers acknowledged that the existing volume of bilateral trade remains significantly below its true potential and emphasised the need for coordinated efforts to identify new opportunities and strengthen commercial linkages.
The discussions particularly focused on expanding cooperation in agriculture, minerals, textiles, auto parts and manufacturing, with both sides recognising considerable opportunities for mutually beneficial partnerships in these sectors.
Khan emphasised that Pakistan and Tunisia could benefit from each other's experience, technical expertise and industrial capabilities in specialised sectors, and highlighted the importance of sharing knowledge, adopting improved production practices and encouraging joint ventures to enhance productivity and competitiveness.
Both ministers agreed on the importance of closer institutional coordination and greater private-sector engagement to unlock untapped trade potential and translate identified opportunities into practical economic partnerships.
The meetings focused on strengthening bilateral economic relations, expanding trade and investment opportunities, promoting joint ventures and enhancing industrial cooperation in sectors of mutual interest.
Khan reiterated Pakistan's commitment to strengthening economic relations with friendly countries through enhanced trade, investment, industrial cooperation, knowledge sharing and greater private-sector participation.
The engagements reflected efforts to strengthen economic diplomacy, diversify export markets, attract investment and promote mutually beneficial economic partnerships with countries across the Middle East, North Africa and beyond.

items.content:
Minister of State and Chairman Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (PVARA) Bilal Bin Saqib met Mastercard Division President for East Asia Mark Elliott to discuss opportunities arising from the convergence of traditional financial systems and emerging digital-asset technologies, according to a statement issued on Thursday.
The engagement focused on the evolving role of blockchain-enabled financial infrastructure, including opportunities to improve cross-border payments, strengthen remittance efficiency, facilitate the responsible tokenisation of financial assets and expand access to modern financial services.
With Pakistan receiving over $40 billion in annual remittances and possessing a rapidly growing digital economy, discussions highlighted the potential for next-generation financial technologies to deliver tangible economic benefits, particularly for overseas Pakistanis, freelancers, small businesses and financial institutions.
The two sides also exchanged perspectives on emerging global developments in digital payments, cybersecurity, financial integrity and the importance of regulatory frameworks that enable responsible innovation while protecting consumers and safeguarding financial stability.
The minister said, "The next generation of global financial infrastructure is being built today. Pakistan has an opportunity not merely to participate in this transformation, but to help shape how emerging economies benefit from it. Our priority is to translate technological innovation into real economic value for citizens, businesses and the broader economy."
He said the future of finance would increasingly depend on cooperation between established financial institutions, technology providers and regulators.

Arif Habib Limited (AHL) stated that the KSE-100 index advanced 1.96% on the day, with 83 shares rising and only 15 declining, as follow-through demand lifted the benchmark. UBL, Lucky Cement and Meezan Bank were among the stocks that contributed the most to the gains.
AHL report also highlighted a modest year-on-year rise in total cement dispatches for October, driven mainly by stronger domestic demand that offset weaker exports, and remarks from FBR Chairman Rashid Mahmood Langrial that the government intended to abolish the super tax gradually after an initial two-percentage-point cut.
Topline's market review said that the PSX extended its bullish momentum for the fourth consecutive session on Thursday, as strong buying interest across major sectors continued to support the benchmark index. The KSE-100 maintained its upward trajectory, gaining 3,366 points (+1.96%) to reach 175,380 at close, further strengthening investor confidence and market sentiment.
The positive momentum was primarily driven by easing geopolitical concerns, declining international oil prices and expectations of improved global economic stability following the US midterm election developments. Buying activity remained broad-based, with key sectors, including commercial banks, cement, automobile assemblers, oil and gas exploration firms and oil marketing companies, attracting significant investor interest.
The KSE-100 touched the intra-day high of 176,605 points before witnessing some profit-taking at higher levels. Nevertheless, the broader market maintained a positive tone, as per Topline. UBL, LUCK, MEBL, SYS and ENGROH emerged as the leading positive contributors, collectively adding 1,293 points to the index. Their performance provided substantial support to the market's overall upward movement, Topline added.
Overall trading volumes were recorded at 999.8 million shares compared with the previous session's tally of 841.6 million. The value of shares traded during the day was Rs46 billion.
In the ready market, shares of 501 companies were traded. Of these, 365 stocks closed higher, 103 fell, and 33 remained unchanged.
Cnergyico Pk was the volume leader with trading in 74 million shares, gaining Rs0.09 to close at Rs12.06. It was followed by The Bank of Punjab with 70 million shares, gaining Rs0.80 to close at Rs31.70, and K-Electric with 61 million shares, gaining Rs0.14 to close at Rs6.14. During the day, foreign investors sold shares worth Rs1.2 billion, the National Clearing Company reported.

The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) has described the performance of telecom companies pertaining to internet services as excellent in Islamabad and Rawalpindi.
PTA conducted a comprehensive Quality of Experience (QoE) and Quality of Service (QoS) field survey at key locations across Islamabad and Rawalpindi to evaluate the performance, reliability and quality of telecommunication services being provided to consumers. The exercise was led by PTA Chairman Major General (Retd) Hafeez Ur Rehman, Member (Finance) Muhammad Naveed, Member (Compliance & Enforcement) Dr Khawar Siddique Khokhar, Member Telecom Muhammad Jahanzeb Rahim, director general (enforcement), director general (IR & GA) and enforcement officers.
Representatives of the Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication, mobile network operators and media representatives also participated in the performance assessment activity.
Three dedicated teams simultaneously undertook field assessments along designated routes, covering the New Islamabad International Airport, T-Chowk, major roads and connecting corridors, including the Constitution Avenue, Club Road, Murree Road, Rawal Road and areas surrounding the old airport.
During the evaluation, survey teams and media representatives used live data and made voice calls at various locations across the twin cities to assess the actual network performance and consumer experience. Initial results demonstrated excellent performance, reflecting the quality and reliability of telecom services in the areas covered.
The survey was aimed at evaluating the mobile network performance, service availability and actual consumer experience, while identifying the potential service gaps and areas requiring improvement. PTA says it remains committed to strengthening the regulatory oversight through regular field monitoring, evidence-based assessments and close coordination with telecom operators to ensure continuous improvement in service quality and reliable connectivity for consumers.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Addressing social media debates over the scientific validity of Temple’s eponymous brain-monitoring wearable, founder Deepinder Goyal issued a statement directed at “Concerned Indian Doctors”, asserting confidence in the R&D behind the wearables.
Goyal pointed out that Temple had already spent $30 Mn on its development, including $20 Mn of his personal money. He also noted that the company is raising funding from its employees and customers.
“Selling a few thousand devices recovers a small fraction of this investment. A scam that pays nothing is not a scam anyone would run,” the CEO wrote in his post.
Goyal further said the product’s 14-day no-questions-asked return policy would validate its product in the market.
On questions over Temple’s credibility and scientific validation, he argued that many wearable makers initially relied on internal studies before publishing external validation. He said the company would release pre-prints before peer-reviewed publications and it expects independent studies to emerge once the device becomes available more widely.
In a follow-up post, Goyal also said, “Temple is a fitness tracker, and wellness device. We are not a medical device,” adding that the device hasn’t been clinically validated.
Important to highlight that pre-orders for the wearable officially opened on November 1, with a hefty listing price of ₹85,000. Units are hand-made to order and expected to begin shipping roughly three months after purchase, starting in early 2027.
What Doctors Say About Temple?
For context, several medical experts had criticised Temple over its claim that a wearable sensor placed near the temple can reliably measure cerebral blood flow.
Hepatologist Dr Cyriac Abby Philips, popularly known as The Liver Doc, published an Instagram carousel calling the product “the biggest health scam and wellness fraud in India,” saying the device can only detect when blood rushes to one’s face.
Gurugram-based gastroenterologist Dr Zubin Sharma also noted that blood flows to the brain via arteries in the neck and back of head, not the temple.
Additionally, many on social media pointed out that studies published on Temple’s website were not peer-reviewed, and were funded and conducted by the company itself. They also raised questions about the validity of Goyal’s Gravity Ageing Hypothesis, which links the long-term effects of gravity on blood circulation to ageing.
In fact, Dr Philips doubled down on the criticism of Temple in a reply to Goyal’s latest post, calling out Temple’s claims of reading blood flow to the brain and the company’s explanation of its proprietary ‘Entropy’ score.
The Temple Journey So Far
Goyal’s move into brain-monitoring wearables has been taking shape through a series of bets on longevity research. This began with his personal research initiative Continue Research, which he referred to as his personal health and wellness venture back in 2024.
The initiative remained largely under wraps for over a year before unveiling its first hypothesis, Gravity Ageing, in November 2025. The hypothesis proposed that gravity’s effect on cerebral blood flow (CBF) could be an overlooked contributor to human ageing.
Temple emerged around the same time as a commercial extension of this research. Inc42 first reported in November 2025 that Goyal was exploring a wearable device company focused on health monitoring. The device, which he had been seen wearing near his temple, was being used experimentally to measure blood flow to the brain in real time.
“I left the Eternal CEO role to chase purpose with Temple. This is not about money. I have enough of it to last for generations. My incentives are fully aligned with getting the science right. I am not staking a reputation earned over 20 years on making a quick buck,” Goyal said.
On the product front, Temple has been developing a wearable that sits on the forehead near the temple and tracks signals associated with cerebral blood flow. Goyal revealed a smaller version of the device in August, claiming it was less than half the size of its earlier iteration. It has worked with contract manufacturers Zetwerk and Ethereal Machines to scale production, while retaining some manufacturing capabilities in-house.
The startup began taking shape as a standalone venture earlier this year. In February, Temple raised $54 Mn (around ₹493 Cr) in a seed funding round at a post-money valuation of approximately $190 Mn. The round was led by Goyal, who invested a little over ₹100 Cr, with participation from Steadview Capital, Peak XV Partners, Vy Capital, Info Edge Ventures, among others. More than 30 employees also participated in the round.
Temple subsequently expanded its ambitions beyond hardware. In July 2026, it acquired London-based longevity medicine practice Longevous for an undisclosed amount, bringing clinical and scientific expertise into the business.

items.author: Rebecca MacKinnon
items.content:
October’s Spotlight contributors illuminated a range of political, economic, and geographic contexts
Originally published on Global Voices
Image by Gerd Altmann on Pixabay.
Fifteen years ago I wrote an article about “networked authoritarianism,” describing China as “exhibit A” for how an authoritarian state adapts to the internet and then adapts digital technologies to increase its own power. I sought to counter prevailing narratives of the time that the internet and tech companies were intrinsically a liberating, democratizing force. While such narratives were eventually discredited, we must not give up on our ability to use technology to defend and exercise our rights. Nor can we simply demand that governments and companies solve the problems they jointly continue to create.
October’s spotlight on Big Tech and Authoritarianism explored a range of relationships between tech companies and political actors across the global majority. Power is wielded through digital technologies in many ways. There are no quick fixes or easy solutions to stop abuses.
But we are not helpless: our Global Voices community has a role to play in strengthening solidarity and cooperation among people fighting to defend their rights, hold abusers accountable, and claim agency over our information environments.
Spotlight contributors illuminated a range of political, economic, and geographic contexts: from Brazil to Hong Kong, Kenya, Myanmar, Palestine, Venezuela, Xinjiang and beyond. They’ve told stories of how different types of governments (or sometimes political insurgents) leverage geopolitical alliances, relationships with tech companies, regulatory power, or other advantages in order to expand political or military dominance, manipulate public opinion, or exercise direct control over citizens. Meanwhile, companies use their own technologies, resources, and government relationships to expand market access and profit.
Tech power is often wielded in ways that make it harder for ordinary people to fight back against abuses. In some cases it is difficult, if not impossible, to prove who has committed what abuse and whether it was intentional — even while harm to individuals or communities has clearly occurred. In other cases, companies discover abuse of their systems to threaten, silence, surveil, or mislead users only after the damage has been done. In Brazil, one expert warns of “governance washing.” An NGO leader working in West Asia and North Africa warns of the rise of a cottage industry of organizations focused on tech accountability without measurably preventing harms.
The dangers of regulation without accountability and public oversight
In North America and Europe, government regulation of Big Tech is often touted as a silver bullet for protecting citizens from harm. But stories from Bangladesh, Kenya and the DRC illustrate different ways that without rigorous safeguards, regulation and enforcement in the name of holding Big Tech accountable can be abused by governments to threaten, track, or discredit critics and political rivals.
Our contributors pointed to conditions that must be met if we are to prevent government abuse of regulations. Laws and regulations need to be evaluated for their compatibility with human rights standards, and reformed or rejected if they fall short. Citizens — through the free press, watchdog NGOs, whistleblower protections and grievance mechanisms — need to be able to monitor and document harms and abuses with clear process for redress and remedy. Sadly, most democracies fail to hold governments — let alone companies — accountable for protecting human rights.
Then there is the even harder problem of what multinational companies should do after a coup or military takeover, leaving users’ data exposed with deadly consequences. Such cases underscore the vital importance of encryption, data security training for civil society, and corporate data minimization practices.
Rejecting techno-imperialism and great power competition
A number of stories describe how global powers leverage their national tech companies to advance strategic and economic interests well beyond their own borders. The companies in turn benefit from such relationships to expand their own global market access, serving as opaque information intermediaries and channels of digital infrastructure.
There has been much media reporting on China’s global tech strategy as a form of its growing soft power. (At the same time, at least one Chinese company insists it is operating independently and should not be treated as an agent of its home government.) But China is not acting alone: It is actually part of a network of authoritarian states, including Russia, Iran, and North Korea, building an international market for digital surveillance. Customers include many countries often described as democracies.
This eye-opening piece points out that, before the U.S. removal of Venezuelan strongman Nicolás Maduro, then vice president and now interim president Delcy Rodrígues negotiated a deal with the Chinese company iFlytek to jointly develop artificial intelligence. That company has been under U.S. sanctions since 2019, but Australian researchers identified layers of Chinese technology deployed across Venezuela. A UN fact finding mission confirmed that they remain in use despite the interim government’s close relationship with the current U.S. presidential administration.
Meanwhile, this article delves into the consequences of global market competition between the U.S. and China. While highly subsidized Chinese ICT infrastructure brings extra benefits to governments that fear their own people, in many cases Chinese tech is the only affordable option. U.S. reciprocal trade agreements that compel countries to restrict purchases of non-U.S. approved infrastructure may make it harder for signatory countries to bridge their own digital divides — which is another way of disempowering their own citizens by keeping digital services out of reach. The piece raises important questions about how countries can assert digital sovereignty to control their own digital infrastructure.
A call for global solidarity
The Chinese government exercises techno-imperialism against its own citizens. Putin’s regime does the same not only at home but in states the Kremlin views as “near abroad.” The articles in October’s spotlight cover events and harms in the global majority. But as I write from San Francisco on the day after U.S. midterm elections, the people of the U.S. are waking up to how the current occupant of the White House and his allies in Silicon Valley have been practicing techno-imperialism on them.
Tech billionaires and trillionaires have been given free rein to maximize profits at the expense of many Americans’ rights and livelihoods, while hyperscaling the government’s ability to surveil, intimidate and imprison. As this chilling piece from Palestine points out, digital surveillance technologies that are first tested in contexts of military occupation, conquest, and even genocide can be — and are — sold and deployed everywhere that governments can get away with doing so.
Several pieces in the series point to open source, decentralized, and community governed technologies as an antidote to Big Tech, exploitation and weaponization. The challenge lies with finding resources and solid legal footing to build out such technologies and systems — especially when so many governments prefer corporate partners as convenient instruments of control and influence. The good news is that cross-border networks of technologists and grassroots organizations are increasingly collaborating around an alternative vision in which communities have agency over their own information environments.
Networked authoritarianism is a global problem. We will only defeat it with global solidarity. As the African-American voting rights activist Fanny Lou Hamer said in 1971: Nobody’s free until everyone’s free.
Written by Rebecca MacKinnon

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The government has directed banks and other financial institutions to make loans more accessible to small businesses and speed up the financing process.
Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb chaired a meeting to review lending to Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) and discuss ways to help more businesses obtain bank financing.
The meeting reviewed the volume of loans issued to SMEs and the number of businesses receiving financing. Officials noted that although lending had increased, bringing more small businesses into the formal banking system remained a priority.
The finance minister stressed that commercial banks, microfinance banks and non-bank financial institutions should expand their lending to smaller businesses, particularly those involved in exports.
New Portal for Small Business Loans
The meeting also reviewed the newly launched SME Connect portal, which allows small businesses to apply for loans directly and connect with banks.
Aurangzeb welcomed the initial response to the platform, saying thousands of applicants had shown interest since its launch earlier this week.
He directed officials to improve the portal and simplify its procedures so businesses can access financing more easily.
The meeting also discussed better use of financing limits reserved for SMEs, particularly loans for export-related activities.
Aurangzeb called for closer coordination between banks and the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority (SMEDA) to help businesses meet lending requirements and improve their chances of securing loans.
He also directed relevant ministries to identify and resolve regulatory hurdles affecting SME financing.
The government says expanding access to credit for small businesses is part of its broader plan to increase investment, bring more businesses into the formal economy and boost exports.

items.title: SBP Reserves Up $40 Million, Commercial Banks Nearly Double
items.summary:
The State Bank of Pakistan’s (SBP) foreign exchange reserves rose by $39.5 million to $21.6 billion during the week ended October 30, 2026.
According to the central bank, its reserves increased by $39.5 million over the week to $21,561 million. This is the third weekly gain in a row.
Total Liquid Reserves at $26.9 Billion
The country’s total liquid foreign reserves improved by $110.3 million to $26.9 billion as of October 30.
This includes $21.6 billion held by the SBP and $5.3 billion in net reserves held by commercial banks.
Commercial bank reserves were up $70.8 million from $5.233 billion a week earlier.
SBP Targets $25 Billion by June
The latest increase comes weeks after SBP Governor Jameel Ahmed said the central bank expects its reserves to reach $23 billion by December 2026 and $25 billion by June 2027.

items.content:
The media has been urged to play a more active role in holding governments and other stakeholders accountable for policies and interventions in Nigeria’s food system, particularly through evidence-based reporting and sustained public enlightenment.
The call was made at the Sahel Changemakers Conference which held in Abuja, on Thursday.
The Media Dialogue themed “Building Nigeria’s Food System Architecture: The Role of Media in Driving accountability, Evidence and Public Action”, featured Ntiedo Ekott of the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID), Abdulkareem Mojeed of Premium Times and Israel Boboye of CJID, who discussed the role of media in strengthening accountability, promoting informed public discourse and ensuring that issues affecting the agricultural sector receive adequate attention.
The dialogue formed part of broader conversations at the conference on the need for stronger collaboration among government partners, private sector development partners and other sectors to address challenges confronting Nigeria’s food system.

Speaking at the conference, Dr Markus Wagner, Country Director, German Development Cooperation, who was represented byDr Karin Jansen, Head of Development Cooperation at the German Embassy, said transforming Nigeria’s agri-food system required coordinated efforts from public, private and development partners.
She said the transformation should deliver nutritional, economic, environmental and social outcomes, including healthy diets, decent employment opportunities for women and young people, protection of natural resources and support for smallholder farmers to adapt to climate change.Jansen said information often existed within organizations but failed to reach the people who needed it, while projects sometimes produced results that were difficult to sustain after their completion.
Also speaking, Nwuneli Okonkwo, Executive Director Sahel Consulting, called for greater integration efforts across sectors, noting that challenges relating to food, nutrition, healthcare and agriculture were interconnected.
She said the country’s poor nutrition outcomes, maternal health challenges and the difficulties confronting farmers could not be addressed independently, saying “policies on agriculture must bear households in mind to succeed as the country needed to move beyond fragmented approaches and develop more coordinated responses that reflected the realities of Nigerian households”.
She described the conference as a call to action, urging stakeholders to break institutional silos and align their efforts.
In his remarks, Temi Adegoroye, Managing Partner Sahel Consulting, said Nigeria’s food system remained poorly coordinated and the large number of people who livelihood depend on it large number of people whose livelihoods depended on it, saying roughly one in three working Nigerians is connected to agriculture and food in one way or another.
According to him, “Climate shocks, insecurity, rising input costs reduce harvest and incomes and shrink diets and erode nutrition. And poor nutrition holds back health and learning.
“Weaker human capital means lower earnings and lower productivity, which leaves the very same households exposed to the next shock.
“The deeper work ahead of us is not about programmes, not about more programmes. It is not about more investment per se. It is about architecture.”

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has introduced new measures to regulate the verification of plot files and streamline the processing of property-related cases. It has directed officials to avoid unnecessary verification procedures that cause delays and inconvenience to applicants.
According to an official notification issued by the Office of the Member (Estate) on November 5, 2026, officials of the Land and Rehabilitation Directorate have been initiating the verification of plot files in certain cases without cogent justification or objectively established grounds.
The notification states that such practices can cause unnecessary delays in processing cases and inconvenience applicants. It has, therefore, directed that verification of the genuineness of any plot file should only be initiated after obtaining prior approval from the Director General (Land and Estate Management).
The Director General (Land and Estate Management) has also been directed to prescribe and notify clear timelines for completing plot file verifications and processing applications for No Demand Certificates (NDCs) and other property-related matters at the relevant desks.
Under the new directions, preferably, no file should remain pending at a single desk for more than three days.
CDA added that these measures aim to improve administrative efficiency, ensure the timely disposal of property-related cases, and prevent unnecessary delays in the Estate Wing.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Bengaluru-based biotechnology startup Venomics AI has raised $2.7 Mn (around ₹25.5 Cr) in a pre-seed funding round co-led by Speciale Invest and South Park Commons, with participation from Operators Studio.
The startup, spun out of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), combines venom biology, AI and experimental screening to identify and develop venom-derived molecules into potential therapeutic leads.
The fresh capital will be used to expand ‘Venom Atlas’, a molecular dataset of venom-derived compounds, and strengthen its AI and laboratory screening capabilities. The startup also plans to expand its team across venom biology, computational science and drug discovery, while supporting the validation and optimisation of promising molecules.
Founded in 2026 by Kartik Sunagar and Vinay Prabhu, Venomics AI is working to tap the largely unexplored molecular diversity found in animal venoms to identify potential drug candidates.
Animal venoms contain complex molecules that have evolved over millions of years to interact with specific biological targets. Some of these compounds have already inspired medicines.
However, a large part of the molecular diversity across venomous species remains unexplored, presenting an opportunity for drug discovery.
Venomics AI is building a platform that combines molecular sequencing and venom biology to map this diversity through its Venom Atlas. It then uses AI to prioritise promising molecular candidates and validates its predictions through functional laboratory screening.
“Animal venoms represent one of nature’s richest yet least explored sources of potential medicines, and at Venomics AI, we are combining cutting-edge experimental science with artificial intelligence to unlock this extraordinary potential,” Sunagar said.
India’s bioeconomy is on track to reach $300 Bn by 2030, with the country’s rapid emergence as a global biotechnology hub, based on IBEF data. Notably, the biotech sector in the country has been booming in recent years. The country is home to more than 11,000 biotech startups.
Also, as part of the Budget 2027, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced a new ‘Biopharma SHAKTI’ scheme with an outlay of ₹10,000 Cr.
Meanwhile, investor interest in this space has been gradually seeing an uptick, where earlier this year, Cellogen Therapeutics secured ₹20 Cr in funding from Kotak Alternate Asset Managers (Kotak Alts), while StrainX Bioworks has raised $13 Mn in a funding round led by Prime Venture Partners and Leo Capital.

Companies and industry bodies focused on six areas: AI and cloud, cybersecurity, digital governance, IT services trade and investment, digital skills, and quantum computing.
Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, the chief guest, called on firms from both sides to pursue joint ventures, pilot projects and market access. He said Pakistan produces over 75,000 IT graduates a year, aims to train one million AI professionals by 2030, and is setting up seven new AI centres.
PSEB CEO Faisal Jeddy said every participating company would leave with a defined opportunity, a named counterpart and a clear next step. “Partnerships rarely fail for lack of intent; they fail for lack of follow-up,” he said.
Firms including Ebryx, Positive Technologies, TMC and the Russian Quantum Center discussed co-developing cybersecurity, enterprise software, FinTech and AI products for Pakistan, Russia and third countries.
What This Means for Pakistan’s IT Sector
Pakistan’s IT and telecom exports hit a record $4.6 billion in FY2025-26, up about 20%, and the sector is now hunting for new markets. Russia could become one of them.
IT Secretary Zarrar Hasham Khan said the talks produced a shortlist of concrete opportunities, and the ministry will help clear regulatory hurdles so the first pilot projects start without delay. The push follows other recent steps in bilateral ties, including Russian scholarships for Pakistani students.

"If successfully exploited, the actors could change the temperature and possibly cause physical impacts ​such as fire hazards, loss of inventory and changes to the service life of the system," said the statement, which was jointly issued by the FBI, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency ​and the departments of health, transport and agriculture.
"Every organisation that depends on refrigeration ​and monitoring systems should assume it could be a target," said Chris Butera, CISA's acting executive ‌assistant director ⁠for cybersecurity.
FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman said that the government was "seeing these systems targeted across critical infrastructure sectors globally".
The government urged operators of industrial refrigeration control systems to pull their devices off the public internet, isolate them from their corporate ​networks, and promptly apply ​software updates.
At least ⁠three waves of hacks have hit commercial fridges and freezers in the past few months. Pentagon investigators are treating a series ​of mysterious malfunctions that hit grocery store refrigeration units on ​US military ⁠bases in August as a cyberattack, Reuters first reported last week. A sweeping hack of French freezers last month dealt tens of millions of euros' worth of damage, while ⁠a second ​wave of hacking affected more than 100 stores across ​Europe on Monday.

The hacks have raised concerns over the ability of hackers to remotely tamper with refrigerators and other ​critical devices.

items.author: Akshit Pushkarna
items.content:
Travel-focused SaaS company RateGain reported a 46.5% increase in its consolidated net profit to ₹74.7 Cr in the September quarter (Q2 FY27) from ₹51 Cr a year ago.
Operating revenue jumped 152.6% YoY to ₹745.4 Cr, reflecting the consolidation of travel marketing platform Sojern, which RateGain acquired for $250 Mn in November last year.
Sequentially, net profit declined 21.3% from ₹94.9 Cr, while operating revenue fell 5% from ₹785 Cr.
RateGain reported negative other income of ₹26.2 Lakh, taking its total income to ₹745.1 Cr. Total expenses rose about 158% YoY to ₹647.7 Cr.
Adjusted for deferred deal consideration related to the Sojern acquisition, RateGain said its net profit rose 78% YoY to ₹90.8 Cr, while adjusted EBITDA more than tripled to ₹169.1 Cr.
For H1 FY27, operating revenue increased 169.5% YoY to ₹1,530.4 Cr from ₹568 Cr. Reported EBITDA rose 214.2% to ₹324.5 Cr, while adjusted EBITDA increased 250.9% to ₹362.5 Cr.
The company said its reported H1 EBITDA had already exceeded its full-year FY26 EBITDA.
Sojern Integration And Debt
The Sojern acquisition expanded RateGain’s travel marketing business, particularly its presence among destination marketing organisations (DMOs), hotels, and other travel businesses.
To finance the acquisition, RateGain’s UK subsidiary secured a $125 Mn debt facility from HSBC and Citibank, backed by a corporate guarantee from the Indian parent.
Including a repayment of $46.3 Mn today, the subsidiary has repaid $93.8 Mn, or 75%, of the original facility. Its outstanding debt now stands at $31.3 Mn.
Alongside the expansion in revenue, RateGain said the Sojern integration helped broaden its customer base. It had 14,538 customers at the end of September, about 4.5X the 3,224 customers it had at the end of FY25.
Its customers include hospitality companies, online travel agencies (OTAs), airlines, car rental companies, and DMOs.
Marketing Drives Business Mix
RateGain operates across three verticals: data as a service (DaaS), distribution, and marketing technology. Its offerings span competitive pricing and demand intelligence, hotel distribution, digital marketing, and guest engagement.
Marketing technology now accounts for 80.2% of revenue, followed by DaaS at 13.2% and distribution at 6.6%.
By customer industry, hospitality contributed 48.6% of H1 revenue, followed by DMOs at 30.9%, OTAs at 7.2%, airlines at 3.7%, and car rentals at 2.3%.
North America accounted for 63.7% of H1 revenue, followed by Europe at 21.5%, Asia-Pacific at 12.3%, and other markets at 2.5%.
The company’s client roster includes 33 of the world’s top 40 hotel chains, four of the top five airlines, and seven of the top 10 car rental companies.
RateGain also highlighted its AI products. Chairman and MD Bhanu Chopra said shifting travel demand is increasing customers’ reliance on data and AI.
He said RateGain’s priorities included adding customers, increasing their use of its platform, and extending AI into more of their daily operations. In H2 FY27, the company plans to take the combined RateGain and Sojern offering to more customers.
RateGain reported a total pipeline of ₹660 Cr and new contract wins worth ₹277.7 Cr.
The company’s employee headcount stood at 1,244 at the end of September, up 42.8% YoY.
Shares of RateGain ended today’s trading session 3.3% higher at ₹819.50 apiece on the BSE.

items.title: Nearly 600,000 demonstrate across France in biggest turnout of protest movement
items.summary:
Nearly 600,000 people took part in demonstrations across France on Thursday, according to a provisional estimate by the Interior Ministry, marking the largest turnout since the protest movement began, BFMTV reported.
The estimate exceeds the 550,000 demonstrators recorded on October 17, 410,000 on October 24 and 320,000 on October 31.
The General Confederation of Labour (CGT) trade union confederation claimed nearly 1.6 million protesters took part in demonstrations nationwide, compared with the Interior Ministry’s estimate of 600,000.
Read: Mass protests in France spiral into worst riots in years
The union also put participation in the Paris march between Place de la Republique and Place de la Nation at 350,000.
Tens of thousands of trade union members joined nationwide strikes and demonstrations across France, demanding higher wages and backing a growing high school protest movement, in a major show of pressure on president Macron’s government.

items.summary: Bitget has introduced its Open Custody Network (OCN), allowing eligible users to trade on its spot, margin, and futures markets without transferring assets into the exchange’s custody. The system connects independent banks and custodians to Bitget’s trading engine through asset mirroring, allowing participants to access the exchange’s liquidity while retaining custody of their funds. The initiative targets institutional participants, including market makers and asset managers, and builds on Bitget’s existing partnerships with third-party custody providers.

items.title: From US Senate to Israel’s Knesset, Arab and Muslim electoral gains open paths to influence
items.summary:
