items.title: PTA Registers BIGO LIVE and Likee Platforms in Pakistan
items.summary:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) has formally registered BIGO LIVE and Likee platforms in Pakistan under Bigo Service Pakistan (Pvt.) Ltd., in accordance with the Removal and Blocking of Unlawful Online Content (Procedure, Oversight and Safeguards) Rules, 2021.
PTA look forward to strengthening its collaboration with BIGO to enhance content moderation mechanisms, promote responsible platform use, and ensure continued compliance with Pakistan’s applicable laws.
The registration marks an important step towards strengthening PTA’s engagement with major social media platforms and fostering a safe, responsible and secure digital environment for users in Pakistan.
Also Read: 96 Million on YouTube, 100 Million on WhatsApp and TikTok: PTA Maps How Pakistan Uses Social Media

items.content:
US Vice President JD Vance said on Wednesday that the Iran war had doomed Republicans in the midterm elections, moving to distance himself from the unpopular conflict ahead of a possible 2028 White House run.
“The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night,” Vance said in a lengthy post on X — apparently referring to President Donald Trump’s remarks that the Iran war was “part of it” but that it was still justified.
“If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that’s at least honest,” added Vance.
Read: US midterms deliver wave of historic firsts across states, Congress
One of the things the data analysts on our side obsessed over was "composition"—whether the electorate looked close enough to 2024 for Republicans to win. And despite polls that showed a Democrat blowout, the data kept on telling us the same story: in some states turnout was…
— JD Vance (@JDVance) November 4, 2026
“But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there.”
The Democratic wave in Tuesday’s midterms has raised major questions over Vance’s previous status as the frontrunner for the Republican nomination in the 2028 presidential election.
He has not yet formally declared that he will run.
Vance, a longtime vocal critic of US foreign interventionism, had reportedly been sceptical behind the scenes about the war on Iran that Trump and Israel launched in late February.
Vance also acknowledged that Republican voters who backed Trump and himself two years ago had switched sides due to the war and its effects on the US economy.
“The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026,” Vance said.
He said a pollster that he respected showed the Iran war and the economy were key factors in voters abandoning Republicans, along with a desire to “change our relationship to Israel”.
Meanwhile, top Senate Democrat Chuck Schumer said the Iran war “must end” and suggested his party’s incoming majority in Congress could use their control over government funding to press for that goal.
“This war must end. It must end,” Schumer told journalists, later noting that the “power of the purse” is “one of the ways of deterring a president who does war without the consent of the American people”.
"The American people don't know what the heck we're fighting for in Iran."
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer calls for an end to the war, accusing President Trump of repeatedly shifting his explanation for the U.S. mission.
Schumer also warns that Democrats will pursue… pic.twitter.com/7j9QbXY7ZX
— Fox News (@FoxNews) November 4, 2026
White House insists Trump is ‘still your president’ after midterm rout
Donald Trump is “still your president”, the White House said on Wednesday, a day after his Republican Party suffered sweeping losses in midterm elections seen as a referendum on his second term.
The White House delivered the message in a post on X featuring a picture of a glaring Trump looming over the Resolute Desk in the Oval Office.
Read More: Trump hand-picked Senate candidates. Republicans paid the price
“PSA: TRUMP IS STILL YOUR PRESIDENT,” text superimposed on the image said, using the abbreviation for public service announcement.
Thank you for your attention to this matter. pic.twitter.com/Q1ZGYM7idV
— The White House (@WhiteHouse) November 4, 2026
“Thank you for your attention to this matter,” the post added, using a phrase Trump frequently employs in his social media messages.
Opposition Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate on Tuesday, dealing a major blow to Trump and the Republican Party.
The Democratic capture of Congress signals an end to Trump’s stranglehold on US politics and gives Democrats the power to pass legislation, launch investigations into Trump’s administration and thwart his appointments.
The results reflected deep frustration over the cost of living, tariffs and Trump’s war with Iran, which has sent prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president.
But Trump has threatened to use his veto power, raising questions about how much Democrats can achieve even with control of both the House and Senate.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
upGrad has filed an insolvency petition against B9 Beverages Ltd, the maker of Bira91 beer, over alleged unpaid dues of ₹1.02 Cr, adding to the financial and legal challenges facing the brewer.
The petition, filed under Section 9 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016, was submitted to the Delhi bench of the NCLT on October 22, as per documents reviewed by Moneycontrol.
upGrad has named B9 Beverages as the corporate debtor and sought the initiation of the corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP) to recover the outstanding amount.
The petition does not disclose the nature of services provided by upGrad to the beverage maker.
Inc42 has reached out to upGrad and Anicut Capital for a comment on the development. The story will be updated on receiving a response.
The filing comes amid mounting liabilities and creditor disputes at B9 Beverages, which is facing insolvency-related action from multiple creditors.
In September, the NCLT directed B9 Beverages and its creditors to explore a settlement through mediation in connection with multiple insolvency proceedings. The tribunal also restrained the brewer from disposing of its assets while discussions were underway.
The company has also faced action from glass manufacturer Hindusthan National Glass & Industries Ltd (HNGIL), which sought to recover ₹11.8 Cr in alleged unpaid dues.
HNGIL issued a demand notice under Section 8 of the IBC over customised glass bottles manufactured against confirmed purchase orders but allegedly not collected by the brewer. The glassmaker claimed that more than 51 Lakh bottles worth over ₹7 Cr remained stored at its facilities, despite it encashing bank guarantees worth ₹3.91 Cr.
The latest development comes as the startup attempts to restructure its business amid a prolonged financial crisis.
In July, founder Ankur Jain stepped down from the company’s board and relinquished executive control and ownership following a dispute with investors and lenders.
VC firm Anicut Capital, one of Bira’s key lenders, subsequently took control of Jain and his family’s stake in the company, as per reports.
Anicut had extended loans to B9 Beverages between 2017 and 2022, secured against the promoter family’s stake.
The brewer is now expected to be recapitalised by existing investors and lenders under a revival plan aimed at clearing statutory, employee and vendor dues and restarting operations.
Founded by Jain in 2015, Bira 91 raised more than $200 Mn from investors. Its annual revenue crossed $100 Mn in FY23. Its shareholders include Peak XV Partners, Sofina and Japan-based Kirin Holdings. Anicut Capital and Hero Corporate Services’ family office are among its key lenders.
Its troubles began after it converted into a public company, triggering fresh excise approval requirements across multiple states. This disrupted the production and sales of the beer. The company subsequently wrote off inventory worth around ₹80 Cr and fell behind on vendor payments.
The company eventually paused its packaged beer business amid a prolonged funding crunch, mounting vendor liabilities and difficulties in meeting employee and statutory obligations.
The company reported a net loss of ₹748 Cr in FY24, with accumulated losses of ₹2,117.9 Cr. Its auditor also warned that current liabilities exceeded assets by ₹487 Cr as of March 2024.
Under Section 9 of the IBC, an operational creditor can approach the NCLT to initiate insolvency proceedings after serving a demand notice and meeting the prescribed statutory conditions.
However, filing a petition does not automatically trigger insolvency proceedings. The NCLT will examine the application to determine whether the requirements for admission have been met.

Read: Govt cuts petrol price by Rs5.45, HSD by Rs3.68 for Nov 4
On Monday, the government announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.
Read More: Refineries to shoulder Rs15b fuel burden
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.

items.author: Vinaykumar Rai
items.content:
The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has set up a wholly owned subsidiary, NPCI Tech Solutions Ltd (NTSL), to build capabilities in AI, blockchain, and digital financial infrastructure beyond its core payments mandate.
The retail payments operator has appointed Vishal Kanvaty, who has been associated with NPCI for nearly a decade, as the subsidiary’s MD and CEO.
NPCI said NTSL will serve as the group’s technology and innovation arm. Its remit will also include global capability centre (GCC) services and technology services for eKYC Setu, the Unified Ticketing Platform (UTP), and other digital public infrastructure (DPI) programmes.
According to NPCI, Kanvaty has led the development and commercialisation of several platforms that now fall within NTSL’s focus areas.
NPCI MD & CEO Dilip Asbe said advances in AI and other emerging technologies are opening up opportunities across digital infrastructure and financial services. The subsidiary has been established to pursue these opportunities and strengthen the group’s technology capabilities, he added.
NPCI did not disclose the subsidiary’s investment outlay, revenue targets, customer pipeline, or timelines for rolling out new services.
NPCI’s Emerging Technology Push
The formation follows a series of technology initiatives by NPCI. At the Global Fintech Fest in September, it launched AiNxt and AtOM, platforms aimed at helping enterprises build AI agents and automate workflows across the payments ecosystem.
AiNxt enables enterprises to build, test, and deploy custom AI agents, while AtOM is designed to handle integration, change management, and partner onboarding across UPI, with digitally signed interactions providing audit trails.
NPCI’s work in emerging technologies also includes a multi-year research partnership with IISc, announced in March 2024, covering AI and blockchain. The collaboration envisaged developing models and software prototypes, alongside workshops and training programmes.
On the payments side, NPCI demonstrated an agentic AI framework for UPI at GFF 2025. The demonstration showed how user-authorised AI assistants could discover products, place orders, and complete payments within a single conversational flow.
The new technology arm joins NPCI’s existing subsidiaries focused on international payments, bill payments, and BHIM. With NTSL, the group now has four wholly owned subsidiaries: NPCI International Payments Ltd (NIPL), NPCI Bharat BillPay Ltd (NBBL), NPCI BHIM Services Ltd (NBSL), and NTSL.
The expansion comes alongside continued growth in its flagship payments network. UPI processed a record 25.47 Bn transactions in October, up 5.8% MoM, while transaction value increased 7.4% to ₹31.53 Lakh Cr. Average daily transaction value crossed ₹1 Lakh Cr for the first time.
This came ahead of the proposed introduction of merchant discount rate (MDR) charges on select UPI payments. NPCI deferred the rollout, originally scheduled for October 15, until after Diwali, with a revised implementation date yet to be announced.

items.author: Anadolu Agency
items.content:
Democrats’ victory in the US midterm elections has handed them control of both chambers of Congress, setting up a period of divided government that could complicate President Donald Trump’s agenda during the final two years of his term.
Democrats on Tuesday secured a majority in both chambers of Congress, winning a projected 54 seats in the Senate and 224 seats in the House of Representatives.
When the new Congress convenes in January 2027, Trump will face a Democratic-controlled House of Representatives and Senate, limiting his ability to advance legislation and potentially complicating his administration’s spending priorities.
Read: Democrats sweep Congress in US midterm elections
Here is what the shift in power means for the president:
Stronger congressional oversight
One of the biggest changes will be Democrats’ control of congressional committees in both chambers.
Committees can hold hearings, request government documents, and summon officials to testify. They can also issue subpoenas, although disputes over their authority and executive privilege can lead to legal challenges.
Scott Lucas, a professor of international politics at the Clinton Institute, University College Dublin, said that Democrats are more likely to focus on investigations and accountability.
A demonstrator wearing a frog costume and holding a "CLEAN HOUSE" banner near the White House in Washington, DC, during the US midterm elections on November 4, 2026. Photo: Reuters
These could include inquiries into Trump's stockholdings, potential insider trading involving his family, and the wealth he has accumulated while in office.
“What Democrats can also do because they now control the committees in both houses is have hearings for accountability,” he said.
Lucas also expects renewed scrutiny of the files related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, with victims’ families and many Democrats saying the Justice Department has yet to release all the files required under a law passed last year.
“I think you'll see hearings reopen on the Epstein files,” he said.
Other possible inquiries could focus on federal agencies and whether they have been weakened or pressured by the administration, "like the Justice Department to restore the independence of those agencies,” Lucas said.
More legislative obstacles
Democrats will be able to introduce legislation reflecting their own priorities, including proposals on health care, education, and immigration. Lawmakers could also seek legislation to address potential conflicts of interest involving elected officials.
“For example, trying to seek accountability on stockholdings might be a bill that you see very clearly so that representatives don't have conflicts of interest,” he said.
“They could proceed with proposed legislation on health, on education, to push back on the immigration crackdown.”
Supporters react after media outlets projected Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico's victory in Austin, Texas. Photo: Reuters
However, passing such measures will be difficult if Trump opposes them.
“Donald Trump has already been ruling through executive orders, and there is only one major bill that he has passed ... but Democrats can propose their own legislation. They can put forth their own priorities.”
“Now all of that legislation could get vetoed by Trump, of course, and you need a two-thirds majority to override that,” Lucas explained.
A presidential veto can be overturned only if two-thirds of members voting in both the House of Representatives and the Senate support the measure.
This means Democrats would need Republican support to enact major legislation over Trump's objections.
Lucas said some Republicans may become more willing to cooperate with them, as the election result could weaken Trump's influence over his own party and encourage some Republican lawmakers to distance themselves from the president.
Greater leverage over government spending
Democrats will have greater influence over federal spending, including the defense budget, military operations, and foreign military assistance, as Congress controls government appropriations.
They could use budget negotiations to scrutinize Pentagon spending, demand greater transparency over military operations, including the ongoing Iran war, and seek changes to defend funding priorities.
However, the president retains authority as commander-in-chief, and funding already appropriated under existing laws can generally continue to be spent.
Also Read: Trump hand-picked Senate candidates. Republicans paid the price
Lucas, however, said he would be surprised if Democrats deliberately pursued a government shutdown, describing such a move as irresponsible.
"I'd be very surprised if Democrats go for shutting down the government. That won't be responsible.”
Instead, he expects Democrats to wait and see how Trump responds to the new balance of power.
“I think they will wait to see if Trump wants to shut down the government, which is very possible if he feels he's not getting his way,” Lucas said.
Last year, the country witnessed the longest government-wide shutdown in history of 43 days, from Oct. 1 to Nov. 12, 2025, ending after Congress passed a funding measure that Trump signed into law.
Appointment and administration battles
A Democratic-controlled Senate will have the power to scrutinise and reject Trump’s nominees for federal judgeships, Cabinet positions, ambassadorships, and potential Supreme Court vacancies.
Democrats could also use oversight hearings to scrutinise senior administration officials.
Lucas suggested that Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth could face particular scrutiny if the months-long Iran war continues.
“They may open up hearings on certain officials like the Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, especially if the Iran war continues to go so badly and he keeps urging the military,” Lucas said.
Read More: Iranian officials gloat as US voters deal blow to Trump
He also pointed to the possibility of congressional scrutiny of senior Justice Department officials.
“I think they will push back on other officials, maybe short of impeachment, like the head of the Justice Department, Todd Blanche, because he's effectively Trump's lawyer,” he said.
Democrats charge that Trump has weaponised and politicised the Justice Department, using it as a tool to target his political enemies.
Impeachment issue
Democrats could technically launch another impeachment process against Trump, as the House has the power to impeach a president with a simple majority.
But removing him from office would be much harder. Conviction in the Senate requires a two-thirds majority of senators present.
Trump was impeached twice during his first term, in 2019 over his dealings with Ukraine and in 2021 over his role in the events surrounding the Jan. 6 attack on the US Capitol. The Senate acquitted him in both cases.
Lucas does not expect Democrats to make impeachment their priority.
Senator-elect from Kansas Hamilton in Overland Park, November 3, 2026. Photo: Reuters
“Remember, you need a two-thirds majority to convict in the Senate, so you would need 67 seats. At most they're going to have 56 and more likely it's going to be around 54, maybe 55.”
Current projections put Senate Democrats at 54 seats.
Lucas said the emphasis would be on holding officials accountable rather than trying to remove Trump from office.
“I look for them more to go for those hearings for accountability rather than impeachment when it comes to Trump.”
What happens next?
The new Congress is scheduled to begin its term on Jan 3, 2027. Republicans retain control of both chambers until the current congressional term ends.
Democratic control will not automatically reverse Trump’s executive actions or remove his constitutional powers. However, it will give the opposition party greater authority to investigate his administration, challenge his legislative priorities, and influence federal spending.
The next two years could thus see increased congressional scrutiny, prolonged negotiations over government funding, and a more contested relationship between the White House and Capitol Hill.

items.content:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Wednesday received the official results of last week's parliamentary elections as the Central Elections Committee rejected fraud allegations raised by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and right-wing parties.
"Voices are seeking to undermine the election results. This is a real danger," Committee Chairman Judge Noam Sohlberg said during a ceremony attended by Herzog, according to Israeli news website Ynet.
Sohlberg said allegations concerning aspects of the electoral process remained under investigation but warned against questioning the legitimacy of votes cast by Arab citizens.
Read: Israeli opposition leaders say Netanyahu cannot remain in power after US midterm elections
"We must not cast doubt on voting in Arab society, just as we must not cast doubt on any other group in Israeli society," he said.
The election results are "binding on all of us," Sohlberg stressed.
Earlier Wednesday, the committee approved the final results, with 15 members voting in favor, two against and 14 abstaining, according to Ynet.
The approval followed the committee's announcement that it had found no evidence that the integrity of last week's parliamentary elections had been compromised.
Netanyahu and right-wing parties in his bloc had alleged fraud and voting manipulation within Israel's Arab community.
Herzog to begin government formation consultations
Herzog is scheduled to begin consultations with representatives of elected parties Wednesday afternoon to determine which lawmaker should be tasked with forming the next government, Ynet reported.
During the consultations, parliamentary parties are expected to recommend candidates for prime minister.
Herzog will then decide which candidate has the best chance of assembling a governing coalition and grant that lawmaker the mandate to form a government.
Also Read: Eisenkot says Netanyahu's bid to discredit Israeli election results has 'failed'
Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot is expected to receive 48 recommendations from Yashar, Yachad, the Democrats and Yisrael Beytenu.
Netanyahu is expected to secure 46 recommendations from Likud, Otzma Yehudit, Shas and Religious Zionism.
The predominantly Arab parties, including the Joint List and Ra'am, and the ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism party have yet to announce whom they will recommend, according to Ynet.

items.title: Smartphone Financing Framework Remains Unresolved as Operators Seek Regulatory Support
items.summary:

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan’s efforts to make smartphones more affordable through installment plans continue to face regulatory hurdles, as a joint proposal submitted by the country’s four major telecom operators remains unresolved.
Jazz, PTCL/Ufone, Telenor, and Zong approached the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) on May 7, 2026, seeking a regulatory framework to support smartphone financing and address the risks associated with customers failing to repay installments.
According to industry sources, the proposed framework has yet to be finalized, leaving telecom operators and financing providers without a clear mechanism for managing repayment defaults while protecting consumers.
One of the key proposals involved allowing SIM blocking as a last resort in cases of persistent non-payment. However, the operators suggested that such a measure should be subject to customer consent and appropriate consumer protection safeguards.
The issue has become increasingly important as Pakistan struggles to improve smartphone ownership despite the expanding availability of mobile broadband networks.
According to the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics’ Household Integrated Economic Survey 2024–25, only 50% of individuals aged 10 and above owned a mobile phone, including smartphones.
The survey also highlighted a significant gender gap, with mobile phone ownership standing at approximately 70% among males compared to just 30% among females.
Meanwhile, a GSMA report published in August 2025 estimated that mobile broadband networks covered around 80% of Pakistan’s population, but only 30% used mobile internet in 2024.
These figures suggest that network availability alone is not enough to increase digital participation, particularly when millions of consumers cannot afford internet-enabled devices.
Can Open Banking Help Pakistan Expand Smartphone Installment Plans?
One of the biggest challenges in smartphone financing is assessing whether customers can repay their installments, especially those working in the informal economy.
Many potential buyers lack documented salaries, formal credit histories, or the financial records traditionally required by banks and financing companies.
Although companies such as Qistbazar already offer smartphones through installment plans, including arrangements with telecom operators, expanding these services to lower-income customers remains difficult.
A recent development by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) could potentially help address part of this problem.
On October 30, 2026, the central bank released draft Open Banking Regulations for public consultation, proposing a framework for secure financial data sharing with customer consent.
If implemented, the framework could allow authorized financing providers to assess customers using verified financial transaction histories instead of relying entirely on conventional credit scores or salary documentation.
This could be particularly useful for individuals who regularly use digital wallets and banking services but do not have access to traditional credit facilities.
However, the proposed Open Banking Regulations have not been finalized, and their potential application to smartphone financing would depend on the final rules, access to relevant financial data, and participation by authorized institutions.
Meanwhile, the telecom operators’ earlier proposal also called for a structured approach to handling repayment defaults.
Instead of immediately restricting mobile services, such a framework could include payment reminders, advance notifications, opportunities to resolve disputes, and other recovery measures before considering more serious action.
SIM blocking was proposed as an ultimate recourse, rather than an automatic penalty for missed installments.
Consumer protection would remain a critical consideration, particularly regarding customer consent, genuine financial hardship, dispute resolution, and the restoration of services after repayment.
Beyond financing arrangements, smartphone prices remain another major obstacle.
Import dependence, applicable duties, and taxes increase the upfront cost of devices, making even entry-level smartphones difficult to afford for many households.
Reducing these costs could lower the amount consumers need to finance and make installment-based purchasing more accessible.
For now, the regulatory framework requested by telecom operators remains unresolved, while the SBP’s Open Banking proposal is still at the consultation stage.
Without clear financing rules, effective repayment assessment mechanisms, and more affordable devices, expanding smartphone ownership among Pakistan’s underserved population will remain a challenge.
As education, financial services, employment opportunities, and government services increasingly move online, improving access to smartphones could play an important role in narrowing the country’s digital divide.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Indonesia's president sacked his chief of staff on Wednesday after his arrest in a wiretapping scandal ‌that the government said pointed to treason, as the military said thousands of troops were being mobilised in the capital to boost security.
Listyo Sigit Prabowo, who was appointed chief of staff just a few weeks ago, was among three senior police officers detained on Tuesday, accused of illegally tapping the phones of President Prabowo Subianto and unnamed journalists, politicians, government ​officials and business people since early 2025.
The illegal wiretaps were carried out by "rogue individuals" whose actions indicated treason, presidential spokesperson Prasetyo Hadi ​said.
Read: IOC regrets Indonesian decision to block entry for Israeli gymnasts
"It also tends toward acts that endanger state interests and the safety of the nation's leadership, including the safety of ⁠the head of state," Hadi told reporters.
Reuters could not immediately contact the three suspects or their lawyers.
The scandal comes as the president, a retired army ​general, faces pressure on multiple fronts, with widening public discontent about his big-spending populist policies and a slump in investor confidence over his administration's handling ​of the $1.5 trillion G20 economy.
Political intrigue has been growing in Indonesia in recent weeks amid a rift between Prabowo and his two-term predecessor and former backer Widodo, who remains highly influential, despite stepping back from politics.
Listyo, the former national police chief, was known as a loyalist of Widodo.
Military mobilized to ‘safeguard and protect stability'
Troops were deployed to Jakarta to "safeguard and ​protect the stability of Indonesia's security," navy spokesperson Tunggul said late on Wednesday.
The deployment was also related to upcoming training in areas near Jakarta, Tunggul, ​who goes by one name, added.
Soldiers on the capital's streets are not uncommon in Indonesia, where the military has been regularly deployed ahead of anti-government protests.
Elected president in ‌2024 by ⁠a big majority, former special forces commander Prabowo has seen his approval rating slide in his second year in office, with unease over food prices and his troubled free meals and village cooperatives programmes.
His administration has also been under intense investor scrutiny this year, with ratings outlook cuts, concerns about policy unpredictability, and record stock market routs after warnings by global index provider MSCI of an equities market downgrade.
Prabowo's party Gerindra said it would hold talks with other political parties to discuss the ​wiretapping, with its secretary-general Sugiono on Wednesday ​calling the scandal "insubordination" within the government.
In ⁠a post on X on Wednesday, former President Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono appealed to Prabowo to "restore civility to our politics".
Motive for wiretaps unclear
The government has yet to determine the motive for the wiretapping, said Yusril Ihza Mahendra, Indonesia's senior ​minister for legal affairs.
Police late on Tuesday said the suspects were being investigated for unauthorised wiretaps. The targets ​of the wiretaps were ⁠not disclosed.
Amnesty International in Indonesia urged authorities on Wednesday to reveal who the subjects of the wiretaps were and said the public had a right to know.
Also Read: Indonesia says no to $1 billion fee for Trump's 'Board of Peace' seat
"If this scandal is allowed to continue unchecked, it could pave the way for a secret police apparatus used to tame the opposition," it said.
Sana Jaffrey, a state-building ⁠researcher at ​the Australian National University, said the troop deployment in Jakarta could signal concerns about tension ​between the military and police loyal to former chief Listyo.
"If Prabowo increasingly sees threats to his personal security, then this could strengthen the case for relying more heavily on the military," she ​said, adding that the immediate concern was the risk of unintended escalation.

"The US sees the end of its hegemony as distant; we see it as near," he added.
Old foes
Democrats ​captured majorities in both the Senate and House in Tuesday's election, with victories in Republican strongholds underscoring deep frustration with Trump's stewardship of the economy and his decision to ​launch a war that drove up gas prices.
In Iran, a news outlet run by the judiciary shared a joke circulating on X that "Trump failed at ⁠regime change in Iran, but he succeeded in Texas", a reference to the southern state where a Democrat won a Senate race for the first time in decades.
But two senior Iranian sources ​told Reuters that while Iranian leaders welcomed the Democrats’ victory, Tehran was concerned that Trump could seek to compensate for it with a military strike, and remained on high alert.
Read: Anyone expecting shift in US policy after midterm election 'seriously mistaken': Iranian supreme leader
Iran's leaders have long ​regarded the United States as their main enemy, referring to it as "the Great Satan".
At a state-organised rally on Wednesday commemorating the student takeover of the US embassy in Tehran during the 1979 Islamic revolution, demonstrators voiced triumph at an election they linked to Iran's success in surviving months of US attacks.
"The fact that the might of these warmongering Republicans has been broken, something unprecedented in human history, means that from now on we will ​see the real war unfolding inside the US Senate and among American officials," said one, giving only his family name of Nazari.
Mediators have intensified efforts to end the war amid fears it ​could reignite after the election, with Trump on Tuesday declining to rule out a resumption of combat operations after the vote and Iran planning wider retaliation if war resumes.
The US and Israel attacked Iran on February ‌28, and Iran ⁠responded with strikes on Israel and Gulf states that host US bases. Conflict also erupted in Lebanon between Iran-backed Hezbollah and Israel, and more recently spread to Yemen, from where the Iran-aligned Houthis have struck energy facilities, airports and other targets in Saudi Arabia.
Global oil and gas prices have shot up, with shipping through the Strait of Hormuz severely disrupted after Tehran declared it closed, while the US has imposed a naval blockade on Iran, hitting Iran's economy hard.
'Iran’s shadow over US elections'
Ahead of the US election, senior Iranian officials told Reuters that Tehran was deliberately prolonging talks with ​the US to weaken Trump politically ahead of the ​vote.
Some news outlets played on the timing ⁠of the election on the anniversary of the embassy seizure, when radical students cemented Iran's toppling of the US-backed Shah by storming the embassy and holding 52 Americans hostage there for 444 days.
Major Iranian newspaper Hamshahri linked the events with a front-page image showing Trump blindfolded with his head ​bowed.
With a headline declaring "Iran's shadow over US elections", it said Washington had been "47 years Iran's captive: from the capture of the spies' ​nest (US embassy) to the November ⁠2026 US Congress elections".
The Iran war has been unpopular among Americans since it began, and blaming the war for driving up costs was a focus of the Democrats' election campaign.
Also Read: Democrats sweep Congress in US midterm elections
Khamenei's message signalled that Tehran had no intention of showing flexibility on its demands for lasting control over the Strait of Hormuz or conditions to end the conflict.
"The consequences of (US) miscalculations and arrogant delusions have manifested as a heavy burden ⁠of costs, ​borne by the American people and the puppet regimes subservient to the US government," he said.
Trump has offered shifting goals ​and timelines for the war that is now in its ninth month.
"I think a part of it was Iran, but at the same time people understood the importance of what I've done with Iran," Trump told Fox News, referring to the ​election result.
The conservative Iranian newspaper Jam-e Jam declared the election result "The twilight of Trumpism".

items.content:
MapmyIndia reported a 90.6% YoY jump in its consolidated net profit for the September quarter (Q2 FY27) to ₹35.3 Cr from ₹18.5 Cr in the year-ago period. Sequentially, the profit declined 29.1% from ₹49.7 Cr in the preceding quarter.
Operating revenue rose 15.8% to ₹131.7 Cr during the quarter from ₹113.8 Cr in Q2 FY26. The top line declined 5.7% sequentially from ₹139.7 Cr.
Total income, including other income of ₹16.1 Cr, increased 19.1% to ₹147.9 Cr from ₹124.2 Cr in the year-ago period.
The company’s EBITDA increased 60.1% YoY to ₹45 Cr, while EBITDA margin expanded to 34.1% from 24.7% in Q2 FY26. PAT margin also improved to 23.8% from 14.9% in the corresponding quarter last year.
For the first half of FY27 (H1 FY27), operating revenue grew 18.4% YoY to ₹271.5 Cr, while EBITDA increased 20.4% to ₹101.1 Cr. Net profit rose 32.2% to ₹85 Cr from ₹64.3 Cr in H1 FY26.
Automotive, Enterprise Businesses Drive Growth
Commenting on the performance, CMD Rakesh Verma said the company’s automotive business recorded 51.9% YoY growth in Q2 FY27, while its enterprise business grew 44.1%. For H1 FY27, the two verticals recorded growth of 40.4% and 16.5%, respectively.
The automotive business’ performance was driven by increasing adoption of the company’s integrated map-led and IoT-led mobility solutions, Verma said.
From a product perspective, map-led revenue grew 8.9% to ₹175.3 Cr in H1 FY27, while EBITDA margins for the business stood at 47.1%. IoT-led revenue increased 29.1% to ₹96.2 Cr during the period.
The IoT-led business also reported a significant improvement in profitability, with EBITDA increasing to ₹18.5 Cr in H1 FY27 from ₹7.9 Cr in the corresponding period last year. The company attributed this to higher-margin solutions and operating leverage.
MapmyIndia provides digital map data, geospatial software and location-based IoT products, platforms and solutions. Its offerings include mapping APIs, navigation and telematics solutions for automotive and enterprise customers.
MapmyIndia Rejigs Leadership
Alongside its Q2 results, MapmyIndia announced a series of leadership changes across its technology, product and business teams as it looks to expand its AI capabilities and develop new products.
The company appointed Abhit Kalasotra as chief technology officer (CTO), software engineering, and Nitin Sagar as chief product technology officer (CPTO) for Mappls AI, effective November 4, 2026.
Kalasotra brings over 22 years of technical experience, including 12 years of building technology companies. He has previously worked with Microsoft, Nokia, Emuzed, LG and Motorola. He holds a bachelor’s degree in computer science from BITS Pilani.
Sagar, meanwhile, has over 17 years of experience across location intelligence, digital payments and global travel. He previously worked at MapmyIndia between 2009 and 2015, where he led product and platform development and integrations with automotive manufacturers.
The company also re-designated Rashmi Verma, previously CTO and chief human resource officer (CHRO), as chief innovation officer (CIO). In her new role, she will focus on driving innovation and accelerating the adoption of AI and emerging technologies across the group.
Separately, CFO Anuj Kumar Jain has been assigned the additional responsibility of chief operating officer (COO) at Gtropy Systems Private Limited, a subsidiary of MapmyIndia. Vishal Pandey has also been appointed chief business officer (CBO) of Gtropy Systems, with both changes taking effect on November 4.
The leadership changes come as MapmyIndia looks to embed AI, machine learning and neural networks across its map-led and IoT-led platforms. These applications span intelligent mapping, navigation, in-vehicle intelligence, telematics, analytics and workflow automation.
Verma said the company sees long-term growth opportunities across its market and product segments, backed by its proprietary data, geospatial capabilities and IoT portfolio.
Shares of MapmyIndia ended today’s trading session 4.57% higher at ₹890.20 apiece on the BSE.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Listed fintech major Pine Labs has partnered with global payments infrastructure provider Stripe to launch a solution that allows eligible retailers in Singapore to manage online and in-store payments through a single platform.
The offering combines Stripe’s online payment capabilities with Pine Labs’ payment terminals and merchant commerce tools. Participating merchants will be able to process online payments through Stripe and accept card payments at physical stores through Pine Labs’ terminals, starting this month.
The companies plan to expand the offering to other Southeast Asian markets in 2027.
The solution targets retailers selling through both physical stores and digital channels. Managing separate payment providers across these channels can complicate reporting and reconciliation, while adding to operational costs.
Beyond payment acceptance, retailers will get access to Pine Labs’ instalment plans from multiple issuers, loyalty-linked payments, pay-by-points options, merchant-funded promotions, and digital marketing tools.
The companies will showcase the solution at the Singapore Fintech Festival 2026.
Pine Labs’ Overseas Push
The partnership builds on Pine Labs’ expansion of its merchant payments and commerce business across international markets.
As of Q2 FY27, Pine Labs served 11.6 Lakh merchants, up 13% YoY, with a presence across more than 22 markets. Its offerings span merchant payments, payment orchestration, issuing, prepaid instruments, and credit infrastructure, with acquisitions helping broaden its product portfolio.
Pine Labs merged its Singapore holding company with its Indian entity in June 2025. It subsequently listed on the BSE and the NSE at ₹242 apiece, a 9.5% premium to its issue price.
On the financial front, Pine Labs’ net profit jumped more than sixfold to ₹38.6 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹6 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Operating revenue rose 24% YoY to ₹806.2 Cr.
Shares of Pine Labs were trading 1.15% higher at ₹157.70 apiece on the BSE at 14:45 IST.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Cellular mobile operators (CMOs) have reportedly taken steps to improve network performance in Islamabad and Rawalpindi ahead of a planned high-level field inspection by the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) on Thursday.
According to sources, telecom companies appear to have made adjustments to network conditions in areas expected to be covered during the inspection. The development follows an earlier visit by the PTA’s Director General (Enforcement), who assessed cellular service quality in the twin cities last week.
Sources said the upcoming inspection could also be attended by the PTA Chairman, indicating increased regulatory scrutiny of mobile operators amid persistent complaints about poor network services.
The PTA’s Director General (Enforcement) reportedly conducted field inspections in Islamabad and Rawalpindi last week to examine mobile network performance and evaluate the quality of services being provided by different operators.
The latest inspection is expected to involve a senior PTA team assessing call quality, mobile internet speeds, network coverage, and overall service reliability. The visit follows the regulator’s broader field inspections of over 900 mobile sites across Pakistan.
Sources maintained that the prospect of a high-level regulatory visit has prompted telecom operators to pay greater attention to network performance in the areas likely to be inspected.
However, it remains unclear whether the reported improvements are temporary adjustments ahead of the visit or part of sustained efforts to improve service quality.
The upcoming inspection is expected to help PTA assess actual network conditions and determine whether operators are maintaining service standards beyond their reported compliance figures.
PTA Received 7,400 Telecom Complaints in September Despite High Resolution Rate
The planned field inspection comes against the backdrop of continued consumer complaints about poor mobile connectivity, slow internet speeds, dropped calls, and inadequate network coverage. PTA has previously intensified nationwide network checks amid similar problems.
According to official figures, PTA received 7,400 complaints against telecom operators in September 2026, of which 7,071 were resolved, representing a resolution rate of 95.55%.
Cellular mobile operators accounted for 6,658 complaints during the month, with 6,434 cases resolved, resulting in a resolution rate of 96.65%.
Among mobile operators, Jazz received the highest number of complaints at 3,005, of which 2,915 were resolved. Telenor followed with 1,325 complaints, with the operator resolving 1,282 cases during the reporting period. PhoneWorld has separately covered the September 2026 PTA complaint figures.
Despite these resolution rates, consumers continue to report inconsistent network performance, particularly concerning mobile broadband speeds, call connectivity, and coverage across different localities.
The figures also highlight the difference between resolving individual consumer complaints and ensuring consistently reliable network performance.
PTA’s upcoming inspection is therefore expected to focus on conditions experienced by mobile users rather than relying solely on the performance data submitted by telecom operators.
While the reported network adjustments ahead of the visit have raised questions about the consistency of service quality, there is currently no official confirmation that operators deliberately manipulated their networks to influence inspection results.
The outcome of Thursday’s field exercise could provide a clearer picture of whether recent efforts to improve network performance translate into lasting improvements for consumers in Islamabad and Rawalpindi.

Samsung Galaxy S27 Pro Chipset Leak Reveals a Surprising Downgrade
The Galaxy S27 Ultra, on the other hand, is expected to feature Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. Samsung has traditionally reserved Snapdragon processors for its Ultra models across international markets since the Galaxy S22 Ultra.
There have been earlier reports suggesting that Samsung could switch the Galaxy S27 Ultra to the Exynos 2700 because of alleged performance and overheating concerns surrounding Qualcomm’s next-generation chipset. However, the latest database listing suggests that European buyers may still receive the Snapdragon-powered Ultra model.
Galaxy S27 Pro May Get a Less Powerful Snapdragon Chip
The biggest surprise concerns the Galaxy S27 Pro. Unlike the Ultra, the Pro model is reportedly listed with the standard Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 instead of the more powerful Extreme edition.
Both processors are expected to use a 2nm manufacturing process. However, the Extreme variant is tipped to deliver better CPU, GPU, and NPU performance.
There could also be a difference in video recording capabilities. The Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 is reportedly capable of supporting 8K video recording at 60fps, while the standard version may be limited to 30fps.
This could create a noticeable performance gap between the Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra. Users who want the best processing and graphics performance may have to choose Samsung’s most expensive model.
However, using a less powerful processor could help Samsung reduce the manufacturing cost of the Galaxy S27 Pro. It may also help control heat generation, particularly because the smaller device has less space for cooling and heat dissipation.
Whether the lower chipset cost will result in a more affordable retail price remains unclear.
See Also: Galaxy Z Fold9 and Z Fold9 Ultra May Retain Existing Camera Setup
Galaxy S27 Series RAM, Storage and Display Sizes
The database listings also provide details about the memory, storage, and display sizes of the upcoming phones. All four models are expected to offer at least 12GB of RAM and 256GB of internal storage. The Pro and Ultra variants could receive additional memory options.
The reported display sizes are as follows:
Galaxy S27: 6.3-inch display
Galaxy S27 Plus: 6.7-inch display
Galaxy S27 Pro: 6.5-inch display
Galaxy S27 Ultra: 6.9-inch display
Previous leaks have also suggested that the Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra could feature Samsung’s second-generation Privacy Display technology. The Ultra model is additionally expected to receive a larger battery.
Samsung has not officially confirmed these specifications. The Galaxy S27 series is still some time away from launch, so its processor choices and other hardware details could change before the company makes an announcement.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The federal government is considering legal action to recover approximately $800 million that Etisalat has yet to pay for its acquisition of a stake in Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited (PTCL). Pakistan is also seeking compensation for the delayed payment, including its opportunity cost since 2008 and applicable damages.
The issue came under discussion during a joint meeting of the Senate Standing Committees on Information Technology and Privatisation on Tuesday. Officials informed the lawmakers that the federal cabinet had directed the Office of the Attorney General for Pakistan (OAGP) to implement its decision under Rule 24 of the Rules of Business, 1973.
Pakistan Considers Legal Action Against Etisalat Over Unpaid $800 Million
The government is now assessing the legal options available to recover the outstanding amount after nearly two decades of negotiations with the UAE-based telecom group, now known as e&.
Why Has Etisalat Withheld $800 Million?
According to a briefing by the Privatisation Division, Pakistan sold 26% of PTCL shares along with management control to Etisalat International Pakistan in 2005 for $2.59 billion.
The government received approximately $1.76 billion from the transaction, while around $800 million remains unpaid.
The outstanding payment is linked to the transfer of PTCL properties to the new management. Although Pakistan has transferred 99% of the properties, 32 out of a total of 3,246 properties remain outstanding.
Etisalat has continued to withhold the remaining payment over the unresolved property transfers.
Government Considers Legal Action
Pakistan has made several attempts to resolve the dispute since 2015. These efforts included forming committees and holding negotiations with Etisalat to reach an amicable settlement.
However, the matter remained unresolved. In July 2026, the government established another committee led by the Prime Minister’s Adviser on Privatisation. Representatives from the IT and Law Ministries and the Attorney General’s Office also joined the committee.
After reviewing the dispute’s nearly 20-year history, the committee recommended considering international arbitration under the terms of the Sale and Purchase Agreement.
It also proposed recovering the outstanding $800 million along with the financial cost of the delayed payment since 2008 and any applicable damages.
The committee further recommended that the Attorney General examine Pakistan’s legal position, the chances of winning the case, and the possible legal consequences before proceeding.
If the legal assessment supports arbitration, the Attorney General will seek approval from the Prime Minister or the federal government before issuing a formal Notice of Intent to Etisalat.
Senators Raise Questions Over PTCL Sale Agreement
The joint committee meeting also raised concerns about parliamentary access to the original Sale Purchase Agreement (SPA).
IT Secretary Zarrar Hasham Khan initially described the Etisalat payment issue as sensitive and requested that unauthorised participants, including media representatives, leave the meeting. The remaining proceedings were held in camera.
However, some senators later expressed disappointment that lawmakers had not received access to the agreement covering the sale of PTCL shares and management control.
They questioned why government officials could examine the details while parliamentarians responsible for oversight remained unaware of the agreement’s contents.
The senators also called for stronger legal provisions to ensure that parliament receives information about major transactions involving national assets.
The Privatisation Division has submitted a summary to the federal cabinet following the committee’s recommendations. The government’s next step will depend on the Attorney General’s legal assessment and the required federal approval.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
MediaTek is looking to strengthen its position in the global technology industry by expanding its business into artificial intelligence (AI), computing, automotive technology and data centres. The company’s ambitions have received a major boost from Nvidia and Alphabet, which have invested in its convertible bonds.
MediaTek CEO Rick Tsai shared the company’s future plans during the opening ceremony of Taiwan Weeks 2026 on November 3. He said the company is moving beyond its traditional smartphone and connectivity chip business to become a major player in the global AI industry.
MediaTek Aims to Become Global AI Leader as Nvidia Invests $3.5 Billion
Tsai also described the investments from Nvidia and Alphabet as a strong vote of confidence in MediaTek’s future rather than simply financial support.
AI Demand Is Growing at an Unprecedented Pace
According to Tsai, demand for conventional AI computing used to double every 18 to 24 months. However, the pace has increased significantly since the launch of ChatGPT in 2022, with demand now doubling every four to five months.
He also highlighted the growing spending plans of major cloud service providers. Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Meta are expected to spend a combined $700 billion on capital investments in 2026. This figure could increase to $1.1 trillion in 2027.
Tsai described this rapid expansion as a major industry shift, with semiconductor companies playing a central role. He said MediaTek also plans to benefit from this growing demand.
Nvidia Invests $3.5 Billion in MediaTek
MediaTek recently completed a convertible bond issuance worth approximately $3.9 billion. Nvidia contributed $3.5 billion, while Alphabet was also among the investors.
Tsai acknowledged that the investment may not appear particularly large compared with major Nasdaq-listed companies. However, he described it as a significant development for Taiwan’s technology sector.
He also suggested that Nvidia’s investment could be its largest direct investment outside the United States.
Although the funding will support MediaTek’s expansion plans, Tsai said the confidence shown by Nvidia and Alphabet matters even more to the company. He added that MediaTek intends to deliver strong results in return for their trust.
MediaTek’s Growth and Future Plans
Tsai also discussed MediaTek’s growth since its stock market listing in 2001. At the time, the company had a market value of approximately $2 billion. Its market capitalization has now reached around $200 billion.
MediaTek has become Taiwan’s second-largest company by market value, representing approximately 4% to 5% of the country’s total stock market capitalization.
The company has also maintained a strong position in corporate governance. It ranks among the top 5% of companies in the Taiwan Stock Exchange’s corporate governance evaluation. Its average salary for non-managerial employees has also remained the highest in Taiwan for five consecutive years.
MediaTek provides performance-based restricted stock awards to its management team and key employees. These awards depend on individual and company performance rather than years of service.
Beyond its business operations, the company also supports social and technology development projects through its Genius for Home initiative. These include an AI-based scouting platform to help Taiwanese baseball talent reach international opportunities and a microclimate management system designed to improve agricultural productivity.
MediaTek will celebrate its 30th anniversary in 2027. Tsai said the company has developed into a global technology player and plans to continue expanding its international presence.
Its long-term ambition is to become one of the world’s leading AI companies, marking a major shift from its traditional focus on smartphone and connectivity chips.

Toyota will also make several changes to the vehicles to meet the requirements of autonomous taxi services. These include additional rear legroom, automatic doors, a powered tailgate as standard, and ambient lighting.
The specially designed vehicles will become part of Waymo’s growing autonomous taxi fleet. The company already operates self-driving taxi services in several markets and is working to expand its international presence.
Toyota Sees Potential for Self-Driving Technology in Private Cars
Although the initial focus is on autonomous taxis, Toyota has indicated that the technology could eventually reach vehicles sold to individual customers.
This means the partnership could have a wider impact beyond ride-hailing services. However, Toyota has not announced a timeline for introducing Waymo’s autonomous driving technology in privately owned vehicles.
The collaboration also reflects growing competition in the autonomous mobility sector. Companies such as Waymo, Tesla, and Uber are exploring opportunities to expand self-driving taxi services into new markets, including Australia.
Toyota and Waymo Highlight Safety and Reliability
Waymo co-CEO Dmitri Dolgov said the company selected Toyota because of its strong reputation for vehicle safety, reliability, and quality. He also expressed interest in expanding their collaboration as Waymo introduces its autonomous driving technology in more markets.
Toyota Executive Vice President Hiroki Nakajima welcomed the partnership and said the collaboration would support Waymo’s efforts to expand its self-driving technology.
The project marks another step in Toyota’s efforts to explore autonomous mobility. With testing expected to begin in 2027, the partnership could help bring self-driving Toyota vehicles to more markets in the coming years.

However, these dates indicate the beginning of each rollout phase rather than fixed installation dates. Actual availability may vary depending on the region and device.
HyperOS 4 Brings a Redesigned Interface
HyperOS 4 introduces a refreshed user interface with a new design language called “Soft Light Glass.” Xiaomi has redesigned several interface elements to give the software a more modern appearance.
The update brings translucent panels, redesigned notifications, customizable lock screens, flexible app folders, and stacked widgets. It also improves floating-window support and introduces smoother animations to make everyday navigation more responsive.
Xiaomi Promises Better Performance
Apart from visual changes, Xiaomi has focused on improving system performance and responsiveness.
According to the company, HyperOS 4 reduces the time required to launch 30 applications after nine hours of usage from 40.3 seconds to 36.8 seconds. This represents an 8.7% improvement compared with HyperOS 3.
Camera performance is also expected to improve. Xiaomi claims that HDR photo processing time has dropped from 313.38 milliseconds to 240.16 milliseconds. The company also promises fewer dropped frames during video playback.
Super XiaoAi 2.0 Gets More AI Features
Artificial intelligence is another major part of HyperOS 4. Xiaomi is introducing Super XiaoAi 2.0, powered by its MiMo large language model.
The upgraded assistant will support more advanced tasks, including searching through photo libraries, organizing schedules, controlling compatible smart home devices, and identifying products displayed on the screen.
Xiaomi is also improving privacy protections. The system will ask users to confirm sensitive actions, such as deleting or sharing personal data, before proceeding.
Meanwhile, the company’s Super Island feature will support more than 130 services, providing users with additional ways to access information and manage activities.
Some AI features and other improvements may remain limited to specific devices and Chinese software versions. International users may not receive every feature included in the Chinese release.
Overall, HyperOS 4 appears to be a major upgrade for Xiaomi users, combining a redesigned interface, performance improvements, and expanded AI capabilities. The upcoming global rollout will reveal which features Xiaomi brings to its international devices.

Moving Beyond Floor Cleaning
Featured in Inc42’s June 2020 edition
items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Keeping hospital corridors clean or moving goods across factory floors involves repetitive, physically demanding work. For facility management companies, finding people to carry out these tasks is becoming harder.
This workforce gap is the opportunity behind Peppermint Robotics. Founded in 2019 and incubated at SINE, IIT Bombay, the Pune-based startup builds autonomous robots that scrub floors and move materials across commercial and industrial facilities.
Now, it has raised ₹100 Cr (about $10.5 Mn) in a Pre-Series B round to expand manufacturing, develop new robots, and strengthen its US and European businesses.
Led by pi Ventures and Crane Venture Partners, with participation from Asiana Fund, the round comprised primary capital and secondary share transactions. Founder Runal Dahiwade told Inc42 that the bulk of the investment was primary capital. The startup previously raised ₹34 Cr in a Series A round in April 2025.
Moving Beyond Floor Cleaning
Featured in Inc42’s June 2020 edition of ‘30 Startups To Watch’, Peppermint began with a floor-cleaning and sanitising robot. Its portfolio now spans scrubber-dryers, vacuuming and mopping robots, three material-handling models, and automated docking stations.
The startup says its cleanroom scrubber-dryer has passed qualification testing in an EU GMP Grade C cleanroom. Such controlled environments require strict limits on contamination, creating a specialised application beyond routine cleaning.
Dahiwade also claimed Peppermint is the world’s first cleanroom robotics company.
Over the next 12-15 months, Peppermint plans smaller and larger cleaning and material-handling robots, alongside upgrades. Outdoor cleaning robots are planned by 2028.
Its proprietary Peppermint OS powers navigation, while computer vision and LiDAR help machines map spaces and avoid obstacles. Customers can monitor operations through a cloud dashboard and mobile apps.
Selling Machines And Support
Peppermint sells robots primarily to facility management companies, earning additional revenue from spare parts, annual maintenance contracts, and software and hardware upgrades from the second year.
An average robot costs around ₹20 Lakh in India. US prices range from $35,000 to $40,000, depending on installation and other costs, Dahiwade said.
Its operating revenue rose from ₹2.71 Cr in FY23 to ₹6.26 Cr in FY24 and ₹21 Cr in FY25. The founder said revenue doubled last year and grew nearly sixfold between FY24 and FY26.
The US contributes nearly half its revenue, India close to 30%, and other markets the remainder. Peppermint is planning to set up an assembly line in North America, adding to its Pune manufacturing and R&D base.
It competes with China’s Gausium and Singapore’s LionsBot. Dahiwade claimed Peppermint commands over 65% of India’s floor-cleaning robotics market.
Inc42 Take: Can Peppermint Scale Without Stretching Its Service Network?
Selling through facility management companies offers a route to deployments across multiple customer locations. Expanding into material handling and cleanrooms could widen this opportunity.
The bigger test is servicing these machines across markets while funding a broader portfolio. According to Peppermint, its core business has operated profitably for several quarters, but R&D and international expansion have kept the company loss-making overall.
Converting fresh capital into reliable deployments and repeat business will matter more than portfolio breadth alone.
