items.author: Danial Saigra
items.content:
The University of Georgia in the United States has announced funded Master’s and PhD research assistantship opportunities for students interested in aquatic animal health, microbiology, disease prevention, and sustainable aquaculture.
The opportunity is available through the Aquatic One Health Lab at the university’s Warnell School of Forestry and Natural Resources in Athens, Georgia.
According to the research announcement published on October 28, 2026, the university will provide a competitive stipend, tuition support, and graduate student benefits through research and teaching assistantships.
The position requires at least 20 hours of work per week, while previous professional experience is not mandatory.
Interested candidates can apply until January 1, 2027, although the university will review applications on a rolling basis until it fills the position.
University of Georgia Master’s and PhD Assistantship Details
The graduate assistantship is part of a research project titled Development of Integrated Disease Detection, Prevention, and Vaccine Strategies for Sustainable Aquaculture.
The selected student will join the Aquatic One Health Lab under the supervision of Dr. Jie Jessie Ma, Assistant Professor of Aquaculture and Fish Health at the University of Georgia.
The project focuses on developing improved methods for detecting aquatic diseases, preventing infections, studying fish immune responses, and creating vaccines to support sustainable aquaculture.
The selected candidate will conduct laboratory research and may collaborate with universities, diagnostic laboratories, government agencies, aquaculture producers, and industry partners.
The university will develop the student’s specific research project according to their academic background, interests, and the laboratory’s ongoing research activities.
Scholarship Benefits and Financial Support
The University of Georgia will support the selected graduate student through research and teaching assistantships.
The advertised funding package includes a competitive stipend, tuition support, and graduate student benefits.
The University of Georgia’s general assistantship policies also provide tuition waivers for eligible appointments, reducing tuition to $25 per semester. However, students may still have to pay mandatory fees and health insurance costs.
The research advertisement does not specify an exact monthly or annual stipend or guarantee that all personal and educational expenses will be covered.
The final financial package will depend on the assistantship arrangement, university policies, and available research funding.
Eligibility Criteria for Master’s and PhD Applicants
Candidates must hold a Bachelor of Science (BS) or Master of Science (MS) degree in a relevant discipline.
The university has identified Aquaculture, Fisheries, Biology, Microbiology, Veterinary Science, Animal Science, and Bioinformatics among the eligible academic fields.
Applicants with qualifications in closely related disciplines can also apply.
Candidates should demonstrate a strong interest in aquatic animal health, microbiology, immunology, molecular biology, bioinformatics, or related research areas.
The university also requires applicants to have strong written and verbal communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work independently and collaboratively.
Applicants should be willing to design experiments, follow research protocols, analyze scientific data, and contribute to peer-reviewed publications.
English Language and GPA Requirements
The University of Georgia requires international applicants who are subject to English language proficiency requirements to submit acceptable IELTS or TOEFL results.
The university accepts an IELTS Academic overall score of at least 6.5, with no individual band below 6.0.
For TOEFL iBT examinations taken before January 21, 2026, the minimum overall score is 80, with at least 20 in speaking and writing.
For examinations taken on or after January 22, 2026, the university requires an overall score of at least 4.5 on the revised TOEFL scale, including at least 4 in speaking and writing.
The Graduate School generally requires an undergraduate GPA of at least 3.0 or its equivalent for admission eligibility.
Applicants must also meet any additional academic requirements established by their selected graduate program.
Research Areas and Opportunities
The selected student will contribute to research involving aquatic animal diseases, pathogen detection, and sustainable aquaculture practices.
The project will focus on developing molecular diagnostic tools to identify bacterial and viral pathogens affecting aquatic animals.
Researchers will also study pathogen isolation, infection dynamics, and interactions between aquatic pathogens and their hosts.
Another major area involves developing and evaluating vaccines against important bacterial and viral diseases affecting aquaculture species.
The research may examine fish immune responses to infections, vaccinations, and immunostimulants.
Students may also investigate how environmental conditions influence aquatic animal health and disease transmission.
Depending on the research project, the selected candidate may conduct laboratory experiments and fieldwork at aquaculture farms, hatcheries, diagnostic laboratories, and collaborating institutions.
Documents Required for Application
Interested applicants must prepare the documents specified in the research advertisement before contacting the supervisor.
Candidates need a cover letter of one to two pages explaining their research interests, relevant research experience, career goals, and reasons for pursuing a Master’s or PhD degree in aquatic animal health and sustainable aquaculture.
They must also prepare an updated curriculum vitae (CV) highlighting their educational background, research skills, and relevant academic experience.
Applicants must provide contact information for two professional references.
These documents are required for the initial research assistantship application. Candidates who proceed to formal graduate admission must also complete the University of Georgia Graduate School’s separate application requirements.
How to Apply for the University of Georgia Assistantship
Interested candidates must first contact the research supervisor before submitting a formal application to the University of Georgia Graduate School.
Applicants should send their cover letter, updated CV, and contact information for two professional references in a single email to Dr. Jie Jessie Ma at jie.ma@uga.edu.
Applicants should include the required documents and clearly explain how their academic background and research interests relate to the advertised opportunity.
After the initial application process, successful candidates must secure admission to the University of Georgia Graduate School.

The University of Minnesota–Twin Cities in the United States has announced a funded master’s research opportunity in Conservation Sciences, offering an annual salary starting at $30,000.
The university is accepting applications from candidates interested in wildlife conservation, environmental research, community-based studies, and Geographic Information Systems (GIS).
According to the research opportunity published on the Texas A&M University Natural Resources Job Board on October 19, 2026, the selected student will work on a conservation project in partnership with White Earth Natural Resources in Minnesota.
The position requires at least 40 hours per week, while previous professional experience is not mandatory. Interested candidates must submit their applications by November 30, 2026.
University of Minnesota Master’s Research Program Details
The opportunity is available through the Conservation Sciences Graduate Program at the University of Minnesota–Twin Cities in St. Paul, Minnesota.
The selected candidate will join the Umana Laboratory, where researchers Christopher Shaffer and Marissa Milstein are leading a project titled Revitalizing Hunting, Fishing and Trapping in White Earth Using Participatory GIS.
The project aims to understand the declining participation of Indigenous communities in hunting, fishing, and trapping activities.
These activities play an important role in local cultural traditions, livelihoods, food security, and access to traditional food sources.
The researchers will identify barriers to community participation and develop a community-based GIS to support education, traditional knowledge exchange, and natural resource management.
The selected student will participate in research involving community engagement, participatory mapping, and qualitative and quantitative methods.
Salary and Financial Benefits
The advertised master’s research position offers an annual salary starting at $30,000, with a stated workload of at least 40 hours per week.
The University of Minnesota’s Conservation Sciences Graduate Program also provides financial support opportunities through research assistantships, teaching assistantships, and fellowships.
According to the university’s general funding guidelines, eligible graduate assistants may receive tuition benefits and health insurance coverage, depending on their appointment.
However, the specific research advertisement does not confirm a tuition waiver, health insurance benefits, or additional financial support for this position.
Applicants should contact the university to confirm the complete funding package before accepting an offer.
Eligibility Criteria for the Master’s Research Opportunity
The university is seeking applicants with a bachelor’s degree in wildlife, ecology, anthropology, or a related discipline.
Candidates must have basic knowledge of Geographic Information Systems and demonstrate an interest in improving their technical skills.
Applicants should also have an interest in mixed-methods research involving qualitative and quantitative research techniques.
The position requires strong written and verbal communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to conduct research independently while working with tribal partners.
The university also expects applicants to demonstrate respect for Indigenous sovereignty and a commitment to building collaborative relationships with Indigenous communities.
English Language Requirements
International applicants who must demonstrate English language proficiency need to meet the University of Minnesota’s admission standards.
According to the university’s Graduate School requirements, applicants can use recognized English language tests, including IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, Duolingo English Test, and Cambridge C1 Advanced.
The university lists a minimum IELTS Academic overall score of 6.5, with at least 6.5 in writing and reading.
For Fall 2027 admission and later, the university lists a minimum Duolingo English Test overall score of 120, with minimum writing and reading scores of 120.
Applicants using other English language tests should review the current official score requirements. Individual graduate programs may set higher standards.
Documents Required for Application
Applicants must follow the University of Minnesota’s Conservation Sciences graduate admission requirements.
The university requires a personal statement explaining the applicant’s academic background, research interests, career goals, and reasons for pursuing graduate study.
Candidates must also prepare a diversity statement describing how they would contribute their experiences and perspectives to the university community.
Other application requirements include a curriculum vitae (CV), three recommendation letters, and academic records required by the Graduate School’s application system.
The university advises applicants to contact potential research supervisors before applying to discuss their research interests and available funding.
How to Apply for the University of Minnesota Master’s Opportunity
Interested candidates must apply through the University of Minnesota’s official online Graduate School Application System.
Applicants should first review the specific research opportunity and the Conservation Sciences program’s admission requirements.
They can then prepare their academic documents, personal statement, diversity statement, CV, and recommendation letters before submitting their applications.
The university encourages prospective students to contact faculty members whose research interests match their own.
For this position, candidates can contact the researchers leading the project to discuss research expectations, funding arrangements, and eligibility.

Sindh Bureau of Statistics Jobs 2026
The Sindh Bureau of Statistics has announced recruitment for two field staff categories under the SMICS 2026–27 survey.
The available positions include 140 Enumerator/Measurer vacancies for female candidates and 35 Enumerator vacancies for male candidates.
Both categories require at least Intermediate education from a recognized institution.
The age limit is 21 to 40 years, while the department will apply general age relaxation according to government rules.
Educational Qualifications and Experience Requirements
Applicants must have completed Intermediate or an equivalent qualification from a recognized institution.
The department also requires at least one year of post-qualification experience in field surveys related to maternal and child health.
Relevant experience may include surveys covering antenatal care, postnatal care, and child immunization.
Candidates must provide documentary evidence of their experience when submitting their applications.
Applicants who do not meet the required educational qualifications or experience criteria will not qualify for recruitment.
How to Apply for Sindh Field Staff Jobs

items.author: Danial Saigra
items.content:
The National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) has shared a step-by-step guide explaining how citizens can obtain replacement identity cards if their original documents are lost or damaged.
According to a video guide published on NADRA’s official Facebook account, the process covers the reprinting of Computerized National Identity Cards (CNICs), National Identity Cards for Overseas Pakistanis (NICOPs), and Pakistan Origin Cards (POCs).
Applicants can visit a NADRA Registration Centre, complete biometric verification, obtain approval, pay the required fee, and collect their replacement cards after the prescribed processing period.
Documents Required for CNIC Reprinting
NADRA has explained that applicants seeking a replacement must provide the number of their lost or damaged CNIC, NICOP, or POC.
For a duplicate CNIC, NADRA’s official website also identifies the existing CNIC number as the basic requirement.
Applicants should ensure they have the correct identity document number before visiting a NADRA Registration Centre.
How to Reprint a Lost or Damaged CNIC Through NADRA
NADRA has outlined five main steps for obtaining a replacement identity card through its registration centres.
Step 1: Get a Token From the Reception
Applicants must first visit a NADRA Registration Centre and obtain a token from the reception desk.
After receiving the token, they should wait for their turn to complete the application process.
Step 2: Complete Biometric Verification
When their turn arrives, applicants must visit the designated counter for biometric verification.
NADRA staff will verify their identity using fingerprints, a photograph, and an iris scan.
This process allows the authority to authenticate the applicant’s identity before processing the replacement request.
Step 3: Get Your Application Approved
After completing biometric verification, applicants must visit the office in charge.
The relevant official will review and approve the application according to NADRA’s prescribed procedure.
Step 4: Pay the Required Fee
Once NADRA approves the application, the applicant must complete the fee payment process.
According to NADRA’s video guide, applicants can have the QR code printed on their token scanned to proceed with payment.
The applicable fee depends on the type of identity document and the selected processing category.
Step 5: Collect Your Replacement Identity Card
After completing the payment process, applicants will receive a receipt for their application.
They must keep the receipt safe and wait until the prescribed processing period ends.
According to NADRA’s instructions, applicants can collect their replacement identity cards from the same NADRA office after the applicable processing period.
NADRA Duplicate CNIC Fees and Processing Time
NADRA offers different processing categories for duplicate CNIC applications.
According to the authority’s published fee structure, the charges for a standard duplicate CNIC are Rs. 400 for normal processing, Rs. 1,150 for urgent processing, and Rs. 2,150 for executive processing.
The corresponding processing timelines are 15 days, 12 days, and six days, respectively.
These rates apply to standard duplicate CNICs. Fees for Smart CNICs, NICOPs, and POCs may differ.
Applicants should check NADRA’s latest official fee schedule before making payments.
Can You Apply for a Duplicate CNIC Online
NADRA also offers an alternative application facility through its official PakID mobile application.
Citizens can use the app to request reprints of eligible identity documents without visiting a registration centre, where the service is available.
The app allows users to submit their application details, complete the required verification process, and track their application status.
However, NADRA may require applicants to visit a registration centre if additional verification is necessary.

items.author: Naeem Asghar
items.content:
TikTok has around 100 million users in Pakistan, while nearly 150 million videos are watched and uploaded on the platform daily from the country, the National Assembly Standing Committee on Information Technology and Telecommunications was told on Tuesday.
PTA Chairman Major General (retd) Hafeez ur Rehman shared the figures during a briefing on social media usage, highlighting the growing popularity of digital platforms in the country.
He told the committee that 96 million Pakistanis currently use YouTube and watch around 560 million videos on the platform every day, making Pakistan the world's leading country in terms of YouTube video viewership.
Pakistanis also make millions of calls and send millions of messages daily through WhatsApp, he added.
The meeting, chaired by MNA Syed Aminul Haque at Parliament House, also addressed complaints about poor telecom services, frequent internet disruptions and the slow pace of improvements in network infrastructure.
Committee members questioned why users continued to face connectivity problems despite repeated discussions over the past two and a half years.
Member Ahmad Atiq said mobile networks were barely working in his constituency and along the route to Karachi. He complained that connectivity was deteriorating after every committee meeting, adding that even WhatsApp calls were frequently disconnected in Islamabad.
"If this is the situation in Islamabad, what can one expect in rural areas, where even 3G does not work, while you are talking about 5G?" he asked. He also sought details of the fibre-optic network laid over the past two and a half years.
Another member, Asia Ishaq, said 4G services had also deteriorated since the introduction of 5G, asking whether lawmakers would have to approach the Supreme Court to get the telecom companies to improve their services.
The PTA chairman said he had visited 41 districts along with telecom operators to assess service quality and inspect mobile towers. He said the PTA had directed the operators to improve their services, adding that issuing show-cause notices was the authority's last resort because companies often obtained stay orders from courts against financial penalties.
Federal Minister for Information Technology Shaza Fatima Khawaja said data consumption had increased significantly due to the growing use of social media and artificial intelligence.
She said 18 million people were using 5G services in Pakistan and the technology was being rolled out in 24 cities. The government had taken steps to improve telecom services, she added.
Recalling the country's spectrum auctions, the minister said no such auction had been held after Nawaz Sharif left office, adding that his government had introduced 4G services while the present government had conducted the 5G spectrum auction.
Khawaja said disruptions in telecom services had several causes, including theft of infrastructure. In some areas, entire mobile towers were stolen, while diesel and generators installed to keep them operational were also taken away, she told the committee.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Update | November 3, 2026, 21:45 IST
EV maker Ola Electric has allotted 37.03 Cr partly paid-up equity shares under its rights issue, through which it will raise about ₹999.7 Cr once the shares are fully paid.
The shares carry an issue price of ₹27 apiece. Of the issue price, shareholders have paid ₹16.2 per share on application, amounting to ₹599.8 Cr. The remaining ₹10.8 per share, totalling ₹399.9 Cr, will be payable on the first and final call under the terms of the letter of offer.
Ola Electric’s rights issue committee approved the allotment following the finalisation of the basis of allotment in consultation with NSE, the designated stock exchange.
Original | October 7, 2026, 20:08 IST
Ola Electric’s ₹1,000 Cr rights issue is set to open for subscription onOctober 22 and close on October 30, its board of directors finalised today. The last date for on-market renunciation of rights entitlements has been set at October 26.
At an issue price of ₹27 per share, the company expects to raise ₹999.74 Cr, assuming full subscription and payment of call monies. To note, the issue price is set at a discount of over 5% to Ola Electric’s closing price today (₹36.30).
The rights issue will comprise 37.03 Cr partly paid-up equity shares with a face value of ₹10 each. Shareholders will be entitled to two rights shares for every 25 fully paid-up equity shares held as of the record date of October 13.
The ₹27 issue price includes a ₹17 premium. Shareholders will have to pay ₹16.20 per share, or 60% of the issue price, on application. The remaining ₹10.80 per share will be payable through a first and final call.
The company’s board approved the rights issue on September 28. Following that, founder and CMD Bhavish Aggarwal pledged a 4.32% stake in the electric two-wheeler maker to fund his participation in the rights issue.
Ola Electric plans to split the proceeds between debt reduction, business expansion and general corporate requirements.
The company has earmarked ₹350 Cr for repaying or prepaying borrowings at Ola Electric and its material subsidiaries. The allocation will also cover accrued interest and any applicable prepayment penalties.
A larger ₹400 Cr will be directed towards organic growth, with the company planning to invest across its electric mobility and energy storage businesses. The spending will include manufacturing, R&D, stores and dealerships, service infrastructure, as well as sales and marketing.
The balance of the proceeds will be available for general corporate purposes. Ola Electric expects to utilise the funds during FY27 and FY28.
This would be the second fundraise for Ola Electric within 2026. The company raised ₹780.24 Cr via a qualified institutional placement (QIP) earlier in June.
Meanwhile, on the financial front, Ola Electric managed to trim its net loss for the June quarter (Q1 FY27) by 22% to ₹336 Cr from ₹428 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Operating revenue declined 45% to ₹455 Cr from ₹828 Cr in Q1 FY26.

items.author: Shahbaz Rana
items.content:
Pakistan's duty-free access to the European Union (EU) could be in the doldrums because of a deteriorating human rights situation, National Assembly Standing Committee on Finance Chairman Syed Naveed Qamar said on Tuesday, amid the government's assurance that there was no such threat.
The standing committee also expressed disappointment over yet another failed trader scheme, as the government announced enforcement action against all traders except the 222 who joined, subject to approval by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.
"We are getting signals that the GSP+ status is in the doldrums because of human rights issues," Qamar, a former finance and commerce minister, said while chairing the committee.
He did not specify the exact concerns that could lead to an adverse EU decision. The last monitoring report on the Generalised Scheme of Preferences Plus (GSP+) highlighted scores of human rights and fundamental rights violations, a weakening judicial system and curbs on freedom of expression.
The scheme runs until December 2028, and a deputy prime minister-led committee is preparing an application to qualify for the new scheme from January 2029, Minister of State for Finance and Revenue Bilal Kayani told the committee
Pakistan was the top beneficiary of the EU's GSP+ trade scheme, recording €7.5 billion in exports to the bloc in 2024 under preferential tariffs, according to the fifth GSP report, which evaluated the implementation of 27 international core conventions in beneficiary countries.
Continuation of the scheme is critical for Pakistan, which remains unable to bring substantial improvement in its exports despite decades of protection and fiscal incentives given to exporters.
The EU monitoring report underlined that Pakistan needed to take robust steps to reverse negative trends on enforced disappearances and violations of freedom of expression. "In this regard, laws on blasphemy, cybercrime (such as PECA), defamation, counterterrorism and sedition should be amended or repealed."
In view of the revised GSP rules from 2027, the EU said key priorities for future engagement include accountability for human rights violations, increased efforts against torture, in-prison and capital punishment reforms, and reversing negative developments on enforced disappearances and freedom of expression.
During the 2023-2025 monitoring period, Pakistan has faced compliance issues with its GSP+ obligations, the report noted. "It has regressed in a number of areas while positive change was limited."
Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) MNA Dr Nafisa Shah raised the closure of Pakistan's borders with Iran and Afghanistan and its implications for exports to the Central Asian republics.
"There is an impact on trade with Central Asia but we closed our borders with Afghanistan because of national security priorities," Kayani said.
Despite a conflict between China and India, neither country has suspended trade, Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) MNA Jawed Hanif said.
Trade scheme fails
The standing committee expressed disappointment over the failure of the fixed tax scheme for traders, as only 222 new shopkeepers joined against a hope of one million out of 3.7 million non-filers.
"We did not get the kind of response that we had hoped for," Kayani said in response to a question from Dr Nafisa Shah, adding that traders now had no excuse after the government accepted all their demands, including exemption from audit, a fixed tax rate and no dealings with the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR).
There will be no further extension of the scheme after it expires on October 31, and the government is beginning a new phase of imposing fines and taking enforcement action, he said.
Traders remain largely outside the tax net, and the government offered them a new scheme in June, the third since 2022. This too failed, with only 222 new traders joining.
The minister of state said the government had consulted the attorney general for Pakistan before taking legal action and did not disclose the nature of the action.
However, sources said there could be legal and ethical issues if the government gives traders a Rs10,000 first default notice under the new scheme with a direction to file returns, whereas any non-trading person is required to pay a Rs25,000 fine for late filing.
Qamar repeatedly asked whether Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and the federal cabinet were in favour of punitive action and would not budge when traders threatened to observe a strike.
"The government is very much committed to take action and we are preparing an enforcement plan for the approval of the prime minister," Kayani said.
He said there was no reason traders would observe a strike, as the scheme had been prepared with their extensive input, and sought Parliament's support before enforcement action.
The committee chairman was of the view that the FBR did not have the manpower to go after all traders.
Given limited enforcement capacity, the FBR could use powers to suspend bank accounts or other services to compel traders to become filers, Hanif recommended.
Kayani said the government was considering severing services but that these could be measures of last resort.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
December 1999, Pakistan had been left with only $300 million in foreign exchange reserves due to crippling economic sanctions and international isolation and at that time military ruler General Pervez Musharraf appointed Dr Ishrat Husain to turn around the central bank.
Six years later, when he left, the country had $13 billion in foreign exchange reserves, also built by purchasing dollars, and people's trust in banks and in the economy had been restored.
The $300 million reserves that Pakistan had in December 1999 were also the result of a $500 million Chinese loan. After leaving the central bank following two maximum stints, Husain did not rest and contributed to improving economic governance and civil service reforms.
November 2026, in the words of SBP Governor Jameel Ahmad, "Pakistan's economic situation remains challenging". While praising the innumerable achievements of Husain, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said that, as chairman of the Cabinet Committee on State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs), he took inspiration from Husain's reports.
"I have to admit that I took his report as a starting point, but we still have a long way to go, and some of the folks are not happy with that," said Aurangzeb while eulogising the role of the former central bank governor and former adviser to the PM on institutional reforms.
The Sustainable Development Policy Institute (SDPI) on Tuesday awarded Husain the Lifetime Achievement Award in recognition of his public services that began in 1964 as Pakistan's civil servant. He remained the SBP governor from 1999 to the end of 2005, head of many government committees, adviser to the PM and also served in the World Bank.
However, three events – the 1999 economic crisis, the turnaround by 2005 and the persistence of same economic challenges today – underscore that Pakistan produced many great personalities, including Dr Ishrat Husain, but the country remains in the same quagmire with brief intervals of a booming economy.
As part of the World Bank management, Husain advised three countries: Ghana, Tajikistan and Azerbaijan. Ghana was the first country that embraced the World Bank's structural reforms, and it is today a success story, Husain said.
However, Pakistan has taken an unlimited number of World Bank structural reform loans and 25 IMF programmes, but it is still struggling to implement basic reforms that could put the country on a sustainable development path.
Husain said that he helped Tajikistan as the World Bank country director to raise funds for development, which the Tajik leadership still acknowledges, and he was really proud of it.
He said that he advised Azerbaijan to set up a sovereign wealth fund to save the windfall gains from gas sales, and today the state-run sovereign fund had $75 billion of assets.
However, Pakistan established a sovereign wealth fund in 2023 but it had not been able to make the fund operational amid IMF concerns.
"Husain is an institution in himself who turned around the central bank and many other institutions," said Sultan Ali Alana, Chairman Habib Bank Limited.
"The SBP is the best regulator of Pakistan, which was only possible because of the transformational role played by Husain," remarked Finance Minister Aurangzeb.
"Husain is an expert in economy, education, trade and governance reform, and he was Google for us when Google was not that popular in Pakistan," said Dr Abid Qaiyum Suleri, the head of SDPI.
"Retirement is not in the DNA of Dr Ishrat Husain," Aurangzeb said, adding that after leaving the SBP, Husain put a lot of good and hard work into governance reform reports.
"Everyone who comes here in SBP is always in a great hurry, and he will too reconcile with ground realities," were the first remarks by the then deputy governor when he received the news of Husain's appointment in December 1999, revealed incumbent Governor Jameel Ahmad. He said that within six years, Husain transformed the central bank and introduced many reforms.
"Institutional builders must be such that the institution remains the same after they leave," said Ishrat Husain. In his message to the youth, he said "your beginning need not to determine your destination" while sharing his journey from a shy and underdeveloped boy to a towering figure who made his mark in every field where he performed.
Former secretary to the prime minister Nargis Sethi recalled working closely with him during his tenure as chairman of the National Commission for Government Reform, established by the government in 2006.
Dean Emeritus and Professor at Boston University's Pardee School of Global Studies, Dr Adil Najam, said this aspect of his legacy was often underestimated because attention largely remained focused on his achievements as a policymaker.

items.author: ZAFAR BHUTTA
items.content:
Pakistan's economic managers have raised questions about the placement of agricultural professionals trained in China and has directed the food ministry to share their status.
The Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) of the cabinet told the food ministry to disclose the placement status of 885 agricultural professionals following completion of their training.
During discussions in a recent meeting, the ECC, while responding to a query from the minister for power about the placement of 885 trained agricultural professionals, asked the Ministry of National Food Security and Research and the Ministry of Federal Education and Professional Training to share their placement status with the committee to gauge the impact of training.
The Ministry of Education briefed the ECC that the prime minister during his visit to China in June 2024 had said that 1,000 Pakistani agricultural professionals be trained in China to benefit from its expertise in agricultural technology, innovation and research. Accordingly, the Ministry of Food Security developed a training framework, while the Higher Education Commission (HEC) was entrusted with the logistical and financial management of the programme.
The Ministry of Education recalled that the ECC, in its meeting held on November 28, 2024, had approved a technical supplementary grant of Rs3,072 million for implementation of the programme in batches. Of the total, Rs1,950 million was released during fiscal year 2024-25. HEC arranged training of 292 professionals under batch-I, however, batch-II training could not be undertaken within the stipulated timeframe and consequently, Rs1,406 million remained unutilised, while the unutilised balance of Rs544 million was surrendered.
The Ministry of Federal Education apprised the ECC that during FY2025-26 HEC placed a further 593 trainees in two batches, bringing the total number of trained agricultural professionals to 885. The remaining 115 trainees, having Sindh domicile, have met the prescribed requirements and have been registered at the Northwest Agricultural & Forestry University, Xi'an, China. Their departure under Cohort-I, batch-III was scheduled for the last week of September 2026, thereby completing the target of 1,000 trainees.
The Ministry of Education added that to ensure continuity of the programme, a meeting was held with the Finance Division on August 8, 2025, wherein it was agreed in principle that the immediate requirement of Rs1,666 million would be met from HEC's FY2025-26 allocation under the "Promotion of Research" programme and the amount would be recovered through a supplementary grant during the third quarter of FY2025-26. However, the committed grant could not be released during FY26.
Meanwhile, the HEC incurred expenses of Rs897.187 million through internal re-appropriation from its own resources. The Ministry of Education told the meeting that timely release of required funds was essential to ensure the uninterrupted implementation and successful completion of the initiative as well as to recover the released amount, ie, Rs897.187 million, by the commission to safeguard the continuity of the national research ecosystem and meet HEC's committed national and international obligations. The ECC considered a summary dated September 16, 2026, submitted by the Ministry of Federal Education and titled "Technical Supplementary Grant of Rs1,666.176 million for the Prime Minister's Initiative on Short Term Training of three to six months for 1,000 Agricultural Professionals in China", and approved the proposal.

Kazakhstan has developed a five-year roadmap to expand trade and investment with Pakistan, Deputy Prime Minister Sirjan Zhomangarin said during a meeting with Qaiser Ahmad Sheikh, as both countries reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral economic relations, increasing trade and exploring new investment opportunities, according to a statement issued by the Board of Investment on Tuesday.
During the meeting, Sheikh emphasised the need to promote business-to-business cooperation, enhance private-sector engagement and improve banking channels to facilitate trade and investment.
He highlighted opportunities in e-commerce, warehousing, textiles and mining, noting that Kazakhstan's affordable energy could attract Pakistani investment in the textile sector.
The memorandums of understanding signed during President Asif Ali Zardari's visit to Kazakhstan in February required early implementation to translate commitments into tangible economic benefits, Sheikh stressed.
Kazakhstan's deputy prime minister expressed his desire for Pakistan's prime minister to visit Kazakhstan and reaffirmed his country's commitment to strengthening bilateral relations.
He emphasised the need to increase bilateral trade and said a five-year roadmap had been developed to advance cooperation.
He noted that Pakistan's market of approximately 250 million people offered significant opportunities for Kazakhstan, while Pakistan could use Kazakhstan as a gateway to the wider Eurasian market.
The deputy prime minister also highlighted the need for direct air connectivity between Pakistan and Kazakhstan to facilitate business, trade and people-to-people exchanges.
He informed that Kazakhstan's foreign minister would visit Pakistan to attend the preparatory meeting for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.
Both sides emphasised the importance of stronger connectivity, effective implementation of existing agreements and greater private-sector engagement to transform the potential of bilateral relations into concrete economic partnerships.
The statement said the meeting focused on stronger trade, investment and connectivity ties, with both sides exploring ways to increase bilateral trade and new investment opportunities between Pakistan and Kazakhstan.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz has served a Rs5 billion defamation notice on Federal Minister Chaudhry Salik Hussain, an ARY News anchor and the private television channel's chairman, over allegations of widespread corruption in the province, demanding an unconditional apology, retraction of the statements and damages.
However, Salik Hussain, who belongs to a smaller allied party in the ruling coalition, has stood by his allegations, insisting that corruption was taking place in Punjab. 
He has also rejected the suggestion that his remarks were prompted by the appointment of a deputy commissioner on merit, maintaining that the interview had been recorded three weeks earlier.
"If you have proof, bring it forward; if not, I will drag you to court," Maryam said during a laptop distribution ceremony, reiterating the allegation made a day earlier by Information Minister Azma Bukhari that the federal minister had effectively issued a charge sheet against the provincial government out of displeasure over the appointment of a deputy commissioner on merit.
A day earlier, Salik had acknowledged that he had indeed asked the government to appoint a deputy commissioner whose capabilities were better suited to executing mega projects.
During a talk show on a private television channel on Monday, Salik praised his paternal uncle, Chaudhry Pervez Elahi, president of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), for his tenure as Punjab chief minister from 2002 to 2007, saying he had overseen development across the province without political or personal bias.

— Maryam Nawaz Sharif (@MaryamNSharif) November 3, 2026
“Chaudhry Pervez Elahi is the best chief executive Punjab has ever had,” he said, adding that the former chief minister had played a significant role in the province’s development and ensured that public projects were not influenced by political affiliations.
Salik also criticised the incumbent provincial government, alleging that political considerations were increasingly shaping development priorities and the allocation of public funds.
He said complaints about corruption in Punjab were commonplace, claiming that a disproportionate share of the provincial development budget was being spent in Lahore, while districts such as Gujrat, where candidates backed by the government had lost elections, were being overlooked in development planning.
Although Salik acknowledged that he did not possess evidence to substantiate his claims, he went on to say that corruption-related files had filled entire cupboards.
During the interview, the federal minister said: "I have no evidence, but I hear stories about corruption in Punjab every day." He also remarked that "cupboards are filled with files on corruption cases in Punjab".
The notices contend that Salik made sweeping allegations about corruption in Punjab without providing any evidence to substantiate them, damaging the reputation of the chief minister and the provincial administration.
According to the legal notice, the minister had referred to accounts of corruption in Punjab during the interview but failed to provide any documentary or verifiable evidence in support of his assertions.
The chief minister’s counsel said the remarks conveyed serious imputations that corruption was widespread in Punjab, that numerous corruption-related matters existed and that the provincial administration was burdened with a large volume of records relating to corruption.
The notice questioned the factual basis of Salik’s claims, asking which departments, public offices, officials, projects or transactions he was referring to, and whether his remarks were based on any complaints, inquiries, investigations or official records.
It said a federal minister was expected to appreciate the gravity and consequences of making such allegations against another constitutional government.
“The office of a federal minister is not a licence to circulate rumours, convert hearsay into apparent fact, or make sweeping accusations against another constitutional Government without identifying any credible factual basis,” the notice said.
وزیر اعلیٰ پنجاب مریم نواز شریف کی جانب سے وفاقی وزیر چودھری سالک حسین، اینکر نعیم اشرف بٹ اور اے آر وائی انتظامیہ کو قانونی نوٹس ارسال کردیا گیا۔ pic.twitter.com/mxNq6ZQaNa
— PMLN (@pmln_org) November 3, 2026
It added that Salik had not identified a single authentic document, official inquiry, audit observation, investigation, complaint or other verifiable source to support his assertion that corruption-related files had filled entire cupboards in Punjab.
The notice argued that such sweeping remarks could create the impression among viewers that corruption was endemic throughout the provincial administration, rather than confined to isolated instances, and could not be shielded from legal scrutiny by describing them as political commentary.
The notices characterised the allegations as baseless, unverified and defamatory, arguing that Salik had failed to identify any specific incident, investigation or complaint during the interview to support his claims.
They also accused the programme host of broadcasting the allegations and facilitating discussion on the matter without first establishing their authenticity.
پنجاب میں کرپشن کے الزامات لگانے والوں کو ثبوت بھی پیش کرنے چاہئیں۔ میں نے کھربوں روپے کے ترقیاتی منصوبے شروع کیے ہیں اور کسی کو عوامی وسائل میں ایک پائی کی بے ضابطگی کا ثبوت ملے تو جواب دینے کے لیے تیار ہوں۔ اسی لیے بے بنیاد الزامات پر ہرجانے کا نوٹس بھیج رہی ہوں۔ گجرات کی سابقہ… pic.twitter.com/blRm7y1fyS
— PMLN (@pmln_org) November 3, 2026
“The right to question a government cannot be converted into a right to manufacture or circulate damaging impressions without accepting responsibility for their factual basis,” the notice said, adding that the statements had crossed the permissible limits of responsible public discussion.
The chief minister maintained that the remarks had harmed the reputation of both herself and the Punjab government, prompting her to initiate legal proceedings against those responsible for making and broadcasting them.
Earlier, announcing her decision to issue the defamation notice, Maryam said she would not tolerate false allegations. She also challenged the federal minister to leave the government if he believed corruption was so widespread in Punjab.
She maintained that the actual issue was the appointment of a deputy commissioner in Gujrat rather than any development project. 
She said she did not entertain requests or recommendations in the appointment of deputy commissioners, commissioners and regional police officers, insisting that all such appointments were made strictly on merit. Those appointed through influence, she added, ended up harming the country.
Rejecting the federal minister's assessment of Chaudhry Pervaiz Elahi as the best chief minister, Maryam said that when she assumed office, Gujrat resembled a village, with rainfall submerging the entire city and forcing people to travel not in cars but on trolleys.
Referring to her own visit to the city, she said she had undertaken development projects worth billions of rupees and could be held accountable for even a penny's worth of corruption.
It is pertinent to mention that Salik Hussain's brother, Chaudhry Shafay Hussain, is also part of the provincial government and serves directly under Maryam Nawaz as Punjab's minister for industries, commerce and investment.
Responding to the allegations against him, Federal Minister Chaudhry Salik Hussain said he had merely answered the interviewer's questions honestly, reiterating his position that corruption existed in Punjab. 
However, he sidestepped questions about whether he possessed any evidence to support his allegations or whether he should leave the government if corruption was indeed taking place in the province.
Taking an indirect swipe at Maryam Nawaz, he said people holding powerful positions should remain humble.
"May Allah save people from pride and arrogance," he added.
Bokhari's rebuttal
The remarks also drew an immediate response from Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari, who suggested that Salik’s criticism stemmed from personal resentment over a favour being refused rather than a principled objection to the government’s policies.
She claimed that Salik had been displeased after his request to have a deputy commissioner of his choice appointed was turned down.
“Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz does not appoint deputy commissioners on anyone’s recommendation. She makes decisions strictly on merit and in line with the government’s policy,” Bokhari said.
Maintaining that the chief minister had ended the practice of political patronage, personal preferences and recommendations, she said influential individuals could no longer use their political connections to secure government appointments or administrative favours.
“There is no room for land grabbers and strongmen in Punjab anymore. The practice of rewarding employees of political estates with government positions through recommendations has also come to an end. Salik Hussain should not bite the hand that feeds him,” she retorted.

Bokhari also rejected Salik’s allegations of unequal development spending, saying Maryam Nawaz had ensured a transparent and equitable distribution of provincial resources, with similar development schemes being launched in cities across Punjab.
She said the sanitation model introduced in Lahore had also been extended to rural areas, arguing that the provincial government was pursuing development beyond the provincial capital instead of concentrating resources in one city.
Responding to Salik’s criticism of the use of official aircraft, Bokhari said Maryam Nawaz was the first Punjab chief minister to personally bear the expenses incurred through the use of the government aircraft.
She also cited an allocation of Rs12 billion for development projects in Gujrat, describing it as an unprecedented investment in the city’s history.

items.summary: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has upgraded Project Ensemble to support round-the-clock real-value tokenised settlements through its EnsembleTX project. The regulator also plans to extend its trials to regulated stablecoins, following tests involving tokenised bonds, money market funds and bank deposits. Meanwhile, HSBC CEO Georges Elhedery revealed that its Hong Kong dollar stablecoin, RedCoin, attracted 50,000 users within 10 days of launch.

items.author: Fiaz Mahmood
items.content:
The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday issued notices to the federal government and others in a petition seeking registration of a case over the deaths of children in the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) tragedy and compensation for the affected families.
Fourteen newborn babies were killed on August 26 after a fire broke out on the third floor of the Mother and Child Hospital’s ward at the PIMS hospital, while another child died later on September 17.
The notices were issued to the Prime Minister’s Office, Ministry of Health, Establishment Division, Islamabad Healthcare Regulatory Authority, Auditor General, chief commissioner, deputy commissioner, Capital Development Authority, Capital Emergency Services, PIMS executive director, Islamabad inspector general of Police and Federal Investigation Agency director general.
Read: 14 newborns killed in fire at PIMS Hospital in Islamabad
The court also summoned the complete record, including the inquiry report into the incident, and suspended an order passed by a justice of the peace dismissing an application for registration of an FIR.
Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro heard the petition filed by lawyer Riaz Hanif Rahi.
The petitioner told the court that 14 children had caught fire simultaneously in the PIMS incident, while another child died later. He said no FIR had been registered to date over the deaths.
The court asked whether an inquiry had been conducted into the incident. In response, Rahi said the inquiry report had established negligence.
He requested the court to direct the authorities to register an FIR immediately and submit it before the court by the end of the day’s proceedings.
The petitioner further said the justice of peace had dismissed his application for registration of a case because petitions concerning the matter were already pending before the high court.
He maintained that, apart from him, no one had approached the police station with an application, and a case should have been registered. He questioned the purpose of collecting evidence when no criminal case had been registered to pursue the matter.
The court observed that it would summon all reports and evidence and, if negligence was established, direct the registration of cases against those responsible.
After issuing notices to the respondents, the court adjourned further proceedings until November 12.
An inquiry committee presented its interim report to the premier on August 29, which led to the suspension of eight high-ranking officers from PIMS and external agencies, with disciplinary proceedings initiated against them. It also recommended a civil and monetary award for Nurse Razia, who saved a newborn from the fire, while placing the charge nurse and security guard off duty.
Read More: Inquiry report finds systemic, institutional failures at fault in PIMS nursery fire
On September 15, the inquiry committee constituted by the prime minister to investigate the PIMS fire concluded that the tragedy culminated as a result of “systemic and institutional failures”, with the hospital and its senior management bearing primary responsibility for failing to address known safety risks.
The report, based on a 52-point investigation, found that multiple safety measures were either absent, inadequate, not activated in time or had never been independently verified.
The committee concluded that criminal responsibility of an individual would have to be determined separately under the relevant rules and on the basis of available evidence.
It placed primary institutional responsibility on PIMS and its senior management for failing to convert known risks and earlier warnings into an effective safety system.
The inquiry committee recommended immediate fire-safety measures and a comprehensive electrical-safety audit at PIMS. It called for effective fire-detection, alarm, firefighting and evacuation systems, along with dedicated SOPs for newborn evacuation and realistic fire and evacuation drills.

President Donald Trump said on ​Tuesday the United States was close ‌to making a trade deal with Canada.
"Canada is very good, we're going to ​make a deal with Canada ​very soon. We're going to make ⁠a great deal," Trump said ​in an interview with Fox News.
Canada and ​the United States have slapped billions of dollars in tariffs on each other in ​recent months. The imposition of ​tariffs on Canada has emerged as an issue ‌in ⁠some northern US border states like Michigan and Maine before US midterm elections on Tuesday.
Trump and Canadian Prime Minister ​Mark ​Carney said on ⁠Sunday they had spoken about a trade deal, which the ​US president said would be "great ​for ⁠our farmers".
Carney said on X: "Our teams will now be working in ⁠the ​coming weeks to deliver ​that outcome."
Good conversation with President @realDonaldTrump on the future of Canada-U.S. trade.
This builds on our recent constructive discussions on the outlines of a mutually beneficial trade deal that would create jobs for our workers, boost affordability for families, and fully…
— Mark Carney (@MarkJCarney) November 1, 2026
Carney and Trump had discussed the framework of a new bilateral trade agreement in a series of phone calls, signalling a possible breakthrough in resolving a months-long cross-border trade dispute.
Trump had also emphasised that the arrangement would dismantle Canadian agricultural trade barriers, asserting that "our farmers were paying tremendous tariffs to send things to Canada", reaching up to 400% on dairy items.
"All those tariffs will be gone. There will be no tariff," he maintained.
Outlining key provisions of the emerging accord, Trump said Ottawa agreed to finance the cross-border Keystone oil pipeline system connecting Canada and the US.
"They're going to build the Keystone Pipeline. They're going to pay for it," he noted, adding that Washington had largely determined the pipeline's transit route.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday granted protective bail to TikToker Anser Mahmood, alias "Mr Patlu", who was nominated in a case registered over culpable homicide, unlawful assembly, rioting and the death of one person and injuries to several others in a stampede.
A prize draw at a TikToker's wedding celebration on Sunday turned deadly after a stampede at Faraz Ground in Daska left two people dead and 17 others injured.
The court directed the suspect to approach the relevant court by November 10. Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar heard the protective bail petition filed by Mahmood. The petitioner arrived at the court in a wheelchair, accompanied by his counsel, Barrister Qasim Nawaz Abbasi.
Read: Stampede at TikToker's mehndi kills two, injures 17
The petition stated that a case had been registered against him at the Motra Police Station in Sialkot district on charges of culpable homicide, unlawful assembly and rioting, following an incident in which one person was killed and several others were injured in a stampede.
The petitioner argued that the IHC had the authority to grant protective bail to enable him to approach the relevant court for pre-arrest bail without examining the merits of the case. Accepting the request, the court granted him protective bail until November 10.
On Sunday, a crowd had gathered for Mahmood's mehndi ceremony, after he had announced a prize draw featuring cars, motorcycles and cash rewards to attract participants and publicise the event.
The rush at the entrance gate triggered a stampede, during which several people fell to the ground and were trampled underfoot.
One of the victims, Aqeel, a resident of Budha Goraya, died at the scene, while 18 people were initially injured and shifted to hospitals. Among the injured was Rehan, a resident of Glotian Kalan, whose condition was critical.
He was referred to Lahore's Mayo Hospital but later succumbed to his injuries, taking the death toll to two and leaving 17 others injured.
Police registered a case at Motra Police Station on their own complaint under Sections 322, 431, 440, 188, 109, 148 and 149 of the Pakistan Penal Code, along with Section 16 of the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance.
The first information report named nine people, including Mahmood, Kashif, ground owner Haji Shahid Javed and other organisers Daniyal, Munir Ahmed, Mohsin Ali, Irshad Ali, Abdullah and Zohaib Mansha. Another 40 to 45 unidentified security guards had also been included in the case.
