items.content:
Indian VCs And The Deeptech Dilemma
Skyroot has proved that homegrown startups can build rockets, but the bigger challenge may lie in funding them. A recent viral critique of Indian venture capitalists has reignited the debate over deeptech funding gaps, risk appetite of investors and slow diligence.
Founder Grievances: For many early stage founders, deeptech funding in India remains plagued by prolonged due diligence, demands for commercial traction before validation and an over-reliance on founder pedigree. Their criticism is aimed at the current system, which may be underwriting very little genuine technological risk and backing a handful of startups.
Concentration Problem: Data adds further nuance to the debate. Deeptech funding surged 176% YoY in Q3 2026, but the deal count barely moved. This is because most of the capital was heavily concentrated among a few players and that too in Bengaluru. The pattern suggests that the capital is largely flowing to technically validated companies, while early stage founders pursuing unproven scientific experiments still struggle to secure their first cheque.
Why Investors Hesitate? Indian VCs have historically been hesitant towards deeptech bets due to the sector’s long gestation cycles, uncertain exits, specialised diligence and substantial follow-on capital. Venture funds also operate under pressure from limited partners to mint returns and liquidity within defined timelines. As a result, most VCs hesitate to underwrite these uncertain scientific bets.
Changing Ecosystem: However, the picture is not entirely bleak. Founder-led vehicles and specialist funds are expanding and raising big bucks for moonshots. Government initiatives, like the ₹1 Lakh Cr RDI Fund, are also creating more optimism around deeptech. But capital alone will not solve the problem as local frontier ventures still need stronger follow-on funding, patient limited partners and the corporate willing to buy early products.
Indian founders have proved that they can build rockets, but can VCs now step in and show that they can finance these moonshot bets? Let’s find out…
From The Editor’s Desk
Weekly Funding Rundown
Indian startups cumulatively raised $130.2 Mn last week, down 29% from $184 Mn in the preceding week. However, deal count zoomed 88% week-on-week to 32. Cent and Simplismart took the biggest cheques home at $15 Mn and $14 Mn, respectively.
Ecommerce emerged as the most funded sector last week, bagging $33 Mn across nine deals. Following suit were AI ventures, which bagged $30 Mn across five deals.
On the investor front, Blume Ventures and Antler emerged as the most active investors last week and backed three startups each.
E2W Sales In October
Electric two-wheeler registrations grew a marginal 2.9% month-on-month to 2.1 Lakh units in October. Sales also rose 48% YoY from 1.4 Lakh units a year earlier.
Legacy giants TVS Motor and Hero MotoCorp recorded gains and improved their market share to 27.2% and 13.4%, respectively. However, Bajaj Auto reported a decline in sales in October, which led to its market share falling to 21.7% from 23.4% in September.
Growth also tapered off for new-age EV makers in October. Ather’s registrations declined 1.8% to 30,380 units from 30,942 units in September, while its market share slipped to 14.2%. Ola Electric’s sales also tanked 13.7% MoM to 11,614 units last month.
Kickback Allegations At Flipkart
Walmart has launched a probe into allegations that employees at the ecommerce giant received over ₹150 Cr in kickbacks from vendors. The charges have been directed against employees in Flipkart’s smartphones and luggage and travel accessories divisions.
The complaints allege the certain employees accepted payments and favours from vendors in exchange for preferential treatment on the ecommerce platform, including greater visibility that helped drive sales.
This is Walmart’s third investigation into alleged financial misconduct at Flipkart in the past three years. A previous probe resulted in three dismissals two-and-a-half years ago, while another investigation found wrongdoing by an employee barely six months ago.
eMudhra & Accountability
The cybersecurity firm came under fire last month after researchers discovered that its private keys were weak and could be recovered in under a second. The row saw eMudhra exit the global TLS certificate business altogether.
The episode demonstrates that global browser makers, rather than local regulators, became the first line of accountability for eMudhra. This raises a governance question for India: who investigates and prevents a similar failure domestically?
Experts now flag that eMudhra’s exit means that Indian websites may increasingly depend on foreign certificate authorities for trust. This could affect India’s digital sovereignty and its ability to build a domestic public-key infrastructure ecosystem.
Bullish Week For Startup Stocks
Of the 69 new-age tech stocks under Inc42’s coverage, 40 gained between 0.2% and 26.8%, last week. However, the remaining 29 declined by up to 22.3%. Startup stocks largely saw gains as quarterly earnings drove sharp moves in individual counters.
Ather Energy and Zetwerk emerged as the biggest gainers, while shares of CarTrade and AceVector shed the most. The combined market-cap of these 69 stocks jumped to $160.9 Bn at the end of last week, up 5.7% from $152.3 Bn in the week-ago period.
Going forward, investors will track the upcoming US midterm elections, Brent crude oil prices, geopolitical developments and quarterly earnings for market cues this week.
upliance.ai Eyes $4 Mn
The D2C home appliance maker in advanced talks to raise $3 Mn to $4 Mn in its Series A round. The fundraise will likely see participation from a fresh investor, while existing backers, including Khosla Ventures, will also double down.
Founded in 2021, upliance.ai sells AI-powered kitchen appliances like food processors and air fryers. The D2C brand had last raised ₹34 Cr in a seed round led by Khosla Ventures in 2024 at a valuation of ₹143 Cr.
The development comes amid growing activity in India’s smart kitchen appliances market, which is being driven by growing demand for automated products and rising disposable incomes. The space is projected to become a $3 Bn opportunity by 2032.
Inc42 Markets
Inc42 Startup Spotlight
How D-Propulse Is Rethinking Jet Engines
India has pursued indigenous jet-engine capability for decades now, but to no avail. This has created heavy dependence on overseas vendors and costly testing. D-Propulse is betting on a new technology to build lighter, cheaper propulsion for high-speed drones and missiles.
The RDE Approach: Founded in 2025, D-Propulse is developing rotating detonation engines (RDEs), which use supersonic detonation waves to generate thrust. It has already tested a 5 kN air-breathing RDE that is currently at technology readiness level-5. The startup claims its engine will be 15-25% more efficient and at least 60% less expensive than conventional ramjets.
Eye On The Prize: To scale its ambitions, the startup is also building a 5,000+ sq ft combustor test facility at IIT Madras, with air mass flow capacity of around 10 kg/sec and an in-house HPC cluster. It is also exploring infrastructure rental as an early revenue stream while its jet engine business takes shape.
Building For Defence: D-Propulse is targeting the Indian Armed Forces as its intended first customers. It now plans to conduct flight tests between June and December 2027 and limited series production by the end of 2028. The pre-revenue startup also plans to raise a Series A round by early next year.
With the global RDE opportunity projected to surpass $2.4 Bn by 2030, can D-Propulse build commercially viable jet engines for India?

items.author: Suleiman A. Suleiman
items.content:
Religion is a common currency in Nigeria, and just as we love to flaunt money and wealth, so too are we always quick to show off our religiosity. It is difficult, and even unfair, that anyone’s act of religious worship or ritual is not strictly in the name of God or for reasons of advancing personal religious faith or piety. Yet, it is also difficult to avoid such a sense in many different circumstances of the public display of religion by individuals. So, we worship in the name of God, but there is little doubt that we also tend to make sure other people notice that we do.
Politics and social media have transformed this general tendency—to worship for God and for the notice of others—into something uniquely Nigerian. Of course, politicians and other political actors the world over invoke religion and religious ritual and symbolism to advance political objectives, rather than to deepen faith or conviction. The United States, often touted as the world’s bastion of democracy, is also at once the capital of exploiting religious ritual and symbolism for political purposes. The Church—and increasingly the mosque—in the U.S. is both a place of worship, but also a space for doing all kinds of politics.
Still, the way we do it here appears unique to me. At least one uniquely Nigerian—and for me disturbing—way of doing mixing politics with religious ritual and symbolism is the relative balance we accord to religion and governance in public life. This relates, in particular, to the idea of “praying for the nation” frequently enjoined by our political and religious leaders, and even the ordinary Nigerians in diverse contexts. Afterall, nearly all informal conversations about governance among Nigerians end with a resort to praying more or leaving it all to God.
The idea and practice of “praying for the nation” in Nigeria today is a religious, political and commercial activity. In fact, we can say quite safely that is a whole industry in its own right now. Billions of naira, and unquantifiable amount of energy and time are nowadays spent on praying for the nation across all religious and sectarian divides, particularly during elections.
I have always found this tendency among our political class curious, not to diminish the significance of prayers in human or national affairs, but because I always wonder whether the proportion is appropriate for success. Prayers are important for individual or national advancement, but for both, prayers work best with the most effort and preparation.
The federal government and the ruling APC made the most of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s jetting off for the lesser-hajj last week, to “pray for the nation” as the newspapers reported it. I do not begrudge the President his prayers for the nation. But I could not help but wonder if the amount of time, effort, and money spent on this latest episode of praying for Nigeria would not have been better used in redesigning or adjusting his economic policies to make life easier for Nigerians. Even in the context of this 2027 election campaigns, the government and his party have not done enough to convince Nigerians on his policy direction.
The government has not done enough to listen to or respond positively to the mounting challenges its economic policies are inflicting on Nigerians, and however well intentioned, empty stomachs cannot survive on prayers alone.
 
From my mailbox
Re: Tinubu: Lion at home, lamb abroad?
My namesake, we haven’t seen each other and exchanged views for quite some time, but I do read your column religiously. Frankly, you made my day by your insightful, brutally frank and honest October 26, 2026, paper, “Tinubu: Lion at home, lamb abroad?”
Under Tinubu’s administration, Nigeria has become a one-man show. I first read George Orwell’s Animal Farm when growing up, and read it several times again up to the university and into the Foreign Service in 1975. I never imagined or visualised that Nigeria would later become the near basket case it has now become, where everything, poverty, hunger and insecurity would become the lot of Nigerians.
The President has become a sole administrator, surrounded by grovelling cronies who will not tell him the reality of the situation of Nigerians, honestly and truthfully. Nobody has the balls to tell him that Nigeria has become a living hell and that his reputation is far worse than that of Buhari. It is a tragedy.
Civil servants only care about the security of their jobs and the starvation salaries they receive. This National Assembly under Godswill Akpabio is the worst since the return of democratic rule, which, to me, is more appropriately a civilian rule camouflaging as democratic. During the PDP days, an attempt was made to impeach a PDP President, and it patriotically buried the third-term gambit. Nigerians then knew of the existence of an assertive and independent National Assembly. But under Akpabio, the National Assembly has become a poodle of the Presidency.
Civil servants, who are the engines of any government and need to be the middle class, are now emasculated and pauperised. They receive starvation salaries while the politicians live in obscene opulence and make no bones about flaunting it. The Nigerian Labour Congress (NLC) appears to be barking and not biting. The good old days of Adams Oshiomhole appear to have gone forever.
Reforms are periodically undertaken by a government, and these reforms are meant to benefit the people. If the reforms instituted by the Tinubu government are not benefiting Nigerians and they are crying loudly, they should not be ignored.
The government commends the World Bank and IMF when they make favourable comments on some aspects of the reforms, but they get pilloried when they make adverse comments on some aspects. The views of economists and other knowledgeable Nigerians are dismissed as opposition politics.
I supported and campaigned in my own way for Bola Ahmed Tinubu in 2023 because I believed then that he was a democrat who would govern in accordance with the tenets of democracy for which he fought and even went into exile.
Sadly, on assuming office, he began to run a one-man show who must be slavishly obeyed. The Federal Executive became more pliant, and the National Assembly became an extension of the Villa.
As a retired hard-nosed career diplomat, I keep on asking myself about the direction of Nigeria’s foreign policy. It is scandalous to me that, after recalling ambassadors immediately on assumption of office, it took President Tinubu over two years to appoint replacements.
Regrettably, career diplomats who have devoted their service to Nigeria were more marginalised in favour of politicians who were more loyal to themselves than their country.
Under President Tinubu’s chairmanship of ECOWAS, the coup d’état in Niger Republic was badly bungled. If you cannot possess the wherewithal to carry out your threat, do not make it. Otherwise, it becomes an empty threat.
ECOWAS threatened Niger Republic with military action after suspending its membership. Nigeria followed up with the closure of the border between the two countries and went further to cut off electricity, which was a bilateral agreement and not a multilateral one.
Why should Nigeria cut off electricity supply to Niger Republic? This is not only a breach of bilateral agreement but a hostile act. The culmination of what ECOWAS led to Niger Republic, Mali and Burkina Faso breaking away and forming their own Association of Sahel States (AES).
Nigeria and Niger are like Siamese twins. We need each other, and we are closely related ethnically, culturally and religiously. Therefore, Nigeria should have been more tactful and diplomatic. ECOWAS resolution or not, in any case, Nigeria has the clout to moderate ECOWAS decisions.
As President of the Republic, Tinubu must decide whether he wants to be remembered for working to make life better for Nigerians, or for working against them. the choice is his own, and I hope he chooses wisely.
 
May God save Nigeria.
Ambassador Suleiman Dahiru
Abuja, Nigeria

items.author: Faruk Shuaibu
items.content:
Energy experts, policymakers have called for affordable financing, stronger quality control and a phased localisation policy to strengthen Nigeria’s solar industry without making solar products unaffordable for households and businesses.
The call was made during the Abuja Solar Policy Roundtable, organised by the Global Initiative for Food Security and Ecosystem Preservation (GIFSEP) and the Solar Power Nigeria Campaign.
Speaking during the event, the Executive Director of GIFSEP and co-convener of the Solar Power Nigeria Campaign, Dr Michael T. David, described solar energy as a practical route to more reliable and affordable electricity.
He noted that millions of Nigerians continue to contend with unreliable grid power and depend on petrol and diesel generators, which impose significant costs on households and businesses.
He commended the Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr Kingsley Tochukwu Udeh, for stating that Nigeria would not prohibit solar panel imports before developing adequate domestic manufacturing capacity.
“The solar sector is too important to be left with fragmented oversight and inconsistent standards,” he said.
David identified skills development, local manufacturing and assembly, and quality assurance as three priorities for building a sustainable solar industry.
He called for technician certification, continuous training and retraining, including opportunities for generator technicians to acquire solar installation and maintenance skills.
He also advocated predictable government policies, accessible financing and stronger coordination among relevant regulatory and standards institutions, including the Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON), the Nigerian Electricity Management Services Agency (NEMSA) and the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC), within their respective mandates.
The Special Assistant to the President on Climate Change Matters, Comrade Yussuf Olatunji Kelani described affordable and reliable energy as essential to Nigeria’s economic development, climate objectives and resilience.
He said solar energy could help address electricity challenges while supporting agriculture, particularly irrigation, food storage and processing. According to him, expanding access to solar power could reduce operating costs for farmers, minimise post-harvest losses and strengthen food security.
Kelani emphasised that the energy transition must benefit ordinary Nigerians, including young people, women and vulnerable communities, rather than being limited to government institutions and large investors.

items.content:
The Yobe State Government has presented nine investment opportunities to Russian businesses as part of efforts to attract foreign investment into agriculture, energy, infrastructure and other sectors of the state’s economy.
The investment proposals include the development of a 1,500-hectare Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zone (SAPZ) in Damaturu, rice and sesame processing plants, agricultural mechanisation and dedicated power generation capacity of between 50 and 100 megawatts.
The state government also proposed partnerships involving technology transfer, equipment supply, industrial collaboration and possible export-credit facilities.
The proposals were presented by a delegation led by the Special Adviser to Governor Mai Mala Buni on International Relations and Investment, Dr Sa’id Alkali Kori, during engagements with Russian business interests in Moscow on the sidelines of the Russia-Africa Summit.
Dr Kori said the proposed Damaturu SAPZ was designed to attract agro-industrial businesses, increase local processing capacity and create employment opportunities through the development of agricultural value chains.
The delegation also held talks with Sistema Public Joint Stock Financial Corporation, a Russian investment holding company with interests in telecommunications, energy, agriculture, healthcare, retail and technology.
At the meeting, the Yobe delegation presented potential areas of investment cooperation, including agro-industrialisation, power generation, rural electrification, oil and gas, water resources, irrigation, solid minerals, logistics, healthcare and education.
The delegation said the engagement was aimed at exploring areas of mutual interest, assessing commercially viable projects and identifying possible frameworks for technical and investment cooperation.
To attract investors, the delegation outlined proposed government support measures, including access to land with appropriate titles, counterpart funding arrangements, offtake commitments, applicable tax incentives and security support.
Kori said the proposed arrangements would be subject to project-specific negotiations and relevant legal and regulatory requirements.
He said the proposed 1,500-hectare Damaturu agro-industrial hub would accommodate processing and related businesses, with rice and sesame identified as priority commodities.
According to him, the investment would help strengthen agricultural value chains, reduce post-harvest losses and create opportunities for domestic and export trade.
He identified reliable electricity supply as a major requirement for the proposed industrial zone, hence the plan to explore dedicated power generation capacity of between 50 and 100 megawatts.
Kori said potential partnerships with Russian companies could also provide access to modern agricultural machinery, processing equipment, energy systems and technical expertise.
Other investment opportunities presented include infrastructure development, irrigation, solid minerals, healthcare, education and human capital development.
Further technical and commercial discussions are expected to determine the projects, financing arrangements and implementation frameworks that could emerge from the engagements.

items.content:
The Lagos State Government has showcased its technology ecosystem, emerging startups and investment opportunities at GITEX Nigeria 2026, using the international technology event to strengthen partnerships and promote the state’s ambition to become Africa’s innovation capital.
The Lagos State Ministry of Innovation, Science and Technology (MIST), led by Commissioner Olatunbosun Alake, coordinated the state’s participation at the event, held at the Landmark Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos.
The two-day programme featured a technology exhibition, the Future Economy Conference and a Startup Festival, bringing together government officials, technology entrepreneurs, investors and international stakeholders.
A welcome dinner ahead of the programme attracted representatives of Lagos, Katsina, Jigawa, Ondo, Kwara, Delta, Borno and Ogun states, alongside founders, investors and diplomatic guests.
Speakers included Sam Egube, Deputy Chief of Staff to Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, who represented the governor; Trixie LohMirmand, Executive Vice President of Dubai World Trade Centre and Chief Executive Officer of KAOUN International; and representatives of the Moroccan Consulate. Alake also highlighted opportunities within Lagos’ innovation ecosystem.
At the opening of the Lagos programme, Deputy Governor Kadri Obafemi Hamzat described Lagos as a “consequential city”, saying the decision to host GITEX reflected the state’s growing influence in Africa’s technology landscape.
Hamzat reiterated the government’s ambition to position Lagos not only as Nigeria’s commercial capital but also as Africa’s innovation capital. He cited the presence of nearly 1,000 active startups as evidence of the ecosystem’s potential, while emphasising the need for sustained investment in infrastructure, talent, policy and implementation.
Throughout the event, MIST showcased startups, technologies, partnerships and investment opportunities to potential investors and international collaborators.
The Governor’s Special Adviser on Innovation, Technology and Broadband Development and Chairman of the Local Organising Committee, Ganiyu Oseni, stressed that infrastructure and policy must advance together to support a competitive digital economy.
He identified connectivity, electricity, digital identity and talent development as critical requirements, urging investors to establish operational bases in Lagos rather than treat the state merely as a market.
Oseni also called for Nigeria to move beyond adopting foreign technologies and develop home-grown solutions in digital finance, tokenised assets and cross-border settlements that could compete across Africa and globally.
More than two dozen startups and technology companies participated in the exhibition, covering artificial intelligence, financial technology, cybersecurity, education technology, agriculture and logistics.
Among the companies seeking investment and market opportunities were Sidebrief, DawnAI, RollaPay, Hyperspace Technologies, Sowota and Climatrix AI.
The second day placed greater emphasis on financial technology through FDX Nigeria by GITEX, which examined digital payments, banking, financial inclusion, digital assets and cross-border finance.
A major highlight was the Lagos State Employment Trust Fund (LSETF) Pitch Programme, organised in partnership with TechQuest STEM Academy and MIST. The initiative provided selected entrepreneurs with an opportunity to present their businesses, products and growth strategies to investors and other ecosystem stakeholders, strengthening the funding pipeline for Lagos-based innovators.
The programme also featured the launch of MINT Africa by GITEX, a platform focused on the future of finance on the continent.
Oseni maintained that Nigeria had the talent, market scale and entrepreneurial capacity to lead Africa’s digital financial transformation, provided infrastructure, regulation and investor confidence developed alongside innovation.

items.author: Abubakar Auwal
items.content:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has confirmed that its presidential campaign flag-off will take place in Sokoto State on November 4, 2026, vowing to resist any attack on candidates, party members and offices.
The party said no threat, intimidation or unlawful obstruction would prevent it from exercising its constitutional right to organise political activities and campaign for its candidates in the state.
The crisis between the political parties started when the ADC accused suspected All Progressives Congress, APC thugs of attacking women participating in the party’s rally, alleging that some sustained injuries while others had their mobile phones snatched.
There were also allegations that the APC-led state government had booked all available hotel rooms across the state to prevent the ADC from hosting its presidential campaign flag-off.
The party also accused operatives of the Sokoto Marshall and Community Guards of attacking its governorship candidate, Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, while returning from the airport after accompanying Senator Aminu Waziri Tambuwal.
The ADC alleged that the attack resulted in the destruction of the windscreen of one of the vehicles in his convoy.
Meanwhile, the Director General of the Governorship Campaign Council, Bello Muhammad Goronyo, on Sunday during a press conference at the party’s secretariat in Sokoto called on relevant authorities to investigate reported attacks on the party’s governorship candidate, Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, members of its women wing and the party’s office, and ensure that those responsible are brought to book.
He also urged security operatives to remain professional and apolitical in the discharge of their duties, stressing the need to provide a peaceful and secure environment for all political parties to conduct their activities.
“The ADC’s presidential campaign flag-off, now scheduled for November 4, 2026, will proceed. No threat, intimidation or unlawful obstruction will deprive the party of its constitutional right to organise political activities and campaign for its candidates,” he said.
The party called on its supporters across the country to remain calm, peaceful, disciplined and law-abiding, assuring that it would not be provoked, promising that the party would continue to pursue accountability through lawful means.
The press conference was attended by ADC’s governorship candidate, Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, his running mate, Bello Isa Ambarura, and other party chieftains.
Earlier, the All Progressive Congress (APC) in the state had dismissed the allegations of intimidation, describing them as fabricated claims intended to attract public sympathy and divert attention from the ADC’s political challenges.
The state APC Chairman, Alhaji Haruna Adiya, said the allegations were part of what he described as a propaganda campaign against the state government.
He also faulted what he described as inconsistencies in the ADC’s account of the incident, arguing that while the party’s media aide reportedly claimed that security personnel prevented Dan’iya from entering Sokoto metropolis, the candidate’s statement indicated that he had visited different locations in the city to pay condolence visits and attend to other engagements.
 
The APC chairman also dismissed claims that security personnel were deployed to restrict ADC members from entering the state, explaining that Sokoto was preparing to host a major traditional title conferment ceremony scheduled for Sunday.
 
He said the event was expected to attract prominent personalities and visitors from different parts of the country, making adequate security arrangements necessary.
 
Adiya maintained that the deployment of security personnel was aimed at protecting residents and visitors attending the ceremony and had nothing to do with the political activities of the ADC.
 
He further urged the opposition party to address its internal challenges rather than blame the APC and the state government for its political difficulties.
 
He urged the opposition party to substantiate its allegations and focus on presenting policies and development plans to the electorate rather than engaging in what he described as manufactured controversies.

items.content: Mumbai: After aggressively selling in September and the first half of October, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have turned net buyers of Indian equities, investing nearly $1.2 billion over the past 10 trading sessions. Concerns over the outlook for the AI trade could have prompted some overseas investors to shift allocations to beaten-down Indian equities, which have lagged behind various regional peers recently in the absence of a dominant AI industry. The recent purchases, however, may be positional flows looking for avenues that are less impacted by the AI sell-off rather than a fresh bullish call on India by global investors."Indian large-cap stocks, particularly banks and IT companies, are being viewed as an anti-AI trade, attracting model-driven flows rather than a broad-based return of long-only foreign investors, said Ritesh Jain, founder of Pinetree Macro.135441127Between October 16 and October 30, FPIs made net purchases of nearly $1.2 billion in the secondary market, according to NSDL data. On October 30, they bought equities worth ₹3,600 crore, according to provisional NSE data. In the primary market, they were buyers worth $600 million, with Jio Telecom's ₹30,188 crore IPO expected to have cornered a large chunk of these flows."There is a shift in global investment flows because of signs of a deflation in the artificial intelligence (AI) trade," said Jain. "When the AI trade is doing well, money moves from the rest of the world into the US as investors buy dollars to invest in US AI stocks. When they sell these stocks, they also move out of the US dollar."Read more: Nifty IT’s 18% rally may mark a durable leadership cycle; 35,000 next: LKP's Vatsal BhuvaIndian markets delivered a mixed performance in October. The Sensex and Nifty gained 1.9% and 2.7%, respectively, while the BSE Midcap 150 and BSE SmallCap 250 fell 4% and 6.3%. The Nifty IT index surged 17%.Overseas markets, meanwhile, saw sharp corrections, with the Nasdaq and Japan's Nikkei falling 5% each, Hong Kong's Hang Seng declining 5.5%, Shenzhen dropping 13.7%, and Taiwan and South Korea's Kospi falling 8% and 14%, respectively.Fund managers are seeing selective opportunities in India after the recent underperformance, said strategists. "A small portion of the inflows reflected selective foreign investors returning to India on a bottom-up basis, attracted by improving growth prospects and opportunities in certain technology sectors," said Gautam Chhaochharia, head of global markets, India, at UBS.Read more: Bonus issues, stock splits, dividends: Infosys, Asian Paints among over 40 stocks turning ex-date this weekThe recent buying follows a prolonged period of foreign outflows. Between January 1 and October 15, they sold equities worth over $32.7 billion amid the US-Iran war, rising crude oil prices, hardening bond yields, currency depreciation, earnings uncertainty and inflation. They had also sold equities worth over $18.8 billion in 2025.Though overseas investors bought nearly $6.15 billion in Indian equities between mid-June and August, they pulled out $8.6 billion in September and the first half of October as a spike in global oil prices and hardening of US bond yields heightened risk-off sentiment."The recent pressure on Indian markets had been driven more by global factors, including the strength of the AI trade and higher energy prices, than by domestic fundamentals," said Ben Powell, chief investment strategist for Middle East and Asia-Pacific at BlackRock Investment Institute.BlackRock remains strategically overweight on India and is closely monitoring the recent pace of foreign inflows. "We continue to closely watch the encouraging recent pace of inflows and remain strategically overweight India," he said.

items.author: Akinbayo Wahab
items.content:
Nigerian Samson Adamu has been appointed the new General Secretary of the Confederation of African Football (CAF).
CAF announced the appointment on Sunday, on its website following a comprehensive recruitment process conducted by the continental football governing body.
The News Agency of Nigeria reports that Adamu had been serving as acting General Secretary since March, following the resignation of Veron Mosengo-Omba.
Mosengo-Omba subsequently became president of the football federation in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
CAF President, Patrice Motsepe, was quoted in the statement on its website as saying that the appointment followed a competitive recruitment exercise, during which the position was widely advertised and several candidates interviewed.
Adamu has worked with CAF for eight years, serving first as Director of Competitions and later as Director of Tournaments and Events.
“Adamu brings extensive experience in African football administration, having joined CAF in 2018 as Director of Competitions before subsequently serving as Director of Tournaments and Events.
“He has played a leading role in the delivery of several major continental competitions, including CAF’s flagship tournament, the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations,” Motsepe was quoted as saying.
A graduate of the FIFA Master programme in International Management, Law and Humanities of Sport, Adamu brings considerable institutional knowledge and experience to his new role.
NAN reports that Adamu is expected to oversee CAF’s day-to-day administration and support the implementation of its strategic priorities.
He is the son of Amos Adamu, a former Director of Sports in the then Ministry of Sports and a former FIFA Executive Committee member.
The appointment places Adamu among a distinguished line of CAF General Secretaries, including members of Egypt’s Fahmy family.
Mourad Fahmy served from 1961 to 1982, followed by his son, Mustapha Fahmy, from 1982 to 2010, and grandson, Amr Fahmy, who held the position from 2017 to 2019.

Midfielder Favour Nkwocha was also cautioned as Nigeria continued to press for an opening goal. Head Coach Hakeem Busari made his first change of the evening, introducing Precious Oscar for Oluwakemi Adegbuyi as Nigeria looked to find a way through.
The deadlock remained unbroken until the 88th minute, when the referee initially awarded Nigeria a penalty before being invited to the VAR monitor to review the decision. Following the review, the penalty was upheld, and Oduntan stepped forward to convert from the spot with a minute left on the clock, giving Nigeria the breakthrough.
Top scorer Oluebube Umejiaku had won the penalty for the Flamingos, setting up Oduntan to deliver the decisive moment of the contest. The victory sends Nigeria into the semi-finals, where they will face Brazil, who secured a 2-1 win over China in their quarter-final encounter.

…Bishop Obodo demands removal of his name, warns of legal action
By Anayo Okoli
The Catholic Diocese of Enugu has disowned the inclusion of the Auxiliary Bishop of Enugu, Most Rev. Ernest Anezichukwu Obodo, in the Enugu State All Progressives Congress, APC, Campaign Council, saying he was listed without his knowledge or consent.
The Diocese also demanded the immediate removal of the bishop’s name and those of other Catholic priests allegedly included in the campaign council without their authorisation.
Obodo, who is also the Enugu State Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria, CAN, was reportedly named Director of the Faith-Based Campaign Group in the APC campaign council.
In a disclaimer dated October 30, 2026, and signed by the Diocesan Chancellor and Secretary, Very Rev. Fr. Wilfred Chidi Agubuchie, the Diocese described the inclusion as unauthorised, misleading and a misrepresentation of the bishop’s political disposition.
The statement said the action was a “malicious act of misrepresentation and defamation,” adding that it undermined the bishop’s integrity and ecclesiastical reputation.
“The Catholic Diocese of Enugu has become aware of reports concerning the inclusion of the name of Most Rev. Ernest Anezichukwu Obodo, Auxiliary Bishop of Enugu and Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), Enugu State, as Director of the Faith-Based Campaign Group in the Enugu State APC Campaign Council, alongside the names of some Catholic priests.
“We categorically state that the inclusion of the Bishop’s name without his knowledge or consent is wholly unauthorised, misleading and unacceptable,” the statement said.
The Diocese stressed that the Catholic Church did not engage in partisan politics, participate in political campaigns or endorse political parties.
It said the Church remained politically neutral and committed to its spiritual mission and the promotion of peace, justice and the common good.
While acknowledging the right of individual Christians to participate in civic and democratic activities, the Diocese warned against using the name, office or identity of the Church and its ministers for partisan political interests.
“We therefore demand the immediate removal of Bishop Ernest Obodo’s name, as well as the names of all other Catholic priests included without their knowledge and consent, from the said campaign list and any related publications,” it said.
The Diocese further warned that any continued or subsequent unauthorised use of the bishop’s name, title, image or ecclesiastical office for partisan political purposes would attract appropriate legal action.
“For the avoidance of doubt, the Catholic Church is not a political campaign organisation and must not be presented as one,” the statement added.

Gov. Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra has urged South-East political leaders to abandon opposition politics and embrace greater integration with the Federal Government.
Soludo made the call at a stakeholders’ meeting on Sunday in Awka.
The meeting had political leaders and grassroots mobilisers from the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), All Progressives Congress (APC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and Accord Party.
The governor said that the coalition of political parties in support of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election represented a new direction for the region’s political engagement.
According to him, the era of opposition politics, which became prominent in the South-East during the 2015 general elections, should give way to active participation in governance at the centre.
He said that considerable work was required at the grassroots to change public perception of the government and mobilise support for the president.
He argued that the 5,000 votes Tinubu received in Anambra in the 2023 presidential election had contributed to attracting significant projects to the state and the region.
“If 5,000 votes could attract these projects to our state and the region, imagine what would happen if we mobilised the electorate to give him massive support,” he said.
On the economic reforms of the government, Soludo acknowledged efforts to stabilise foreign exchange availability and address fiscal challenges, noting that, although progress had been made, more work was required.
He called for structural realignment of the coalition, saying existing campaign and mobilisation structures would be streamlined during the week.
The governor urged grassroots mobilisers to adopt door-to-door campaigns, drawing lessons from successful political mobilisation strategies used during the 1983 elections.
He also advised campaign teams not to be distracted by opposition criticism and verbal attacks on social media, but to remain focused on communicating what he described as the truth.
Soludo reaffirmed his commitment to long-term governance, saying that the decisions being taken by his administration were aimed at securing a prosperous future for generations to come.
Earlier, APGA National Chairman, Mr Sly Ezeokenwa, described the gathering as a landmark in the political history of Anambra.
Ezeokenwa said that the coalition was an unprecedented political alignment involving different parties united in support of Tinubu’s re-election.
He commended Soludo for providing leadership and facilitating the alliance, assuring that APGA would fully support the governor’s political direction.
“Our party structure is ready to execute the instructions and deliver results at the polls,” he said.
Also speaking, APC Chairman in Anambra, Sen. Emma Anosike, expressed appreciation for the development strides in the state.
Anosike said that the political realignment was aimed at positioning Anambra more directly within the government’s political and developmental framework.
He called for cooperation and solidarity among political parties, irrespective of their differences, to achieve the objectives of the coalition.

items.content:
Threatens arrest for anyone obstructing rival parties
By Steve Oko & Ugochukwu Alaribe
UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has warned Labour Party supporters against disrupting the campaign activities of opposition parties ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring that he has not authorised anyone to interfere with their democratic rights.
Otti said anyone found obstructing rival political parties from holding lawful rallies or other campaign activities would face arrest, irrespective of party affiliation.
The governor gave the warning on Sunday in Umuahia while flagging off the Labour Party’s 2027 campaign in the state, where he stressed that political competition must be conducted within the confines of the law.
He said opposition parties were free to use public facilities, including stadia, provided they followed the necessary procedures, obtained relevant approvals and paid the stipulated fees.
Otti added that he had directed security agencies to ensure that no political group was prevented from carrying out legitimate campaign activities.
“I have since given a public directive, and I am repeating it here, that opposition parties should not be restricted from the use of public facilities, including the stadium, once they apply and obtain the necessary approvals,” he said.
Addressing party loyalists, the governor warned that membership of the ruling party would not confer immunity on anyone who attempted to undermine the democratic process.
“You do not have my mandate to attack people or to stop people from campaigning.
“Security agencies have been mandated to arrest and deal decisively with anyone who attempts to obstruct any political group from holding their legitimate activities, even if they are Labour Party members. I hope I am heard clearly,” he said.
Beyond campaign conduct, Otti challenged opposition parties to focus their campaigns on policy alternatives and the future development of the state rather than personal attacks or issues he said his administration had addressed.
He argued that political debate in Abia should move beyond the payment of salaries and pensions, road construction and environmental sanitation to broader development priorities.
“Do not forget that in Abia we have gone past the era of campaigning on the payment of salaries and pensions, construction of roads or urban sanitation.
“The hygiene issues have been dealt with. If you are unable to raise your campaign pitch to the development realities of our state, you will definitely struggle to convince any informed voter,” the governor said.
He urged opposition parties to examine available performance data before making claims about the state, citing its ratings in the Citizen Satisfaction Index, State Performance Index and Fiscal Performance Ranking by governance-monitoring organisations.
“You should go and do your research first before coming out to open your mouth, because there are data everywhere to show what has been achieved. Evidently, the world knows that Abia is on the right track,” Otti said.
The governor also cited feedback from Abians at home and abroad, as well as development opportunities offered by multilateral institutions, as indications of progress under his administration.
“It would therefore be unthinkable that anyone will ever be allowed to return us to the old era of irresponsibility and misery,” he said.

By Anayo Okoli
ENUGU — A chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Barrister Peter Agubuzu, has faulted the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, over his criticism of a proposal for the South-East to accept a single four-year presidential term.
Agubuzu described Kalu’s remarks as misplaced, urging him to focus on addressing the economic hardship and rising cost of living confronting Nigerians rather than dwelling on how long the South-East might wait to produce a President.
Kalu had reportedly criticised South-East stakeholders advocating a single four-year presidential term for the region, an arrangement attributed to the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi.
Speaking at an All Progressives Congress (APC) women’s rally in Enugu on Saturday, the Deputy Speaker reportedly said the Igbo could not afford to wait 60 years to produce a President who would serve for only four years.
Reacting, Agubuzu, a senior lawyer, said the immediate concern of Nigerians was the worsening economic situation and the need for leadership capable of addressing the country’s challenges.
He argued that Obi’s proposal was driven by the need to transform Nigeria’s economy from consumption to production and lift millions of citizens out of poverty.
“While Nigerians across the country are chanting ‘Tinubu Must Go’ because of the economic hardship they are experiencing and their fear of a worsening economic crisis if Tinubu is re-elected, our brother, the Deputy Speaker, is talking about 60 years.
“He forgot that Obi’s primary objective is to transform Nigeria from consumption to production to lift millions out of poverty. This is why Nigerians are chanting Tinubu Must Go,” Agubuzu said.
He maintained that the major concern of Obi was how to address the country’s economic difficulties and restore hope to millions of Nigerians struggling with the rising cost of living.
“What Nigerians are saying is straightforward: Peter Obi should come and salvage the country from the impending economic disaster they fear will follow if President Tinubu is re-elected.
“Nigerians are worried about their survival, their livelihoods and the future of their children. That is the urgent issue before us, not a speculative debate about waiting 60 years for an Igbo President,” he said.
The NDC chieftain further argued that discussions about a single presidential term should be considered within the broader context of national unity, equity and political inclusion.
He urged political leaders to pay greater attention to the concerns of ordinary Nigerians and focus on practical solutions to the country’s economic challenges rather than allow debates over regional claims to the presidency to overshadow demands for effective leadership.

By Henry Umoru
ABUJA — President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, has expressed confidence that Akwa Ibom State will deliver the highest number of votes for President Bola Tinubu in the South-South region in the 2027 presidential election.
Akpabio made the declaration on Sunday during a special church service at the International Christian Worship Centre, Uyo, organised to dedicate the All Progressives Congress (APC) 2027 election campaigns to God.
The service had the theme, “We Are Well Able”.
In a statement by his Special Assistant on Media, Jackson Udom, the Senate President said Akwa Ibom indigenes, particularly APC members, must close ranks and present a united front to ensure the party’s success at the polls.
He said the state had a responsibility to reciprocate the support President Tinubu had given him by mobilising votes for the President.
According to him, the support of Tinubu contributed to his emergence as Senate President, making him the number three citizen in the country.
“Whether you like him or not, he is there today. The only way to thank Mr President for that support is to give him all our votes.
“From what I have seen here today, Akwa Ibom State will give Mr President the highest number of votes in the South-South region,” he said.
In an address titled, “One Family, One Destiny, One Akwa Ibom Under God”, Akpabio said while the people acknowledged God’s sovereignty over their individual and collective destinies, they must also uphold righteousness, justice and mercy.
He described Akwa Ibom as a Nigerian success story, attributing its progress to purposeful leadership, peace and development.
The Senate President said development should not be measured only by roads and buildings but also by the bridges built between people and the hope restored in their lives.
He urged political leaders and party members to sustain the state’s progress and ensure that its future achievements surpassed those already recorded.
On party unity, Akpabio cautioned against divisions between old and new members of the APC, insisting that all members should be treated equally.
“In the APC family, there should be no aborigines and no newcomers; no landlords and no tenants; no first-class members and no second-class members. There should be only one big family, united by a common purpose and a shared responsibility,” he said.
Using a biblical reference from John 14:2, he said there was room for everyone in the party, regardless of when they joined or their political standing.
He added that political ambitions should not override the welfare of the people, urging party members to conduct their campaigns in ways that respect human dignity.
Akpabio further said the development of Akwa Ibom was inseparable from the progress of Nigeria, stressing that the state could not remain indifferent to insecurity and hardship in other parts of the country.
“Nigeria is not merely the nation to which Akwa Ibom belongs; it is the larger destiny to which Akwa Ibom contributes,” he said.
Earlier, Governor Umo Eno thanked the people for their support during the last election and appealed for increased support for Tinubu, Akpabio, himself and other APC candidates in the 2027 elections.
Eno also pledged to continue serving the people with the fear of God if given another mandate.

items.content:
By Vincent Ujumadu
AWKA — Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has described the political coalition formed by parties in the state to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid as a battle for the soul of Nigeria and Ndigbo.
Soludo, who is the Anambra State Coordinator of Tinubu’s re-election campaign, spoke on Sunday during the inauguration of the presidential campaign structure at the International Convention Centre, Awka.
He said the coalition, which brings together political leaders across party lines, was formed primarily to secure Tinubu’s re-election, arguing that Ndigbo must actively participate in national politics rather than remain on the sidelines.
The governor described the forthcoming political contest as a clash between emotion and reason, expressing the view that emotional politics could only dominate temporarily before giving way to strategic calculations.
Addressing candidates contesting other elective positions on different party platforms, Soludo assured them of a level playing field, but stressed that the coalition’s common objective was to ensure Tinubu’s return to office.
He recalled that prominent Igbo political leaders, including Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe, Dr. Alex Ekwueme and Dr. Chuba Okadigbo, played significant roles in national politics, insisting that the South-East could not afford to isolate itself from developments at the centre.
According to him, the All Progressives Grand Alliance, APGA, recognised the importance of national political engagement and consequently resolved to align with the Federal Government.
He said APGA and the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, shared progressive ideals anchored on federalism and shared prosperity, adding that Tinubu understood the need for progressives to work together for national development.
Reflecting on his political journey, which he said began in 1980 under the principle of “one nation, one destiny”, Soludo urged Ndigbo to consider their long-term political and economic interests.
He argued that state revenues alone could not adequately finance major infrastructure such as federal rail lines and gas pipelines without strategic partnerships with the Federal Government.
The governor also noted that despite Tinubu securing about 5,000 votes in Anambra State during the 2023 presidential election, his administration had extended support to the state.
He expressed optimism that greater federal interventions could come if more people in Anambra supported the President in the next election.
Soludo called for an end to what he described as opposition and protest politics practised in the state since 2015, urging Ndigbo to embrace active participation in governance at the national level.
He further argued that a fragmented opposition would find it difficult to defeat an incumbent president, adding that his assessment was informed by his claimed record of correctly predicting presidential election outcomes in Nigeria since 1983.
On the future of presidential power rotation, Soludo said that following the completion of the South’s second term, power was expected to return to the North before rotating back to the South around 2039.
He urged Ndigbo to position themselves within the national political structure ahead of that period.
On political differences within Anambra, the governor said he maintained cordial personal and family relationships with political opponents, stressing that their disagreements were limited to political strategies and ideologies.
He also acknowledged federal fiscal interventions aimed at improving foreign exchange availability for importers, noting that although progress had been made, more work remained.
Outlining the campaign’s next steps, Soludo said political structures across the state would be streamlined before the end of the following week.
He maintained that elections were won at polling units and ward levels, urging supporters to remain focused despite criticism and verbal attacks on social media.
In his remarks, the APC state chairman, Senator Emma Anosike, said he had initially been sceptical about the meeting but expressed appreciation for what he described as the developmental strides recorded in Anambra.
Anosike said the coalition was intended to ensure the state’s direct participation in national governance.
He called for unity among party members, while noting that candidates contesting on different platforms were free to demonstrate their individual political strengths. He, however, urged all stakeholders to work together towards Tinubu’s re-election.
Also speaking, the APGA National Chairman, Barrister Sly Ezeokenwa, described the gathering as an unprecedented coalition united by the objective of securing Tinubu’s re-election.
He commended Soludo for facilitating the political alignment and pledged the readiness of APGA’s structures to implement campaign directives and mobilise support for the President.
The event attracted representatives of several political parties, including the PDP, Accord Party, APGA and APC, in what organisers described as a broad-based political alliance ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

Reflecting on the challenges
items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has criticised Cristiano Ronaldo’s fitness and commitment during their time together at Old Trafford, saying the Portuguese forward could “no longer deliver” at the highest level after leaving Juventus in 2021.
Ten Hag, who is now the technical director of Dutch club FC Twente, made the remarks during an interview with ESPN NL’s Goedemorgen Eredivisie on Sunday, reflecting on his strained relationship with the five-time Ballon d’Or winner.
Ronaldo returned to Manchester United from Juventus in 2021 and scored 27 goals in 54 appearances under Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Ten Hag.
However, his relationship with the Dutch manager deteriorated as he was frequently left out of the starting line-up.
United eventually terminated his contract in November 2022 following his explosive interview with Piers Morgan, in which he said he felt “betrayed” by Ten Hag and criticised the club’s hierarchy.
Reflecting on the challenges of managing the forward, Ten Hag said Ronaldo’s reluctance to put the team first created problems within the squad.
“The challenge is to get the team functioning, really as always. Every player is important in that and you need top players to be able to win. Every top team must embrace the top player, but the top player must work for the team. And that was simply the problem with Ronaldo.”
He acknowledged Ronaldo’s influence among his teammates but insisted the forward’s performances had declined.
“The players wanted to work for him and they looked up to him because let there be no misunderstanding about that. He is of course a tremendous player, one of the greats of all time. But that is also the reality over the last seven, eight years he simply can no longer deliver. From Juventus onwards it’s simply over.
“And that is actually the great gift of Real Madrid — they always know when to say goodbye to players at the right moment. They recognise when a player’s level is declining and they say goodbye at a moment when to the outside world, they still appear to be at their peak. But they can no longer actually deliver.”
Ronaldo was 36 when he returned to the Premier League, where his perceived inability to press opposition defenders attracted criticism from pundits and commentators.
Ten Hag, however, argued that the issue went beyond the forward’s age, claiming he was no longer willing to push himself physically during training.
“I naturally gave him a special status,” Ten Hag said. “I also went to him, I spoke to him prior to that job, I explained to him how we were going to play, what his role in that would be, what I expected of him, and what he could expect from me and from the team. But ultimately you also have to deliver yourself and he was no longer capable of pushing himself to the limit.
“As I just said, he could no longer bring himself to push through the pain, to give everything every single day and to train at his maximum in order to get fit. And if you’re not fit in the Premier League, Champions League, or with the Portuguese national team, well, then you simply have no chance.”
Asked about Ronaldo’s reputation for exceptional dedication to physical fitness, Ten Hag said the perception did not entirely reflect the situation during their time together.
“That’s not entirely true, but that is the image. And that is of course how he became so good. But ultimately he could no longer bring himself to do that.
“If you can’t do it, well, then the laws of the Premier League are merciless. Then you can no longer keep up, you are no longer able to get into the box. He can still finish a chance, you still see that. But to get into that power and intensity of the Premier League, that’s no longer possible. For that you need to be fit.”
The former United manager also dismissed suggestions that Ronaldo’s goals had changed his assessment of the forward’s performances, saying the player arrived late for pre-season preparations.
“That didn’t happen because he arrived very late due to personal circumstances. By then the season had already started and things went wrong straight away. He wasn’t fit and couldn’t deliver.”
Despite his criticism, Ten Hag praised Ronaldo’s contribution to football but maintained that he had to make decisions in the interest of Manchester United.
He also compared the forward’s approach to that of Argentina captain Lionel Messi, arguing that even the greatest players must prioritise their teams.
“No one is bigger than a club or a country,” Ten Hag said. “Not even Cristiano Ronaldo and not even Messi. In the end, the team always comes first. And so, as I just said, every top team must embrace the top player, but the top player must yield to the team. And if he no longer does that, well then it can’t be a success and it will never become a success. Then it simply stops.
“That is also what’s remarkable about Messi — how he worked at Argentina. That was fantastic to see. But that also required a big investment from Messi himself. Ultimately everyone went along with it and everyone worked for him but he of course gave an enormous amount back.”
Ten Hag’s latest comments come after Ronaldo was suspended for 30 days by the Portuguese Football Federation following his walkout on the national team during the October international break. He was also fined €255 but has indicated his willingness to represent Portugal again.
The Dutchman also addressed his departure from Manchester United, dismissing suggestions of bitterness towards the club.
Asked whether restrictions surrounding his exit had prevented him from speaking publicly for two years, Ten Hag said:
“I was allowed to give interviews, but not to damage the club. But I wouldn’t have done that anyway — that goes without saying.
“United gave me so much and I worked there with such great pleasure, with the people. [We] simply had a fantastic relationship, built fantastic connections. And the fans, such fantastic moments in those FA Cup finals, League Cup, [they] always supported. So there’s no bitterness.”
Vanguard News

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
…Calls for Measurable Results for Govt Spending, Says Revenue Gains Must Translate into Better Lives for Nigerians
The Chairman of the Alliance for Economic Research and Ethics, Dele Kelvin Oye, has called on the Federal and state governments to ensure that increased public revenues translate into better living conditions for Nigerians, noting that Nigeria’s fiscal positions have improved but yet to produce a level of citizen satisfaction that reflects the gains.
Oye said governments must move beyond revenue generation and focus on delivering measurable improvements in public services, infrastructure and economic opportunities.
He made the call while commenting on the revised 2026 State Performance Index (pSPI) by Phillips Consulting, which showed that despite improved fiscal conditions across parts of the federation, citizens’ experience of government performance remained only marginally positive.
The report recorded a national composite citizen satisfaction score of 3.01 out of five, barely above the neutral midpoint of 3.00.
Oye said the findings underscored the need for governments to demonstrate how increased revenues were improving the lives of citizens, rather than relying on budget figures and financial performance indicators.
He noted that higher revenues should create room for governments to repair roads, improve water systems, equip health facilities, support businesses and strengthen education, adding that revenue was only a resource for development, not development itself.
According to the report, finding employment recorded the lowest citizen rating at 2.31, placing it in the critical category. Clean water scored 2.67, government support for businesses 2.71, security 2.84, while law-enforcement conduct recorded 2.85.
Oye said the figures reflected the everyday challenges confronting Nigerians and highlighted the gap between fiscal performance and the quality of public services.
He cautioned that higher revenue could fail to produce meaningful development where funds were poorly allocated, released late, lost through weak procurement or spent on projects that were never completed or maintained.
He said government budgets should therefore be assessed not only by the amount allocated or spent, but by the results achieved and the number of citizens who benefited.
Oye called for the inclusion of measurable service-delivery outcomes in the assessment of government performance, including whether projects were completed on time and within budget, whether public facilities were functional and whether citizens experienced improvements after delivery.
He also urged governments to publish transparent information on public spending, procurement, project completion and service outcomes to enable citizens to monitor how public funds were being used.
The Alliance for Ethics chairman proposed that every state, the Federal Capital Territory and local government publish a 90-day public delivery plan focused on no more than three of its weakest service areas.
He said the plans should contain clear targets, timelines, funding arrangements and publicly accessible monitoring systems, with governments required to explain missed milestones and publish corrective measures.
Oye stressed that the proposed 90-day plans should serve as the first phase of a longer-term delivery programme, rather than promises to resolve complex challenges such as unemployment, insecurity or water access within three months.
He said the objective was to ensure that citizens could track public funds from allocation to project completion and determine whether the resulting services were improving their lives.
Oye further called for stronger coordination among the Federal, state and local governments, noting that challenges such as employment, public safety, water, sanitation and primary healthcare required cooperation across the different tiers of government.
He said the Federal Government should provide a stable national economic environment and transparent funding arrangements, while state and local governments must ensure that resources within their control were efficiently managed and directed towards the needs of citizens.
Oye maintained that stronger fiscal conditions offered governments an opportunity to improve public welfare, but insisted that the opportunity must be matched by transparency, accountability and effective use of public resources.
He said the ultimate test of government performance was not the size of its revenue or budget, but the quality of life that public spending made possible for Nigerians.
According to him, “Nigeria is at a crucial point in its public-finance journey. State governments have recently received and reported higher nominal revenues. That should create room to repair roads, improve water systems, equip health facilities, support enterprise and strengthen education. But revenue is not development; it is only the resource from which development may be built.
“The revised 2026 pcl. State Performance Index (pSPI) puts this challenge in clear view. It records stronger fiscal conditions across parts of the federation, aided by larger Federation Account distributions, higher VAT receipts, exchange-rate effects and other national macroeconomic adjustments. Yet the report’s 2026 citizen survey records a national composite score of only 3.01 out of 5, just above its neutral midpoint of 3.00.
“The conclusion should be sober. The figure does not prove that public services have not improved at all. It does show that stronger fiscal conditions have not yet translated into a level of citizen experience that commands broad confidence. Under the report’s own scale, satisfaction only marginally outweighs dissatisfaction.”
He added, “Alliance for Ethics will treat the pSPI as a starting point for accountability, not a final judgment on any state. We will ask whether governments publish delivery compacts, make data usable, manage fiscal risks, complete projects, maintain public assets and respond to the services citizens rate most weakly.
“Citizens, journalists, civil society and businesses should keep asking five questions: What exactly changed? Where is the independent evidence? Who benefited and who was left out? What did it cost, including future debt? Can the public inspect the result without an appointment, a press pass or special access?
“Nigeria does not lack revenue headlines, plans or project announcements. What it needs is a more rigorous public ethic: money must be allocated well, released on time, spent transparently, converted into functioning services and measured by the change it produces in people’s lives.
“The pSPI’s score of 3.01 is not a reason for despair. It is a reason for discipline. Higher nominal receipts create an opportunity; only effective utilisation and measurable outcomes create development. A government should be judged not only by the size of its budget, but by the quality of life its budget makes possible.”
The post Oye laments rising hardship, poverty despite higher revenue for FG, States appeared first on Vanguard News.

By Henry Umoru
ABUJA- THE Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin, APC, Kano North has expressed optimism that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu will emerge victorious in the January 16, 2027, presidential election, citing assessments by political analysts and the prevailing political situation in the country.
Senator Barau spoke at the weekend during the inauguration of campaign committees for Dawakin Tofa, Tofa and Rimin Gado Local Government Areas of Kano State, where he charged party members to work collectively towards securing victory for all candidates of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the forthcoming general elections.
In a statement signed on Sunday by his Special Adviser, Media and Publicity, Ismail Mudashir, the Deputy President of the Senate said the foundation laid by President Tinubu during his first term would, by the grace of Allah, yield the desired results in his second term.
Barau Jibrin who expressed appreciation to party leaders, elected representatives, local government chairmen, Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf and other stakeholders for their support and commitment to the APC, assured them that the unity and cooperation currently enjoyed by the party would be sustained.
“Based on the assessments of political analysts and the current state of Nigerian politics, all indications suggest that, by Allah’s grace, Bola Ahmed Tinubu will win the presidential election,” he said.
He noted that Kano, being one of the largest states in the country and second only to Lagos in terms of the latest registered voters, deserved greater attention and opportunities from the Federal Government.
According to him, the Governor’s decision to lead the people from the New Nigeria People’s Party (NNPP) to the APC was a strategic move that have enhanced Kano’s political relevance and improved its access to developmental opportunities.
The Deputy President of the Senate expressed confidence that the political unity achieved in Kano would translate into tangible benefits for the people, particularly with the alignment of councillors, local government chairmen, state legislators, members of the National Assembly and the Governor under the APC.
He added that the coming elections would usher in a new phase of political and developmental activities, with elected representatives expected to contribute meaningfully to the development of their respective constituencies.
Senator Barau explained that the campaign committees were carefully constituted to accommodate party leaders, members of the party’s executive committees, former and serving legislators, councillors, local government chairmen, new party members and respected elders.
He urged members of the committees to take their responsibilities seriously and mobilise effectively for the APC ahead of the elections.
“What is required of you is to play your part actively in securing victory. Mobilise, campaign and ensure that all APC candidates emerge victoriously from top to bottom. May Allah grant us success and enable us to achieve our goals,” he said.
ENDS

items.title: AB InBev sets aside $30 mn for Telangana dues

items.content: Mumbai: Anheuser-Busch InBev, the world's largest brewer, has set aside $30 million against outstanding payments from the Telangana government, highlighting the financial risks of operating in India's state-controlled alcohol market, where delayed payments and restrictions on price increases are squeezing brewers.The disclosure comes amid wider industry concerns over nearly $400 million Telangana owes to alcohol companies in dues. Industry groups have accused the state of breaching accounting rules over the outstanding payments.Also read: Govt to meet liquor firms as domestic giants join foreign peers in Scotch disputeUnder the state's system, liquor companies supply products to government-run depots, which then distribute them to retailers, leaving manufacturers dependent on the government for payments.Telangana is one of India's biggest beer-consuming states by volume. AB InBev chief financial officer Bernardo Novick said the company's total receivables from Telangana had remained relatively stable during the year, but some payments had been outstanding for an extended period."We decided to recognise this provision of $30 million," Novick said during the company's earnings call, adding that the brewer was making its best efforts to recover the outstanding amount and protect shareholders.The company does not expect further meaningful one-off provisions from the situation, Novick said, while cautioning that circumstances could change.The problem extends beyond AB InBev. United Breweries, which controls about half of India's beer market, had temporarily halted supplies to Telangana Beverages Corporation about a year ago because of operating losses and overdue payments. The brewer had said selling each beer at a loss had made continued operations in the state unsustainable, while substantial delays in payments for supplies to the state corporation had further complicated the situation.Last week, United Breweries managing director Vivek Gupta said the company's business in Telangana had remained flat and it had lost some market share as a competitor continued to spend.

items.content:
By Luminous Jannamike
ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has challenged President Bola Tinubu to account for his failure to deliver on his 2023 electricity pledge, insisting that he should not seek re-election without fulfilling the promise.
The council said Nigerians had not forgotten Tinubu’s categorical declaration during the 2023 presidential campaign that they should not vote for him for a second term if he failed to deliver electricity, dismissing attempts by the APC to reinterpret his words as an afterthought.
In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC was reacting to comments by Dele Alake, spokesperson of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, defending the President’s electricity record.
“Don’t vote for me for second term if I fail to deliver electricity,” the President had told Nigerians during the 2023 campaign.
The opposition campaign council argued that more than three years after the pledge, Nigerians were still grappling with persistent power outages, repeated national grid collapses and inadequate electricity supply.
It accused the Tinubu administration of increasing the financial burden on consumers through higher electricity bills, discriminatory tariff classifications and continued estimated billing, despite the much-publicised Presidential Metering Initiative.
The council also said businesses, including hotels and other hospitality facilities, had resorted to rationing electricity by switching off power for guests during daytime hours to reduce operating costs.
Dismissing the administration’s reliance on the Electricity Act and bond programmes to defend its record, the ADC-PCC insisted that policy documents and financial instruments could not substitute for actual electricity supply.
“An Act is not electricity. A bond prospectus does not power homes and factories. Nigerians cannot eat statutes. What Nigerians need is electricity that works, not another round of explanations and publicity,” the council said.
It further accused the administration of imposing higher tariffs without ensuring reliable supply, leaving households, manufacturers and small businesses to contend with rising operating costs.
The ADC-PCC also questioned the implementation of the Presidential Metering Initiative, alleging that electricity distribution companies continued to impose estimated bills on consumers.
“The President’s own condition for seeking a second term was straightforward: deliver electricity or do not ask Nigerians for another mandate,” the council maintained.
It urged the APC to address the President’s 2023 commitment directly, rather than attempt to dilute his words, warning that the administration’s electricity record would be a major issue as Nigerians prepare to decide whether to renew Tinubu’s mandate in the January 16, 2027 election.
