items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
By Steve Oko & Ugochukwu Alaribe
UMUAHIA – Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has cautioned supporters of the Labour Party against taking the law into their hands or interfering with the campaign activities of rival political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The governor warned that no political affiliation would shield anyone from arrest for disrupting the lawful activities of opposition parties, stressing that political competition must be conducted within the ambit of the law.
Otti spoke on Sunday in Umuahia while formally flagging off the Labour Party’s 2027 campaign in the state, where he declared that his administration would not tolerate political intolerance or the denial of opponents’ democratic rights.
He said opposition parties were free to use public facilities, including stadiums, provided they complied with established procedures, obtained necessary approvals and paid the stipulated fees.
Reiterating his position, the governor said security agencies had been instructed to ensure that no political group was prevented from holding legitimate rallies or other campaign activities.
“I have since given a public directive, and I am repeating it here, that opposition parties should not be restricted from the use of public facilities, including the stadium, once they apply and obtain the necessary approvals,” Otti said.
In a strong message to party loyalists, he warned against assuming that membership of the ruling party conferred immunity for acts capable of undermining the democratic process.
“You do not have my mandate to attack people or to stop people from campaigning.
“Security agencies have been mandated to arrest and deal decisively with anyone who attempts to obstruct any political group from holding their legitimate activities, even if they are Labour Party members. I hope I am heard clearly,” he said.
Beyond the conduct of campaigns, Otti challenged opposition parties to raise the quality of political debate by offering alternative policy directions rather than relying on personal attacks or recycling issues he said had been addressed by his administration.
According to him, the political conversation in Abia should now be centred on development priorities and the next phase of governance rather than basic issues such as salaries, pensions, roads and environmental sanitation.
“Do not forget that in Abia we have gone past the era of campaigning on the payment of salaries and pensions, construction of roads or urban sanitation.
“The hygiene issues have been dealt with. If you are unable to raise your campaign pitch to the development realities of our state, you will definitely struggle to convince any informed voter,” the governor said.
He urged political opponents to interrogate available performance data before making claims about the state, pointing to Abia’s ratings in the Citizen Satisfaction Index, State Performance Index and Fiscal Performance Ranking by governance-monitoring organisations.
“You should go and do your research first before coming out to open your mouth, because there are data everywhere to show what has been achieved. Evidently, the world knows that Abia is on the right track,” Otti said.
The governor also argued that the experiences of Abians within and outside the country had lent credibility to external assessments of the state’s development trajectory, adding that multilateral institutions had opened development assistance opportunities for Abia.
“It would therefore be unthinkable that anyone will ever be allowed to return us to the old era of irresponsibility and misery,” he declared.
Otti, who expressed appreciation to residents for their turnout at the campaign flag-off, called on party supporters to intensify grassroots mobilisation and take the message of the party to communities across the state.
“This is your project, and as you return to the communities, knock on every door and remind our people that we still have a job to complete. Invite them to join the campaign so that together we can conclude the journey that began 12 years ago in faith and optimism,” he added.
Highlight of the event was the presentation of the party flag to national and state house of assembly candidates of Labour Party for the 2027 polls.
The event was massively attended by party members including the candidates for the various elections and their supporters who were competing for recognition as they chanted solidarity songs for their various candidates.

items.content:
Kylian Mbappe moved on from a tumultuous week by scoring a penalty to help Real Madrid win 3-0 at Racing Santander on Sunday.
The French forward narrowly lost out on the Ballon d’Or to Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane on Monday and then had to apologise after a social media storm following a video in which he joked about former Chinese leader Mao Zedong.
Real Madrid’s match, along with other Spanish fixtures this weekend, was not broadcast by Chinese state television because of the fallout.
Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomande were also on target to keep third-place Madrid within three points of leaders Barcelona, who thrashed Alaves 6-1 on Saturday.
Jose Mourinho’s side have won six straight games across all competitions and are a point behind city rivals Atletico Madrid, who beat Levante 2-0.
Mbappe won a soft penalty as he went down under little pressure from Matteo Prati, smashing it home to put Madrid ahead at the Sardinero stadium in the 11th minute.
Madrid had control of the game and a fine pass from Arda Guler sent Bellingham through on goal for the second.
The England international knocked the ball past the goalkeeper and rolled home for his 50th goal since joining Madrid in 2023.
Guler spurned a good opportunity for the third after being set up by Mbappe, before Madrid’s record signing Diomande lashed home from the edge of the box.
The hosts started the second half well, pushing Madrid back, much to the chagrin of Mourinho, who yelled at his players.
Madrid regained their control and racked up several more chances, with Mbappe hitting the post and Bellingham denied by Racing goalkeeper Julen Agirrezabala.
Racing won a penalty after Madrid’s Aurelien Tchouameni handled in the box, but the award was cancelled after a VAR review.
Bellingham had a second goal ruled out in stoppage time after he strayed offside before finding the net and Endrick bent an effort narrowly wide from distance.
Hosts Racing, 16th, back in La Liga for the first time in 14 seasons, fell to their first home defeat of the campaign.
Earlier Sevilla, sixth, suffered a 3-1 loss at Getafe, who moved into mid-table.
Later Sunday Athletic Bilbao host Real Sociedad in a Basque derby and Valencia visit Elche.

items.content:
….as traditional rulers, religious leaders, APC stakeholders endorse Tinubu, Nwifuru, others
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki
The Minister of Works Senator David Umahi has said that as a Lion of South East, he’s strongly behind President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for reelection in 2027 due to his indileable achievements in South East zone and across the country.
Umahi while speaking at the All Progressives Congress (APC) Town Hall meeting at Ecumenical Centre Abakaliki, Ebonyi State said that Tinubu is a blessing to South East zone and shoukd be supported for second term.
The town hall meeting was organized the office of the Senior Special Assistant to the President Southeast on Community Engagement Barr. Chioma Nweze to mobilize support for the President Tinubu, governor and other APC candidates in forthcoming election.
The former Senator representing Ebonyi Central Sen. Julius Ali Ucha moved a motion adopting APC, President Tinubu for reelection, governor Francis Nwifuru and all APC candidates in 2027 general elections.
The motion was seconded by Senator who represented Ebonyi North Sen. Anthony Agbo while Senator Umahi put the motion in voice votes and was generally endorsed.
Those who spoke at the meeting, include, Traditional rulers Ezeogo Charles Nkpume, and Ezeogo Sunday Oketa, Bishop Onyeuwa Omar and CAN Chairman Stan Nwokolo, Pastor Eunice Oyeyemi of Divine Mandate Pastors and Former Deputy of Ebonyi State Prof. Chigozie Ogbu.
Addressing the party faithful, Umahi charged the traditional rulers and religious leaders to throw full support to President Tinubu and should not sit on the fence over regional sentiments.
The Minister urged the leaders of various clans, villages, communities and local government areas to talk to their brothers contesting against the zoning arrangement already in place in the state and should the reelection of Governor Francis Nwifuru.
“I want to tell our religious leaders and Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), do not stay on the fence. I know when I was struggling to be Governor, CAN took a descion and said justice must prevail. CAN don’t keep quiet, let us toe the path that must sustain our freedom.
“There is no way an Igbo man after staying for 60 years, will want to be President for four years. There is nobody that can accept that. The North has not accepted to be President for four years
“Somebody was telling me that Atiku”s son bought buses and donated to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and said this is personal donation.
“Igbo man needs wisdom, not sentiments. Igbo man should not allow people to be dishing hate speeches in the social media on their behalf. Today, our people in Commerce, we clear our goods with ease. Today our roads are being revived in the path of economic activities.
“Today, we can boldly say we have been integrated. The last time there were choosing service chiefs, it was Naval Chief. This time, it is Chief of Air Staff , Minister of Works, otter Ministers, SSAs, what else? When I say South East have been fully integrated and included, I mean it.
“My mouth will not shut up because I am telling our people for a reference for tomorrow. We are supporting President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to finish his remaining four years so that the South East would have strategically supported another region. So that when it is our turn, we will not get this thing by hate speeches, they will not give to us by sentiments It is strategic leaders of South East say this, you will now insult them.
“You insult anybody that is not supporting Peter Obi. Anybody that is not supporting Peter Obi, is a saboteur, you insult the person. Who is Peter Obi better than, who is he better than? Is he better than Sam Egwu? Is he better than Elias Mbam,? Is he better than the lion of South East myself? Is he better than Anyim Pius? Whom is he better than?
“So, I don’t want us to be deceiving ourselves. Traditional fathers, do not stay on the fence, religious leaders, do not stay on the fence. Our people in the North do not, our people in the South West, they do not. We should support President Tinubu for his love for South East and infrastructural development in the zone” he stated.

By John Alechenu ABUJA-
Governor Alex Otti has unveiled his 2027 re-election manifesto titled ‘The New Abia: From Rescue to Consolidation’, saying he needs four more years to institutionalise transparency and kill mediocrity in the state.
Otti unveiled the manifesto on Saturday during his re-election campaign flag-off at the Umuahia Township Stadium, an event that brought Umuahia to a standstill.
This was contained in a statement signed by the National Publicity Secretary of the Labour Party, LP, Ken Asogwa in Abuja, on Sunday.
According to Asogwa, thousands of Labour Party supporters from the 17 Local Government Areas stormed the venue with dance troupes and support groups in a carnival-like atmosphere.
The Governor said his administration ended years of man-made hardship and siege after his attempts to rescue Abia in 2015 and 2019 failed, until victory in 2023.
“We ended the era of political profiteers. We defied intimidation to liberate Abia. Never shall we go back to the era of irresponsibility. Nothing will make us go back to Egypt,” he declared.
He recalled how properties were demolished in the past on account of political affiliations, declaring: “Never again will anyone’s fence be pulled down on account of political choices. I declare Abia free.”
Otti said the next phase is to protect the gains of 2023 with enduring institutional safeguards to prevent the state from relapsing into its past.
He said, “The only battle worth fighting is the one geared towards leaving Abia better than I met it. I appeal to you to join me in fighting that battle in the next four years to consolidate on our records of performance.
“We need the next four years to institutionalise transparency in Abia and ensure that the last vestiges of mediocrity in the state are totally eradicated.”
According to him, the manifesto contains step-by-step plans on how his government will consolidate on successes of the past three and a half years.
He listed about 400 road projects covering over 1,000 kilometres, including Port Harcourt Road in Aba, Oboha Road, Ohanku Road and Arochukwu Road which were hitherto considered impossible.
“We have transformed primary healthcare. We have employed over 9,000 teachers and built smart schools in almost all enclaves. We have invested billions in revitalising Abia State University, Uturu, and Ogbonnaya Onu Polytechnic, Aba,” he said.
“We have invested heavily in reviving ailing industries in Aba, supported SMEs and made significant investments to ensure food sufficiency.”
“Above all, I have restored the dignity of Abians,” Otti added, urging voters to vote Labour Party all the way.
In a demonstration of political tolerance, he directed all state functionaries to make public facilities available to any political party or candidate who pays requisite fees and observes regulations, and wished opponents well.

items.content:
The recent conference on Pakistan at Harvard University, themed "From Potential to Performance", has generated considerable debate in Pakistan, partly because of the deep pessimism expressed by two highly acclaimed economists about the country's economic performance compared with its peers.
One of the panellists, Nobel laureate Professor Acemoglu, described Pakistan's economy as having been "comatose" for the past three decades. He attributed this to weak institutions, inadequate investment in education and low tax collection. Unless these serious political economy failures are recognised and addressed, reversing the downward trajectory will be extremely difficult. With the world now being transformed by artificial intelligence (AI), he warned that Pakistan appears largely unprepared, lacking the digital infrastructure needed to keep pace and risking further marginalisation.
Another panellist, Professor Atif Mian, argued that Pakistan lacked the strategic vision needed to tackle fundamental problems, including elite capture, the failure to achieve inclusive growth and insufficient efforts to establish peace within the country. He particularly noted that although Pakistan could address its energy crisis by electrifying its transport sector, it had been unable to do so because it could not confront powerful pressure groups.
Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, who also participated in the panel, acknowledged that these challenges were well understood but argued that political economy constraints had repeatedly delayed difficult decisions and their implementation. However, he maintained that the situation was changing for the better, as decisions previously postponed were now being taken and implemented. In particular, he cited long-stalled tariff reforms, the taxation of agricultural income by provincial governments and the privatisation of state-owned enterprises.
The question is whether these developments represent a genuine shift in Pakistan's political economy, with reforms overcoming resistance from powerful interest groups, or whether the country remains on the downward trajectory described by the two economists. Let us first examine three areas where reforms have been blocked for decades.
The first is the powerful industrial lobby, which has long feared that opening the economy before addressing fundamental issues such as energy costs, interest rates, taxation, and law and order could seriously damage domestic manufacturing. With the launch of the five-year National Tariff Policy, the government has indeed embarked on a radical programme of trade liberalisation and making the industry competitive. The reforms are now in their second year of implementation and, with the notable exception of the automotive sector, have faced less resistance from other industrial sectors than many had anticipated. Furthermore, the predicted collapse of domestic industry and a big fall in import-related revenue have not materialised, while several indicators point towards a more positive outcome.
The second major lobby comprises those opposing the expansion of the tax net to previously undertaxed sectors, particularly agricultural income and the retail and wholesale sectors. Here, the picture is mixed. Although provincial governments have enacted legislation to tax agricultural income, it remains unclear whether these measures will deliver the intended results. The government's experience with the retail sector shows that legislation and concessions alone cannot achieve the desired outcomes without the political will to confront resistance from powerful interest groups. Nevertheless, after remaining below 10% for almost a decade, the tax-to-GDP ratio rose from 8.8% in FY2024 to 10.3% in FY2025. This 1.5-percentage-point increase is a significant achievement.
Another major source of resistance has been trade unions and organised labour, which have opposed the privatisation of state-owned enterprises for decades. However, the government has begun to break this longstanding stalemate through the sale of Pakistan International Airlines and the closure of Utility Stores Corporation. It is now proceeding with a broader programme involving 27 state-owned enterprises. Whether this momentum can be sustained remains to be seen, but the willingness to take decisions previously considered politically difficult is an encouraging development.
Regarding Professor Acemoglu's assertion that Pakistan is poorly prepared for the AI revolution, the finance minister has rightly pointed out that the country has already taken important steps in this direction. Pakistan approved its National AI Policy in 2025, while its IT exports have reached $4.6 billion and are growing at around 20% annually. The government plans to upskill its IT workforce, already the world's third largest in terms of outsourcing talent, and invest $1 billion in AI by 2030. The World Bank also recognises Pakistan as one of the leading hosts of data centres in the MENAP region, alongside Saudi Arabia and the UAE. Its initiatives in blockchain technology and the regulation of digital assets, including cryptocurrencies, further demonstrate that Pakistan is beginning to position itself to benefit from emerging technologies.
As for Professor Mian's observation that Pakistan has failed to make full use of its solar potential, it is true that the country has moved relatively slowly towards the electrification of transport, partly because powerful automobile lobbies have sought to slow the transition. However, the picture is quite different when it comes to solar energy. Pakistan has emerged as one of the more successful developing countries in adopting solar power, with installed solar capacity estimated at around 8,000 MW. It is now among the countries where renewable energy has overtaken fossil fuels in electricity generation.
The overall picture is mixed, but there are reasons for cautious optimism. Recent initiatives in tariff liberalisation, taxation, privatisation, solar energy, digitalisation and AI suggest that Pakistan may finally be beginning to turn a corner. But after decades of economic underperformance, incremental change will not be enough. The pace of reform must accelerate, and difficult decisions must no longer be postponed to accommodate entrenched interests.
The real test is whether these reforms can be implemented consistently, withstand political and institutional resistance, and translate into higher productivity, greater investment, stronger exports and sustained economic growth. Pakistan does not suffer from a shortage of ideas, diagnoses or policy prescriptions. Its real challenge is to overcome the resistance to change and turn sound policies into action. The time for promises and plans is over; what Pakistan needs now is execution.
The writer is a Senior Fellow at PIDE and has previously served as Pakistan's ambassador and permanent representative to the World Trade Organisation

items.author: SHAMSUL ISLAM KHAN
items.content:
Every year, as winter approaches, Lahore and other cities across Punjab are engulfed by hazardous smog, posing serious risks to public health, disrupting daily life and reducing visibility. Environmental experts frequently identify crop-residue burning, particularly rice-stubble burning in Punjab and across the border in India, as a major contributor to seasonal air pollution.
However, smog also results from vehicle emissions, industrial smoke, brick kilns, construction dust and other pollutants. Weather conditions, including low wind speeds and temperature inversions, further trap pollutants close to the ground. Addressing this recurring crisis requires scientific assessment of pollution sources, stricter emissions controls, cleaner agricultural practices and coordinated regional action.
Pakistan's smog problem also exposes a wider economic failure: agricultural waste that could generate income is often treated as a nuisance. According to a UNDP report on rural revitalisation in China, more than 647 million tonnes of crop straw were recycled in 2021, achieving a utilisation rate of nearly 90%. This demonstrates the potential of converting agricultural residues into valuable economic resources.
Rice straw can be used for animal feed, bio-fertilisers, industrial raw materials and mushroom cultivation. Rice bran can be used for bran edible oil, husk can support biomass co-generation energy, ash, silica, blocks and other industrial applications. Research and investment can also explore rice straw-based boards, packaging materials, yarn and other products.
In Pakistan, however, rice straw is frequently burnt in fields, husk accumulates at rice mills, and valuable byproducts remain underutilised. At a time when the country urgently needs higher exports, rural employment, affordable energy and import substitution, this represents a substantial missed opportunity.
Beyond subsidies and penalties
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz has launched a subsidy under the Punjab Clean Air Programme, offering rice growers Rs5,000 per acre, subject to a maximum of Rs25,000 per farmer, to discourage stubble burning. The initiative provides immediate assistance, but financial incentives alone cannot establish a permanent solution. Similarly, imposing fines on farmers and FIRs without providing practical and economically viable alternatives are unlikely to eliminate the problem sustainably. Pakistan needs to transform stubble management from a pollution-control exercise into a commercially viable agricultural industry.
Waste-to-Wealth Company
The Punjab government should establish an Agricultural Waste-to-Wealth Company to develop an integrated system for collecting, processing and marketing agricultural residues, beginning with rice straw and husk. Its principal responsibilities should include:
1-Rice-straw collection network: Establish collection centres in major rice-producing districts and provide balers, shredders and transportation through cooperatives and private contractors. Farmers should receive commercially viable prices for usable straw, creating a financial incentive to stop burning it. Collection operations must be organised around the short interval between rice harvesting and the planting of the next crop. Timely removal is essential if farmers are to adopt alternative practices.
2-Industrial utilisation and value addition: Encourage rice mills to utilise paddy husk for biomass power generation and industrial heat where economically feasible. Develop composting and organic-fertiliser facilities, and promote rice straw-based boards, packaging materials and other suitable manufactured products. Research institutions and businesses should investigate advanced applications, including biofuels and cellulose-based products. Where technically and commercially viable, cellulose extracted from rice straw could provide raw material for industrial applications, potentially including textile fibres and yarn. The objective should be to develop multiple uses for agricultural residues rather than depend on a single technology or market.
3-Private-sector investment: Invite domestic and foreign investors' joint ventures to establish agricultural waste processing facilities in rice-producing regions. The government should offer transparent, time-bound incentives linked to actual production, investment and verified residue utilisation. Long-term supply agreements between farmers, collection companies, rice mills and industrial consumers would help establish reliable supply chains and reduce commercial uncertainty.
4-Farmer participation and mechanisation: Farmers must be partners in the proposed system, not merely the targets of enforcement. Machinery for chopping, collecting, baling and transporting straw should be made accessible through service providers, cooperatives and affordable financing. Financial institutions, including Zarai Taraqiati Bank Limited and Apna Kissan Bank, could support eligible investments in agricultural machinery, collection centres, storage facilities and residue-processing projects. The government should aid coordination among agricultural departments, rice mills, research institutions and trade associations to ensure that collection and processing systems operate efficiently.
From agricultural waste to economic value
An integrated waste-to-wealth system could deliver several benefits simultaneously. These include reducing open-field burning and helping mitigate seasonal air pollution, generating additional income for rice farmers, creating rural employment and new businesses, supplying raw materials to energy and manufacturing industries, encouraging investment in agricultural technology, reducing waste and supporting import substitution, and developing new products with potential for domestic sales and exports.
However, success will depend on suitable technology, transport costs, reliable buyers and the economics of individual applications. Not all rice straw can be collected or processed profitably. Local feasibility studies and pilot projects should therefore precede large-scale investment. Punjab and Sindh should adapt their approaches to local agricultural conditions, infrastructure and industrial demand. The objective should be to establish commercially sustainable systems rather than create permanent dependence on subsidies.
Role of trade associations
Trade associations also have a responsibility beyond lobbying for their members' immediate demands. They should help develop the research, technology and industrial capabilities needed to make entire sectors more competitive. Pakistan's rice industry offers an opportunity to build clusters around agricultural residues, including straw, husk, bran and other byproducts. Such industries could diversify revenue streams, strengthen rural economies and improve the sector's overall competitiveness. After 79 years of independence, Pakistan needs less ceremonial and more economic leadership: laboratories instead of excessive ceremony, technology instead of trophy sales, and measurable results instead of publicity.
Stubble management must evolve from a policy focused primarily on controlling burning into a comprehensive resource-recovery industry. The government should facilitate investment, establish collection infrastructure, support research and create a regulatory environment in which agricultural waste becomes a commercially valuable resource. Farmers should earn from residues that currently impose disposal costs, while businesses should have incentives to convert them into marketable products. Pakistan's next rice revolution should not be measured solely by how much rice the country grows or exports, but by how much additional value it creates from every ton, and how little it wastes.
The writer is a former vice president of Karachi Chamber of Commerce & Industry and former board member of REAP

items.content:
Only 220 new shopkeepers have joined the tax net under the government’s simplified registration scheme for retailers, despite the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) identifying 3.6 million potential non-filers in the retail sector.
According to sources, just 1,750 shopkeepers have availed the scheme so far.
Only 1,750 retailers have filed tax returns under its new fixed tax scheme, with just 220 of them being new filers.
The scheme was introduced to widen the tax base and help the government collect Rs. 50 billion from the retail sector.
Fines and Shop Sealing for Non-Filers
To bring more retailers into the net, the FBR plans to geo-tag markets across the country, building on its nationwide mapping of markets and shops.
Shopkeepers who fail to register face escalating penalties. Non-filers could be fined Rs. 10,000 in the first month, Rs. 25,000 in the second month, and Rs. 50,000 in the third month. Authorities also have the power to seal the shops of retailers who stay outside the tax net.
The slow uptake follows earlier figures showing only 91 new retailers had joined the scheme in early October.
Revenue Shortfall Adds Pressure
The weak response comes as the FBR struggles to meet its revenue targets. The tax authority collected Rs. 975 billion in the first 30 days of October against a monthly target of Rs. 1,132 billion, a shortfall of Rs. 157 billion.
For the first four months of the current fiscal year (July to October), the FBR collected Rs. 4,058.5 billion against a target of Rs. 4,185 billion, leaving a gap of Rs. 126.5 billion.
Meanwhile, the deadline for filing income tax returns was extended twice this year. By October, the FBR had received 7.6 million income tax returns.

Saudi Arabia is encouraging companies in the Kingdom to hire more Pakistani workers, according to the chairman of a Pakistani overseas recruitment firm.
Issam Baig, chairman of Jan Mohammad & Sons, said executives of several major Saudi companies told him during recent visits to Riyadh and Jeddah that Saudi authorities had asked them to take on more Pakistanis.
“They have told us that they have been told and pushed by Riyadh and their ministries to accommodate more Pakistanis,” Baig told Arab News.
Three to Four Big Companies
Baig said three to four major Saudi companies had conveyed the same message. He called it a positive sign for bilateral ties and for job seekers in Pakistan.
He added that Pakistan must send skilled workers to keep that trust. “We should uphold that trust by sending them quality manpower,” he said.
Saudi Arabia Leads Overseas Jobs
Saudi Arabia remains the top destination for Pakistani workers. Data from the Bureau of Emigration and Overseas Employment (BE&OE) shows that more than 1.21 million of the 1.87 million Pakistanis who registered for jobs abroad between January 2024 and September 2026 went to the Kingdom. That is nearly 65 percent.
Registrations for Saudi Arabia rose from 426,951 in 2023 to 452,648 in 2024 and 530,437 in 2025. In the first nine months of 2026, 258,178 workers registered.
A senior BE&OE official said the government is studying developments in the Middle East to understand recent employment trends and prepare future projections.
Gulf countries employ millions of Pakistanis and are a major source of foreign currency. Pakistan received a record $41.6 billion in remittances in FY26.
Earlier this year, officials also said getting jobs in Saudi Arabia would get easier for Pakistanis.

items.author: ProPK Staff
items.content:
President Asif Ali Zardari has approved the Tamgha-e-Shujaat (Medal of Bravery) for Shaheed Furqan Ali, the Karachi firefighter who lost his life trying to save people trapped in the Gul Plaza fire.
The award follows efforts by Karachi Mayor Barrister Murtaza Wahab to secure national recognition for the firefighter’s courage and service.
Who Was Furqan Ali
Furqan, 36, was posted at the Nazimabad Fire Station and had served in the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) Fire Department since 2018. He joined the department on the deceased quota after his father, also a firefighter, passed away while in service.
He had married about a year and a half ago and had a child.
Killed Under the Debris
Furqan was part of the team battling the blaze at Gul Plaza on Karachi’s M.A. Jinnah Road, which broke out on the night of January 17, 2026, and burned for around 36 hours before it was brought under control on the morning of January 19.
During the operation, he fell into the wreckage and was trapped under the debris, where he lost his life.
The fire was one of the deadliest in Karachi’s history. The final investigation report put the death toll at 79, and the tragedy pushed Punjab to issue new fire safety rules for commercial buildings.
Fire Station to Carry His Name
After his death, Mayor Wahab announced that the Nazimabad Fire Station would be renamed after Shaheed Furqan Ali. He also announced Rs. 10 million in financial assistance for the family and assured them that all of Furqan’s benefits and entitlements would continue to be paid.
The Tamgha-e-Shujaat now adds national recognition to his sacrifice, which officials described as an act of exceptional courage and devotion to saving human lives.

items.title: Oil Likely to Cross $120 Again: Here’s Why
items.summary:
Global oil prices are currently trading around $118 per barrel, and traders are preparing for a highly volatile $120-rates-in-November scenario as fears of renewed hostilities between the US and Iran grow despite attempts by Pakistan and Gulf parties to help mediate an end to the war.
Despite mediation efforts by Qatar and Pakistan, most signals point towards a resumption of US-Iran hostilities in the coming weeks.
What Is Pushing Oil Towards $120
The rally comes just days before the US midterm elections. Brent, the global benchmark, was trading above $116 per barrel only last week, when oil prices entered the danger zone.
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said three unidentified vessels struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, caught fire, and were abandoned after taking an “unauthorised” route and ignoring Tehran’s warnings. The US Central Command (Centcom), like always, denies everything IRGC says.
How Governments and Producers Are Responding

What Is Pushing Oil Towards $120
The rally comes just days before the US midterm elections. Brent, the global benchmark, was trading above $116 per barrel only last week, when oil prices entered the danger zone.
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said three unidentified vessels struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, caught fire, and were abandoned after taking an “unauthorised” route and ignoring Tehran’s warnings. The US Central Command (Centcom), like always, denies everything IRGC says.
How Governments and Producers Are Responding
EU governments will release 42 million barrels of strategic oil and fuel reserves over the next three months, half of it diesel. France, which is releasing 10 million barrels, expects pump prices to fall by €0.12 to €0.18 per litre within days.
Producers in the Gulf are also trying to work around the strait. Saudi Aramco has reportedly started offering discounted spot cargoes to European buyers for October and November arrivals, aiming to maximize loadings from its Red Sea coast.
Abu Dhabi’s ADNOC has told clients that its second 1.5 million barrels per day pipeline to Fujairah, which bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, will see first deliveries in early 2027.
What This Means for You
Pakistan now revises fuel prices daily, so movements in global oil prices reach the pump much faster than under the old fortnightly system. A volatile week in international markets could therefore mean frequent changes in what Pakistanis pay for petrol and diesel.
Petrol currently costs Rs. 377.91 per litre. At that rate, a motorist who uses 40 litres a month spends about Rs. 15,116 on fuel. Every Rs. 1 per litre increase adds Rs. 40 to that monthly bill, while a Rs. 10 increase would add Rs. 400.
The government has already stepped in once to hold prices steady. In the latest notification, it cut the petroleum levy on petrol from Rs. 80 to Rs. 65.29 per litre and made local refineries absorb a Rs. 14.71 per litre rise in import costs. Whether it can keep cushioning consumers if Brent crosses $120 remains to be seen.
Other Developments in Energy Markets
Russia plans to extend its diesel export restrictions through January, while granting separate quotas for US-bound cargoes.
Egypt bought six fuel oil cargoes for November-December delivery as soaring LNG prices strain its finances. It has already spent 60% of the $10.1 billion it budgeted for LNG imports in 2026/27.
An armed group again shut a valve on Libya’s Hamada-Zawiya pipeline, halting flows to the country’s largest refinery, the 120,000 barrels per day Zawiya plant.
Record freight costs from Europe pushed fuel oil price spreads in Asia to record highs.
Japan is set to overtake China as the world’s largest LNG importer this year, with 62 million tons of imports compared to China’s expected 61 million tons.

items.author: Danial Saigra
items.content:
The Punjab government has invited applications for 285 postgraduate scholarships for faculty members working at public-sector nursing institutions across the province.
According to the official announcement, the scholarships include 15 PhD and 270 Master of Science in Nursing (MScN) opportunities under the Punjab Nursing and Health Workforce Reform Program.
The Program Implementation Unit (PIU), working under the Specialized Healthcare and Medical Education Department, will oversee the scholarship process.
The initiative aims to improve nursing education by helping eligible faculty members pursue advanced qualifications at national and international universities.
The government will award scholarships on a rolling basis until it fills the approved number of places.
Available Nursing Scholarships
The Punjab government has announced two categories of postgraduate scholarships for eligible nursing faculty members.
The first category includes 15 PhD scholarships for doctoral studies. According to the program’s official website, the doctoral scholarships focus on international education and research opportunities for nursing faculty.
The second category includes 270 MScN scholarships for postgraduate nursing education. The program offers these opportunities through recognized universities in Pakistan.
The scholarships aim to help nursing educators improve their academic qualifications, research skills, and teaching capabilities.
The initiative forms part of the government’s wider efforts to strengthen nursing education and improve the quality of healthcare training in Punjab.
Eligibility Criteria for Nursing Scholarships
According to the advertisement, the scholarships are available to eligible faculty members working at public-sector nursing institutions.
Candidates must meet the academic and professional requirements established for their chosen MScN or PhD program.
The government has advised applicants to review the detailed eligibility criteria before submitting their applications.

items.author: ProPK Staff
items.content:
The National Cyber Emergency Response Team (National CERT) has urged TeamViewer users to update the remote-access app after a high-severity flaw was found that could let attackers crash it or run malicious code on a computer.
The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-111585, has a CVSS score of 8.8. It affects TeamViewer clients older than version 15.83 on Windows, macOS, and Linux, according to the advisory, which cites TeamViewer’s own security bulletin.
How the Attack Works
The bug is an integer overflow in the part of TeamViewer that processes remote screen data. A malicious or hacked remote computer can send data that triggers it, causing a crash or memory corruption.
Depending on the platform, this could allow an attacker to run code with the same privileges as the TeamViewer app. However, the attack is not automatic. It only works when a user connects to a computer controlled by the attacker.
Which Versions Are Affected
The advisory lists the TeamViewer Full Client for Windows, macOS, and Linux, TeamViewer Portable for Windows, and the Android Remote Control app. Users should move to version 15.83 or later. Older branches have separate fixes, including 14.7.48868 for 14.x and 13.2.36231 for 13.x.
What Users Should Do
National CERT, which recently warned staff about another security risk, advised users and organizations to:
Update all TeamViewer installations, including portable and older versions
Accept remote sessions only from verified, trusted people
Limit remote access to approved users and devices
Review unattended access and admin privileges
Watch for unexpected TeamViewer crashes or unusual sessions
Where patching is not immediately possible, the advisory suggests blocking untrusted remote connections. If a device may be compromised, organizations should preserve logs, restrict remote access, and seek incident-response help.

items.author: Danial Saigra
items.content:
The Punjab Medical Faculty (PMF) has announced admissions for 17 two-year paramedical diploma courses at government medical training institutions across Punjab for the 2026–28 academic session.
According to the official admission notice, students who have passed Matriculation with Science can apply for courses in medical laboratory technology, operation theatre technology, radiology, dental technology, and other healthcare disciplines.
The admissions are open through the Punjab Medical Faculty’s online admission system. Candidates must submit their applications by November 20, 2026.
The faculty has also announced the eligibility criteria, application fee, merit requirements, and admission procedure for the upcoming session.
Available Medical Diploma Courses
The Punjab Medical Faculty is offering admissions in 17 paramedical and allied health disciplines.
These include Dispenser Technician, Medical Laboratory Technician, Operation Theatre Technician, Radiography and Imaging Technician, and Public Health Technician.
The available dental courses include Dental Technician, Dental Hygienist, and Dental Surgery Assistant.
Other programs include Dialysis Technician, Ophthalmic Technician, Physiotherapy Technician, Anesthesia Technician, and Central Sterilization Technician.
Students can also apply for Pharmacy Assistant, Dispensing Opticianry, Cardiac Technician, and Endoscopy Technician courses.
All the advertised diploma courses have a duration of two years. Candidates can select their preferred courses and institutions through the online admission system, subject to eligibility and available seats.
Eligibility Criteria for Admission
According to the Punjab Medical Faculty, applicants must have passed Matriculation with Science, including Physics, Chemistry, and Biology.
Candidates must have secured at least a second division in Matriculation, with a minimum combined score of 45% in the three science subjects.
The admission notice does not specify an upper age limit, allowing eligible candidates of different age groups to apply.
The faculty has also reserved a 2% quota for candidates with disabilities, subject to the relevant medical board’s assessment.
Eligible applicants with the required disability certificate can receive 20 additional merit marks. Candidates who have memorized the Holy Quran can receive 10 additional marks, provided they submit the required certificate from a recognized institution.
Admission will depend on academic merit, eligibility requirements, available seats, and the relevant institutional criteria.
Application Fee and Admission Requirements
The Punjab Medical Faculty has set a non-refundable application fee of Rs. 500. Applicants must generate the fee challan through the official online admission portal and pay it according to the stated instructions.
The faculty will not accept payment through bank drafts or pay orders.
Candidates must also submit the required documents, including their Matriculation certificate or result card, domicile certificate, CNIC or B-Form, and a recent passport-size photograph.
Applicants seeking additional merit marks or admission under the disability quota must provide the relevant supporting certificates.
The admission notice allows candidates to select up to five preferences for courses and institutions.
However, once a candidate receives admission against one preference, the remaining preferences will no longer remain active.
How to Apply for Punjab Medical Faculty Admissions
Interested candidates must submit their applications through the Punjab Medical Faculty’s official admission portal.
Applicants should visit admission.pmfpunjab.edu.pk and register using their CNIC or B-Form information.
They must complete the online application form and provide their personal details, academic qualifications, and domicile information.
Candidates should then select their preferred courses and institutions and upload the required documents.
After completing the form, applicants must generate and pay the Rs. 500 application fee challan.
The faculty has instructed candidates to review their applications carefully before submission.
Only online applications will be accepted. Candidates cannot submit their forms directly to the Punjab Medical Faculty office.

items.author: ProPK Staff
items.content:
The Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (DRAP) has issued alerts over counterfeit influenza vaccines being supplied in the country under the names of two multinational brands, Influvac Tetra and Vaxigrip Tetra.
Abbott Laboratories and Sanofi Winthrop, the companies whose names appear on the packaging, have confirmed that the vaccines are fake.
Batches Identified
According to DRAP, Vaxigrip Tetra batch Y4B34 is counterfeit and was never officially imported into Pakistan. Its packaging lists Sanofi Winthrop, France, as the manufacturer. Sanofi’s local distributor was the first to alert authorities.
Fake Influvac Tetra vaccines from batch P13 have also been found in Lahore. Their packaging lists Abbott Biologicals, Netherlands.
DRAP has issued separate rapid alerts for Vaxigrip Tetra and Influvac Tetra.
Serious Safety Concerns
The regulator warned that the quality, efficacy, and safety of these vaccines are unknown and that their use may pose serious safety and quality risks to public health. It urged doctors not to prescribe them.
Doctors, distributors, and pharmacies have been told to report any suspected fake vaccines to DRAP immediately. Citizens have been asked to report any side effects to the National Pharmacovigilance Centre (NPC).
Provinces Told to Seize Stock
DRAP has also directed provincial authorities to take emergency measures to stop the supply chain, trace the source of the counterfeit vaccines, and confiscate the affected batches.
The alert comes days after reports that Pakistan is facing a shortage of flu vaccines. Last month, DRAP also warned against life-threatening fake medicines.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
Dalal Street emerged as a founder’s paradise in 2025, with 18 Indian startups listing on the bourses and collectively mopping up a record ₹41,248 Cr from the public markets.
The surge was driven by a combination of macroeconomic tailwinds and regulatory support. While robust GDP growth projections helped revive investor appetite, SEBI’s reforms played a key role. Measures such as simplified DRHP filings reduced red tape, while more flexible ESOP rules allowed founders to retain meaningful ownership.
Retail investors also fuelled the frenzy as demat accounts crossed the 20 Cr mark. The OFS component dominated public issues last year, providing liquidity to the early backers of the new-age tech companies. Post-listing performance also followed the usual curve, with investors rewarding companies that prioritised profits, sustainable growth and governance over hype.
“⁠Besides the readiness that startups showed in their unit economics, there is also an increase in the founders committing to their businesses for next couple of decades and grow their businesses by adding adjacent profit pools – something that the public markets reward handsomely,” said Ashish Kumar, cofounder and general partner at Fundamentum Partnership.
Building on the momentum, seventeen new-age tech companies have already made their D-Street debut so far this year. Of these, ESDS Software Solution, Klassroom, RentoMojo, SEDEMAC, Kissht, LEAP India and Shiprocket made a bumper debut on the bourses.
Nevertheless, the IPO pipeline remains strong. Twenty five startups have already filed their DRHPs with SEBI, while over 25 are in various stages of finalising their IPO plans. Unicorns like OYO and Razorpay alone could raise nearly ₹20,000 Cr in 2026, making it one of the biggest years for startup IPOs.
However, recalibration is likely to define 2026 as investors are expected to prioritise strong fundamentals, profitability and low cash burn when backing new-age tech companies.
“IPO-bound startups in 2026 will be increasingly defined by their ability to demonstrate predictable cash flows, sustainable unit economics, and operational discipline rather than headline growth alone. Public market investors will place greater emphasis on governance, capital efficiency and long-term value creation, favouring companies that balance scale with financial prudence,” Orios Venture Partners’ managing partner Rehan Yar Khan told Inc42.
There are other challenges as well. Average retail subscription levels are moderating, while foreign institutional investors (FIIs) are pulling back in droves, reflecting caution amid geopolitical tensions and muted secondary market performance. The ongoing conflict in West Asia has further complicated the situation.
Yet, the overall outlook remains bullish for new-age tech IPOs. Maturing business models, deeper domestic capital pools and an evolving regulatory framework favouring transparency position India as a leading startup IPO hub.

Markets regulator SEBI has greenlit consumer appliances maker Atomberg’s IPO, which likely comprises a fresh issue worth ₹450 Cr and an OFS of up to 7.65 Cr shares

Defence tech company Tonbo Imaging made a stellar debut on the bourses and listed at ₹1,162 on the BSE, a premium of 66% to its issue price of ₹700 per share
