items.title: Iran ready for both ‘defence and diplomacy’, says Araghchi as Tehran, Qatari mediators hold third day of talks
items.summary:
Iran's Foreign ⁠Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that Tehran was prepared for "both defence and diplomacy", adding that the purpose of the "ongoing and progressing" talks ​was to continue consultations with the Qatari mediators.
Iranian negotiators were in Doha on Sunday for a third consecutive day of talks with Qatari mediators aimed at pushing for a deal to end the United States-Israeli war on Iran, an official briefed on the discussions told Reuters.
Speaking ​to state media, Araghchi said discussions on a "two-day proposal" were continuing, but that no final conclusion had been reached.
Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi in an interview with ICANA News Agency:
🔹 The Iranian delegation’s visit to Qatar took place at the deputy foreign minister level. Its purpose was to continue consultations with Qatari mediators, who had also visited Tehran in… pic.twitter.com/2DIvhRnH7c
— Tehran Times (@TehranTimes79) November 1, 20
items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Iran's Foreign ⁠Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that Tehran was prepared for "both defence and diplomacy", adding that the purpose of the "ongoing and progressing" talks ​was to continue consultations with the Qatari mediators.
Iranian negotiators were in Doha on Sunday for a third consecutive day of talks with Qatari mediators aimed at pushing for a deal to end the United States-Israeli war on Iran, an official briefed on the discussions told Reuters.
Speaking ​to state media, Araghchi said discussions on a "two-day proposal" were continuing, but that no final conclusion had been reached.
Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi in an interview with ICANA News Agency:
🔹 The Iranian delegation’s visit to Qatar took place at the deputy foreign minister level. Its purpose was to continue consultations with Qatari mediators, who had also visited Tehran in… pic.twitter.com/2DIvhRnH7c
— Tehran Times (@TehranTimes79) November 1, 2026
Qatari broadcaster Al Jazeera quoted Araghchi as saying in an interview on Saturday that Iranian and Qatari ​negotiators had developed a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days ​of a potential agreement with Washington.
"We are doing our best in this process, and we hope that there is rationality on the other side so that they prioritise diplomacy ​over other paths," Araghchi ​said of the ⁠talks with Qatari officials.
Iran boosting military capabilities to respond ‘without geographical limits’: defence minister
Iran was rapidly strengthening its armed forces’ combat capabilities to enable them to respond “without geographical limits,” Defence Minister Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi said on Sunday.
Speaking to reporters, Akhlaghi said Iran was moving “resolutely” to enhance its armed forces’ smart combat capabilities under directives from Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei.
“We are rapidly increasing our armed forces’ combat capabilities to be able to respond without geographical limits,” he said.
Defense minister: #Iran will deliver immediate response without geographic limitshttps://t.co/pAWzp33a3q pic.twitter.com/xS55RH6EZB
— Isna English (@Isna_English) November 1, 2026
Iran “will not be caught off guard, nor will we be stopped, and any type of attack will receive an appropriate, decisive and effective response,” he added.
Akhlaghi stressed that Iran “would not be surprised by threats, halted by pressure or dependent on the will of others in pursuing scientific and technological progress.”
His remarks come as Qatar and Pakistan continue mediation efforts to revive negotiations between Washington and Tehran, amid reports of progress in indirect talks in Doha.
The efforts seek understandings on Iran’s nuclear program, sanctions relief and the security of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.
Iranian negotiators in Doha to continue talks to end the US-Iran war, official says
Iranian negotiators were in Doha on Sunday for a third consecutive day of talks with Qatari mediators aimed at pushing for a deal to end the United States-Israeli war on Iran, an official briefed on the discussions told Reuters.
The talks come amid concerns that the conflict could escalate again after the November 3 US midterm elections. President Donald Trump has said the US will not launch new attacks on Iran before the vote and that talks with Tehran have been productive, though he has not ruled out further military action thereafter.
Iranian negotiators are in Doha for a third consecutive day of talks with Qatari mediators aimed at pushing for a deal to end the US-Iran war – Reuters, citing an official pic.twitter.com/V46nyTNUO0
— TRT World Now (@TRTWorldNow) November 1, 2026
Iran has repeatedly said it would respond to any new attacks by striking US and Israeli targets in neighbouring countries, as the eight-month-old war continues to disrupt global oil supplies and spill over across the Middle East.
Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei issued a statement on Saturday ordering the armed forces to be prepared to respond to any attacks. The Iranian military later announced it was taking steps to improve its readiness.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday that Trump has not decided whether to launch new strikes against Iran, but would prefer to resolve the conflict diplomatically.
Qatari mediators were in Tehran on Friday for discussions with Iranian officials before moving the talks to Doha on Saturday, an official had told Reuters. The talks were being coordinated in regular contacts with Washington, the official added.
Trump says US could strike Iran's remaining nuclear sites in '10 minutes'
United States President Donald Trump on Saturday said that Washington could strike Iran's remaining suspected nuclear facilities in "10 minutes," signaling the possibility of further military action despite ongoing diplomatic negotiations.
Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida, Trump claimed that US military operations had severely weakened Iran's armed forces and nuclear infrastructure, leaving only a few sites to be targeted.
"We still have to take care of, I would say, one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes. So, we have that plan," Trump said. "You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly," he added, referring to a suspected Iranian nuclear facility.
🇺🇸 President Donald Trump said on Saturday that the United States has knocked out much of Iran's military but still has to "take care of" one or two targets, as Tehran warned of reprisals if attacked ➡️ https://t.co/gl06h3LgJQ pic.twitter.com/dgSxdclo3H
— AFP News Agency (@AFP) November 1, 2026
Trump made the remarks when asked whether there was a timeline for ongoing Qatari-mediated negotiations between Washington and Tehran.
He said the US was not in a hurry to reach an agreement, claiming that American military operations had destroyed much of Iran's navy, air force, air defences, military equipment and nuclear infrastructure.
Asked whether Washington could resume military operations against Iran as soon as this week, Trump declined to provide a direct answer. "Why would you ask such a stupid question?" he said, before adding: "I can't tell you."
Trump also reiterated Washington's opposition to Iran acquiring nuclear weapons. "Iran will never have a nuclear weapon. They want to make a deal; we'll find out about that," he said.
Asked about the progress of negotiations, Trump expressed skepticism about Tehran's reliability despite describing the talks as progressing. "They're going fine, but they're not very reliable. I will tell you, they make a deal and then they back out. They want to make a deal. We'll see if they make a deal," he said.
Iran designates UK's Royal Navy, Air Force as 'terrorist' organisations
Iran designated Britain's Royal Navy and Royal Air Force as "terrorist" organisations and its foreign intelligence agency MI6 as a "hostile group" on Sunday, according to the Iranian Foreign Ministry.
In a statement carried by state-run news agency IRNA, the ministry said the move came in response to London's "malicious" actions, particularly its designation of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a "terrorist organisation."
Iran designates MI6 as ‘hostile group’, British navy and air force as ‘terrorist organizations’https://t.co/heLVhyzrPP pic.twitter.com/mVSnarvCg7
— IRNA News Agency ☫ (@IrnaEnglish) November 1, 2026
The ministry said the decision was taken under a resolution by Iran's Supreme National Security Council and followed the United Kingdom's designation of the IRGC under the State Threats Act 2026 on July 13.
Tehran also accused London of participating in the United States-Israeli war against Iran by providing access to military and logistical bases and facilities under British jurisdiction.
IRGC commander says military 'fully prepared for any scenario enemy may devise'
IRGC's Deputy for Political Affairs Brigadier-General Yadollah Javani said that Tehran's military was “fully prepared for any scenario the enemy may devise" and that forces were operating on the assumption that the US or Israel could strike at any moment, Al Jazeera reported.
Javani, cited by Al Jazeera, told Iran's Fars News Agency that Tehran would not be caught off guard and would respond as necessary.
Brigadier-General Yadollah Javani, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ deputy for political affairs, says Iranian forces are operating on the assumption that the US or Israel could strike at any moment.

— Al Jazeera English (@AJEnglish) November 1, 2026
The deputy also noted that Tehran's military capabilities now allowed it to confront the enemy defensively and as well as through preemptive and offensive operations.
According to Al Jazeera, Javani said Iran could inflict heavy, devastating strikes on US warships and warned that any region that enemy forces try to enter, whether by air assault or across a border, would become a “killing ground” for them.
Separately, Iran's army spokesperson Brigadier General Mohammad Akraminia warned that any renewed US aggression would be met with an "immediate, decisive" response on a “larger” scale than before, Press TV reported.
🔴 Spokesman of the Iranian Army Brigadier General Akrami-Nia:
🔺 Any renewed US aggression will be met with an immediate, decisive response on a larger scale than before.
🔺 In the event of a new war, its scope will not be confined to West Asia. pic.twitter.com/kmNoSNYysF
— Press TV 🔻 (@PressTV) November 1, 2026
The spokesperson added that in the event of a new war, its scope will not be confined to West Asia, Press TV said.
At least three wounded in air raids on Yemen oil facility
Al Jazeera reported that two air raids hit an oil facility in Yemen’s Hodeidah, citing Al Masirah TV.
It added that the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis had conducted two raids on an oil facility in Bajil district in the western Hodeidah governorate, with at least three civilians wounded.
Tensions in the Middle East have remained high since the US and Israel launched attacks against Iran on February 28, triggering Iranian retaliation across the region.
Despite subsequent diplomatic efforts and a memorandum signed by Washington and Tehran in June, tensions have persisted over security arrangements and navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

items.content:
•CSOs knock PDP, APGA, Accord leaders
By Luminous Jannamike, Dickson Omobola, Henry Obeta & Esther Onyegbula
The decision by some opposition governors to align with President Bola Tinubu’s re-election campaign has raised questions about party loyalty, political survival and the ability of opposition parties to present a united front ahead of the 2027 general election.
At the centre of the unfolding political drama are the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, who remains a member of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP); Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA); and Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke of the Accord Party.
Findings by Sunday Vanguard showed that their political choices have placed their respective parties in a delicate position as they grapple with the implications of their members’ involvement in a campaign to return the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to power.
Crisis
Wike, a prominent PDP figure and former Rivers State governor, has maintained his support for Tinubu despite the protracted crisis within the PDP and his strained relationship with members of the party opposed to his position. Soludo, on his part, has had to navigate the implications of his political relationship with the President while remaining in APGA, a party with its own electoral ambitions and identity. Adeleke’s emergence under the Accord Party banner has also drawn attention to the political calculations surrounding his relationship with the Tinubu-led administration and the implications for his party.
Although the circumstances surrounding the three politicians differ, their positions have triggered debate over whether opposition politicians can support the electoral ambitions of a rival party without undermining the platforms on which they built their political careers.
Against the backdrop of the approaching 2027 elections, the development presents a test of the PDP, APGA and Accord Party’s capacity to manage internal disagreements, defend their political identities and determine the limits of acceptable conduct by their prominent members.
It has also raised questions about the strength of party discipline in Nigeria, where political allegiances are frequently shaped by personal interests, strategic calculations and the search for relevance in the corridors of power.
Also, many are unsure whether what the politicians have done amounts to anti-party activities.
Constitution
Accordingly, the constitutions of the affected parties, in various sections, spell out actions that could constitute anti-party activities.
Specifically, Section 10(6) of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) Constitution provides that no member shall align with other parties or groups to undermine the party or any of its elected governments.
The provision formed the basis of the party’s August 2025 warning against members publicly supporting President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. Section 59(1) was also cited by the party’s National Working Committee in issuing a reprimand over alleged anti-party activities.
“The National Working Committee of the Peoples Democratic Party has reviewed the anti-party activities of certain members of the Party, particularly those endorsing President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for re-election in 2027,” the party’s National Publicity Secretary, Debo Ologunagba, warned.
Also, Article 21 of the APGA Constitution, which deals with party discipline and disciplinary measures, provides for sanctions against members whose conduct brings the party into disrepute or ridicule. The provision requires members to maintain discipline in their public and private conduct.
Like the PDP, APGA’s Anambra State chapter, in August 2022, specifically warned members against campaigning for candidates of other political parties, soliciting votes for them or promoting them on social media, describing such actions as anti-party activities.
Similarly, Article 20(A)(vi) of the Accord Party Constitution, under discipline and offences, expressly identifies engaging in anti-party activities as an offence.
Dismissed
Article 14(3) also provides that a member may be dismissed by the appropriate party organ for anti-party activities, gross misconduct or violation of the constitution. These provisions establish a basis for disciplinary action against members found to have acted against the party’s interests.
Adeleke’s spokesperson, Olawale Rasheed, reportedly said: “We must avoid anti-party activities. Severe sanction awaits any party member who works against the candidates of the party.”
Sunday Vanguard also observed that, irrespective of these provisions, Wike, Adeleke and Soludo have openly identified with President Tinubu’s campaign while still supporting other members vying for positions in their respective parties.
For instance, Wike, who has openly declared support for Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, described the emerging cross-party alliance as a “National Rainbow Coalition” involving politicians from different political platforms.
On October 14, 2026, he attended the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council at the State House Conference Centre, Abuja, where he reaffirmed his support for Tinubu, citing the President’s handling of the country’s challenges. Wike was also named coordinator of Tinubu’s campaign in Rivers State and the Federal Capital Territory. He also disclosed in September that he had urged Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke to publicly reaffirm his support for Tinubu after winning re-election.
Inauguration
Similarly, Soludo, who attended the inauguration of the APC campaign council, declared that APGA would not field a presidential candidate in 2027, saying the party was supporting the government at the centre.
He described Tinubu as his friend and said the President deserved a second term. The Anambra governor was subsequently appointed coordinator of the campaign in the state.
Adeleke also publicly declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid at the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja on October 14, 2026. Addressing the gathering, Adeleke pledged to mobilise support for Tinubu’s return to Aso Rock in 2027, saying: “I am here to throw my weight behind Tinubu’s return to Aso Rock. Let us rise from every nook and corner to support the President. Let him come and complete the good work he has begun.”
The governor, popularly known for his energetic dance moves, subsequently joined Tinubu in dancing at the event, drawing cheers from the audience. The APC had named him coordinator of the President’s re-election campaign in Osun State.
When Sunday Vanguard sought the positions of the concerned parties, they presented complex arguments, supporting the politicians while still insisting on party supremacy.
Defence
PDP spokesman Jungudo Haruna Mohammed, while defending Wike’s inclusion, argued that the minister had the right to decide whom he supported.
He said: “Wike has every constitutional and democratic right to decide whom he supports politically. His support for President Tinubu is legitimate, and as a serving appointee of the President, there is nothing contradictory about supporting the President while maintaining his political identity and relationships within the PDP.
“The FCT minister got the blessing of the PDP during the era of its former National Chairman, Umar Damagum, to work with Mr President. His inclusion in the Presidential Campaign Council was therefore expected, but this does not make him a member of the APC National Working Committee.
“Every political party, including the PDP, would like to have Mr Nyesom Wike in their campaign council, but the party had already endorsed his invitation to help the current administration from day one. He is working for President Tinubu and not for APC.”
In the same vein, APGA National Chairman, Sly Ezeokenwa, described Soludo’s case as a strategic alignment rather than a decision taken by the Anambra governor on his own.
“The All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), the National Working Committee, had already taken the decision that we will stay aligned and we will still share the same accord with the All Progressives Congress (APC) and accept the idea of adopting Mr President as our presidential candidate,” he said.
Verdict
Ezeokenwa argued that the arrangement served the interests of the South-East, suggesting that the region stood to gain from closer engagement with the Federal Government.
On his part, Ogun State Chairman of the Accord Party, Michael Oke, told Sunday Vanguard that the national leadership learnt of Adeleke’s reported appointment through the media.
Oke warned against reaching a verdict before the party had examined the circumstances and heard from those concerned.
“Until the national leadership has studied the case and heard all concerned persons, it would be too early to conclude that the incident is anti-party,” Oke said.
He cited Articles 13, 14 and 20 of the Accord Party Constitution, which he said deal with members’ obligations to comply with party decisions and provide for disciplinary action over anti-party activities or misconduct.
Meanwhile, a chieftain of the party and member representing Ede South/Ede North/Ejigbo/Egbedore Federal Constituency of Osun State, Bamidele Salam, described Adeleke’s appointment to lead Tinubu’s re-election campaign in Osun as a welcome development.
The Imole Campaign Council (TICC) of Governor Adeleke also promised to deliver 1.5 million votes for Tinubu.
In a statement, TICC Director-General, Olalere Oyewumi, described Adeleke’s appointment as well deserved, vowing that all Accord Party structures in Osun would work for Tinubu’s re-election.
Oyewumi said Tinubu’s trust in Adeleke would be justified through unwavering commitment and a strong electoral performance.
“The Imole Campaign Council welcomes the appointment of Governor Adeleke as State Coordinator of PBAT Presidential Campaign Council in Osun,” the statement added.
A PDP chieftain, however, Chief Emmanuel Ogidi, accused Wike of maintaining a relationship with the PDP while allegedly supporting the interests of the APC, arguing that such conduct raised serious questions about loyalty and commitment to the opposition party.
“You can’t serve two masters. He (Wike) is supposed to be serving us in PDP, but he is serving APC. This is a threat to democracy. APC is using him to destroy democracy, and it’s deliberate, but we are very conscious of that, and very soon you will hear what will happen,” Ogidi said.
Values
Meanwhile, some civil society organisations (CSOs), in conversations with Sunday Vanguard, disagreed with party leaders defending the development, arguing that the politicians’ actions amounted to anti-party activities that warranted disciplinary measures.
Country Lead of the Society for Promotion of Democratic Values and Ethos, Dr Fredrick Manaseh, said the situation had significantly undermined party development and democratic values.
He said: “Since the APC came to power, we have witnessed a systematic erosion of democratic values. The party, with its one-party-state agenda, has ensured that the growth of other parties is stunted. Regrettably, they have the likes of Wike and other politicians to promote that agenda. Therefore, let nobody deceive Nigerians, they are working against their parties and should receive disciplinary action.”
Similarly, Executive Director of the Centre for Accountability and Good Governance, Prof Usman Monde, blamed political parties for failing to enforce their constitutional provisions.
He said: “The answer to your question is obvious. They are rooting for other parties against the general wishes of their groups. Parties are governed by constitutions. When a party abandons its constitution because of the ambition of certain individuals within its fold, how can such a party grow and become competitive?
“Political parties cannot claim to be serious about democracy if they fail to enforce their own rules. The constitution of a party should not apply only to ordinary members while prominent politicians are allowed to act as they please. There must be equal treatment and accountability for all members, irrespective of their status.
“Where a party’s members openly support the presidential candidate of another party, the leadership must clarify whether such actions are consistent with its decisions and political objectives. If they are not, the appropriate disciplinary procedures should be invoked in accordance with the party’s constitution.
“Democracy thrives when political parties have clear identities, competing visions and the discipline to hold their members accountable. When prominent members of opposition parties openly campaign for the re-election of the ruling party’s candidate, it raises legitimate questions about the opposition’s cohesion and capacity to offer Nigerians credible alternatives.
“Ultimately, the responsibility rests with the leadership of these parties. They must demonstrate that their constitutions are binding on everyone, rather than allowing individual ambitions to override collective decisions. Without discipline, internal democracy and respect for party rules, political parties will struggle to build public confidence and remain competitive.”
The post Anti-party claims:Wike, Soludo, Adeleke fight back appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
By Daniel Abia, P/Harcourt
With dexterity and some sense of candor, he strode purposefully along the red carpet isle to the podium.
His assigned role for the day was unambiguously defined: To unveil the Rainbow Coalition candidates for the 2027 general elections in Rivers State.
But unknown to many, Governor Siminalayi Fubara had a special announcement to make.
First, he took a brisk eye scan through the sea of heads at the Yakubu Gowon Stadium, then announced: “I am no more your leader. Stop calling me ‘my leader, my leader’”
The day was Tuesday, October 27, 2026, when a political group formed by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Mr Nyesom Wike, organized a rally which drew participants from the 23 local government areas of the state.
They converged on the Yakubu Gowon Stadium Port Harcourt to display which candidate from the six-member political parties that constitute the Rainbow Coalition for the coming elections.
Fubara was tactically chosen to perform the unveiling and handover the flag of the All Progressives Congress, APC, to Hon Ogundu Kingsley Chinda, the anointed governorship candidate of Wike.
Fubara did not only surrender his potential second term as a sitting governor to Chinda but also relinquished his role as the political leader of Rivers to Wike.
The governor veered off the track of duty and handed down a stern warning, or so it seemed, to his organic supporters who stood by him in thick and thin during the dark moment of the political crisis in Rivers, telling them unreservedly that he was no more their leader.
“Let me say something here so that it will always help us while we move forward”, he started.
“I’m aware there are some issues where some persons who followed me when we had the crisis when you’re in your meeting you say ‘my leader, my leader’.
“We are now in one house. And because we have one house, there is no issue about who is the leader.
“I might be your oga (governor) but we have a common leader now. So, please, going forward, this issue of ‘my leader, my leader, my leader’, I want it resolved here and now.”
There was a cumulus of silence at first, then a deafening applause.
Governors as leaders
 Way back in January 2025, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, through his Vice, Kasim Shettima, had declared that all APC governors were political leaders of the party in their states.
The implication is that as the highest political position in the state, a governor is seen as a leader politically.
Tinubu made this known during the defection of Governor Agbu Kefas of Taraba State from PDP to APC.
That pronouncement also covered Fubara the moment he defected from the same PDP to APC on December 9, 2025 and picked the 001 registration number of the ruling party.
Also, shortly after Fubara’s defection, APC national leaders—including National Chairman, Prof Nentawe Yilwatda, National Secretary, Ajibola Basiru, and Deputy National Organising Secretary, Duru Eze, officially affirmed the Rivers governor as the leader of the APC in the state.
They cited the APC Constitution, which designates sitting state governors as party leaders in their respective states.
Rainbow/Fubara reconciliation
 Reeling in the deep cut injury occasioned by the over three years of political crisis that culminated into the declaration of a state of emergency on March 18, 2025 by President Tinubu, Wike and his political group soon realized the need to bring in Fubara and his structure to form a formidable force for 2027.
Between August 16 and October 7, 2026, the Rainbow Coalition led by Wike held a back-to-back peace meeting with the governor in his private residence in Port Harcourt.
The last meeting, expanded to include all the 23 LGA chairmen, had lawmakers from both state and national assemblies and political appointees loyal to Wike in attendance.
At the meeting, Fubara accepted to return to the “family”.
And the three suspended lawmakers loyal to him were reinstated while members of his political camp were promised juicy positions in the next dispensation. 
The peace meeting generated outrage in Rivers with many describing the governor as the “weakest” political leader in the history of Rivers.
Fubara was alleged to have told his loyalists to go to the rural areas across the state and preach the gospel of Rainbow Coalition.
State capture?
 Political observers are of the opinion that, having used his structure to propel Fubara to become governor, Wike was making a grand plan to capture the soul of the state.
The internecine crisis witnessed in the past, obviously testified to the fact that the minister “was desperate for a third term by proxy”, said Franklin Uket, a public commentator.
Uket noted that from the fight to regain his structure, “Wike never wanted Fubara to be independent minded as a governor. “He never wanted Fubara to draw any of his (Wike) political enemies close to his government”.
Now politically suffocated, Fubara’s decision to throw in the towel of leadership also gives credence to the fact that the crisis is deeper than what appears in the surface.
“The governor has been stampeded and bullied out of power”, Uket alleged.
Public perception
 Apparently miffed by the recent development, Fubara’s former ally and royal father, HRH Ubokikwan Gabriel Ogbologwung, PhD, Paramount Ruler of Egwebe in Andoni LGA of the state, said “the summersault position taken by the Executive Governor of Rivers State, Siminalayi Joseph Fubara, in my thinking is not an excellent decision”.
The monarch said Fubara’s statement gives credence to what many see as using the governor “as a tool for the state’s total capture placing the state under Minister Nyesom Wike’s political egoistic jackboot”
He said the governor’s latest move has made most of his followers, especially as the grassroots, to shrink back into their political shells.
“With Fubara’s ignominious move, he has totally surrendered his political life for a terminal crush by Nyesom Wike, who left nothing for Governor Fubara on the negation tables, which architect -in-chief is Wike and Wike alone”.
Ogbologwung said as a Rivers man, “I see the governor’s total surrender to Wike as a ship captain who swims ashore with the only life-buoy available during a wreck without bothering about the safety of his crew members.
“The governor’s action has sadly demonstrated to the world how not to have a leader with a borrowed mind.
“As a result, he has, by his own inconsiderate machinations deliberately sunk his political ship, having eaten to his own belle-full, that he desires less of neither the survival of his followers nor the state itself”.
Another supporter of the governor and an elder statesman of Ijaw extraction, Chief Anabs Sara-Igbe, reiterated that Rivers people are not in sync with Wike’s political posturing.
He said Fubara must have been forced to relinquish his leadership role because “he has found himself in a web”.
Sara-Igbe said the governor’s action may have serious future implication on political balance of the state.
“What he did may have a deeper meaning. Wike has been begging Fubara since, it means that he wanted to take total power from Fubara. But we are waiting”.
Speaking differently, a former member of the House of Representatives and a political analyst, Prince Ogbonna Nwuke, said the governor’s action could be deduced from the context of how he sees himself presently.
“There is nothing too big for anybody to do to bring peace. You can’t have two masters in the same boat”, Ogbonna said, adding that only Fubara can answer why he voluntarily surrender his leadership to Wike.
The former commissioner however stated that as things stand now, “Fubara has taken a backstage in the state politics. I don’t know if I should say it is humility or weakness. But the governor is not ego-driven or power-drunk”.
According to him, the governor’s supporters must have felt let down, disappointed and shocked.
“He may have plans for his people on what to do for them to ameliorate the pains of what has just happened”, Ogbonna concluded.
For the President of the pan Niger Delta Elders Forum, PANDEF, Prof (Amb) Godknows Igali, there was nothing strange about what Fubara did.
“He is entitled to his opinion or action. In the beginning, they were in the same political family”, Igali said.
The diplomat said that interest, in whatever form or shape, is determined by whoever is the political leader of the state. “It is Fubara’s right to relinquish authority or to hold onto it”, he said.
Implication
Governor Fubara may not envisage any further political power again after his tenure.
But the question many are asking is: What possible impact will that action have on the people of Opobo, his ancestral home! Will they be trusted with political in the nearest future!
More so, what is the assurance that Fubara and his team are in the Rainbow Coalition camp with their full chest! The answers are in the belle of the 2027 governorship election in the state. But for now, he is on hangar’s cliff.

items.content:
By Henry Umoru, Luminous Jannamike & Omeiza Ajayi
With barely 77 days to the 2027 general elections, concerns over the preparedness of the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, have become disturbing, especially following the discovery of artificial intelligence-generated photographs in the commission’s preliminary voters’ register.
The development has raised fresh questions about the integrity of the electoral database, the effectiveness of INEC’s internal monitoring mechanisms and the commission’s capacity to conduct elections that would command public confidence.
Accordingly, the worries have been compounded by complaints about other irregularities in the preliminary register, including questionable names, addresses, genders and photographs.
Although INEC has acknowledged the problem and promised to clean up the register before the final version is released on December 15, 2026, the development has exposed vulnerabilities in the registration process.
The commission’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, ICT, Dr Lawrence Bayode, disclosed that some registration officers allegedly used their official login credentials to introduce irregular entries into the database.
He, however, assured Nigerians that the commission had identified those responsible and was taking steps to address the situation.
Registered voters
 INEC’s preliminary register, uploaded on October 26, 2026, contains over 103.4 million registered voters. Bayode explained that the figure reflected the more than 93 million voters recorded in the 2023 register and additional registrations from the continuous voter registration exercise ahead of the forthcoming elections.
He said INEC was deploying technology to address the identified shortcomings, adding that its Automated Biometric Identification System, ABIS, had detected several questionable photographs before the preliminary register was released.
Against this backdrop, Sunday Vanguard spoke with officials of political parties to ascertain their assessment of INEC’s preparations, the implications of the AI-generated images and what the commission needs to do to guarantee credible elections.
While some parties expressed reservations about the development and called for urgent measures to restore public confidence, others maintained that the discovery should not be exaggerated, insisting that INEC had sufficient time to address the identified problems.
LP: INEC must go back to drawing board
 For the Labour Party, LP, the discovery of AI-generated photographs in the preliminary voters’ register is a development that requires urgent attention, particularly given the proximity of the elections.
The party’s National Publicity Secretary, Ken Asogwa, said the situation had moved beyond speculation following the commission’s admission that irregularities had occurred.
He said: “This is quite concerning. This is no longer a rumour because even INEC Director of ICT came out to admit it.”
Asogwa expressed concern that such a development was occurring under the leadership of the current INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Ojo Amupitan, SAN, whom he described as a person with considerable academic and professional credentials.
He said: “This is happening at a time when we have an INEC Chairman who is not just a lawyer, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria at that. If you look at his CV, he is also an academic of repute, an individual who was a Deputy Vice Chancellor of a University.”
According to him, the proximity of the elections makes the development particularly disturbing.
“That this is happening with less than 90 days to a crucial election is worrisome,” he added.
On the commission’s preparedness, the LP spokesman said INEC was in the best position to assess and explain its readiness. However, he insisted that the commission had a responsibility to reassure Nigerians and rebuild confidence in the electoral process.
He said: “As to their preparedness, the commission is in the best place to say. But we will suggest that they go back to the drawing board and inspire public confidence in the process.
“Election also has a lot to do with public perception.”
PDP: No cause for alarm
However, the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, adopted a different position, expressing confidence in the commission’s activities and urging political parties and other stakeholders not to make the discovery appear bigger than it is.
The party’s National Publicity Secretary, Jungudo Haruna Mohammed, acknowledged that complaints had emerged from different quarters over the preliminary voters’ register, particularly allegations involving AI-generated images.
He, however, said INEC’s admission and commitment to correcting the anomalies should be acknowledged.
He said:
“We have received complaints from different quarters, particularly about the preliminary voters’ register, where it was alleged that AI-generated images had been included. It is no longer an allegation because INEC has owned up to it.
“The good thing is that INEC has acknowledged the issue and reassured Nigerians that it is doing everything possible to correct it and prevent a recurrence.”
AI-generated
Mohammed argued that the emergence of AI-generated images in the register was not entirely surprising, considering the growing influence of artificial intelligence in contemporary society.
He, however, maintained that the discovery did not necessarily suggest that the electoral process had been compromised.
“In today’s world, where AI has become the order of the day, it is not surprising that such images may have found their way into the register. However, now that the issue has been discovered, I do not think it has the potential to discredit the credibility of the electoral process.
“Whatever number of AI-generated images of purported eligible voters may have infiltrated the register is unlikely to be significant enough to affect the outcome of the elections.”
The PDP spokesman further noted that the register currently in circulation was preliminary and not the final document to be used for the elections.
According to him, the commission still has the opportunity to identify and eliminate questionable entries before the final register is published.
“The good thing is that this is not the final register, and these issues have been detected very early. We believe INEC will deploy all necessary technologies to clean up the register and prevent it from being infiltrated by questionable and unverifiable entries,” he said.
On the general preparedness of the commission, Mohammed said his party had not identified anything that suggested that the forthcoming elections were under threat.
“For our party, we have not seen anything so far that has the capacity to truncate the 2027 elections. I think INEC’s preparations so far deserve a level of commendation.
“The commission has outlined about 14 or 15 items it intends to achieve, and from the last information I received from the INEC chairman, it has achieved about 10 of them.
“Our party is therefore not worried. We are making our own preparations, and so far, INEC’s activities have not given us any cause for concern.”
Electoral process
He also called on opposition parties and public commentators to be measured in their public statements, warning against utterances that could undermine confidence in the electoral process.
“I will call on opposition parties and public commentators to guard their utterances.
“We need the country. We need a peaceful country. We need to encourage INEC, and I must also commend Nigerians for being very vigilant.
“This shows that the level of civic responsibility among Nigerians has risen. In the past, Nigerians did not really pay much attention to the voters’ register. But now, they are clearly watching, observing every step and scrutinising everything INEC does.”
Mohammed said the growing public scrutiny should encourage the commission to remain committed to transparency.
“Overall, INEC is now aware that Nigerians are very vigilant. The commission, on its part, will not contemplate doing anything that could truncate or compromise the electoral process.
“The PDP is confident in INEC’s activities, and we believe the concerns that have been raised are minor issues. INEC owned up to them, which is commendable.
“If it had denied the issue, that would have given us reason to doubt. But it did not. It acknowledged that it had identified the problem and was cleaning up the register.
“We must all rally support behind INEC, commend the Commission and remain positive about the 2027 elections and transition,” he added.
APM: AI must not undermine credible elections
 On its part, the Allied People’s Movement, APM, expressed concerns about the application of artificial intelligence in the electoral process, stressing the need for caution and responsible deployment of the technology.
The party’s National Publicity Secretary, Abubakar Yusuf, said INEC must remain alive to its responsibilities, particularly as the country approaches another crucial electoral exercise.
According to him, the commission must ensure that the introduction of technology does not defeat the fundamental objective of conducting credible elections.
He said: “INEC is expected to be alive to its responsibilities, particularly when it comes to elections at any level.
“On the issue of artificial intelligence, the need for caution and its responsible deployment is obvious. This is necessary to ensure that the objectives of using the technology are not defeated.”
Yusuf insisted that the 2027 elections must be conducted in a manner that leaves no room for questions about their credibility, acceptability and verifiability.
He said:“The 2027 polls must be seen to be acceptable, credible and verifiable in every respect. Anything short of that will raise questions about INEC’s conduct of the elections.
“The deployment of AI should not undermine the genuine objective of ensuring credible polls.”
For the APM, therefore, the controversy surrounding the preliminary register reinforces the need for INEC to exercise greater vigilance in deploying technology and managing the electoral database.
SDP: INEC is compromised
Taking the same position, the Adewole Adebayo-Bugaje Presidential Campaign Council of the Social Democratic Party, SDP, faulted INEC’s preparations in view of prevailing issues.
The council said the current level of preparation was fundamentally compromised, characterised by severe vulnerabilities in technological integrity and institutional transparency, just 77 days before citizens head to the polls.
Speaking to Sunday Vanguard in Abuja, the campaign council’s Chief Media and Communications Adviser, Comrade Mark Adebayo, said while Prof. Joash Amupitan-led INEC continued to offer verbal assurances of its readiness, the SDP’s empirical analysis of the National Voters’ Register, biometric infrastructure deployment and logistical timelines revealed systemic red flags that threatened the credibility of the upcoming elections.
Vulnerabilities
 Adebayo said: “Our campaign maintains that the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) current level of preparation is fundamentally compromised, characterised by severe vulnerabilities in technological integrity and institutional transparency just 80 days before citizens head to the polls. While INEC continues to offer verbal assurances of its readiness, our empirical analysis of the National Voters’ Register, biometric infrastructure deployment, and logistical timelines reveals systemic red flags that threaten the credibility of the upcoming elections.
“We refuse to allow structural defects to be swept under the rug. We seriously suspect that distinct algorithmic anomalies consistent with Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) may have been deployed and active on INEC platforms. These are not human voters; they are synthetic identities designed to pad the register.
“Statistical analysis reveals an improbable statistical spike in registered voters aged 18-22 in specific strategic clusters, where the registration curve completely diverges from historical census data and local birth rates.
“INEC’s Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) was legally mandated to eliminate duplicates and non-human data. The presence of these glaring AI fabrications is empirical proof that either the ABIS software is malfunctioning, or it has been deliberately bypassed.
“Beyond the compromised register, our active tracking of INEC’s field readiness indicates a dangerous lag in critical operational benchmarks.
BVAS auditing
“On the limited mock trials, field reports show unrectified battery degradation and software latency in rural local governments. We explicitly demand electoral integrity.
“We will not sit idly by while the democratic will of the people is subverted by technological malpractice. On behalf of our candidate, Prince Adewole Adebayo, and millions of hopeful citizens, we demand that INEC immediately execute the following corrective measures:
“Independent Digital Audit: INEC must grant accredited joint-party IT experts and independent international observers direct read-only access to the central backend register to conduct a comprehensive algorithmic sweep for AI-generated faces.
“Transparent BVAS Auditing: A public, televised stress-test of the BVAS machines across all senatorial districts must be conducted within the next 14 days to verify biometric match speeds and battery resilience.
“Purging of the Register: A comprehensive, publicly verifiable list of all deleted, duplicated, or flagged synthetic entries must be published by polling unit, ensuring absolute mathematical reconciliation before final printing.
“Let us be clear, our campaign wants an election, but we insist on a legitimate election. We are not asking for favours; we are demanding compliance with the law and technological accountability. INEC has exactly 80 days to cleanse its systems, secure its portals, and prove to the world that it is an umpire, not an accomplice. The resilience of our democracy depends entirely on their next move.”
Preparations
Also speaking with Sunday Vanguard on the development, the National Chairman of the Action Democratic Party, ADP, Yabagi Yusuf Sani, said that with elections barely 80 days away, INEC must demonstrate its preparedness through verifiable actions, not mere assurances.
The ADP has called for an immediate, transparent and independent investigation into the irregularities, identification of those responsible, appropriate sanctions where wrongdoing is established, and a comprehensive forensic audit of the voters’ register before its final certification.
Sani said: “The position of the Action Democratic Party (ADP) is that the credibility of any election begins long before polling day. It starts with the integrity of the voters’ register, the transparency of electoral preparations, the neutrality of electoral officials and the confidence of Nigerians in the entire electoral process.
“The recent revelations concerning alleged AI-generated photographs and other irregularities in the voters’ register are deeply concerning. The reported acknowledgement by INEC’s Director of ICT that some registration officers introduced AI-generated photographs into the system raises serious questions about the effectiveness of the Commission’s internal controls and safeguards against electoral manipulation.
Investigation
“ADP therefore calls for an immediate, transparent and independent investigation into these irregularities, identification of those responsible, appropriate sanctions where wrongdoing is established, and a comprehensive forensic audit of the voters’ register before its final certification.
“With elections barely 80 days away, INEC must demonstrate its preparedness through verifiable actions rather than mere assurances. Nigerians deserve clear evidence that the voters’ register is credible, electoral technologies are reliable, sensitive materials are secure, and arrangements for voting, collation and transmission of results are sufficiently robust to prevent manipulation.
“We are particularly concerned that technological innovations intended to strengthen electoral credibility could become instruments for undermining public confidence if adequate safeguards, transparency and accountability are lacking.
“INEC must also deepen its engagement with political parties, civil society organisations, security agencies and other stakeholders. The Commission must address outstanding concerns arising from previous elections and demonstrate measurable improvements in its operational readiness.
“For ADP, the fundamental issue is not simply whether INEC can conduct elections on schedule, but whether every eligible Nigerian can exercise the right to vote freely and whether every lawful vote will be accurately counted, transparently collated and faithfully reflected in the declared results.
“Nigeria cannot afford another electoral process overshadowed by avoidable controversies, technological uncertainties and allegations of manipulation.
“Our message to INEC is clear: electoral credibility must be demonstrated, not merely proclaimed.
“The integrity of the 2027 elections is too important to be compromised by administrative lapses, technological vulnerabilities or institutional complacency.”
NDC: Remove names of deceased Nigerians
Reacting to the development, the National Presidential Campaign Council, NPCC, of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, urged INEC to remove the names of deceased Nigerians from the voters’ register.
According to the NDC, reports that deceased Nigerians still appear on the voters’ register raise serious questions about its accuracy and integrity.
A statement by the spokesperson for the NPCC of the NDC, Dr Chiogo Constance Ikokwu, called on the electorate and political parties to take advantage of their rights and file objections with the electoral body so that INEC could effect the removals.
The statement reads:
“Reports that deceased Nigerians, including prominent figures such as Raymond Dokpesi, Ifeanyi Ubah, Muhammadu Buhari and Rotimi Akeredolu, still appear on the voters’ register raise serious questions about its accuracy and integrity.
“These are just a few names. What about the 774 local government areas across Nigeria? How many deceased persons remain on the register? When was it last comprehensively updated? Is this an oversight, institutional failure or something more troubling?
Citizens
“INEC has the legal responsibility to cleanse the register, especially if it has been notified by citizens. The electoral body owes Nigerians answers. We demand a credible, up-to-date and verifiable voters’ register ahead of the 2027 elections.
“We call on Nigerians and political parties to take advantage of their rights and file objections to the electoral body so INEC can effect removals. On its part, INEC needs to look into these complaints, establish a portal to put all names under objection and give persons against whom a complaint has been lodged the opportunity to respond (in the case of the living), as well as publishing the procedure to object to illegal names in the interest of the public. The electoral body is a well-funded organisation paid for by citizens, and therefore must provide value for money.
“Nigerians will accept nothing less than the highest standards of efficiency, professionalism and accountability from INEC. The electoral body must demonstrate that it has the capacity, competence and commitment to deliver an election whose credibility cannot reasonably be called into question. This is not too much to ask; it is the bare minimum expected of an institution entrusted with the people’s democratic mandate.
“Furthermore, in light of the 2023 election credibility challenges, it is time for an independent, unbiased and professional audit of INEC processes and mechanisms. The 2027 election is too critical for unanswered questions about the very foundation of our democracy. No excuses. No complacency. No questionable register. INEC must do its job.”
4,800 claims, 600 objections
 Meanwhile, INEC said it had received over 4,800 claims and about 600 objections to the preliminary voters’ register, with a promise that the discrepancies would be corrected before the final register was certified on December 15, 2026.
INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, SAN, disclosed this on Friday when the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) Pre-Election Fact-Finding Mission paid a courtesy visit to the commission’s headquarters in Abuja. The mission is led by Victor Bockarie Foh, a former Vice-President of Sierra Leone.
Amupitan said the claims, received at the registration areas where the register was displayed as of Thursday, were mainly corrections and other minor matters.
On objections, he said the commission had received “about 600 complaints on the register” through electoral officers and Resident Electoral Commissioners from the various wards. He added that “the display of the register online is also confirming some of the complaints we had earlier received.”
According to him, the register now stands at over 103 million registered citizens, adding that it is a huge figure and that the discrepancies noticed would be corrected so that “the register will be properly cleaned up” ahead of the final list.
8,809 Registration Areas
 The commission completed three phases of the Continuous Voter Registration exercise and recently ended the physical display of the preliminary register at registration areas nationwide. It has also published the register on its online portal, display.inecnigeria.org, for public scrutiny, claims and objections.
He again restated that the Presidential and National Assembly elections will hold on Saturday, January 16, 2027, while the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections are scheduled for Saturday, February 6, 2027.
He said the commission will deploy personnel and technology across 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, covering 774 Local Government Areas, 8,809 Registration Areas (Wards) and 176,846 polling units.
Amupitan said the commission had executed nine of the 14 major milestones in its Revised Timetable and Schedule of Activities for the election.
He said INEC had also moved “away from administrative assumptions” by personally conducting zonal readiness assessment tours. It has covered the South-West in Lagos, the North-West in Kaduna, the South-East in Enugu and the North-East in Gombe, and the team is heading to Port Harcourt for the South-South. The North-Central, the last zone, will be visited next week.
Accreditation
 He said the tours had shown that some areas needed higher deployments than planned because of terrain and security challenges.
Amupitan disclosed that the commission was planning a mock accreditation across the country, which he said should hold “sometime in November.” He said it would test accreditation and the transmission of results simultaneously in all the states, to be sure the commission can “cure the problem of glitch that took place in 2023.”
On technology, he said the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) would be deployed for dual biometric accreditation, by fingerprint and face. The commission has also introduced a new electronic verification platform, eEC8A, for results transmitted to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV).
Electoral integrity
 However, beyond the positions of the parties, the controversy has placed renewed attention on the responsibility of INEC to demonstrate that the problems identified in the preliminary register are being addressed.
Observers believe the commission’s December 15 deadline for the release of the final register will, therefore, be an important test of its ability to resolve the concerns raised by stakeholders.
INEC, therefore, faces the task of convincing Nigerians that the preliminary register’s shortcomings will not translate into weaknesses in the final electoral process.
The post 77 days to polls:Parties clash over INEC’s preparations appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
Old guard moves to form ‘Afenifere Independent’
Oba Olaitan calls for truce
Forceful acquisition of pan-Yoruba group is dead on arrival —Ex-spokesman
‘Without Adebanjo’s camp support for Peter Obi, Tinubu may not have been president’
By Dapo Akinrefon
The leadership crisis within the pan-Yoruba socio-political organization, Afenifere, may be far from being over.
This is as a result of a factional camp asking other factions to unite behind the leadership of Oba Oladipo Olaitan.
But while most of the Fasoranti camp vowed to resist such a move, some of the old guards, it was gathered, plan to form another Afenifere.
Most of them, who belong to various factions, disagree over cultural succession norms and the potential emergence of a break-away Yoruba group. A source told Sunday Vanguard that discussions are ongoing to jettison both camps and start on a clean slate.
Multiple sources said there is a need to resuscitate Afenifere and give the Yoruba race a formidable platform.
A credible source informed Vanguard that while some members of the group are making moves to throw up what they called Afenifere Independent, the Akure camp is gearing up to name a former governor as Fasoranti’s successor.
The source said: “One thing I know is that the Akure camp will not approve that Oba Oladipo Olaitan emerges as Afenifere leader. I know who they are planning to name as Fasoranti’s successor. He is a former governor. The two camps cannot be united as it is and that is why some of us having made up our mind to come up with Afenifere Independent.”
Last week, following the death of Pa Reuben Fasoranti, the Oba Olaitan camp formally announced the consolidation of its collective leadership under his (Olaitan’s) stewardship.
It said the transition was a tribute to Fasoranti’s legacy and a step towards promoting unity and defending Yoruba socio-political interests.
The factional National Publicity Secretary and Secretary-General, Prince Justice Faloye and Alade Rotimi-John respectively, said Olaitan had demonstrated sincerity of purpose and the capacity to champion the group’s interests while promoting national unity.
The statement read: “The modern history of the Yoruba people and the political evolution of Nigeria bear the indelible mark of Fasoranti. As a patriarch of principles, Pa Fasoranti carried the sacred torch of Afenifere with unyielding grace, following in the visionary footsteps of Chief Obafemi Awolowo, Chief Adekunle Ajasin and Senator Abraham Adesanya. Through seasons of national uncertainty, he stood as a steadfast moral compass, a relentless advocate for true federalism, equity, fairness and the progressive advancement of his people. His leadership anchored the Yoruba nation in wisdom, courage and an unshakeable commitment to justice and fair play.”
In their defence, they were of the view that the consolidation of the great legacy now rests upon Oba Oladipo Olaitan, while they insisted that the time for division is over.
The statement further said: “Over the years, Oba Olaitan has demonstrated a profound sincerity of purpose and the strategic capacity to champion the core interests of Afenifere while simultaneously promoting the greater unity of Nigeria. His track record reflects a leader who understands the delicate balance between popular advocacy within a region and the broader imperative of national cohesion. Afenifere hereby issues a solemn clarion call to all factions, political actors and upcoming generations within the Yoruba nation that the time for division is over. The survival, stability and prosperity of the Yoruba people now depend on absolute pan-Yoruba unity. We urge all sons and daughters of Omo kaaro oojiire to close ranks, eschew the politics of bitterness and hatred, and unite firmly behind the leadership of Oba Olaitan. Together, we look towards a future in which historical injustices will be rectified and Yoruba heritage and interests secured in a fair and equitable society under God. In assuming this sacred mandate, Oba Olaitan is entrusted with the responsibility of leading with an absolute sense of purpose and unassailable dignity. As a traditional ruler, he is steeped in the exercise of restraint, the application of wisdom and the dignified statesmanship assured by his royal pedigree. He knows how to remain immune to transient political persuasions and undue pressures, holding his leadership position not as a political office but as a divine trust for the collective protection of our institutions and people.”
The statement drew the ire of some Afenifere chieftains who expressed disappointment over the faction’s position.
Following the backlash of the statement, Oba Olaitan, Sunday Vanguard gathered, had called for a meeting.
This reporter was informed that Oba Olaitan had seen the handwriting on the wall that his leadership may not go down well even within his camp, hence the need for a meeting on Thursday.
It’s premature to discuss succession plan —Falae
The Chairman of the National Executive Committee of Afenifere, Oba Olu Falae, distanced himself from the Olaitan camp’s stand, saying the move was premature.
Falae also said it was contrary to Yoruba culture to discuss leadership succession before the burial of its late leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti.
Oba Falae, who spoke in Akure when a condolence message was delivered to the family, had said it was inappropriate to discuss who succeeds a leader before he is buried.
Taking a swipe at the Olaitan camp, the former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF) insisted that the priority of the organization is to give Pa Fasoranti a befitting burial, after which a credible leader would emerge to lead the group.
He had said: “Any discussion on leadership succession is premature and contrary to Yoruba culture. It is inappropriate to discuss who succeeds a leader before he is buried.”
Forceful acquisition of Afenifere is dead on arrival —Adejumo
Shedding light on the controversy surrounding Afenifere, a former spokesperson for the Yoruba body, Mogaji Gboyega Adejumo—an Afenifere Independent—spoke on the ideological divide and question of leadership.
He also emphasised that Yoruba politics has been divided since the era of Chief Obafemi Awolowo.
Awolowo championed egalitarianism, democratic socialism, and ethical civic responsibility (Omoluabi).
Adejumo said: “How does someone simply wake up one day and announce himself as the leader in a situation where two distinct and ideologically different factions exist?”
Going down memory lane, the Afenifere chieftain explained the Yoruba concept of Omoluabi, which he said has shaped Yoruba politics for decades.
His words: “Ever since Chief Obafemi Awolowo entered Yoruba politics, and perhaps Nigerian politics more broadly, two distinct tendencies have existed side by side. On the one hand is the progressivism Awolowo introduced which, in some ways, reflects the Yoruba concept of Omoluabi, although it goes much further. This ideological divide has shaped Yoruba politics for decades. Consider everything Awolowo accomplished: His many firsts, his exemplary personal life and integrity, and what he achieved in just nine years in office. Reproducing that record would be extraordinarily difficult because of his commitment to ethics, civic responsibility, social development, and a clear pathway to success across different sectors. His achievements included Africa’s first television station, a modern secretariat, a modern stadium, and the development of Government Reserved Areas such as Bodija and Ikeja GRA. He also helped attract industries and businesses through the philosophy of democratic socialism. Yet reactionary tendencies have persisted throughout Yorubaland among people who present themselves as progressives. Given enough time, those tendencies often reveal themselves. These forces gained the upper hand during the 1962 crisis, when some Yoruba political actors chose to align themselves with the North. We associate that tendency with feudalism and entrenched corruption.
Some Yoruba people simply did not appreciate the Spartan lifestyle Awolowo practised and expected others in public life to embrace. Awolowo wanted a society founded on the principle of the idea that people should be treated with equal dignity, regardless of their background. His vision was one of egalitarianism, fairness, equal opportunity, and justice. But the reactionaries prevailed, contributing to the 1962 crisis, the ensuing counter-accusations, and a series of political irregularities. Today, we have development commissions across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones. Yet Awolowo had already demonstrated the importance of institutionalised development through the Western Region’s development initiatives, particularly the Western Nigeria Development Corporation (WNDC). Awolowo’s ideas were far ahead of those of his reactionary opponents. But the reactionaries had an advantage: They understood the appeal of local loyalties and used it to draw people to their side. The crisis ultimately contributed to Awolowo’s prosecution on charges of treasonable felony, which he maintained were trumped up, and his imprisonment. Other members of his political circle, including S. G. Ikoku and Ayo Adebanjo, also faced persecution. Following the overthrow of Kwame Nkrumah in Ghana, where they had sought refuge, they were deported to Nigeria and served prison terms.
There is something we may never forget, Awolowo never meant for Afenifere to be a Yoruba irredentist group and that should be something that should guide anyone who wants to be the leader. In one of Papa Awolowo’s book, he almost placed a curse on anyone who wants to turn Afenifere into a Yoruba irredentist group. Awolowo maintained that till the end of his life and charged all members to look at Afenifere as a national party. The reason we are Afenifere is because Chief Akinloye gave us that name in 1951 so as to express the meaning of ‘life more abundant’ to the people at the grassroots. If Nigeria must progress, the feudal system in the North must die and Awolowo has said that many times. He maintained it to the end and charged all members that any part of the country that is not aligned with this philosophy, we must go there and plant it, so that we can all begin to see a country that is devoid of feudalism and other forms of cultural interferences that are anti civilisation. Take for example, if Awolowo was not right, how come Afenifere was leader of the opposition in the East when S.G Ikokwu of the Action Group defeated his father, Alvan Ikokwu, of the NCNC. Afenifere later became the leader of the opposition winning at least six seats in the Eastern region. In the North, Afenifere became the leader of opposition with Alhaji Maito of the Action Group and we had about eight members. No other party succeeded in having that. Northern People Congress (NPC) did not have a single seat in any of the places to form the opposition leader. Only the NCNC was able to do that in the West.
That is the philosophy written down in plain sight that Pa Adebanjo followed. Awolowo would cry in his grave to know that a leader, chosen after him, playing the Yoruba irredentist politics that will make it look like Afenifere is only for the Yoruba. That is the bastardization of the Awolowo philosophy. It was only Adebanjo that followed it to the last. The successor of Adebanjo, who is the present Chairman of the SMBLF, has already thrown Adebanjo under the bus. It would lead us to know that the adage of Uthman Dan Fodio which he said that do not trust any man that goes into his household to steal their valuables to give a stranger because such a man will not hesitate to give yours away to other suitors. Forceful acquisition is dead on arrival. So, if someone is trying to throw Adebanjo and those who believe in him under the bus and is tracing his predecessors (Fasoranti, Adesanya, Ajasin and Awolowo) and painfully excluded Adebanjo, then, it is never going to be easy. We are going to have a serious crisis. The Akure people, I have certain feelings and have been getting certain feelers that they will not go along with this. They have formidable people. The Yoruba are not going to be forcefully taken by anyone, it is not going to happen. Let us be clear that this forceful acquisition is dead on arrival.”
Forming a third force in Afenifere
Adejumo continued: “My final contribution to this development would be a concerning call I received from one of our respected elders in the Afenifere, Dr Femi Okurounmu, about three weeks ago and said to me that the two factions of Afenifere are on their death rows. It is almost as if life has departed from Afenifere. He said ‘I and some others have decided to form a third force.’ I promptly rejected that idea because my position is that we have a greater danger ahead of us in the forthcoming elections. The people may not be readily open to having another group because the focus now is the January presidential election. I said ‘why don’t we wait till after the elections and see how we can fit in, where leadership should go and see how we can return Afenifere back to factory mode. Enough of the usurpers and pretenders’.
That is what I told him not knowing that a lot of these things will begin to unfold to lend credence to my position that nothing should be done for now. In the tradition of the Yoruba, when a leader dies, nobody talks about succession until that leader has been given a befitting burial. Then, of course, we cannot be having all these controversial tendencies. That is why what we are seeing is a bit disturbing and destabilising development. Some of us are committed to a true leadership that will emerge from the Afenifere, that will look back and walk the path of the founding fathers such as the Awolowo, Ajasin, Adesanya and Adebanjo mould, especially the Adebanjo mould who followed through to the letter; progressivism. It saddens me greatly that Oba Olaitan, who presided over a meeting of the Afenifere at the country home of the leader, Pa Ayo Adebanjo, in which the whole body of the Afenifere faithful passed a vote of confidence on Pa Adebanjo’s leadership and promptly proclaimed Chief Ayo Adebanjo as the de facto leader and a press release to that effect signed by Oba Olaitan and the Secretary General was promptly issued, to now read from Oba Olaitan’s statement which totally removed the truest leader, Pa Ayo Adebanjo, from the list of his predecessors, simply smack of an act that could not be more ridiculous.
Lastly, there is a huge fundamental gorge that exists between the Adebanjo group and the Fasoranti group. Let us not deceive ourselves that some people exploited Fasoranti at his most vulnerable period so well advanced in age, and these powerful people are with President Tinubu. How on earth would Oba Olaitan think that he would lead a united Afenifere? I think it would be a cheap trick to think that the Fasoranti group would gobble at it and simply fall over and allow Oba Olaitan to lead them. It is not going to happen. It is the Adebanjo faction of the Afenifere that is now aligned with the SDP. There is an arrangement that Afenifere will handle everything that has to do with the SDP in the South-West. A lot has happened in that regard. Who again will be thrown under the bus? Is it President Tinubu and his APC, or will it be Mr. Adewole Adebayo of the SDP that will be thrown under the bus? So, we are a long way from straight forward solution. I am just waiting for the time this whole exercise will begin to look ridiculous.”
According to Adejumo, Adebanjo historically embodied the true, uncompromising ideals of the original Afenifere movement.
He said: “Against this historical background, one can argue that, among those who claimed to represent the true ideals of Afenifere, Chief Ayo Adebanjo embodied those ideals particularly well. Chief Reuben Fasoranti himself reportedly captured this sentiment in his resignation letter, describing Adebanjo as the personification of Afenifere. When Fasoranti eventually left the scene, one could reasonably ask whether he had navigated the political situation successfully. After all, it was Adebanjo who had helped bring him into the leadership position in the first place.”
Sharing a perspective of how Fasoranti emerged as Afenifere leader, Adejumo explained how Adebanjo declined to take the leadership position.
He said: “This was not the first time Afenifere had faced the question of succession. When Chief Abraham Adesanya became seriously ill and suffered a stroke, he wanted to identify a successor. He called two senior Afenifere members, Olanihun Ajayi and Chief Ayo Adebanjo, and asked them to choose between themselves.”
Ijebu mafia
Adejumo explained further: “Adebanjo, however, declined to take the position. He explained that he and others from Ijebu had long been labelled the Ijebu mafia, a description he rejected. He worried that his emergence as leader might reinforce that perception and deepen divisions within the organisation. Instead, he proposed finding someone who was respected, approachable, and capable of bringing the different tendencies within Afenifere together without being immediately identified with a particular faction. When asked whom he had in mind, Adebanjo suggested Fasoranti. The suggestion initially surprised Adesanya, who did not immediately recall Fasoranti as a prominent member of the inner caucus. Adebanjo explained that Fasoranti had been involved with the organisation since 1953 and had served as Commissioner for Finance under Chief Michael Ajasin when Ajasin was governor of Ondo State. Fasoranti was not a member of the inner caucus, but that was precisely part of the attraction. He had not been at the forefront of the controversies surrounding the treasonable felony case, nor had he been among those most traumatised by the military repression associated with the Abacha era. At the time, he was a retired school principal, who was only managing his business. Adebanjo believed that someone with this background could provide the organisation with the kind of leadership capable of rallying together its different members. And so Fasoranti emerged as leader. Unfortunately, from around 2008,
Afenifere entered a period of turbulence. The organisation struggled to maintain its momentum, while Fasoranti faced pressure from political forces that opposed his leadership. Those forces encouraged the emergence of competing figures, including Ayo Fasanmi, followed by Biyi Durojaiye and Chief Olusi, deepening the internal divisions. The situation troubled Fasoranti greatly. By 2015, he had reportedly had enough and was considering stepping aside. This was despite Afenifere’s significant contribution, alongside the Jonathan administration, to the 2014 National Conference. Once again, Adebanjo intervened and persuaded Fasoranti to continue. Meanwhile, Fasoranti was increasingly inclined to retire. Some members of his inner circle in Akure, Ondo State, were reportedly spreading claims that he was becoming senile, and there were concerns that some were positioning themselves to take control from him. Fasoranti therefore moved quickly and announced Adebanjo as acting leader. Many of us regarded this as one leader doing the right thing by another. Oba Olaitan was subsequently made deputy leader. Afenifere gained renewed visibility under Adebanjo. He became a prominent public voice, attracting new members and reviving the organization’s reputation as a principled political movement.”
Support for Peter Obi in 2023
Adejumo noted: “As the 2023 presidential election approached, Adebanjo began consulting members about the organisation’s political position. The discussions had reportedly started as early as 2021 and continued over approximately two years. I was the Publicity Secretary at the time, and I participated alongside other members of the executive. Adebanjo’s argument was rooted in equity. He maintained that the Igbo had not yet had an opportunity to produce a Nigerian president, while the North and the Yoruba had each held the presidency for eight years. The South-South had also produced President Goodluck Jonathan, although his tenure was shorter than eight years. Adebanjo argued that Nigerians should consider giving the Igbo a chance. Equity, he believed, was an essential route to justice. His objective was a Nigeria in which no region felt permanently excluded from the nation’s highest office. That was how we rallied behind the presidential candidacy of Peter Obi.
There is much more to say about that election, but one point deserves emphasis. Without Obi’s candidacy, President Bola Tinubu might not have become president. The votes Obi attracted in the seven states he won, together with the Federal Capital Territory, could otherwise have substantially strengthened Atiku Abubakar’s position against Tinubu. Given the historical voting patterns in the South-East, where the PDP had traditionally performed strongly, it is reasonable to argue that Obi’s emergence significantly altered the electoral contest. We must also acknowledge the longstanding tensions between the Yoruba and Igbo. I had previously tried to help bring the two groups closer together through Afenifere. That effort has not yet achieved all its objectives, but reconciliation remains a work in progress. In supporting Obi, Adebanjo was acting on his conviction that political equity could help strengthen national unity. Paradoxically, however, the votes Obi attracted may also have benefited President Tinubu by dividing the opposition vote. In that sense, one could argue that Adebanjo’s decision indirectly helped create the electoral conditions that enabled President Tinubu to win the presidency.
Let us leave that debate for another occasion and turn to the present crisis.
