items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The federal government on Friday increased the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.29 per litre while keeping the petrol price unchanged for the next three days.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, petrol will continue to be sold at Rs377.91 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs402.96 per litre from Oct 31 to Nov 2.
The latest revision comes a day after the government raised the price of diesel by 85 paisa per litre for Oct 29, taking its price above the Rs400 mark.
Read: Diesel crosses Rs400 mark, petrol remains unchanged for Oct 30
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Also Read: Oil set for fourth monthly gain as Hormuz tanker attack highlights supply risks
Oil prices jumped by more than 2 per cent on Friday, on pace for a fourth straight monthly gain, as a tanker was struck in the Strait of Hormuz and the US reiterated the possibility of renewing hostilities in Iran.
Brent, the benchmark for two-thirds of the world's crude, was up 2.37 per cent at $117.56 a barrel at 7.32pm UAE time. West Texas Intermediate, the gauge that tracks US crude, added 2.13 per cent to $104.17 a barrel.
The Yemeni army targeted Saudi Aramco in a massive wave of missile ​attacks, according to a media report.
Those reports of a new spate of attacks helped oil recoup some losses later in the session, said ​John Kilduff, partner at Again Capital.
Earlier, US Vice President JD Vance sought to revive peace negotiations by sending a ⁠letter to Mohsen Rezaei, the head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, the Wall Street Journal said on Wednesday, citing US officials and people familiar with ​the matter.
"Oil prices are under pressure today amid renewed diplomatic efforts to de-escalate the conflict in the Middle East," UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo said.

items.author: Meha Agarwal
items.content:
OfBusiness is heading for the stock market with a business that earns most of its revenue in one place and most of its profits in another. Commerce, which spans raw-material trading, manufacturing and apparel, brings in almost all its sales. Yet its lending business, led by Oxyzo, contributes more than half its segment profits despite being a fraction of commerce’s size. Ahead of the IPO, the question is whether commerce can earn more from its scale, or whether lending will keep carrying the profits.
The startup began its journey by helping small and medium enterprises buy raw materials and access working capital. Over the past decade, it has gone from sourcing steel and chemicals for manufacturers to making some of those products itself, expanding into apparel and building a sizable lending business through Oxyzo.
Along the way, it has achieved something relatively rare in India’s B2B commerce sector. Not only has OfBusiness built a ₹20,000 Cr-plus profitable business, but both the company and its lending arm Oxyzo have independently achieved unicorn status.
That’s a notable contrast with B2B commerce peers such as Udaan, Moglix and Zetwerk, which have struggled with losses. Infra.Market is another exception, having reported ₹220 Cr in net profit on ₹18,472 Cr in revenue in FY25.
But as the company prepares for its stock market debut, its FY26 financials reveal an interesting shift. Consolidated operating revenue declined nearly 8% year on year, even as net profit climbed 21% to ₹724 Cr. One business is key on revenue and another on balance sheet with both contributing to ~50% of profits
Commerce, which includes raw-material trading and manufacturing, generated 93% of OfBusiness’ ₹20,472 Cr consolidated operating revenue in FY26. Yet financial services, led by Oxyzo, accounted for more than half its segment pre-tax profits. The lending-led business generated ₹505 Cr in profit before tax, compared with ₹422 Cr from commerce.
Considering the varying nature of the commerce and lending business, the key question is if OfBusiness can simultaneously deliver growth in returns on its commerce business along with the lending business as both scale.
The answer lies in how its procurement, manufacturing, customer-discovery and financing operations work together. Here’s how the business makes money, and where its economics are changing.
The Commerce Engine Is Changing
OfBusiness’ commerce business runs on three layers: raw-material trading, manufacturing and finished goods. Trading brings scale, manufacturing helps improve margins, and finished goods open up new markets.
The first layer is straightforward. OfBusiness aggregates demand from manufacturers, sources materials and manages pricing, quality and delivery. More than 12,000 SMEs and emerging corporates transacted on OfCommerce in FY26, across a catalogue of 103 products.
Its business-discovery platforms help build the pipeline: BidAssist matches companies with government tenders. It had crossed 1.3 Mn subscribers by FY26 and reached 1.7 Mn in October 2026. Nexizo, launched in 2025, offers AI-led buyer discovery, market intelligence and raw-material price insights.
These services give the group a way to reach SMEs before they need procurement or credit; neither platform’s standalone revenue is disclosed. But there’s a limitation to this model. Commodity trading is a high-volume, low-margin business, and fluctuations in prices can quickly affect revenue.
This was evident in FY26. Owing to exit of some the low-return products, Metals, OfBusiness’ largest category, saw sales decline 20% to ₹10,434 Cr. Chemicals grew just 4% to ₹3,663 Cr, while food processing and other products fell 55% to ₹1,636 Cr.
Part of the contraction was strategic. OfBusiness said it exited lower-return commerce categories and discontinued operations to prioritise margins and manufacturing integration. But the shareholder letter also cites lower mild-steel prices and delays in two mega projects. The disclosures do not isolate how much of the metal’s decline came from deliberate exits versus these headwinds.
The second layer, manufacturing, is OfBusiness’ attempt to improve these economics. As cofounder Asish Mohapatra said in September 2026, “As these ecosystems deepen, we are building manufacturing capabilities selectively in categories where we see an opportunity to add value to the supply chain.”
Instead of simply buying and reselling materials, it selectively manufactures products where greater control over production can improve quality, supply and margins.
In metals, the FY26 annual report identifies six of 26 products manufactured in-house under brands including Noble, Bison and Sangam Steel, with more than 1.1 Mn tonnes of annual capacity. It also reports that structural-steel capacity expanded from 100,000 to 500,000 tonnes a year.
Chemicals follow the same logic. The FY26 report identifies in-house manufacturing for eight of 26 chemical products, with annual capacity exceeding 80,000 tonnes, and an expansion in ethyl acetate capacity from 10,000 to 80,000 tonnes. The aim is to capture more value from selected products without abandoning the broader trading catalogue.
The strategy is selective rather than a complete shift away from trading. In a September 2026 update, the company described manufacturing capabilities across more than 40 products and plans to expand into herbicides and pesticides.
The economics are improving, even as sales contract. Commerce revenue fell 9.7% to ₹19,056 Cr in FY26, but its reported segment result excluding other income rose from ₹303 Cr to ₹527 Cr.
In his shareholder letter, cofounder Asish Mohapatra separately reported commerce EBITDA of ₹769 Cr, up 37.9%.
The two measures are not interchangeable, and neither reveals manufacturing’s standalone margin. What they do establish is that commerce earnings improved despite lower revenue.
The question is whether this improvement can continue as the business invests in capacity, rather than relying on commodity-price recovery or portfolio exits.
Fashion And Apparel Is Emerging As Fastest-Growing Business
If metals are OfBusiness’ biggest revenue generator, fashion and apparel is becoming its fastest-growing category.
The segment, which includes apparel, footwear and accessories, saw its revenue surge 141% from ₹1,171 Cr in FY25 to ₹2,828 Cr in FY26, more than doubling in a year. Interestingly, of the where ₹1,171 Cr segment revenue in FY25, INR 376 Cr was apparel alone.
Unlike its traditional raw-material business, OfBusiness’ apparel operations focus on supplying finished products to global brands. It works with smaller manufacturers, manages product development, quality approvals and production, and handles everything from order fulfilment to international deliveries.
As of March 2026, OfBusiness had developed capabilities to serve over 70 brands, including Michael Kors, Uniqlo, Adidas, IKEA, GAP and Zara. Its apparel operations spanned 21 processing facilities, with annual in-house manufacturing capacity exceeding 40 Mn units.
Acquisitions have played a major role in OfBusiness’ apparel expansion. It acquired footwear manufacturer Alpine Shoes in October 2024, followed by Bengaluru-based garment and home-textile exporter Indian Designs Exports in FY26, which became wholly owned in January 2026.
The acquisitions have broadened the product range and manufacturing footprint, but the report does not separate acquired growth from organic growth.
In an August 2026 statement, cofounder Vasant Sridhar said, “Apparel has demonstrated how our model scales when we combine manufacturing capability with deep customer relationships and global market access.”
The statement describes the company’s strategic rationale, not a separately disclosed measure of apparel profitability. That matters when assessing whether the sevenfold increase can be sustained.
For smaller apparel manufacturers, OfBusiness takes on global customer acquisition, certifications, quality approvals and delivery, allowing suppliers to concentrate on production.
Unlike commodity resale, this model can capture value through product development, processing and fulfilment.
Oxyzo: The Bigger Profit Contributor
Oxyzo is an equal profit contributor to the Group. In FY26, OfBusiness’ financial services segment, led by the NBFC, generated ₹1,415 Cr in revenue, up 23%, and ₹505 Cr in profit before tax, up 11%. That is nearly 55% of the group’s combined segment PBT from less than 7% of consolidated operating revenue as Oxyzo is a lending/ balance sheet business and the major driver of profitability is AuM instead of revenue which was INR 10,706 Cr as of March 2026.
Oxyzo lends for working capital, raw-material purchases and business expansion. Its advantage is access to SMEs already engaging with OfBusiness’ commerce and business-discovery platforms. A company finding contracts through BidAssist or buyers through Nexizo may later need supplies and credit; that creates cross-selling potential, although the annual report does not quantify conversions or acquisition-cost savings.
Its underwriting combines financial and external data with customer information and technology. In an October 2026 company commentary on account management, cofounder Mohapatra observed, “We got there because of sales, but we stayed there because of KAM.”
That emphasis on maintaining customer relationships also matters to a model that seeks repeat procurement and financing business. For some purchase-financing loans, Oxyzo pays suppliers directly, offering greater visibility over how the funds are used. That is a structural link between the commerce transaction and the lending product, not simply a referral arrangement.
At FY26-end, Oxyzo reported a ₹10,706 Cr loan book, more than 60,000 MSME and emerging corporate borrowers, a 0.74% gross NPA ratio and operating expenses at 2.4% of average assets. These metrics indicate scale and reported asset quality, but do not remove exposure to funding costs and credit losses.
Its acquisition of fixed-income distribution platform Golden Pi broadens the financing proposition. OfBusiness held 74.43% of Oxyzo at FY26-end, so the subsidiary’s profits are not entirely attributable to parent shareholders.
Management wants to lift Oxyzo’s return on equity from the early double digits to the mid-double digits and diversify funding beyond banks. The challenge is to grow the loan book without requiring disproportionate capital or weakening credit quality.
What Lies Ahead For OfBusiness?
For OfBusiness, the next phase will be judged less by how much it sells than by what it earns on the capital tied up in commerce and lending.
Manufacturing can lift the value captured from each industrial order; BidAssist and Nexizo can help originate customer relationships; Oxyzo can finance their purchases. The opportunity is to make those activities reinforce one another rather than merely add to revenue.
Mohapatra’s targets make the test measurable: lift commerce return on capital employed from the late single digits to the early double digits, and financing return on equity from the early to the mid-double digits.
The group generated ₹1,256 Cr in operating cash flow, invested ₹881 Cr and reported ₹375 Cr of free cash flow in FY26, with an ambition to fund expansion without shareholder dilution.
International sales are also rising. Consolidated revenue from outside India increased 62% to ₹2,058 Cr in FY26, about 10% of operating revenue. Separately, an August 2026 company update described exports exceeding ₹2,500 Cr.
US tariffs pressured apparel exports during FY26, even as OfBusiness expanded men’s woven apparel and established a Bangladesh manufacturing footprint for outerwear.
Mohapatra has identified European expansion and additional chemicals capacity and marketing presence as priorities for the start of FY28, while flagging West Asian chemical supply disruptions and rising Indian labour costs. Apparel remains much smaller than metals, but its next test is whether growth translates into durable returns.
The unresolved question ahead of the IPO is whether better commerce margins, profitable exports and disciplined lending can sustain that cash generation as capacity and credit demand grow.
Edited By Nikhil Subramanium

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Pakistan’s military is “cautiously optimistic” about its mediation between Iran and the United States, its spokesman said on Friday in his ​first interview since a high-level delegation visited Tehran this week.
Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir — Pakistan's chief mediator in its efforts to ‌de-escalate the now eight-month-old Iran war — has been to Tehran twice this month, most recently on Monday alongside Saudi and Turkish officials.
“Why would the field marshal be going twice if it is not for some positivity? So yes, of course,” spokesman Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said when asked whether the trips were a positive sign.
Pact does not bar new members
“The word ​that we would use is always cautiously optimistic,” added Chaudhry, director general of Inter-Services Public Relations.
There were still "powerful spoilers and detractors," who believed ​conflict serves them, he added without naming them.
Speaking in the garrison city of Rawalpindi, where Pakistan's armed forces are headquartered, ⁠Chaudhry declined to say what was discussed or whether the United States had backed the trip.
Also Read: CDF Munir meets senior Iranian officials as Pakistan continues diplomatic push to end conflict
Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman and Turkish intelligence chief ​Ibrahim Kalin joined CDF Munir in Tehran on Monday.
The two countries signed a joint defence pact with Pakistan on August 7, saying an attack on any signatory will ​be treated as an attack on all.
The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement has taken on added significance as the Iran war has redrawn regional alliances and raised fears of a broader Middle East conflict.
While the three signatories say the agreement is aimed at collective deterrence and regional security, analysts see its evolution as closely tied to efforts by regional powers to manage ​the fallout from the Iran-US confrontation.
After Monday’s talks, Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, said regional security should be ensured by regional ​countries without foreign intervention.
The wording of the pact does not bar new members, Chaudhry said on Friday when asked whether Iran could join.
“Anyone who has a shared vision of collective ‌deterrence and ⁠regional peace, why not? Everyone is most welcome,” he said, adding that it was for the political leadership of the three principal parties to decide.
Asked whether more Pakistani troops were being sent to Saudi Arabia under the agreement, Chaudhry said that would depend on the situation and the decision of both countries’ political leadership.
He said Pakistan was committed to defending Saudi Arabia and the holy sites of Makkah and Madina. "We are not part of the Yemeni conflict, which is an ​intra-Yemen conflict," he added.
Fighting between Saudi ​Arabia and Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi group ⁠has been reignited by the Iran conflict, stoking fears of a wider war.
Home front
On the home front, the federal government suspended the provincial government in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, led by jailed former prime minister Imran Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), on October 11 ​and detained Chief Minister Sohail Afridi.
The government had accused the provincial administration of failing to tackle militancy. The PTI ​rejected the allegations and ⁠says its government took part in counter-terrorism efforts. PTI leaders called the move a pretext to crush protests.
Asked if there would now be larger military-led campaigns in the province, Chaudhry said that was not how the army conducted counter-terrorism.
Read: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia agree to deepen cooperation in oil and energy sector
"Our counter-terrorism operations are based on what we call IBOs, intelligence-based operations... The tempo of the freedom of ⁠action of (those) ​IBOs will further increase," he said.
Independents backed by Khan’s PTI won the most directly elected seats ​in the February 2024 election but fell short of a majority. K-P was the only province controlled by Khan’s party.
Khan has been in jail since 2023, and his supporters see the ​military behind his imprisonment and the dismantlement of the PTI. The army denies involvement in politics.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
PB Fintech’s consolidated net profit zoomed 42.5% to ₹192.4 Cr in the second quarter (Q2) of the fiscal year 2026-27 (FY27), up from ₹135 Cr in the same quarter last year. Sequentially, the company’s net profit rose 18% from ₹163 Cr.
The jump in the bottom line came on the back of operating revenue rising almost 35% to ₹2,177.7 Cr in the quarter under review as against ₹1,613.6 Cr in Q2 FY26. On a quarter-on-quarter (QoQ), the top line jumped 15% from ₹1,888.3 Cr in Q1 FY27.
Including other income of ₹100 Cr, PB Fintech’s total income for the quarter stood at ₹2,277.6. Meanwhile, the insurtech company’s total expenses rose 32.6% to ₹2,067.7 Cr in the September 2026 quarter as against ₹1,558.8 Cr in Q2 FY26.
Giving a segment-wise breakdown of its results, PB Fintech’s core online business, which includes Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, contributed a revenue of ₹1,336 Cr during the quarter under review, up 39.5% YoY. On the other hand, the new initiatives arm added ₹842 Cr to the total revenue tally, up 28% YoY.
In its investor presentation, the company also noted that its adjusted EBITDA profitability further improved by 39% to ₹216 Cr in Q2 FY27, while adjusted EBITDA margins stayed flat YoY at 10%.
On the operational front, PB Fintech’s total insurance premium stood at ₹9,385 Cr in Q2 FY27, growing 38% YoY. The jump came on the back of broad-based growth in both core online new protection and new protection (which include both health and term insurance) premiums at 38% and 42% YoY, respectively.
The company also said that its core renewal/ trail revenue on a 12-month rolling-basis stood at ₹1,097 Cr in Q2 FY27, up 41.7% from ₹774 Cr in the year-ago quarter. On a quarterly annualised basis, core insurance renewal revenue reached ₹1,153 Cr, up 52% YoY.
PB Fintech also said that Policybazaar has onboarded 17.3 Cr registered customers and nearly 3 Cr transacting users to date. It also claims to have facilitated the sale of 7.7 Cr insurance policies since its inception.
On the flip side, Paisabazaar’s loan disbursals tanked 80% to ₹4,739 Cr in the quarter under review as against ₹8,570 in Q2 FY26. The vertical also clocked an annualised run rate of 4 Lakh for card issuances during the quarter ended September 2026.
On the operational front, Paisabazaar expanded to 6.3 Cr users who have checked their credit scores, with 82 Lakh transacting customers to date. The vertical also logged 33 Lakh average monthly enquiries in Q2 FY27.
Besides its flagship platforms, PB Fintech’s partner enablement platform, PB Partners, expanded to over 5.7 Lakh partners across nearly 19,000 pincodes. Its corporate insurance arm also booked 22,000 unique policies for enterprises and small businesses in Q2 FY27.
Shares of PB Fintech closed Friday’s trading session 1.76% lower at ₹1,000 apiece on the BSE.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
WhatsApp is rolling out a new profile customization feature that allows users to add cover photos to their personal accounts. The feature gives users another way to personalize their profiles with a landscape image displayed above their profile picture.
Previously, cover photos were available only to WhatsApp Business accounts. However, the company is now bringing the same option to personal accounts, allowing regular users to customize their profiles without creating a business account.
WhatsApp Introduces Profile Cover Photos for Android Users
According to WABetaInfo, the feature has started rolling out to some Android beta testers through WhatsApp beta version 2.26.43.11, available on the Google Play Store.
WhatsApp Profiles Get a New Cover Photo Option
The new cover photo appears as a landscape banner at the top of a user’s profile page. It does not replace the existing profile picture, so users can display both images at the same time.
WhatsApp will also show the cover photo at the top of the app’s settings section. When someone opens a user’s chat information screen, the cover image will appear above their profile picture, name and phone number.
Users who have not selected a cover photo will see a default image until they upload their own.
How to Add a Cover Photo on WhatsApp
WhatsApp is offering several ways to set up a cover photo. Users can open their profile page and tap the Edit button to access the available options.
They can then take a new picture using their phone’s camera, select an existing image from their gallery or use Meta AI to generate a cover image.
Once users select an image, WhatsApp automatically adjusts and crops it to fit the landscape layout.
WhatsApp Adds Privacy Controls for Cover Photos
The new feature also includes separate privacy settings, allowing users to control who can view their cover photos.
WhatsApp provides four visibility options:
Everyone: Allows all WhatsApp users to see the cover photo.
My Contacts: Limits visibility to people saved in the user’s contacts.
My Contacts Except: Allows users to exclude specific contacts from viewing the image.
Nobody: Hides the cover photo from everyone without removing it from the profile.
The default setting is Everyone. However, users can change this option at any time through their privacy settings.
If someone does not have permission to view a user’s cover photo, WhatsApp will not display the image on the chat information screen.
WhatsApp Cover Photos Rolling Out to Android Beta Testers
The feature is currently available to some users running WhatsApp beta for Android version 2.26.43.11. However, the rollout is gradual, meaning not every beta tester will receive the option immediately.
WhatsApp plans to make the feature available to more beta testers over the coming weeks. Users who cannot see the cover photo option yet may receive it through a future update.
The company has not confirmed when profile cover photos will become available to all Android and iOS users.

Samsung has officially launched its new W27 foldable smartphone in China, introducing a more premium version of its Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra. The new device features an upgraded exterior design, gold-coloured frame details, and high-end specifications, but its price is even higher than Apple’s iPhone Duo.
Samsung Launches W27 Foldable Phone With Premium Design and $2,852 Starting Price
The Samsung W27 is part of the company’s China-exclusive W series, which typically offers Galaxy Z Fold devices with more luxurious designs and additional features. The smartphone is available in two storage configurations, with prices starting at approximately $2,852.
Samsung W27 Features a Premium Design
The Samsung W27 comes with a distinctive design featuring a gold-coloured frame and camera module. Its frame also has a textured finish, while buyers can choose between dark red and dark blue rear panels.
The back panel uses Gorilla Glass Ceramic 3 protection. However, the device retains an IP48 rating, which provides limited protection against dust and water.
Despite its redesigned appearance, the W27 maintains the same dimensions as the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra. It measures 8.9mm when folded and weighs 215 grams.
Samsung W27 Display and Performance
The new foldable smartphone features an 8-inch folding OLED display and a 6.5-inch OLED cover screen. These displays provide a large viewing area when unfolded while allowing users to perform everyday tasks through the external screen.
Samsung has equipped the W27 with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy chipset. The device also packs a 5,000mAh battery to support daily usage.
The smartphone comes with 16GB of RAM and offers two storage options: 512GB and 1TB.
200MP Main Camera and Quad-Camera Setup
The camera system is another major feature of the Samsung W27. It carries a 200MP primary camera, accompanied by a 50MP ultra-wide camera and a 10MP telephoto lens with 3x optical zoom.
For selfies and video calls, the smartphone includes a 10MP camera on both the main folding display and the external screen.
This camera configuration is identical to the one found on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra.
Samsung W27 Price Is Higher Than iPhone Duo
Samsung has launched the W27 in two configurations, with both carrying premium price tags.
The 16GB RAM and 512GB storage model costs 18,999 yuan, approximately $2,852. Meanwhile, the 16GB RAM and 1TB storage variant carries a recommended price of 21,999 yuan, or around $3,303.
For comparison, the 16GB/1TB Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra has a recommended US price of $2,700.
The W27 is also more expensive than Apple’s iPhone Duo in China. The 256GB iPhone Duo costs approximately $2,401, while its 512GB version is priced at around $2,702.
Samsung Includes Additional Accessories
Despite its high price, Samsung is including several accessories in the W27 retail package. Buyers will receive a Kevlar magnetic case, a 45W charging adapter, and a USB-C cable.
The Samsung W27 is currently a China-exclusive release. The company has not announced international availability, so buyers in other markets will have to wait for further details.
With its luxury design, powerful hardware, and high starting price, the W27 targets buyers looking for a premium foldable smartphone rather than a standard Galaxy Z Fold experience.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
To expand welfare coverage for the emerging gig economy, the Labour Ministry has notified the constitution of the National Social Security Board for Unorganised Workers and Gig and Platform Workers under the Code on Social Security, 2020.
The board will be chaired by the Union Minister for Labour & Employment and comprise representatives from the Central and state governments, aggregator companies, employers, civil society organisations, workers’ unions and gig and platform worker associations.
Launched in 2020, the Code on Social Security consolidates nine existing labour laws into a single framework to extend social security benefits, including provident fund, pension, health insurance, maternity benefits and gratuity, to workers across organised and unorganised sectors.
It formally recognises gig and platform workers as employees, making them eligible for government-notified welfare schemes. It also requires eligible aggregators to contribute 1-2% of annual turnover, subject to a cap. The Code came into force on November 21, 2025.
The NSSB’s is tasked with the following functions:
Recommend to the Centre for framing suitable schemes for different sections of unorganised workers, gig workers and platform workers.
Advise the government on such matters arising out of the administration of the code.
Monitor such social welfare schemes for unorganised workers, gig workers and platform workers as are administered by the government.
Review the record keeping functions performed at the State level as well as the expenditure from the fund and account.
“The National Social Security Boards shall meet at least thrice a year and shall observe rules of procedure relating to the transaction of business at its meetings, as prescribed by the Central Government,” the ministry said.
The constitution of the board marks another step towards operationalising the social security framework for gig and platform workers.
The Code provides for social security schemes covering life and disability insurance, accident insurance, health and maternity benefits, and old-age protection.
However, it could translate into additional financial and administrative obligations for companies operating in India’s platform economy, including food delivery, quick commerce, ride hailing and ecommerce players such as Swiggy, Zomato, Blinkit, Zepto, Ola, Uber, Amazon and Flipkart.
The development also comes amid parallel efforts by state governments to extend welfare coverage to gig workers. The Karnataka government, for instance, has constituted a separate Gig Workers’ Welfare Board to oversee social security measures for workers in the state.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) has stepped up its nationwide monitoring of mobile network infrastructure, inspecting more than 900 telecom sites as part of efforts to identify technical problems and improve service quality across the country.
According to an official statement issued on October 30, 2026, the authority inspected 184 mobile sites between October 22 and 28, bringing the cumulative number of monitored sites to over 900.
The inspections covered several cities and districts, including Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Quetta, Swat, Rahim Yar Khan, Nankana Sahib, Mirpur, Kotli, Gilgit, Torghar, South Karachi and Shaheed Benazirabad.
PTA teams also conducted inspections in rural areas of Arifwala to assess network infrastructure and identify issues affecting telecom services.
The monitoring exercise was carried out in coordination with district administrations, elected representatives, local stakeholders and telecom operators to ensure that identified problems could be addressed through the relevant authorities.
Power Failures, Battery Faults and Fibre-Optic Issues Identified
During the inspections, PTA identified several infrastructure-related shortcomings that could affect the reliability and quality of mobile network services.
The major findings included electricity supply problems, inadequate power backup arrangements, faulty batteries and generators, and deficiencies in telecom equipment.
The authority also highlighted concerns regarding the safety of fibre-optic cables, along with administrative and other infrastructure-related issues at mobile sites.
Such problems can affect the availability and reliability of mobile services, particularly in areas where network infrastructure depends on backup power during electricity outages.
According to PTA, the nationwide field monitoring initiative aims to identify these deficiencies and work with telecom operators and other stakeholders to resolve them.
The authority said it is pursuing corrective measures through continued inspections and coordination with relevant departments.
The latest exercise reflects PTA’s ongoing efforts to strengthen mobile network infrastructure and improve telecom service quality in both urban and rural areas.
However, PTA has not specified how many of the identified issues have already been resolved or provided a timeline for completing all corrective measures.
For mobile users, the effectiveness of these inspections will ultimately depend on whether the identified infrastructure problems are addressed and result in more reliable network coverage and connectivity.

Motorola has officially confirmed November 5 as the launch date for its upcoming flagship smartphone, the Motorola Signature 27. The announcement follows earlier teasers in India, where the company had indicated that the device would arrive sometime in November.
Motorola Signature 27 Launch Set for November 5 With Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6
First showcased at the Qualcomm Snapdragon Summit in September, the Signature 27 is designed to deliver flagship-level performance, advanced camera capabilities, and improved thermal management. The smartphone will feature Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 Mobile Platform, positioning it as a high-performance device for gaming, photography, and AI-powered tasks.
Snapdragon Processor and Improved Cooling System
Motorola has focused on thermal management to maintain performance during demanding activities such as gaming, extended camera use, and on-device AI processing.
The Signature 27 features an ArcticMesh cooling system with a vapor chamber that is 40 percent larger than the one used in its predecessor. The upgraded cooling solution is designed to control heat more effectively and maintain stable performance during intensive workloads.
Motorola Signature 27 Camera Features
The camera system is another major highlight of the upcoming flagship. Motorola has equipped the Signature 27 with Sony’s LYTIA 910 50MP primary sensor. It will come alongside a 200MP periscope telephoto camera designed to capture detailed images of distant subjects.
The company has also introduced a multi-layer stabilisation system to reduce camera shake and motion blur in photographs and videos.
The system includes 3.5-axis Optical Image Stabilisation (OIS), which helps minimise physical camera movement during low-light photography and longer exposures. Qualcomm Electronic Image Stabilisation (EIS) works alongside the device’s image signal processor to improve handheld video recording.
Motorola’s Video Enhancement Engine further optimises dynamic range, exposure and frame consistency while recording videos.
Android 17 and Seven Years of Updates
On the software side, the Motorola Signature 27 will ship with Android 17. Motorola has also committed to providing up to seven years of system updates, offering users a longer software support period.
Another major development is the smartphone’s expected compatibility with GrapheneOS, a privacy-focused operating system based on Android.
In September, GrapheneOS developers confirmed on X that the Signature 27 would become the first non-Google Pixel smartphone to officially support the operating system.
GrapheneOS focuses on security and privacy through hardware-level protection, restricted tracking mechanisms, sandboxed Google Play services, and additional kernel-level security features.
However, it remains unclear whether Motorola will offer the Signature 27 with GrapheneOS pre-installed or require users to install it manually after purchasing the device. Further details are expected following the official launch.
Launch Details Expected Soon
Motorola has confirmed November 5 as the official launch date for the Signature 27.
More information about the India launch, availability, and pricing is expected soon. The November 5 announcement should also reveal additional details about the smartphone’s specifications and market availability.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan is targeting up to 50 percent domestic value addition in mobile phone manufacturing under a new policy being formulated by the government. The initiative aims to shift the industry from import-dependent assembly towards local component manufacturing and higher-value industrial production.
According to an official document, the Ministry of Industries and Production is evaluating a new Mobile Device Manufacturing Policy to build on the investment attracted under the previous Mobile Device Manufacturing Policy 2020–2023. The earlier policy facilitated the establishment of domestic and foreign-invested mobile phone assembly and manufacturing facilities in the country.
Pakistan Targets 50% Localisation in New Mobile Phone Manufacturing Policy
The proposed policy envisages progressively increasing localisation to as much as 50 percent over time through the development of local component manufacturing and a supporting industrial ecosystem.
Currently, domestic value addition in mobile device manufacturing is estimated at around 10 to 20 percent, indicating considerable room for improvement.
The government is pursuing a broader policy agenda to reduce reliance on imported components and promote higher domestic value addition across key engineering and manufacturing sectors.
In this regard, the Ministry of Industries and Production is working on sector-specific policies covering the automotive industry, mobile device manufacturing, battery energy storage systems and other engineering sectors.
In the electronics and mobile device sector, the government intends to promote local component production, technology transfer and the development of supporting industries through the proposed policy.
The initiative aims to move beyond basic assembly operations towards a stronger domestic manufacturing base. It could also create opportunities for local suppliers and increase the industry’s contribution to industrial development.
However, the success of the proposed policy will depend on the development of a competitive local component supply chain and the ability to attract investment in higher-value manufacturing activities.
Pakistan Assembles Over 20 Million Mobile Phones in 2026
Pakistan’s local mobile phone manufacturing plants produced 20.08 million handsets during January-September 2026, compared to just 2.85 million units imported commercially. The figures reflect the growing role of local assembly in meeting domestic demand.
According to official data, locally assembled handsets included around eight million smartphones and 12 million 2G phones.
Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) data shows that smartphones account for 71 percent of active mobile devices on local networks, while 2G phones make up the remaining 29 percent.
Mobile Phone Import Bill Declines in FY2026-27
Pakistan’s mobile phone import bill declined by 16.6 percent in dollar terms during the first quarter of fiscal year 2026-27, falling to $417.24 million from approximately $500.01 million in the same period last year.
In September 2026, mobile phone imports increased by 7.1 percent month-on-month to $143.14 million, compared to $133.66 million in August. However, imports remained 28.2 percent lower than the $199.27 million recorded in September 2025.
In rupee terms, the mobile phone import bill stood at Rs39.75 billion in September, up seven percent from Rs37.17 billion in August. On a year-on-year basis, however, it declined by 29.2 percent from Rs56.17 billion.
During July-September FY27, the cumulative mobile phone import bill fell to Rs116.01 billion, down 18 percent from Rs141.42 billion in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year.
The figures show that despite a monthly recovery in September, mobile phone imports remained significantly lower than a year earlier, while local assembly continued to supply the bulk of handsets entering the domestic market.
VGO TEL Becomes Pakistan’s Largest Local Phone Producer
Pakistan’s local mobile phone assembly industry is expanding, with VGO TEL emerging as the largest producer in January-September 2026. The company overtook Infinix and Itel, while local manufacturers continued to dominate the country’s handset market.
According to data on locally assembled and manufactured mobile devices, VGO TEL produced 2.50 million handsets during the first nine months of 2026, followed by Infinix at 1.96 million and Itel at 1.59 million.
TECNO ranked fourth with 1.16 million units, followed by Samsung at 1.04 million, Vivo at 0.99 million and Nokia at 0.97 million. Other major producers included China Mobile at 0.72 million, X Mobile at 0.71 million and G’FIVE at 0.64 million.
Infinix Previously Led Local Mobile Phone Production
The data reflects a shift in production rankings compared with previous years, when Infinix topped the list of local assemblers.
In 2024, Infinix produced 3.98 million handsets, followed by Itel at 3.64 million and VGO TEL at 3.37 million.
In 2025, Infinix retained the top position with 3.65 million units, narrowly ahead of VGO TEL at 3.57 million. Vivo ranked third with 2.80 million, followed by Itel at 2.34 million.
The figures highlight the growing presence of local assembly operations across multiple brands, including Chinese manufacturers and established international handset companies.
However, production remains spread across a range of manufacturers rather than concentrated in a single brand. VGO TEL’s performance in the first nine months of 2026 marks a notable change in the competitive landscape.
Future Growth Depends on Local Component Manufacturing
The expansion of domestic assembly has become an important feature of Pakistan’s mobile phone market, helping reduce reliance on commercially imported finished handsets.
However, the sustainability of this trend will depend on consumer demand, access to imported components, exchange-rate stability and the ability of local assemblers to maintain competitive prices.
The proposed 50 percent localisation target represents a further step towards developing Pakistan’s domestic mobile manufacturing industry. Achieving this goal will require investment in local component production, technology transfer and a competitive supply chain.
It is worth noting that the production figures for 2026 cover January to September only, while the figures for 2024 and 2025 represent full calendar years.

items.author: Akshit Pushkarna
items.content:
Logistics company Delhivery reported a consolidated net profit of ₹40.6 Cr in the September quarter of FY27 (Q2) against a loss of ₹50.5 Cr in the year-ago period, as revenue growth outpaced the increase in expenses. Sequentially, net profit rose 27.4% from ₹31.9 Cr in Q1 FY27.
Operating revenue increased 19.8% YoY and 4.6% QoQ to ₹3,066.4 Cr during the quarter. Including other income of ₹66.6 Cr, Delhivery’s total income stood at ₹3,133 Cr, compared with ₹2,651.5 Cr in Q2 FY26.
Total expenses rose 14.2% YoY to ₹3,093 Cr from ₹2,708.1 Cr. Freight, handling and servicing costs, the company’s largest expense head, increased 19.1% to ₹2,195.1 Cr from ₹1,842.9 Cr.
Delhivery reported a pre-tax profit of ₹39 Cr against a pre-tax loss of ₹53.2 Cr in the year-ago quarter. A net tax credit of ₹1.6 Cr took its consolidated net profit to ₹40.6 Cr.
However, the profit comparisons reflect the impact of the Ecom Express’ acquisition on earlier quarters. Delhivery said its net profit in Q2 FY26 and Q1 FY27 would have stood at ₹59 Cr and ₹62 Cr, respectively, excluding the acquisition’s impact.
Delhivery’s Operating Performance
Delhivery handled 325 Mn express parcel shipments in Q2 FY27, up 32.1% YoY. Part truckload (PTL) freight volumes rose 14.2% to 5.45 Lakh metric tonnes during the quarter.
The company attributed express volume growth to market share gains and demand across its diversified customer base. It said October volumes had exceeded initial expectations, providing an encouraging start to the December quarter.
Express parcel revenue grew 21.7% YoY to ₹1,961 Cr, while PTL revenue increased 23.1% to ₹672 Cr.
Delhivery also reported improvements in realisations, or revenue earned per shipment or unit of freight. Express and PTL realisations increased 4.1% and 5.6% QoQ, respectively, primarily driven by fuel-linked price increases and revisions to cover minimum wage inflation.
PTL realisations also benefited from new customer additions, repricing of existing accounts, and a better customer and shipment mix.
Adjusted EBITDA increased 48% YoY to ₹123 Cr, with its margin improving to 4% from 3.3% in Q2 FY26. Reported EBITDA more than tripled to ₹205 Cr from ₹68 Cr, while its margin expanded to 6.7% from 2.7%.
Delhivery incurred no Ecom Express integration costs during the quarter, compared with ₹90 Cr a year earlier and ₹17 Cr in Q1 FY27.
The company expects service EBITDA margins in both its express and PTL businesses to expand through the remainder of FY27, supported by pricing revisions and higher network utilisation. It expects express service EBITDA margins to reach 16-18% by the end of FY27 and PTL margins to exceed 15%.
New Businesses, Technology Investments
Alongside its core logistics operations, Delhivery is scaling newer businesses, including its intra-city logistics platform Delhivery Local, international operations and financial services.
Delhivery Local is currently operational across eight cities, including Delhi NCR, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Pune and Chennai. Its annualised revenue run rate has doubled from around ₹100 Cr at the end of Q1 FY27 to approximately ₹200 Cr.
The company has raised its FY27 exit annualised revenue target for the business to ₹280 Cr from its earlier guidance of ₹250 Cr. It also aims to scale the business to an annualised revenue run rate of ₹800-1,000 Cr over the next two years.
Meanwhile, its financial services business is building distribution channels for financial products across its vendor ecosystem and developing co-lending partnerships.
Delhivery’s board also approved an equity investment of up to ₹36 Cr in wholly owned subsidiary Delhivery Fintech Distribution, in one or more tranches, to support its operational and business requirements.
It also highlighted its investments in AI and automation to improve productivity and reduce operating costs. It said AI-led automation has reduced customer support and proof-of-delivery validation costs by over 50%, without compromising output quality.
The company said it has started producing customised autonomous mobile robots through Delhivery Labs and plans to deploy 100 self-developed autonomous pallet transportation vehicles by Q4 FY27.
Shares of Delhivery ended today’s trading session 3.02% lower at ₹386 apiece on the BSE.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
Markets regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has cleared the ₹450 Cr IPO of consumer appliances company Atomberg today.
In its update, the SEBI informed that it had issued its observation letter to Atomberg on October 30, over a couple months after the company filed its draft IPO papers. In SEBI parlance, the issuance of the final observation marks the regulator’s formal clearance to a company to proceed with its public offering.
As per its DRHP, Atomberg’s proposed IPO could comprise a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to ₹450 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) component of up to 7.65 Cr equity shares.
The company plans to use ₹90 Cr from the fresh issue proceeds to repay or prepay certain borrowings, ₹150 Cr towards brand awareness and performance marketing, and ₹100 Cr towards research and development (R&D). The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.
Meanwhile, its investors like A91 partners, Temasek Holdings, Inflexor Ventures, among others, intend to dilute their stake in the appliance manufacturer via the IPO.
Founded in 2012 by Manoj Meena, who was joined by Sibabrata Das as cofounder in 2013, Atomberg builds consumer appliances such as ceiling fans, mixer grinders, water purifiers and cold-pressed juicers. It also manufactures proprietary components, including motors and controllers, for enterprise customers such as Voltas, Godrej and Blue Star through its subsidiary, Atomberg Innovations.
The company operates two business segments — consumer appliances and proprietary components. It sells its products through online channels, including ecommerce marketplaces and quick commerce platforms, as well as offline distributors, retailers and modern trade chains.
For FY26, Atomberg reported operating revenue of ₹1,293.77 Cr, up 34.8% from ₹959.51 Cr in FY25. Meanwhile, the company’s consolidated net loss widened 26.8% to ₹148.9 Cr from ₹117.4 Cr.
On the operational front, Atomberg had a network of 626 distributors and direct dealers, with 46,932 retail touchpoints across around 1,600 cities and towns as of March 31, 2026. Its distribution network covered all Indian states, while its after-sales service network extended to more than 18,000 pin codes.
Meanwhile, tier II and smaller cities contributed the largest share of its offline consumer appliances revenue at 49.57% in FY26. Metropolitan cities accounted for 30.91%, while Tier 1 cities contributed the remaining 19.52%.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Spacetech startup Manastu Space raised ₹22 Cr ($2.3 Mn) from Gandhi Securities and Investments, the Thacker Legacy Trusts, and a clutch of angel investors in what appears to be an extension of its Series A funding round.
It appears the startup intends to raise a further ₹9.2 Cr from Capital A that has yet to be confirmed. The round size can change before its closure.
Beyond this sum, the startup also initially issued CCPS worth a further ₹2.5 Cr to Aakash founder Aakash Chaudhry, which were later cancelled.
Inc42 accessed the funding details through Manastu’s regulatory filings. Queries sent to the startup went unanswered until the time of publication.
“The purpose of the offer is to raise funds for the research & development, growth, expansion, marketing and general corporate activities of the Company,” its disclosures with the MCA read.
Notably, the science and technology ministry’s Technology Development Board (TDB) also recently announced that it had committed ₹116 Cr in funding to Manastu in the form of optionally convertible debentures.
Founded in 2017 by Tushar Jadhav and Ashtesh Kumar, Manastu is developing a green propulsion system for satellites coupled with its in-orbit refuelling system and debris avoidance technology to reduce the risk of orbital congestion.
The startup has developed a proprietary hydrogen peroxide-based fuel that it claims gives 50% higher performance and is less harmful to the environment than conventional toxic propellants like hydrazine.
Besides, its debris avoidance systems enable satellites to manoeuvre in orbit, avoid collisions with space debris, adjust trajectories and de-orbit at the end of their operational lives.
Until now, it has raised $9 Mn from Capital-A, Capital 2B, Indian Angel Network (IAN), E2MC, BIG Capital, and others. It last raised $3 Mn in another Series A round extension back in August 2025 to commercially roll out its green propulsion and debris-avoidance system.
Manastu competes with the likes of Bellatrix Aerospace and Dhruva Space in the global market for satellite propulsion systems, which is projected to grow at 17.6% CAGR to reach $4.7 Bn by 2031.

items.author: Michael Robuck
items.content:
Global smartphone shipments fell 20% year-on-year to 254.7 million units in Q3, the lowest volume for the period in more than a decade, Omdia reported.
Omdia noted rising device costs and component shortages continued to weaken consumer demand in emerging markets. Distributors and retailers also remained cautious about restocking as higher device costs raised working capital needs and limited inventories.
Principal analyst Sanyam Chaurasia said regions which once drove shipment growth faced the greatest pressure on affordability.
Shipments in Africa fell 39%, the largest regional decline, forcing vendors to prioritise margins over volumes.
Samsung remained the largest vendor, shipping 57.8 million smartphones globally, though this was 5% less than in Q3 2025.
Its entry-level Galaxy A series and the Z8 foldable range are credited as contributing to Samsung’s performance.
Apple’s shipments were flat at 56.5 million units: Omdia noted the vendor’s iPhone 18 launch schedule effectively extended the run of its previous model, which it stated continued to ship well in North America and China.
Chinese vendors experienced larger declines.
Xiaomi’s shipments fell 29% to 30.7 million units as it adjusted prices in China and India.
Oppo and Vivo’s shipments dropped 39% and 33%, respectively as they raised prices to cover higher component costs.
Omdia forecast full-year shipments would decrease by around 12%, while persistent shortages of high-bandwidth and conventional memory could keep hardware costs high well into 2027.
The data is broadly in line with IDC figures showing shipments dropped 22% to 255.3 million.

During September, PTA recorded 6,658 complaints against cellular operators, of which 6,434 were resolved, representing a resolution rate of 96.65 percent.
Jazz Records Highest Complaints, Followed by Telenor and Zong
According to the operator-wise breakdown, Jazz received the highest number of complaints at 3,005, of which 2,915 were resolved, reflecting a 97 percent resolution rate.
Telenor followed with 1,325 complaints, with 1,282 addressed, while Zong received 1,309 complaints and resolved 1,263.
Meanwhile, Ufone recorded 985 complaints, of which 943 were resolved during the reporting period.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
Nigerian AI engineering talent platform Talent Nation, co-founded by serial entrepreneur Iyinoluwa Aboyeji, has raised an undisclosed pre-seed funding round as it looks to train and deploy one million African AI engineers over the next decade.
Co-founded by Aboyeji, who was behind Andela, Flutterwave and Moove, and South Africa-born lawyer Kesiah Valkin, who previously co-founded London-based 01 Founders, Talent Nation trains, certifies and deploys AI engineers into organisations looking to build their own AI capability.
The startup is betting that AI will increase demand for engineering talent rather than reduce it. As AI models generate more code, it argues, businesses need more engineers who can review, test and integrate that code into reliable systems.
“Talent is the final constraint to super intelligence. Engineers who can implement AI solutions are some of the most expensive talent to recruit anywhere. Talent Nation puts certified AI engineering talent within the reach of any organisation for a fraction of the cost of frontier labs and traditional consulting firms,” said Aboyeji, who serves as executive chairman.
The undisclosed round of funding was co-led by Enza Capital and UK-based LocalGlobe, with participation from Future Africa, Kaleo Ventures, Ajim Capital, Solving.org and Accelerate Africa.
Talent Nation’s academy, Learn2Earn, has received more than 63,000 applications in 18 months, assessed over 32,000 people, and now has around 1,400 fellows training across nine campuses in six cities. Fewer than three per cent of applicants are admitted.
Applicants first complete an online test on their phones, before progressing to weekly in-person trials at the company’s centres across Nigeria. Experienced engineers who meet the startup’s standards move straight to deployment, while others go through three-, six- or 12-month training programmes that include internships and practical work experience. Training is peer-led and project-based, with intensive build-athons held across its campuses.
Training carries no upfront fees. Revenue from enterprise clients is reinvested into developing more engineers, who in turn contribute towards future cohorts once employed. Its engineers are already working with clients including IHS Towers, and organisations can engage them on defined projects, as direct hires, or in embedded teams.
“The benefits of AI should extend far beyond the companies with the resources to develop and deploy it today. But technological breakthroughs alone will not deliver widespread adoption. That requires a fundamental shift in the cost and availability of AI engineering talent,” said Valkin, who is CEO.
Sir John Lazar, general partner at Enza Capital and president of the Royal Academy of Engineering, said engineering talent was a crucial bedrock of innovation.
“Enza is proud to co-lead this investment into Talent Nation because we believe the company’s remarkable founders can identify this talent, build pathways for African engineers into valuable work, not just in Lagos but in London, and hold their engineers to a global standard of excellence,” he said.

items.author: Albert Cuesta
items.content:
SpaceX/SI ha entrado en el top 10 de las empresas de infraestructura en la nube por ingresos de servicios en el tercer trimestre, mientras la demanda de IA sigue transformando el mercado, según Synergy Research Group.
La empresa inició su despliegue comercial este año, tras la adquisición de xAI por parte de SpaceX en febrero.
La unidad de IA y computación en la nube adoptó su nombre actual en octubre, siguiendo la propuesta del presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, de rebautizar esta tecnología como superinteligencia.
El analista jefe John Dinsdale ha explicado a Mobile World Live que SpaceX/SI ocupa el sexto lugar por ingresos del tercer trimestre, por detrás de Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Oracle y Alibaba.
Entre los proveedores con mayor crecimiento en el trimestre figuran Oracle y las neoclouds CoreWeave, Crusoe, Nebius, Fluidstack, Together AI y Nscale, según Synergy Research.
Dinsdale ha apuntado que la expansión de estas últimas está restando cuota de mercado a los proveedores de nube más consolidados.
La firma de análisis añade que Anthropic y OpenAI también se sitúan «en buena posición» en las partes de su negocio relacionadas con plataformas.
Dinsdale ha afirmado que la IA ha transformado los servicios en la nube, la demanda de los clientes y las perspectivas de crecimiento.
En la década previa al lanzamiento de ChatGPT, los proveedores trasladaron cargas de trabajo e inversiones desde centros de datos propios a nubes públicas; ahora, la IA impulsa una expansión a una escala que hace cuatro años era impensable.
«Con un crecimiento que supera el 50%, los principales proveedores de servicios en la nube se benefician de un fuerte aumento de los ingresos, pero también se enfrentan a un mercado muy transformado, en el que los laboratorios de IA y las neoclouds surgen como socios y competidores», ha añadido.
Métrica
Amazon sigue encabezando el mercado, con una cuota del 26%, seguido de Microsoft (19%) y Google (16%).
El gasto empresarial en servicios de infraestructura en la nube ha aumentado un 55% interanual, hasta los 167.700 millones de dólares (unos 146.000 millones de euros), mientras que los ingresos de los últimos 12 meses suman 558.000 millones de dólares (unos 487.000 millones de euros).
El mercado ha necesitado ocho trimestres para duplicar su tamaño, y los servicios en la nube específicos para IA suponen ya alrededor de un tercio del total.
El crecimiento del mercado de la nube ha sido sostenido en todas las regiones. Estados Unidos es, con diferencia, el mayor mercado y el que más ha crecido entre los principales países, con el 44% del total mundial.
En moneda local, India, Indonesia, Irlanda, Canadá y Taiwán figuran también entre los países con mejor evolución. Reino Unido y Alemania siguen siendo los mayores mercados de computación en la nube de Europa.
Con información de Michael Robuck.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan’s telecom market has witnessed a major shift following Ufone’s consolidation with Telenor Pakistan, bringing the operator almost level with Jazz in terms of cellular market share.
According to the latest figures for September 2026, Jazz held 36.15 percent of Pakistan’s cellular market, while Ufone reached 36.08 percent, leaving a difference of just 0.07 percentage points between the two operators.
The development marks a significant change in Pakistan’s telecom industry, where Jazz has maintained a leading position for years.
Ufone’s reported market share increased sharply from 15.05 percent in August to 36.08 percent in September, primarily reflecting the addition of Telenor Pakistan’s subscriber base following the acquisition by Pakistan Telecommunication Mobile Limited (PTML), which operates Ufone.
The consolidation has effectively transformed Ufone into a major challenger to Jazz, creating two operators with nearly identical shares of the cellular market.
Zong Remains Third as Telecom Competition Intensifies
While Jazz and Ufone are now competing closely for the top position, Zong retained its place as Pakistan’s third-largest cellular operator.
According to the September figures, Zong’s market share stood at 26.78 percent, slightly lower than the 26.83 percent recorded in August.
Meanwhile, the Special Communications Organisation (SCO) accounted for approximately one percent of the market, compared to 1.01 percent a month earlier.
The latest figures suggest that Pakistan’s telecom market is moving toward a new competitive structure following the Ufone-Telenor consolidation.
With Jazz and Ufone holding almost equal market shares, competition could become more intense in areas such as network coverage, mobile internet services, pricing, and customer experience.
The changing market dynamics could also influence future investment in mobile networks, particularly as Pakistan’s telecom operators prepare for wider adoption of 5G services.
However, Ufone’s sharp increase in market share largely reflects the consolidation of Telenor Pakistan rather than organic subscriber growth during a single month.
For consumers, the real impact of this development will depend on whether stronger competition leads to better network quality, improved services, and more competitive mobile packages.

items.author: Albert Cuesta
items.content:
Las ventas mundiales de smartphones han caído un 20% interanual en el tercer trimestre, hasta los 254,7 millones de unidades, el volumen más bajo para ese período desde 2013, según Omdia.
La consultora ha indicado que el encarecimiento de los dispositivos y la escasez de componentes siguen lastrando la demanda de los consumidores, sobre todo en los mercados emergentes.
Distribuidores y minoristas se han mostrado además prudentes a la hora de reponer existencias de cara a la campaña navideña, ya que esa subida de costes eleva sus necesidades de capital circulante y limita los inventarios.
El analista Sanyam Chaurasia ha afirmado que las regiones que antes impulsaban el crecimiento de las ventas soportan ahora una fuerte presión en materia de asequibilidad. Según el analista, las ventas en África han descendido un 39%, la mayor caída regional, porque los proveedores han priorizado los márgenes y la venta selectiva pese a que la demanda de fondo se mantiene. Asia-Pacífico (sin la Gran China), Oriente Medio y América Latina han retrocedido más de un 20%, mientras que Norteamérica ha resistido mejor, con un mercado de gama alta y programas de financiación, canje y renovación de los operadores.
Chaurasia añade que la depreciación de las monedas, la inflación y el aumento del coste de la vida han mermado el poder adquisitivo, lo que ha llevado a muchos consumidores a aplazar la compra de un nuevo teléfono o a optar por smartphones reacondicionados y, en algunos mercados de renta baja, por teléfonos básicos.
Samsung continúa como mayor proveedor, con 57,8 millones de smartphones distribuidos, un 5% menos que un año antes. Según Omdia, la serie Galaxy A, de gama de entrada y media, le ha permitido mantenerse competitivo mientras sus rivales Android afrontaban restricciones de memoria y precios más altos. El lanzamiento en agosto de la serie Galaxy Z8, con programas de canje y renovación, ha reforzado además su posición en la gama premium.
Las ventas de Apple se han mantenido estables, en 56,5 millones de unidades.
Omdia atribuye este resultado a la demanda sostenida del iPhone 17, sobre todo en China y Norteamérica, y a las compras anticipadas de los canales ante posibles subidas de precios.
Apple presentó en septiembre el iPhone 18 Pro, el 18 Pro Max y su primer plegable, el iPhone Duo, y aplazó el iPhone 18 básico hasta 2027.
Según la consultora, esta estrategia alarga el ciclo de ventas del iPhone 17 y concentra la demanda de novedades en los modelos premium durante la campaña navideña.
Los proveedores chinos han registrado descensos más acusados. Xiaomi mantiene el tercer puesto con 30,7 millones de unidades, un 29% menos, con caídas del 20% en China y del 28% en India.
La empresa ha seguido ajustando precios en todos los mercados ante el encarecimiento de los componentes para proteger su margen, lo que ha pesado más en el volumen en los mercados emergentes sensibles al precio.
Los Redmi A7 Pro y Redmi 17 han ayudado a sostener las ventas, pero no han bastado para compensar el descenso general.
Oppo, que incluye realme y OnePlus, ocupa el cuarto puesto con 23,4 millones de unidades, un 39% menos. Vivo es quinta, con 19,3 millones y un descenso del 33%. Ambas han seguido subiendo precios en sus mercados principales por el aumento del coste de los componentes, lo que complica la planificación de los inventarios en los canales.
Según Omdia, los grandes fabricantes de gama masiva dan prioridad a los mercados rentables y a sus catálogos básicos mientras el suministro de componentes sigue limitado: ajustan las configuraciones de RAM y almacenamiento, reducen referencias y absorben de forma selectiva parte de los costes, al tiempo que amplían la oferta de mayor valor para proteger la rentabilidad.
Omdia prevé que las ventas de todo el año disminuyan en torno a un 12%, con nuevas subidas de precios y poco margen para descuentos durante la campaña navideña.
Amber Liu, responsable de práctica de Omdia, ha apuntado que los minoristas independientes son los más expuestos por la menor rotación de inventarios y la reducción de márgenes, lo que podría acelerar su salida del mercado.
Para 2027 la consultora espera un nuevo descenso, más moderado, ya que la escasez persistente de memoria convencional y de alto ancho de banda mantendrá elevados los costes.
Estos datos coinciden en buena medida con los de IDC, que sitúa la caída en el 22%, hasta los 255,3 millones de unidades.
Con información de Michael Robuck.
The post Las ventas de smartphones cayeron un 20% en el tercer trimestre appeared first on Mobile World Live.

Since its inception, Carrum has grown into a sizable fleet operator with 5,500 vehicles on its books, all the while remaining profitable, according to Jain. The startup has also received $17 Mn funding from Uber this year alone.
How Carrum Makes Money From Its Fleet
Carrum’s biggest strength is its partnership with Uber. It claims to be India’s largest supplier of Uber Black vehicles. By managing vehicles and drivers across Uber’s Go, Premium and Black services, the startup gets access to a large pool of ride demand without having to build its own customer-facing app. Its job is to keep cars running, drivers earning and vehicles productive.
This is also where Carrum’s business model shines the most. Many drivers want to earn through ride-hailing but cannot afford to buy a car or take on the cost of maintaining one. Carrum helps bridge that gap by managing vehicles and driver partners. The model has helped Carrum build a network of thousands of drivers and vehicles in a relatively short period.
Here’s a snapshot of its operations:
Driver network: Carrum has a base of 28,000+ driver partners
Ride volumes: Its fleet facilitates 35,000+ rides a day and 1 Mn+ rides a month
Fleet mix: Uber Go vehicles account for an estimated 65–70% of its fleet, while a little over 20% comprises Uber Black vehicles
Revenue contribution: Uber Black contributes around 28% of Carrum’s revenue. Each Black vehicle generates around ₹1 Lakh a month, compared with ₹65,000 for an Uber Go vehicle, according to Jain.
Keeping The Engines Running
Managing thousands of vehicles requires more than simply putting drivers behind the wheel. Carrum uses technology to track vehicle performance, coordinate maintenance, manage driver onboarding and handle financial settlements. It also uses data analytics, including heat maps and recommendations on where and when to log in, to help drivers find more ride opportunities.
The aim is to keep vehicles on the road for longer, reduce downtime and improve the earnings generated by each car. The more productively Carrum’s fleet operates, the better it can spread the cost of maintenance, financing and other operations across its rides.
Drivers also pay an onboarding fee to Carrum, which helps the company recover some of the costs of bringing new drivers into the network amid high churn.
Jain estimates that revenue is split roughly 60:40 between drivers and Carrum. The company uses its share to cover vehicle maintenance, financing and other fleet-related expenses, while drivers bear fuel costs.
For Carrum, Uber provides the demand that keeps its fleet moving, while its own technology and operations determine how efficiently it can serve that demand.
The fleet-management model is already competitive. Everest Fleet, Uber India’s largest overall fleet partner, reports over 23,500 vehicles. Globally, Moove operates a similar mobility infrastructure model.
In42 Take: Carrum Needs To Drive Solo
Carrum claims to have been profitable since its first month of operations, reporting a PAT of ₹6.5 Cr on operating revenue of ₹233 Cr in FY26. It aims to double both figures in the ongoing fiscal year while expanding its fleet to 7,700 vehicles. However, growth and profitability alone do not guarantee a sustainable business, as the bigger concern is customer concentration.
Uber is Carrum’s biggest source of business, and any change in Uber’s fleet requirements or commercial terms could affect Carrum’s business.
Then, the startup has no plans to partner with rival ride-hailing platforms. Instead, it is considering adjacent services such as chauffeur-driven cars and employee transport. These could diversify its revenue, but would require new customers, fresh partnerships and a different operating playbook. Uber’s presence in these segments could also leave Carrum facing the same dependency problem.
For now, Carrum has shown that it can build a profitable fleet business around Uber. What remains unproven is its independent growth. So, can Carrum turn its Uber-led growth into a sustainable business without depending on a single customer?

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
Managed workspace provider Smartworks reported a consolidated net profit of ₹25.6 Cr in the September quarter of FY27 as against a loss of ₹3.1 Cr a year earlier. Sequentially, profit jumped 95% from ₹13.1 Cr.
Operating revenue grew 39.2% to ₹591.4 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹424.8 Cr in the year-ago quarter. It increased 8.3% from ₹546.2 Cr in the preceding quarter.
Revenue growth outpaced the increase in total expenses, helping Smartworks post a pre-tax profit of ₹34.9 Cr against a pre-tax loss of ₹4.4 Cr a year earlier. Total expenses rose 28.1% YoY to ₹570.4 Cr from ₹445.5 Cr.
Smartworks recorded a tax expense of ₹9.2 Cr as against a tax credit of ₹1.2 Cr a year earlier.
Following the first-half performance, Smartworks raised its FY27 revenue growth guidance to 33-35% from 28-30% earlier. It retained its normalised EBITDA margin guidance of 19-20%, saying it was trending towards the upper end of the range.
“We have delivered a strong performance in the first half and are tracking well ahead of the plan we set for FY27,” founder and MD Neetish Sarda said.
Founded in 2015 by Sarda and Harsh Binani, Gurugram-based Smartworks operates a managed office platform that transforms large commercial properties into fully managed workspaces for enterprises. Its campuses offer customised office spaces along with amenities such as cafeterias, gyms, recreation zones, convenience stores and creches.
The company caters to Fortune 500 companies, multinational corporations, Indian conglomerates, Global Capability Centres (GCCs) and startups.
Lease rental revenue, which forms the bulk of Smartworks’ business, grew 29% YoY to ₹489.7 Cr. Other operating revenue more than doubled to ₹101.7 Cr from ₹45.3 Cr.
The latter includes ancillary services, termination income, software services, construction and fit-out projects, and sales of traded goods.
The company reported normalised EBITDA of ₹116.9 Cr, up 68% YoY, with the margin increasing to 19.8% from 16.4%. Normalised EBITDA deducts lease liability repayments from reported EBITDA.
Enterprise Demand Drives Expansion
Smartworks said contracted rental revenue stood at around ₹5,800 Cr, supported by existing clients expanding across cities and new enterprise customers. Enterprise clients contributed around 91% of rental revenue during the quarter, while global capability centres (GCCs) accounted for around 22%.
Clients occupying more than 1,000 seats contributed 41% of rental revenue, up from 35% a year earlier. Multi-city clients accounted for 35%, compared with 31% in Q2 FY26.
The company’s client base increased to 785 from 767 a year earlier.
Its operational footprint expanded to 10.9 Mn sq ft from 9.1 Mn sq ft. Overall occupancy remained at 81%, while committed occupancy stood at 86%, down from 88% a year earlier.
Including signed and upcoming properties, Smartworks’ total footprint stood at 17.5 Mn sq ft. across 71 centres in 15 cities in India and Singapore.
Smartworks expects its Eastside campus in Pune and Eastbridge campus in Mumbai to become operational in H2 FY27. The campuses span around 8.6 Lakh sq ft and 8.2 Lakh sq ft, respectively.
Its Singapore business expanded to four centres with around 1,600 seats. During the quarter, subsidiary Smartworks Space completed the acquisition of Singapore-based coworking operator Workstudio Spaces for ₹18.1 Cr. The 100% stake purchase from a related party was completed in July.
Shares of Smartworks ended today’s trading session marginally lower at ₹484 on the BSE.

items.title: LHC Rules IRIS Portal Access Alone Does Not Count as Legal Service of Tax Orders

The court clarified that making an order available on the online tax system does not automatically mean that the taxpayer has been legally notified.
The ruling came in three connected reference applications led by Tahir Mehmood. A division bench comprising Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf and Justice Anwaar Hussain heard the cases after taxpayers challenged decisions by the Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue (ATIR).
