LHC Rules IRIS Portal Access Alone Does Not Count as Legal Service of Tax Orders
In one of the cases, a taxpayer argued that he could not access the IRIS portal because of Covid-19 restrictions
items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has ruled that simply uploading an appellate order to the Federal Board of Revenue’s (FBR) IRIS portal does not qualify as valid legal service under the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001. The court clarified that making an order available on the online tax system does not automatically mean that the taxpayer has been legally notified.
The ruling came in three connected reference applications led by Tahir Mehmood. A division bench comprising Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf and Justice Anwaar Hussain heard the cases after taxpayers challenged decisions by the Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue (ATIR). The tribunal had dismissed their appeals as time-barred, treating the uploading of orders to IRIS as sufficient notification.
LHC Rules IRIS Portal Access Alone Does Not Count as Legal Service of Tax Orders
In one of the cases, a taxpayer argued that he could not access the IRIS portal because of Covid-19 restrictions and quarantine requirements after returning from a foreign trip. In the other two cases, taxpayers said they only became aware of the Commissioner (Appeals) orders when they received recovery notices in April 2026, several months after the decisions had been issued.
Justice Anwaar Hussain, who authored the judgement, explained that Section 218(1)(d) of the Income Tax Ordinance allows electronic service only when authorities follow the prescribed legal procedure.
The court referred to Rule 74 of the Income Tax Rules, which recognises a fax number or email address as an electronic address for service. The rule also requires authorities to confirm that they successfully transmitted the communication.
However, the judge observed that IRIS is an internal, web-based system used by the FBR for tax administration. Uploading an order to a taxpayer’s account does not prove that the authorities sent the document to an electronic address as required by law.
The judgment highlighted the difference between making a document accessible and legally serving it. According to the court, taxpayers being able to view an order through IRIS does not necessarily mean they have received formal notification under the applicable law.
The court also rejected the argument that taxpayers must regularly check their IRIS accounts to remain informed about departmental decisions. It clarified that the legal limitation period for filing an appeal cannot begin from an event that the law does not recognise as valid service.
Responding to the FBR’s position that Rule 74 could not restrict the main provision of the Income Tax Ordinance, the judge observed that the requirement to serve notices in the prescribed manner already forms part of the ordinance.
See Also: LHC Stops FBR From Seeking Bank Records Beyond Legal Deadlines
The court further stated that technology should support the administration of laws rather than replace legal requirements. Modernising government systems cannot come at the cost of established legal safeguards and taxpayers’ rights.
The judgment also referred to decisions by the Peshawar High Court, Islamabad High Court and Delhi High Court, along with Articles 4 and 10A of the Constitution, which protect the right to be treated in accordance with law and the right to a fair trial.
As a result, the LHC set aside the challenged tribunal orders and directed the Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue to hear the taxpayers’ appeals again and decide them on merit.
The ruling clarifies that the FBR cannot rely solely on uploading orders to IRIS to establish legal service. Tax authorities must follow the prescribed notification procedure before treating an order as formally communicated and calculating the limitation period for an appeal.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
Ghanaian startup TrustCheck has built a review and trust platform that allows consumers to check out businesses, especially social media sellers, before they part with their money.
Launched in January of this year by Elliot Brenya, Tema-based TrustCheck lets users look up a business, read verified customer reviews, and see a trust score out of 100. The score combines a business’s rating, review volume, how responsive it is to customers, verification status and any open disputes.
“A lot of buying in Ghana now happens on Instagram, TikTok, X and WhatsApp. You see a product, message the seller, send money by Mobile Money and hope it arrives,” Brenya told Disrupt Africa. “Most of the time it does, but when it doesn’t, there is usually no way to get your money back and no record that warns the next person. TrustCheck is meant to be that record.”
Brenya was inspired to build the platform after being scammed while buying a mobile device, having relied on fake ratings for the vendor.
All reviews on TrustCheck are moderated before going live, and reviewers can attach proof of purchase, such as MoMo receipts or order chats, which only moderators can see. Businesses cannot pay to have reviews removed, but can claim their pages for free, respond to reviews and apply for verification. This month the startup also launched a scam check for phone numbers, MoMo numbers, social media handles and websites, as well as a public API that returns a business’s trust score.
“There are global review sites, but they were built around formal businesses with websites and card payments. The sellers people in Ghana worry about most are an Instagram page, a TikTok shop or a WhatsApp number,” Brenya said. “Nothing gives you one searchable place, built for how people here actually buy and pay, that you can check in a minute before sending money.”
The platform is free for shoppers, and makes money by charging businesses for verification and premium tools. It also runs display advertising. Bootstrapped so far, TrustCheck has around 300 registered reviewers and over 50 businesses listed, 20 of which have signed up to manage their pages. It has secured its first paying business customers, though Brenya said revenue remains small.
“Encouraging on the consumer side and slower on the business side, which is what we expected,” he said. “A page they don’t control, with reviews they can’t delete, feels like a risk at first. The ones who have engaged see it the other way round: a page with real reviews and replies is the best proof a small online seller can show a new customer.”
TrustCheck is focused on Ghana for now, but sees West Africa as the obvious next step.
“The problem is the same in Nigeria, Ivory Coast, Kenya and anywhere else where social commerce and mobile money have grown faster than ways to check who you are paying,” Brenya said.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
WhatsApp has announced four new features to help users keep track of conversations and important updates in group chats. The latest changes focus on pinned messages, chat history sharing, group status updates, and a new filter for mentions and replies.
The updates aim to make group conversations easier to manage, especially for users in several active groups. They will help members find important information without scrolling through long conversations.
WhatsApp Introduces Four New Features to Make Group Chats Easier to Manage
According to WABetaInfo, the new features are rolling out for WhatsApp users on both Android and iOS.
WhatsApp Allows Users to Pin Messages Forever
WhatsApp is improving its existing pinned messages feature by adding an option to keep a message pinned permanently. Previously, users could pin a message for 24 hours, seven days, or 30 days.
With the new option, users will no longer need to select a time limit. They can keep important messages at the top of a group conversation for as long as needed.
This feature can be useful for sharing group rules, meeting details, important announcements, and other information that members may need to access regularly.
Users Can Share Recent Chat History with New Members
WhatsApp is also improving the way group members share conversation history with people who recently join a group.
The platform already allows existing members to share previous messages with new participants. However, the latest update makes this process more flexible by allowing users to share recent messages even after someone has joined the group.
Users can access this option by tapping the new member’s name in the conversation. WhatsApp also protects shared messages with end-to-end encryption to maintain conversation privacy.
WhatsApp Introduces Group Status Updates
Another major addition allows users to share status updates directly within group chats.
Instead of sharing a status with their entire contact list, users can now post updates for a specific group. Other members can view the status, react to it, and share their own updates.
Like regular WhatsApp Status updates, group statuses automatically disappear after 24 hours. This feature provides an easier way to share photos, videos, and updates with a selected group of people.
New Filter Helps Users Find Mentions and Replies
WhatsApp is also officially introducing a dedicated filter for mentions and replies. It helps users find unread group conversations where someone has mentioned them or replied to their messages.
The filter also includes messages in which group administrators mention all members. This can help users avoid missing important announcements in busy group chats.
The feature also supports community chats. Users can choose whether to keep the filter in their main chat list or move it to the separate section for secondary chat filters.
WhatsApp Features Rolling Out Gradually
WhatsApp is gradually releasing all four features to users on Android and iOS. The updates are compatible with the latest versions of the app, but availability may vary between accounts.
Users who cannot see these features yet may receive them over the coming weeks. Keeping WhatsApp updated can help users get the latest additions as they become available.

items.content:
Pine Labs Sees Profits Swell
Pine Labs put up a strong show in Q2 FY27. Buoyed by broad-based improvement across its core verticals and rising margins, the fintech major’s revenue growth hit a five-quarter high during the quarter while its net profit skyrocketed six-fold.
Here’s the breakdown of Pine Labs’ Q2 numbers:
Net profit surged over 6X YoY to ₹38.6 Cr
Operating revenue rose 24% YoY to ₹806.2 Cr
Total expenses rose 16% YoY to ₹770.4 Cr
Adjusted EBITDA rose 27% YoY to ₹215.5 Cr
Double Growth Engine: The startup’s Q2 performance reflected higher GTV, new products, an expanding merchant ecosystem and double-digit growth across its core digital infrastructure and issuing platform verticals. In addition, increased operating leverage outpaced expense growth, further strengthening cash flows.
The company also continued to deepen its monetisation capabilities through new value-added services and AI-led credit underwriting tools that process over 1 Lakh loans monthly.
The MDR Boost: Pine Labs sees a “meaningful upside” from the proposal to re-introduce merchant discount rate on UPI transactions above ₹2,000. Given that enterprise merchants drive a substantial share of its volume, the company plans to aggressively deploy additional soundbox devices to capture a bigger chunk of merchant wallet share.
Around The World: International markets are also becoming a bigger part of Pine Labs’ business, contributing 15% of its top line in Q2. The company now operates across more than 22 markets and is seeing strong momentum in Southeast Asia, where revenue and digital checkout points expanded rapidly in the quarter. While the UAE business crossed a meaningful daily transaction milestone, the company is also building presence in the Philippines and Singapore.
These markets give Pine Labs a broader runway beyond India and reduce dependence on any single regulatory environment. With its underlying businesses compounding, here’s a closer look at Pine Labs performed in Q2 FY27…
From The Editor’s Desk
Ace Blend Bags $9.9 Mn
The D2C nutrition brand has raised about ₹95 Cr in its Series A2 round led by 3one4 Capital to invest in clinical trials, R&D, supply chain improvements and testing of its products.
Founded in 2018, Ace Blend offers supplements across heart health, brain health, sleep, gut health and immunity. Its portfolio comprises around 14 SKUs. It is targeting ₹250-300 Cr in annual recurring revenue over the next 12-18 months.
Ace Blend operates in the broader Indian dietary supplements market, which is being driven by growing consumer demand, user awareness and the rise of preventive healthcare. The space is projected to become a $12 Bn opportunity by 2033.
Shadowfax’s Q2 Profit Run
The listed logistics major’s net profit surged over 5X YoY to ₹68 Cr in Q2 FY27, while operating revenue jumped 57% YoY to a record ₹1,537.7 Cr. Shadowfax’s adjusted EBITDA also rose 177% YoY to ₹77 Cr, with margins expanding to 5% from 2.8%.
On the operational front, the platform delivered 27.1 Cr orders across its express parcel and hyperlocal businesses in Q2. Its 360 platform also crossed 6,700 transacting sellers within two quarters of launch.
Founded in 2015, Shadowfax provides last-mile delivery services to ecommerce platforms and D2C brands. The company listed on the stock exchanges in January this year following its bumper ₹1,907 Cr IPO.
Venttup Raises $3 Mn
The precision manufacturing startup has raised the funding in its Pre-Series A round led by Rainmatter and Unicorn India Ventures to scale hiring, its rapid prototyping infrastructure and AI-led sourcing.
Founded in 2021, Venttup combines in-house engineering with its network of manufacturing partners to support component development, testing, and production. It claims to have grown its revenue to ₹10 Cr in FY26.
On the operational front, the startup added more than 15 blue-chip customers over the past 12 months and built an approximately ₹30 Cr business opportunity pipeline across new energy, mobility, and smart infrastructure.
Bijnis Rebrands As Zorit
The B2B ecommerce startup has rebranded as Zorit and raised ₹27 Cr in a funding round led by Sparrow Capital. Zorit now plans to double down on an inventory-led quick commerce model for offline retailers and expand its product assortment.
Founded in 2015, Bijnis initially operated an online marketplace that connected manufacturers with retailers. It pivoted to an inventory-led B2B quick commerce model in late 2024. As Bijnis, the startup had raised over $43 Mn.
In its new avatar, the startup allows retailers to source products within 60 minutes. Zorit currently claims to operate 12 dark stores across 12 cities and claims to have reached ₹120 Cr in annualised sales. Nearly half of its stores have achieved break-even.
Crypto Startups Under ED Lens
The Enforcement Directorate has launched a probe into alleged forex violations by crypto platforms Mudrex, Saber.money and Instadapp. The investigation involves alleged unauthorised cross-border fund transfers worth more than ₹4,940 Cr.
The agency said its Bengaluru Zonal Office conducted searches at three premises in Bengaluru and one in Madhya Pradesh on October 27.
The investigations centre on the alleged use of cryptocurrencies, particularly stablecoins such as USDT and USDC, to facilitate cross-border money transfers outside authorised channels.
Inc42 Markets
Inc42 Startup Spotlight
Can Physioplus’ AI Stack Track India’s Recovery Journey?
Physiotherapy often breaks down between appointments. While patients struggle to follow exercises, therapists lack real-time visibility into progress. To solve this, Physioplus is building a digital layer that keeps assessment and recovery tracking connected beyond the clinic.
A Digital Coach: Founded in 2022, Physioplus’ AI-powered platform helps patients discover physiotherapists, book consultations, request home visits and receive support for chronic pain and post-surgery rehabilitation. The platform is designed to make access more convenient while helping clinicians understand a patient’s history before treatment begins.
The Rehabilitation Stack: For practitioners, Physioplus combines digital practice management, patient records, clinical assessments, documentation and tech-enabled monitoring. Its monitoring layer also supports home-based rehabilitation by capturing exercise adherence, pain changes and functional progress over time.
Growing Steadily: Physioplus claims to have so far onboarded over 1,000 patients. It is now focusing on scaling product development, expanding its physiotherapist network and fueling growth across India. With the homegrown digital health and rehabilitation market projected to become a $14.8 Bn opportunity by 2033, can Physioplus make physiotherapy more measurable and consistent beyond the clinic?

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
D2C cat food startup Smylo is in advanced talks to raise around ₹30 Cr (about $3.2 Mn) in a mix of equity and debt, sources told Inc42.
The proposed round is likely to bring a new venture capital firm onto Smylo’s cap table, with existing backer DSG Consumer Partners also looking to invest further, the sources added.
While the split between equity and debt could not be ascertained, the sources said equity would account for the majority of the round.
Smylo is likely to use the fresh capital for new product launches, R&D, and setting up a manufacturing facility.
Inc42 has reached out to Smylo for comment. The story will be updated on receiving a response.
Founded in 2024 by former Titan Capital executives Abhishek Agrawal and Kartikeya Gupta, Smylo offers cat food that it claims is preservative-free, high in protein, and made from fresh meat.
Its portfolio includes wet food, dry food, and broths for kittens and adult cats. Besides its website, the startup sells through ecommerce marketplaces and quick commerce platforms such as Blinkit and Zepto.
In an interaction with Inc42 in February, the founders said Smylo was clocking average monthly sales of ₹50–55 Lakh. Its website and ecommerce channels contributed about 80% of revenue, with quick commerce accounting for the remainder.
At the time, the startup had raised smaller rounds before securing investment during its appearance on Shark Tank India in early 2026. However, the startup did not disclose the total funding raised.
The development comes amid continued investment in India’s pet care market, with startups across food, supplies, and healthcare raising capital to expand their operations.
In September, D2C pet food startup Lickicious raised ₹19 Cr through a mix of equity and debt in a round led by Prath Ventures. It planned to use the capital to expand manufacturing, strengthen R&D, and widen its product range and sales channels.
Pet care marketplace Supertails raised $30 Mn in a Series C round in February to expand its pet clinic network and quick commerce infrastructure.
Investor interest is being driven by India’s growing pet care market, with rising pet ownership and higher spending on pet nutrition and healthcare.
India’s pet care market is estimated to be worth $3.6 Bn in 2024 and is projected to grow at a CAGR of 20% to reach $24.8 Bn by 2032, according to IBEF.

items.content: India's executive search firms are experiencing a surprising growth despite broader job market challenges such as layoffs, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven disruptions and heightened geopolitical uncertainties. Business increased 15-25% in the first half of this financial year, and the momentum continues to be strong, fuelled by a broad range of sectors, according to executives from leading search firms.Companies are willing to spend heavily on leaders capable of navigating disruption and executing large investment plans, in an apparent contradiction to the larger market, which is seeing many organisations cutting roles, automating functions and becoming more cost-conscious, they said.Manufacturing, industrials, power, infrastructure and global capability centres (GCCs) are among the strongest drivers, while financial services and technology are showing renewed demand, particularly in specific segments. Consumer, retail and some traditional IT services remain more measured, but even in these sectors, companies are scouting for leaders who can improve productivity and profitability or reposition businesses."The market is growing at more than 25% (year-on-year) on a large base. This is our best year," said Atul Vohra, managing partner of Transearch India. "All consultants are working at 110%," he said, adding that the firm is expanding its teams as demand remains high across sectors.Vohra highlighted thousands of crores of new investment, particularly in manufacturing, chemicals and infrastructure, as a key driver of leadership demand. "We were sceptical in the January-March quarter, fearing that companies would become conservative, but that did not happen. The India growth story is fundamentally strong," he said.Investments and focus on new areas are creating a demand for senior executives even in industries where automation is reducing conventional employment. Large projects in areas such as data centres, renewable energy and clean tech require leaders capable of building businesses and executing complex expansion plans. Technology presents a similar paradox: companies are hiring aggressively in AI and adjacent areas to cash in on new opportunities, even as AI may make some jobs redundant."The last two quarters have been very good, up 25-30%," said Shiv Agrawal, managing director at search and talent advisory firm ABC Consultants. Manufacturing, infrastructure, industrials, power, auto have been particularly strong, he said, while consumer, retail and fast-moving consumer goods have remained sluggish. Technology, he said, was decent, leaving the overall market firmly positive.BTI Executive Search managing director James Agarwal said conditions stabilised after a challenging start to the year. Energy, utilities and core manufacturing, including greenfield and brownfield projects, are performing well, according to him.K Sudarshan, managing director at executive search firm EMA Partners India, said the market was "looking pretty good", with industrial and manufacturing mandates looking particularly strong and financial services showing a revival. He pointed to a flurry of public listings and domestic capital raising as evidence of the market resilience despite geopolitical concerns and foreign investor caution.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
Binance is investigating a suspected hack after wallets linked to it on the Ethereum, Bitcoin, and TRON networks saw outflows of around $5.7 billion, according to The Kobeissi Letter.
The outflows reportedly include $1.45 billion worth of Bitcoin and $875 million worth of Ether. If confirmed, it would be the biggest hack in crypto history, far ahead of the $1.5 billion stolen from Bybit in February 2025.
What Binance Has Said
Binance has not confirmed the total amount stolen. Co-founder Yi He said the exchange is aware of reports of a potential security issue and its security teams are reviewing the matter urgently.
Binance founder Changpeng Zhao said the activity looks like a hack on Binance. He said user funds are safe and he expects them to be fully covered.
The exchange has temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while it investigates.
Billions Frozen
Binance said $2.54 billion in assets linked to the incident has been frozen so far, and the figure could rise as funds are traced. Tether said it froze more than 1.567 billion USDT, while Circle froze over 800 million USDC.
Blockchain tracker Arkham Intelligence shows about $5.8 billion held across wallets linked to the attacker, though this is not a confirmed loss figure.
Binance has been active in Pakistan, where it received an NOC to begin the registration process last year.

items.content: ET Intelligence Group: Hero MotoCorp delivered strong revenue growth in the September quarter, driven by double-digit volume growth, market share gain and improving traction in scooters and EVs. However, its stock fell 3.6% on Thursday post results amid concerns over rising input cost inflation and competitive pressure. Its operating margin before depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda margin) declined 160 basis points year-on-year to 13.4% in the September quarter while improving a tad 10 basis points sequentially. Hero's growth in the coming quarters will depend upon the success of new launches expected in the second half of the current fiscal year and recovery in international markets. In addition, traction in the premium motorcycle segment and the VIDA electric vehicle portfolio are expected to reduce its reliance on the mature economy segment. Capacity expansion to 9.2 million units by March 2027 from 8.6 million currently, alongside growing EV adoption and rising demand for Harley-Davidson motorcycles, is expected to drive Hero's medium-term growth.Read more: IndiGo Q2 Results: Loss narrows YoY to Rs 1,879 crore; revenue rises 26%The company expects to maintain the margin stable for the December quarter despite persistent input cost inflation. It plans to offset the impact through cost rationalisation, better VIDA unit economics and calibrated price increase. It also retained the medium-term Ebitda margin guidance of 14-16%.135337770Hero is increasingly shifting its growth focus beyond commuter motorcycles. Scooter volumes continued to outpace the industry, helping the company improve the market share to 7.3% from 6.2% in the year-ago quarter, marking it to be the fifth consecutive quarter of market share gain. The VIDA retail sales nearly doubled during the quarter to 67,000 units from 38,000 units year-on-year. The company is aggressively scaling the EV business, with monthly VIDA production capacity set to rise to 45,000 units by the end of FY27 from 30,000 currently and to over 80,000 units by first half of FY28. This is expected to strengthen VIDA's profitability over time.Read more: Suzlon Energy Q2 Results: Profit plunges 69% YoY to Rs 394 crore due to one-time deferred taxPremiumisation is another key growth driver. Hero plans to launch three-four premium motorcycles during the remainder of FY27, while continued traction in the Harley-Davidson portfolio, strong demand for the Xpulse range and expansion of the Premia network created specifically to sell and service its high-end vehicles, are expected to improve product mix and support earnings growth. Exports, which faced temporary disruptions in markets such as Colombia and Bangladesh, are also expected to recover. Hero expects export volume to return to double-digit growth in the second half of FY27 as logistical challenges ease.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
‎
‎…ILO backs modern employment service, stronger labour market data to improve job opportunities
‎
‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
‎
‎ABUJA –The National Directorate of Employment (NDE) has launched a five-year strategic plan aimed at expanding job creation and upgrading its 87 Skills Training Centres, many of which need rehabilitation, modern equipment, or full renovation to meet present-day training requirements.
‎
‎The 2027–2031 plan also aims to enhance employment services, strengthen labour-market information systems, and better align vocational training with industry needs, as the Directorate works to boost job creation and promote sustainable livelihoods throughout Nigeria.
‎
‎Speaking at the unveiling ceremony in Abuja, Thursday, NDE Director-General Silas Agara said the strategy would equip the agency to address shifting labour-market needs through coordinated, evidence-based and results-oriented interventions.
‎
‎He said the plan would give the Directorate’s departments, state offices, and programme delivery structures a shared direction, focusing on demand-driven skills development, entrepreneurship, enterprise growth, strategic partnerships, and inclusive employment.
‎
‎According to him: “The NDE is not merely unveiling a policy document; but setting out a clear strategic direction for the next five years, reaffirming our institutional purpose and strengthening our commitment to creating employment opportunities, developing skills, promoting entrepreneurship and improving the livelihoods of Nigerians.”
‎
‎Speaking on the condition of the agency’s training infrastructure, the Director-General revealed that the NDE operates 87 Skills Training Centres, as well as Agricultural Training Centres and Common Facility Centres. He explained that many of these facilities require varying degrees of retooling, upgrading, rehabilitation, or complete overhaul.
‎
‎He said: “We are committed to modernising these facilities and harmonising our training curricula to ensure uniform standards and alignment with industry needs.”
‎Agara, who was a former deputy governor of Nasarawa state, however, acknowledged that modernising the facilities and improving the quality of training would require sustained support from the Federal Government, development partners and the private sector.
‎
‎He said the Directorate would also strengthen collaboration with employers and industry partners, improve data-driven decision-making and provide more effective post-training support to help beneficiaries secure employment, establish viable businesses and sustain their livelihoods.
‎
‎The NDE boss stressed that employment interventions must respond to the changing nature of work, shaped by technological advancement, emerging industries, demographic pressures and evolving business models.
‎
‎He said the plan would guide resource allocation, performance assessment and programme monitoring, adding that its priorities must be integrated into the Directorate’s annual work plans and budgets to ensure accountability.
‎
‎”The real test of this Plan begins after its launch,” Agara said, emphasising that implementation would require clear responsibilities, adequate resources, measurable targets and effective monitoring mechanisms.
‎
‎In her remarks, the Director of the International Labour Organization (ILO) Country Office for Nigeria, Ghana, Liberia, Sierra Leone and the Liaison Office for ECOWAS, Vanessa Phala, highlighted the importance of modern employment services and improved labour-market information in translating skills development into better job opportunities.
‎
‎She said the plan’s proposed establishment of a modern Public Employment Service, alongside stronger labour-market information systems and institutional capacity, could improve the connection between job seekers, employers and available economic opportunities.
‎
‎”The planned establishment of a modern Public Employment Service, enhanced labour market information systems, and stronger organisational capacities will not only improve service delivery but also enable more responsive, evidence-based support for job seekers, entrepreneurs, and employers alike,” Phala said.
‎
‎She explained that a modern employment service and reliable labour-market information could help the NDE make better-informed decisions, improve support for job seekers and entrepreneurs, and ensure that employment interventions responded more closely to employers’ needs.
‎
‎Phala described the strategic plan as timely, given the effects of technological change, demographic transitions and evolving skills requirements on Nigeria’s labour market.
‎
‎She also said the plan was well positioned to support the implementation of the National Employment Policy (NEP) 2025 and advance the country’s efforts to promote productive employment and decent work.
‎
‎The ILO director disclosed that the organisation supported the development of the plan through the Strengthening Employment and Employability Systems in Nigeria (SEESIN) project, implemented through the GIZ-ILO collaboration under the Skills Development for Youth Employment Programme (SKYE II).
‎
‎According to her, the process involved consultations with NDE management and staff and a broad range of stakeholders, whose contributions helped identify institutional priorities and strengthen the plan’s relevance to Nigeria’s employment challenges.
‎
‎However, Phala cautioned that achieving the plan’s objectives would require clear institutional leadership, adequate resources, effective partnerships and regular assessment of results.
‎
‎She urged the NDE to assign clear responsibilities for each priority area and called on government institutions, employers’ and workers’ organisations and development partners to align their support with the plan’s objectives.
‎
‎She also emphasised the importance of using results-based management and monitoring, evaluation and learning mechanisms to track progress and strengthen accountability throughout the implementation period.
‎
‎The ILO reaffirmed its commitment to working with the Nigerian government and social partners to translate national employment policies and related frameworks into practical improvements in employment opportunities and livelihoods.
‎
‎Agara, in turn, expressed appreciation to the governments of Germany and Switzerland, the ILO and other development partners for supporting the development of the plan through the GIZ-implemented SKYE II programme.
‎
‎He also acknowledged the contributions of the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment, organised labour, employers’ organisations, civil society organisations and other stakeholders who participated in the consultations and validation process.
‎
The post ‎NDE targets job growth with five-year plan, revamp of 87 training centres appeared first on Vanguard News.

This reverses the broader trend in favour of small- and mid-caps seen thus far this year, underscoring the recent divergence between frontline stocks and the broader market.The average advance-to-decline (A/D) ratio fell to 0.9 in October so far, its lowest level since March 2026, when the Iran-US war triggered a selloff in global equities. The ratio fell below 1 for the second consecutive month, indicating that declining stocks outnumbered advancing ones and signalling continued weakness in market breadth.135337101Ravi Singh, chief research officer at Master Capital Services, attributed a significant part of the recent weakness to the Jio Platforms IPO, which diverted liquidity from the secondary market as investors set aside funds for the issue.Profit-booking after the strong rally in midcap and smallcap stocks, stretched valuations and uneven corporate earnings have also weighed on sentiment, market experts said. Investors are becoming less willing to pay high prices based on future growth expectations when earnings and cash flows do not justify valuations. Institutional money is also rotating towards larger, more liquid companies with stronger balance sheets and predictable earnings, helping benchmark indices remain relatively resilient.Read more: Market Trading Guide: Eternal among 2 stocks to buy for Friday for healthy returnsRising energy costs pose an additional concern for India, given its dependence on imports, with implications for inflation and corporate margins. Uncertainty over global interest rates, rising US bond yields, a stronger dollar, geopolitical risks and foreign investor selling have further dampened risk appetite, experts said.Read more: Trent Q2 Results: Cons profit jumps 25% YoY to Rs 468 crore; revenue climbs 22%Tejas Shah, head of trading at Equirus Securities, said these factors had made investors more selective, increasing selling pressure on fundamentally weaker, highly leveraged and overvalued companies.Leverage in the market remains another concern. The margin trading facility (MTF) book has declined for three consecutive weeks, but the extent of the reduction depends on the period being measured. items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
‎
‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
‎
‎ABUJA —PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has responded to criticism, especially from opposition leaders, over new loans the country has accessed from international institutions and banks.
‎
‎In an essay titled “From reforms to delivery: Our infrastructure investment and growth strategy,” to be published on Nigerian news platforms, President Tinubu wrote: “The real question is not how much we borrow, but what we build, what value we create and what future we leave behind.”
‎
‎He identified the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, Trans-Sahara Superhighway, electricity grid upgrades and the modernisation of key commercial ports in Lagos as major projects expected to strengthen Nigeria’s productive capacity.
‎
‎The President said the projects, alongside investments in healthcare, education and vocational training, would connect economic regions, reduce logistics costs, unlock agricultural and industrial potential and attract private investment.
‎
‎The Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is expected to cut logistics costs along its corridor by 15 to 20 per cent. It could add up to two per cent to Nigeria’s GDP through expanded trade, tourism, and industrial activity.
‎
‎The project is also projected to generate about 100,000 direct jobs in construction and engineering, alongside more than 150,000 indirect jobs in logistics, materials and related services.
‎
‎According to him: “We are not simply building highways. We are opening economic corridors, connecting markets, unlocking industries and reshaping Nigeria’s economic geography.”
‎
‎He said the administration’s ambition to build a $1 trillion economy by 2030 would require sustained infrastructure investment to support higher productivity, industrialisation and trade.
‎
‎“We cannot build a USD 1 trillion economy with infrastructure designed for an economy a fraction of that size,” Tinubu said.
‎
‎He wrote that improving economic indicators and growing international investor confidence are creating opportunities for Nigeria to attract long-term investment and expand critical infrastructure.
‎
‎The President said the economic reforms his administration introduced in May 2023 helped restore macroeconomic stability, strengthen public finances, and improve the country’s standing in international financial markets.
‎
‎He said a $1 trillion economy would not emerge by declaration alone but must be built through sustained investment, higher productivity, industrialisation, and trade, stressing that infrastructure development would be critical to achieving the target by 2030.
‎
‎In an article titled “From reforms to delivery: Our infrastructure investment and growth strategy,” Tinubu said real Gross Domestic Product growth reached 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, while headline inflation fell to 14.63 per cent in September from 20.98 per cent a year earlier.
‎
‎He also said gross external reserves rose to $55.1 billion as of October 9, 2026, including about $46 billion in net reserves, while the tax-to-GDP ratio increased to 12.5 per cent from seven per cent.
‎
‎Tinubu said real Gross Domestic Product growth reached 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, while headline inflation fell to 14.63 per cent in September from 20.98 per cent a year earlier.
‎
‎The President attributed the improvements to measures including petrol subsidy removal, exchange rate unification, tax reforms and coordinated efforts to tackle inflation.
‎
‎“The decisions taken since 2023 were difficult but necessary,” he said, referring to the reforms.
‎
‎Tinubu said the gains have strengthened Nigeria’s ability to attract investment and finance projects that support long-term economic growth.
‎
‎“Confidence has a price; our cost of borrowing is going down, and the country risk premium has drastically decreased,” he said.
‎
‎The President cited positive assessments by international credit rating agencies as evidence of improved confidence in the economy.
‎
‎
‎“These are not political endorsements; they are independent assessments by global rating agencies, index providers, regulators and investors, recognising stronger external reserves, improved macroeconomic management and greater financial credibility,” Tinubu said.
‎
‎According to the President, the improved standing could help Nigeria attract more institutional investors, secure longer-term financing and reduce borrowing costs.
‎
‎He said the administration was shifting public borrowing away from financing short-term fiscal pressures towards investments that would generate economic returns, create jobs and expand opportunities for future generations.
‎
‎The President said the government was also pursuing longer-term financing arrangements to match the lifespan of infrastructure assets, reduce refinancing pressures and secure more competitive funding for productive investments.
‎
‎President Tinubu said Nigeria must convert renewed international confidence into capital expenditure, completed infrastructure and lasting economic benefits for citizens.
‎
‎He identified five priorities for the next phase of the Federal Executive Council’s economic strategy: food affordability and energy price stability; budget harmonisation and fiscal discipline; completion of high-impact projects and investment in critical infrastructure; an improved economic policy framework and regulatory efficiency; and targeted household support alongside investment in human development.
‎
‎The President stressed that the success of the current administration’s economic schemes would be measured by completed projects, increased investment, employment generation and improved living standards.
‎
‎“Securing financing is not the achievement. Completing the project, delivering value and improving the lives of Nigerians is the achievement,” he said.
‎
‎He added that the nation’s economic ambition must be supported by responsible borrowing and investments that create lasting opportunities for future generations.

items.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has upheld 41 of the 69 petitions filed against the final list of governorship candidates for the 2027 general election, while rejecting 28.
Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee (IVEC) of the commission, Mohammed Kudu Haruna, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday night.
According to him, the petitions came from 12 political parties across 26 states.
He said, “The complaints concerned the omission of certain political parties, the wrongful inclusion of candidates of political parties whose names were not contained in the membership registers submitted by their political parties, and instances of alleged multiple nominations.”
Haruna said the commission examined the complaints against its records and the law.
“Following a review of the complaints, relevant records and applicable legal provisions, the Commission found merit in some representations and approved the inclusion of affected candidates and their political parties, while complaints found to be without merit were declined.
“In addition, some names that were wrongfully published in the final list were removed after verifying that their names were not on the register.
“The Commission also approved the removal of candidates whose nominations were found to be inconsistent with the applicable legal requirements,” the statement said.
Although INEC did not name any candidate or state, a source had earlier revealed that the commission’s meeting on Thursday to review complaints from parties and candidates left out of the lists had cleared a former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Prof. Isa Ali Ibrahim Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections, subject to the outcome of pending court cases.
The source also said the petition by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, seeking a review of his exclusion from the list, did not succeed.
“Yes, Pantami has been cleared,” the source said when asked about the PDP governorship candidate in Gombe State.
“He did not succeed,” the source said when asked about Adebutu.
On the State Houses of Assembly, the commission said the decisions affecting candidates sponsored by political parties “were informed by specific complaints received and determined in accordance with the law and the Commission’s established criteria.”
For those elections, INEC received 61 petitions from 11 political parties across 11 states. Twenty-five succeeded, while 36 failed.
The commission said the affected candidates, political parties and states “will be reflected in the updated list on the Commission’s website.”
“Once again, the Commission assures the public of its commitment to transparency and the credibility of the electoral process,” the statement said.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
Everton swept into the League Cup quarter-finals with a 3-1 win against Newcastle on Thursday as they booked a clash against giant-killers Fleetwood.
David Moyes’s side took the lead through James Garner’s first-half goal at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.
Hayden Hackney doubled the lead with his first goal since his close-season move from Middlesbrough.
Everton striker Thierno Barry netted in the second half and Dan Burn’s reply for Newcastle came far too late to stop the Toffees ending their three-match winless run.
Chasing their first League Cup final appearance in 43 years, Everton will travel to fourth-tier minnows Fleetwood in the week commencing December 14.
The ‘Cod Army’ caused one of the biggest shocks in League Cup history on Tuesday when they beat Premier League champions Arsenal in a penalty shoot-out after a 1-1 draw at Highbury.
Everton have never won the League Cup, losing their two final appearances in 1977 and 1984.
Everton fans do not need reminding that it is 31 years since the club won the FA Cup in their most recent trophy triumph.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, a noted Everton fan, is old enough to remember that success and he was cheering from the stands as Moyes’s men made light work of their last-16 tie.
Newcastle will have the chance for revenge when the sides meet again in the Premier League at St James’ Park on Monday.
Everton dropped a pre-match bombshell, saying Jack Grealish was unavailable for selection “due to a breach of club discipline”.
Grealish, beset by criticism of his behaviour off the pitch, was reported to have taken an unauthorised absence from training.
But the on-loan Manchester City winger’s absence was no problem for his team-mates.
– Everton hit their stride –
Newcastle tested Jordan Pickford early on when Joe Willock’s low drive was palmed away by the Everton goalkeeper, who repelled Fabian Schar’s long-range strike moments later.
Garner steadied Everton’s nerves with a clinical opener in the 34th minute.
Hackney teed up Garner just inside the area and the midfielder stretched to guide a fine finish into the far corner for his first goal since January.
Everton had hit their stride and Hackney struck on the stroke of half-time.
At the climax of a blistering Everton counter-attack, Barry hooked a cross into the six-yard box and Hackney timed his run perfectly to volley past Lukas Hornicek.
Frustrated Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle sent on Joelinton, Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa at the interval.
Wissa had an immediate chance after sprinting onto Willock’s pass, but he misjudged the high bounce and ended up heading straight at Pickford.
It was a costly miss as Barry put the result beyond doubt in the 69th minute.
Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall provided the cross and Barry lashed home from close range for his seventh goal this season.
Burn scored with a header from Willock’s 88th-minute cross, sparking a brawl between several players.
But Newcastle’s brief show of defiance was too little, too late as Everton moved a step closer to Wembley.
AFP

Chieftains of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) have urged Nigerians to mobilise grassroots support for the party’s presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, come 2027.
The party chieftains, including a political economist, Prof Pat Utomi, Enugu State NDC governorship candidate, Chief Chinyeaka Ohaa and human rights activist, Aisha Yesufu, made the call on Thursday during the Obi-Kwankwaso Town Hall Meeting held in Enugu.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Obi, his running mate, Sen. Rabiu Kwankwaso, and other NDC stakeholders attended the meeting, which attracted a large crowd of supporters.
Addressing the crowd, Utomi expressed confidence that the Obi-Kwankwaso presidential ticket would provide the leadership needed to address Nigeria’s economic, political and security challenges.
He lamented that Nigeria’s potential to become one of the greatest countries in the world had been undermined by corruption, criminality and disunity.
According to him, the time has come for Nigerians to unite and work towards achieving meaningful political change.
“We have done our research, and I know that a combination of Peter Gregory Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso will deliver Nigeria,” he said.
Utomi urged Nigerians to turn out massively during the elections, vote for their preferred candidates and defend their votes through lawful means.
In his remarks, Ohaa, the NDC governorship candidate in Enugu State, described the Obi-Kwankwaso political alliance as a historic opportunity to strengthen national unity and promote inclusive governance.
He said the partnership represented the possibility of building political bridges across Nigeria’s geopolitical zones.
According to him, the alliance is reminiscent of the historic political understanding between the late Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe and Sir Ahmadu Bello during Nigeria’s early political development.
“My message today is simple: we must seize this opportunity and work with our brothers and sisters across the South-South, South-West, North-East, North-West and North-Central to secure an NDC president in 2027,” he said.
Ohaa explained that the campaign was not merely about producing a president of Igbo extraction but about establishing a government committed to justice, accountability, security and prosperity for all Nigerians.
He expressed confidence that NDC candidates in Enugu State were prepared to earn the trust of voters and secure victory in the elections.
Yesufu, a human rights activist, urged Nigerians to take ownership of the 2027 elections by mobilising voters and actively participating in the democratic process.
She said the election was not merely about Obi’s presidential ambition but about the collective responsibility of Nigerians to rescue the country from its numerous challenges.
According to her, the election is not about Obi but about every one of us, as the mistake we made in 1999 must be corrected.
“The class of 1999 has destroyed this country. The class of 2027 must fix this country.
“We must take this election as our own election. Mr Peter Obi and his running mate have one business, and that is to be on the ballot paper.You and I must do the remaining work to ensure victory,” she said.
Yesufu challenged every supporter to mobilise at least 20 eligible voters for Obi, stressing that political change required collective action rather than depending solely on candidates.
The activist also urged Nigerians to demonstrate courage and determination in protecting their votes during the elections, saying that Nigerians must reject political intimidation and insist on credible elections that reflect the will of the people.
Earlier, the NDC Chairman in Enugu State, Mr Ibuchukwu Obetta, welcomed Obi, Kwankwaso and other party leaders to the state, describing their visit as a significant moment in the party’s preparations for the 2027 elections.
Obetta said the visit had renewed the confidence of party members and strengthened their determination to work for a Nigeria founded on integrity, accountability, competence, justice and inclusive development.
(NAN)

Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, has reiterated willingness to work closely with his vice-presidential candidate, Sen. Rabiu Kwankwaso, to move the country forward.
Obi gave the assurance on Thursday during a town hall meeting in Enugu, where he engaged supporters and stakeholders on the country’s challenges and his vision for national development.
The former Anambra State governor said they would work together to tackle insecurity and restore safety across Nigeria if elected president in 2027.
He said that securing lives and property would be a priority of his administration, promising to confront the security challenges threatening communities and livelihoods across the country.
The presidential candidate regretted that the current administration had failed to protect the lives and property of Nigerians, which he maintained was the primary responsibility.
Obi assured voters in the South East to vote for him because of his competence and ability to tackle challenges facing the nation.
He challenged other presidential candidates to meet and discuss their plans, and warned the people not to be deceived by rhetoric and propaganda.
On education, Obi said he would declare a state of emergency on education to enable his administration to tackle the issue of out-of-school children head-on, hinting that Nigerian children deserved quality education.
In his remarks, the vice-presidential candidate of NDC, Kwankwaso, advised that nobody should be deceived by ethnicity, saying, “It’s obvious that Nigerians are going through numerous difficulties”.
Kwankwaso lamented that people were facing challenges like insecurity, unemployment, poverty, hunger and so many other challenges.
He explained that the only solution to achieve a new Nigeria was unity, diligence, perseverance and willingness.
He urged Nigerians to come out en masse to cast, protect and follow up on their votes until results were announced, noting that it was not a one-man show but a collective responsibility.
Also, Sen Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central in the National Assembly, described Obi and his running mate, Kwankwaso, as the “best presidential ticket” to lead Nigeria.
Umeh expressed confidence that the South-East would rally behind Obi in the 2027 presidential election, urging the people to remain resolute and resist attempts to intimidate or discourage them from pursuing their political choice.
He also commended the resilience of supporters who, according to him, ensured that the meeting held despite reported attempts to frustrate the gathering.
The senator further praised Kwankwaso for his efforts to build support in Northern Nigeria, expressing optimism that the Obi-led ticket could attract votes across the country.
Umeh urged the people of the South-East to use their votes to make a strong political statement in 2027, declaring his support for Obi’s presidential ambition and calling on the region to unite behind the project.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
Inter and AC Milan unveiled their new “Generali Stadium” Thursday, which will replace the iconic San Siro stadium from the 2031/32 season.
It will be shaped “low in the body, and it rises up at either end” behind the goals, architect Norman Foster said during a press conference in Milan.
The design aims to bring spectators as close to the pitch as possible, with the stands behind the goals set at a steep 37-degree incline, said David Manica, a stadium specialist who collaborated with Foster on the project.
“The most important thing that we realised when we designed this project is that the San Siro is a feeling,” he said.
“It’s more than a building, it’s a feeling, and everything that we needed to do here was to carry it into the (new) building”.
Manica said the design team “started with proximity”.
“We brought all the seats as close as possible to the field. They could not be any closer, it’ll actually feel as though you’re sitting on the grass,” he said.
They also paid great attention to acoustics: the roof covers the stands, leaving only the pitch exposed, and is designed to “amplify the roar” of the fans, Manica said.
“This building is steeper than many other new buildings are built today, and that’s intentional, because it allows us to bring those seats up and over the field as much as possible, and create that sense of intimacy and atmosphere,” he said.
The stadium, sponsored by the Italian insurance giant Generali, will also be capable of hosting American football games, rugby matches and concerts.
“I want the crowd to come to the new stadium and to feel that excitement that they felt before, and to feel the building, living and breathing with them as it does currently,” Manica said.
AC Milan and Inter paid 197 million euros ($219 million) to acquire the current stadium and its adjacent parking areas, where they intend to build their new, shared home.
The project for the new San Siro — which will have a capacity of 71,500 seats, compared to the current 75,000 — will cost the two clubs 1.2 billion euros.
Construction is set to begin in 2028.
Foster and Manica previously worked together on London’s Wembley Stadium.
Milan’s current stadium — one of the most iconic in European football and often likened to a “concrete cathedral” — is the largest in Italy.
But the venue, which opened in 1926, no longer meets the needs of spectators or the clubs, despite undergoing several renovations over the decades.
San Siro, also known as the Giuseppe Meazza Stadium, will be largely demolished once construction work on the new stadium nears completion.

By Omeiza Ajayi & Ben Ngwakwe
There were strong indications on Thursday night that the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC might have provisionally cleared a former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Gombe State, Prof. Isa Ali Ibrahim Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections.
The clearance of both men is subject to the outcome of pending court cases, it was learned on Thursday night.
In Gombe, Pantami’s supporters took over some major areas celebrating the development on Thursday night.
INEC officials did not immediately react to Vanguard’s questions regarding the development. But a source said the decisions were reached at the commission’s meeting on Thursday to consider complaints from political parties and candidates whose names were left out of the lists published ahead of the 2027 elections.
The source added that the commission had no objection to their candidacies, but that the pending legal proceedings could still affect the final outcome.
The development comes after INEC dropped Pantami’s name from the final list of governorship candidates for Gombe State, although he appeared on the provisional list published on August 29.
Pantami emerged as the PDP candidate after leaving the All Progressives Congress (APC) on May 19. One of the aspirants for the ticket, Ahmed Mailantarki Mailantarki, challenged his victory in court. A Federal High Court sitting in Gombe nullified the election and ordered a fresh primary, which Pantami won again.
His biggest hurdle was the September 24 Supreme Court judgement, which restored Sections 77(5), (6), (7) and 84(2) of the Electoral Act 2026. The provisions bar parties from fielding candidates whose names were not in the membership register submitted to INEC within the stipulated time.
Mohammed Haruna, an INEC National Commissioner, had previously said that, in line with the Supreme Court ruling, some parties would not field candidates in 2027.
The commission, however, rejected a petition by the PDP governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, who had asked it to review his exclusion from the list of candidates.

“We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” the statement said.

items.content:
By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri
The troops of Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), have killed 15 Boko Haram terrorists, including two (2) prominent ISWAP Qayids, Abu Musanna and Hassan Abu Huraira in Kerenoa, Marte Local Government Area of Borno State.
This is as the Theatre Commander of OPHK, Major General Ibikunle Ajose on Thursday commissioned the newly constructed three blocks of 12-family Corporals and Below Quarters (CBQ) at Maimalari Cantonment, Maiduguri.
The commissioning forms part of activities to commemorate the Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu’s one year in office, which also reflects his commitment to improving troops’ living conditions, strengthening morale and enhancing operational effectiveness.
In a press statement signed by the Media Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force North East Operation HADIN KAI, Captain Mohammed Goni on Thursday said: “Troops of OPHK continued to record operational successes through sustained intelligence-led offensive operations aimed at degrading terrorist capabilities and dismantling their networks across the theatre.
“In a further operation, OPHK air assets, at about 9:20 pm on 28 October 2026, conducted an armed reconnaissance and air interdiction mission in the Kerenoa Marte Local Government Area of Borno State, resulting in the neutralisation of 15 terrorists and the destruction of an IED hideout.
“The mission followed intelligence reports on terrorist activities in the area. During the operation, the air assets tracked two terrorists on a motorcycle to a makeshift structure beneath a tree. Further surveillance revealed additional movements around the location, indicating the presence of other terrorists. Consequently, the location was engaged with precision strikes.
“Following the strikes, Battle Damage Assessment (BDA) indicated that 15 terrorists were neutralised, while structures at the location were destroyed. Additionally, a secondary fire observed after the engagement suggested that the targeted structure may have been used for the storage of terrorist IED logistics hub.
“It has been confirmed that 2 prominent ISWAP Qayids, Abu Musanna and Hassan Abu Huraira were amongst those neutralised while several other fighters were severely wounded, including the Wali (ISWAP Governor) of the area who is reported to be critically injured.
“The operation forms part of OPHK’s sustained intelligence-led air offensive aimed at degrading terrorist capabilities, disrupting their hideouts and dismantling logistics networks across the theatre. The Joint Task Force continues to conduct coordinated operations against terrorist elements in the North East to achieve its Operational mandate of restoring total and long-lasting peace in the region,” Goni stated.
Meanwhile, the Nigerian Army has reaffirmed its commitment to personnel welfare with the commissioning of three blocks of 12-family Corporals and Below Quarters (CBQ) at Maimalari Cantonment, Maiduguri. The commissioning reflects the commitment of the Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu NAM, to improving troops’ living conditions, strengthening morale and enhancing operational effectiveness. The commissioning forms part of activities to commemorate the COAS one year in office.
The COAS was represented at the ceremony by the Theatre Commander, Joint Task Force (North East) Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), Major General Ibikunle Ajose, on Thursday, 29 October 2026, at Maimalari Cantonment, Maiduguri.
Delivering the COAS’ remarks, Major General Ajose stated that decent accommodation and a conducive living environment were essential to sustaining troops’ morale, discipline and effectiveness.
He emphasised that operational excellence on the battlefield must be supported by adequate welfare provisions and a strong administrative foundation at home.
He described investments in accommodation as investments in human capital and a practical demonstration of the Nigerian Army’s appreciation of personnel’s sacrifices and contributions to national security.
The COAS expressed profound appreciation to the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, His Excellency Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, for his continued support to the Nigerian Army, particularly in force development and personnel welfare. He also acknowledged the contributions of relevant departments and directorates, contractors, project supervisors and other stakeholders whose efforts supported the execution of the projects, noting that sustained institutional support remains vital to the Army’s transformation and operational effectiveness.
The COAS charged beneficiary personnel and their commanders to maintain a strong culture of discipline, accountability and proper maintenance to preserve the facilities for long-term use. The commissioning reinforces the Nigerian Army’s Soldiers First Concept, which places the welfare, wellbeing and professional development of personnel at the centre of its institutional priorities and recognises their importance to sustained morale, operational readiness and effective service to the nation.
Beyond the quarters commissioned, several other projects are ongoing at Maimalari Cantonment to improve living and working conditions. These include additional Corporals and Below Quarters, the drilling of two boreholes, construction of a 50-bed ward for 7 Division Medical Services and Hospital, a new Headquarters 7 Division complex, Senior Officers’ Quarters and the renovation of existing family accommodation.
These interventions reflect broader efforts to strengthen military infrastructure and provide personnel and their families with improved housing, healthcare and essential facilities.
In his welcome address, the Acting General Officer Commanding 7 Division and Commander Sector 1 OPHK, Brigadier General Solomon Diwa, described the commissioning as another significant milestone in the Army’s welfare initiatives. He noted that Corporals and Below constitute a vital component of the Army’s fighting strength and perform indispensable roles at the tactical level. He stressed that providing them with decent accommodation demonstrates the Army’s recognition of their service and sacrifices while reinforcing the connection between personnel welfare, high morale and combat readiness. Similarly, the Acting GOC urged occupants to uphold high standards of cleanliness, take ownership of the quarters and ensure their responsible use.
In his project description, the Commander, 47 Engineer Brigade, Brigadier General Abubakar Saleh, disclosed that the renovation was awarded to Messrs Ammah Contractors Limited by the Office of the Chief of Army Staff, Directorate of Procurement. He explained that following a site assessment, six blocks of six-family Corporals and Below Quarters, comprising 36 two-bedroom flats, were selected for renovation as suitable alternatives to the originally designated structures. He noted that the buildings were previously in a severely dilapidated condition, with leaking roofs, structural cracks and damaged floors. The renovation involved extensive structural rehabilitation, including the introduction of columns and beams, repairs to damaged floor slabs and masonry, replacement of roofing sheets, doors and windows, and complete electrical and plumbing installations.
He added that 47 Engineer Brigade supervised the project under the guidance of Headquarters 7 Division to ensure compliance with approved specifications and quality standards.
While delivering the vote of thanks on behalf of the beneficiaries, Warrant Officer Ogunmodede Sunday expressed his sincere appreciation to the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, NAM, for prioritising personnel welfare through the Soldiers First Concept. He also thanked the Theatre Commander for his leadership and for representing the COAS at the occasion. He noted that the renovated quarters and other ongoing infrastructure projects demonstrate the Nigerian Army’s commitment to improving personnel welfare and living conditions. He pledged that the beneficiaries would maintain the facilities responsibly and reciprocate the gesture through discipline, professionalism and dedication to duty.
He concluded by appreciating the project supervisors, contractors and everyone who contributed to the success of the project, while praying for God’s continued protection of troops, blessings upon their families and lasting peace and security for Nigeria.

items.author: Peter Moses
items.content:
The Department of State Services (DSS), Ogun State Command, has reportedly invited the three principal officers of the Fusengbuwa ruling house over the alleged sale of expression of interest forms to aspirants seeking to become the next Awujale of Ijebuland.
The selection process for the vacant stool, which became vacant in July 2025 following the death of 91-year-old Oba Sikiru Adetona, who reigned for 65 years, has been marred by controversy, litigation and repeated postponements.
Our correspondent gathered that those invited by the DSS include Otunba Abdulateef Owoyemi, chairman of the ruling house; Otunba Dokun Ajidagba, deputy chairman; and Prof. Fassy Yusuf, vice chairman.
In its letter, the three family heads were directed to appear at the DSS state office in Abeokuta at 4 p.m. on Thursday, October 29, 2026.
The letter partly read: “I am directed to invite you for a meeting with the State Director of Security (SDS), Department of State Services (DSS), Ogun State, Oke-Mosan, Abeokuta, today, 29th October, 2026, at 1600 hours (4 p.m.).
“The meeting is in furtherance of investigations into activities relating to the sale of expression of interest forms to princes interested in contesting for the vacant stool of Awujale of Ijebuland.
“Kindly note that an officer has been designated at the main gate to facilitate your entrance clearance into the premises. Accept the Director’s best wishes, please.”
Yusuf, when contacted, confirmed receiving the letter of invitation but said he was attending to a matter at the Supreme Court in Abuja and could not honour the invitation.
The professor of mass communication and lawyer said, “I just received the letter from the DSS not long ago, but I am in Abuja attending to a matter at the Supreme Court. I have discountenanced their letter.”
The deputy chairman of the ruling house, Otunba Dokun Ajidagba, also confirmed receiving the DSS invitation at about 2:30 p.m. on Thursday.
Ajidagba said, “I received the DSS invitation on Thursday at about 2:30 p.m. and was told to report at their office by 4:30 p.m. There was, however, no way I could honour such an invitation when all these matters are already in court. The status quo must be allowed to remain; that is the position of the law.”
Daily Trust reports that security agencies, including the Ogun State Police Command, had twice summoned nine Ijebu-Ode kingmakers and the three ruling house officials to appear at the police headquarters in Eleweran, Abeokuta, over allegations of bribery and financial inducement in connection with the selection of a new Awujale and paramount ruler of Ijebuland.
Owoyemi has repeatedly denied any wrongdoing in the selection process during media engagements.
He, alongside Ajidagba and Yusuf, has also instituted legal action against the state government over its decision to halt the selection process in January.
The Fusengbuwa ruling house had also dragged Governor Dapo Abiodun, the Awujale kingmakers and five others before the High Court sitting in Ijebu-Ode, seeking orders compelling the completion of the process for selecting the next Awujale and paramount ruler of Ijebuland.
The suit, numbered HCJ/149/2026 and dated August 21, 2026, was filed by Owoyemi, Ajidagba and Yusuf.
Also joined as defendants were the state Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Mr Oluwasina Ogungbade (SAN); the Ogun State Executive Council; the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Ganiyu Hamzat; and the Secretary of Ijebu-Ode Local Government.
Other defendants include members of the Awujale Afobaje/Kingmakers Council: Olorogun Sonny Kuku, Chief Rasheed Adesanya, Chief Oluwaranti Lekan Osifeso, Chief Jimi Lawal, Chief Abimbola Okenla, Chief Kunle Ogunade, Chief Agboola Alausa, Chief Adebisi Adaran and Chief Ayotunde Ola Odulaja.
The claimants are asking the court to determine whether the state government had the legal authority to order or facilitate the alleged entry into and locking of the Awujale Palace on January 20, 2026, “to physically prevent” the kingmakers from convening and concluding the statutory selection process for the new Awujale.
On Tuesday, Governor Abiodun reassured the people of Ijebuland that a new Awujale would emerge before May 29, 2027.
According to a statement issued on Wednesday, the governor gave the assurance on Tuesday at the Ogun East Senatorial District stakeholders’ meeting in Ijebu-Ode, where he engaged representatives of various interest groups on traditional affairs, governance and the district’s economic prospects.
He was quoted as saying, “On the succession process for the revered Awujale stool, my administration is committed to facilitating a smooth, peaceful and widely acceptable process leading to the emergence of a new monarch.”
The governor acknowledged the importance of the Awujale institution to the cultural heritage, identity and unity of Ijebuland, appealing to the people to remain calm and patient while the necessary processes were being concluded.
He said his administration was giving the matter the attention it deserved to ensure that the process was concluded peacefully and that the emergence of a new Awujale enjoyed the acceptance and support of the people.
The Awujale stool became vacant in July 2025 following the death of Oba Sikiru Adetona at the age of 91, after 65 years on the throne.
The Ogun State Government halted the selection process in January 2026, citing petitions from security agencies and stakeholders, following an earlier suspension in December 2025 over procedural concerns.
A total of 95 aspirants—94 princes and one princess—emerged from the ruling house’s nomination process held in Ijebu-Ode in December 2025 before the government halted the selection process.

items.title: Just In: Tinubu lands in Saudi Arabia for Umrah
items.summary:
President Bola Tinubu on Thursday evening arrived in Saudi Arabia, landing at the King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah.
He was received by Nigeria’s ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Yakubu Gambo, and the Saudi head of royal protocol Ahmad bin Thafir.
The President is scheduled to perform Umrah, also known as the lesser hajj, and is expected to return to Nigeria next week after completing the religious exercise.
Thursday’s trip marks the second time Tinubu has travelled to Makkah to perform Umrah since assuming office on May 29, 2023.
President Tinubu visited the holy city in November 2023, shortly after attending the Saudi-African Summit in Riyadh, where he also prayed for divine guidance in leading Nigeria.
The latest trip is part of a series of foreign engagements undertaken by Tinubu since becoming president. He has visited more than 30 countries in over 50 unique and recurring trips.
