items.author: Leocadia Bongben
items.content:
Oil rigs threaten biodiversity and compromise the well-being of coastal and Indigenous communities
Originally published on Global Voices
Offshore platform from Garand-Batanga Beach, Kribi South region of Cameroon. Photo by Leocadia Bongben. Used with permission.
This story by Leocadia Bongben was produced with the support of Internews’ Earth Journalism Network.
Dede Sluk, 35, a father of three, sits pensively in front of his plank house, fishing nets hanging at the corner, wondering how to fish for his family and prepare his children for school. Sluk lives in the village of Grand-Batanga 2 in Kribi, in southern Cameroon. Like many fishermen there, Sluk is annoyed by the lack of access to fish beyond the offshore platforms. He states,
We don’t have access to areas with high fish stock; the Battaillon D’intervention Rapid (BIR), a special army unit guarding the petroleum platform, prohibits passage.
According to the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative’s (EITI) 2023 report, oil and gas contributed FCFA 774.51 billion (USD 1.3 million) to Cameroon’s budget. However, these oil rigs threaten biodiversity and compromise the well-being of coastal and Indigenous communities.
Offshore oil and gas platforms are massive marine structures used to explore, drill, extract, and process petroleum and natural gas from rocky layers beneath the ocean floor; some require the laying of pipes. The yellow flames and smoke from the Ebome Marine Terminal, a petroleum rig operated by Perenco and SNH west of Grand Batanga, are visible 6.5 kilometers (4.04 miles) from the Kribi coastline.
Two other platforms are the Sanaga 2 offshore facility around Kribi, connected via undersea pipelines from onshore in Bipaga. West of the Kribi Port is the Kome-Kribi 1 Terminal (FSO), built in 2003, operated by Cameroon Oil Transport Company — the Chad-Cameroon pipeline. Meanwhile, the Hilli Episeyo, operated by Golar LNG, Perenco, and the National Hydrocarbons Corporation (SNH), departed in July 2026, after eight years.
Among the platforms of concern are those operated by Perenco, a Franco-British company and a prominent player in the oil and gas sector, tagged as an opaque multinational by Friends of the Earth for oil spills, wastewater discharges, gas flaring, and old pipelines crossing rivers. An Info Congo investigation indicted Perenco for flaring and environmental hazards, endangering the coastal ecosystem and the health of local communities.
Tar balls found in a marine protected area, dolphin and whale strandings, and fish scarcity are hidden costs of offshore oil and gas exploitation, which seems to stall Cameroon’s progress towards the 30×30 marine target under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.
Fish scarcity linked to petroleum platforms
Laure Ndingue, 50, a mother of five who worked as a fish roaster along Grand Batanga beach for over 10 years, knows that, opposite her charcoal braise, an oil and gas platform sits in the ocean. She recalls,
Growing up, six barfish were sold for FCFA 500 (USD 0.85); the price jumped to FCFA 1,000 (USD 1.70) and now is FCFA 5000 (USD 8.54) per kilogram. Even frozen fish is now expensive. Before, we were not suffering; fish stocks have declined.
Petroleum exploitation is done when the platform is planted on a rock, and most times, the rocks are marine ecosystems that breed fish. Now, the rocks are occupied by offshore installations, contributing to reduced fish stocks, explains Divine Francois Xavier Mbunje, a fisherman, geologist, and president of the 150-fishermen union at the Grand Batanga beach.
He suggests the government can demarcate platforms and areas of high fish concentration. About a kilometer or two from the beach, there is no fish, and three kilometers deep, we can have around forty kilograms of fish. Sluk proposes that oil and gas platforms should help the local population with activities like fish farming, loans to make up for the fish scarcity, recommending that the government provide a loan scheme and subsidize the purchase of motorized equipment, as this will help the fishers go further into the ocean.
He estimates the required nylon fishing gear for a fisherman at FCFA 1 million (USD 1,720) and FCFA 1,500,000 (USD 2,572) for an engine. Sluk explains,
Motorised gear will help us fish towards Ntem, Lokonje, and Douala away from the offshore platforms. We now rely on crabs to feed the family, with fish becoming rare.
Smelly, oily nets and tar balls
Early in 2026, fishermen reported oil on their nets smelling like crude. “I was fishing and witnessed this strange phenomenon, which lasted for more than three weeks and gradually disappeared,” says Ebodje Emile, a fisherman in Ebodje village, where the marine protected area is situated, 50 kilometers (31.1 miles) from Kribi. Leon Kisito Bekwale, who has fished for about 35 years, still has nets his fishermen used, colored by oil. Still looking worried, he turns the nets dumped at the corner of the house to reveal the dark, oily parts.
Leon Kisito holding oily nets in Ebodje, Cameroon. Photo by Leocadia Bongben. Used with permission.
“I don’t know if this is linked to the offshore gas and oil,” Bekwale says, explaining that the wooden local boats only go for about three kilometers, suggesting the substance was inside the marine protected area, far from the petroleum platforms. Fishermen reported the phenomenon to the park conservator and NGOs.
A Perenco spokesperson told Global Voices via email:
We are not aware of any issues in the field across our sites, whether at the Northern or Southern sites. The comment may be referring to the northern coast of Cameroon, bordering Nigeria, where we have witnessed oil slicks drifting from Nigeria to Cameroon over recent years (possibly related to tanker discharge of oily waste or activities in Nigerian oil fields). This does not relate to any Perenco activity. Cameroon security forces are patrolling our sites and have also not reported any incidents.
Dr Jean Kenfack, focal point for seas and oceans at the Ministry of Environment, Nature Protection and Sustainable Development, MINEPDED, also doubts the incident, outlining the procedure to inform the ministry of the incident: “In case of an incident, the departmental delegate sends the information to the ministry. In case of a spillage, an inspection mission is deployed to identify the author for sanctions if confirmed, and there is a pumping station in Kribi managed by the ministry with SNH and the Marines.”
Meanwhile, marine biologist Joel Wanba, Megafauna Officer at Tube Awu in Ebodje, who links the oily substance to activities along the coast, says, “But we do not have the means to analyze the substance given the small NGO budget; it is difficult to conduct such research.
Tar balls linked to offshore platforms form when crude oil spills into water. They are frequent along the coast and in the Manyange Na Elombo Campo marine protected area”, says Wamba. “This area is noted for sea turtles that may mistake tar balls for food, leading to indigestion and death. When we see residues, it indicates a malfunction. Contaminants build up in fish and other marine life over time when exposed to polluted water. When we eat contaminated fish, those toxins build up in our own bodies too, ” Wanba states. By obstructing sunlight, hurting living tissue, and harming the surrounding ocean environment, oil and gas spills damage seagrass beds and coral reefs, he adds.
Tar-Balls-in-Ebodje-Kribi-Cameroon by Leocadia Bongben. Used with permission.
Tube Awu surveyed eight sites using bioindicators (living plants, animals, and microbes whose presence or absence suggests environmental health), which were not found at all sites, revealing an unhealthy environment and dying corals, according to Wamba.
Whales and dolphins stranding
The African Marine Mammal Organization (AMCO), Cedric Fogwan, a marine biologist, reveals how offshore exploitation affects marine biodiversity. “Offshore exploitation impacts mostly whales, dolphins, and marine turtles, as their activities disrupt animal freedom. The sharks and whales no longer have any space for their nesting activity and the possibility of feeding on coral reefs,” he states. “Whales and dolphins that live in shallow waters use echolocation to communicate. Offshore activities’ noise interferes with echolocation behavior, leading to strandings — whales or dolphins washing up on the shore — because they are disoriented and lose direction getting to areas too shallow for them to survive or get entangled in a net they couldn’t locate,” Fogwan says.
Experts say installing pipes destroys coral balance, the most important marine biodiversity habitats that support animals like dolphins, sharks, turtles, and whales. Consequently, platforms reduce bottom diversity, killing everything underneath when the structure is placed over their habitat. However, for those platforms that stay for only a short time, the ecosystem can restore itself, Fogwan states.
Citing model nations like the Seychelles and Zanzibar Island, growing tourism based on the conservation of their natural resources, he laments that development is frequently perceived as building harbors and exploiting oil, activities that are not sustainable.
Management of marine environmental hazards
MINEPDED oversees environmental protection, including offshore exploitation. The Petroleum Code and the Abidjan Convention set out rules to combat marine pollution in West and Central Africa, while SNH oversees the National Oil Spillage Contingency Plan. Cameroon adopted its National Environmental Management Plan (NEMP) in 1996, which incorporates pollution control, risk mitigation, and environmental impact assessments (EIAs) before starting development projects. However, it is not clear how regulations are respected.
According to J. Folack, a researcher at IRAD RHSM, budgetary constraints, a lack of target-oriented research, and competing responsibilities of the ministries involved in coastal zone management hinder NEMP implementation.
MINEPDED's yearly inspections verify if environmental impact studies on potential hazards are updated, and semester environmental management plans for offshore platforms are checked for grey areas; however, the results are not public.
“With demarcation and good fishing gear, we can get enough to feed our families, and sell some to change our standard of living,” Sluk concludes.
Fisherman with a wooden boat at Ebodje Beach in Cameroon. Photo by Leocadia Bongben. Used with permission.
Written by Leocadia Bongben

items.summary:

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
Healthtech startup Cent, launched by Practo cofounder Shashank ND earlier this year, announced the raise of $15 Mn (about ₹143 Cr) in a Series A round led by Blume Ventures and existing investor South Park Commons (SPC), with participation from individual investors including former Vodafone CEO Arun Sarin and former OpenAI B2B CTO Srinivas Narayanan, among others.
The fresh capital will be deployed to strengthen the preventive healthcare startup’s R&D function. Besides, the startup also intends to expand its AI, engineering and clinical teams.
Apart from the fundraise, Cent also announced the acquisition of Medsee, an AI-powered radiology reporting workflow platform, to help it deliver faster and more consistent reporting as scan volumes increase.
Cent was launched by Shashank, along with ex-Ola Electric CMO Anshul Khandelwal and former Lenskart product head Arpit Garg earlier this year. It last raised a $5 Mn seed funding round back then from OneFlow Holdings and South Park Commons.
Bidding to build a positioning of helping users live a hundred years, Cent combines precision radiology, AI, and biomarkers to screen asymptomatic patients for over 300 conditions like cardiac disease, cancer, and neurological disorders.
Its flagship offering, Cent Check, combines full-body MRI, low-dose CT, DEXA scans, ECG, echocardiography in a single visit lasting around two hours. Its proprietary CCNM protocol is designed to assess cancer, cardiac, neurological and metabolic health risks.
It uses AI to consolidate findings from different diagnostic modalities and generate organ-level risk assessments, while AI-assisted imaging helps reduce MRI scan times, with an aim to identify serious conditions before symptoms begin to surface.
Its comprehensive health screening package is priced at ₹27,500, positioning itself as an alternative to conventional preventive health checkups that largely rely on blood tests and limited imaging.
The startup said it has completed 10,000 preventive whole-body scans across Bengaluru, Mumbai and Delhi NCR since inception. It aims to scale this to 1 Cr scans by 2035.
Cent plans to use the data generated through its scans to establish health baselines for asymptomatic Indians, train models to identify disease risks earlier and support clinical research.

items.summary:

The company was preparing to obtain the financing to strengthen its financial resources amid ongoing military tensions in the Middle East, risks to oil exports and an uncertain economic outlook.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Saudi Arabia’s state-owned oil company Saudi Aramco is close to securing a $10 billion loan from a large group of international banks, according to a special report published by Bloomberg on Monday.
The company was preparing to obtain the financing to strengthen its financial resources amid ongoing military tensions in the Middle East, risks to oil exports and an uncertain economic outlook.
The report said Saudi Aramco could sign an agreement with global banks for a new loan of around $10b in the coming weeks, adding that talks with US, British, Chinese and Japanese banks had reached their final stages.
Sources familiar with the development, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the company was seeking a credit facility that would let it draw funds up to a specified limit as needed. The facility would be revolving credit, meaning Aramco would not have to take the entire amount at once.
Read: Aramco halts October crude deliveries to some European refiners after pipeline attack: report
Saudi Arabian state-backed oil company Aramco is nearing agreement with international banks on a $10 billion loan that would bolster its finances as conflicts in the Middle East threaten crude exports https://t.co/J8WYQJisYx
— Bloomberg (@business) October 26, 2026
It could use the funds when needed and, after repayment, draw them again under the agreed terms.
Major banks from US, UK, China and Japan to provide loan
According to Bloomberg, several major global banks were expected to participate in the proposed loan for Saudi Aramco. They include JPMorgan Chase and Citigroup of the United States, HSBC of the United Kingdom, Bank of China and Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, and Japan’s Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group.
The participation of financial institutions from several countries indicates that major international banks remain interested in providing financial facilities to Saudi Aramco despite ongoing military tensions in the region. Sources said the proposed interest rate could be 60 basis points above SOFR, the benchmark rate used for US dollar financing.
In financial terms, 60 basis points equal 0.60%. Thus, the applicable interest rate would be 0.60% above the relevant benchmark, although the final cost would depend on the agreement’s terms and any other potential fees.
Bloomberg reported that Saudi Aramco and some of the major banks involved declined to comment, while an immediate response could not be obtained from the Chinese banks. Therefore, the loan amount and terms are being viewed as details of ongoing negotiations rather than a finalised agreement.
أرامكو تقترب من توقيع اتفاقية قرض بـ10 مليارات دولار مع بنوك عالمية بحسب بلومبرغ #العربيةـBusiness
— العربية Business (@AlArabiya_Bn) October 26, 2026
Important decision amid Iran war and risks to oil exports
Saudi Aramco’s plan comes as ongoing military tensions in the Middle East have affected global energy markets and oil shipments from Gulf countries. The war with Iran has pushed up crude oil prices in global markets, increasing the possibility of higher revenue for Saudi Aramco.
At the same time, military attacks, disruptions to maritime routes and threats to oil facilities have created new challenges for the company. In recent weeks, Yemen’s Houthi group has claimed attacks on Saudi oil facilities, refineries and key facilities in Yanbu on the Red Sea coast.
Read More: Houthis hit Aramco HQ, vow more attacks
These actions, along with disruption to commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, have increased uncertainty surrounding oil exports and transportation costs. In these circumstances, securing a $10b credit facility from banks could provide Aramco with additional financial flexibility, allowing it to access capital quickly when needed and continue its business activities.
Saudi Aramco previously arranged a $10b revolving credit facility in 2024, according to Bloomberg. Of this, $7b was provided through international banks, while an additional $3b was obtained from regional banks under Islamic murabaha financing.
Murabaha is a method used in Islamic finance in which capital is provided under specific commercial and financial terms instead of a conventional interest-bearing loan. The new agreement would give Aramco another important facility to meet its financial needs.
However, it is unclear whether the company will replace or renew the existing facility under the new arrangement, or use it as additional financial capacity. It is also important not to equate the $10b credit facility immediately with an equal increase in the company’s debt, as a revolving facility allows the company to use funds according to its needs, while undrawn funds do not necessarily become payable debt.
Gulf energy companies increasing reliance on global debt markets
Amid the ongoing war and trade disruptions in the Middle East, major Gulf energy and power companies have also increasingly sought financial resources from banks. Bloomberg reported that QatarEnergy, Qatar’s state-owned energy company, obtained a $3b loan this month with significant participation from Chinese banks.
Saudi Electricity Company arranged Islamic murabaha financing worth 15.8b riyals, or approximately $4.1b, in July. Seven Gulf banks participated in that agreement.
These financial arrangements indicate that major companies in the region are trying to diversify their sources of funding amid uncertain global conditions, reducing reliance on any single market or financing method.
Saudi Aramco is considered one of the world’s largest oil-producing companies and plays a fundamental role in Saudi government revenues and the national economy. Changes in the company’s financial position, oil production and exports are important not only for Saudi Arabia but also for global energy markets.
According to Bloomberg, the proposed $10b loan could be signed in the coming weeks. However, the company or the relevant banks have not yet formally announced a finalised agreement.

items.author: Debarghya Sil
items.content:
VerSe Innovation, the parent of news aggregator Dailyhunt and short-video platform Josh, has seen two investment funds managed by Baillie Gifford mark down the value of their holdings by around 80% over different periods.
Pacific Horizon Investment Trust valued its holding in VerSe at £4.08 Mn as of July 2026, down 51.4% from £8.39 Mn a year earlier. The holding’s value has fallen 80.3% from £20.69 Mn ($27.7 Mn) in July 2024.
Separately, The Schiehallion Fund valued its VerSe holding at $7.47 Mn as of August 2026, down 78.2% from $34.31 Mn in January 2025.
ET reported that Schiehallion’s investment represented a 1.3% stake in VerSe, implying a company valuation of about $576 Mn – nearly 90% below its $5 Bn valuation in 2022.
The implied valuation reflects the fund’s assessment of its investment, rather than a price established through a fresh funding round.
VerSe’s $5 Bn Valuation Under Pressure
VerSe last raised a major funding round in April 2022, when it secured $805 Mn at a reported valuation of $5 Bn.
In August 2024, TechCrunch reported that investor 360 ONE had valued VerSe at around $2.9 Bn, about 42% below its 2022 valuation.
VerSe disputed that interpretation, saying the assessment did not represent its overall valuation and that other investors continued to value it at around $5 Bn. At the time, the company also said it had not conducted a price-discovery funding round since April 2022.
The latest portfolio disclosures show that investors continue to reassess the value of their holdings. However, they do not establish a definitive company-wide valuation.
Founded in 2007 by Virendra Gupta and later joined by cofounder Umang Bedi, VerSe Innovation operates news aggregator Dailyhunt and short-video platform Josh. The company has raised nearly $1.7 Bn across funding rounds from investors including Google, Microsoft, Peak XV Partners, Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan, and Luxor Capital.
Revenue Growth, Lower Burn
Schiehallion had flagged concerns about VerSe’s performance in its interim report for the six months ended July 2025. The fund cited a deterioration in the company’s trajectory, including declining revenue, as the reason for a substantial downward revaluation during that period.
VerSe subsequently reported an improvement in its FY25 financial performance. According to the company, operating revenue rose 88% to ₹1,930 Cr from ₹1,029 Cr in FY24. Excluding acquisitions, operating revenue grew 33% to ₹1,373 Cr.
Its EBITDA burn, excluding non-cash expenses, narrowed 20% to ₹738 Cr from ₹920 Cr.
VerSe has been betting on acquisitions and adtech to diversify revenue. Its 2024 acquisition of Valueleaf was intended to strengthen advertiser targeting through NexVerse.ai, while Magzter expanded its subscription content business beyond advertising.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
Ugandan startup XenFi is helping internet service providers (ISPs) and Wi-Fi hotspot operators sell internet access, manage customers and collect payments via mobile money from a single platform.
Founded in 2025, XenFi has built a hotspot billing and management platform that also lets operators monitor transactions and manage multiple MikroTik routers from a centralised dashboard.
“Many hotspot operators need to manage customer access, sell vouchers, collect payments, monitor revenue and administer multiple routers. Handling these processes through disconnected tools or manual systems can make it difficult to track transactions, maintain operational efficiency and scale,” said Charles Wasswa, XenFi’s CEO.
“XenFi brings these functions together through a centralised platform that supports mobile money payments and simplifies the management of hotspot businesses.”
The startup is self-funded by its founders, which Wasswa said forced discipline from the start.
“Starting without relying on external investors required us to be disciplined in how we allocated resources, developed our technology and acquired customers,” he said.
That approach has paid off. XenFi is already profitable and employs more than 100 people.
“Rather than treating profitability as the end goal, we are using it to strengthen our technology, expand our operations and reach more customers,” Wasswa said.
The platform serves approximately 6,000 active users in Uganda and has customers in close to 15 African countries, including Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi and Gabon. XenFi has also set up a physical presence in Kenya.
“Uptake has been encouraging,” said Wasswa. “Beyond Uganda, we are seeing adoption across other African markets, with businesses welcoming our system as a solution for managing their hotspot operations and payments.”
XenFi makes money through platform charges and billing and transaction fees, which vary by service and market.
“As our customers grow and process more activity through our platform, we have opportunities to grow our revenue alongside them,” Wasswa said.
The startup competes with international hotspot billing platforms, regional providers, locally developed billing tools and operators still relying on manual systems. Wasswa said XenFi stands out through its focus on African market needs, payment integration and ease of use.
Expansion has brought its own challenges.
“Payment systems, customer expectations, connectivity infrastructure and regulatory requirements differ from country to country, making international expansion a continuous learning process,” Wasswa said.
“Customers need reliable systems that support their businesses consistently, so we place considerable importance on product reliability, customer support and continuous improvement.”
XenFi now plans to deepen its presence in existing markets, strengthen local partnerships and move into more African countries.
“We are proud of how far we have come, but we see this as the beginning of a much larger journey,” said Wasswa.

items.author: Meha Agarwal
items.content:
Remember the charm of walking into a Crossword store, picking up a book and spending hours reading it without anyone expecting you to buy it? With cosy reading corners, a café on the side and occasional author interactions, it gave book lovers a place to unwind, explore and lose themselves in stories. Or Hamleys, where little eyes light up and young hearts skip a beat at the sight of colourful toys and a magical world that feels straight out of a storybook.
Brands such as Pepperfry have also made shopping more personal by letting customers experience how furniture and décor would look and feel in fully furnished living rooms, bedrooms and dining spaces. Chumbak, meanwhile, brings its playful personality to life through colourful interiors and distinctive designs that make its stores as vibrant as the products on display. Of course, how can one forget Decathlon?
Long before experiential retail became a buzzword, these stores gave customers several reasons to visit beyond simply making a purchase.
Now, a new wave of fashion and lifestyle brands is borrowing this playbook to take experiential retail a step further. Rather than simply creating attractive spaces or encouraging product discovery, brands such as Gully Labs, Comet, Nothing, Almost Gods and Broadway are experimenting with store design and riffing on traditional retail motifs to bring their brand identity to life.
Take Comet’s flagship store in Bengaluru’s Indiranagar, for instance. With shattered walls, suspended rock formations and sneakers seemingly emerging from concrete, the space resembles the aftermath of a comet crashing to the ground rather than a conventional footwear showroom.
Yet, the experience isn’t just about aesthetics. Instead of crowding shelves with inventory, Comet displays a curated selection of sneakers, with additional sizes stored in concealed drawers. Its dedicated section, The Vault, showcases sold-out sneakers like museum exhibits, even though they are no longer available for purchase.
The D2C sneaker brand spent around seven to eight months designing and building the store, working with an architecture firm to bring its unusual concept to life.
While store design has increasingly become a way to communicate brand identity, build communities and create unique experiences, how are brands balancing creative ambition with the unit economics realities? And can their distinctive retail experiences become a lasting competitive advantage?
Reinventing The Storefront
For years, the conventional retail store followed a familiar pattern. Products occupied shelves, promotional displays highlighted the latest collections, and layouts were designed to move shoppers towards the billing counter.
That formula works, but does not really motivate customers, who can buy almost anything from their phones, to make the effort to visit a store. The reason is simple. They are looking for more than a transaction.
The influence of this thinking is visible at Broadway, a multi-brand fashion and lifestyle retailer housing more than 200 brands. Rather than relying entirely on merchandise displays, it has integrated services and activities that encourage customers to explore products in different ways.
For example, its stores feature salon experiences for beauty product trials and sampling, alongside dedicated stages where brands can organise events and interact with their communities. It also offers AI-assisted analysis to help shoppers identify shades and products that suit their skin tones and complexion, with stylists able to recommend products accordingly.
However, the process involves continuous experimentation. “A service that appears attractive during planning may not necessarily appeal to customers once introduced. These decisions are refined based on customer behaviour rather than treated as permanent elements of the original design,” said a sectoral expert.
But the push towards experiential retail is not being driven by changing consumer expectations alone. For digital-first brands, it is also becoming a question of customer acquisition.
Ujwal Sutaria, founding partner at VC firm TDV Partners believes the rising cost of digital advertising is making physical stores an increasingly interesting brand-building channel.
“Digital acquisition costs in India have become brutal, and a store on a 100 ft road can work as a better ad than any Instagram budget,” Sutaria said.
This is particularly relevant for brands selling premium products. For a shopper considering a pair of sneakers north of ₹5K, the opportunity to examine the product, understand its craftsmanship and experience the brand firsthand could help overcome hesitation that digital advertising alone may struggle to address.
Are There Execution Challenges?
According to Mitali Juneja, creative director at architectural design planning and studio, Studio Ordonnance, the architecture firm behind Comet and Almost Gods’ stores, most established retailers still prefer conventional formats.
The hesitation may not be financial. In larger organisations, proposals have to go through multiple levels of approval. Also, many decision-makers could be wary of committing to unfamiliar or unconventional ideas.
On the flip side, founder-led brands have greater flexibility to experiment, offering the reason why some of the more visible experiments are emerging from younger brands rather than established retail chains.
Next, even after a concept is approved, a transition to a physical space can be difficult. Unconventional installations often require techniques that local fabricators have little experience with.
For Comet’s suspended rock structures, for instance, Mitali’s team had to repeatedly guide workers accustomed to making traditional sculptures.
To minimise errors, detailed working drawings and inspections at different construction stages are needed. Architects must also adapt designs to the property’s structural limitations, including ceiling heights and building specifications.
However, she believes the bigger challenge is balancing creativity with functionality. Product visibility, customer comfort and the ease of trying or purchasing merchandise cannot be compromised simply to create an unusual-looking store.
The goal, therefore, is not just to deliver an impressive space, but one that works equally well for the brand and its customers.
Can The Experience Pay For Itself?
For fashion and lifestyle brands already grappling with high rentals and operating costs, the question is whether a distinctive store can generate enough value to justify the additional investment.
Sutaria believes that looking at store-level sales alone misses the wider contribution of experiential retail. A customer may discover a sneaker brand offline, try its products and eventually purchase online. Similarly, a store event could generate interest well beyond its immediate neighbourhood.
“Store P&L alone is the wrong lens. I’d look at the halo effect: Is online traffic and conversion rising in nearby pincodes? What’s the blended CAC for customers who discover the brand in-store? Do they repeat more often?” Sutaria explained.
However, the challenge is establishing whether these interactions generate additional business or simply create visibility. For multi-brand retailers such as Broadway, this becomes even harder, as product trials, sampling and engagement with individual brands may not immediately translate into sales.
Yet, the investment can pay off. According to Comet cofounder Utkarsh Gupta, its Indiranagar flagship achieved a seven-month capex payback despite costing 20–50% more than a conventional store. He also claims it records the highest conversion rate among footwear stores on that high street.
However, Sutaria cautions that the economics must ultimately justify the experience. “If the store lowers blended CAC and improves repeat rates enough to lift brand-level LTV, the capex is justified. Otherwise, it’s just an expensive billboard.”
Can Every Store Be A Flagship?
Even if an experiential store delivers strong returns, replicating the same concept across dozens of locations can be expensive and time-consuming.
Comet is addressing this by standardising most of its design elements while experimenting at select locations. According to Gupta, nearly 90% of the brand’s design elements are scalable, allowing it to retain a consistent identity without repeating the seven-to-eight-month development process required for its first flagship.
However, Sutaria also believes that most single-brand D2C companies will follow a different approach. “The scalable version is a hub-and-spoke model: one or two flagships build culture, while smaller formats and shared-shelf platforms drive reach. That’s why Broadway is interesting. Its 40,000 sq ft Bandra flagship houses 200+ brands, spreading the cost of the experience across multiple businesses.”
Such shared formats could offer emerging fashion and lifestyle brands access to product discovery, sampling and community engagement without requiring each to build an expensive standalone store.
Still, expansion is not the only challenge. An elaborate store can lose its novelty, while excessive investment in physical retail can divert resources from product development and distribution.
Juneja of Studio Ordonnance believes some experimental design elements will eventually disappear because they are impractical. However, she expects the broader shift towards stores that express a brand’s identity to continue.
The real test, therefore, will be creating spaces that remain distinctive without compromising the shopping experience or the economics of running a retail business.
THE STARTUP SPOTLIGHT | HOW KOBSOOK IS BRINGING NEURODIVERGENT ARTISTS TO SNEAKER DESIGN
KobSook turns original artwork by neurodivergent artists into limited-edition canvas sneakers. The brand works with AEMP (Inclusive Accessible TechEd) as a training partner to help artists develop skills in design and other business operations.
Its portfolio spans high-tops, low-top sneakers, loafers and slip-ons for men and women, with designs featuring doodles, abstract patterns, colourful checks and other original artwork. Products listed on its website span roughly ₹1,700 to ₹2,500 at sale prices.
KobSook produces limited quantities of each design rather than relying on mass production, and also accepts requests for customised designs. The brand sells through its own website and ecommerce marketplaces including Myntra, Amazon, AJIO and Flipkart.
The Deep Dive
Ecommerce Buzz
L Catterton Bets On Glance: The consumer-focused investment firm has invested in InMobi-backed Glance to support the latter’s US expansion. Currently, Glance uses agentic AI to drive product discovery and purchases across smartphones and connected TVs, including through partnerships with Samsung, Motorola and DIRECTV in the US.
Myntra Swings To Loss: Flipkart-owned Myntra reported a net loss of ₹581.8 Cr in FY26, reversing a ₹546.3 Cr profit a year earlier. This came on the back of its operating revenue falling 13.5% to ₹5,242.5 Cr.
Swiggy’s Pivot To Inventory Model: Swiggy will begin shifting Instamart to an inventory-led model by mid-Q3 FY27, with the transition expected to take 2–3 quarters and improve contribution margins by 80 basis points. The move comes as Instamart’s adjusted EBITDA loss widened to ₹895 Cr in Q2 FY27
PharmEasy Veterans Raise ₹63 Cr: Founded by five former PharmEasy executives, Chapter Homes raised ₹63 Cr at a valuation of nearly ₹1,000 Cr. The startup plans to expand beyond its HOKIPO home furnishings brand into cookware, home décor and small kitchen appliances, using AI and a shared supply chain to scale its portfolio.
The Operator Question
How can pop-up shops at festive carnivals (Durga Puja/Diwali/Christmas melas) help unconventional new-age lifestyle brands? What is the cost involved? Is it worth the investment? How should brands measure the ROI?
Speaking to Inc42, Cure By Design founder Daanish Matheen spoke about the pop-up shop aspect of D2C retail. The startup offers hemp-based CBD oils, balms and pain-relief solutions, alongside personal care and nutrition products such as shampoos, face washes, serums and food items.
For unconventional lifestyle brands like Cure By Design, festive pop-ups offer an opportunity to reach new audiences, build trust, and increase brand awareness. Since cannabidiol (CBD) is still an emerging category in India, these events allow the brand to educate consumers, address misconceptions, and encourage first-time purchases.
Costs vary depending on the event, location, and footfall, with expenses including stall rentals, staffing, logistics, and branding.
We’ve participated in pop-ups occasionally but have reduced them significantly since opening our retail stores in Bengaluru and Chennai. Permanent stores provide better customer engagement, stronger credibility, and more consistent conversions.
For us, ROI goes beyond immediate sales. We evaluate customer acquisition costs, leads generated, repeat purchases, and long-term customer value. Ultimately, pop-ups are worthwhile when they attract the right audience and build lasting customer relationships rather than simply generating footfall.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Ather’s Profit Milestone Meets A Manufacturing Crunch
Electric two-wheeler maker Ather Energy turned its maiden profit in Q2 FY27, and now plans to sustain its growth momentum via accelerated investments in its manufacturing capabilities as demand continues to outpace its production.
Let’s steal a glance at the OEM’s Q2 FY27 numbers:
Net profit of ₹1.3 Cr against a net loss of ₹154.1 Cr in Q2 FY26
Operating revenue climbed 62.9% to ₹1,464.2 Cr, up 20.3% QoQ
EBITDA profit widened to ₹74.2 Cr from ₹9 Cr a year ago
Sales of scooters rose 42% YoY to 93,211 units
Other Income Drives Maiden Profit: After 13 years of innovating EV technology, Ather Energy posted its first-ever profitable quarter after turning EBITDA profitable in the preceding quarter as revenue growth far outpaced expenses, which rose 39.4% YoY to ₹1,526 Cr. However, its operating revenue was ₹61.5 Cr lower than total expenses during the quarter, and the difference was plugged by other income, highlighting a continued quest to improve profitability margins.
Manufacturing Boost On The Cards: The OEM will invest ₹122 Cr to add 2.25 Lakh units annually to its manufacturing capacity. Its under-construction Factory 3.0 in Maharashtra will receive ₹64 Cr to add 1.5 Lakh units of annual capacity over the planned 5 Lakh units. At its Hosur plant, Ather will invest ₹53 Cr to add capacity for 75,000 units and also set up a new battery line to offset supply chain worries.
Ather Bleeds On Demand Front: The EV maker believes that it is losing 18,000-20,000 units in demand monthly due to its supply shortfall, with the Hosur plant now operating at 98% capacity and Factory 3.0 yet to go live. This comes as customer enquiries surged 109% YoY to around 10 Lakh, and pre-orders more than doubled to 1.8 Lakh.
With demand outpacing production and factories nearing capacity, its next challenge is to keep the growth engine running. While we will keep an eye out for just that, here’s how Ather Energy fared in the second quarter of FY27.
From The Editor’s Desk
Paytm’s Profit Spree
The fintech major’s Q2 FY27 net profit surged 10.7X YoY to ₹225 Cr from ₹21 Cr a year ago, edging up from ₹220 Cr in Q1 FY27.
Operating revenue grew 28% YoY and 8% QoQ to ₹2,648 Cr, while total expenses rose 23% YoY to ₹2,531 Cr.
Paytm’s profitability gains follow a strong Q1 FY27, when net profit rose 78.8% YoY to ₹220 Cr and EBITDA profit jumped 182% to ₹203 Cr, with an EBITDA margin of 8%.
Imarticus To File ₹1,000 Cr IPO Soon
The edtech startup is planning to file its DRHP with SEBI through the confidential route in the next two to three months for a ₹1,000 Cr IPO, up from its earlier ₹750 Cr plan.
The company plans to use the proceeds to expand its business, set up more Centres of Excellence, strengthen its School of Finance and Business and B2B operations, and pursue acquisitions. This follows its recent ₹800 Cr acquisition of Singapore’s BELLS Institute of Higher Learning.
The IPO plans come amid a slowdown in edtech funding and growing consolidation, with upGrad recently acquiring Unacademy in a deal valuing the startup at just over $200 Mn, down more than 90% from its peak valuation of $3.5 Bn.
Unacademy Cofounders’ ₹700 Cr VC Play
Gaurav Munjal and Roman Saini are raising ₹700 Cr for Longshot Capital, an early stage fund that has secured ₹250-300 Cr in commitments and is targeting its first close in January 2027.
The Bengaluru-based fund plans to back 25-28 AI and deeptech startups at the seed and pre-Series A stages, with initial cheques of 500K-1.5 Mn across sectors such as manufacturing, space, defence and robotics.
The move follows upGrad’s acquisition of Unacademy in an all-stock deal valuing the edtech startup at ₹1,955 Cr, over 90% below its peak valuation. The fund also builds on the founders’ track record of over 200 angel investments worth more than ₹25 Cr.
Pronto Founder Finds Her New Gig In AI
Anjali Sardana has launched an AI venture, Provision Labs, to collect real-world data for training and testing AI systems designed to perform physical tasks using robots and machines.
The launch follows scrutiny over Pronto’s pilot that involved recording household chores to generate robotics training data, raising concerns around customer consent, data privacy and the use of footage.
Provision Labs enters a growing market for real-world AI training data, with startups such as Human Archive, Awign and Objectways building pipelines to supply footage of human activities to AI and robotics developers.
Aequs Bloats Its Losses In Q2
The contract manufacturer reported a consolidated net loss of ₹52.4 Cr in Q2 FY27, widening 154.4% YoY from ₹20.6 Cr. It reported a net loss of ₹53.2 Cr in Q1.
Operating revenue grew 45.3% YoY to ₹409.1 Cr, led by its aerospace business, which contributed ₹351.4 Cr, while consumer business revenue rose 52% to ₹57.7 Cr.
Expenses excluding finance costs, depreciation and amortisation surged 56.2% to ₹395.2 Cr, outpacing revenue growth. Sequentially, the net loss narrowed marginally from ₹53.2 Cr in Q1 FY27.
AI Trading Platform Tradl Raises $4.1 Mn
Bengaluru-based Tradl raised $4.1 Mn in a seed round led by Nexus Venture Partners and Stellaris Venture Partners, with participation from angel investors.
Founded in 2025 by IIT Guwahati graduates Shubham Bansal and Nilesh Raj, Tradl combines AI and quantitative analysis to help retail traders screen stocks, analyse markets, and backtest strategies.
The fundraise comes amid rising investor interest in AI startups, with the segment attracting $438 Mn across 35 deals in Q3 2026, up 265% YoY.
Inc42 Markets
Inc42 Startup Spotlight
Inside Pulse’s Bet To Make Medical Equipment In India
India’s hospitals remain dependent on imported medical devices that can be costly, difficult to service and poorly adapted to local needs. Pulse is trying to build a domestic alternative by combining MSME manufacturing with product design under a single medtech brand.
Going Asset-Light: Founded in 2025, Pulse designs, sources and supplies medical devices and consumables. Instead of owning a large manufacturing base, it provides engineering, product standardisation, certifications, regulatory compliance and service infrastructure to small businesses. This enables these SMEs to build medical equipment that can compete with global manufacturers.
The Essential Approach: Pulse is initially targeting low- and mid-complexity devices across critical care, renal care and cardiac care. The company is also focusing on mid-tier hospitals, particularly facilities with 50-200 beds, where reliable equipment at accessible prices can have a direct impact on healthcare delivery.
The Quality Layer: The startup currently works with nearly 20 MSME partners across Delhi NCR, Gujarat, Kolkata and Mumbai. It is also establishing an R&D hub at the Andhra Pradesh MedTech Zone in Visakhapatnam. Going forward, the 3one4 Capital-backed startup plans to scale product development and distribution.
As hospitals seek affordable and dependable alternatives to imported equipment, can Pulse turn India into a medtech manufacturing hub?

items.content:
Today, the Reserve Bank released the October 2026 issue of its monthly Bulletin. The Bulletin includes two speeches, four articles and current statistics.
The four articles are: I. State of the Economy; II. Transmission to Lending Rates of SCBs: Price versus Composition Effects in WALR; III. Performance of the NBFC Sector: Review for 2025; and IV. Nowcasting State-Level Economic Activity in India with Night-Time Light and Google Trends.
I. State of the Economy
Renewed geopolitical frictions in West Asia and supply chain disruptions have amplified inflationary pressures, prompting major central banks to raise policy rates. Elevated sovereign bond yields in advanced economies (AEs) have also brought into focus concerns about fiscal sustainability and its implications for financial stability. The Indian economy continued to demonstrate strength as evidenced by high-frequency indicators across both industry and services. The headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation edged up in September driven by a broad-based increase in food, fuel, and core components. Double-digit growth in merchandise exports during the first six months of 2026-27 helped in narrowing the trade deficit. FDI, ECB and remittance flows strengthened in August. Strong inflows under the FCNR(B) swap window augmented reserves.
II. Transmission to Lending Rates of SCBs: Price versus Composition Effects in WALR
By Yuvraj Kashyap, Kamal Gupta and Arvind Jha
This article analyses the transmission of monetary policy to the fresh lending rates of scheduled commercial banks by decomposing variations in the weighted average lending rate (WALR) into interest rate effects and compositional effects. Using an index-number based framework on bank and sector level lending rates and loan weights, the study examines the extent to which changes in the aggregate WALR reflect changes in lending rates and shifts in credit composition.
Highlights:
In response to a cumulative reduction of 125 basis points (bps) in the policy repo rate, the WALR on fresh lending declined by 93 bps, with interest rate effect of 80 bps and composition effect of 13 bps during February 2025 to March 2026.
The movements in aggregate WALR reflect both repricing of loans and changes in the composition of credit across banks and sectors, highlighting the importance of both effects while assessing monetary policy transmission.
III. Performance of the NBFC Sector: Review for 2025
By Pallavi Pant, Monalisa Poali, Abhyuday Harsh, Brijesh P and Sona Chinngaihlian
This article assesses the performance of the non-banking financial company (NBFC) sector up to end-December 2025. It also provides a bird’s-eye-view of India’s financial system. Employing a text-mining approach, the article also explores the extent and nature of orientation towards artificial intelligence (AI) by select NBFCs.
Highlights:
The NBFC sector continued to register double-digit y-o-y credit growth at end-December 2025.
Share of bank borrowings showed a moderate rise indicating continued concentration in funding profile. Asset quality of the sector has continued to improve in recent years as reflected in consistent decline in NPA ratios.
Preliminary text-mining analysis shows that NBFCs are increasingly orienting towards AI for customer and financial applications, governance and digital infrastructure, and data analytics.
IV. Nowcasting State-Level Economic Activity in India with Night-Time Light and Google Trends
By Bipul Ghosh, Narendra Singh and Sandhya Kuruganti
Timely measurement of state-level economic activity remains a challenge in India, as official Gross State Value Added (GSVA) data are released annually with a considerable lag. This study demonstrates how alternative data sources, specifically satellite-based night-time lights and digital search behaviour, can be used to generate high-frequency estimates of state-level economic activity. The framework is applied to three major states — Maharashtra, Karnataka and Gujarat. It shows how combining geospatial and behavioural signals can provide a real-time view of regional economic dynamics and strengthen short-term economic assessment.
Highlights:
The combined use of night-time lights and Google Trends improves nowcast accuracy of quarterly GSVA growth relative to univariate approach.
The approach enables near real-time monitoring of state-level economies, improving early detection of turning points and shocks.
The methodology is scalable and demonstrates the potential of alternative data in supplementing official statistical systems and high-frequency macroeconomic analysis.
The views expressed in the Bulletin articles are those of the authors and do not represent the views of the Reserve Bank of India.
(Brij Raj)           
Chief General Manager
Press Release: 2026-2027/1381

items.content:
The Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, today inaugurated the Reserve Bank of India’s newly established Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. This marks a significant milestone in strengthening the technological foundation of India’s financial system. Hon’ble Governor of Odisha, Shri Brajmohan Ram, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Odisha, Shri Mohan Charan Majhi; Hon’ble Union Finance and Corporate Affairs Minister, Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman; Hon’ble Union Minister for Tribal Affairs, Shri Jual Oram; Hon’ble Deputy Chief Ministers of Odisha, Shri Kanak Vardhan Singh Deo and Smt. Pravati Parida, and Hon’ble Members of Parliament, Shri Manmohan Samal and Smt. Aparajita Sarangi, also graced the event.
2. In his address, the Hon’ble Prime Minister highlighted the significance of the institutions inaugurated today - the Data Centre and the Cybersecurity Training Institute - in strengthening India’s digital financial infrastructure and advancing its technological self-reliance. The PM described the facility as a reflection of India’s changing approach to governance focused on taking the benefits of economic development to every region and every citizen. He emphasised that a secure banking system needs secure digital infrastructure supported by robust data centres and powerful computing systems and RBI’s new Data Centre is a critical step in this direction.
3. In her address, the Hon’ble Union Minister of Finance and Corporate Affairs underscored the strategic importance of resilient infrastructure in safeguarding financial stability and supporting sustained economic growth. She further said that the new Data Centre will house RBI’s mission-critical systems, including RTGS and NEFT, while the Training Institute will build expertise in cybersecurity, AI and other emerging technologies.
4. In his welcome address, Reserve Bank Governor Shri Sanjay Malhotra expressed gratitude to the Hon’ble Prime Minister for his participation in the event. He emphasised the Reserve Bank’s commitment to leveraging emerging technologies, strengthening digital infrastructure, enhancing cybersecurity, developing indigenous technological capabilities and supporting the country’s aspiration to become a developed nation by 2047.
5. The event was attended by distinguished dignitaries from the Central Government, State Government, industry, academia, persons of eminence, Directors of the Central Board of the Reserve Bank, heads of banks, technology providers and senior officials of the Reserve Bank.
(Brij Raj)           
Chief General Manager

items.author: Haruna Gimba Yaya
items.content:
There is growing confusion in Gombe State following the appearance of the name of former Governor Ibrahim Hassan Dankwambo on the list of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Council.
Dankwambo, who is the leader of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in the state, is contesting for the Gombe North Senatorial seat in the 2027 general elections under the PDP platform.
The list, published in national dailies on Monday, includes Dankwambo as a member of the APC campaign structure—a development that has stirred confusion among PDP supporters in the state.
However, the state chapter of the PDP has officially disassociated Dankwambo from the APC’s advisory and campaign council list.
The 666-member campaign council, chaired by Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, contains the names of prominent APC figures, including Senator Muhammad Danjuma Goje, Senator Usman Bayero Nafada, and Senator Sa’idu Ahmed Alkali. Senator Dankwambo’s name is listed alongside these top party chieftains appointed to drive the APC campaign ahead of the 2027 elections.
Specifically, Senator Dankwambo appears at number seven on the 666-member campaign council list and number six on the 66-member advisory council, placing him above key figures within the state APC.
The development is already generating intense reactions. As a former governor and serving political leader, Dankwambo is widely regarded as the face of the PDP in Gombe State, making his inclusion on the ruling party’s campaign list a major talking point.
The inclusion has sparked questions about whether the senator has defected to the APC or relinquished his senatorial bid to enter into an alliance with the ruling party in the state.
This development comes at a time when former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Prof. Isa Ali Pantami, is fighting to secure a place on the ballot under the PDP after his name was omitted from the final list released by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).
Our correspondent reports that Dankwambo belongs to the faction of the PDP led by the Minister of the FCT, Barr. Nyesom Wike.
The State Publicity Secretary of the PDP, Abdulkadir Ahmad Dukku, said in a statement that the inclusion of Dankwambo’s name on the APC campaign list was intended to create confusion among PDP members and supporters in the state.
“Our attention has been drawn to the publication of a list of members of the APC campaign council in Gombe State, recently published in national dailies and across social media platforms,” Dukku said.
“The list, which contains the name of the Gombe State PDP Leader, Senator Ibrahim Hassan Dankwambo, as a member of the Advisory Committee of the APC Campaign Council in Gombe State, is fake and intended to cause confusion among members and supporters of the PDP in the state.”
He further disassociated the party and its leader from the purported list, adding that Senator Dankwambo was unaware of the development.
The publicity secretary stressed that Dankwambo remains a leading member of the PDP at both state and national levels and is “also the PDP senatorial candidate for Gombe North in the forthcoming general elections.”
Dukku accused the ruling APC in the state of engaging in “fabricated acts, calculated to cause mistrust and chaos among members and supporters of the PDP in Gombe State ahead of the 2027 general elections.”

items.author: Mohammed I. Yaba
items.content:
The Kaduna State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has urged former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar to withdraw from the 2027 presidential race and support President Bola Tinubu, asserting that the North has clearly demonstrated its preference for the incumbent.
According to the party, the massive turnout at the APC presidential campaign flag-off in Kaduna on Saturday proved that Atiku can no longer rely on northern votes to push his presidential ambitions.
The APC State Publicity Secretary, Mohammed Sani Haruna, made the call on Monday during a press briefing in Kaduna, where he described the crowd at the rally as overwhelming evidence of growing support for Tinubu across the region.
Haruna urged Atiku to align with Tinubu in the interest of national unity, recalling what he described as the President’s past political gesture toward the former Vice-President.
“It is on record that President Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu did Atiku Abubakar a favour by giving him a platform in 2011 to contest for the presidency of Nigeria,” Haruna said.
He argued that Atiku should reciprocate that gesture by supporting Tinubu rather than seeking another bid for the nation’s top office.
“There is no better time to align with Mr. President and show his patriotism for Nigeria than now—to work for the greater interest of the country,” Haruna added.
The APC spokesperson also advised Atiku, who is approaching 80 years of age, to drop his presidential ambition, warning that another failed attempt could expose him to further political embarrassment.
He noted that the Kaduna rally had shattered opposition expectations of securing dominant support in the North, a zone long considered central to Atiku’s electoral calculations.
Haruna accused Atiku and other opposition figures of exploiting ethnic, religious, and regional sentiments to court northern voters, rather than highlighting tangible contributions to the region’s development.
Addressing claims circulating on social media that crowd footage from the rally was generated using Artificial Intelligence (AI) and that attendees were paid to be there, the party spokesman dismissed the allegations as baseless.
He insisted that the turnout was purely organic, pointing out that thousands of supporters arrived early and waited patiently for hours to gain entry.
“People slept over at the venue. People queued as early as 4:00 a.m. to gain access into the stadium. You cannot buy that kind of sentiment,” he emphasized.

items.author: Shraddha Goled
items.content:
AI-native cybersecurity startup Protectt.ai plans to acquire a controlling stake in AIShield, an AI security platform incubated within Bosch Global Software Technologies (BGSW). Bosch will retain a minority stake in AIShield following the transaction.
Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Protectt.ai will acquire the stake through a deal comprising primary and secondary components. The companies have not disclosed the transaction value or timeline.
“There will be cash, a secondary component and future investments as required. The current structure is a combination of cash and ESOPs. Future investments will depend on the requirements of the business,” Protectt.ai cofounder Manish Mimani told Inc42.
Founded in 2022 by Shiv Kumar and Amit Phadke, AIShield was incubated within BGSW. It develops security solutions for machine learning models, generative AI applications and AI supply chains, helping enterprises defend against attacks designed to manipulate AI systems and address compliance risks.
The partnership will combine AIShield’s AI security capabilities with Protectt.ai’s mobile security platform, allowing the latter to expand into enterprise AI security.
AIShield will continue to operate as an independent entity under Protectt.ai once the deal is completed, with its own professional management team and a focus on AI security research and product development. It will also be able to raise external funding in the future.
Protectt.ai plans to work with private companies and government organisations through AIShield to build an India-developed AI security platform, Mimani said.
From Mobile Security To Enterprise AI
Founded in 2020 by Manish Mimani and Mohanraj Selvaraj, Protectt.ai provides mobile threat defence solutions that help businesses protect applications against cyber threats and fraud. Its platform also serves as a compliance hub for app owners, helping them adhere to regulations issued by entities such as the RBI, SEBI and NPCI.
The startup also offers a full-stack AI security platform with tools to test AI agents for vulnerabilities, secure connections between AI applications and external tools, and monitor AI agents while they operate.
Protectt.ai’s security technology runs on more than 1 Bn mobile devices and processes 15 Bn mobile application sessions every month, Mimani said.
He expects mobile applications to increasingly rely on AI agents to perform tasks, potentially reducing the need for users to navigate conventional app interfaces over the next one to two years.
Protectt.ai had already been researching AI model scanning and AI agent security as part of its product roadmap. Through the AIShield acquisition, the startup aims to extend these capabilities beyond mobile applications to enterprise use cases across sectors.
Some members of Protectt.ai’s AI security team will move to AIShield, although the number has yet to be finalised.
AIShield currently has around 12–15 employees and plans to expand its team to 50–60 people by March 2027. It plans to hire PhD researchers, master’s graduates and other technical talent from leading institutions to strengthen its research and engineering capabilities.
The team will focus on developing products, conducting research and filing patents, Mimani said.
Protectt.ai Eyes Further Acquisitions
The AIShield deal is Protectt.ai’s first such acquisition. The startup set up an M&A team earlier in 2026 to evaluate potential acquisitions and partnerships, with a focus on building capabilities and addressing gaps in its existing offerings.
Protectt.ai is exploring opportunities in areas such as API security and cloud security that could complement its current capabilities, Mimani said.
The startup secured around $16 Mn in a Series A funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners and Bajaj Finance in 2025. Mimani added that Protectt.ai is evaluating opportunities and expects to consider raising fresh funds in 2027.

items.content: Mumbai: Retail investors returned to the secondary market in September after sitting out two months on the trot, buying equities worth ₹10,572 crore as an oil spike induced a sharp market correction after the first week.Buying in the primary market continued for the ninth straight month.Retail investors' secondary-market purchases were their highest since June, when they bought equities worth ₹19,046 crore. They had sold shares worth ₹3,721 crore in July and ₹1,983 crore in August, NSE data showed.135221921In the primary market, retail investors bought shares worth ₹5,650 crore in September, compared with ₹6,791 crore in July and ₹5,827 crore in August."September's retail buying was a classic buy-the-dip response, not a return of speculative froth," said Akshat Garg, head of research & product at Choice Wealth. Retail investors stepped back in at lower prices after selling in July and August, even as foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) were heading for the exit, he said.Read more: Paytm Q2 Results: Profit rockets 976% YoY to Rs 226 crore, revenue jumps 28%The Sensex and Nifty fell about 6% in September, their sharpest monthly decline since March, and were down nearly 14% in 2026.So far this year, retail investors have bought equities worth ₹47,556 crore in the secondary market and ₹19,382 crore in the primary market, taking their combined purchases to ₹66,938 crore.Retail participation in the primary market has remained strong, with close to 30 mainboard companies listing in September. The IPO index was among the few to end the month in positive territory.Read more: The Rs 1.5 lakh crore MTF problem: How shrinking leveraged positions are deepening India's smallcap sell-off"Buying may continue selectively, supported by a strong IPO pipeline and domestic investor confidence," said Ravi Singh, chief research officer at Master Capital Services. However, valuations, corporate earnings, crude oil prices, foreign investor outflows and global uncertainty could influence participation, he said. Sustained buying will depend on market performance and the availability of attractive opportunities in both the primary and secondary markets.With foreign portfolio investors pulling out more than ₹44,000 crore in October alone, market volatility remains a key consideration. Experts advise investors to stagger their investments, prioritise companies with visible earnings growth and assess IPOs on business quality rather than potential listing gains.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
US President Donald Trump hit back at Barack Obama on Monday after the former president jokingly said his successor’s White House looked as if it were a cheesecake restaurant run by Saddam Hussein.
“For you to say it’s a Cheesecake Factory, that just shows why you were a lousy president,” Trump said in a three-minute diatribe when asked about Obama’s comments over the weekend.
“Guys like Obama, they would pass the front door, they would see the broken masonry… He doesn’t notice dirt and filth where the walls haven’t been cleaned for years,” Trump told reporters as he headed for his latest midterm election rally.
Cheesecake Factory is a popular restaurant chain known for its lengthy list of indulgent dishes and an eclectic interior design.
Obama made a series of scathing criticisms of Republican Trump’s “chaos and cruelty” as he hit the stump for Democrats in Ohio and Michigan ahead of next week’s midterm elections.
But it was Obama’s jabs at billionaire Trump’s prized renovations at the White House — including building a massive ballroom and adding gold-leafed ornamentation throughout the Oval Office — that really appeared to sting.
“He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory,” Obama said on Saturday, referring to the Iraqi dictator who was executed in 2006 following the US invasion of Iraq.
Trump has long had a bitter rivalry with Obama.
He launched his own political career by pushing the racist and false “birther” conspiracy theory that the Democrat was lying about being born in the United States.
But Trump’s rant over the cheesecake comments was also a sign of the 80-year-old’s increasingly short temper as the midterms loom.
On Sunday night, Trump sent his longest ever post on his Truth Social network — a 1,300-word screed in which he railed not about Iran or the economy but about US comedian Bill Maher.
Last week Trump also lashed out at a series of reporters as he faced questions about the midterms, in which Republicans face losing control of Congress, and his dealings with Russia.
AFP

De la Fuente emerged victorious ahead of fellow nominees Mikel Arteta of Arsenal, Luis Enrique of Paris Saint-Germain, Vincent Kompany of Bayern Munich and Unai Emery of Aston Villa.
Former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez presented the award, although the announcement was briefly interrupted by an unexpected mix-up involving the winner’s name on the card.

The award adds to De la Fuente’s achievements with the Spanish national team, following Spain’s triumph at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

The National Leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, has inaugurated its newly acquired national secretariat in Abuja as part of efforts to strengthen its operations ahead of the 2027 general election.
The facility, located in the Jabi area of the Federal Capital Territory, was unveiled shortly after an emergency meeting of the party’s National Executive Committee (NEC), as it marks a significant step in the party’s efforts to strengthen its organisational structure and establish a permanent administrative base as preparations for the forthcoming elections gather momentum.
The new secretariat is expected to serve as the party’s administrative centre and headquarters for its presidential campaign as preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum, just as the development marks a step in the NDC’s efforts to establish a permanent national base for coordinating its activities and managing its expanding political structure.
It is a strategic centre for coordinating its activities, strengthening communication among state chapters and mobilising supporters across the country and is also expected to play a central role in organising the party’s presidential campaign and coordinating other electoral activities ahead of the 2027 general elections
In his remarks, the National Leader of the party, Senator Seriake Dickson, described the facility as its new “Noah’s Ark” ahead of the 2027 general elections as he congratulated members and supporters on the acquisition, describing the new secretariat as a unifying centre that would provide a befitting home for the party’s growing membership.
He referred to the facility as the NDC’s newly acquired “Noah’s Ark,” a description underscoring its importance as a rallying point for members and supporters as the party pursues its political ambitions.
The inauguration attracted the party’s National Chairman, Senator Moses Cleopas; National Leader, Senator Seriake Dickson; and Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central in the National Assembly.
Also present was the party’s Rivers State governorship candidate, Dumo Lulu-Briggs, alongside other party leaders and members.
With this, the NDC has positioned itself as an alternative political platform for Nigerians seeking a change from the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).
With the new facility, the party is expected to strengthen coordination between its national leadership, state chapters and other structures as election preparations continue.

In April, the company reportedly offered around seven percent of its US workforce the option to retire early.
Around 30 percent of those eligible took the voluntary retirement plan, according to CNBC.
Microsoft had 223,000 employees globally at the end of June, down from 228,000 at the end of 2025, according to regulatory filings.

The company is expected to report quarterly earnings later this week.

The chairman of the APC North Central, Hon. Mu’azu Rijau, while congratulating the council leadership, stressed that the 2027 campaign council should not underestimate opponents, saying the party aimed to re-elect Governor Bago alongside its senators, House of Representatives members and state assembly members.
Director-General of the campaign council, Ahmed Ibeto, accepted the assignment on behalf of members, pledging hard work, strategic coordination, grassroots engagement, unity, discipline and compliance with electoral guidelines.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
AI-powered healthtech platform BioStack has raised $9.5 Mn (₹90.4 Cr) in its seed funding round led by Peak XV Partners, Afore Capital, DCVC, Emerson Collective, SV Angel, Verdict Capital, Streamlined Ventures, and Y Combinator.
The startup plans to utilise the fresh capital to continue expanding its presence in the US and other international markets, including India, Brazil, and Argentina. A chunk of the capital will also be used to scale its tech stack and ramp up hiring across engineering and research teams.
Founded in 2025 by Sanat Mishra and Parth Patwa, BioStack claims to be building the data infrastructure for the next generation of medical AI.
It combines fragmented clinical information across systems such as electronic health records, medical imaging, clinical notes and medications. The startup then uses this data to create proprietary datasets for research, biotechnology, and the development and training of medical AI models.
“We’re building the infrastructure that connects all of the clinical information and makes it useful, both for clinicians making decisions today and for the researchers and AI developers building the future of medicine,” said BioStack cofounder and CEO Mishra.
BioStack currently works with multiple hospitals across the US, Brazil and Argentina. In India, it is also connecting cancer patients with an investigational cancer vaccine program.
The startup also claims that it offers use cases such as AI model evaluation, disease modeling, biomarker discovery, patient stratification and treatment-response analysis.
Besides offering custom workflows to protect patient privacy, the startup claims to have so far processed 10 Cr de-identified patient records, more than “several hundred thousand” fragmented X-Rays, MRIs and CT scans, and “several million” telehealth audio transcripts.
For context, de-identified patient records are medical datasets that have had all personal and direct identifiers removed so that the individual cannot reasonably be linked to the data.
The fundraise comes as India becomes a training ground to collect datasets for powering AI models and physical AI products. Startups are tapping India’s huge population to collect recordings of workers performing physical tasks, processing the footage, and selling the resulting datasets to frontier AI labs and robotics companies.
For instance, the likes of Awign, Objectways and Human Archive are building pipelines to supply first-person footage of human activity to AI developers. Just a day ago, instant home services startup Pronto’s founder Anjali Sardana launched Provision Labs, a US-based venture to collect data for physical AI systems.
At the heart of all this is the Indian AI training dataset, which is projected to become a $1.3 Bn opportunity by 2033.

The list features players from Europe, Africa and the Caribbean, reflecting the growing global reach of women’s football.
Chawinga’s historic finish represents a breakthrough for African representation in the prestigious individual award and further highlights her rise as one of the leading figures in the women’s game.

By Steve Oko
Abia State Police Command has confirmed that a man who attempted to rescue a teenage girl from a water-filled ditch at Faulks Road, Aba, was swept away alongside the girl during Sunday’s downpour.
The Police Public Relations Officer, Maureen Chinaka, disclosed this while responding to Vanguard inquiries, confirming that the incident occurred around the popular Ukwu Mango area of the commercial city.

An adult who witnessed the incident reportedly plunged into the water in an attempt to rescue her, but both were swept away.
“Unfortunately, we have not been able to see them. The police are aware, and the matter has been reported. Efforts are in place to see how they can be rescued,” Chinaka said.

The tragedy has raised concerns about the safety of construction sites during heavy rainfall, particularly where excavations and drainage channels are left uncovered and become submerged in floodwater.
Aba’s flat terrain makes parts of the commercial city vulnerable to flooding during heavy downpours, increasing the risks posed by waterlogged roads, open drains and excavations.
